Those <s>sūtras</s> taught for the purpose of entering the fruit — these are called of provisional meaning. Those <s>sūtras</s> taught as gateways to liberation through emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), signlessness (<s>animitta</s>), wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>), non-fabrication (<s>anabhisaṃskāra</s>), non-birth (<s>ajāta</s>), non-arising (<s>anutpāda</s>), non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>), no-self (<s>nirātma</s>), no-being (<s>niḥsattva</s>), no-life-principle (<s>nirjīva</s>), no-person (<s>niḥpudgala</s>), and ownerlessness (<s>asvāmika</s>) — these are called of definitive meaning. This, Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is called taking <s>sūtras</s> of definitive meaning as one's refuge, not taking <s>sūtras</s> of provisional meaning as one's refuge.'

body.text: tathā ca āryasamādhirājasūtre-
body.translated_text: And also in the noble <s>Samādhirājasūtra</s>:

children.translated_text: One who knows the distinctive quality of <s>sūtras</s> of definitive meaning, as emptiness was taught by the <s>Sugata</s>,

children.text: yasmin punaḥ pudgalasattvapūruṣā neyārthato jānati sarvadharmān ||
children.translated_text: and wherever persons, beings, and individuals [are mentioned], knows all <s>dharmas</s> to be of provisional meaning. //

body.text: tasmādutpādādideśanāṃ mṛṣārthāṃ pratipādayituṃ pratītyasamutpādānudarśanamārabdhavānācāryaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, in order to demonstrate that the teaching of arising and so forth is of false meaning, the <s>Ācārya</s> undertook this examination of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination).

body.text: nanu ca- utpādādīnāmabhāve sati yadi sarvadharmāṇāṃ mṛṣātvapratipādanārthamidamārabdhavānācāryaḥ nanvevaṃ sati yanmṛṣā na tadastīti na santyakuśalāni karmāṇi, tadabhāvānna santi durgatayaḥ, na santi kuśalāni karmāṇi, tadabhāvānna santi sugatayaḥ, sugatidurgatyasaṃbhavācca nāsti saṃsāraḥ, iti sarvārambhavaiyarthyameva sthāt | ucyate | saṃvṛtisatyavyapekṣayā lokasya idaṃsatyābhiniveśasya pratipakṣabhāvena mṛṣārthatā bhāvānāṃ pratipādyate 'smābhiḥ | naiva tvāryāḥ kṛtakāryāḥ kiṃcidupalabhante yanmṛṣā amṛṣā vā syāditi | api ca | yena hi sarvadharmāṇāṃ mṛṣātvaṃ parijñātaṃ kiṃ tasya karmāṇi santi, saṃsāro vā asti? na cāpyasau kasyaciddharmassya astitvaṃ nāstitvaṃ vopalabhate | yathoktaṃ bhagavatā āryaratnakūṭasūtre-
body.translated_text: But surely — if, in the absence of arising and so forth, the <s>Ācārya</s> has undertaken this in order to demonstrate the falsity of all <s>dharmas</s>, then since what is false does not exist, unwholesome deeds do not exist; since they do not exist, bad destinations do not exist; wholesome deeds do not exist; since they do not exist, good destinations do not exist; and since good and bad destinations are impossible, <s>saṃsāra</s> does not exist — thus all endeavor would be pointless! It is replied: With reference to conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>), as an antidote to the world's clinging to 'this is real,' the falsity of entities is demonstrated by us. But the Noble Ones who have accomplished their task do not apprehend anything whatsoever that would be either false or not false. Moreover, for one who has fully comprehended the falsity of all <s>dharmas</s>, do deeds exist for him, or does <s>saṃsāra</s>? Nor does he apprehend the existence or non-existence of any <s>dharma</s>. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> stated in the noble <s>Ratnakūṭasūtra</s>:

body.text: cittaṃ hi kāśyapa parigaveṣyamāṇaṃ na labhyate | yanna labhyate tannopalabhyate | yannopalabhyate tannaiva atītaṃ na anāgataṃ na pratyutpannam | yannaivātītaṃ nānāgataṃ na pratyutpannam, tasya nāsti svabhāvaḥ | yasya nāsti svabhāvaḥ, tasya nāstyutpādaḥ | yasya nāstyutpādaḥ, tasya nāsti nirodhaḥ || iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'For, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the mind, when sought, is not found. What is not found is not apprehended. What is not apprehended is neither past, nor future, nor present. What is neither past, nor future, nor present has no intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>). What has no intrinsic nature has no arising. What has no arising has no cessation.' Thus in detail.

body.text: yastu viparyāsānugamānmṛṣātvaṃ nāvagacchati, pratītya bhāvānā svabhāvamabhiniviśate, sa dharmeṣvidaṃsatyābhiniveśādabhiniviṣṭaḥ san karmāṇyapi karoti, saṃsāre 'pi saṃsarati, viparyāsāvasthitatvānna bhavyo nirvāṇamadhigantum ||
body.translated_text: But one who, through following wrong views (<s>viparyāsa</s>), does not comprehend the falsity [of phenomena], and who clings to the intrinsic nature of entities dependent on conditions — he, clinging to 'this is real' with regard to <s>dharmas</s>, performs deeds, transmigrates in <s>saṃsāra</s>, and being established in wrong views, is not capable of attaining <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ- mṛṣāsvabhāvā api padārthāḥ saṃkleśavyavadānanibandhanaṃ bhavanti | tadyathā māyāyuvatistatsvabhāvānabhijñānām, tathāgatanirmitaśca upacitakuśalamūlānām | uktaṃ hi dṛḍhādhyāśayaparipṛcchāsūtre-
body.translated_text: But furthermore — do even entities whose nature is false serve as the basis for defilement and purification? Yes, just as an illusory young woman [serves as a basis] for those who do not understand her true nature, and just as a <s>Tathāgata</s>-emanation [serves as a basis] for those whose wholesome roots have been accumulated. For it is stated in the <s>Dṛḍhādhyāśayaparipṛcchāsūtra</s>:

body.text: tadyathā kulaputra māyākāranāṭake pratyupasthite māyākāranirmitāṃ striyaṃ dṛṣṭvā kaścidrāgaparītacittāḥ parṣacchāradyabhayena utthāyāsanādapakrāmet, so 'pakramya tāmeva striyamaśubhato manasikuryāt, anityato duḥkhataḥ śūnyato 'nātmato manasikuryāt | iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as, son of good family, when a magician's performance is presented, someone, seeing a woman created by the magician, with his mind overcome by passion, out of shame before the audience, would rise from his seat and depart. Having departed, he would contemplate that very woman as impure, as impermanent, as suffering, as empty, as non-self.' Thus in detail.

body.text: vinaye ca-
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Vinaya</s>:

body.text: yantrakārakāritā yantrayuvatiḥ sadbhūtayuvatiśūnyā sadbhūtayuvatirūpeṇa pratibhāsate, tasya ca citrakārasya kāmarāgāspadībhūtā | tathā mṛṣāsvabhāvā api bhāvā bālānāṃ saṃkleśavyavadānanibandhanaṃ bhavanti ||
body.translated_text: 'A mechanical young woman, created by a machine-maker, empty of a real young woman, appears in the form of a real young woman, and becomes the object of sensual desire for that painter. Even so, entities whose nature is false serve as the basis for defilement and purification for the foolish.'

body.text: tathā āryaratnakūṭasūtre-
body.translated_text: And also in the noble <s>Ratnakūṭasūtra</s>:

body.text: atha khalu tāni pañcamātrāṇi bhikṣuśatāni bhagavato dharmadeśanāmanavatarantyanavagāhamānānyanadhimucyamānāni utthāyāsanebhyaḥ prakrāntāni | atha bhagavān [tasyāṃ velāyāṃ] yena mārgeṇaite bhikṣavo gacchanti sma, tasmin mārge dvau bhikṣū nirmimīte sma ||
body.translated_text: Then those five hundred monks, not entering, not penetrating, not accepting the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, rose from their seats and departed. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, on the road by which those monks were going, created two monks by magical power.

body.text: atha tāni pañca bhikṣuśatāni yena [mārgeṇa] tau dvau bhikṣū [nirmitakau] tenopasaṃkrāmanti sma | upasaṃkramya tāvavocan- kutrāyuṣmantau gamiṣyathaḥ? nirmitakāvavocatām- gamiṣyāva āvāmaraṇyāyataneṣu, tatra dhyānasukhasparśavihārairvihariṣyāvaḥ | yaṃ hi bhagavān dharmaṃ deśayati, tamāvāṃ nāvatarāvo nāvagāhāvahe nādhimucyāmahe uttrasyāvaḥ saṃtrāsamāpadyāvahe | atha tāni pañca bhikṣuśatānyetadavocan- vayamapyāyuṣmanto bhagavato dharmadeśanāṃ nāvatarāmo nāvagāhāmahe nādhimucyāmahe uttrasyāmaḥ saṃtrasyāmaḥ saṃtrāsamāpadyāmahe | tena vayamaraṇyāyataneṣu dhyānasukhasparśavihārairvihariṣyāmaḥ | nirmitakāvavocatām- tena hi āyuṣmantaḥ saṃgāsyāmo na vivadiṣyāmaḥ | avivādaparamā hi śramaṇasya dharmāḥ | kasyāyuṣmantaḥ prahāṇāya pratipannāḥ? tānyavocan- rāgadveṣamohānāṃ prahāṇāya vayaṃ pratipannāḥ | nirmitakāvavocatām- kiṃ punarāyuṣmatāṃ saṃvidyante rāgadveṣamohā yān kṣapayiṣyatha? tānyavocan- na te 'dhyātmaṃ na bahirdhā nobhayamantareṇopalabhyante, nāpi te 'parikalpitā utpadyante | nirmitakāvavocatām- tena hi āyuṣmanto mā kalpayata, [mā vikalpayata] | yadā cāyuṣmanto na kalpayiṣyatha na vikalpayiṣyatha, tadā na raṃkṣyatha na viraṃkṣyatha | yaśca na rakto na viraktaḥ, sa śānta ityucyate | śīlamāyuṣmanto na saṃsarati na parinirvāti | samādhiḥ prajñā vimuktirvimuktijñānadarśanamāyuṣmanto
body.translated_text: Then those five hundred monks approached the two monks [who were emanations] by the path [they were taking]. Having approached, they said to them: 'Where will you venerable ones go?' The two emanations said: 'We shall go to forest retreats; there we shall dwell experiencing the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). For the <s>Dharma</s> that the <s>Bhagavān</s> teaches — we do not penetrate it, we do not fathom it, we do not have confidence in it; we are frightened, we fall into alarm.' Then those five hundred monks said: 'We too, venerable ones, do not penetrate the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, we do not fathom it, we do not have confidence in it; we are frightened, we are alarmed, we fall into alarm. Therefore we too shall dwell in forest retreats experiencing the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s>.' The two emanations said: 'If so, venerable ones, let us dwell together and not quarrel. For the virtues of an ascetic are those which are supreme in non-contention. For the abandonment of what, venerable ones, have you set out?' They said: 'We have set out for the abandonment of passion, hatred, and delusion.' The two emanations said: 'Do the venerable ones actually possess passion, hatred, and delusion that you would exhaust? They said: 'They are not found internally, nor externally, nor in between the two; nor do they arise unconstructed.' The two emanations said: 'Then, venerable ones, do not construct, do not discriminately construct. When you will not construct and not discriminately construct, then you will not be attached and not be detached. And one who is neither attached nor detached is called "at peace." <s>Śīla</s> (morality), venerable ones, neither transmigrates nor attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. <s>Samādhi</s> (concentration), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>vimukti</s> (liberation), <s>vimuktijñānadarśana</s> (the knowledge and vision of liberation), venerable ones,

body.text: na saṃsarati na parinirvāti | ebhiścāyuṣmanto dharmairnirvāṇaṃ sūcyate | ete ca dharmāḥ śūnyāḥ prakṛtiviviktāḥ | prajahītaitāmāyuṣmantaḥ saṃjñāṃ yaduta parinirvāṇamiti | mā ca saṃjñāyāṃ saṃjñā kārṣṭa, mā ca saṃjñāyāṃ saṃjñāṃ parijñāsiṣṭa | yo hi saṃjñāyāṃ saṃjñāṃ parijānāti, saṃjñā bandhanamevāsya tadbhavati | saṃjñāvedayitanirodhasamāpattimāyuṣmantaḥ samāpadyadhvam | saṃjñāvedayitanirodhasamāpattisamāpannasya bhikṣornāstyuttarīkaraṇīyamiti vadāvaḥ ||
body.translated_text: neither transmigrate nor attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. And by these <s>dharmas</s>, venerable ones, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is indicated. And these <s>dharmas</s> are empty, by nature isolated. Abandon, venerable ones, this notion — namely, '<s>parinirvāṇa</s>.' Do not form a notion about the notion, and do not fully know the notion through the notion. For one who fully knows the notion through the notion — the notion becomes a bondage for him. Venerable ones, enter the <s>saṃjñāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti</s> (the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling). For a monk who has entered the <s>saṃjñāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti</s>, we say there is nothing further to be done.'

body.text: atha teṣāṃ pañcānāṃ bhikṣuśatānāmanupādāyāśravebhyaścittāni vimuktānyabhūvan | tāni vimuktacittāni yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāni | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandyaikānte nyasīdan |
body.translated_text: Then the minds of those five hundred monks were liberated from the <s>āśravas</s> (defilements) without clinging. Those liberated minds approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and sat down to one side.

body.text: athāyuṣmān subhūtistān | bhikṣūnetadavocat- kutrāyuṣmanto gatāḥ kuto vāgatāḥ te 'vocan- na kvacidgamanāya na kutaścidāgamanāya bhadanta subhūte bhagavatā dharmo deśitaḥ āha- ko nāmāyuṣmatāṃ śāstā? āhuḥ- yo notpanno na parinirvāsyati | āha- kathaṃ yuṣmābhirdharmaḥ śrutaḥ? āhuḥ- na bandhanāya na mokṣāya | āha- kena yūyaṃ vinītāḥ? āhuḥ- yasya na kāyo na cittam | āha- kathaṃ yūyaṃ prayuktāḥ? āhuḥ- nāvidyāprahāṇāya na vidyotpādanāya | āha- kasya yūyaṃ śrāvakāḥ? āhuḥ- yena na prāptaṃ nābhisaṃbuddham | āha- ke yuṣmākaṃ sabrahmacāriṇaḥ? āhuḥ- ye traidhātuke nopavicaranti | āha- kiyaccireṇāyuṣmantaḥ parinirvāsyanti āhuḥ- yadā tathāgatanirmitāḥ parinirvāsyanti | āha- kṛtaṃ yuṣmābhiḥ karaṇīyam? āhuḥ- ahaṃ kāramamakāraparijñānataḥ | āha- kṣīṇā yuṣmākaṃ kleśāḥ? āhuḥ- atyantakṣayātsarvadharmāṇām | āha- dharṣito yuṣmābhirmāraḥ? āhuḥ- skandhamārānupalambhāt | āha- dharṣito yuṣmābhirmāraḥ? āhuḥ- skandhamārānupalambhāt | āha- paricarito yuṣmābhiḥ śāstā? āhuḥ- na kāyena na vācā na manasā | āha- viśodhitā yuṣmābhirdakṣiṇīyabhūmiḥ? āhuḥ- agrāhato 'pratigrāhataḥ | āha- uttīrṇo yuṣmābhiḥ saṃsāraḥ? āhuḥ- anucchedato 'śāśvatataḥ | āha- pratipannā yuṣmābhirdakṣiṇīyabhūmiḥ? āhuḥ- sarvagrāhavinirmuktitaḥ | āha- kiṃgāmina āyuṣmantaḥ? āhuḥ- yaṃgāminastathāgatanirmitāḥ | iti hyāyuṣmataḥ subhūteḥ paripṛcchatasteṣāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ prativisarjayatāṃ tasyāṃ parṣadi aṣṭānāṃ bhikṣuśatānāmanupādāyāśravebhyaścittāni vimuktāni, dvātriṃśataśca prāṇisahasrāṇāṃ virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmacakṣurviśuddham | iti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to those monks: 'Where did you venerable ones go, and from where have you come?' They said: 'The <s>Dharma</s> has been taught by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as being neither for going anywhere nor for coming from anywhere, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>.' He said: 'Who is the teacher of the venerable ones?' They said: 'He who is neither arisen nor will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.' He said: 'How was the <s>Dharma</s> heard by you?' They said: 'Neither for bondage nor for liberation.' He said: 'By whom were you disciplined?' They said: 'By one who has neither body nor mind.' He said: 'How were you exerted?' They said: 'Neither for the abandonment of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) nor for the production of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge).' He said: 'Whose disciples are you?' They said: 'Of one by whom nothing was attained nor fully awakened to.' He said: 'Who are your fellow practitioners of the holy life?' They said: 'Those who do not range through the three realms.' He said: 'When will you venerable ones attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>?' They said: 'When the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s emanations attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.' He said: 'Has what was to be done been done by you?' They said: 'Through the full understanding of "I-making" and "mine-making."' He said: 'Are your <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) exhausted?' They said: 'Through the ultimate exhaustion of all <s>dharmas</s>.' He said: 'Has <s>Māra</s> been vanquished by you?' They said: 'Through the non-apprehension of the <s>skandha</s>-<s>Māra</s> (the Māra of the aggregates).' He said: 'Has <s>Māra</s> been vanquished by you?' They said: 'Through the non-apprehension of the <s>skandha</s>-<s>Māra</s>.' He said: 'Has the Teacher been served by you?' They said: 'Not by body, not by speech, not by mind.' He said: 'Has the field worthy of offerings been purified by you?' They said: 'Through non-grasping and non-receiving.' He said: 'Has <s>saṃsāra</s> been crossed over by you?' They said: 'Through neither annihilation nor eternalism.' He said: 'Has the field worthy of offerings been reached by you?' They said: 'Through freedom from all grasping.' He said: 'Where are you going, venerable ones?' They said: 'Where the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s emanations are going.' Thus, as the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> questioned and those monks answered, in that assembly the minds of eight hundred monks were liberated from the <s>āśravas</s> (defilements) without clinging, and the <s>dharmacakṣus</s> (Dharma-eye) — free from dust, free from stain — was purified in thirty-two thousand beings.

body.text: ityevaṃ mṛṣāsvabhāvābhyāṃ tathāgatanirmitābhyāṃ bhikṣubhyāṃ pañcānāṃ bhikṣuśatānāṃ vyavadānanibandhanaṃ kṛtamiti ||
body.translated_text: Thus, by two monks who were emanations of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, of false nature, the cause of purification was accomplished for five hundred monks.

body.text: uktaṃ ca āryavajramaṇḍāyāṃ dhāraṇyām-
body.translated_text: And it is said in the Noble <s>Vajramaṇḍā Dhāraṇī</s>:

body.text: tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ kāṇḍaṃ ca pratītya mathanīṃ ca pratītya puruṣasya hastavyāyāmaṃ ca pratītya dhūmaḥ prādurbhavatīti agnirabhinirvartate | sa cāgnisaṃtāpo na kāṇḍasaṃniśrito na mathanīsaṃniśrito na puruṣahastavyāyāmasaṃniśritaḥ | evameva mañjuśrīḥ asadviparyāsamohitasya puruṣapudgalasya utpadyate rāgaparidāho dveṣaparidāho mohaparidāhaḥ | sa ca paridāho nādhyātmaṃ na bahirdhā nobhayamantareṇa sthitaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, dependent on a kindling-stick, dependent on a drill, and dependent on the exertion of a person's hand, smoke appears and fire is produced — and that heat of fire is not located in the kindling-stick, not located in the drill, and not located in the exertion of the person's hand — even so, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, for a person deluded by false perversion, there arises the burning of passion, the burning of hatred, and the burning of delusion. And that burning is not located internally, nor externally, nor in between the two.

body.text: api tu mañjuśrīḥ yaducyate moha iti, tatkena kāraṇenocyate moha iti? atyantamukto hi mañjuśrīḥ sarvadharmairmohastenocyate moha iti | tathā narakamukhā mañjuśrīḥ sarvadharmā idaṃ dhāraṇīpadam |
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, what is called 'delusion' — for what reason is it called 'delusion'? Because delusion, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is utterly released from all <s>dharmas</s> — therefore it is called 'delusion.' Likewise, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> have the gateway of hell — this is the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-word.

body.text: āha- kathaṃ bhagavannidaṃ dhāraṇīpadam? āha- narakā mañjuśrīḥ bālapṛgthajanairasadviparyāsaviṭhapitāḥ svavikalpasaṃbhūtāḥ | āha- kutra bhagavannarakāḥ samavasaranti? bhagavānāha- ākāśasamavasaraṇā mañjuśrīḥ narakāḥ | tatkiṃ manyase mañjuśrīḥ svavikalpasaṃbhūtā narakā uta svabhāvasaṃbhūtāḥ? āha- svavikalpenaiva bhagavan sarvabālapṛthagjanāṃ narakatiryagyoniyamalokaṃ saṃjānanti | te ca asatsamāropeṇa duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayanti duḥkhamanubhavanti triṣvapyapāyeṣu ||
body.translated_text: He said: 'How is this <s>dhāraṇī</s>-word to be understood, <s>Bhagavān</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Hells, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, are erected by foolish ordinary beings through false perversion; they arise from their own conceptual constructions.' He said: 'Where, <s>Bhagavān</s>, do the hells converge?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'The hells converge in space, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>. What do you think, <s>Mañjuśrī</s> — are the hells produced from one's own conceptual constructions, or produced from their own nature?' He said: 'It is by their own conceptual constructions alone, <s>Bhagavān</s>, that all foolish ordinary beings perceive the hells, the animal realm, and the world of <s>Yama</s>. And through false superimposition, they experience painful feeling, they undergo suffering in all three lower realms.'

body.text: yathā cāhaṃ bhagavan narakān paśyāmi tathā nārakaṃ duḥkham | tadyathā bhagavan kaścideva puruṣaḥ suptaḥ svapnāntaragato narakagatamātmānaṃ saṃjānīte | sa tatra kvathitāyāṃ saṃprajvalitāyāmanekapauruṣāyāṃ lohakumbhyāṃ prakṣiptamātmānaṃ saṃjānŌṣyāt | sa tatra kharāṃ kaṭukāṃ tŌṣvrāṃ duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayet | sa tatra mānasaṃ paridāhaṃ saṃjānŌṣyāt uttraset saṃtrāsamāpadyeta | sa tatra pratibuddhaḥ samānaḥ- aho duḥkham, aho duḥkham, iti krandet śocet paridevet | atha tasya mitrajñāti sālohitāḥ paripṛccheyuḥ- kena tatte duḥkhamiti | sa tān mitrajñātisālohitānevaṃ vadet- nairayikaṃ duḥkhamanubhūtam | sa tānākrośet paribhāṣet- ahaṃ ca nāma nairayikaṃ duḥkhamanubhavāmi | yūyaṃ ca me uttari paripṛcchatha kenaitattava duḥkhamiti | atha te mitrajñātisālohitāstaṃ puruṣamevaṃ vadeyuḥ- mā bhairmoḥ puruṣa | supto hi tvam | na tvamito gṛhāt kvacinnirgataḥ | tasya punarapi smṛti rutpadyate- supto 'hamabhūvam | vitathametanmayā parikalpitamiti | sa punarapi saumanasyaṃ pratilabhate ||
body.translated_text: And just as I, <s>Bhagavān</s>, see the hells, so too is the suffering of hell-beings. Just as, <s>Bhagavān</s>, a certain person, having fallen asleep and entered into a dream, perceives himself as having gone to hell. There, he perceives himself as having been thrown into a boiling, blazing iron cauldron many times the height of a man. There he would experience a harsh, bitter, terrible, painful feeling. There he would perceive a mental burning; he would be frightened, he would fall into alarm. There, upon awakening, he would cry out — 'Oh, the suffering! Oh, the suffering!' — he would weep, grieve, and lament. Then his friends, relatives, and kinsmen would ask: 'Why do you have this suffering?' He would say to those friends, relatives, and kinsmen: 'I have experienced the suffering of hell.' He would scold and rebuke them: 'I am experiencing the suffering of hell, and you ask me further — "Why do you have this suffering?"' Then those friends, relatives, and kinsmen would say to that person: 'Do not be afraid, do not be deluded, person! You were asleep. You have not gone anywhere from this house.' Then his memory would return again: 'I was asleep. This was falsely constructed by me.' And he would regain his joy.

body.text: tadyathā bhagavan sa puruṣo 'satsamāropeṇa suptaḥ svapnāntaragato narakagatamātmānaṃ saṃjānīyāt, evameva bhagavan sarvabālapṛthagjanā asadbhāgaparyavanaddhāḥ strīnimittaṃ kalpayanti | te strīnimittaṃ kalpayitvā tābhiḥ sārdhaṃ ramamāṇamātmānaṃ saṃjānanti | tasya bālapṛthajanasyaivaṃ bhavati- ahaṃ puruṣaḥ, iyaṃ strī, mamaiṣā strī | tasya tena cchandarāgaparyavasthitena cittena bhogaparyeṣṭiṃ cittaṃ krāmayanti | sa tatonidānaṃ kalahavigrahavivādaṃ saṃjanayati | tasya praduṣṭendriyasya vairaṃ saṃjāyate | sa tena saṃjñāviparyāsena kālagataḥ samāno bahūni kalpasahasrāṇi narakeṣu duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānamātmānaṃ saṃjānāti ||
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Bhagavān</s>, that person, through false superimposition, asleep and having entered into a dream, would perceive himself as having gone to hell — even so, <s>Bhagavān</s>, all foolish ordinary beings, enveloped by the portion of the unreal, construct the sign of 'woman.' Having constructed the sign of 'woman,' they perceive themselves as enjoying themselves with them. The thought arises in that foolish ordinary being: 'I am a man; this is a woman; this woman is mine.' With his mind obsessed by desire and passion, he directs his mind toward the pursuit of enjoyments. From that cause he generates quarrel, conflict, and dispute. With his faculties corrupted, enmity arises in him. Having died through that perversion of perception, he perceives himself experiencing painful feeling in the hells for many thousands of aeons.

body.text: tadyathā bhagavan tasya puruṣasya mitrajñātisālohitā evaṃ vadanti- mā bhaiḥ, mā bhaiḥ, bho puruṣa | supto hi tvam | na tvamito gṛhyat kutaścinnirgataḥ iti | evameva buddhā bhagavantaścaturviparyāsaviparyastānāṃ sattvānāmevaṃ dharmaṃ deśayanti- nātra strī na puruṣo na sattvo na jīvo na puruṣo na pudgalaḥ | vitathā ime sarvadharmāḥ | asanta ime sarvadharmāḥ | viṭhapitā ime sarvadharmāḥ | māyopamā ime sarvadharmāḥ | svapnopamā ime sarvadharmāḥ | nirmitopamā ime sarvadharmāḥ | udakacandropamā ime sarvadharmāḥ | iti vistaraḥ | te imāṃ tathāgatasya dharmadeśanāṃ śrutvā vigatarāgān sarvadharmān paśyanti | vigatamohān sarvadharmān paśyanti asvabhāvānanāvaraṇān | te ākāśasthitena cetasā kālaṃ kurvanti | te kālagatāḥ samānā nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvānti | evamahaṃ bhagavan narakān paśyāmi | iti ||
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the friends, relatives, and kinsmen of that person say: 'Do not be afraid, do not be afraid, good person! You were asleep. You have not gone anywhere from this house.' Even so, <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings who are perverted by the four perversions: 'There is no woman here, no man, no being, no soul, no person, no individual. All these <s>dharmas</s> are false. All these <s>dharmas</s> are unreal. All these <s>dharmas</s> are erected [by construction]. All these <s>dharmas</s> are like illusions. All these <s>dharmas</s> are like dreams. All these <s>dharmas</s> are like magical creations. All these <s>dharmas</s> are like the moon in water.' And so forth in detail. Having heard this <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, they see all <s>dharmas</s> as free from passion, free from delusion, without own-nature, without obstruction. With minds established in space, they die. Having died, they attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-element without remainder. Thus do I, <s>Bhagavān</s>, see the hells.

body.text: uktaṃ ca āryopāliparipṛcchāyām-
body.translated_text: And it is said in the Noble <s>Upāliparipṛcchā</s>:

children.text: bhaya darśita nairayikaṃ me sattvasahasra savejita naike |
children.translated_text: The suffering of hell has been shown to me, and thousands of beings have been terrified by the sight. /

children.text: na ca vidyati kaściha sattva yo cyutu gacchati ghoramapāyam ||
children.translated_text: Yet there is no being here who, having departed, goes to the terrible lower realm. //

children.text: na ca kāraku kāraṇa santi yehi kṛtā asitomaraśastrāḥ |
children.translated_text: There are no agents or causes by which swords, spears, and weapons are made. /

children.text: kalpavaśena tu paśyati tatra kāyi patanti apāyita śastrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Yet through the power of conceptual construction, one sees there — bodies falling, assailed by weapons. //
Beautiful, delightful, well-adorned flowers, golden palaces, and lovely things blaze forth. /

children.text: teṣvapi kāraku nāstiha kaści te 'pi ca sthāpita kalpavaśena ||
children.translated_text: Yet even for those there is no agent here — they too are established through the power of conceptual construction. //

children.text: kalpavaśena vikalpitu lokaḥ saṃjñagaheṇa vikalpitu bālaḥ |
children.translated_text: Through conceptual construction the world is discriminately constructed; through the grasping of perception, the fool discriminately constructs. /

children.text: so ca gaho agaho asabhūto māyamarīcisamā hi vikalpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: That grasping is a non-grasping, unreal — for conceptual constructions are like illusions and mirages. //

body.text: tadevamete 'svabhāvā bhāvāḥ svaviparyāsaviṭhapitā bālānāṃ saṃkleśahetavo bhavanti saṃsāre iti sthitam ||
body.translated_text: Thus it is established that these entities, which are without own-nature, erected by the perversions of fools, become causes of affliction in <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text: yathā ca mṛṣāsvabhāvānāṃ padārthānāṃ saṃkleśavyavadānahetutvaṃ tathā madhyamakāvatārādvistareṇāvaseyam ||
body.translated_text: And how entities of false nature serve as causes of both affliction and purification should be understood in detail from the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s>.

body.text: atrāha- yadi svataḥ parataḥ ubhayato 'hetutaśca nāsti bhāvānāmutpādaḥ, tatra kathamavidyā pratyayāḥ saṃskārā ityuktaṃ bhagavatā? ucyate | saṃvṛtireva na tattvam ||
body.translated_text: Here one objects: If there is no arising of entities from themselves, from others, from both, or from no cause, then how did the <s>Bhagavān</s> say 'from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) as condition arise <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations)'? The reply is: that is said from the perspective of <s>saṃvṛti</s> (conventional truth) alone, not of ultimate reality.

body.text: kiṃ saṃvṛtervyavasthānaṃ vaktavyam? idaṃpratyayatāmātreṇa saṃvṛteḥ siddhirabhyupagamyate | na tu pakṣacatuṣṭayābhyupagamena sasvabhāvavādaprasaṅgāt, tasya cāyuktatvāt | idaṃpratyayatāmātrābhyupagame hi sati hetuphalayoranyonyāpekṣatvānnāsti svābhāvikī siddhiriti nāsti sasvabhāvavādaḥ | ata evoktam-
body.translated_text: What establishment of the conventional (<s>saṃvṛti</s>) is to be stated? The establishment of the conventional is accepted through mere conditionality (<s>idaṃpratyayatā</s>) alone. It is not through the acceptance of the fourfold thesis, because that would entail the position of inherent existence (<s>sasvabhāvavāda</s>), and that is shown to be untenable. For when mere conditionality is accepted, since cause and effect are mutually dependent, there is no establishment through inherent nature — hence there is no doctrine of inherent existence. Therefore it is said:

children.translated_text: Self-caused, caused by another, caused by both, or causeless — /
thus suffering is conceived by logicians, but you have declared it to be dependently arisen. //

body.text: ihāpi vakṣyati-
body.translated_text: Here too he will say:

children.text: pratītya kārakaḥ karma taṃ pratītya ca kārakam |
children.translated_text: The agent acts in dependence on the action, and in dependence on it the agent /
acts. We see no other cause of their establishment. //

body.text: bhagavatāpyetāvanmātramevoktam-
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> too said only this much:

body.text: tatrāyaṃ dharmasaṃketo yadutāsmin satīdaṃ bhavati, asyotpādādidamutpadyate, yaduta avidyā pratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ, saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānamityādi ||
body.translated_text: 'Herein, this is the summary of the <s>Dharma</s>: namely, this existing, that comes to be; from the arising of this, that arises — that is, conditioned by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) there are formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>); conditioned by formations there is consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>)' and so forth.

body.text: atra kecitparicodayanti- anutpannā bhāvā iti kimayaṃ pramāṇajo niścaya utāpramāṇajaḥ? tatra yadi pramāṇaja iṣyate, tadedaṃ vaktavyam- kati pramāṇāni kiṃlakṣaṇāni kiṃviṣayāṇi, kiṃ svata utpannāni kiṃ parata ubhayato 'hetuto veti | athāpramāṇajaḥ, sa na yuktaḥ, pramāṇādhīnatvātprameyādhigamasya | anadhigato hyartho na vinā pramāṇairadhigantuṃ śakyata iti pramāṇābhāvādarthādhigamābhāve sati kuto 'yaṃ samyagniścaya iti na yuktametadaniṣpannā bhāvā iti | yato vāyaṃ niścayo bhavato 'nutpannā bhāvā iti bhaviṣyati, tata eva mamāpi sarvabhāvāḥ santīti | yathā cāyaṃ te niścayaḥ- anutpannāḥ sarvadharmā iti, tathaiva mamāpi sarvabhāvotpattirbhaviṣyati | atha te nāsti niścayo 'nutpannāḥ sarvabhāvā iti, tadā svayamaniścitasya parapratyāyanāsaṃbhavācchāstrārambhavaiyarthyameveti santyapratiṣiddhāḥ sarvabhāvā iti ||
body.translated_text: Herein, some raise an objection: 'Entities are unarisen' — is this conclusion born from a means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) or is it not born from a <s>pramāṇa</s>? If it is accepted as born from a <s>pramāṇa</s>, then one must state: how many are the means of valid cognition, what are their characteristics, what are their objects, and are they arisen from self, from another, from both, or from no cause? But if it is not born from a <s>pramāṇa</s>, that is not correct, because the ascertainment of knowable objects depends on means of valid cognition. For an unascertained object cannot be ascertained without means of valid cognition. Hence, in the absence of means of valid cognition, since there is no ascertainment of objects, how can there be a correct conclusion? Therefore it is not correct to say 'entities are unproduced.' Or, from whatever source your conclusion 'entities are unarisen' arises, from that very source my conclusion 'all entities exist' will also arise. And just as you have this conclusion — 'all dharmas are unarisen' — just so, my conclusion regarding the arising of all entities will also hold. But if you have no conclusion that 'all entities are unarisen,' then since one who is himself uncertain cannot convince others, the commencement of the treatise is futile — and therefore all entities remain unrefuted.

body.text: ucyate | yadi kaścinniścayo nāmāsmākaṃ syāt, sa pramāṇajo vā syādapramāṇajo vā | na tvasti | kiṃ kāraṇam? ihāniścayasaṃbhave sati syāttatpratipakṣastadapekṣo niścayaḥ | yadā tvaniścaya eva tāvadasmākaṃ nāsti, tadā kutastadviruddhāviruddho niścayaḥ syāt saṃbandhyantaranirapekṣatvāt, kharaviṣāṇasya hrasvadīrghatāvat | yadā caivaṃ niścayasyābhāvaḥ, tadā kasya prasiddhayarthaṃ pramāṇāni parikalpayiṣyāmaḥ? kuto vaiṣāṃ saṃkhyā lakṣaṇaṃ viṣayo vā bhaviṣyati- svataḥ parata ubhayato 'hetuto vā samutpattiriti sarvametanna vaktavyamasmābhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: We reply: If we had something called a 'conclusion,' it would be either born from a <s>pramāṇa</s> or not. But we have none. For what reason? Where non-certainty exists, there could be a conclusion as its counterpart, dependent on it. But when for us there is not even non-certainty to begin with, how could there be a conclusion either opposed or not opposed to it? — because of the independence from any relational counterpart, just as a donkey's horn has no shortness or length. And when there is thus an absence of any conclusion, for the establishment of what shall we construct means of valid cognition? How could there be their number, their characteristics, or their objects — whether arising from self, from another, from both, or from no cause? All this need not be stated by us.

body.text: yadyevaṃ niścayo nāsti sarvataḥ, kathaṃ punaridaṃ niścitarūpaṃ vākyamupalabhyate bhavatām- na svato nāpi parato na dvābhyāṃ nāpyahetuto bhāvā bhavantīti? ucyate | niścitamidaṃ vākyaṃ lokasya svaprasiddhayaivopapattyā, nāryāṇām | kiṃ khalu āryāṇāmupapattirnāsti? kenaitaduktamasti vā nāsti veti | paramārtho hyāryāṇāṃ tūṣṇīṃbhāvaḥ | tataḥ kutastatra prapañcasaṃbhavo yadupapattiranupapattirvā syāt?
body.translated_text: If there is no conclusion at all, how then is this statement of yours, which has the form of a definitive assertion, perceived: 'Not from self, not from another, not from both, not from no cause do entities arise'? We reply: This statement is definitive by the reasoning (<s>upapatti</s>) that is well-established for the world itself, not for the noble ones (<s>ārya</s>). What? Do the noble ones have no reasoning? Who has said whether they do or do not? For the ultimate nature (<s>paramārtha</s>) of the noble ones is silence. Hence, how could there be a proliferation of concepts (<s>prapañca</s>) there, whether in the form of reasoning or non-reasoning?

body.text: yadi hyāryā upapattiṃ na varṇayanti, kena khalvidānīṃ paramārthaṃ lokaṃ bodhayiṣyanti? na khalvāryā lokasaṃvyavahāreṇopapattiṃ varṇayanti, kiṃ tu lokata eva yā prasiddhopapattiḥ, tāṃ parāvabodhārthamabhyupetya tayaiva lokaṃ bodhayanti | yathaiva hi vidyamānāmapi śarīrāśucitāṃ viparyāsānugatā rāgiṇo nopalabhante, śubhākāraṃ cābhūtamadhyāropya parikliśyante, teṣāṃ vairāgyārthaṃ tathāgatanirmito
body.translated_text: If the noble ones do not set forth reasoning, then by what will they awaken the world to ultimate reality? In fact, the noble ones do not set forth reasoning by means of worldly conventions. Rather, whatever reasoning is well-established for the world itself, that they adopt for the purpose of instructing others, and by means of that very reasoning they awaken the world. Just as lustful persons, though the impurity of the body actually exists, do not perceive it due to being subject to perversion, and having superimposed an unreal attribute of beauty upon it, they are afflicted — to produce dispassion in them, an emanation created by the <s>Tathāgata</s>

body.text: devo vā śubhasaṃjñayā prāk pracchāditān kāyadoṣānupavarṇayet- santyasmin kāye keśā ityādinā | te ca tasyāḥ śubhasaṃjñāyā vimuktā vairāgyamāsādayeyuḥ | evamihāpyāryaiḥ sarvathāpyanupalabhyamānātmakaṃ bhāvānāmavidyātimiropahatamatinayanatayā viparītaṃ svabhāvamadhyāropya kvacicca kaṃcidviśeṣamatitarāṃ parikliśyanti pṛthagjanāḥ | tānidānīmāryāḥ tatprasiddhayaivopapattyā paribodhayanti | yathā vidyamānasya ghaṭasya na mṛdādibhya utpāda ityabhyupetam, evamutpādātpūrvaṃ vidyamānasya vidyamānatvānnāstyutpāda ityavasīyatām | yathā ca parabhūtebhyo jvālāṅgārādibhyo 'ṅkurasyotpattirnāsti iti abhyupetam, evaṃ vivakṣitebhyo 'pi bījādibhyo nāstītyavasīyatām ||
body.translated_text: , or a deity, might describe the previously concealed defects of the body under the guise of the perception of beauty, saying: 'There are hairs in this body' and so forth. And they, freed from that perception of beauty, would attain dispassion. Even so here, ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), who though the entities are in every way beyond apprehension, having superimposed a distorted inherent nature due to the impairment of their mental vision by the darkness of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), and in some cases superimposing some further distinction, are exceedingly afflicted. Now the noble ones awaken them by means of the reasoning that is well-established for those very beings. Just as it is accepted that an existing pot does not arise from clay and the rest, so too let it be concluded that what exists prior to arising, being already existent, has no arising. And just as it is accepted that a sprout does not arise from things that are altogether different, such as flames and embers, so too let it be concluded that it does not arise from even the intended causes such as seeds and the rest.

body.text: athāpi syāt- anubhava eṣo 'smākamiti, etadapyuktam | yasmādanubhava eṣa mṛṣā, anubhavatvāt, taimirikadvicandrādyanubhavavaditi | tataścānubhavasyāpi sādhyasamatvāttena pratyavasthānaṃ na yuktamiti | tasmādanutpannā bhāvā ityevaṃ tāvadviparītasvarūpādhyāropapratipakṣeṇa prathamaprakaraṇārambhaḥ | idānīṃ kvacidyaḥ kaścidviśeṣo 'dhyāropitaḥ, tadviśeṣāpākaraṇārthaṃ śeṣaprakaraṇārambhaḥ, gantṛgantavyagamanādiko 'pi niravaśeṣo viśeṣo nāsti pratītyasamutpādasyeti pratipādanārtham ||
body.translated_text: If it be said: 'But this is our direct experience!' — this too has been addressed. Because this experience is false, being an experience, like the experience of the two moons by one with an eye-disease (<s>taimirika</s>) and the like. And therefore, since experience itself is equally to be proven (<s>sādhyasama</s>), it is not correct to respond with it. Therefore, 'entities are unarisen' — thus, first, the commencement of the first chapter is as a counteragent to the superimposition of a distorted nature. Now, the commencement of the remaining chapters is for the purpose of removing whatever particular distinction has been superimposed somewhere — to demonstrate that there is no distinction whatsoever, such as goer, that which is gone to, the act of going, and so forth, in <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>.

body.text: atha syāt- eṣa eva pramāṇapremeyavyavahāro laukiko 'smābhiḥ śāstreṇānuvarṇita iti, tadanuvarṇanasya tarhi phalaṃ vācyam | kutārkikaiḥ sa nāśito viparītalakṣaṇābhidhānena, tasyāsmābhiḥ samyaglakṣaṇamuktamiti cet, etadapyayuktam | yadi hi kutārkikairviparītalakṣaṇapraṇayanātkṛtaṃ lakṣyavaiparītyaṃ lokasya syāt, tadarthaṃ prayatnasāphalyaṃ syāt | na caitadevam | iti vyartha evārya prayatna iti ||
body.translated_text: If it be said: 'This very worldly convention of means of valid cognition and knowable objects has been described by us in the treatise' — then the fruit of that description must be stated. 'It has been destroyed by bad logicians through their statement of distorted characteristics; we have stated the correct characteristics' — if this be said, this too is not correct. For if the defective characterization by bad logicians had actually caused a reversal in the characterized object for the world, then the effort would be fruitful. But this is not the case. Therefore, O noble one, the effort is futile.

body.text: api ca | yadi pramāṇādhīnaḥ prameyādhigamaḥ, tāni pramāṇāni kena paricchidyanta ityādinā vigrahavyāvartanyāṃ vihito doṣaḥ | tadaparihārāt samyaglakṣaṇadyotakatvamapi nāsti ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, if the ascertainment of knowable objects depends on means of valid cognition, by what are those means of valid cognition themselves ascertained? — this and other defects have been set forth in the <s>Vigrahavyāvartanī</s>. Since those defects remain unresolved, there is no capacity to illuminate correct characteristics either.

body.text: kiṃ ca | yadi svasāmānyalakṣaṇadvayānurodhena pramāṇadvayamuktaṃ yasya tallakṣaṇadvayam, kiṃ tallakṣyamasti atha nāsti? yadyasti, tadā tadaparaṃ prameyamastīti kathaṃ pramāṇadvayam? atha nāsti lakṣyam, tadā lakṣaṇamapi nirāśrayaṃ nāstīti kathaṃ pramāṇadvayam? vakṣyati hi-
body.translated_text: Furthermore, if two means of valid cognition are stated in accordance with the two types of characteristics — particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) and universal (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>) — does the object possessing those two characteristics exist, or does it not? If it exists, then there is another knowable object — so how can there be only two means of valid cognition? If the characterized object does not exist, then the characteristic too, being without a basis, does not exist — so how can there be two means of valid cognition? For he will say:

children.translated_text: When the characteristic does not operate, the characterized object is not established. /
And when the characterized object is not established, the characteristic too is impossible. //

body.text: atha syāt- na lakṣyate 'neneti lakṣaṇam, kiṃ tarhi 'kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam'; iti karmaṇi lyuṭaṃ kṛtvā lakṣyate taditi lakṣaṇam | evamapi tenaitasya lakṣyamāṇatvāsaṃbhavādyenaitallakṣyate, tasya karaṇasya karmaṇo 'rthāntaratvāt sa eva doṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: If it be said: 'The characteristic is not in the sense of "that by which it is characterized" (agent-derivation), but rather, applying the rule "<s>kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam</s>," making <s>lyuṭ</s> an object-derivation: "that which is characterized" is the characteristic' — even so, since there is no possibility of its being characterized by that, and since the instrument (that by which it is characterized) and the object (that which is characterized) are different things, the same defect applies.

body.text: atha syāt- jñānasya karaṇatvāttasya ca svalakṣaṇāntarbhāvādayamadoṣa iti, ucyate | iha bhāvānāmanyāsādhāraṇamātmīyaṃ yatsvarūpaṃ tatsvalakṣaṇam, tadyathā pṛthivyāḥ kāṭhinyaṃ vedanāyā viṣayānubhavo vijñānasya viṣayaprativijñaptiḥ | tena hi tallakṣyata iti kṛtvā prasiddhānugatāṃ ca
body.translated_text: If it be said: 'Since knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) has the nature of an instrument, and since it falls within the scope of <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, there is no defect' — we reply: Here, the unique, proper form of entities that is not shared with anything else is their <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular characteristic) — for example, the hardness of earth, the experience of an object in the case of feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), and the cognition of an object in the case of consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>). In accepting the object-derivation on the grounds that 'it is characterized by that,' one rejects the well-established and commonly accepted derivation

body.text: vyutpattimavadhūya karmasādhanamabhyupagacchati | vijñānasya ca karaṇabhāvaṃ pratipadyamānenetyuktaṃ bhavati svalakṣaṇasyaiva karmatā svalakṣaṇāntarasya karaṇabhāvaśceti | tatra yadi vijñānasvalakṣaṇaṃ karaṇam, tasya vyatiriktena karmaṇā bhavitavyamiti sa eva doṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: . And in accepting the instrument-nature of consciousness, this amounts to saying that the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> itself has the nature of the object, and that another <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> has the nature of the instrument. Therein, if the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> of consciousness is the instrument, it must have an object distinct from itself — hence the same defect arises.

body.text: atha syāt- yatpṛthivyādigataṃ kāṭhinyādikaṃ vijñānagamyaṃ tattasya karmāstyeva, tacca svalakṣaṇāvyatiriktamiti | evaṃ tarhi vijñānasvalakṣaṇasya karmatvābhāvātprameyatvaṃ na syāt, karmarūpasyaiva svalakṣaṇasya prameyatvāt | tataśca dvividhaṃ prameyaṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ ca ityetadviśeṣya vaktavyam- kiṃcitsvalakṣaṇaṃ prameyaṃ yallakṣyata ityevaṃ vyapadiśyate, kiṃcidaprameyaṃ yallakṣyate 'neneti vyapadiśyata iti | atha tadapi karmasādhanaṃ tadā tasyānyena karaṇena bhavitavyam | jñānāntarasya karaṇabhāvaparikalpanāyāmanavasthādoṣaścāpadyate ||
body.translated_text: If it be said: 'The hardness and so forth belonging to earth and the rest, which are cognized by consciousness, are indeed its object, and that is not distinct from <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>' — then, since the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> of consciousness itself would not have the status of an object, it would not be a knowable (<s>prameya</s>), because only <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> in its object-form is knowable. Therefore, regarding the twofold knowable — <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> and <s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s> — one must make the further distinction: some <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> is knowable, being designated as 'that which is characterized,' while some is unknowable, being designated as 'that by which it is characterized.' And if that too is in the object-derivation, then it must have another instrument. In positing the instrument-nature of yet another cognition, the defect of infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>) arises.

body.text: atha manyase- svasaṃvittirasti, tatastayā svasaṃvityā grahaṇātkarmatāyā satyāmastyeva prameyāntarbhāva iti, ucyate | vistareṇa madhyamakāvatāre svasaṃvittiniṣedhāt svalakṣaṇaṃ svalakṣaṇāntareṇa lakṣyate, tadapi svasaṃvittyā iti na yujyate | api ca | tadapi nāma jñānaṃ svalakṣaṇavyatirekeṇāsiddherasaṃbhavāllakṣyābhāve nirāśrayalakṣaṇapravṛttyasaṃbhavāt sarvathā nāstīti kutaḥ svasaṃvittiḥ? tathā coktamāryaratnacūḍaparipṛcchāyām-
body.translated_text: If you think: 'Self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvitti</s>) exists, and through that self-awareness, since there is apprehension, the status of an object is real, and hence inclusion among knowables exists' — we reply: Since self-awareness is extensively refuted in the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s>, it is not tenable that <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> is characterized by another <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, and that too by self-awareness. Moreover, that very cognition, being unestablished apart from <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> — since it is impossible, and since when the characterized object is absent the operation of a baseless characteristic is impossible — does not exist in any way whatsoever. Hence, how can there be self-awareness? Thus it is said in the noble <s>Ratnacūḍaparipṛcchā</s>:

body.text: sa cittamasamanupaśyan cittadhārāṃ paryeṣate kutaścittasyotpattiriti | tasyaivaṃ bhavati- ālambane sati cittamutpadyate | tatkimanyadālambanamanyaccittam, atha yadevālambanaṃ tadeva cittam? yadi tāvadanyadālambanamanyaccittam, tadā dvicittatā bhaviṣyati | atha yadevālambanaṃ tadeva cittam, tatkathaṃ cittena cittaṃ samanupaśyati? na ca cittaṃ cittaṃ samanupaśyati | tadyathāpi nāma tayaivāsidhārayā saivāsidhārā na śakyate chettum, na tenaivāṅgulyagreṇa tadevāṅgulyagraṃ śakyate spraṣṭum, evameva na tenaiva cittena tadeva cittaṃ śakyaṃ draṣṭum | tasyaivaṃ yoniśaḥ prayuktasya yā cittasyānavasthānatā anucchedāśāśvatatā na kūṭasthatā nāhetukī na pratyayaviruddhā na tato nānyato na saiva nānyā | tāṃ cittadhārāṃ cittalatāṃ cittadharmatāṃ cittānavasthitatāṃ cittāpracāratāṃ cittādṛśyatāṃ cittasvalakṣaṇatāṃ tathā jānāti tathā paśyati yathā tathatāṃ na ca nirodhayati | tāṃ ca cittavivekatāṃ tathā prajānāti tathā paśyati | iyaṃ kulaputra [bodhisattvasya] citte cittānupaśyanā smṛtyupasthānamiti ||
body.translated_text: 'He, not perceiving the mind, searches for the stream of mind — whence does the mind arise? He thinks thus: "When there is an object, mind arises. Is the object one thing and the mind another, or is the object itself the mind?" If the object is one thing and the mind another, then there would be two minds. But if the object itself is the mind, then how does mind perceive mind? Mind does not perceive mind. Just as a sword-blade cannot cut that very sword-blade, just as a fingertip cannot touch that very fingertip — even so, that very mind cannot see that very mind. For one thus properly engaged, the non-abiding of mind, its non-annihilation and non-permanence, its non-fixity, its non-causelessness, its non-contradiction with conditions, its being neither the same nor different from them — that stream of mind, that creeper of mind, that nature of mind (<s>cittadharmatā</s>), that non-abiding of mind, that non-operation of mind, that invisibility of mind, that particular characteristic of mind (<s>cittasvalakṣaṇatā</s>) — he knows and sees it as it truly is, as <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), and does not extinguish it. And he thus comprehends and sees that seclusion of mind. This, son of good family, is the mindfulness-establishment (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the contemplation of mind in mind.'

body.text: tadevaṃ nāsti svasaṃvittiḥ | tadabhāvāt kiṃ kena lakṣyate?
body.translated_text: Thus, self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvitti</s>) does not exist. In its absence, what is characterized by what?

body.text: kiṃ ca | bhedena vā tallakṣaṇaṃ lakṣyātsyādabhedena vā? tatra yadi tāvad bhedena, tadā lakṣyād bhinnatvādalakṣaṇavallakṣaṇamapi na lakṣaṇam | lakṣaṇācca bhinnatvādalakṣyavallakṣyamapi na lakṣyam | tathā lakṣyādbhinnatvāllakṣaṇasya lakṣaṇanirapekṣaṃ lakṣyaṃ syāt | tataśca na tallakṣyaṃ lakṣaṇanirapekṣatvāt khapuṣpavat | athābhinne lakṣyalakṣaṇe, tadā lakṣaṇādavyatiriktattvāllakṣaṇasvātmavadvihīyate
body.translated_text: Moreover, would that defining characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) be related to the thing defined (<s>lakṣya</s>) through difference or through non-difference? If first through difference, then since it is different from the thing defined, the characteristic, like what has no characteristic, would also not be a characteristic. And since it is different from the characteristic, the thing defined, like what has no thing defined, would also not be a thing defined. Likewise, since the characteristic is different from the thing defined, the thing defined would be independent of the characteristic. And in that case, it would not be a thing defined, because of being independent of a characteristic — like a sky-flower. If, on the other hand, the thing defined and the characteristic are non-different, then since it is not distinct from the characteristic, just as the characteristic's own nature [is not characterized], the thing-defined-ness of the thing defined is lost.

body.text: lakṣyasya lakṣyatā | lakṣyāccāvyatiriktatvāllakṣyasvātmavallakṣaṇamapi na lakṣaṇasvabhāvam | yathā coktam-
body.translated_text: And since it is not distinct from the thing defined, just as the thing defined's own nature [is not a characteristic], the characteristic too would not have the nature of a characteristic. As it has been said —

children.translated_text: If the characteristic were other than the thing defined, then that thing defined would be without a characteristic. /
The non-existence of both in the case of non-otherness has been clearly stated by you. //

body.text: na ca vinā tattvānyatvena lakṣyalakṣaṇasiddhau anyā gatirasti | tathā ca vakṣyati-
body.translated_text: Nor is there any other way to establish the thing defined and the characteristic without [recourse to] identity and difference. And thus it will be said —

children.translated_text: The establishment of two things either through identity or through difference /

children.text: na vidyate, tayoḥ siddhiḥ kathaṃ nu khalu vidyate || iti ||
children.translated_text: is not found — how then could the establishment of those two possibly be found? //

body.text: athavocyate- avācyatayā siddhirbhaviṣyatīti cet, naitadevam | avācyatā hi nāma parasparavibhāgaparijñānābhāve sati bhavati | yatra ca vibhāgaparijñānaṃ nāsti, tatra idaṃ lakṣaṇam, idaṃ lakṣyam, iti viśeṣataḥ paricchedāsaṃbhave sati dvayorapyabhāva eveti | tasmādavācyatayāpi nāsti siddhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: If it be said that their establishment will come about through inexpressibility — that is not so. For inexpressibility arises when there is no cognition of the mutual distinction [between two things]. And where there is no cognition of distinction, the impossibility of specific determination — 'this is the characteristic,' 'this is the thing defined' — means that both simply do not exist. Therefore, even through inexpressibility, there is no establishment.

body.text: api ca | yadi jñānaṃ karaṇaṃ viṣayasya paricchede, kaḥ kartā? na ca kartāramantareṇāsti karaṇādīnāṃ saṃbhavaḥ chidikriyāyāmiva | atha cittasya tatra kartṛtvaṃ parikalpyate, tadapi na yuktam, yasmādarthamātradarśanaṃ cittasya vyāpāraḥ, arthaviśeṣadarśanaṃ caitasānām,
body.translated_text: Furthermore, if cognition is the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) in the determination of an object, who is the agent? For without an agent, there is no possibility of instruments and so forth, just as in the action of cutting. If the agency of <s>citta</s> (mind) is imagined here, that too is improper, because the activity of <s>citta</s> is merely the seeing of the object in general, while the seeing of the specific features of the object belongs to the mental factors (<s>caitasa</s>) —

body.text: tatrārthadṛṣṭirvijñānaṃ tadviśeṣe tu caitasāḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the seeing of the object [in general] is <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness); in its specific features, [the seeing belongs to] the mental factors. /

body.text: ityabhyupagamāt | ekasyāṃ hi pradhānakriyāyāṃ sādhyāyāṃ yathāsvaṃ guṇakriyānirvṛttidvāreṇāṅgībhāvopagamāt | karaṇādīnāṃ karaṇāditvam | na ceha jñānavijñānayorekā pradhānakriyā, kiṃ tarhi, arthamātraparicchittirvijñānasya pradhānakriyā, jñānasya tu arthaviśeṣapariccheda iti nāsti jñānasya karaṇatvaṃ nāpi cittasya kartṛtvam | tataśca sa eva doṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: — this being the accepted position. For, since a single principal action is to be accomplished, through the accomplishment of their respective subsidiary actions, the instruments and so forth assume the status of being instruments and so forth. But here, the principal action of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is not one and the same; rather, the principal action of <s>vijñāna</s> is the determination of the mere object, while that of <s>jñāna</s> is the determination of the specific features of the object. Therefore, <s>jñāna</s> does not have the nature of an instrument, nor does <s>citta</s> have agency. And thus the same fault [applies].

body.text: atha syāt- anātmānaḥ sarvadharmā ityāgamāt kartuḥ sarvathābhāvāt kartāramantareṇāpi vidyata eva kriyādivyavahāra iti, etadapi nāsti | āgamasya samyagarthānavadhāraṇāt | etadevoktaṃ madhyamakāvatāre ||
body.translated_text: If one were to say that, from the scriptural statement 'All <s>dharmas</s> are without self,' because of the complete absence of an agent in every respect, the operation of action and so forth is possible even without an agent — this too is not so, because of the failure to ascertain correctly the meaning of scripture. This very point has been stated in the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s>.

body.text: athāpi syāt- yathā śilāputrakasya śarīram, rāhoḥ śiraḥ, iti śarīraśirovyatiriktaviśeṣaṇāsaṃbhave 'pi viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvo 'sti, evaṃ pṛthivyāḥ svalakṣaṇamiti svalakṣaṇavyatiriktapṛthivyasaṃbhave 'pi bhaviṣyatīti, naitadevam | atulyatvāt | śarīraśiraḥśabdayohi buddhayādipāṇyādivatsahabhāvipadārthāntarasāpekṣatāpravṛttau śarīraśiraḥ śabdamātrālambano buddhayupajananaḥ sahacāripadārthāntarasākāṅkṣa eva vartate, kasya śarīram, kasya śira iti | itaro 'pi viśeṣaṇāntaraḥ saṃbandhanirācikīrṣayā | śilāputrakarāhuviśeṣaṇadhvaninā laukikasaṃketānuvidhāyinā pratikartuḥ kāṅkṣāmapahantīti yuktam | iha tu kāṭhinyādivyatiriktapṛthivyādyasaṃbhave sati na yukto viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: If one were to say: 'Just as in the [expressions] "<s>Śilāputraka</s>'s body" and "<s>Rāhu</s>'s head," even though a qualifier distinct from the body and head is impossible, there exists the relation of qualifier and qualified — so too, in "the own-characteristic of earth," even though an earth distinct from its own-characteristic is impossible, [the relation] will exist' — that is not so, because of dissimilarity. For the words 'body' and 'head' function in dependence on another co-existing entity, just as <s>Buddhaya</s>'s hand and so forth. The cognition generated by the words 'body' and 'head' alone is one that expects a co-existing entity — [namely] 'whose body?' 'whose head?' The other qualifier too, with the intention of determining the relation, dispels the expectation of the listener by means of the qualifiers <s>Śilāputraka</s> and <s>Rāhu</s>, which conform to common worldly convention — and this is proper. But here, when there is no earth and so forth distinct from hardness and so forth, the relation of qualifier and qualified is improper.

body.text: tīrthikairvyatiriktalakṣyābhyupagamāttadanurodhena viśeṣaṇābhidhānamaduṣṭamiti cet, naitadevam | na hi tīrthikaparikalpitā yuktividhurāḥ padārthāḥ svasamaye 'bhyupagantuṃ nyāyyāḥ, pramāṇāntarāderapyabhyugamaprasaṅgāt | api ca | pudgalādiprajñaptivat saśarīropādānasya śilāputrakasyopādāturlaukikavyavahārāṅgabhūtasya viśeṣaṇasyāvicāraprasiddhasya sadbhāvāt, śiraupādānasya ca rāhorupādātuḥ sadbhāvādayuktametannidarśanam | śarīraśirovyatiriktasyārthāntarasyāsiddhestanmātrasyopalambhāt siddhameva nidarśanamiti cet, naitadevam | laukike vyavahāre itthaṃ vicārāpravṛtteravicārataśca laukikapadārthānāmastitvāt | yathaiva hi rūpādivyatirekeṇa vicāryamāṇa ātmā na saṃbhavati, api ca lokasaṃvṛtyā skandhānupādāya asyāstitvam, evaṃ rāhuśilāputrakayorapīti nāsti nidarśanasiddhiḥ ||
body.translated_text: If it be said that since the non-Buddhists accept a thing defined that is distinct [from its characteristics], the statement of the qualifier in conformity with them is not faulty — that is not so. For entities imagined by the non-Buddhists, devoid of reasoning, ought not to be accepted in one's own system, since there would be the consequence of accepting other [positions] as well by other means of knowledge. Moreover, just as in the case of the designation of <s>pudgala</s> (person) and so forth, since the qualifier — which is the basis of worldly convention and which is well-known without examination — exists for <s>Śilāputraka</s> who possesses the body as his basis of designation, and since <s>Rāhu</s> who possesses the head as his basis of designation exists, this illustration is improper. If it be said that the illustration is valid precisely because an entity distinct from the body and head is unestablished and only that much is apprehended — that is not so. Because in worldly convention, examination does not operate thus, and because worldly entities exist without examination. For just as the self (<s>ātman</s>), when examined apart from form and so forth, is impossible — and yet by worldly convention its existence is [accepted] in dependence upon the aggregates — even so with <s>Rāhu</s> and <s>Śilāputraka</s>. Thus the illustration does not hold.

body.text: evaṃ pṛthivyādīnāṃ yadyapi kāṭhinyādivyatiriktaṃ vicāryamāṇaṃ lakṣyaṃ nāsti, lakṣyavyatirekeṇa ca lakṣaṇaṃ nirāśrayam, tathāpi saṃvṛtireveti parasparāpekṣayā tayoḥ siddhayā siddhiṃ vyavasthāpayāṃbabhūvurācāryāḥ | avaśyaṃ caitadevamabhyupeyam | anyathā hi saṃvṛtirupapattyā na viyujyeta, tadeva tattvameva syānna saṃvṛtiḥ | na ca upapattyā vicāryamāṇānāṃ śilāputrakādīmevāsaṃbhavaḥ, kiṃ tarhi vakṣyamāṇayā yuktyā rūpavedanādīnāmapi nāsti saṃbhava iti teṣāmapi saṃvṛtyā śilāputrakādivannāstitvamāstheyaṃ syāt | na caitadevamityasadetat ||
body.translated_text: Thus, although the thing defined of earth and so forth, when examined apart from hardness and so forth, does not exist, and although the characteristic, apart from the thing defined, is without support — nevertheless, this is merely conventional reality (<s>saṃvṛti</s>). The <s>Ācāryas</s> have established their establishment through their mutual dependence. And this must necessarily be accepted. For otherwise, conventional reality would not be separated from reasoning — it would be ultimate truth itself, not conventional. Nor is it only the case that <s>Śilāputraka</s> and so forth are impossible when examined by reasoning; rather, by the reasoning that will be stated, even form, feeling, and so forth are impossible. Therefore, their existence too should be maintained as merely conventional, like <s>Śilāputraka</s> and so forth. And this is not otherwise — so this [argument] is groundless.

body.text: atha syāt- kimanayā sūkṣmekṣikayā? naiva hi vayaṃ sarvapramāṇaprameyavyavahāraṃ satyamityācakṣmahe, kiṃ tu lokaprasiddhireṣā amunā nyāyena vyavasthāpyata iti | ucyate | vayamapyevaṃ brūmaḥ- kimanayā sūkṣmekṣikayā laukikavyavahāre 'vatārika(ta?)yā? tiṣṭhatu tāvadeṣā viparyāsamātrāsāditātmabhāvasattākā saṃvṛtiḥ mumukṣūṇāṃ mokṣāvāhakakuśalamūlopacayahetuḥ, yāvanna tattvādhigama iti | bhavāṃstu etāṃ saṃvṛtiparamārthasatyavibhāgadurvidagdhabuddhitayā kvacidupapattimavatārya anyāyato nāśayati | so 'haṃ saṃvṛtisatyavyavasthāvaicakṣaṇyāllaukika eva pakṣe sthitvā saṃvṛtyekadeśanirākaraṇopakṣiptopapattyantaramupapattyantareṇa vinivartayan lokavṛddha iva lokacārātparibhraśyamānaṃ bhavantameva nivartayāmi na tu saṃvṛtim | tasmād yadi laukiko vyavahāraḥ, tadā avaśyaṃ lakṣaṇavallakṣyeṇāpi bhavitavyam | tataśca sa eva doṣaḥ | atha paramārthaḥ, tadā lakṣyābhāvāllakṣaṇadvayamapi nāstīti kutaḥ pramāṇadvayam?
body.translated_text: If one were to say: 'What is the point of this hair-splitting? We do not at all declare the entire operation of all means of knowledge and objects of knowledge to be true. Rather, this common worldly [convention] is being established by this method' — we reply: We too say the same thing — what is the point of this hair-splitting that introduces [examination] into worldly convention? Let this conventional reality — whose existence-nature has been acquired through mere perversion alone — stand for now as the cause for the accumulation of wholesome roots that lead to liberation for those who seek liberation, so long as the ultimate truth has not been realized. But you, through your intelligence ill-versed in the distinction between conventional truth and ultimate truth, having introduced reasoning in one place, improperly destroy [conventional truth] from another. I, standing on the side of worldly convention alone — through my skill in establishing conventional truth — by means of another reasoning counteract the reasoning introduced for the partial destruction of the conventional, and like an elder of the world, I turn back you yourself, who are straying from the way of the world — I do not turn back the conventional. Therefore, if this is worldly convention, then necessarily there must be a thing defined just as there is a characteristic. And thus the same fault [applies]. But if it is ultimate reality, then since the thing defined does not exist, neither do the two characteristics exist — so whence the two means of knowledge?

body.text: atha śabdānāmevaṃ kriyākārakasaṃbandhapūrvikā vyutpattirnāṅgīkriyate, tadidamatikaṣṭam | taireva kriyākārakasaṃbandhapravṛttaiḥ śabdairbhavān vyavaharati, śabdārthaṃ kriyākaraṇādikaṃ ca necchatīti aho vata icchāmātrapratibaddhapravṛttito (vṛttiḥ?) bhavataḥ |
body.translated_text: If the etymological derivation of words in terms of the relation of action and agent is not accepted — this is extremely distressing. For you conduct your discourse with those very words that function through the relation of action and agent, yet you do not accept that the meaning of words is action, instrument, and so forth. Alas, what a [theory] whose operation is bound merely to wish!

body.text: yadā caivaṃ prameyadvayamavyavasthitaṃ tadā svasāmānyalakṣaṇāviṣayatvena āgamādīnāṃ pramāṇāntaratvam | kiṃ ca ghaṭaḥ pratyakṣa ityevamādikasya laukikavyavahārasyāsaṃgrahādanāryavyavahārābhyupagamācca avyāpitā lakṣaṇasyeti na yuktametat ||
body.translated_text: And when the two objects of knowledge are thus not established, the other means of knowledge such as scripture and so forth would be [merely] means that do not have their own general and specific characteristics as their objects. Moreover, since the worldly convention of such [statements] as 'a pot is perceptible' and so forth is not included [in the definition], and since non-noble conventions are [thereby] accepted, the definition is not pervading (<s>avyāpti</s>) — therefore this is improper.

body.text: atha syāt- ghaṭopādānanīlādayaḥ pratyakṣāḥ pratyakṣapramāṇaparicchedyatvāt | tataśca yathaiva kāraṇe kāryopacāraṃ kṛtvā buddhānāṃ sukha utpāda iti vyapadiśyate, evaṃ pratyakṣanīlādinimittako 'pi ghaṭaḥ kārye kāraṇopacāraṃ kṛtvā pratyakṣa iti vyapadiśyate | naivaṃviṣaye upacāro yuktaḥ | utpādo hi loke sukhavyatirekeṇopalabdhaḥ, sa ca saṃskṛtalakṣaṇasvabhāvatvādanekaduṣkaraśatahetutvādasukha eva, sa sukha iti vyapadiśyamānaḥ asaṃbaddha evetyevaṃviṣaye yukta upacāraḥ | ghaṭaḥ pratyakṣa ityatra tu- na hi ghaṭo nāma kaścidyo 'pratyakṣaḥ pṛthagupalabdho yasyopacārātpratyakṣatvaṃ syāt | nīlādivyatiriktasya ghaṭasyābhāvādaupacārikaṃ pratyakṣatvamiti cet, evamapi sutarāmupacāro na yuktaḥ, upacaryamāṇasyāśrayasyābhāvāt | na hi kharaviṣāṇe taikṣṇyamupacaryate | api ca | lokavyavahārāṅgabhūto ghaṭo yadi nīlādivyatirikto nāstīti kṛtvā tasyaupacārikaṃ pratyakṣatvaṃ parikalpyate, nanvevaṃ sati pṛthivyādivyatirekeṇa nīlādikamapi nāstīti nīlāderasyaupacārikaṃ pratyakṣatvaṃ kalpyatām | yathoktam-
body.translated_text: If one were to say: 'The blue and other [components] that constitute the pot are perceptible, because of being determinable by the means of knowledge of perception. And just as, by the figurative transfer (<s>upacāra</s>) of effect to cause, the arising of <s>Buddhas</s> is designated as "happiness," so too the pot, though [actually] caused by perceptible blue and so forth, is designated as "perceptible" by the figurative transfer of cause to effect' — figurative usage in such a case is not proper. For arising is apprehended in the world as distinct from happiness, and since it has the nature of a characteristic of the conditioned, and because it is the cause of hundreds of difficult deeds, it is indeed unhappy. When it is designated as 'happiness,' this is indeed incoherent — and figurative usage in such a case is proper. But in the case of 'the pot is perceptible,' there is no pot whatsoever that is imperceptible and is apprehended separately, whose perceptibility would be by figurative transfer. If it be said: 'Since a pot distinct from blue and so forth does not exist, its perceptibility is figurative' — even so, figurative usage is all the more improper, because of the non-existence of the substrate of the figurative application. For sharpness is not figuratively attributed to a hare's horn. Moreover, if the pot — which is the basis of worldly convention — is said not to exist apart from blue and so forth, and therefore its perceptibility is imagined to be figurative, then surely in that case, since blue and so forth too do not exist apart from earth and so forth, let the perceptibility of blue and so forth be imagined as figurative. As it is said —

body.text:
rūpādivyatirekeṇa yathā kumbho na vidyate |
vāyvādivyatirekeṇa tathā rūpaṃ na vidyate || iti |
body.translated_text:
Just as a pot is not found apart from form and so forth, /
so too form is not found apart from wind and so forth. //

body.text: tasmādevamādikasya lokavyavahārasya lakṣaṇenāsaṃgrahādavyāpitaiva lakṣaṇasyeti | tattvavidapekṣayā hi-
body.translated_text: Therefore, since worldly convention of this and other kinds is not included by the definition, the definition is indeed not pervading. From the perspective of one who knows the ultimate truth —

body.text: pratyakṣatvaṃ ghaṭādīnāṃ nīlādīnāṃ ca neṣyate |
body.translated_text: The perceptibility of pots and so forth, and of blue and so forth, is not accepted. /

body.text: lokasaṃvṛtyā tvabhyupagantavyameva pratyakṣatvaṃ ghaṭādīnām | yathoktaṃ śatake-
body.translated_text: But by worldly convention, the perceptibility of pots and so forth must indeed be accepted. As it is said in the <s>Śataka</s> (the Hundred [Verses]) —

children.text: sarva eva ghaṭo 'dṛṣṭo rūpe dṛṣṭe hi jāyate |
children.translated_text: A pot is entirely unseen; for when form is seen, there arises /
the [perception of a pot]. Who that knows reality would say 'the pot is perceptible'? //

body.text:
etenaiva vicāreṇa sugandhi madhuraṃ mṛdu |
pratiṣedhayitavyāni sarvāṇyuttamabuddhinā || iti |
body.translated_text:
By this very examination, fragrant, sweet, soft — /
all these should be negated by one of supreme intelligence. //

body.text: api ca | aparokṣārthavācitvātpratyakṣaśabdasya sākṣādabhimukho 'rthaḥ pratyakṣaḥ, pratigatamakṣamasminniti kṛtvā ghaṭanīlādīnāmaparokṣāṇāṃ pratyakṣatvaṃ siddhaṃ bhavati | tatparicchedakasya jñānasya tṛṇatuṣāgnivat pratyakṣakāraṇatvāt pratyakṣatvaṃ vyapadiśyate | yastu akṣamakṣaṃ prati vartata iti pratyakṣaśabdaṃ vyutpādayati, tasya jñānasyendriyāviṣayatvād viṣayaviṣayatvācca na yuktā vyutpattiḥ | prativiṣayaṃ tu syāt pratyarthamiti vā ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, since the word <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) means 'that whose meaning is not hidden' (<s>aparokṣārthavācitvāt</s>), the meaning [of the word] is: what is directly present, face to face, is <s>pratyakṣa</s> — taking 'pratyakṣa' as 'that in which the sense-faculty has approached' — the perceptibility of pots, blue, and so forth, which are not hidden, is established. The cognition that determines them is designated as <s>pratyakṣa</s> because of being the cause of perception, like a fire of grass and chaff. But one who derives the word <s>pratyakṣa</s> as 'what operates in relation to each sense-faculty' — for such a one, the derivation is improper, because cognition is not the object of the sense-faculties, and [yet] it has the object [of the sense-faculties] as its object. Rather, it should be <s>prativiṣaya</s> ('in relation to each object') or <s>pratyartha</s> ('in relation to each thing').

body.text: atha syāt- yathā ubhayādhīnāyāmapi vijñānapravṛtau āśrayasya paṭumandatānuvidhānād vijñānānāṃ tadvikāravikāritvādāśrayeṇaivavyapadeśo bhavati cakṣurvijñānamiti, evaṃ yadyapi arthamartha prati vartate, tathāpi akṣamakṣamāśritya vartamānaṃ vijñānamāśrayeṇa vyapadeśāt pratyakṣamiti bhaviṣyati | dṛṣṭo hi asādhāraṇena vyapadeśo bherīśabdo yavāṅkura iti | naitatpūrveṇa tulyam | tatra hi viṣayeṇa
body.translated_text: If one were to say: 'Even though the arising of consciousness depends on both [sense-faculty and object], since consciousness conforms to the sharpness or dullness of the basis [i.e., the sense-faculty], and since consciousnesses are modified by the modifications of the basis, the designation is by the basis — as in "eye-consciousness." So too, even though the object operates in relation to each object, consciousness which operates depending on each sense-faculty will be called <s>pratyakṣa</s> because of the designation by the basis. For designation by the uncommon [factor] is observed — as in "drum-sound" and "barley-sprout."' — This is not the same as the previous [cases]. For there, by the object

body.text: vijñāne vyapadiśyamāne rūpavijñānamityevamādinā vijñānaṣaṭkasya bhedo nopadarśitaḥ syāt, manovijñānasya cakṣurādivijñānaiḥ sahaikaviṣayapravṛttatvāt | tathā hi nīlādivijñānaṣaṭke vijñānamityukte sākāṅkṣa eva pratyayājjāyate kimetadrūpīndriyajaṃ vijñānamāhosvinmānasamiti | āśrayeṇa tu vyapadeśe manovijñānasya cakṣurādivijñānaviṣaye pravṛttisaṃbhave 'pi parasparabhedaḥ siddho bhavati | iha tu pramāṇalakṣaṇavivakṣayā kalpanāpoḍhamātrasya pratyakṣatvābhyupagame sati vikalpādeva tadviśeṣatvābhimatatvādasādhāraṇakāraṇena vyapadeśe sati na kiṃcit prayojanamupalakṣyate | prameyaparatantrāyāṃ ca pramāṇasaṃkhyāpravṛttau prameyākārānukāritāmātratayā ca samāsāditātmabhāvasattākayoḥ pramāṇayoḥ svarūpasya vyavasthāpanānnendriyeṇa vyapadeśaḥ kiṃcidupakarotīti sarvathā viṣayeṇaiva vyapadeśo nyāyyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: When consciousness is designated [by its object], the sixfold division of consciousness — such as 'form-consciousness' and so forth — would not be shown, since <s>manovijñāna</s> (mental consciousness) operates on the same object as the eye-consciousness and other [sense-consciousnesses]. For when, in the sixfold consciousness of blue and so forth, merely 'consciousness' is stated, the expectation arises from the condition: 'Is this consciousness born from the form-faculty, or is it mental?' But when designation is by the sense-basis, even though it is possible for <s>manovijñāna</s> to operate on the same objects as eye-consciousness and so forth, their mutual distinction is established. However, here, when — with the intention of defining the characteristics of a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) — perception is accepted as being merely free from conceptual construction, and since its distinctiveness is held to derive from conceptual construction alone, no purpose is observed in designation by the uncommon cause. And since the enumeration of <s>pramāṇas</s> operates dependently upon the objects to be cognized (<s>prameya</s>), and since the two <s>pramāṇas</s> whose existence-as-entities has been arrived at merely by conforming to the aspect of the <s>prameya</s> have their own nature established thereby, designation by the sense-faculty contributes nothing. Therefore, designation by the object alone is proper in every way.

body.text: loke pratyakṣaśabdasya prasiddhatvādvivakṣite 'rthe pratyarthaśabdasyāprasiddhatvādāśrayeṇaiva vyutpattirāśrīyata iti cet, ucyate | astyayaṃ pratyakṣaśabdo loke prasiddhaḥ | sa tu yathā loke, tathā asmābhirucyata eva | yathāsthitalaukikapadārthatiraskāreṇa tu tadvayutpāde kriyamāṇe prasiddhaśabdatiraskāraḥ prasiddhaḥ syāt, tataśca pratyakṣamityevaṃ na syāt | ekasya ca cakṣurvijñānasya ekendriyakṣaṇāśrayasya pratyakṣatvaṃ na syād vīpsārthābhāvāt, ekaikasya ca pratyakṣatvābhāve bahūnāmapi na syāt ||
body.translated_text: If it is objected: 'Since the word <s>pratyakṣa</s> ("perception") is well-known in the world, and since the word <s>pratyartha</s> ("per-object") is not well-known for the intended meaning, etymological derivation by the sense-basis alone is relied upon' — the reply is: This word <s>pratyakṣa</s> is indeed well-known in the world. And just as it is [used] in the world, so it is spoken by us too. But if the derivation is made by setting aside the established worldly meaning, then the setting aside of the established word would itself be established, and hence <s>pratyakṣa</s> [in the opponent's technical sense] would not exist. Moreover, for a single eye-consciousness, having a single momentary sense-faculty as its basis, there would be no <s>pratyakṣatva</s> (perceptuality), since there is no distributive meaning; and if each individual consciousness is not <s>pratyakṣa</s>, many together would not be either.

body.text: kalpanāpoḍhasyaiva ca jñānasya pratyakṣatvābhyupagamāt, tena ca lokasya saṃvyavahārābhāvāt, laukikasya ca pramāṇaprameyavyavahārasya vyākhyātumiṣṭatvād vyarthaiva pratyakṣapramāṇakalpanā saṃjāyate | cakṣurvijñānasāmaṅgī nīlaṃ jānāti no tu nīlamiti cāgamasya pratyakṣalakṣaṇābhidhānārthasyāprastutatvāt, pañcānāmindriyavijñānānāṃ jaḍatvapratipādakatvācca nāgamādapi kalpanāpoḍhasyaiva vijñānasya pratyakṣatvamiti na yuktametat | tasmālloke yadi lakṣyaṃ yadi vā svalakṣaṇaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ vā, sarvameva sākṣādupalabhyamānatvādaparokṣam, ataḥ pratyakṣaṃ vyavasthāpyate tadviṣayeṇa jñānena saha | dvicandrādīnāṃ tu ataimirikajñānāpekṣayā apratyakṣatvam, taimirikādyapekṣayā tu pratyakṣatvameva ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, since perception is accepted as being only cognition free from conceptual construction, and since the world has no transactions by means of such [cognition], and since it is desired to explain the worldly operation of <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s>, the postulation of perception as a <s>pramāṇa</s> [in this sense] becomes entirely pointless. And since the scriptural statement that 'the aggregate of eye-consciousness knows blue but not as blue' is irrelevant to the scripture's purpose of defining the characteristic of perception, and since it only establishes the insentience of the five sense-consciousnesses, it is not correct that even from scripture the perceptuality of consciousness free from conceptual construction alone is established. Therefore, in the world, whether it be an object, its particular characteristic, or its general characteristic — all of it, being directly apprehended, is non-mediate (<s>aparokṣa</s>), and hence is established as <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), together with the cognition that has it as its object. But as for double moons and such — with respect to the cognition of one without an eye-disease, they are non-perceptual; with respect to one with an eye-disease, they are indeed perceptual.

body.text: parokṣaviṣayaṃ tu jñānaṃ sādhyāvyabhicāriliṅgotpannamanumānam ||
body.translated_text: Cognition that has a mediate object and arises from an inferential mark that does not deviate from what is to be established is <s>anumāna</s> (inference).

body.text: sākṣādatīndriyārthavidāmāptānāṃ yadvacanaṃ sa āgamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The statement of trustworthy persons (<s>āpta</s>) — those who directly know supersensory objects — is <s>āgama</s> (scripture).

body.text: sādṛśyādananubhūtārthadhigama upamānaṃ gauriva gavaya iti yathā ||
body.translated_text: The cognition of an object not previously experienced through similarity is <s>upamāna</s> (analogy) — as when one says 'a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) is like a cow.'

body.text: tadevaṃ pramāṇacatuṣṭayāllokasyārthādhigamo vyavasthāpyate ||
body.translated_text: Thus, the world's cognition of objects is established through a fourfold <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition).

body.text: tāni ca parasparāpekṣayā sidhyanti- satsu pramāṇeṣu prameyārthāḥ, satsu prameyeṣvartheṣu pramāṇāni | no tu khalu svābhāvikī pramāṇaprameyayoḥ siddhiriti | tasmāllaukikamevāstu yathādṛṣṭamityalaṃ prasaṅgena | prastutameva vyākhyāsyāmaḥ | laukika eva darśane sthitvā buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ dharmadeśanā || 3 ||
body.translated_text: And these are established in mutual dependence: when there are <s>pramāṇas</s>, there are objects to be cognized; when there are objects to be cognized, there are <s>pramāṇas</s>. But the establishment of <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s> is not intrinsic. Therefore, let it be just as it appears in the world — enough with this digression. We shall explain the subject at hand. It is by standing in the worldly way of seeing that the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> teach the <s>Dharma</s>. // 3 //

body.text: atrāhuḥ svayūthyāḥ- yadidamuktaṃ na svata utpadyante bhāvā iti, tadyuktam, svata utpattivaiyarthyāt | yaccoktaṃ na dvābhyāmiti, tadapi yuktam, ekāṃśavaikalyāt | ahetupakṣastu
body.translated_text: Here those of the same school object: 'What was stated — that entities do not arise from themselves — that is correct, since arising from self would be purposeless. And what was stated — not from both — that too is correct, since each part is defective. And since the position of no cause is utterly base, its refutation is also correct. But what is stated here — not from another either — that is incorrect, since the <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared that entities have causes of arising that are other [than themselves]:'

body.text: ekāntanikṛṣṭa iti tatpratiṣedho 'pi yuktaḥ| yattu khalvidamucyate nāpi parata iti, tadayuktam yasmātparabhūtā eva bhagavatā bhāvānāmutpādakā nirdiṣṭāḥ |
