body.translated_text: 'since the causeless position is utterly base, its refutation too is correct. But what is stated here — not from another either — that is incorrect, since the <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared that entities have causes of arising that are other [than themselves]:'

children.translated_text: There are four conditions: the cause, the object-support, the immediately antecedent, /
and likewise the dominant — there is no fifth condition. // 4 //

body.text: tatra nirvartako heturiti lakṣaṇāt, yo hi yasya nirvartako bījabhāvenāvasthitaḥ, sa tasya hetu pratyayaḥ | utpadyamāno dharmo yenālambanenotpadyate, sa tasyālambanapratyayaḥ | kāraṇasyānantaro nirodhaḥ kāryasyotpattipratyayaḥ, tadyathā bījasyānantaro nirodho 'ṅkurasyotpādapratyayaḥ | yasmin sati yadbhavati tattasyādhipateyamiti | ta ete catvāraḥ pratyayāḥ | ye cānye purojātasahajātapaścājjātādayaḥ, te eteṣveva antarbhūtāḥ | īśvarādayastu pratyayā eva na saṃbhavantīti, ata evāvadhārayati- pratyayo nāsti pañcama iti | tasmādebhyaḥ parabhūtebhyo bhāvānāmutpattirasti parata utpattiriti || 4 ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the cause-condition (<s>hetupratyaya</s>) is defined as 'the producer' — that which, existing in the form of a seed, produces something, is its cause-condition. The object-support condition (<s>ālambanapratyaya</s>) is that object-support depending on which a <s>dharma</s> arises as it is being produced. The immediately antecedent condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>) is the cessation of the cause immediately [prior to] the arising of the effect — for example, the cessation of a seed immediately [prior to] the arising of a sprout. The dominant condition (<s>adhipatipratyaya</s>) is: that in the presence of which something comes to be is its dominant condition. These are the four conditions. And whatever other [conditions] there may be — such as those preceding, co-arising, and succeeding — they are included within these very ones. But conditions such as <s>Īśvara</s> (God) are simply impossible — therefore he states definitively: 'There is no fifth condition.' Therefore, since there is arising of entities from these conditions, which are other [than the effect], there is arising from another. // 4 //

body.text: atrocyate- naiva hi bhāvānāṃ parabhūtebhyaḥ pratyayebhya utpattiriti | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: In reply it is said: There is indeed no arising of entities from conditions that are other. For —

children.text: na hi svabhāvo bhāvānāṃ pratyayādiṣu vidyate |
children.translated_text: The <s>svabhāva</s> (own-nature) of entities is not found in conditions and the rest. /
When own-nature is absent, <s>parabhāva</s> (other-nature) is not found. // 5 //

body.text: iti | yadi hi hetvādiṣu parabhuteṣu pratyayeṣu samasteṣu vyasteṣu vyastasamasteṣu hetupratyaya sāmagyā anyatra vā kvacid bhāvānāṃ kāryāṇāmutpādātpūrvaṃ sattvaṃ syāt, syāttebhya utpādaḥ | na caivaṃ yadutpādātpūrvaṃ saṃbhavaḥ syāt | yadi syāt, gṛhyeta ca, utpādavaiyarthyaṃ ca syāt | tasmānnaṃ cāsti bhāvānāṃ pratyayādiṣu svabhāvaḥ | avidyamāne ca svabhāve nāsti parabhāvaḥ | bhavanaṃ bhāva utpādaḥ, parebhya utpādaḥ parabhāvaḥ, sa na vidyate | tasmādayuktametat parabhūtebhyo bhāvānā mutpattiriti ||
body.translated_text: For if, prior to arising, the entities that are effects had existence in the conditions that are other — namely the cause and so forth — whether taken collectively, individually, or both collectively and individually, in the cause-condition, in the aggregate of conditions, or anywhere else, then their arising from those [conditions] would be possible. But this is not so — there is no existence prior to arising. If there were, it could be apprehended, and arising would be purposeless. Therefore, entities have no <s>svabhāva</s> in conditions and the rest. And when <s>svabhāva</s> is absent, there is no <s>parabhāva</s>. <s>Bhāva</s> means arising; <s>parabhāva</s> means arising from others — and that is not found. Therefore, it is incorrect that there is arising of entities from what is other.

body.text: athavā bhāvānāṃ kāryāṇāmaṅkurādīnāṃ vījādiṣu pratyayeṣu satsvavikṛtarūpeṣu nāsti svabhāvo nirhetukatvaprasaṅgāt ||
body.translated_text: Alternatively: the entities that are effects — sprouts and so forth — do not have <s>svabhāva</s> (own-nature) in the conditions such as seeds, which remain in their unmodified form, because otherwise they would be causeless.

body.text: tatkimapekṣaṃ paratvaṃ pratyayādīnām? vidyamānayoreva hi maitropagrāhakayoḥ parasparāpekṣaṃ paratvam? na caivaṃ bījāṅkurayoryaugapadyam | tasmādavidyamāne svabhāve kāryāṇāṃ parabhāvaḥ paratvaṃ bījādīnāṃ nāstīti paravyapadeśābhāvādeva na parata utpāda iti | tasmādāgamābhiprāyānabhijñataiva parasya | na hi tathāgatā yuktiviruddhaṃ vākyamudāharanti | āgamasya cābhiprāyaḥ prāgevopavarṇitaḥ || 5 ||
body.translated_text: By reference to what, then, would the conditions and the rest have their otherness? For otherness, through mutual reference, exists only between two entities that both exist — like <s>Maitra</s> and <s>Upagrāhaka</s>. But there is no simultaneity of seed and sprout. Therefore, when the <s>svabhāva</s> (own-nature) of the effects does not exist, the <s>parabhāva</s> (otherness) of the seeds and so forth does not exist either — and since the designation 'other' is absent, there is no arising from another. Therefore, the opponent simply does not understand the intent of scripture. For the <s>Tathāgatas</s> do not utter a statement that contradicts reasoning. And the intent of scripture has been explained earlier. // 5 //

body.text: tadevaṃ pratyayebhya utpādavādini pratiṣiddhe kriyāta utpādavādī manyate- na cakṣūrūpādayaḥ pratyayāḥ sākṣādvijñānaṃ janayanti | vijñānajanikriyāniṣpādakatvāttu pratyayā ucyante | sā ca kriyā vijñānaṃ janayati | tasmātpratyayavatī vijñānajanikriyā vijñānajanikā, na pratyayāḥ | yathā pacikriyā odanasyeti | ucyate-
body.translated_text: Thus, when the proponent of arising from conditions has been refuted, the proponent of arising from action thinks: 'The conditions — eye, form, and so forth — do not directly produce consciousness. But because they bring about the action of producing consciousness, they are called conditions. And it is that action that produces consciousness. Therefore, the action of producing consciousness, which possesses conditions, is what produces consciousness — not the conditions themselves. Just as the action of cooking [produces] rice.' In reply it is said:

body.text: kriyā na pratyayavatī
body.translated_text: Action does not possess conditions.

body.text: yadi kriyā kācit syāt, sā cakṣurādibhiḥ pratyayaiḥ pratyayavatī vijñānaṃ janayet | na
body.translated_text: If there were some action, it, being possessed of conditions such as the eye and so forth, would produce consciousness. But there is not.

body.text: tvasti | kathaṃ kṛtvā? iha kriyeyamiṣyamāṇā jāte vā vijñāne iṣyate, ajāte vā jāyamāne vā? tatra jāte na yuktā | kriyā hi bhāvaniṣpādikā | bhāvaścenniṣpannaḥ, kimasya kriyayā?
body.translated_text: How so? Here, this action that is posited — is it posited with respect to consciousness already arisen, not yet arisen, or being arisen? In the first case, with respect to what has already arisen, it is not appropriate. For action accomplishes the coming-into-being of an entity. But if the entity is already accomplished, what need is there for action?

body.text: jātasya janma punareva ca naiva yuktam |
body.translated_text: The birth of what is already born is simply not appropriate. /

body.text: ityādinā ca madhyamakāvatāre pratipāditametat | ajāte 'pi na yuktā,
body.translated_text: And so forth — this has been demonstrated in the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s>. Nor is it appropriate with respect to what has not yet arisen:

body.text: kartrā vinā janiriyaṃ na ca yuktarūpā |
body.translated_text: This birth without an agent is not of a proper form. /

body.text: ityādivacanāt | jāyamāne 'pi bhāve kriyā na saṃbhavati, jātājātavyatirekeṇa jāyamānābhāvāt | yathoktam-
body.translated_text: Because of such statements. Nor is action possible with respect to an entity that is being born, since there is no 'being born' apart from 'born' and 'not yet born.' As stated:

body.text:
jāyamānārthajātatvājjāyamāno na jāyate |
atha vā jāyamānatvaṃ sarvasyaiva prasajyate || iti |
yataścaivaṃ triṣu kāleṣu janikriyāyā asaṃbhavaḥ, tasmānnāsti sā | ata evāha- kriyā na pratyayavatī iti |
body.translated_text:
'What is being born does not arise, because what-is-being-born is already born.
Or else, the state of being-born would apply to everything.' //
Since thus the action of arising is impossible in the three times, therefore it does not exist. Hence he says: 'Action does not possess conditions.'

body.text: viśeṣaṇaṃ nāsti vinā viśeṣam |
body.translated_text: A qualifier does not exist without the qualified. /

body.text: ityādinā pratipāditametanmadhyamakāvatāre | na hi vandhyāputro gomānityucyate ||
body.translated_text: And so forth — this has been demonstrated in the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s>. For one does not say 'the son of a barren woman possesses cows.'

body.text:
yadyevam, apratyayavatī tarhi bhaviṣyatīti, etadapyayuktamityāha-
nāpratyayavatī kriyā |
body.translated_text:
If so, then it will be without conditions — this too is inappropriate, hence he says:
Nor is action without conditions.

body.text: yadā pratyayavatī nāsti, tadā kathamapratyayavatī nirhetukā syāt? na hi tantumayaḥ paṭo na yukta iti vīraṇamayo 'bhyupagamyate | tasmātkriyā na bhāvajanikā ||
body.translated_text: When action with conditions does not exist, how could action without conditions — that is, without cause — exist? For if cloth made of threads is not appropriate, one does not thereby accept cloth made of grass. Therefore, action does not produce entities.

body.text: atrāha- yadyevaṃ kriyāyā asaṃbhavaḥ, pratyayāstarhi janakā bhaviṣyanti bhāvānāmiti | ucyate-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: 'If action is thus impossible, then the conditions themselves will be the producers of entities.' The reply is:

body.text: pratyayā nākriyāvantaḥ
body.translated_text: Conditions are not without action.

body.text: yadā kriyā nāsti, tadā kriyārahitā akriyāvanto nirhetukāḥ pratyayāḥ kathaṃ janakāḥ? atha kriyāvanta eva janakā iti, ucyate-
body.translated_text: When action does not exist, how can conditions that are devoid of action — without action, without cause — be producers? If it is said that they are producers only when possessed of action, the reply is:

body.text: kriyāvantaśca santyuta || 6 ||
body.translated_text: And do they also exist with action? // 6 //

body.text: neti prakṛtenābhisaṃbandhaḥ | utaśabdo 'vadhāraṇe | tatra kriyāyā abhāva uktaḥ, kathaṃ kriyāvattvaṃ pratyayānāmiti? yathā ca vijñānajanikriyoktā, evaṃ parikriyādayo 'pi bhāvā uktā veditavyā iti nāsti kriyāto 'pi samutpattirbhāvānāmiti bhavatyutpādābhidhānamarthaśūnyam || 6 ||
body.translated_text: 'No' — this is to be connected with the main topic. The word 'also' (<s>uta</s>) is emphatic. Since the non-existence of action has been stated, how can the conditions have action? And just as the action of producing consciousness has been discussed, so too all other entities such as transformation and the rest should be understood to have been discussed — thus there is no arising of entities from action either. Hence the declaration of arising becomes devoid of meaning. // 6 //

body.text: atrāha- kiṃ na etena kriyāvantaḥ pratyayā ityādivicāreṇa? yasmāccakṣurādīn pratītya pratyayān vijñānādayo bhāvā jāyante, tasmāccakṣurādīnāṃ pratyayatvaṃ tebhyaścotpādo vijñānādīnāmiti | etadapyayuktamityāha-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: 'What need is there for this investigation — "do conditions have action?" and so forth? Since visual consciousness and other entities arise dependent on the conditions of the eye and so forth, therefore the eye and so forth have the status of conditions, and from them there is the arising of consciousness and so forth.' This too is inappropriate, hence he says:

children.translated_text: 'These are conditions,' they say, 'because dependent on them, these arise.' /
As long as they have not arisen, how are those not non-conditions? // 7 //

body.text: yadi cakṣurādīn pratyayān pratītya vijñānamutpadyate iti asya ime pratyayā ucyante, nanu yāvattadvijñānākhyaṃ kāryaṃ notpadyate tāvadime cakṣurādayaḥ kathaṃ nāpratyayāḥ? apratyayā evetyabhiprāyaḥ na cāpratyayebhya utpattiḥ sikatābhya iva tailasya |
body.translated_text: If it is said that consciousness arises dependent on the conditions of the eye and so forth, and hence these are called its conditions — then surely, as long as that effect called consciousness has not arisen, how are these — the eye and so forth — not non-conditions? The implication is: they are indeed non-conditions. And there is no arising from non-conditions — just as oil [does not arise] from sand.

body.text: atha matam- pūrvamapratyayāḥ santaḥ kiṃcidanyaṃ pratyayamapekṣya pratyayatvaṃ pratipadyanta iti, etadapyayuktam | yat tat pratyayāntaramapratyayasya tasya pratyayatvena kalpyate, tadapi pratyayatve sati asya pratyayo bhavati | tatrāpyeṣaiva cintaneti na yuktametat || 7 ||
body.translated_text: If it is thought: 'Being non-conditions initially, they come to be conditions by depending on some other condition' — this too is inappropriate. For that other condition which is postulated as making this non-condition into a condition, it too becomes its condition only when it already has the status of a condition. And there the same reasoning applies — hence this is not correct. // 7 //

body.text: kiṃ ca | iha ime cakṣurādayo vijñānasya pratyayāḥ kalpyamānāḥ sato vā asya kalpyeran, asato vā? sarvathā ca na yujyate ityāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover: here, when the eye and so forth are being postulated as conditions of consciousness, are they postulated as conditions of an existent [effect] or of a non-existent one? In every case, it is not appropriate, hence he says:

children.translated_text: A condition is not appropriate for either a non-existent or an existent object. /
Why? He says:

children.text: asataḥ pratyayaḥ kasya sataśca pratyayena kim || 8 ||
children.translated_text: Of what that is non-existent would there be a condition? And for what that already exists, what need is there of a condition? // 8 //

body.text: asato hyarthasya avidyamānasya kathaṃ pratyayaḥ syāt? bhaviṣyatā vyapadeśo bhaviṣyatīti cet, naivam-
body.translated_text: For how could there be a condition for an object that is non-existent, that does not exist? If it is said: 'The designation will be by means of what will be [in the future]' — this is not so:

body.text:
bhaviṣyatā cedvayapadeśa iṣṭaḥ
śaktiṃ vinā nāsti hi bhāvitāsya |
body.translated_text:
If designation by means of what will be is accepted,
then without a potentiality, the entity's futurity does not exist.

body.text: ityādinoktadoṣatvāt | sato 'pi vidyamānasya labdhajanmano niṣphalaiva pratyayakalpanā ||
evaṃ samastānāṃ pratyayānāṃ kāryotpādanāsāmarthyena apratyayatvamudbhāvya ataḥ paraṃ vyastānāmapratyayatvaṃ pratipādyate ||

atrāha- yadyapyevaṃ pratyayānāmasaṃbhavaḥ, tathāpi astyeva lakṣaṇopadeśātpratyayaprasiddhiḥ | tatra nirvartako heturiti lakṣaṇamucyate hetupratyayasya | na cāvidyamānasya lakṣaṇopadeśo yukto bandhyāsutasyeveti | ucyate | syāddhetupratyayo yadi tasya lakṣaṇaṃ syāt | yasmāt-

children.text: na sannāsanna sadasan dharmo nirvartate yadā |
kathaṃ nirvartako heturevaṃ sati hi yujyate || 9 ||

body.text: tatra nirvartaka utpādakaḥ | yadi nirvartyo dharmo nirvarteta, tamutpādako heturutpādayet | na tu nirvartate, sadasadubhayarūpasya nirvartyasyābhāvāt | tatra sanna nirvartate vidyamānatvāt | asannapi, avidyamānatvāt | sadasannapi, parasparaviruddhasyaikārthasyābhāvāt, ubhayapakṣābhihitadoṣatvācca | yata evaṃ kāryasyotpattirnāsti, hetupratyayo 'pyato nāsti | tataśca yaduktaṃ lakṣaṇasaṃbhavādvidyate hetupratyaya iti, tadevaṃ sati na yujyate || 9 ||

iha sālambanadharmāḥ katame? sarvacittacaittā ityāgamāt | cittacaittā yenālambanenotpadyante yathāyogaṃ rūpādinā, sa teṣāmālambanapratyayaḥ | ayaṃ ca vidyamānānāṃ vā parikalpyeta avidyamānānāṃ vā | tatra vidyamānānāṃ nārthastadālambanapratyayena | dharmasya hi utpattyarthamālambanaṃ parikalpyate, sa cālambanātpūrvaṃ vidyamāna eveti | athaivamanālambane dharme svātmanā prasiddhe kimasya ālambanayogena parikalpitena, ityanālambana evāyaṃ san vidyamāno dharmaḥ cittādikaḥ kevalaṃ sālambana ityucyate bhavadbhiḥ svamanīṣikayā, na tvasya ālambanena kaścitsaṃbandho 'sti | athāvidyamānasyālambanaṃ parikalpyate, tadapi na yuktam, anālambana evāyamityādi | avidyamānasya hi nāsti ālambanena yogaḥ ||

atrāha- tantvādibhyaḥ paṭādikamupalabhya paṭādestantvādayaḥ pratyayā iti | ucyate paṭādiphalapravṛttireva svarūpato nāsti, kutaḥ pratyayānāṃ pratyayatvaṃ setsyati? yathā ca paṭādiphalapravṛttirasatī, tathā pratipādayannāha-

body.text: tatra vyasteṣu tantuturīvematasaraśalākādiṣu pratyayeṣu paṭo nāsti, tatrānupalabhyamānatvāt kāraṇabahutvācca kāryabahutvaprasaṅgāt | samuditeṣvapi tantvādiṣu nāsti paṭaḥ, pratyekamavayaveṣvavidyamānatvāt, ekasya kāryasya khaṇḍaśa utpattiprasaṅgāt | tasmātphalābhāvānna santi pratyayāḥ svabhāvata iti || 13 ||
athāsadapi tattebhyaḥ pratyayebhyaḥ pravartate |

yadi pratyayamayaṃ pratyayavikāraḥ phalamiti vyavasthāpyate, tadayuktam | yasmātte 'pi pratyayā asvayaṃmayā apratyayasvabhāvā ityarthaḥ | tantumayo hi paṭa ityucyate | syāt paṭo yadi tantava eva
svabhāvasiddhāḥ syuḥ | te hi aṃśumayā aṃśuvikārā na svabhāvasiddhāḥ | tataśca tebhyo 'svayaṃmayebhyo 'svabhāvebhyo yatphalaṃ paṭākhyam, tatkathaṃ tantumayaṃ bhaviṣyati? yathoktam-

asvabhāvu paru kiṃ janīṣyati eṣa hetu sugatena deśitaḥ ||

body.text:
śailaparvata yathā akampiyā evaṃ dharma avikampiyāḥ sadā |
no cyavati na pi copapadyayu evaṃ dharmata jinena deśitā || ityādi |
tathā-

taṃ jinu deśayatī narasiṃhaḥ tatra niveśayi sattvaśatāni |

nāntarato na pi bāhirato vā labhyati tatra niveśayi nāthaḥ ||

body.text:
śānta gatī kathitā sugatena no ca gati upalabhyati kāci |
tatra ca voharasī gatimukto muktaku mocayamī bahusattvān || iti vistaraḥ || 16 ||
ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacitāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau pratyayaparīkṣā nāma prathamaṃ prakaraṇam ||
gatāgataparīkṣā dvitīyaṃ prakaraṇam |

atrāha- yadyapi utpādapratiṣedhātpratītyasamutpādasya anirodhādiviśeṣaṇasiddhiḥ, tathāpi anāgamanirgamapratītyasamutpādasiddhaye lokaprasiddhagamanāgamanakriyāpratiṣedhārthaṃ kiṃcidupapattyantaramucyatāmiti | ucyate | yadi gamanaṃ nāma syānniyataṃ tadgate vā adhvajāte parikalpyeta agate gamyamāne vā | sarvathā ca na yujyate ityāha-

children.text: gataṃ na gamyate tāvadagataṃ naiva gamyate |

body.text: tatra uparatagamikriyamadhvajātaṃ gatamityucyate | āviśyamānaṃ gamikriyayā vartamānaṃ gamyata ityucyate | yadgatamuparatagamikriyaṃ tadvartamānagamikriyāyogavācinā gamyate ityanena śabdenocyamānamasaṃbaddhamiti kṛtvā gataṃ tāvad gamyata iti na yujyate | tāvacchabdena ca pratiṣedhakramaṃ darśayati ||

agatamapi na gamyate | agataṃ hi anupajātagamikriyamanāgatamucyate, gamyata iti ca vartamānam | ato 'nāgatavartamānayoratyantabhedādagatamapi gamyata iti na yujyate | yadi agataṃ kathaṃ gamyate, atha gamyate na tadagatamiti ||
body.translated_text: The not-yet-gone-to (<s>agata</s>) is also not being gone to. For 'not-yet-gone-to' means what has not yet had the action of going arise in it — i.e. the future; and 'is being gone to' is present. Therefore, because of the absolute difference between the future and the present, it is not correct that 'the not-yet-gone-to is being gone to.' If it is not-yet-gone-to, how can it be being gone to? And if it is being gone to, it is not the not-yet-gone-to.

body.text: gamyamāne 'pi nāsti gamanam, yasmāt-
body.translated_text: There is no going in what is being gone to either, because —

body.text: gatāgatavinirmuktaṃ gamyamānaṃ na gamyate |
body.translated_text: Freed from what has been gone to and the not-yet-gone-to, what is being gone to is not being gone to.

body.text: iha hi gantā yaṃ deśamatikrāntaḥ sa tasya deśo gataḥ, yaṃ ca nātikrāntaḥ so 'syānāgataḥ | na ca gatāgatavyatirekeṇa tṛtīyamaparamadhvajātaṃ paśyāmo gamyamānaṃ nāma | yataścaivaṃ gamyamānaṃ na gamyate, gamyata iti na prajñāyate, tasmānnāsti gamyamānam | ato na tad gamikriyayā āviśyate na gamyata iti nāsti gamyamāne 'pi gamanam ||
body.translated_text: For here, the place that the goer has passed beyond is the 'gone-to' for him, and the place he has not passed beyond is the 'not-yet-gone-to' for him. And apart from the gone-to and the not-yet-gone-to, we do not see a third distinct path-segment called 'being gone to.' And since the being-gone-to is thus not being gone to and is not known as 'is being gone to,' therefore there is no being-gone-to. Hence it is not pervaded by the action of going, it is not being gone to — thus there is no going even in the being-gone-to.

body.text: atha syāt- ganturgacchato yaścaraṇākrānto deśaḥ, sa gamyamānaḥ syāditi | naivam, caraṇayorapi paramāṇusāṃghātatvāt | aṅgulyagrāvasthitasya paramāṇoryaḥ pūrvo deśaḥ, sa tasya gate 'ntargataḥ | pārṣṇyavasthitasya caramaparamāṇorya uttaro deśaḥ, sa tasya agate 'ntargataḥ | na ca paramāṇuvyatirekeṇa caraṇamasti | tasmānnāsti gatāgatavyatirekeṇa gamyamānam | yathā caivaṃ caraṇe vicāraḥ, evaṃ paramāṇūnāmapi pūrvāparadigbhāgasaṃbandhena vicāraḥ kārya iti | athārdhagataṃ gamyamānam, uktamuttaraṃ jāyamānavicāreṇa | tasmādgamyamānaṃ na gamyate iti siddham || 1 ||
body.translated_text: One might suggest: the space covered by the goer's feet as he walks would be the being-gone-to. Not so, because the feet too are aggregates of atoms. The place in front of the atom situated at the tip of the toe — that falls within what has been gone to. The place behind the last atom situated at the heel — that falls within the not-yet-gone-to. And there is no foot apart from the atoms. Therefore there is no being-gone-to apart from the gone-to and the not-yet-gone-to. And just as this analysis applies to the foot, so too should the analysis be applied to the atoms themselves in terms of their connection with the front and back portions of space. If the being-gone-to is 'half-gone-to,' the answer has already been given by the analysis of the arising [entity]. Therefore it is established that the being-gone-to is not being gone to. // 1 //

body.text: tatrāha- gamyata eva gamyamānam | iha hi-
body.translated_text: To this one says: the being-gone-to is indeed being gone to. For —

children.text: ceṣṭā yatra gatistatra gamyamāne ca sā yataḥ |
children.translated_text: Where there is effort, there is going; and since that [effort] is in the being-gone-to,

children.text: na gate nāgate ceṣṭā gamyamāne gatistataḥ || 2 ||
children.translated_text: and effort is not in the gone-to nor in the not-yet-gone-to — going is in the being-gone-to. // 2 //

body.text: tatra ceṣṭā caraṇotkṣepaparikṣepalakṣaṇā | yato vrajato ganturyatra deśe ceṣṭā gatiḥ tatraiva deśe | sā ca ceṣṭā na gate 'dhvani saṃbhavati nāpyagate, kiṃ tu gamyamāna eva | tataśca gamyamāne gatiḥ | yatra hi gatirupalabhyate tadgamyamānam, tacca gamikriyayā āviśyate | tasmād gamyamānameva gamyate iti | eko 'tra gamirjñānārthaḥ, aparaśca deśāntarasaṃprāptyartha iti || 2 ||
body.translated_text: Here, 'effort' has the characteristic of lifting up and putting down of the feet. The going of the goer who walks is in that very place where there is effort. And that effort does not occur in the gone-to path, nor in the not-yet-gone-to, but only in the being-gone-to. Hence going is in the being-gone-to. For that in which going is observed is the being-gone-to, and that is pervaded by the action of going. Therefore the being-gone-to alone is being gone to. Here one occurrence of 'going' (<s>gami</s>) has the sense of knowledge, and the other has the sense of arriving at another place. // 2 //

body.text: evamapi parikalpyamāne gamyamānaṃ na gamyata ityāha-
body.translated_text: Even when imagined thus, the being-gone-to is not being gone to — he says:

children.translated_text: How will the going of the being-gone-to be possible,
when a double going in the being-gone-to is simply not possible? // 3 //

body.text: iha hi gamikriyāyogādeva gamyamānavyapadeśamicchati bhavān, tacca iti gamyata bravīti | ekā cātra gamikriyā, tayā gamyamānavyapadeśo bhavatu kāmamadhvanaḥ | gamyata iti bhūyaḥ kriyāsaṃbandho gamyamānasya na yujyata iti
body.translated_text: For you desire the designation 'being-gone-to' precisely because of the connection with the action of going, and you say 'is being gone to.' There is here a single action of going; by that, let the designation 'being-gone-to' of the path be granted. But a connection of a second action to the being-gone-to is not justified — thus,

body.text: gamyamānasya gamanaṃ kathaṃ nāmopapatsyate |
body.translated_text: how will the going of the being-gone-to be possible?

body.text: kāraṇamāha-
body.translated_text: He states the reason:

body.text: gamyamāne dvigamanaṃ yadā naivopapadyate || iti ||
body.translated_text: When a double going in the being-gone-to is simply not possible. //

body.text: gamyamānamiti gamyata ityarthaḥ | dvigataṃ gamanaṃ dvigamanam | ekasyā gamikriyāyā gamyamānamityatropayuktatvād dvitīyāyā abhāvācca, gamyata ityayaṃ vyapadeśo vinā gamanena yadā naivopapadyate, tadā gamyamānaṃ gamyata iti paripūrṇo vākyārtho nāstītyabhiprāyaḥ | gamyamānamityetāvanmātrameva saṃbhavati dvitīyakriyābhāvāt, na tu gamyata iti || 3 ||
body.translated_text: 'Being-gone-to' means 'is being gone to.' 'Double going' means two acts of going. Since one action of going is employed in 'being-gone-to,' and since there is no second one, the designation 'is being gone to' without going — when this is simply not possible, then the full meaning of the statement 'the being-gone-to is being gone to' does not exist — this is the intent. Only 'being-gone-to' by itself is possible, since there is no second action, but not 'is being gone to.' // 3 //

body.text: atha gamyate ityatraiva gamikriyāsaṃbandha iṣyate, evaṃ sati gamyamānavyapadeśe nāsti kriyāsaṃbandha iti na paripūrṇatā vākyārthasyetyāha-
body.translated_text: But if the connection of the action of going is desired in 'is being gone to' alone, then in that case there is no connection of action in the designation 'being-gone-to,' and thus the statement's meaning is incomplete — he says:

children.translated_text: The going of the being-gone-to, for one who [asserts] that, entails the consequence:
The being-gone-to [would exist] without going — for the being-gone-to is indeed being gone to. // 4 //

body.text: yasya vādino gamyamānasya gamanamiti pakṣaḥ, gamyamāne saṃjñābhūte gamikriyāśūnye yo gamikriyāmādheyabhūtāmicchati, tasya pakṣe ṛte gatergamyamānamiti prasajyate, gatirahitaṃ gamanaṃ syāt, yasmādasya gamyamānaṃ hi gamyate | hi śabdo yasmādarthe | yasmād gatirahitameva gamyamānaṃ sat tasya vādino gamyate, gamyata ityatra kriyopayogāt, tasmād gatirahitaṃ gamanaṃ prasajyate || 4 ||
body.translated_text: For the proponent whose thesis is 'the going of the being-gone-to' — who desires to add the action of going to the being-gone-to which is [already] a designation devoid of the action of going — for his thesis, the consequence follows that 'the being-gone-to [exists] without going,' i.e. there would be going devoid of going, because this proponent's being-gone-to, devoid of going, is being gone to, since the action is employed in 'is being gone to.' Therefore the consequence of going devoid of going follows. // 4 //

body.text: atha ubhayatrāpi kriyāsaṃbandha iṣyate gamyamāne gamyate ityatra ca, evamapi-
body.translated_text: But if the connection of the action is desired in both — in 'being-gone-to' and in 'is being gone to' — even then:

children.translated_text: In the going of the being-gone-to, there follows a double going:

children.text: yena tadgamyamānaṃ ca yaccātra gamanaṃ punaḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: that by which it is 'being-gone-to,' and also that going which is here [in 'is being gone to']. // 5 //

body.text: yena gamanena yogādgamyamānavyapadeśaṃ pratilabhate 'dhvā, tadekaṃ gamanam || tatra gamyamāne 'dhikaraṇabhute dvitīyaṃ gamanaṃ yena so 'dhvā gamyate | etadgamanadvayaṃ gamyamānasya gamane sati prasaktam || 5 ||
body.translated_text: That going by whose connection the path acquires the designation 'being-gone-to' — that is one going. And in the being-gone-to as the substrate, the second going by which that path is being gone to [exists]. This double going follows when there is going of the being-gone-to. // 5 //

body.text: bhavatu gamanadvayam, ko doṣa iti cet, ayaṃ doṣaḥ | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Let there be a double going — what is the fault? This is the fault: because —

body.text: dvau gantārau prasajyete prasakte gamanadvaye |
body.translated_text: Two goers would follow when a double going follows.

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ gantṛdvayaprasaṅge ityāha-
body.translated_text: What further is the reason for the consequence of two goers? He says:

body.text: gantāraṃ hi tiraskṛtya gamanaṃ nopapadyate || 6 ||
body.translated_text: For going does not occur when one sets aside the goer. // 6 //

body.text: yasmādavaśyaṃ kriyā svasādhanamapekṣate karma kartāraṃ vā | gamikriyā caivaṃ kartaryavasthitā, ato gantāramapekṣate | nāsti ca ekasminneva gacchati devadatte dvitīyaḥ karteti | ataḥ kartṛdvayābhāvānnāsti gamanadvayam | tataśca gamyamānaṃ gamyata iti nopapadyate ||
body.translated_text: Because an action necessarily requires its own accomplisher — either the object (<s>karma</s>) or the agent (<s>kartṛ</s>). And the action of going is established in an agent in this way — therefore it requires a goer. And there is no second agent when a single <s>Devadatta</s> alone is going. Therefore, due to the absence of two agents, there is no double going. Hence 'the being-gone-to is being gone to' is not possible.

body.text: atha syāt- yadāyaṃ devadattaḥ sthitaḥ, sa na bhāṣate? paśyati na? tadaiko 'nekakriyo dṛṣṭaḥ, evamekasmin gantari kriyādvayaṃ bhaviṣyati iti | naivam | śaktirhi kārako na dravyam | kriyābhedācca tatsādhanasyāpi śakteḥ siddha eva bhedaḥ | na hi sthitikriyayā vaktā syāt | dravyamekamiti cet, bhavatu evam, na tu dravyaṃ kārakaḥ, kiṃ tarhi śaktiḥ, sā ca bhidyata eva | api ca | sadṛśakriyādvaya kārakatvaṃ naikadeśikasya dṛṣṭam, ato naikasya ganturgamanadvayam || 6 ||
body.translated_text: One might say: when this <s>Devadatta</s> is standing, does he not speak? Does he not see? Thus a single [person] is seen to have multiple actions; similarly, there will be two actions in one goer. Not so. For it is the capacity (<s>śakti</s>) that is the agent, not the substance (<s>dravya</s>). And because of the difference in actions, the difference in the capacity that accomplishes them is already established. For one is not a speaker by the action of standing. If [you say] the substance is one — let it be so; but the substance is not the agent; rather, the capacity is, and that indeed differs. Moreover, agenthood of two similar actions has not been observed in a single locus; therefore, there is no double going for one goer. // 6 //

body.text: atrāha- yadyapyevaṃ tathāpi gantari devadatte gamanamupalabhyate devadatto gacchatīti vyapadeśāt | tataśca vidyata eva gamanaṃ gamanāśrayagantṛsadbhāvāt | ucyate | syādevaṃ yadi gamanāśrayo gantā syāt, na tvasti | kathamityāha-
body.translated_text: To this one says: even if so, nevertheless going is observed in the goer <s>Devadatta</s>, from the designation '<s>Devadatta</s> goes.' And so going does exist, because the goer who is the substratum of going exists. It is replied: this would be so if the goer were the substratum of going; but he is not. How so? He says:

children.translated_text: If, setting aside the goer, going does not occur,
then in the absence of going, whence will a goer come to be? // 7 //

body.text: gantāramantareṇa nirāśrayaṃ gamanamasadityuktam, tataśca gantāraṃ cetiraskṛtya pratyākhyāya gamanaṃ nāsti, asati gamane kuto nirhetuko gantā? ato nāsti gamanam || 7 ||
body.translated_text: It has been said that going, being without a substratum, without the goer, is non-existent. And therefore, setting aside — i.e. excluding — the goer, going does not exist. In the absence of going, whence would the goer [come to be], without a cause? Therefore going does not exist. // 7 //

body.text: atrāha- vidyata eva gamanam, tadvatastena vyapadeśāt | iha gantā gamanena yuktaḥ, tadyogācca gacchati | yadi gamanaṃ na syāt, gamanavato devadattasya gacchatīti vyapadeśo na syāt, daṇḍābhāve daṇḍivyapadeśābhāvavat | ucyate | syādgamanam, yadi gacchatītyevaṃ vyapadeśaḥ syāt | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: To this one says: going does indeed exist, because of the designation of one who possesses it. Here, the goer is connected with going; and through that connection, he goes. If going did not exist, the designation 'goes' for <s>Devadatta</s> who possesses going would not exist — just as in the absence of a staff, the designation 'one with a staff' would not exist. It is replied: going would exist if the designation 'goes' were [justified]. Since —

children.text: gantā na gacchati tāvadagantā naiva gacchati |
children.translated_text: First, a goer does not go; further, a non-goer does not go at all.
What third [person] other than a goer and a non-goer goes? // 8 //

body.text: iha gacchatīti gantā, sa tāvanna gacchati, yathā ca na gacchati tathottareṇa ślokatrayeṇa pratipādayiṣyati | agantāpi na gacchati | agantā hi nāma yo gamikriyārahitaḥ | gacchatīti ca gamikriyāyogapravṛttaḥ śabdaḥ | yadyasāvagantā, kathaṃ gacchati? atha gacchati, nāsau agantā iti | tadubhayavyatirikto gacchatīti cennaivam | ko hi ganturaganturvinirmuktastṛtīyo 'sti yo gacchatīti kalpyeta? tasmānnāsti gamanam || 8 ||
body.translated_text: Here, a goer is one who goes — he, first, does not go, and how he does not go he will demonstrate with the next three verses. A non-goer also does not go. For a 'non-goer' means one who is devoid of the action of going. And 'goes' is a word that operates through connection with the action of going. If he is a non-goer, how does he go? But if he goes, he is not a non-goer. And [does someone] distinct from both go? Not so, for who is there, a third, freed from goer and non-goer, who could be imagined to go? Therefore going does not exist. // 8 //

body.text: atrāha- nāgantā gacchati nāpyubhayarahitaḥ, kiṃ tarhi gantaiva gacchatīti | etadapyasat kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmāt-
body.translated_text: To this one says: a non-goer does not go, nor does one distinct from both; rather, a goer alone goes. This too is wrong — what is the reason? Because —

children.translated_text: How can 'a goer goes' be possible at all,
when without going a goer is simply not possible? // 9 //

body.text: gantā gacchatītyatra vākye ekaiva gamikriyā, tayā ca gacchatīti vyapadiśyate | ganteti tu vyapadeśe nāsti dvitīyā gamikriyā iti | gamanena vinā gantā, agacchan ganteti yadā na saṃbhavati, tadā gantā gacchatīti na yujyate | kāmaṃ gacchatītyastu, ganteti tu na saṃbhavatīti tadayuktam || 9 ||
body.translated_text: In the statement 'a goer goes,' there is a single action of going, and by that he is designated as 'goes.' But in the designation 'goer,' there is no second action of going. Since 'a goer without going' — a non-going goer — is when that is not possible, then 'a goer goes' is not justified. Granted, let 'goes' stand; but 'goer' is not possible — thus this is wrong. // 9 //

body.text: atha gatiyogātsagatika eva gantā, tathāpi dvitīyagamikriyābhāvadgacchatīti vyapadeśo na syādityāha-
body.translated_text: But if the goer is precisely one who possesses going, and hence inherently a goer — even so, due to the absence of a second action of going, the designation 'goes' would not apply. He says:

children.text: pakṣo gantā gacchatīti yasya tasya prasajyate |
children.translated_text: The thesis 'a goer goes' entails for the one who holds it the consequence:
A goer without going — for one who desires going for the goer. // 10 //

body.text: yasya vādino gamikriyāyogādeva ganteti pakṣaḥ, tasya ganturgamanamicchataḥ sagamanagantṛvyapadeśādgamanena vinā gantā gacchatīti syāt, dvitīyagamikriyābhāvāt | ato gantā gacchatīti na yujyate | gacchatītyetasyārthe ganteti śabdo gamanena vinā gantetyatra vākye || 10 ||
body.translated_text: For the proponent whose thesis is 'goer' precisely because of the connection with the action of going — for him, desiring going for the goer, it follows from the designation 'goer-who-has-going' that 'a goer goes' would be [a goer] without going, since there is no second action of going. Therefore 'a goer goes' is not justified. The word 'goer' in the meaning of 'goes' [is used] in the statement 'a goer without going.' // 10 //

body.text: atha ubhayatrāpi gatiyoga iṣyate gantā gacchatīti, evamapi-
body.translated_text: But if the connection of going is desired in both — 'goer' and 'goes' — even then:

children.text: gamane dve prasajyete gantā yadyuta gacchati |
children.translated_text: Two goings would follow if a goer indeed goes —

children.text: ganteti cocyate yena gantā san yacca gacchati || 11 ||
children.translated_text: that by which he is called a goer, and that which he, being a goer, goes. // 11 //

body.text: yena gamanena yogād gantetyucyate vyapadiśyate tadekaṃ gamanam | gantā bhavan yacca gacchati, yāṃ ca gatikriyāṃ karoti, tadetadgamanadvayaṃ prasaktam | ato gantṛdvayaprasaṅga iti pūrvavad dūṣaṇaṃ vaktavyam | tasmānnāsti gacchatīti vyapadeśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The going by whose connection he is called — designated — 'goer,' that is one going. And the action of going that he, being a goer, performs — this double going follows. Therefore the consequence of two goers, as before, should be stated as the refutation. Therefore the designation 'goes' does not exist.

body.text: atrāha- yadyapyevam, tathāpi devadatto gacchatīti vyapadeśasadbhāvādgamanastīti | naivam | yasmāddevadattāśrayaivaiṣā cintā kimasau gantā san gacchati, uta agantā gacchati, tadvayatirikto veti | sarvathā ca nopapadyata iti yatkiṃcidetat ||
body.translated_text: To this one says: even if so, nevertheless, since the designation '<s>Devadatta</s> goes' does exist, going exists. Not so. Because this very inquiry concerns <s>Devadatta</s> himself — whether he, being a goer, goes, or being a non-goer, goes, or one distinct from both — and in every case it is not possible. Hence this is nothing.

body.text: atrāha- vidyata eva gamanam, tadārambhasadbhāvāt | iha devadattaḥ sthityupamardena gamanamārabhate | na ca avidyamānakūrmaromaprāvārādikamārabhate | ucyate | syādgamanaṃ yadi tadāramme eva syāt | yasmāt-

children.translated_text: In the gone-to, going is not initiated; in the not-yet-gone-to, going is not initiated;
In the being-gone-to, going is not initiated — where then is going initiated? // 12 //

body.translated_text: To this one says: going does indeed exist, because of the existence of its initiation. Here, <s>Devadatta</s>, by the cessation of standing, initiates going. And one does not initiate something non-existent, like a garment made of tortoise-hairs. It is replied: going would [exist] if it were indeed initiated. Since —

body.text: yadi gamanārambho bhavet, tad gate vādhvanyāramyeta, agate vā gamyamāne vā | tatra gate gamanaṃ nārabhyate, taddhi nāma uparatagamikriyam | yadi tatra gamanamārabhyeta, tad gatamityevaṃ na syād atītavartamānayorvirodhāt | agate 'pi gamanaṃ nārabhyate, anāgatavartamānayorvirodhāt | nāpi gamyamāne, tadabhāvāt kriyādvayaprasaṅgāt kartṛdvayaprasaṅgācca | tadevaṃ sarvatra gamanārambhamapaśyannāha- gantumārabhyate kuheti || 12 ||
body.translated_text: If there were a commencement of going, it would be commenced either in what has been gone to, in what has not been gone to, or in what is being gone to. Therein, going is not commenced in what has been gone to, for that is by definition something whose act of going has ceased. If going were commenced there, then 'gone to' would not be so designated, because of the contradiction between past and present. Nor is going commenced in what has not been gone to, because of the contradiction between future and present. Nor in what is being gone to, because of its non-existence, because of the absurd consequence of two acts, and because of the absurd consequence of two agents. Thus, seeing no commencement of going anywhere, he says: 'Where is going commenced?' // 12 //

body.text: yathā ca gamanaṃ na saṃbhavati tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And showing how going is impossible, he says:

children.text: na pūrvaṃ gamanārambhādgamyamānaṃ na vā gatam |
children.translated_text: Prior to the commencement of going, there is neither a 'being gone to' nor a 'gone to' /
in which going could be commenced — how can there be going in the 'not yet gone to'? // 13 //

body.text: iha devadatto yadāvasthita āste, sa tadā gamanaṃ nārabhate | tasya gamanārambhātpūrvaṃ na gamyamānamadhvajātamasti, na ca gataṃ yatra gamanamārabhyeta | tasmād gatagamyamānābhāvādenayorna gamanārambhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Here, when <s>Devadatta</s> is sitting in a stationary position, he does not then commence going. Prior to his commencement of going, there is no path being gone to that has arisen, nor any that has been gone to, in which going could be commenced. Therefore, because of the non-existence of the gone-to and the being-gone-to, there is no commencement of going for him.

body.text: atha syāt- yadyapi gamanārambhātpūrvaṃ na gataṃ na gamyamānaṃ tathāpyagatamasti, tatra gamanārambhaḥ syāditi | ucyate | agate gamanaṃ kutaḥ | anupajātagamikriyamanārabdhagamikriyamagatam | tatra gamanārambha ityasaṃbaddhametadityāha- agate gamanaṃ kutaḥ iti || 13 ||
body.translated_text: Now, one might say: even though prior to the commencement of going there is neither a 'gone to' nor a 'being gone to,' there still exists a 'not yet gone to' — the commencement of going could occur there. The reply is: how can there be going in the 'not yet gone to'? The 'not yet gone to' is that in which the act of going has not yet arisen, in which the act of going has not been commenced. That there should be a commencement of going there is incoherent — hence he says: 'How can there be going in the not yet gone to?' // 13 //

body.text: yadyapi gatāgatagamyamāneṣu gamanārambho nāsti, gatāgatagamyamānāni tu santi | na cāsati gamane etāni yujyanta iti | ucyate | syād gamanaṃ yadyetānyeva syuḥ | sati hi gamikriyāprārambhe yatroparatā gamikriyā tad gatamiti parikalpyeta, yatra vartamānā tad gamyamānam, yatrājātā tadagatamiti | yadā tu gamikriyāprārambha eva nāsti, tadā-
body.translated_text: Even though there is no commencement of going in the gone-to, the not-yet-gone-to, and the being-gone-to, the gone-to, not-yet-gone-to, and being-gone-to themselves do exist. And without going, these are not tenable — thus one might object. The reply is: going would exist if these themselves existed. For when there is a commencement of the act of going, that in which the act of going has ceased could be conceived as the 'gone to,' that in which it is present as the 'being gone to,' and that in which it has not yet arisen as the 'not yet gone to.' But when there is no commencement of the act of going at all, then:

children.text: gataṃ kiṃ gamyamanaṃ kimagataṃ kiṃ vikalpyate |
children.translated_text: What is the 'gone to,' what is the 'being gone to,' what is the 'not yet gone to' that is conceived, /
when the commencement of going itself is in no way perceived? // 14 //

body.text: prārambhe 'nupalabhyamāne kiṃ mithyādhvatrayaṃ parikalpyate, kuto vā tadvayapadeśakāraṇaṃ gamanamityayuktametat || 14 ||
body.translated_text: When the commencement is not apprehended, why is the false triad of paths conceived, and from where would going — the designating cause of that triad — arise? This is untenable. // 14 //

body.text: atrāha- vidyata eva gamanaṃ tatpratipakṣasadbhāvāt | yasya ca pratipakṣo 'sti, tadasti, ālokāndhakāravat pārāvāravat saṃśayaniścayavacca | asti ca gamanasya pratipakṣaḥ sthānamiti | ucyate | syād gamanaṃ yadi tatpratipakṣaḥ sthānaṃ syāt | kathamihedaṃ sthānaṃ ganturagantustadanyasya vā parikalpyeta? sarvathā ca na yujyata ityāha-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: going does indeed exist, because its opposite exists. That which has an opposite exists, like light and darkness, the near shore and the far shore, doubt and certainty. And the opposite of going is standing — so going exists. The reply is: going would exist if its opposite, standing, existed. But how can this standing be conceived — of a goer, of a non-goer, or of someone other than both? In no way is it tenable — hence he says:

children.text: gantā na tiṣṭhati tāvadagantā naiva tiṣṭhati |
children.translated_text: A goer does not stand still; a non-goer certainly does not stand still. /
What third person, other than a goer and a non-goer, stands still? // 15 //

body.text: yathā gantā na tiṣṭhati tathottareṇa ślokenākhyāsyati | agantāpi na tiṣṭhati, sa hi tiṣṭhatyeva, tasya kimaparayā sthityā prayojanam? agantāpi na tiṣṭhati? sa hi tiṣṭhatyeva, tasya
body.translated_text: That a goer does not stand still will be explained in the following verse. A non-goer too does not stand still — for he is already standing; what need has he of another standing? A non-goer does not stand still — for he is already standing; what need has he

body.text: kimaparayā sthityā prayojanam? ekayā sthityā agantā aparayā tiṣṭhatīti sthitidvayaprasaṅgāt sthātṛdvayaprasaṅga iti pūrvavaddoṣaḥ | gantragantṛrahitaścānyo nāsti || 15 ||
body.translated_text: of another standing? Because of the absurd consequence of two standings and the consequent absurd consequence of two standers — this defect is as before. And there is no third person who is neither goer nor non-goer. // 15 //

body.text: atrāha- nāgantā tiṣṭhati, nāpi ganturagantuścānyaḥ, kiṃ tarhi gantaiva tiṣṭhatīti naivam | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: it is not a non-goer who stands still, nor is it someone other than a goer and a non-goer. Rather, it is precisely the goer who stands still. But this is not so. Because:

children.translated_text: How can it ever be tenable that a goer stands still, /
when a goer is never tenable without going? // 16 //

body.text: yadāyaṃ tiṣṭhatītyucyate, tadā sthitivirodhi gamanamasya nāsti, vinā ca gamanaṃ gantṛvyapadeśo nāsti | ato gantā tiṣṭhatīti nopapadyate || 16 ||
body.translated_text: When one is said to be standing still, at that time going — which is contradictory to standing — does not belong to him, and without going there is no designation of 'goer.' Therefore, 'a goer stands still' is not tenable. // 16 //

body.text: atrāha- vidyata eva gamanam, tannivṛttisadbhāvāt | iha gaternivartamānaḥ sthitimārabhate gamanābhāve tu na tato nivarteta | ucyate | syād gamanaṃ yadi tannivṛttireva syāt | [na tvasti] yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: going does indeed exist, because its cessation exists. Here, one who is ceasing from going commences standing; but in the absence of going, he would not cease from it. The reply is: going would exist if its cessation existed. But it does not exist, because:

body.text: na tiṣṭhati gamyamānānna gatānnāgatādapi |
body.translated_text: One does not cease [from going] in the being-gone-to, nor in the gone-to, nor in the not-yet-gone-to. /

body.text: tatra gantā gatādadhvano na nivartate gatyabhāvāt | agatādapi, gatyabhāvādeva | gamyamānādapi na nivartate tadanupalabdheḥ gamikriyābhāvācca | tasmānna gatinivṛttiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the goer does not cease from the gone-to path, because of the absence of going. Nor from the not-yet-gone-to, because of the very absence of going. Nor does he cease from the being-gone-to, because it is unapprehended and because of the absence of the act of going. Therefore, there is no cessation of going.

body.text: atrāha- yadi gamanapratidvandvisthityabhāvādgatirasatī, evaṃ tarhi gamanaprasiddhaye sthiti sādhayāmaḥ, tatsiddhau gamanasiddhiḥ | tasmādvidyata eva sthānaṃ pratidvandvisadbhāvāt, sthiterhi pratidvandvi gamanam, tadasti, tataśca sthitirapi, pratidvandvisadbhāvāt | etadapyayuktam | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: if going is non-existent because standing — its opposite — is non-existent, then let us establish standing in order to establish going; once that is established, going too will be established. Therefore, standing does indeed exist, because its opposite exists — for the opposite of standing is going, and that exists; therefore standing too exists, because its opposite exists. This too is untenable. Because:

body.text: gamanaṃ saṃpravṛttiśca nivṛttiśca gateḥ samā || 17 ||
body.translated_text: Going, commencement, and cessation of going are the same [in their refutation]. // 17 //

body.text: atra hi yadgamanaṃ sthitisiddhaye varṇitaṃ tadgatyā samaṃ gatidūṣaṇena tulyamityarthaḥ | yathā gantā na tiṣṭhati tāvadityādinā gatiprasiddhaye sthiterhetutvenopāttāyā dūṣaṇamuktam, evamihāpi sthitiprasiddhaye gamanasya hetutvenopāttasya sthātā na gacchati tāvadityādinā ślokadvayapāṭhaparivartena dūṣaṇaṃ vaktavyamiti nāsti gamanam, tadabhāvātpratidvandvinī sthitirapīti | evaṃ tāvad gamanaṃ gatyā tulyaṃ pratyākhyeyam ||
body.translated_text: Here, the going that was adduced to establish standing is the same as going — equal to [the refutation of] going — this is the meaning. Just as standing, which was adopted as the reason for establishing going, was refuted by means of 'a goer does not stand still' and so forth, so too here, when going is adopted as the reason for establishing standing, the refutation should be stated by transposing the pair of verses to read 'a stander does not go' and so forth. Thus going does not exist, and because of its non-existence, standing — its opposite — does not exist either. In this way, going is first to be rejected as being the same as going.

body.text: atha syāt- vidyata eva sthānaṃ tadārambhasadbhāvāt | iha gatyupamardena sthānamārabhyate, kathaṃ tanna syāt? ucyate | saṃpravṛttiśca gateḥ samā vācyā | tatra yathā pūrvaṃ gate nārabhyate gantumityādinā gamanārambho niṣiddhaḥ, evamihāpi-
body.translated_text: Now, one might say: standing does indeed exist, because its commencement exists. Here, by the destruction of going, standing is commenced — how could it not exist? The reply is: the commencement too is the same as going. Just as previously the commencement of going was negated by 'going is not commenced in the gone-to' and so forth, so too here:

children.translated_text: Standing is not commenced in the standing; standing is not commenced in the not-standing. /
Standing is not commenced in the being-stood-in — where is standing commenced? //

body.text: ityādinā ślokatrayaparivartena sthānasaṃpravṛttirapi gateḥ samā | sthānanivṛttirapi gatinivṛttyā samā pratyākhyeyā | yathā gatiniṣedhe-
body.translated_text: And so forth — by the transposition of three verses, the commencement of standing too is the same as going. The cessation of standing too should be rejected as being the same as the cessation of going. Just as in the negation of going:

body.text: na tiṣṭhati gamyamānānna gatānnāgatādapi |
body.translated_text: One does not cease [from going] in the being-gone-to, nor in the gone-to, nor in the not-yet-gone-to. /

body.text: iti gaterdūṣaṇamuktam, evaṃ sthitiniṣedhe 'pi
body.translated_text: — this was the refutation of going — so too in the negation of standing:

body.text: na gacchati sthīyamānānna sthitānnāsthitādapi |
body.translated_text: One does not go in the being-stood-in, nor from the stood-in, nor from the not-yet-stood-in. /

body.text: iti gatyā tulyaṃ dūṣaṇamiti nāsti sthitiḥ | tadabhāvātkuto gatipratipakṣasthitisadbhāvavādināṃ gateḥ siddhiriti || 17 ||
body.translated_text: — the refutation is the same as that of going. Thus standing does not exist. In its absence, how can going be established for those who assert the existence of standing as the opposite of going? // 17 //

body.text: api ca | yadi gamanaṃ syāt, gantṛvyatirekeṇa vā syādavyatirekeṇa vā? sarvathā ca vicāryamāṇaṃ na saṃbhavatītyāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, if going existed, it would exist either as identical with the goer or as different from the goer. When examined in every way, it is impossible — hence he says:

children.text: yadeva gamanaṃ gantā sa eveti na yujyate |
children.translated_text: That going is the same as the goer — this is not tenable. /

children.text: anya eva punargantā gateriti na yujyate || 18 ||
children.translated_text: That the goer is different from going — this too is not tenable. // 18 //

body.text: kathaṃ punarna yujyata ityāha-
body.translated_text: How is it not tenable? He says:

children.text: yadeva gamanaṃ gantā sa eva hi bhavedyadi |
children.translated_text: If going were the same as the goer, /

children.text: ekībhāvaḥ prasajyeta kartuḥ karmaṇa eva ca || 19 ||
children.translated_text: then it would follow that the agent and the action are one. // 19 //

body.text: yeyaṃ gamikriyā, sā yadi ganturavyatiriktā nānyā syāt, tadā kartuḥ kriyāyāścaikatvaṃ syāt | tataśca iyaṃ kriyā, ayaṃ kartā, iti viśeṣo na syāt | na ca chidikriyāyāḥ chettuśca ekatvam | ato yadeva gamanaṃ sa eva ganteti na yujyate || 19 ||
body.translated_text: If this act of going were not different from the goer, not other than him, then there would be an identity of agent and action. Then there would be no distinction: 'this is the action, this is the agent.' But there is no identity of the act of cutting and the cutter. Therefore, 'going is the same as the goer' is not tenable. // 19 //

body.text: anyatramapi gantṛgamanayoryathā nāsti tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Demonstrating that even elsewhere the goer and going do not exist, he says:

children.translated_text: If, on the other hand, the goer is conceived as different from going, /
then there would be going without a goer and a goer without going. // 20 //

body.text: yadi hi gantṛgamanayoranyatvaṃ syāt, tadā gamananirapekṣo gantā syāt, gantṛnirapekṣaṃ ca gamanaṃ gṛhyeta pṛthak siddhaṃ ghaṭādiva paṭaḥ | na ca gantuḥ pṛthaksiddhaṃ gamanaṃ gṛhyata iti | anya eva punargantā gateriti na yujyate iti prasādhitametat || 20 ||
body.translated_text: For if goer and going were different, then the goer would exist independently of going, and going would be apprehended independently of the goer, established separately like a pot from a cloth. But going is not apprehended as established separately from the goer. Hence, 'the goer is different from going' — this is not tenable. This has been demonstrated. // 20 //

body.text: tadevam-
body.translated_text: Thus:

children.translated_text: That whose establishment is not possible either through identity or through difference — /

children.text: na vidyate, tayoḥ siddhiḥ kathaṃ nu khalu vidyate || 21 ||
children.translated_text: how indeed can there be establishment of those? // 21 //

body.text: yayorgantṛgamanayoryathoditanyāyena ekībhāvena vā nānābhāvena vā nāsti siddhiḥ, tayoridānīṃ kenānyena prakāreṇa siddhirastu? ata āha- tayoḥ siddhiḥ kathaṃ nu khalu vidyata iti | nāsti gantṛgamanayoḥ siddhirityabhiprāyaḥ || 21 ||
body.translated_text: Of those two — the goer and going — for which, by the reasoning stated above, there is no establishment either through identity or through difference, by what other means can there now be establishment? Therefore he says: 'How indeed can there be establishment of those?' The intended meaning is: there is no establishment of the goer and going. // 21 //

body.text: atrāha- iha devadatto gantā gacchatīti lokaprasiddham | tatra yathā vaktā vācaṃ bhāṣate, kartā kriyāṃ karoti, iti prasiddham, evaṃ yayā gatyā gantetyabhivyajyate tāṃ gacchatīti na yathoktadoṣaḥ | tadapyasat | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: it is well-established in the world that <s>Devadatta</s>, a goer, goes. Just as it is well-established that a speaker speaks a word, a doer does an action — so the goer goes that going by which he is identified as a goer. Thus there is no defect as stated. This too is wrong. Because:

body.text: gatyā yayocyate gantā gatiṃ tāṃ sa na gacchati |
body.translated_text: The goer does not go that going by which he is designated a goer. /

body.text: yayā gatyā devadatto gantetyabhivyajate, sa gantā san tāṃ tāvanna gacchati, na prāpnoti yadi vā na karotītyarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: The going by which <s>Devadatta</s> is identified as a goer — that going, being a goer, he does not go, does not reach, or does not perform — this is the meaning.

body.text: yasmānna gatipūrvo 'sti
body.translated_text: Because there is no one prior to going —

body.text: gateḥ pūrvo gatipūrvaḥ | yadi gantā gateḥ pūrvaṃ siddhaḥ syāt, sa tāṃ gacchet | katham yasmāt-
body.translated_text: 'prior to going' means established before going. If the goer were established prior to going, he could go that going. How [is this impossible]? Because:

body.text: kaścitkiṃciddhi gacchati || 22 ||
body.translated_text: someone goes to something. // 22 //

body.text: kaściddevadattaḥ kiṃcidarthāntarabhūtaṃ grāmaṃ nagaraṃ vā gacchatīti dṛṣṭam | na caivaṃ yayā gatyā gantetyucyate, tasyāḥ pūrvaṃ siddharūpo gatinirapekṣo gantā nāma asti yastāṃ gacchet || 22 ||
body.translated_text: It is observed that some <s>Devadatta</s> goes to some other thing — a village or a city. But it is not the case that prior to the going by which he is designated a goer, there exists a goer of established form, independent of going, who could go that going. // 22 //

body.text: atha manyase- yayā gatyā gantetyabhivyajyate, tāmeva asau na gacchati, kiṃ tahi tato 'nyāmiti | etadapyasat | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Now you may think: the going by which he is identified as a goer — that going he does not go; but rather he goes another going different from that. This too is wrong. Because:

children.text: gatyā yayocyate gantā tato 'nyāṃ sa na gacchati |
children.translated_text: The goer does not go a going other than that by which he is designated a goer, /
because two goings are not tenable, since he goes as a single one. // 23 //

body.text: yayā gatyā gantā abhivyajyate, tato 'nyāmapi sa gantā san na gacchati, gatidvayaprasaṅgāt | yayā gatyā gantā abhivyajyate, gantā san yāṃ cāparāṃ gacchatītyetad gatidvayaṃ prasaktam | na ca ekasmin gantari gatidvayam | ityuktametat | etena vaktā vācaṃ bhāṣate kartā kriyāṃ karoti, iti pratyuktam || 23 ||
body.translated_text: Even a going other than that by which the goer is identified — that too, being a goer, he does not go, because of the absurd consequence of two goings. The going by which the goer is identified, plus the other going which, being a goer, he goes — this makes two goings that are entailed. But there are not two goings in a single goer. This has been stated. By this, the argument that 'a speaker speaks a word' and 'a doer does an action' has also been answered. // 23 //

body.text: tadevam-
body.translated_text: Thus:

children.text: sadbhūto gamanaṃ gantā triprakāraṃ na gacchati |
children.translated_text: An existent goer does not go to a threefold going. /
A non-existent goer too does not go to a threefold going. // 24 //

body.text: gamanaṃ sadasadbhūtastriprakāraṃ na gacchati |
body.translated_text: Nor does an existent-and-non-existent goer go to a threefold going. /

body.text: tatra gamyata iti gamanamihocyate | tatra sadbhūto gantā yo gamikriyāyuktaḥ | asadbhūto gantā yo gamikriyārahitaḥ | sadasadbhūto ya ubhayapakṣīyarūpaḥ | evaṃ gamanamapi triprakāraṃ gamikriyāsaṃbandhena veditavyam | tatra sadbhūto gantā sadbhūtamasadbhūtaṃ sadasadbhūtaṃ triprakāraṃ gamanaṃ na gacchati | etacca karmakārakaparīkṣāyāmākhyāsyate | evamasadbhūto 'pi gantā triprakāraṃ gamanaṃ na gacchati | sadasadbhūto 'pīti tatraiva pratipādayiṣyati | yataścaivaṃ gantṛgantavyagamanāni vicāryamāṇāni na santi,
body.translated_text: Herein, 'the act of going' (<s>gamyate</s>) is what is called going. Therein, an 'existent goer' is one who is conjoined with the act of going. A 'non-existent goer' is one who is devoid of the act of going. An 'existent-and-non-existent goer' is one who partakes of the nature of both positions. Likewise, going too should be understood as threefold through its connection with the act of going. Therein, an existent goer does not go to a threefold going — existent, non-existent, and existent-and-non-existent. This will be explained in the examination of agent and action (<s>karmakārakaparīkṣā</s>). Likewise, a non-existent goer too does not go to a threefold going. And the existent-and-non-existent goer — that too will be demonstrated there. Since, when thus examined, goer, that which is gone to, and going do not exist:

body.text: tasmādgatiśca gantā ca gantavyaṃ ca na vidyate || 25 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, going, the goer, and that which is to be gone to do not exist. // 25 //

body.text: yathoktamāryākṣayamatinirdeśasūtre-
body.translated_text: As stated in the Noble <s>Akṣayamati-nirdeśa-sūtra</s>:

body.text: agatiriti bhadanta śāradvatīputra saṃkarṣaṇapadametat | gatiriti bhadanta śāradvatīputra niṣkarṣaṇapadametat | yatra na saṃkarṣaṇapadaṃ na niṣkarṣaṇapadaṃ tadāryāṇāṃ padam | apadayogena anāgatiragatiścāryāṇāṃ gatiriti ||
body.translated_text: 'Coming' (<s>āgati</s>), Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is a word of attraction. 'Going' (<s>gati</s>), Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, is a word of repulsion. Where there is neither a word of attraction nor a word of repulsion — that is the domain of the noble ones. Through the yoga of non-domain, non-coming and non-going is the way of the noble ones.

body.text: yadi bījamevāṅkure saṃkramati, bījameva tatsyānna yadaṅkuraḥ śāśvatadoṣaprasaṅgaśca | athāṅkuro 'nyata āgacchati, ahetukadoṣaprasaṅgaḥ syāt | na cāhetukasyotpattiḥ kharaviṣāṇasyeva ||
body.translated_text: If the seed itself were to transmigrate into the sprout, the seed itself would be that and not the sprout — and the defect of eternalism would follow. But if the sprout were to come from something altogether different, the defect of causelessness would follow. And there is no arising of something causeless, like a donkey's horn.

body.text: ata evāha bhagavān-
body.translated_text: Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

children.text: bījasya sato yathāṅkuro na ca yo bīju sa caiva aṅkuro |
children.translated_text: Just as, when the seed exists, the sprout [arises] — yet the seed is not itself the sprout, /

children.text: na ca anyu tato na caiva tadevamanuccheda aśāśvata dharmatā || iti ||
children.translated_text: nor is it something different from it, nor is it that very thing — thus the nature of things (<s>dharmatā</s>) is neither annihilation nor permanence. //
From a seal, an impression is seen, yet no transfer from the seal is apprehended. /

children.text: na ca tatra na caiva sānyato evaṃ saṃskāranucchedaśāśvatāḥ || iti ca ||
children.translated_text: It is neither in that [seal] nor from something other than it — thus formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>) are neither annihilation nor permanence. //

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: ādarśapṛṣṭhe tatha tailapātre nirīkṣate nārimukhaṃ alaṃkṛtam |
children.translated_text: On the back of a mirror or in a vessel of oil, one sees a woman's face adorned. /

children.text: so tatra rāgaṃ janayitva bālo pradhāvito kāmi gaveṣamāṇo ||
children.translated_text: That fool, having generated desire there, runs about seeking like a lustful one. //

children.text: mukhasya saṃkrānti yadā na vidyate bimbe mukhaṃ naiva kadāci labhyate |
children.translated_text: When no transfer of the face exists, and the face is never found in the reflection, /

children.text: mūḍho yathā so janayeta rāgaṃ tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān ||
children.translated_text: just as that deluded one generates desire — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like such a simile. //

body.text: tathā [āryasamādhirājasūtre 'pi]-
body.translated_text: Likewise [in the noble <s>Samādhirāja Sūtra</s>]:

children.text: tahi kāli so daśabalo anagho jinu bhāṣate imu samādhivaram |
children.translated_text: At that time, that faultless Victor of tenfold power proclaimed this supreme <s>samādhi</s>: /

children.text: supinopamā bhagavatī sakalā na hi kaści jāyati na co mriyate ||
children.translated_text: all things pertaining to the <s>Bhagavān</s> are like a dream — indeed, no one is born and no one dies. //

children.text: na ca sattvu labhyati na jīvu naro imi dharma phenakadalīsadṛśāḥ |
children.translated_text: No being is found, no life-force, no person — these <s>dharmas</s> are like foam and the plantain tree; /
like an illusion, like lightning in the sky, like the moon in water, like a mirage. //

children.text: na ca asmi loki mṛtu kaści naro paraloka saṃkramati gacchati vā |
children.translated_text: No one dies in this world, and no person transmigrates or goes to another world. /

children.text: na ca karma naśyati kadāci kṛtaṃ phalu deti kṛṣṇa śubha saṃsarato ||
children.translated_text: Yet <s>karma</s> once done is never destroyed — it gives its fruit, dark and bright, to those in <s>saṃsāra</s>. //

children.text: na ca śāśvataṃ na ca uccheda puno na ca karmasaṃcayu na cāpi sthitiḥ |
children.translated_text: Neither permanent nor annihilated; neither accumulation of <s>karma</s> nor even abiding. /

children.text: na ca so 'pi kṛtva punarāspṛśati na ca anyu kṛtva puna vedayate ||
children.translated_text: Nor does he who did it touch [the result] again; nor does one who did not do it experience [it]. //

children.text: na ca saṃkramo na ca punāgamanaṃ na ca sarvamasti na ca nāsti punaḥ |
children.translated_text: Neither transmigration nor coming again; neither everything exists nor does it not exist. /

children.text: na ca dṛṣṭa sthānagatiśuddhiriho na ca satvacāra supaśāntagati ||
children.translated_text: Neither the purification of abiding and going is seen here, nor the conduct of beings, which is utterly peaceful. //

children.text: supinopamaṃ hi tribhavaṃ vaśikaṃ laghu bhagnamanityena māyasamam |
children.translated_text: For the three realms of existence are like a dream, subject to power, easily broken, impermanent, like an illusion. /

children.text: na ca āgataṃ na ca ihopagataṃ śūnyānimitta sada saṃtatiyo ||
children.translated_text: Neither come nor arrived here — the continuities are always empty and signless. //

children.text: anutpāda śānta animittapadaṃ sugatāna gocara jināna guṇā |
children.translated_text: Unarisen, peaceful, the signless state — the domain of the <s>Sugatas</s>, the qualities of the <s>Jinas</s>, /

children.text: bala dhāraṇī daśabalāna balaṃ buddhāna iyaṃ vṛṣabhitā paramā ||
children.translated_text: powers, <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, the strength of the ten-powered ones — this is the supreme bull-like nature of the <s>Buddhas</s>. //
The accumulation of the qualities of supreme bright <s>dharmas</s>, the supreme power of the <s>dhāraṇīs</s> of qualities and knowledge, /
the supreme display of magical powers and transformations, the method of attaining the five supreme <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges). //

body.text: iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus the detailed exposition.

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacitāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau gatāgataparīkṣā nāma dvitīyaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter, 'Examination of Coming and Going' (<s>Gatāgataparīkṣā</s>), in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary composed by the venerable <s>Ācārya Candrakīrti</s>.

body.text: cakṣurādīndriyaparīkṣā tṛtīyaṃ prakaraṇam |
body.translated_text: The third chapter: 'Examination of the Sense Faculties Beginning with the Eye' (<s>Cakṣurādīndriyaparīkṣā</s>).

body.text: atrāha- yadyapi gatiśca gantā ca gantavyaṃ ca na vidyate, tathāpi pravacanasiddhayapekṣayā draṣṭṭadraṣṭavyadarśanādīnāmastitvamāstheyam | tathā cābhidharme ucyate |
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: Even if going, the goer, and that which is gone to do not exist, nevertheless, with respect to what is established in scripture (<s>pravacana</s>), the existence of seeing, that which is to be seen, the act of seeing, and so forth must be maintained. For thus it is said in the <s>Abhidharma</s>:

children.text: darśanaṃ śravaṇaṃ ghrāṇaṃ rasanaṃ sparśanaṃ manaḥ |
children.translated_text: Seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting, touching, and the mind — /
these are the six faculties; their objects are that which is to be seen and so forth. // 1 //

body.text: tasmātsanti darśanādīni svabhāvata iti | ucyate | na santi | iha hi paśyatīti darśanaṃ cakṣuḥ, tasya ca rūpaṃ viṣayatvenopadiśyate || 1 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore seeing and the rest exist by their own nature. We reply: They do not exist. For here, the eye is 'seeing' because it sees (<s>paśyati iti darśanam</s>), and visible form is indicated as its object. // 1 //

body.text: yathā darśanaṃ rūpaṃ na paśyati tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Demonstrating that seeing does not see visible form, he says:

children.text: svamātmānaṃ darśanaṃ hi tattameva na paśyati |
children.translated_text: Seeing itself does not see its own self. /

children.text: na paśyati yadātmānaṃ kathaṃ drakṣyati tatparān || 2 ||
children.translated_text: If it does not see its own self, how will it see others? // 2 //

body.text: tatra tadeva darśanaṃ svātmānaṃ na paśyati svātmani kriyāvirodhāt | tataśca svātmādarśanācchrotrādivannīlādikaṃ na paśyati | tasmānnāsti darśanam || 2 ||
body.translated_text: Therein, seeing itself does not see its own self, because of the contradiction of an action operating on itself. And therefore, since it does not see its own self, it does not see blue and the rest, like the ear and so forth. Therefore seeing does not exist. // 2 //

body.text: yadyapi svātmānaṃ darśanaṃ na paśyati, tathāṣyagnivat parān drakṣyati | tathā hi agniḥparātmānameva dahati na svātmānam, evaṃ darśanaṃ parāneva drakṣyati na svātmānamiti | etadatyayuktam | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Even if seeing does not see its own self, it will still see others, like fire. For fire burns only the other, not its own self — so too, seeing will see only others, not its own self. This is completely wrong, because:

body.text: na paryāpto 'gnidṛṣṭānto darśanasya prasiddhaye |
body.translated_text: The fire-analogy is not adequate for establishing seeing. /

body.text: yo 'yamagnidṛṣṭānto darśanasya prasiddhaye bhavatopanyastaḥ, sa na paryāpto nālaṃ na samartho na yujyata ityarthaḥ | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: This fire-analogy that you have adduced for establishing seeing is not adequate — not sufficient, not competent, it does not work — that is the meaning. Because:

body.text: sadarśanaḥ sa pratyukto gamyamānagatāgataiḥ || 3 ||
body.translated_text: That, together with seeing, has been refuted by the being-gone-to, the gone-to, and the not-yet-gone-to. // 3 //

body.text: saha darśanena vartata iti sadarśanaḥ | yo 'yamagnidṛṣṭānto darśanaprasiddhaye bhavatopanyastaḥ, so 'pi saha darśanena dārṣṭāntikārthena pratyukto dūṣitaḥ | kena punarityāha- gamyamānagatāgataiḥ | yathā gataṃ na gamyate nāgataṃ na gamyamānam, evamagnināpi dagdhaṃ na dahyate nādagdhaṃ dahyata ityādinā samaṃ vācyam | yathā ca na gataṃ nāgataṃ na gamyamānaṃ gamyate, evam-
body.translated_text: 'Together with seeing' (<s>sadarśana</s>) means 'existing with seeing.' This fire-analogy that you have adduced for establishing seeing, that too, together with seeing as the thing illustrated, has been refuted — i.e., invalidated. By what? He says: by the being-gone-to, the gone-to, and the not-yet-gone-to. Just as the gone-to is not being gone to, nor the not-yet-gone-to, nor the being-gone-to — even so, the same must be said of fire: the already-burnt is not being burnt, nor the not-yet-burnt, and so on. And just as the gone-to, not-yet-gone-to, and being-gone-to are not being gone to, similarly:

children.text: na dṛṣṭaṃ dṛśyate tāvadadṛṣṭaṃ naiva dṛśyate |
children.translated_text: The already-seen is not being seen; the not-yet-seen is certainly not being seen; /
and what is freed from the already-seen and not-yet-seen — the being-seen — is not being seen. //

body.text: ityādi vācyam || 3 ||
body.translated_text: And so forth must be stated. // 3 //

body.text: yathā ca gantā na gacchati tāvadityādyuktam, evaṃ na dagdhā dahati tāvadityādi vācyam | evaṃ na draṣṭā paśyati tāvadityādinā agnidṛṣṭāntena saha gamyamānagatāgatairyasmātsamaṃ dūṣaṇam, ato 'gnivad
body.translated_text: And just as it was said 'the goer does not go, first' and so on, similarly 'the burner does not burn, first' and so on must be stated. Thus 'the seer does not see, first' and so on — since the refutation is the same by means of the being-gone-to, the gone-to, and the not-yet-gone-to together with the fire-analogy, therefore the establishment of seeing as being like fire

body.text: darśanasiddhiriti na yujyate | tataśca siddhametat- svātmavad darśanaṃ parānapi na paśyatīti || 3 ||
body.translated_text: is not justified. And therefore it is established that seeing does not see others, just as it does not see its own self. // 3 //

body.text: yadaivaṃ tadā-
body.translated_text: When this is so, then:

children.translated_text: When seeing does not see anything at all, /
how is it justified to say 'seeing sees'? // 4 //

body.text: yadā caivamapaśyanna kiṃciddarśanaṃ bhavati, tadānīmapaśyato darśanātvāyogāt stambhādivat, paśyatīti darśanamiti vyapadeśo na yujyate | yadyapi darśanaśabdādanantaraṃ ślokabandhānurodhena darśana paśyatīti pāṭhaḥ, tathāpi vyākhyānakāle paśyatīti darśanamityevaṃ kathametattu yujyate iti paṭhitavyam || 4 ||
body.translated_text: When seeing, not seeing anything, comes to be, then — since what does not see lacks the nature of seeing, like a pillar and the like — the designation 'seeing sees' is not justified. Even if the reading in the verse-text is 'seeing sees' after the word 'seeing,' nevertheless at the time of commentary it should be read: 'How is it justified to say that this is seeing because it sees?' // 4 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat- iha paśyatīti darśanamityucyamāne darśanakriyayā darśanasvabhāvasya vā cakṣuṣaḥ saṃbandhaḥ parikalpyeta, adarśanasvabhāvasya vā? ubhayathā ca na yujyate ityāha-
body.translated_text: What further is this: when it is said 'seeing is so called because it sees,' is the connection of seeing as an action imagined with the eye — whose nature is seeing — or with what is not of the nature of seeing? In both cases it is not justified. He says:

body.text: paśyati darśanaṃ naiva naiva paśyatyadarśanam |
body.translated_text: Seeing does not see at all; non-seeing does not see at all. /

body.text: darśanasvabhāvasya tāvad dṛśikriyāyuktasya bhūyaḥ paśyatītyādinā saṃbandho nopapadyate dṛśikriyādvayaprasaṅgāt darśanadvayaprasaṅgācca | adarśanamapi na paśyati darśanakriyārahitatvādaṅgūlyagravadityābhiprāyaḥ | yadā
body.translated_text: The connection of seeing — whose nature is already seeing — with a further act of seeing is not established, because the consequence would be a double act of seeing and a double seeing. Non-seeing too does not see, because it is devoid of the action of seeing, like a fingertip — this is the intent. When

body.text: paśyati darśanaṃ naiva naiva paśyatyadarśanam |
body.translated_text: seeing does not see at all, and non-seeing does not see at all, /

body.text: tadā
body.translated_text: then

body.text: darśanaṃ paśyatītyevaṃ kathametattu yujyate ||
body.translated_text: how is it justified to say 'seeing sees'? //

body.text: ityanenaiva saṃbandhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: — the connection is with this very [verse]. //

body.text: ye tu manyante- nirvyāpāraṃ hīdaṃ dharmamātramutpadyamānamutpadyate iti, naiva kiṃcit, kaścidviṣayaṃ paśyati kriyāyā abhāvāt, tasmāddarśanaṃ na paśyatīti siddhametatprasādhyata iti | atrocyate | yadi kriyā vyavahārāṅgabhūtā na syāt, tadā dharmamātramapi na syāt, kriyāvirahitatvāt, khapuṣpavaditi kutaḥ kriyārahitaṃ dharmamātraṃ bhaviṣyati? tasmādyadi vyavahārasatyaṃ dharmamātravat kriyāpyabhyupagamyatām | atha tattvacintā, tadā kriyāvad dharmamātramapi nāstīti bhavatābhyupagamyatām | yathoktaṃ śatake-
body.translated_text: As for those who think: 'This is merely a <s>dharma</s> (phenomenon) devoid of activity, and arising, it simply arises — nothing at all, no one, sees any object, because action does not exist; therefore seeing does not see — this is what is being established' — to this we reply: If the action that is part of conventional usage did not exist, then even the mere <s>dharma</s> would not exist, because it is devoid of action, like a flower in the sky. So how could there be a mere <s>dharma</s> devoid of action? Therefore, if conventional truth is accepted, just as mere <s>dharma</s>, let action too be accepted. But if this is an inquiry into ultimate reality, then let it be accepted by you that, like action, even mere <s>dharma</s> does not exist. As stated in the <s>Śataka</s> (Catuḥśataka):

body.text:
kriyāvān śāśvato nāsti nāsti sarvagate kriyā |
niṣkriyo nāstinā tulyo nairātmyaṃ kiṃ na te priyam || iti |
body.translated_text:
There is no eternal being that possesses action; there is no action in an omnipresent being.
One without action is equal to a non-existent — is selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) not dear to you? //

body.text: tasmānnāyaṃ vidhirbādhakaḥ parasya, nāpyasmākaṃ siddhasādhanadoṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therefore this method does not refute the other, nor does the defect of proving what is already established apply to us.

body.text: atrāha- naiva hi paśyatīti darśanamiti kartṛsādhanamabhyupagamyate, kiṃ tarhi paśyatyanenetī darśanamiti karaṇasādhanam, tataśca uktadoṣāprasaṅgaḥ | yaścānena darśanena karaṇabhūtena paśyati, sa draṣṭā, eṣa ca vidyate vijñānamātmā vā, kartṛsadbhāvācca darśanamapi siddhamiti | ucyate-
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: It is not the agent-derivation 'seeing is that which sees' that is accepted, but rather the instrument-derivation 'seeing is that by which one sees.' Hence the stated defects do not apply. And the seer (<s>draṣṭṛ</s>) who sees by means of this seeing as instrument is either consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) or the self (<s>ātman</s>). And from the existence of the agent, seeing too is established. We reply:

body.text: vyākhyāto darśanenaiva draṣṭā cāpyupagamyatām || 5 ||
body.translated_text: The seer too is to be understood as explained by means of seeing itself. // 5 //

body.text: yathā svamātmānaṃ darśanaṃ hītyādinā dūṣaṇamuktam, evaṃ draṣṭurapi darśanavaddūṣaṇaṃ veditavyam | tadyathā-
body.translated_text: Just as the refutation was stated beginning with 'Seeing does not see its own self,' so too the refutation of the seer should be understood in the same way as for seeing. Namely:

children.translated_text: The seer does not see its own self through seeing. /

children.text: na paśyati yadātmānaṃ kathaṃ drakṣyati tatparān ||
children.translated_text: If it does not see its own self, how will it see others? //

body.text: ityādi vācyam | tasmāddarśanavad draṣṭāpi nāstīti siddham || 5 ||
body.translated_text: And so forth must be stated. Therefore, it is established that, like seeing, the seer too does not exist. // 5 //

body.text: atrāha- vidyata eva draṣṭā tatkarmakaraṇasadbhāvāt | iha yannāsti iti, na tasya karmakaraṇe vidyete tadyathā vandhyāsūnoḥ | asti ca draṣṭuḥ karaṇaṃ darśanaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ ca karma | tasmācchettṛvadvidyamānakarmakaraṇo vidyata eva draṣṭeti | ucyate | naiva hi draṣṭavyadarśane vidyete, tatkuto draṣṭā syāt? draṣṭusāpekṣe hi draṣṭavyadarśane | sa ca nirūttyamāṇaḥ-
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: The seer does indeed exist, because of the existence of its object (<s>karma</s>) and instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>).
