Here, what does not exist has no object or instrument — for example, the son of a barren woman. But the seer has an instrument, namely seeing, and an object, namely that which is to be seen. Therefore, just as one who cuts, who possesses an existing object and instrument, exists — so too the seer exists. We reply: Indeed, neither the object (that which is to be seen) nor the instrument (seeing) exists; so whence would a seer be? For that which is to be seen and seeing depend on the seer. And he, when examined:

body.text: tiraskṛtya draṣṭā nāstyatiraskṛtya ca darśanam |
body.translated_text: Setting aside seeing, the seer does not exist; and without setting aside seeing [the seer does not exist either]. /

body.text: iha draṣṭā nāma yadi kaścitsyāt, sa darśanasāpekṣo vā syānnirapekṣo vā | tatra yadi darśanasāpekṣo 'tiraskṛtya darśanamiṣyate, tadā siddhasya vā darśanāpekṣā syādasiddhasya vā | tatra siddho draṣṭā na hi darśanamapekṣate | kiṃ siddhasya sato draṣṭuḥ punardarśanāpek ṣā kuryāt? na hi siddhaṃ punarapi sādhyata iti | athāsiddho 'pekṣeta, asiddhatvādvandhyāsutavaddarśanaṃ nāpekṣate | evaṃ tāvadatiraskṛtya darśanamapekṣya draṣṭā nāsti | tiraskṛtyāpi, darśananirapekṣatvāt ityuktaṃ prāk | tadevaṃ tiraskṛtyātiraskṛtya vā darśanaṃ yadā draṣṭā nāsti, tadā-
body.translated_text: Here, if there were some entity called 'seer,' it would either depend on seeing or not. If it depends on seeing — if it is posited without setting aside seeing — then the dependence would be of one already established or of one not yet established. A seer already established does not depend on seeing — what would the further dependence on seeing accomplish for an already established seer? For what is already established is not established again. But if not yet established, then, being unestablished, like the son of a barren woman, it does not depend on seeing. Thus, without setting aside seeing — that is, depending on it — the seer does not exist. And even setting it aside, since it would be independent of seeing — as was stated before. Thus, whether setting aside or not setting aside seeing, when the seer does not exist, then:

body.text: draṣṭavyaṃ darśanaṃ caiva draṣṭaryasati te kutaḥ || 6 ||
body.translated_text: When the seer does not exist, whence to you are the object-to-be-seen and seeing? // 6 //

body.text: draṣṭaryasati nirhetuke draṣṭavyadarśane na saṃbhavataḥ iti kutastatsadbhāvād draṣṭā prasetsyati?
body.translated_text: When the seer does not exist, being without a cause, the object-to-be-seen and seeing are not possible. So from the existence of what will the seer be inferred?

body.text: atrāha- vidyete eva draṣṭavyadarśane, tatkāryasadbhāvāt | tatra-
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: The object-to-be-seen and seeing do indeed exist, because of the existence of their effect. Therein:

children.translated_text: Just as the arising of a son is said to be in dependence on a mother and father, /
even so the arising of consciousness is said to be in dependence on the eye and visible forms. // 7 //

body.text: iti draṣṭavyaṃ darśanaṃ ca pratītya vijñānamutpadyate | trayāṇāṃ saṃnipātātsāsravasparśaḥ, sparśasahajā vedanā, tatpratyayā tṛṣṇeti | evaṃ catvāryapi bhavāṅgāni draṣṭavyadarśanahetukāni vidyante | tasmātkāryasadbhāvād draṣṭavyadarśane vidyete iti | 7 ||
body.translated_text: Consciousness arises in dependence on the object-to-be-seen and seeing. From the conjunction of the three there is contact with defilements (<s>sāsravasparśa</s>); feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) is co-arisen with contact; craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) is conditioned by that. Thus all four limbs of existence arise from the object-to-be-seen and seeing as causes. Therefore, from the existence of the effect, the object-to-be-seen and seeing exist. // 7 //

body.text: ucyate- syātāmete, yadi vijñānādicatuṣṭayameva syāt | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: We reply: These would exist if the fourfold group of consciousness and the rest existed. Since:

body.text:
draṣṭavyadarśanābhāvādvijñānādicatuṣṭayam |
nāstīti
body.translated_text:
Due to the non-existence of the object-to-be-seen and seeing, the fourfold group of consciousness and the rest
does not exist —

body.text: iha draṣṭurabhāvād draṣṭavyadarśane api na sta ityuktam | ataḥ kuto vijñānādicatuṣṭayaṃ vijñānasparśavedanātṛṣṇākhyam? tasmānna santi vijñānādīni ||
body.translated_text: Here, since the seer does not exist, it has been said that the seeing of the object of seeing also does not exist. Therefore, whence the fourfold set beginning with consciousness — namely, consciousness, contact, feeling, and craving? Therefore, consciousness and the rest do not exist.

body.text: atrāha- santyevatāni tatkāryasadbhāvāt | iha tṛṣṇāpratyayamupādānamityādinā upādānabhavajātijarāmaraṇādikaṃ vijñānādicatuṣṭayādutpadyate, tasmātsanti vijñānādīni tatkāryasadbhāvāt |
body.translated_text: Here one says: they do indeed exist, because of the existence of their effects. Here, '<s>upādāna</s> (grasping) arises from <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) as condition' and so forth — grasping, becoming, birth, old age, death, and so forth arise from the fourfold set beginning with consciousness. Therefore, consciousness and the rest exist, because their effects exist.

body.text: ucyate | syurupādānādīni yadi vijñānādicatuṣṭayameva syāt | yadā tu draṣṭavyadarśanābhāvādvijñānādicatuṣṭayaṃ naivāsti, tadā-
body.translated_text: It is replied: Grasping and the rest would exist if the fourfold set beginning with consciousness existed. But since, due to the non-existence of the object of seeing and the seeing, the fourfold set beginning with consciousness simply does not exist, then —

body.text: upādānādīni bhaviṣyanti punaḥ katham || 8 ||
body.translated_text: How will grasping and the rest come to be? // 8 //

body.text: na santyupādānādīnītyarthaḥ || 8 ||
body.translated_text: The meaning is: grasping and the rest do not exist. // 8 //

body.text: idānīṃ darśanavaccheṣāyatanavyākhyānātideśārthamāha-
body.translated_text: Now, in order to extend the explanation to the remaining sense-bases, just as with seeing, he says —

children.text: vyākhyātaṃ śravaṇaṃ ghrāṇaṃ rasanaṃ sparśanaṃ manaḥ |
children.translated_text: Hearing, smelling, tasting, touching, and the mind /
have been explained. One should understand the hearer, the object of hearing, and so forth, just as with seeing. // 9 //

body.text: iti ||
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: uktaṃ hi bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: For the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said —

children.text: na cakṣuḥ prekṣate rūpaṃ mano dharmānna vetti ca |
children.translated_text: The eye does not see form, nor does the mind know <s>dharmas</s>. /

children.text: etatta paramaṃ satyaṃ yatra loko na gāhate ||
children.translated_text: This is the supreme truth which the world does not grasp. //
The Guide illuminates seeing as arising from the assemblage [of conditions]; /
the wise one declared that to be the domain of figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>), not of the ultimate. //

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise —

children.translated_text: Dependent on the eye and on form, eye-consciousness arises here; /

children.text: no cakṣuṣi rūpa niśritaṃ rūpasaṃkrānti na caiva cakṣuṣi ||
children.translated_text: form is not inherent in the eye, nor does form transfer to the eye. //
These <s>dharmas</s> are selfless and impure; yet self and purity are imagined in them. /
That which is falsely imagined through perversion — from that too eye-consciousness arises. //
The yogin sees the arising and cessation of consciousness, the origination and decay of consciousness — /

children.text: na kahiṃci gataṃ na cāgataṃ śūnya māyopama yogi paśyati ||
children.translated_text: gone nowhere and come from nowhere — empty, like an illusion. //

body.text: tathācāryopālipṛcchāyām-
body.translated_text: And likewise in the <s>Ācārya Upāliparipṛcchā</s> —

children.text: sarva sayogi tu paśyati cakṣustatra na paśyati pratyayahīnam |
children.translated_text: Everything is seen when in conjunction; the eye does not see when devoid of conditions. /

children.text: naiva ca cakṣu prapaśyati rūpaṃ tena sayogaviyogavikalpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The eye itself does not see form; therefore [arises] the conceptualization of conjunction and disjunction. //
Dependent on light, the eye sees form — delightful, variegated, and excellent. /

children.text: yena ca yogasamāśritacakṣustena na paśyati cakṣu kadāci ||
children.translated_text: But by that very conjunction on which the eye depends, the eye never sees. //

children.text: yo 'pi ca śrūyati śabdu manojñaḥ so 'pi ca nāntari jātu praviṣṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: And that pleasant sound which is heard — it too has never entered within. /

children.text: saṃkramaṇaṃ na ca labhyati tasya kalpavaśāttu samucchritu śabdaḥ || iti ||
children.translated_text: Its transference is not found; rather, through the power of conceptual construction, sound arises. //

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise —

children.text: gītaṃ na nṛtyamapi vādyarutaṃ na grāhyaṃ svapnopamā hi ratayo 'budhamohanāśca |
children.translated_text: Song, dance, and the sound of music are not to be grasped — for delights are like dreams, and they are the delusions of the foolish. /

children.text: saṃkalpalālasa gatā abudhā 'tra nāśaṃ kiṃ kleśadāsa iva bālajano bhavāmi || iti ||
children.translated_text: Carried away by the desire of conceptual constructions, the foolish perish here — shall I become like a childish person, a slave to the afflictions? //

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacitāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau cakṣurādīndriyaparīkṣā nāma tṛtīyaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter, 'The Examination of the Eye and Other Sense-Faculties,' in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary composed by <s>Ācārya Candrakīrtipāda</s>.

body.text: skandhaparīkṣā caturtha prakaraṇam |
body.translated_text: The Examination of the Aggregates (<s>Skandhaparīkṣā</s>), the Fourth Chapter.

body.text: atrāha- yadyevaṃ cakṣurādīnīndriyāṇi na santi, na skandhāḥ, apratiṣedhāt tadantargatāni cendriyāṇi, atastānyapi bhaviṣyantīti | ucyate | syureva, yadi skandhāḥ syuḥ tatra rūpaskandhamadhikṛtyāha-
body.translated_text: Here one says: Even if the sense-faculties such as the eye do not exist, the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) are not [thereby] negated. The sense-faculties, being included within them, will also exist [if the aggregates exist]. It is replied: They would exist indeed, if the aggregates existed. Regarding the form-aggregate, he says —

children.translated_text: Form is not found apart from the cause of form; /
nor is the cause of form seen apart from form. // 1 //

body.text: tatra rūpaṃ bhautikam | tasya kāraṇaṃ catvāri mahābhūtāni | tadvayatiriktaṃ pṛthagbhūtaṃ rūpaṃ rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyākhyaṃ nopalabhyate ghaṭādiva paṭaḥ | rūpeṇāpi na nirmuktaṃ rūpātpṛthagbhūtaṃ rūpakāraṇamupalabhyate || 1 ||
body.translated_text: Here, 'form' means derivative form (<s>bhautika</s>). Its cause is the four great elements (<s>mahābhūta</s>). Form — called visible form, sound, smell, taste, and tangible — existing separately and apart from these, is not found — just as cloth is [not found] apart from a pot. Nor is the cause of form — existing separately and apart from form — found. // 1 //

body.text: tadetatpratijñādvayaṃ prasādhayitukāma āha-
body.translated_text: Wishing to establish this pair of propositions, he says —

children.translated_text: If form [were to exist] apart from the cause of form, form without a cause would follow; /
but nothing whatsoever exists anywhere without a cause. // 2 //

body.text: yathā ghaṭādarthāntarabhūtaḥ paṭo na ghaṭahetukaḥ, evaṃ rūpakāraṇacaturmahābhūtavyatirikta bhautikaṃ rūpamiṣyamāṇaṃ na bhūtahetukaṃ syāt | na cāstyarthaḥ kaścidāhetukaḥ kvacit | tasmādahetukatvadoṣaprasaṅgānna rūpakāraṇanirmuktaṃ rūpamabhyupetavyamiti || 2 ||
body.translated_text: Just as cloth, being a different entity from a pot, is not caused by the pot, so too derivative form, if imagined as distinct from the four great elements that are the cause of form, would not be caused by the elements. But nothing whatsoever exists anywhere without a cause. Therefore, because of the consequence of the fault of being without a cause, form apart from the cause of form should not be maintained. // 2 //

body.text:
idānīṃ rūpeṇāpi vinirmuktaṃ yathā rūpakāraṇaṃ nāsti, tathā pratipādayannāha-
rūpeṇa tu vinirmuktaṃ yadi syādrūpakāraṇam |
body.translated_text:
Now, in order to demonstrate that the cause of form likewise does not exist apart from form, he says —
'But if the cause of form were to exist apart from form' —

body.text: yadi kāryarūpavinirmuktaṃ rūpakāraṇaṃ syāt, tadā, yathā ghaṭātkuṇḍaṃ pṛthaksiddhaṃ ghaṭahetukaṃ na bhavati, evaṃ kāryātpṛthagbhūtaṃ kāraṇamiṣyamāṇam-
body.translated_text: If the cause of form were to exist apart from effect-form, then, just as a water-pot that is established separately from a pot is not caused by the pot, so too the cause, imagined as separate from the effect, would be —

body.text: akāryakaṃ kāraṇaṃ syāt
body.translated_text: a cause without an effect.

body.text: nirhetukaṃ syāt | kāraṇasya hi kāraṇatve kāryapravṛttirhetuḥ, kāryanirapekṣācca kāraṇāt pṛthaksiddhā nāsti kāryapravṛttiḥ | yaccākāryakaṃ kāraṇaṃ tannirhetukatvānnaroragaturagaviṣāṇavannāstyevetyāha-
body.translated_text: It would be without a basis. For the activity of the effect is the reason for the cause's being a cause; and from a cause that is separate and independent of the effect, there is no activity of the effect. And a cause without an effect, being without a basis, does not exist at all — like the horn of a man, a snake, or a horse. He says —

body.text: nāstyakāryaṃ ca kāraṇam || 3 ||
body.translated_text: And there is no cause without an effect. // 3 //
Thus. // 3 //

body.text: atha cedaṃ rūpasya kāraṇamiṣyamāṇaṃ sati vā rūpe kāraṇatveneṣyate 'sati vā? ubhayathā ca nopapadyata ityāha-
body.translated_text: Now, is this imagined cause of form posited as a cause when form exists or when it does not exist? And in either case it is untenable — he says —

children.translated_text: When form already exists, a cause of form is not tenable; /
when form does not exist, a cause of form is not tenable. // 4 //

body.text: sati vā saṃvidyamāne rūpe kiṃ rūpakāraṇena prayojanam? asati asaṃvidyamāne rūpe kiṃ kiṃ rūpakāraṇena prayojanam, kasya vā tatkāraṇaṃ parikalpyate? tasmādasatyapi rūpe rūpakāraṇaṃ nopapadyate || 4 ||
body.translated_text: When form exists — is present — what purpose is served by a cause of form? When form does not exist — is not present — what purpose is served by a cause of form, and of what would that be the cause? Therefore, even when form does not exist, a cause of form is not tenable. // 4 //

body.text: atha syāt- yadyapi evaṃ rūpakāraṇaṃ na saṃbhavati, tathāpi kāryaṃ rūpaṃ saṃvidyate, sadbhāvāt kāraṇamapi bhaviṣyatīti | syādevam, yadi kāryaṃ rūpaṃ syāt | na tvasti | ysmāt-
body.translated_text: If one were to say: 'Even though the cause of form is thus impossible, nevertheless the effect-form exists; since it exists, the cause too will exist' — it would be so, if the effect-form existed. But it does not. Because —

body.text: niṣkāraṇaṃ punā rūpaṃ naiva naivopapadyate |
body.translated_text: And form without a cause is simply, simply not tenable. /

body.text: rūpakāraṇaṃ yathā nāsti tathoktam | asati kāraṇe kuto nirhetukaṃ kāryaṃ rūpaṃ bhavet? naiva naivetyanena sāvadhāraṇena pratiṣedhadvayena ahetukatvādasyātyaniṣṭatāṃ darśayati | yataścaivaṃ rūpaṃ sarvathā vicāryamāṇaṃ na saṃbhavati,
body.translated_text: It has been stated how the cause of form does not exist. In the absence of a cause, whence would causeless effect-form come to be? By the emphatic double negation 'simply, simply not,' he shows the extreme undesirability [of this position] because of its being without a cause. And since form, when examined in every way, is thus impossible —

body.text: tasmāt
body.translated_text: therefore

body.text: tattvadarśī yogī
body.translated_text: the yogin who sees reality

body.text: rūpagatān kāṃścinna vikalpān vikalpayet || 5 ||
body.translated_text: should not fabricate any conceptualizations regarding form. // 5 //

body.text: sapratighāpratighasanidarśanānidarśanātītānāgatanīlapītādivikalpān rūpālambanānna kāṃścitparikalpayitumarhatītyarthaḥ || 5 ||
body.translated_text: The meaning is: one ought not to fabricate any conceptualizations based on form — such as resistant and non-resistant, visible and invisible, past and future, blue and yellow, and so forth. // 5 //

body.text: api ca | idaṃ rūpakāraṇamiṣyamāṇaṃ sadṛśaṃ kāryaṃ niṣpādayedasadṛśaṃ vā? ubhayathā ca nopapadyate ityāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, does this imagined cause of form produce an effect that is similar to it or dissimilar? And in either case it is untenable — he says —

children.translated_text: It is not tenable that the effect is similar to the cause; /
it is not tenable that the effect is dissimilar to the cause. // 6 //

body.text: tatra rūpakāraṇaṃ kaṭhinadravoṣṇataralasvabhāvam | bhautikaṃ tu cakṣurādhyātmikaṃ pañcacakṣurvijñānādyāśrayakarūpaprasādātmakam | bāhyaṃ tu rūpādyāyatanādikaṃ cakṣurvijñānādigrāhyalakṣaṇaṃ na mahābhūtasvabhāvamiti | ato bhinnalakṣaṇatvānnirvāṇavatkāryakāraṇayoḥ sādṛśyameva nāstīti
body.translated_text: The cause of form has the nature of hard, fluid, hot, and mobile [i.e., earth, water, fire, and air]. But derivative form — the internal [form] such as the eye, which is a subtle material faculty serving as the support for the five types of eye-consciousness and so forth — and the external [form] such as the visible-form sense-base, having the characteristic of being graspable by eye-consciousness and so forth — is not of the nature of the great elements. Therefore, since their characteristics are different, there is no similarity between cause and effect — as with <s>nirvāṇa</s> — and thus

body.text: na kāraṇasya sadṛśaṃ kāryamityupapadyate |
body.translated_text: it is not tenable that the effect is similar to the cause. /

body.text:
na cāpi sadṛśānāṃ śālibījādīnāṃ parasparakāryakāraṇabhāvo dṛṣṭaḥ, ityataḥ
na kāraṇasya sadṛśaṃ kāryamityupapadyate |
body.translated_text:
Nor has a cause-and-effect relation been observed among things that are similar, such as rice-grains; therefore —
it is not tenable that the effect is similar to the cause. /

body.text: tathāpi
body.translated_text: Even so,

body.text: na kāraṇasyāsadṛśaṃ kāryamityupapadyate |
body.translated_text: it is not tenable that the effect is dissimilar to the cause. /

body.text: bhinnalakṣaṇatvānnirvāṇavadevetyabhiprāyaḥ || 6 ||
body.translated_text: The intent is: because their characteristics are different — as with <s>nirvāṇa</s> itself. // 6 //

body.text: yathā cedaṃ rūpaṃ vicāryamāṇaṃ sarvathā nopapadyate, evaṃ vedanādayo 'pi, ityatidiśannāha-
body.translated_text: Just as this form, when examined, is in every way untenable — so too feeling and the rest. Extending [the analysis], he says —

children.translated_text: Of feeling, <s>citta</s> (mind), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), and the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) — /
of all entities whatsoever, the procedure is the same as with form. // 7 //

body.text: vedanādikamapi sarvaṃ rūpavicāreṇaiva samaṃ yojyam | yathaiva hyekasya dharmasya śūnyatā pratipādayitumiṣṭā mādhyamikena, tathaiva sarvadharmāṇāmapīti || 7 ||
body.translated_text: All of feeling and the rest too should be construed by the very same examination as that of form. For just as the <s>Mādhyamika</s> wishes to demonstrate the emptiness of a single <s>dharma</s>, so too of all <s>dharmas</s>. // 7 //

body.text: ataḥ-
body.translated_text: Therefore —

children.text: vigrahe yaḥ parīhāraṃ kṛte śūnyatayā vadet |
children.translated_text: He who, regarding an objection, would reply by means of emptiness — /
for him, everything that is unanswered becomes equal to the thesis to be proved. // 8 //

body.text: tatra parapakṣadūṣaṇaṃ vigrahaḥ | śūnyatayā kāraṇabhūtayā rūpaṃ niḥsvabhāvamityevaṃ sasvabhāvavāde pratiṣiddhe, yadi paraḥ parihāraṃ brūyāt- vedanādayastāvatsanti, tadvadrūpamapyastīti, tadetatsarvaṃ tasyāparihṛtaṃ bhavati | yasmādvedanādīnāmapi sadbhāvaḥ sādhyena rūpasadbhāvena samo veditavyaḥ | yathā rūpaṃ svakāraṇāttattvānyatvena vicāryamāṇamasat, evaṃ sparśapratyayā vedanā, vijñānasahajā saṃjñā, avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ, saṃskārapratyayaṃ ca vijñānaṃ svakāraṇātsparśādeḥ tattvānyatvādinā vicāryamāṇaṃ nāstīti sarvametatsādhyasamaṃ bhavati | yathā vedanādayaḥ sādhyasamāḥ, evaṃ lakṣyalakṣaṇakāryakāraṇāvayavyavayavādayo 'pi sarva eva padārthāḥ rūpeṇa sādhyena samā iti kutaḥ parasya parīhāra saṃbhavet? sarvaṃ vacanamasya sādhyasamaṃ bhavatīti sarvatra śāstre parīhāreṇa sādhyasamatvaṃ mādhyamikenā grāhaṇīyamityācāryaḥ śikṣayati || 8 ||
body.translated_text: Here, 'objection' (<s>vigraha</s>) is the refutation of the opponent's position. When, through emptiness as the cause, it has been established that 'form is without intrinsic nature,' and thus the doctrine of intrinsic nature has been refuted — if the opponent were to reply: 'But feeling and the rest exist; therefore form too exists' — all of that remains unanswered for him. Because the existence of feeling and the rest too should be understood as equal to the thesis to be proved — namely, the existence of form. Just as form, when examined through identity and difference from its own cause, is non-existent — so too feeling conditioned by contact, perception co-arising with consciousness, formations conditioned by ignorance, and consciousness conditioned by formations — when examined through identity, difference, and so forth from their own causes such as contact — do not exist. Thus all of this becomes equal to the thesis to be proved. Just as feeling and the rest are equal to the thesis, so too the defined and the defining characteristic, cause and effect, whole and parts, and so forth — all entities whatsoever are equal to form, the thesis to be proved. Whence then could the opponent's reply be possible? Every statement of his becomes equal to the thesis to be proved. Therefore, the <s>Ācārya</s> teaches that throughout the entire treatise, the <s>Mādhyamika</s> should counter the reply with [the charge of] equality with the thesis to be proved. // 8 //

body.text: yathā ca parapakṣadūṣaṇe vihi 'toyaṃ vidhiḥ, evaṃ vyākhyānakāle 'pītyāha-
body.translated_text: And just as this is the procedure in refuting the opponent's position, so too at the time of exposition — he says —

children.text: vyākhyāne ya upālambhaṃ kṛte śūnyatayā vadet |
children.translated_text: He who, regarding an exposition, would raise an objection by means of emptiness — /
for him, everything that is unobjected becomes equal to the thesis to be proved. // 9 //

body.text: vyākhyānakāle 'pi yaḥ śiṣyadeśīyaścodyamupālambhaṃ kuryāt, tasyāpi taccodyamupālambhākhyaṃ pūrvavatsādhyasamaṃ veditavyam | yathoktam-
body.translated_text: Even at the time of exposition, if a student or disputant were to raise a charge — an objection — for him too, that charge, called 'objection,' should be understood as equal to the thesis to be proved, just as before. As it is said —

body.text:
bhāvasyaikasya yo draṣṭā draṣṭā sarvasya sa smṛtaḥ |
ekasya śūnyatā yaiva saiva sarvasya śūnyatā || iti |
body.translated_text:
He who sees the emptiness of one entity is declared to be the seer of all. /
The emptiness of one is the very emptiness of all. //

body.text: āryagaganagañjasamādhisūtre 'pi-
body.translated_text: And in the noble <s>Gaganagañjasamādhisūtra</s> too —

children.text: ekena dharmeṇa tu sarvadharmān anugacchate māyamarīcisādṛśān |
children.translated_text: By one <s>dharma</s> one follows all <s>dharmas</s>, which are like illusions and mirages, /

children.text: agrāhyatucchānalikānaśāśvatān so bodhimaṇḍaṃ nacireṇa gacchati || iti ||
children.translated_text: ungraspable, trifling, hollow, and impermanent — such a one quickly reaches the seat of awakening. //

body.text: samādhirājasūtre 'pi-
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Samādhirājasūtra</s> too —

children.text: yatha ñāta tayātmasaṃjña tathaiva sarvatra peṣitā buddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: As one has understood the notion of self, so let the intelligence be applied everywhere. /

children.text: sarve ca tatsvabhāvā dharma viśuddhā gaganakalpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> are of that same nature — purified, like space. //

body.text:
ekena sarvaṃ jānāti sarvamekena paśyati |
kiyadbahu pi bhāvetvā na tasyotpadyate madaḥ || iti |
body.translated_text:
By one, one knows all; by one, one sees all. /
No matter how much one reflects, no pride arises in such a one. //

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacittāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau skandhaparīkṣā nāma caturtha prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter, 'The Examination of the Aggregates,' in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary composed by <s>Ācārya Candrakīrtipāda</s>.

body.text: dhātuparīkṣā pañcamaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: The Examination of the Elements (<s>Dhātuparīkṣā</s>), the Fifth Chapter.

body.text: atrāha- dhātavaḥ santi pratiṣedhābhāvāt | uktaṃ ca bhagavatā- ṣaḍdhāturayaṃ mahārāja puruṣapudgala ityādi | tataśca pravacanapāṭhāddhātuvatskandhāyatanānyeva santīti | ucyate | syuḥ skandhāyatanāni yadi dhātava eva syuḥ | kathamityāha-
body.translated_text: Here one says: The elements (<s>dhātus</s>) exist, because they have not been negated. And the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said: 'This person-individual (<s>puruṣa-pudgala</s>), great king, consists of six elements' — and so forth. And therefore, from the scriptural passage, just as the elements [exist], so too the aggregates and sense-bases exist. It is replied: The aggregates and sense-bases would exist if the elements existed. How so? He says —

children.translated_text: Space does not exist at all prior to the defining characteristic of space. /
It would follow that it would be without a defining characteristic, if it existed prior to the defining characteristic. // 1 //

body.text: tatra ṣaḍ dhātava uktāḥ pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśavijñānākhyāḥ | tatrākāśamadhikṛtyocyate dūṣaṇaṃ svarūpanirūpaṇāt | ihākāśasyānāvaraṇaṃ lakṣaṇamucyate | yad yasmātpūrvamākāśamanāvaraṇa lakṣaṇāllakṣyaṃ syāt, tatra lakṣaṇapravartanādanāvaraṇalakṣaṇātpūrvaṃ nākāśaṃ lakṣyarūpamiti | yadā caivam-
tathāhi alakṣaṇaṃ pravartatām | tadabhāve khapuṣpavannāstyākāśamityāha-
alakṣaṇo na kaścicca bhāvaḥ saṃvidyate kvacit |
iti | atrāha- lakṣaṇapravṛttirlakṣye bhavet, tatsadbhāvāllakṣyamapyastīti | etadapi nāsti | yasmāt-
asatyalakṣaṇe bhāve kramatāṃ kuha lakṣaṇam || 2 ||
lakṣaṇātpūrvamalakṣaṇo bhāvo nāstītyuktam | tataśca asati asaṃvidyamāne alakṣaṇe lakṣaṇarahite bhāve kuha idānīṃ lakṣaṇaṃpravartatāmiti nāsti lakṣaṇapravṛttiḥ || 2 ||
api ca | idaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ pravartamānaṃ salakṣaṇe vā pravarteta alakṣaṇe vā? ubhayathā ca nopapadyata ityāha-

tatra alakṣaṇe kharaviṣāṇavanna lakṣaṇapravṛttiḥ | salakṣaṇe 'pi bhāve na lakṣaṇapravṛttirūpapadyate prayojanābhāvāt | kiṃ hi lakṣaṇavataḥ prasiddhasya bhāvasya punarlakṣaṇakṛtyaṃ syāt? ityanavasthā atiprasaṅgaścaivaṃ syāt | na hyasau kadācinna salakṣaṇaḥ syāditi sadaiva lakṣaṇapravṛttiḥ prasajyeta | na caitadiṣṭam | tasmātsalakṣaṇe 'pi bhāve na lakṣaṇapravṛttiparupadyate prayojanābhāvāt | tatraivaṃ syāt- salakṣaṇālakṣaṇābhyāmanyatra pravartiṣyata iti | ucyate-
salakṣaṇālakṣaṇābhyāṃ nāpyanyatra pravartate |

kiṃ kāraṇam? asadbhāvāt | yadi salakṣaṇo nālakṣaṇaḥ, athālakṣaṇo na salakṣaṇaḥ | ataḥ salakṣaṇaśca alakṣaṇaśceti vipratiṣiddhametat | na ca vipratiṣiddhaṃ saṃbhavati | tasmādasaṃbhavādeva salakṣaṇe cālakṣaṇe ca lakṣaṇapravṛttirnopapadyate iti || 3 ||
athāpi syāt- yadyapi na lakṣaṇapravṛttiḥ, tathāpi lakṣyamastīti etadapi nāsti | yasmāt-
lakṣaṇāsaṃpravṛttau ca na lakṣyamupapadyate |
yadā lakṣaṇapravṛttireva nāsti tadā kathaṃ lakṣyaṃ syāt? naiva saṃbhavatītyabhiprāyaḥ |
atrāha- lakṣaṇapravṛttistvayā niṣiddhā na tu lakṣaṇam, tataśca vidyate lakṣyam, lakṣaṇa sadbhāvāt | ucyate-
lakṣyasyānupapattau ca lakṣaṇasyāpyasaṃbhavaḥ || 4 ||
lakṣaṇāsaṃpravṛttau ca na lakṣyamupapadyate iti pratipāditam | tadā
lakṣyasyānupapattau ca lakṣaṇasyāpyasaṃbhavaḥ |
nirāśrayatvāt || 4 ||
yadā caivaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ nāsti, tadā lakṣaṇasadbhāvādvidyate lakṣyamiti yaduktaṃ tanna yataścaitadevam-
tasmānna vidyate lakṣyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ naiva vidyate |
iti nigamanam ||
atrāha- yadyāpi lakṣyalakṣaṇe na staḥ, tathā (pyā)kāśamasti, bhāvarūpaṃ ca bhavadākāśa lakṣyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vā syāt | tasmāllakṣyalakṣaṇe api ṣṭa iti | etadapyayuktamityāha-
lakṣyalakṣaṇanirmukto naiva bhāvo 'pi vidyate || 5 ||
lakṣyalakṣaṇe yathā na staḥ, tathoktaṃ prāk | yadā anayorabhāvaḥ, tadā lakṣyalakṣaṇarahitatvādākāśakusumavannāstyākāśam || 5 ||
yadyākāśaṃ bhāvo na bhavati, abhāvastarhi astu? etadapi nāsti | yasmāt-
avidyamāne bhāve ca kasyābhāvo bhaviṣyati |
yadā ākāśaṃ bhāvo na bhavati, tadā bhāvasyāsattve kasyābhāvaḥ kalpyatām? vakṣyati hi-

bhāvasya cedaprasiddhirabhāvo naiva sidhyati |
bhāvasya hyanyathābhāvamabhāvaṃ bruvate janāḥ || iti |

tasmād bhāvābhāvādabhāvo 'pyākāśaṃ na saṃbhavati | rūpābhāvaścākāśamiti vyavasthāpyate | yadyapi rūpaṃ syāttadā rūpābhāva ākāśamiti syāt | yadā ca yathoktena nyāyena rūpameva nāsti, tadā kasyābhāva ākāśaṃ syāt?
atrāha- vidyete eva bhāvābhāvau, tatparīkṣakasadbhāvāt | asti ca bhavān bhāvābhāvayoḥ parīkṣakaḥ, ya evāha-
avidyamāne bhāve ca kasyābhāvo bhaviṣyati |
iti | tasmād bhavato bhāvābhāvaparīkṣakasya sadbhāvāt parīkṣyāvapi bhāvābhāvau vidyete iti | ucyate | etadapyayuktam | yasmāt-
bhāvābhāvavidharmā ca bhāvābhāvamavaiti kaḥ || 6 ||
syātāṃ bhāvābhāvau yadi, tadā tayoḥ parīkṣako bhāvo va syādabhāvo vā | yadi bhāva iṣyate, tasya
lakṣyalakṣaṇanirmukto naiva bhāvo 'pi vidyate |
ityuktaṃ dūṣaṇam | atha abhāvaḥ,
avidyamāne bhāve ca kasyābhāvo bhaviṣyati |
ityatroktametadduṣaṇam | na ca bhāvābhāvavisadṛśadharmā kaścit tṛtīyaḥ padārtho 'sti, yo 'nayoravagamaka iti nāsti bhāvābhāvayoḥ parīkṣakaḥ | ata evoktaṃ bhagavatā-

bhāvānabhāvāniti yaḥ prajānati sa sarvabhāveṣu na jātu sajjate |
yaḥ sarvabhāveṣu na jātu sajjate sa ānimittaṃ bhajate samādhim || iti |
tathā-

children.text: yo 'pi ca cintayi śūnyakadharmān so 'pi kumārgapapannaku balaḥ |
akṣara kīrtita śūnyaka dharmāḥ te ca anakṣara akṣara uktāḥ ||
śānta paśānta ya cintayi dharmān so 'pi ca cinta na jātu na bhūtaḥ |
cittavitarkaṇa sarvi papañcāḥ sūkṣma acintiya budhyatha dharmān ||

body.text: iti vistaraḥ || 6 ||

idānīṃ pratipāditamarthaṃ nigamayannāha-
tasmānna bhāvo nābhāvo na lakṣyaṃ nāpi lakṣaṇam |
ākāśam
iti | yathā cākāśam, evam-
ākāśasamā dhātavaḥ pañca ye pare || 7 ||
pṛthivyādidhātavo ye pañca pare 'vaśiṣyante, te 'pi ākāśavad bhāvābhāvalakṣyalakṣaṇaparikalpasvarūparahitāḥ parijñeyā ityarthaḥ || 7 ||
tadevaṃ padārthānāṃ svabhāve vyavasthite avidyātimiropahatamatinayanatayā anādisaṃsārābhyastatayā bhāvābhāvādiviparītadarśanā nirvāṇānugāmyaviparītanaiḥsvabhāvyadarśanasanmārgaparibhraṣṭāḥ

children.text: astitvaṃ ye tu paśyanti nāstitvaṃ cālpabuddhayaḥ |
bhāvānāṃ te na paśyanti draṣṭavyopaśamaṃ śivam || 8 ||

body.text: draṣṭavyopaśamaṃ śivalakṣaṇaṃ sarvakalpanājālarahitaṃ jñānajñeyanivṛttisvabhāvaṃ śivaṃ paramārthasvabhāvam | paramārthamajaramamaramaprapañcaṃ nirvāṇaṃ śūnyatāsvabhāvaṃ te na paśyanti mandabuddhitayā astitvaṃ nāstitvaṃ cābhiniviṣṭāḥ santa iti | yathoktamāryaratnāvalyām-
āryasamādhirāje coktaṃ bhagavatā-

children.text: astīti nāstīti ume 'pi antā śuddhī aśuddhīti ime 'pi antā |
tasmādume anta vivarjayitvā madhye 'pi sthānaṃ na karoti paṇḍitaḥ ||

body.text:
astīti nāstīti vivāda eṣaḥ śuddhī aśuddhīti ayaṃ vivādaḥ |
vivādaprāptyā na dukhaṃ praśāmyate avivādaprāptyā ca duḥkhaṃ nirudhyate || iti |
tasmādasaṃbhava eva yatsāṃsārikeṇa mārgeṇa nirvāṇamadhigamyata iti || 8 ||
ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacitāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau dhātuparīkṣā nāma pañcamaṃ prakaraṇam ||
rāgaraktaparīkṣā ṣaṣṭhaṃ prakaraṇam |

atrāha- vidyanta eva skandhāyatanadhātavaḥ | kutaḥ? tadāśrayasaṃkleśopalabdheḥ | iha yannāsti, na tadāśrayasaṃkleśopalabdhirasti bandhyāduhituriva vandhyāsūnoḥ | santi ca rāgādayaḥ kleśāḥ saṃkleśanibandhanam | yathoktaṃ bhagavatā- bālo bhikṣave aśrutavān pṛthagjanaḥ prajñaptimanupatitaḥ cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā saumanasyasthānīyānyabhiniviśate | so 'bhiniviṣṭaḥ san rāgamutpādayati | raktaḥ san rāgajaṃ dveṣajaṃ mohajaṃ karmābhisaṃskaroti kāyena vācā manaseti vistaraḥ | ucyate | syuḥ skandhāyatanadhātavo yadi rāgādaya eva kleśāḥ syuḥ | ihāyaṃ rāgaḥ parikalpyamāno bālapṛthagjanaiḥ sati rakte nare parikalpyeta asati vā? ubhayathā ca na yujyata ityāha-

children.text: taṃ pratītya bhavedrāgo rakte rāgo bhavetsati || 1 ||

body.text: tatra rāgaḥ saktiradhyavasānaṃ saṅgo 'bhiniveśa iti paryāyāḥ | rakto rāgāśrayaḥ | sa yadi rakto rāgātpūrvaṃ rāgatiraskṛto rāgarahito bhavet, tadā taṃ rāgatiraskṛtaṃ raktaṃ pratītya rāgo bhavet | evaṃ sakti rakte rāgo bhavediti yuktam | na tvevaṃ saṃbhavati, yadrāgarahito raktaḥ syāt | arhatāmapi rāgaprasaṅgāt || 1 ||
yadyevaṃ sati rakte na rāgaḥ, asati tarhi rakte rāgo 'stu | etadapyayuktamityāha-
rakte 'sati punā rāgaḥ kuta eva bhaviṣyati |
yadā sati rakte rāgo nāsti, tadā kathamasati rakte nirāśrayo rāgaḥ setsyati? na hi asati phale tatpakvatā saṃbhavatīti ||

atrāha- yadyapi tvayā rāgo niṣiddhaḥ, tathāpi rakto 'sti, apratiṣedhāt | na ca rāgamantareṇa rakto yuktaḥ, tasmādayamapyastīti | ucyate | syādrāgo yadi raktaḥ syāt | yasmādayaṃ rakta iṣyamāṇaḥ sati vā rāge parikalpyeta, asati vā? ubhayathā ca nopapadyate ityāha-
sati vāsati vā rāge rakte 'pyeṣa samaḥ kramaḥ || 2 ||
tatra yadi sati rāge raktaḥ parikalpyeta, tatrāpi eṣa eva rāgānupapattikramo 'nantarokto rakte 'pi tulyaḥ |
raktādyadi bhavetpūrvaṃ rāgo raktatiraskṛtaḥ |
ityādi | athāsati rāge rakta iṣyate, etadapyayuktam | yasmāt-
rāge 'sati punā raktaḥ kuta eva bhaviṣyati |
iti | tasmādrakto 'pi nāsti | rāgaraktābhāvācca skandhādayo 'pi na santīti || 2 ||

atrāha- naiva hi rāgaraktayoḥ paurvāparyeṇa saṃbhavo yata idaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ syāt, kiṃ tarhi rāgaraktayoḥ sahaivodbhavaḥ | cittasahabhūtena rāgeṇa hi cittaṃ rajyate, tacca raktamiti | ato vidyete eva rāgaraktāviti | ucyate | evamapi-
body.translated_text: To this one says: it is not that passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the passionate one (<s>rakta</s>) arise in temporal sequence so that this refutation would apply; rather, passion and the passionate one arise simultaneously. For by a passion co-existent with the mind, the mind becomes passionate, and that [mind] is the 'passionate one.' Therefore passion and the passionate one do indeed exist. It is replied: even so —

body.text: sahaiva punarudbhūtirna yuktā rāgaraktayoḥ |
body.translated_text: The co-arising of passion and the passionate one is again not justified.

body.text: sahotpādo 'pi na yukto rāgaraktayoḥ | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Simultaneous arising too is not justified for passion and the passionate one, because —

body.text: bhavetāṃ rāgaraktau hi nirapekṣau parasparam || 3 ||
body.translated_text: For passion and the passionate one would then be mutually independent. // 3 //

body.text: sahabhāvāt savyetaragoviṣāṇavadityabhiprāyaḥ || 3 ||
body.translated_text: The intent is: because of [their] simultaneous existence, like the left and right horns of a cow. // 3 //

body.text: api ca | anayo rāgaraktayoḥ sahabhāvaḥ ekatve parikalpyeta pṛthaktve vā? tatra yadi ekatve, tanna yujyate | yasmāt
body.translated_text: Moreover, this simultaneous existence of passion and the passionate one — is it conceived in [their] unity or in [their] separateness? In that case, if in unity, that is not justified, because —

body.text: naikatve sahabhāvo 'sti
body.translated_text: In unity, simultaneous existence does not obtain.

body.text: kasmātpunarnāstītyāha-
body.translated_text: Why not? He says:

body.text: na tenaiva hi tatsaha |
body.translated_text: For that very thing is not 'together with' itself.

body.text: na hi rāgasvātmā rāgādavyatirikto rāgeṇa saheti vyapadiśyate ||
body.translated_text: For the self-nature of passion, which is not different from passion, is not designated as 'together with passion.'

body.text: idānīṃ pṛthaktve 'pi sahabhāvābhāvamāha-
body.translated_text: Now he states the absence of simultaneous existence even in separateness:

body.text: pṛthaktve sahabhāvo 'tha kuta eva bhaviṣyati || 4 ||
body.translated_text: And how then would simultaneous existence obtain in separateness? // 4 //

body.text: na hi pṛthagbhūtayorālokāndhakārayoḥ saṃsāranirvāṇayorvā sahabhāvo dṛṣṭa iti || 4 ||
body.translated_text: For the simultaneous existence of two separate things — such as light and darkness, or <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s> — has not been observed. // 4 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat-
body.translated_text: What is more —

children.translated_text: If simultaneous existence obtained in unity, it would be [possible] even without a companion.
If simultaneous existence obtained in separateness, it would be [possible] even without a companion. // 5 //

body.text: yadi ekatve sahabhāvaḥ syāt, tadā yatra yatraikatvaṃ tatra tatra sahabhāva ityekasyāpi sahabhāvaḥ syāt | pṛthaktve 'pi sahabhāve iṣyamāṇe yatra yatra pṛthaktvaṃ tatra tatra sahabhāva iti aśvādivyatiriktasya pṛthagavasthitasya goḥ asahāyasya sahabhāvaḥ syāt || 5 ||
body.translated_text: If simultaneous existence obtained in unity, then wherever there is unity, there would be simultaneous existence; and so even a single thing would have simultaneous existence. And if simultaneous existence is desired in separateness, then wherever there is separateness, there would be simultaneous existence; and so a cow, standing apart from a horse and so forth, without a companion, would have simultaneous existence. // 5 //

body.text: kiṃ ca-
body.translated_text: What is more —

children.translated_text: If simultaneous existence [obtained] in separateness, then why should there be, for passion and the passionate one,
an established separate existence of each, by which their simultaneous existence [would follow]? // 6 //

body.text: pṛthaktve sahabhāvaśca rāgaraktayoḥ parikalpyate | kimanayoḥ siddhaḥ pṛthakpṛthagbhāvaḥ? kiṃ rāganirapekṣo raktaḥ siddho yatastayoḥ sahabhāvaḥ syāt? pṛthakpṛthaksiddhayoreva hi gavāśvayoḥ sahabhāvo dṛṣṭaḥ | na tvevaṃ rāgaraktau pṛthakpṛthaksiddhāviti nāstyanayoḥ sahabhāvaḥ || 6 ||
body.translated_text: Simultaneous existence for passion and the passionate one is conceived in separateness. But is their separate existence of each established? Is the passionate one established independently of passion, such that their simultaneous existence would follow? For the simultaneous existence of a cow and a horse, separately established, is observed. But passion and the passionate one are not separately established in this way — therefore their simultaneous existence does not exist. // 6 //

body.text: athavā | pṛthakpṛthagasiddhayorna sahabhāva iti kṛtvā-
body.translated_text: Alternatively, since there is no simultaneous existence for things not separately established —

body.text: siddhaḥ pṛthakpṛthagbhāvo yadi vā rāgaraktayoḥ |
body.translated_text: If indeed the separate existence of passion and the passionate one

body.text: parikalpyate bhavatā, kimidānīṃ sahabhāvenākiṃcitkareṇa parikalpitenetyāha-
body.translated_text: is established, then — it is conceived by you — what now is the point of a fruitless simultaneous existence so conceived? He says:

body.text: sahabhāvaṃ kimarthaṃ tu parikalpayase tayoḥ || 7 ||
body.translated_text: For what purpose do you conceive simultaneous existence for those two? // 7 //

body.text: rāgaraktayoḥ siddhayarthaṃ sahabhāvaḥ parikalpyate | saca pṛthakpṛthagasiddhayornāstīti pṛthakpṛthak siddhirabhyupagamyate tvayā | nanvevaṃ sati siddhatvātkimanayoḥ sahabhāvena kṛtyam?
body.translated_text: Simultaneous existence is conceived for the purpose of establishing passion and the passionate one. And that [simultaneous existence] does not exist for things not separately established — so you accept their separate establishment. But in that case, since they are [already] established, what need is there for their simultaneous existence?

body.text: atha-
body.translated_text: But —

body.text: pṛthaṅ na sidhyatītyevaṃ sahabhāvaṃ vikāṅkṣasi |
body.translated_text: If [they] are not separately established, you desire their simultaneous existence;

body.text: pṛthakpṛthag rāgaraktayoḥ siddhirnāstīti kṛtvā yadyanayoḥ sahabhāvamicchasi, sa ca pṛthakpṛthagasiddhayornāstīti-
body.translated_text: since the separate establishment of passion and the passionate one does not exist, and therefore you desire their simultaneous existence — but that [simultaneous existence] does not exist for things not separately established — therefore:

body.text: sahabhāvaprasiddhayartha pṛthaktvaṃ bhūya icchasi || 8 ||
body.translated_text: You again desire their separateness for the purpose of establishing their simultaneous existence. // 8 //

body.text: nanvevaṃ sati itaretarāśrayāyāṃ siddhau sthitāyāṃ kasyedānīṃ siddhau satyāṃ kasya siddhirastu? || 8 ||
body.translated_text: Since this amounts to the establishment of mutual dependence, in what case would the establishment of one depend on the establishment of the other? // 8 //

body.text: yāvatā-
body.translated_text: Inasmuch as —

children.translated_text: And since separateness is not established, simultaneous existence is not established.
In which separateness do you desire simultaneous existence to exist? // 9 //

body.text: nāstyeva sa pṛthagbhāvaḥ sahabhāvānapekṣo yasmin pṛthagbhāve sati sahabhāvasiddhiḥ syādityasaṃbhāvayannāha-
body.translated_text: There is no such separateness, independent of simultaneous existence, in whose existence the establishment of simultaneous existence would follow — indicating the impossibility, he says:

body.text: katamasminpṛthagbhāve sahabhāvaṃ satīcchasi || 9 ||
body.translated_text: In which separateness do you desire simultaneous existence to exist? // 9 //

body.text: tadevaṃ yathoditavicāraparāmarśena rāgaraktayorasiddhiṃ nigamayannāha-
body.translated_text: Thus, concluding the non-establishment of passion and the passionate one through the review of the analysis set forth above, he says:

body.text: evaṃ raktena rāgasya siddhirna saha nāsaha |
body.translated_text: Thus, the establishment of passion is not [possible] either together with or without the passionate one.

body.text: iti | yathā ca rāgaraktayorna paurvāparyeṇa siddhiḥ nāpi sahabhāvena, evaṃ sarvabhāvānāmapītyatidiśannāha-
body.translated_text: And just as the establishment of passion and the passionate one is not [possible] either in temporal sequence or in simultaneity, even so for all entities — extending [the argument], he says:

body.text: rāgavatsarvadharmāṇāṃ siddhirna saha nāsaha || 10 ||
body.translated_text: Like passion, the establishment of all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) is not [possible] either together with or without [their counterpart]. // 10 //

body.text: iti dveṣadviṣṭamohamūḍhādīnāṃ rāgaraktavadasiddhiryojyate || 10 ||
body.translated_text: Thus for hatred and the hater, delusion and the deluded, and so forth, the non-establishment should be applied just as for passion and the passionate one. // 10 //

body.text: ata evoktaṃ bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: Hence the <s>Bhagavān</s> has stated:

body.text: yo rajyeta yatra vā rajyeta yena vā rajyeta, yo duṣyeta yatra vā duṣyeta yena vā duṣyeta, yo muhyeta yatra vā muhyeta yena vā muhyeta, sa taṃ dharma na samanupaśyati taṃ dharma nopalabhate | sa taṃ dharmamasamanupaśyannanupalabhamāno 'rakto 'duṣṭo 'mūḍho 'viparyastacittaḥ samāhita ityucyate | tīrṇaḥ pāraga ityucyate | kṣemaprāpta ityucyate | abhayaprāpta ityucyate | yāvat kṣīṇāsrava ityucyate | niḥkleśo vaśībhūtaḥ suvimuktacittaḥ suvimuktaprajña ājāneyo mahābhāgaḥ kṛtakṛtyaḥ kṛtakaraṇīyaḥ apahatabhāro 'nuprāptasvakārthaḥ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanaḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittaḥ sarvacetovaśitāparamapāramiprāptaḥ śramaṇa ityucyate | iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Whoever would be passionate, wherever he would be passionate, by whatever he would be passionate; whoever would be hateful, wherever he would be hateful, by whatever he would be hateful; whoever would be deluded, wherever he would be deluded, by whatever he would be deluded — he does not perceive that <s>dharma</s>, he does not apprehend that <s>dharma</s>. Not perceiving, not apprehending that <s>dharma</s>, he is called unpassionate, unhateful, undeluded, with mind not perverted, concentrated. He is called one who has crossed over, who has gone to the far shore. He is called one who has attained security. He is called one who has attained fearlessness. He is called one whose defilements are exhausted. He is free from afflictions, self-mastered, with well-liberated mind, with well-liberated wisdom, a thoroughbred, one of great fortune, one who has done what was to be done, whose task is accomplished, whose burden is laid down, who has attained his own goal, whose fetters of existence are exhausted, whose mind is well-liberated through right knowledge, who has reached the supreme perfection of mastery over all minds — he is called an ascetic.' Thus in detail.

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: And also —

children.translated_text: Those who, having known the nature of passion, hatred, intoxication, and delusion to be arisen from conceptual construction and of false operation,

children.text: na vikalpayanti na virāgamapīha teṣām [āśu] sarvabhavabhāvavibhāvitānām ||
children.translated_text: do not conceptually construct, nor do they even cultivate dispassion — those [are the ones] who have fully penetrated the nature of all states of existence. //

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacittāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau rāgaraktaparīkṣā nāma ṣaṣṭhaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the examination of passion and the passionate one, the sixth chapter, in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary, composed by the venerable <s>Ācārya Candrakīrti</s>.

body.text: saṃskṛtaparīkṣā saptamaṃ prakaraṇam |
body.translated_text: The examination of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>), the seventh chapter.

body.text: atrāha- vidyanta eva saṃskṛtasvabhāvāḥ, skandhāyatanadhātavaḥ utpādādisaṃskṛtalakṣaṇasadbhāvāt | uktaṃ hi bhagavatā- trīṇīmāni saṃskṛtasya saṃskṛtalakṣaṇāni | saṃskṛtasya bhikṣavaḥ utpādo 'pi prajñāyate, vyayo 'pi, sthityanyathātvamapīti | na ca avidyamānasya kharaviṣāṇasyeva jātyādilakṣaṇamasti | tasmātsaṃskṛtalakṣaṇopadeśādvidyanta eva skandhāyatanadhātavaḥ iti | ucyate | syuḥ skandhāyatanadhātavaḥ saṃskṛtasvabhāvāstāvakena matena, yadi jātyādilakṣaṇameva bhavet | ihāyamutpādaḥ saṃskṛtalakṣaṇatveneṣyamāṇaḥ saṃskṛto vā tallakṣaṇatveneṣyate, asaṃskṛto vā? tatra-
body.translated_text: Here one says: entities of conditioned nature do indeed exist — namely, the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), sense-spheres (<s>āyatanas</s>), and elements (<s>dhātus</s>) — because of the existence of the conditioned marks such as arising and so forth. For the <s>Bhagavān</s> has stated: 'There are these three conditioned marks of the conditioned. The arising of the conditioned is known, monks; its decay is also [known]; and the alteration while persisting is also [known].' And the marks of birth and so forth do not belong to something non-existent like a donkey's horn. Therefore, from the teaching of conditioned marks, the aggregates, sense-spheres, and elements do indeed exist. It is replied: the aggregates, sense-spheres, and elements would be conditioned entities according to your view, if birth and other marks were indeed [established]. Now, this arising — posited as a conditioned mark — is it posited as a mark of the conditioned because it is conditioned, or because it is unconditioned? In that case —

body.text: yadi saṃskṛta utpādastatra yuktā trilakṣaṇī |
body.translated_text: If arising is conditioned, then the three marks apply to it.

body.text: trayāṇāṃ lakṣaṇānāṃ samāhārastrilakṣaṇī | iyaṃ ca utpādasthitibhaṅgasamāhārasvabhāvasarvasaṃskṛtāvyabhicāriṇīti kṛtvā yadi utpādaḥ saṃskṛta iti parikalpyate, tadā utpāde 'pi trilakṣaṇī prasajyate | tataśca rūpādivallakṣyatvamutpādasya syāt, na saṃskṛtalakṣaṇatvam | athotpāde 'pi trilakṣaṇī neṣyate, tadā trilakṣaṇīrahitatvādākāśavat saṃskṛtalakṣaṇatvamasyāvahīyate ityāha-
body.translated_text: The aggregate of three marks is the 'three marks.' And since this, consisting of the aggregate of arising, persistence, and cessation, pervades all conditioned things without exception — if arising is conceived as conditioned, then the three marks would apply to arising too. And then arising would be a 'thing to be marked,' like form and so forth, not a 'conditioned mark.' But if the three marks are not desired for arising, then, being devoid of the three marks, its status as a conditioned mark would be forfeited, like space. He says:

body.text: athāsaṃskṛta utpādaḥ kathaṃ saṃskṛtalakṣaṇam || 1 ||
body.translated_text: If arising is unconditioned, how can it be a conditioned mark? // 1 //

body.text: iti | naitatsaṃskṛtalakṣaṇamityabhiprāyaḥ || 1 ||
body.translated_text: The intent is: it would not be a conditioned mark. // 1 //

body.text: api ca | ime utpādādayaḥ saṃskṛtasya lakṣaṇatvena parikalpyamānā vyastā vā pṛthagvā lakṣaṇatvena parikalpyeran, samastā vā sahabhūtā vā? ubhayathā ca na yujyata ityāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, these arising and others, conceived as marks of the conditioned — are they conceived as marks separately, i.e. individually, or collectively, i.e. simultaneously? In both cases, it is not justified — he says:

children.translated_text: Arising, persistence, and cessation, separately, are not capable of the function of marking
the conditioned. How could they be [operative] collectively, in one [thing], at one [time]? // 2 //

body.text: tatra vyastā lakṣaṇakarmaṇi na yujyante | yadi utpādakāle sthitibhaṅgau na syātāṃ tadā sthitibhaṅgarahitasya ākāśasyeva saṃskṛtalakṣaṇatvenānupapadya evotpādaḥ | atha sthitikāle utpādabhaṅgau na staḥ, tadā tadrahitasya sthitiḥ syāt | utpādabhaṅgarahitaśca padārtho nāstyeveti na asyāvidyamānasya khapuṣpavat sthitiryujyate | kiṃ ca | sthitiyuktasya paścādanityatayāpi yogo na syāt, tadvirodhidharmākrāntatvāt | atha syāt- pūrvaṃ śāśvato bhūtvā paścādaśāśvata iti, na caikapadārthaḥ śāśvataścāśāśvataśca yukta iti notpādabhaṅgarahitasya sthitiḥ | tathā yadi bhaṅgakāle sthityutpādau na syātām, evamapyanutpannasya sthitirahitasya khapuṣpasya vināśo 'pi nāstīti | evaṃ tāvadutpādādayo vyastā nālaṃ lakṣaṇakarmaṇi nālaṃ na paryāptā ityarthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Here, separately, they are not justified for the function of marking. If at the time of arising, persistence and cessation did not exist, then arising — devoid of persistence and cessation, like space — would simply not be possible as a conditioned mark. And if at the time of persistence, arising and cessation do not exist, then persistence would be that which is devoid of them. But a thing devoid of arising and cessation simply does not exist — and therefore persistence of something non-existent, like a sky-flower, is not justified. What is more, if persistence is [first] established, afterward impermanence too would not apply to it, since it would be pervaded by a contradictory property. If one were to say 'first it was eternal, afterward non-eternal' — a single entity cannot be both eternal and non-eternal. Thus persistence devoid of arising and cessation is not [possible]. Likewise, if at the time of cessation, persistence and arising did not exist, even so the destruction of something unarisen and without persistence — like a sky-flower — does not exist. Thus arising and the others, separately, are 'not capable' — i.e. not sufficient — for the function of marking.

body.text: idānīṃ samastā api na yujyanta ityāha-
body.translated_text: Now he states that collectively too they are not justified:

body.text: samastāḥ syurekatra kathamekadā |
body.translated_text: How could they be [operative] collectively, in one [thing], at one [time]?

body.text: ekatra padārthe, ekasmin kāle, parasparaviruddhatvādrāgavairāgyavat, ālokāndhakāravadvā na yujyanta ityabhiprāyaḥ | yasminneva kṣaṇe padārtho jāyate, tasminneva tiṣṭhati vinaśyati ceti kaḥ sacetāḥ pratipadyeta? tasmātsamastānāmapi utpādādīnāṃ saṃskṛtasya lakṣaṇakarmaṇi nāsti sāmarthyam || 2 ||
body.translated_text: In one entity, at one time, because of mutual contradiction — like passion and dispassion, or like light and darkness — they are not justified. This is the intent. At the very moment when an entity arises, it also persists and also perishes — what sentient person would accept this? Therefore, even collectively, arising and the others do not have the capacity for the function of marking the conditioned. // 2 //

body.text: atha yaduktaṃ 'yadi saṃskṛta utpādaḥ'; ityādi, tena yadi utpādādīnāṃ trilakṣaṇī prāptā prasaktā, tataḥ ko doṣaḥ? athāsaṃskṛtaḥ, evamapyadoṣa iti | ucyate-
body.translated_text: Now, regarding what was said — 'if arising is conditioned' and so forth — if the three marks follow for arising and the others, what is the fault? And if [arising is] unconditioned, even so there is no fault. It is replied:

body.text: utpādasthitibhaṅgānāmanyatsaṃskṛtalakṣaṇam

children.text: asti cedanavasthaivaṃ nāsti cette na saṃskṛtāḥ || 3 ||
children.translated_text: there would be an infinite regress. If there is none, then they are not conditioned. // 3 //

body.translated_text: If there is another conditioned mark for arising, persistence, and cessation,

body.text: nanu ca pakṣadvaye 'pi vihita eva doṣaḥ, tatra kiṃ punaruktābhidhāneneti | satyamukto doṣaḥ sa khalu nācāryeṇa, kiṃ tarhi vṛttikāreṇa | atha pūrvapratijñātameva dūṣaṇāntarābhidhānena spaṣṭīkaraṇārthaṃ punarācāryo 'bhihitavān | yadi utpādasthitibhaṅgānāmanyadutpādādikaṃ saṃskṛtalakṣaṇamiṣyate, tadā teṣāmapyanyat, teṣāmapyanyat, ityaparyavasānadoṣaḥ syāt | sati ca aparyavasānadoṣe, kiṃ pūrvaṃ syād yata uttarakālamaparaṃ bhavediti vyavasthābhāvādasaṃbhava evaṃ utpādādīnāmityabhiprāyaḥ | athavā, pūrvaṃ mukhyatvādutpādasyaiva dūṣaṇamuktam, adhunā tu sāmānyeneti | nāsti cette na saṃskṛtā iti gatārthametat || 3 ||
body.translated_text: But surely the fault has already been stated in both alternatives — so what is the purpose of repeating it? True, the fault was stated, but not by the <s>Ācārya</s> — rather, by the commentator. Or else, the <s>Ācārya</s> restated what was already asserted earlier, for the purpose of clarifying it through a different refutation. If another arising and so forth is desired as the conditioned mark for arising, persistence, and cessation, then for those too [there would need to be] another, and for those too another — and so the fault of infinite regress would follow. And given the fault of infinite regress, since there is no ground for determining what would come first so that something later would follow — there is the impossibility of arising and the others in this way. This is the intent. Alternatively, formerly the refutation was stated specifically for arising, as it is primary; but now [it is stated] in general. 'If there is none, then they are not conditioned' — this is self-evident. // 3 //

body.text: atrāhuḥ sāṃmitīyāḥ- santi cotpādādīnāmutpādādayaḥ, na ca anavasthāprasaṅgaḥ, lakṣaṇānulakṣaṇānāṃ parasparaniṣpādakatvāt | yasmādiha saṃskṛtadharmaḥ kuśalaḥ kliṣṭo vā utpadyamānaḥ ātmanā pañcadaśaḥ utpadyate | sa dharmastasya cotpādaḥ samanvāgamaḥ sthitirjarā anityatā | yadyasau dharmaḥ kliṣṭo bhavati, tasya mithyāvimuktiḥ | atha śubhaḥ, tasya samyagvimuktiḥ | yadi nairyāṇiko bhavati tasya nairyāṇikatā | atha anairyāṇikaḥ, tasya anairyāṇikatā | ityeṣa parivāraḥ | idānīmutpāda syāpara utpādaḥ yāvadanairyāṇikatānairyāṇikatetyeṣa parivārasya parivāraḥ | tatra yo 'yaṃ maula utpāda sa ātmānaṃ vihāya anyāṃścaturdaśa dharmān janayati | utpādotpādasaṃjñakastu anulakṣaṇabhūta utpādo maulamevotpādaṃ janayati | evaṃ yāvadanairyāṇikatā caturdaśa dharmān na niryāṇayati, na tannirvāṇaṃ prāpayatītyarthaḥ | anairyāṇikatānairyāṇikatā tu na niryāṇayati | tadevamutpādādīnāmanavasthāṃ pariharannāha-
body.translated_text: Here the <s>Sāṃmitīyas</s> object: There are indeed arisings of arising and so forth, and yet there is no infinite regress, because the characteristics and sub-characteristics mutually accomplish each other. For here, a conditioned <s>dharma</s>, whether wholesome or defiled, when arising, arises as fifteenfold in itself. That <s>dharma</s>, and its arising, its association, its duration, its aging, and its impermanence. If that <s>dharma</s> is defiled, it has wrong liberation. If it is wholesome, it has right liberation. If it leads to liberation, it has the quality of leading to liberation. If it does not lead to liberation, it has the quality of not leading to liberation. This is its retinue. Now, the arising has another arising, and so on up to the not-leading-to-liberation of the not-leading-to-liberation — this is the retinue of the retinue. There, the root arising, setting aside itself, produces the other fourteen <s>dharmas</s>. But the arising named 'arising-of-arising,' being a sub-characteristic, produces only the root arising. Similarly, up to: 'not-leading-to-liberation' does not lead the fourteen <s>dharmas</s> to liberation, meaning it does not cause them to attain <s>nirvāṇa</s>. But the 'not-leading-to-liberation of not-leading-to-liberation' only does not lead to liberation. Thus, in order to avoid the infinite regress of arising and so forth, he says:

children.translated_text: The arising-of-arising is the arising of the root arising alone. /
The root arising, in turn, produces the arising-of-arising. // 4 //

body.text: dvividho hyutpādaḥ | eko maula utpādaḥ, aparaśca utpādotpādasaṃjñakaḥ, utpādasyotpāda iti kṛtvā | tatra yo 'yamutpādotpādasaṃjñaka utpādaḥ, sa mūlotpādasya kevalamutpādakaḥ | taṃ cedānīmutpādopādākhyamutpādaṃ
body.translated_text: For arising is twofold. One is the root arising, and the other is designated 'arising-of-arising,' since it is the arising of arising. Therein, that arising designated 'arising-of-arising' is the producer of the root arising alone. And now that arising called 'arising-of-arising'

body.text: maula utpādo janayati | tadevaṃ parasparanirvartanādasti ca trilakṣaṇī utpādādīnām, na cānavasthāprasaṅga iti || 4 ||
body.translated_text: is produced by the root arising. Thus, through mutual production, the three characteristics of arising and so forth exist, and yet there is no infinite regress. // 4 //

children.translated_text: In reply it is said:
If the arising-of-arising, in your view, is the arising of the root arising, /
how will that one, not produced by the root, produce it? // 5 //

body.text: yadi tava utpādasyotpādo mūlotpādasya janaka iti matam, sa kathamidānīṃ maulenotpādenānutpāditaḥ san utpādotpādo maulaṃ janayiṣyati? || 5 ||
body.translated_text: If you think that the arising of arising is the producer of the root arising, how then, being not yet produced by the root arising, will that arising-of-arising produce the root? // 5 //

body.text: atha manyase- utpādita eva maulenotpādena utpādotpādo maulaṃ janayiṣyati, etadapyasadityāha-
body.translated_text: If you think: 'Only when produced by the root arising will the arising-of-arising produce the root' — this too is wrong, hence he says:

children.text: sa te maulena janito maulaṃ janayate yadi |
children.translated_text: If that [arising-of-arising], produced by the root, produces the root, /
how does the root, not produced by it, produce it? // 6 //

body.text: sa utpādotpādasaṃjñaka utpādo maulena janito yadi maulaṃ janayati, sa maula utpādotpādenājanito 'vidyamānaḥ kathamutpādotpādaṃ janayiṣyati? tasmānmaulena janitaḥ san utpādotpādo maulaṃ janayatīte na yujyate | tataśca parasparanirvartyanirvartakatvābhāvātsa eva anavasthāprasaṅga iti nāstyutpādaḥ || 6 ||
body.translated_text: If that arising designated 'arising-of-arising,' produced by the root, produces the root — that root arising, not produced by the arising-of-arising, being non-existent, how will it produce the arising-of-arising? Therefore, the view that 'the arising-of-arising, having been produced by the root, produces the root' is not correct. And since there is no mutual production, the very same consequence of infinite regress [follows] — hence arising does not exist. // 6 //

body.text: atrāha- utpadyamāna eva mūlotpāda utpādotpādamutpādayati, sa evotpādotpādo mūlotpādaṃ janayiṣyatīti | ucyate-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: 'The root arising, while itself arising, produces the arising-of-arising, and that very arising-of-arising will produce the root arising.' The reply is:

children.translated_text: This one while arising may well produce that, /
if indeed this one, while unborn, could produce that. // 7 //

body.text: kāmamayaṃ mūlotpāda utpadyamāna utpādayedutpādam, yadyayameva ajātaḥ śaknuyādaparamajātamutpādayitum | utpadyamāno hi nāma anāgataḥ | sa ca ajātaḥ kathamutpādayiṣyatīti na yuktamevaitadityabhiprāyaḥ evamutpādotpāde 'pi vācyam || 7 ||
body.translated_text: This root arising, while arising, may well produce the arising — if indeed this very one, while unborn, could produce another unborn [arising]. For 'while arising' means 'not yet arrived.' And that which is unborn — how will it produce? Hence this is simply not correct — this is the intent. The same should be said regarding the arising-of-arising as well. // 7 //

body.text: atrāha- naiva hi utpādasyāpara utpādo 'sti yato 'navasthāprasaṅgaḥ syāt | kiṃ tarhi-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: 'There is indeed no separate arising of arising, from which an infinite regress would follow. Rather —'

children.translated_text: Just as a lamp illuminates both itself and others, /
so too arising would produce both itself and others. // 8 //

body.text: yathā pradīpaḥ prakāśasvabhāvatvādātmānaṃ prakāśayati ghaṭādīṃśca, evamutpādo 'pyutpādasvabhāvatvādātmānamutpādayiṣyati paraṃ ceti || 8 ||
body.translated_text: Just as a lamp, being of the nature of illumination, illuminates itself and pots and so forth, even so arising, being of the nature of arising, will produce itself and others. // 8 //

body.text: ucyate | syādetadevaṃ yadi pradīpaḥ svaparātmānau saṃprakāśayet | na caivam | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: The reply is: This would be so if a lamp illuminated both itself and others. But it is not so. Because —

children.translated_text: There is no darkness in a lamp, nor in the place where it is situated. /

children.text: kiṃ prakāśayati dīpaḥ prakāśo hi tamovadhaḥ || 9 ||
children.translated_text: What does a lamp illuminate? For illumination is the destruction of darkness. // 9 //

body.text: iha prakāśo nāma tamasya (so?) vadhaḥ | tamaśca pradīpasvātmani tāvanna saṃbhavati virodhāt, yattamo nighnataḥ svātmaprakāśatvaṃ syāt | na cāpi pradīpo yatra deśe tiṣṭhati tatra tamo 'sti, yattamo nighnataḥ pradīpasya paraprakāśakatvaṃ syāt | ato 'pi nāsti pradīpasya svaparātmaprakāśakatvam | yadā caivam, tadā pradīpavadutpādasya svaparātmotpādakatvaṃ na saṃbhaviṣyati, iti ayuktametat || 9 ||
body.translated_text: Here, illumination is indeed the destruction of darkness. And darkness does not occur in the lamp itself, due to their mutual opposition — such that by destroying darkness, it would illuminate itself. Nor is there darkness in the place where the lamp stands — such that by destroying the darkness, the lamp would illuminate other things. Hence, the lamp does not illuminate either itself or others. And when this is so, the self-and-other-producing nature of arising, like a lamp, will not be possible — hence this is not correct. // 9 //

body.text: atrāha- yadetaduktaṃ pradīpe nāndhakāro 'stīti, etadasatyandhakāradhāte yuktameva vaktum | yasmāttu utpadyamānenaiva pradīpena tamo nihatam, tatra pradīpe nāndhakāro 'sti, yatra ca pradīpo 'sti, tatrāpyandhakāro nāstīti yujyate | yadi pradīpena nāndhakāradhātaḥ kṛtaḥ, tadā anutpanne iva pradīpe utpanne 'pi ghaṭādayo nopalabhyeran, andhakāraghātābhāvātprāgavasthāmiva | tasmādastyeva andhakāraghātalakṣaṇaṃ prakāśanaṃ pradīpasya | taccānena utpadyamānena pradīpena kṛtamiti | ucyate-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: 'What was stated — "there is no darkness in a lamp" — that would be correct to say only if no destruction of darkness occurred. But since by the lamp, even as it is arising, darkness is destroyed — therefore there is no darkness in the lamp, and where the lamp is, there too darkness does not exist — this is correct. If the lamp did not destroy darkness, then even when the lamp had arisen, pots and so forth would not be apprehended — just as before, when the lamp had not arisen — due to the non-destruction of darkness. Therefore, the illumination of the lamp, characterized as the destruction of darkness, does indeed exist. And that is accomplished by this lamp even as it is arising.' The reply is:

children.translated_text: How is darkness destroyed by a lamp that is [still] arising, /

children.text: notpadyamāno hi tamaḥ pradīpaḥ prāpnute yadā || 10 ||
children.translated_text: when the lamp that is arising does not reach the darkness? // 10 //

body.text: iha ālokāndhakārayoryaugapadyābhāvāt prāpterabhāvaḥ | yadā caivaṃ prāpterabhāvaḥ, tadā kathaṃ kena prakāreṇedānīmutpadyamānena pradīpena tamo hatamiti yuktaṃ parikalpayitum? yasmācca evamutpadyamāna pradīpaḥ tamo na prāpnoti, tasmānnaiva aprāptatvātpradīpaḥ kiṃcidapi prakāśayatītyavasīyatām || 10 ||
body.translated_text: Here, because of the impossibility of simultaneity of light and darkness, there is an absence of contact. And when there is thus an absence of contact, how, in what manner, is it correct to suppose that darkness is destroyed by a lamp that is arising? And since thus the arising lamp does not reach the darkness, it should be concluded that the lamp does not illuminate anything at all, because of not having reached [the darkness]. // 10 //

body.text: atha manyase- yathā aprāptāmeva avidyāṃ jñānaṃ nihanti, aprāptameva rūpaṃ cakṣuḥ paśyati aprāptameva ayaḥ ayaskānto maṇirākarṣati, evameva aprāptamevāndhakāraṃ pradīpo nihaniṣyatīti etadapyasāramityāha-
body.translated_text: If you think: 'Just as knowledge destroys ignorance without reaching it, just as the eye sees form without reaching it, just as a lodestone attracts iron without reaching it, even so the lamp will destroy darkness without reaching it' — this too is without substance, hence he says:

children.text: aprāpyaiva pradīpena yadi vā nihataṃ tamaḥ |
children.translated_text: If, alternatively, darkness is destroyed by the lamp without reaching it, /
then, situated here, it will destroy the darkness situated in the entire world. // 11 //

body.text: yadi aprāpyaiva pradīpena tamo nihatam, evaṃ sati, ihastha eva pradīpaḥ sarvalokasthaṃ tamo nihaniṣyati, aprāptatvātsamīpasthamivetyabhiprāyaḥ | etena nyāyena jñānena avidyāghātaḥ, cakṣuṣā rūpadarśanam, ayaskāntamaṇinā ayaākarṣaṇamiva ityevamādikaṃ sādhyasamaṃ jñeyam ||
body.translated_text: If darkness is destroyed by the lamp without reaching it, then in that case, the lamp, situated right here, will destroy the darkness situated in the entire world — since the non-reaching is the same for what is nearby [as for what is far] — this is the intent. By this same reasoning, the destruction of ignorance by knowledge, the seeing of form by the eye, and the attraction of iron by a lodestone — all these should be known as being equally unestablished.

body.text: atha aprāptāvapi satyāmayaskāntamaṇiprabhṛtīnāṃ yogyadeśāvasthānāmeva svakāryakṛtvaṃ debhaviṣyatīti cet, tadapi na yuktam | aprāptau hi satyāṃ viprakṛṣṭadeśāntarāvasthitavadavyavahitaśāntarāvasthita vacca aprāptatvād yogyadeśāvasthitānāmapi yogyadeśāvasthitatvaṃ na yuktamiti kuto yogyadeśāvasthitānāṃ svakāryakṛttvaṃ prasetsyati?
body.translated_text: If it is objected that, even in the absence of contact, only those situated in a suitable location — the lodestone and so forth — will perform their respective functions, that too is not correct. For when there is no contact, those situated at a suitable location are no different from those situated at a distant or intervening location, since the absence of contact is the same. Thus, how will the capacity of those situated at a suitable location to perform their respective functions be established?

body.text: dṛṣṭametallokata iti cennaitadevam | yathā hi bhavān parikalpayati na tathā loke dṛṣṭam | yasmāt na lokaḥ prāptyaprāpticintāmevamādau viṣaye 'vatārya pradīpādīnāṃ prakāśakatvādikaṃ kalpayati | yathoditaṃ tu vicāramanavatārya pradīpena tamo hatam, cakṣuṣā rūpadarśanam, ayaskāntamaṇinā ayaākarṣaṇam ityādi icchati | paśyatu vā loka evam | tattvavicārakāle tu lokasyāprāmāṇyānna tena bādhā śakyate kartum | evaṃ tāvadaprāpya prakāśanamayuktam | prāptāvapi viṣayādigrahaṇamayuktameva | prāptirhi ekatve sati bhavati | yadā caikatvaṃ tadā svarūpavaddarśanākarṣaṇādikaṃ nāsti ||
body.translated_text: 'This is observed in the world' — if so said, it is not so. For as you imagine, that is not how it is observed in the world. For the world does not first introduce the investigation of contact and non-contact regarding such matters and then postulate the illuminating capacity and so forth of lamps and the like. Rather, without introducing the investigation as stated, it accepts that 'darkness is destroyed by a lamp,' 'form is seen by the eye,' 'iron is attracted by a lodestone,' and so forth. Or let the world see it thus. But at the time of investigating ultimate reality, since the world has no authority, it cannot create an obstruction [to the analysis]. Thus, illumination without contact is not appropriate. Even with contact, the apprehension of objects and so forth is not appropriate. For contact occurs when there is identity. And when there is identity, seeing, attracting, and so forth, as of one's own nature, do not exist.

body.text: yadyapi ceyaṃ prāptyaprāptyādicintā laukikavyavahāre nāvataratīti nirupapattikatvena mṛṣārthatvādasya, tathāpi tattvavicāre 'vatāryā, mā bhūtparamārthato 'pi nirupapattikapakṣābhyupagama ityalaṃ prasaṅgena || 11 ||
body.translated_text: Even though this investigation of contact and non-contact does not enter into worldly convention — and the investigation is without basis and hence of false meaning — nevertheless, it must be introduced in the investigation of ultimate reality, lest there be an acceptance of a baseless position from the ultimate standpoint as well. But enough of this digression. // 11 //

body.text: yadi ca svaparātmānau pradīpaḥ prakāśayatīti parikalpyate tvayā, tamaso 'pi tarhi pratipakṣa bhūtasya svaparātmanoḥ pracchādanaṃ prakalpyatamityāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, if you imagine that the lamp illuminates both itself and others, then let it be imagined that darkness too, being its opposite, conceals both itself and others — hence he says:

children.translated_text: If the lamp illuminates both itself and others, /
then darkness too will undoubtedly conceal both itself and others. // 12 //

body.text: pratidvandvitvātpradīpavat tamo 'pi svaparātmagataṃ vyāpāraṃ kariṣyati, tataśca paravadātmānamapi chādayiṣyati | yadi ca ātmānaṃ chādayettamaḥ, tasyaivānupalabdhiḥ syāt, ghaṭādivattamasā pracchāditatvāt | ata evoktamāryopālipṛcchāyām-
body.translated_text: Being the counterpart [of the lamp], darkness too, like the lamp, will perform its function with respect to itself and others, and hence will conceal itself as well as others. And if darkness conceals itself, there would be non-apprehension of darkness itself, since it would be concealed by darkness — like a pot [concealed by darkness]. Hence it is said in the noble <s>Upāliparipṛcchā</s>:

children.text: iha sāsani sūramaṇīye pravrajathā gṛhiliṅga jahitvā |
children.translated_text: Go forth in this teaching of the sun-like hero, having abandoned the householder's garb! /

children.text: phalavantu bhaviṣyatha śreṣṭho eṣu nideśitu kāruṇikena ||
children.translated_text: You will become fruitful; the supreme [teaching] has been shown by the compassionate one. //

children.text: pravrajitvā gṛhiliṅga jahitvā sarvaphalasya bhaviṣyati prāptiḥ |
children.translated_text: Having gone forth and abandoned the householder's garb, there will be the attainment of all fruits. /

children.text: puna dharmasabhāva tulitvā sarvaphalāna phalāna ca prāptiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And, having weighed the nature of <s>dharmas</s>, there will be the attainment of all fruits — and of non-fruits. //

children.text: alabhanta phalaṃ tatha prāptiṃ āścariyaṃ puna jāyati teṣām |
children.translated_text: They have attained the fruit and the attainment; and yet again wonder arises in them — /

children.text: aho 'tikāruṇiko narasiṃho suṣṭhupadeśita yukti jinena || iti ||
children.translated_text: Oh, how supremely compassionate is the lion among men! How well the method has been taught by the Conqueror! //

body.text: tathāryaratnakūṭasūtre-
body.translated_text: Similarly, in the noble <s>Ratnakūṭasūtra</s>:

children.text: yathā hi dīpo layane cirasya kṛto hi gehe puruṣeṇa kenacit |
children.translated_text: Just as when a lamp is placed by some person in a chamber after a long time, /

children.text: tatrāndhakārasya na bhoti evaṃ cirasthito nāhamito gamiṣye ||
children.translated_text: the darkness there does not say: 'I have been here long; I shall not depart.' //

children.text: tamondhakārasya na śaktirasti kṛte pradīpe na vigacchanāya |
children.translated_text: Darkness has no power, when a lamp is made, not to disappear. /

children.text: pratītya dīpaṃ ca vinaśyate tama ubhayaṃ pi śūnyaṃ na ca kiṃ ca manyati ||
children.translated_text: Dependent on the lamp, darkness perishes — both are empty; one should not conceive of either as something. //

children.text: jñānaṃ tathā ārya pratītya nāsravaṃ ajñāna kleśopacitaṃ vigacchati |
children.translated_text: Likewise, O Noble One, dependent on knowledge free from defilements, ignorance accumulated by afflictions disappears. /

children.text: saṃparka teṣāṃ na kadāci vidyate jñānasya kleśasya ca nityakālam ||
children.translated_text: There is never any contact between knowledge and affliction, at any time. //

body.text:
jñānaṃ na kalpeti añānu no bhavet jñānaṃ pratītyaiva vinaśyate tamo |
bhayaṃ pi agrāhya khapuṣpasaṃnibhaṃ jñānaṃ tathājñānu bhayaṃ pi śūnyam || iti || 12 ||
body.translated_text:
Knowledge does not construct; ignorance would not exist; dependent on knowledge alone, darkness perishes. /
Fear too is ungraspable, like a sky-flower; knowledge, ignorance, and fear are all empty. //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat- ihāyamutpādo yadyātmānamutpādayet, sa utpanno vā svātmānamutpādayet, anutpanno vā? ubhayathā ca nopapadyate ityāha-
body.translated_text: Furthermore: if this arising were to produce itself, would it produce itself as arisen or as unarisen? In both cases it is not possible — hence he says:

children.translated_text: This unarisen arising — how could it produce itself? /

children.text: athotpanno janayate jāte kiṃ janyate punaḥ || 13 ||
children.translated_text: Or, if as arisen it produces — what is produced when it is already born? // 13 //

body.text: yadi anutpanna utpādaḥ svātmānamutpādayet, maṇḍūkajaṭāśiromaṇirapyātmānamutpādayet | atha utpanna utpādayet, kimutpannasyāpareṇotpādena prayojanamiti | evaṃ tāvadutpāda ātmānaṃ notpādayati || 13 ||
body.translated_text: If unarisen arising were to produce itself, then even the crest-jewel on a frog's head would produce itself. And if arisen, it were to produce — what purpose would another production serve for what is already arisen? Thus, arising does not produce itself. // 13 //

body.text: idānīṃ paramapi yathā notpādayati tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, in order to demonstrate that it does not produce another either, he says:

children.translated_text: Neither what is being produced, nor what is [already] produced, nor what is unproduced, in any way, /
is produced — as has been explained [in the analysis of] the being-gone-to, the gone-to, and the not-yet-gone-to. // 14 //

body.text: yadi hi kiṃcidutpadyeta tadutpāda utpādayet | na tu kiṃcidutpadyate 'dhvatraye 'pyutpādāsaṃbhavāt | etacca gamyamānagatāgataiḥ prāgevoktam | tatra yathā gataṃ na gamyate, atītavartamānayorvirodhāt | nāpyagataṃ gamyate, anāgatavartamānayorvirodhāt | nāpi gamyamānaṃ gamyate, gatāgatavyatiriktagamyamānānupalambhādityuktam | evamutpadyamāno bhāvo notpadyate, utpannānutpannavyatirekeṇotpadyamānābhāvāt | utpanno 'pi notpadyate, atītavartamānayorvirodhāt | utpanna ityuparatotpattikriya ucyate, utpadyata iti vartamānakriyāviṣṭaḥ | tataśca utpanna utpadyate ityucyamāne atītavartamānayorekakālatā syāt | anutpanno 'pi notpadyate, anāgatavartamānayorvirodhāt | tasmādutpādaḥ paramutpādayatīti na yuktam || 14 ||
body.translated_text: For if something were to arise, arising would produce it. But nothing arises, because arising is impossible in any of the three times. And this has been stated earlier by means of the being-gone-to, the gone-to, and the not-yet-gone-to. Just as the gone-to is not being gone to, because of the contradiction between past and present; nor is the not-yet-gone-to being gone to, because of the contradiction between future and present; nor is the being-gone-to being gone to, because the being-gone-to is unapprehended apart from the gone-to and the not-yet-gone-to — so too, an entity that is arising does not arise, because the arising entity is non-existent apart from the arisen and the unarisen. The arisen too does not arise, because of the contradiction between past and present — for 'arisen' designates that whose productive action has ceased, while 'arises' designates that which is engaged in a present action. Therefore, when one says 'the arisen arises,' there would be a simultaneity of past and present. The unarisen too does not arise, because of the contradiction between future and present. Therefore, it is not tenable that arising produces something to be arisen. // 14 //

body.text: atrāha- utpadyamānamevotpadyate notpannaṃ nāpyanutpannamiti | atha manyase- utpannānutpannavyatirekeṇa utpadyamānāsaṃbhavānnotpadyamānamutpadyata iti, etacca nāsti, yasmādiha utpattikriyāyuktamutpadyamānamiti vyapadiśyate | tasmādutpattau satyāmutpattiṃ pratītya utpadyamānasiddheḥ utpadyamānamevotpadyate, taccotpadyamānamutpāda utpādayatīti | ucyate-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: it is precisely the arising entity that arises — not the arisen, nor the unarisen. Now, if you think that because the arising entity is impossible apart from the arisen and the unarisen, the arising entity does not arise — this is not so, because here what is conjoined with the productive action is designated as 'arising.' Therefore, since arising exists, and since the arising entity is established in dependence on arising, it is the arising entity itself that arises, and arising produces that arising entity. The reply is:

children.translated_text: When this arising entity does not proceed to arising, /
how can the arising entity be said to exist in dependence on arising? // 15 //

body.text: yaduktam- utpattiṃ pratītya utpadyamānaṃ bhavati, taccotpadyata iti | nanu | viśeṣata etadvaktavyaṃ syāt- asyotpattiṃ pratītya idaṃ nāmotpadyamānaṃ bhavatīti | na caivamucyate | na hi tadutpadyamānaṃ viśeṣato nirdhārayituṃ śakyate idaṃ tadutpadyamānamiti, anutpannatvāttannimittagrahaṇataḥ | tataśca utpadyamānāsaṃbhavādutpattikriyāpi nāstīti | kathamasatyāmutpattau tāṃ pratītya utpadyamānaṃ syāt? tasmādutpadyamānamutpadyate, tacca utpāda utpādayatītyayuktam || 15 ||
body.translated_text: It has been stated that the arising entity exists in dependence on arising, and that it arises. But surely this should be stated with specificity: 'In dependence on this arising, this particular thing becomes an arising entity.' But it is not said thus.
