For that arising entity cannot be specifically determined as 'this is the arising entity,' because being unarisen, it cannot be grasped through its defining mark. And therefore, since the arising entity is impossible, the productive action too does not exist. How then, in the absence of arising, can there be an arising entity in dependence on it? Therefore it is untenable that the arising entity arises, and that arising produces it. // 15 //

body.text: atrāha- aho bata ahamatīva bhavato dṛṣṭādṛṣṭapadārthanirapekṣādatyantanāstikādvibhemi, yo hi nāma bhavāṃstathāgatapravacanavyākhyānavyājena dūṣaṇamātrakauśalamevātmanaḥ prakaṭayan paramarṣigaditamidaṃ pratyayatāpratītyasamutpādalakṣaṇaṃ paramārthasatyaṃ tathāgatānāṃ nihanti | iha bhagavatā tathāgatena prakṛtīśvarasvabhāvakālāṇunārāyaṇajaiminikaṇādakapilāditīrthakarakartṛvādanirāsena sarvabhāvānāṃ tattvamādarśitam, yaduta asmin sati idaṃ bhavati, asyotpādādidamutpadyate, yaduta avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ ityādyaviparītaṃ pratītyasamutpādaṃ prakaṭayatā | tasya ca tvayā notpadyamānaṃ notpannaṃ nānutpannamityādinā dūṣaṇaṃ vidadhatā tathāgatajananyāḥ pratītyasamutpattimāturvadha evācarita ityalaṃ bhavatā sarvanāstikena tvayeti | ucyate | nāhaṃ sakaladaśabalajananīṃ pratītyasamutpattimātaraṃ nihanmi | bhavāneva tu paramagambhīrapratītyasamutpādādhimuktivirahādviparītaṃ tadarthamavadhārya asmākameva adhilayaṃ karoti | nanu ca idaṃ pratītyedaṃ bhavatītyevamabhidhānena bhagavatā tathāgatena niḥsvabhāvatvameva sarvadharmāṇāṃ spaṣṭamāveditam | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: Oh, I am exceedingly afraid of you — an extreme nihilist who disregards all entities, whether seen or unseen! For you, under the guise of expounding the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, merely display your own skill in refutation, while you destroy this ultimate truth of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> — the characteristic of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) as conditionality (<s>pratyayatā</s>), which was declared by the supreme sage! For the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, by rejecting the doctrines of agents proposed by the non-Buddhist founders (<s>tīrthakara</s>) such as <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>svabhāva</s> (inherent nature), <s>kāla</s> (time), <s>aṇu</s> (atoms), <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Jaimini</s>, <s>Kaṇāda</s>, <s>Kapila</s> and others, revealed the true nature of all entities — namely, 'this existing, that comes to be; from the arising of this, that arises; that is, conditioned by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) there are <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations)' and so forth — manifesting the unerring <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>. And you, by presenting the refutation 'neither the arising entity, nor the arisen, nor the unarisen,' have committed the murder of the mother of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>, the mother of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>! Enough of you, you complete nihilist! The reply is: I do not destroy the mother of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>, the mother of all the ten-powered ones. Rather, it is you who, lacking devotion to the supremely profound <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>, ascertain its meaning in a distorted way, and thereby bring ruin upon us. For the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, by the statement 'this existing, that comes to be,' has clearly revealed precisely the absence of inherent nature (<s>niḥsvabhāvatva</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s>. Because:

body.text: pratītya yadyadbhavati tattacchāntaṃ svabhāvataḥ |
body.translated_text: Whatever arises dependently — that is, by its own nature, at peace. /

body.text: yo hi padārtho vidyamānaḥ sa sasvabhāvaḥ svenātmanā svaṃ svabhāvamanapāyinaṃ bimarti | sa saṃvidyamānatvānnaivānyatkiṃcidapekṣate, nāpyutpadyate, iti kṛtvā sasvabhāvabhāvābhyupagame sati kutaḥ pratītyasamutpāda iti bhavateva sasvabhāvatāṃ bhāvānāmabhyupagacchatā sarvathā pratītyasamutpāda eva bādhito bhavati | tataśca paramadharmabuddhadarśanamapi bādhitaṃ bhavati- yaḥ pratītyasamutpādaṃ paśyati sa dharmaṃ paśyati, yo dharmaṃ paśyati sa buddhaṃ paśyatītyāgamāt | mayā tu yatpratītya bījākhyaṃ kāraṇaṃ yadbhavatyaṅkurākhyaṃ kāryam, tacca ubhayamapi śāntaṃ svabhāvavirahitaṃ pratītyasamutpannaṃ pratipādayatā sarvathā bhagavatāṃ tathāgatānāṃ pratītyasamutpattimātā dyotitā bhavati | yata evam-
body.translated_text: For an entity that exists possessing inherent nature grasps its own nature through its own self, without its inherent nature departing. Since it exists, it does not depend on anything else whatsoever, nor does it arise. Therefore, when the existence of entities possessing inherent nature is accepted, whence could there be <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>? Thus it is precisely you who, by accepting the inherent-nature-possessing character of entities, completely obstruct <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> itself. And thereby the supreme <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Buddha</s>-vision too is obstructed — because of the scripture: 'Whoever sees <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> sees the <s>Dharma</s>; whoever sees the <s>Dharma</s> sees the <s>Buddha</s>.' But I, by demonstrating that whatever arises in dependence on a cause called a seed, producing an effect called a sprout, and that both of these are at peace, devoid of inherent nature, and dependently arisen — thereby illuminate the mother of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> of all the <s>Bhagavāns</s> and <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Since it is thus:

body.text: tasmādutpadyamānaṃ ca śāntamutpattireva ca || 16 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, the arising entity is at peace, and arising itself [is at peace]. // 16 //

body.text: iti sphuṭamavasīyatām || 16 ||
body.translated_text: Let this be clearly concluded. // 16 //

body.text: atrāha- yaduktam-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: it has been stated —

children.translated_text: When this arising entity does not proceed to arising, /
how can the arising entity be said to exist in dependence on arising? //

body.text: iti, tadayuktam | yasmādidamutpadyamānamityeva saṃbhavati | tathā hi ghaṭotpattiṃ pratītya ghaṭa utpadyamāno bhavati, taṃ ca utpadyamānamutpāda utpādayatītyucyate | etadapyayuktam | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: — this is not correct. Because it is possible that 'this is an arising entity.' For a pot, in dependence on its arising, becomes an arising entity, and it is said that arising produces that arising entity. This too is not correct. Because:

children.translated_text: If some unarisen entity were to exist somewhere, /

children.text: utpadyeta sa kiṃ tasmin bhāva utpadyate 'sati || 17 ||
children.translated_text: it could arise. But when that entity does not exist, what arises? // 17 //

body.text: yadi kaścidanutpannaḥ utpādātpūrvaṃ ghaṭo nāma kvacitsaṃvidyeta, sa utpattikriyāṃ pratītyotpadyeta na caivaṃ kaścidutpādātpūrvaṃ kvacidasti | tasminnasati ghaṭe kimutpadyate?
body.translated_text: If some unarisen thing called a pot existed somewhere prior to arising, it could arise in dependence on the productive action. But nothing whatsoever exists anywhere prior to arising. When that pot does not exist, what arises?

body.text: atha syāt- yadyutpādātpūrvaṃ ghaṭo nāsti, tathāpi utpannaḥ san ghaṭasaṃjñāṃ pratilapsyate, tadbhāvinyā saṃjñayā na doṣa iti | etadapyayuktam | yadi hi utpattikriyā pravarteta, tadā vartamānībhūto bhāvo ghaṭākhyāṃ pratilabheta | yadā tu anāgatabhāvāsaṃbandhena kriyāyā apravṛttiḥ, tadā kuto vartamānatā? atha aghaṭāśrayeṇa kriyā prārabhyeta, tadvaktavyam- yo 'sau aghaṭaḥ, sa kiṃ bhaviturmahati paṭaḥ, uta naiva kiṃcit? yadi paṭa utpadyamānaḥ sa kathamutpannaḥ san ghaṭo bhaviṣyatīti atha naivaṃ kiṃcit, kathaṃ tadāśrayā kriyā kriyā pravartate? kathaṃ vā sa utpannaḥ san ghaṭo bhavet? iti sarvathā bhāvitatvakalpanāpyayuktā | tasmādutpadyamānamapyutpādo notpādayatiti siddham || 17 ||
body.translated_text: Now, one might say: even though the pot does not exist prior to arising, nevertheless, having arisen, it will acquire the designation 'pot,' and since the designation pertains to its future state, there is no fault. This too is not correct. For if the productive action were to proceed, then the entity, having become present, would acquire the name 'pot.' But when, because of its non-connection with a future entity, the action does not proceed, whence would there be presentness? Or if the action were to begin with something that is a non-pot as its basis, then one must say: that which is a non-pot — is what is about to come into being a cloth, or nothing at all? If it is a cloth that is arising, how, having arisen, will it become a pot? And if it is nothing at all, how does an action based on that proceed? And how could it, having arisen, become a pot? Thus, in every way, the supposition of its future becoming is untenable. Therefore it is established that arising does not produce even the arising entity. // 17 //

body.text: api ca | evaṃ na yujyamānāyāmapyutpadyamānasyotpattau bhavato matamabhyupetyocyate-
body.translated_text: Moreover, even though the arising of the arising entity is not tenable in this way, we state the following by accepting your position for the sake of argument:

children.translated_text: If arising produces the arising entity, /
which arising in turn will produce that arising? // 18 //

body.text: yadyapi utpadyamānaṃ padārthamutpāda utpādayedbhavanmatena, idaṃ tu vaktavyam- tamidānīmutpādaḥ katamo 'paraḥ utpādamutpādayiṣyatīti || 18 ||
body.translated_text: Even if, according to your view, arising were to produce the arising entity, this must be stated: which other arising will produce that arising in turn? // 18 //

body.text:
atha syāt- utpādasyāpara utpādaḥ utpādakaḥ parikalpyeta, tadā anavasthādoṣaprasaṅga ityāha-
anya utpādatyenaṃ yadyutpādo 'navasthitiḥ |
body.translated_text:
Now, if another arising were to be conceived as the producer of arising, then there would be the defect of infinite regress — hence he says:
If another arising produces this one, there is infinite regress. /

body.text: etaccoktam | atha nāsyāpara utpāda iṣyate, nanvevaṃ sati vinā utpādena utpāda utpadyate ityevaṃ prāpnoti | tataśca utpādotpādyānāmapi padārthānāṃ vinaivotpādena utpattirastu bhāvatvādutpādavaditi pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And this has been stated. Now, if no other arising is accepted for it, then it follows that arising arises without an arising. And therefore, let the entities that are to be produced by arising also come into being without any arising at all, since they are entities, just like arising — demonstrating this, he says:

body.text: athānutpāda utpannaḥ sarvamutpadyate tathā || 19 ||
body.translated_text: If, on the other hand, the unarisen arises, then everything arises in the same way. // 19 //

body.text: api ca | utpāda ātmānaṃ parāṃścotpādayatītyatra pakṣe dūṣaṇameva na vaktavyamadhunāsmābhiḥ | yasmādatra pakṣe dūṣaṇam-
body.translated_text: Moreover, regarding the position that arising produces both itself and others, we need not even state a refutation now. Because in this position, the refutation is:

children.translated_text: The arising of what exists and of what does not exist is not tenable — /
nor of what both exists and does not exist — this has been demonstrated previously. // 20 //

body.text: naivāsato naiva sataḥ pratyayo 'rthasya yujyate |
body.translated_text: A condition is tenable neither for an existent object nor for a non-existent one. /

body.text: iti
body.translated_text: Thus,

body.text: na sannāsanna sadasan dharmo nirvartate yadā |
body.translated_text: Since a <s>dharma</s> that is neither existent, nor non-existent, nor both existent and non-existent does not come about — /

body.text: ityādinā utpādo niṣiddha eva pūrvam | tataścaivamutpāde niṣiddhe utpadyamānamutpāda utpādayati, svaparātmānau vā utpādayatītyasyāḥ kalpanāyā nāstyevāvatāra iti kuta etatprasetsyati- utpāda utpadyate, utpadyamānamutpadyate, svaparātmānau cotpādayatīti || 20 ||
body.translated_text: and so forth — arising was already negated previously. And since arising has thus been negated, the supposition that 'arising produces the arising entity' or 'it produces both itself and others' has no entry at all. So how can this be established: 'arising arises,' 'the arising entity arises,' and 'it produces both itself and others'? // 20 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat- ihāyamutpādaḥ parikalpyamānaḥ nirudhyamānasya anityatānugatasya vartamānasya vā bhāvasya parikalpyate, anirudhyamānasya vā atītānāgatasyānityatāvirahitasya? ubhayathā ca nopapadyate ityāha-
body.translated_text: What is more: is this arising, when conceived, conceived of an entity that is perishing — one that is present and attended by impermanence — or of one that is not perishing — one that is past or future and devoid of impermanence? In both cases it is untenable — hence he says:

children.translated_text: The arising of an entity that is perishing is not tenable. /
And an entity that is not perishing — that entity is [itself] not tenable. // 21 //

body.text: tatra nirudhyamānasya vartamānasya vidyamānatvādutpādo nopapadyate | anirudhyamānasyāpi vināśarahitasya atītānāgatasya bhāvalakṣaṇavilakṣaṇasya khapuṣpasyeva nāstyutpāda iti || 21 ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the arising of a perishing, present entity is not tenable because of its [already] being existent. And for one that is not perishing — one that is devoid of destruction, being past or future, differing from the defining characteristic of an entity — there is no arising, just as for a sky-flower. // 21 //

body.text: evaṃ bhāvānāmutpādābhāvaṃ pratipādya ataḥ paraṃ sthitirvicāryate ||
body.translated_text: Having thus demonstrated the non-existence of the arising of entities, hereafter duration (<s>sthiti</s>) is examined.

body.text: atrāha- vidyata eva bhāvānāmutpādaḥ, tadbhāvabhāvidharmasadbhāvāt | nānutpannasya sthiti saṃbhavatītyutpādabhāvena sthiterbhāvāt | sthitirutpādabhāvabhāvinī bhavati | tasmādutpādo 'pyasti, tadbhāvabhāvidharmasadbhāvāt | iha yannāsti, na tadbhāvabhāvidharmasadbhāvaḥ, tadyathā gaganakusumasaurabhyasyeti ucyate | syādutpādaḥ, yadi tadbhāvabhāvinī sthitireva syāt | na tvasti | tadevam-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: the arising of entities does indeed exist, because of the existence of properties that presuppose its existence. For duration is not possible for what has not arisen; hence, from the existence of duration, the existence of arising follows. Duration is that which presupposes the existence of arising. Therefore arising too exists, because of the existence of properties that presuppose it — for what does not exist does not have properties that presuppose its existence, just as the fragrance of a sky-flower does not exist. The reply is: arising would exist if duration, which presupposes its existence, itself existed. But it does not. Thus:

children.translated_text: A standing entity does not stand; a non-standing entity does not stand. /
Nor does a standing-in-process stand. And what unarisen thing stands? // 22 //

body.text: tatra sthitaṃ na tiṣṭhati tatra sthitikriyānirodhāt | asthitabhāvo 'pi na tiṣṭhati sthitirahitatvāt | tiṣṭhamānamapi na tiṣṭhati sthitidvayaprasaṅgāt, sthitāsthitavyatiriktasaṃtiṣṭhamānābhāvācca api ca |
body.translated_text: Therein, what has [already] stood does not stand, because the action of standing has ceased therein. A non-standing entity too does not stand, because it is devoid of standing. That which is in the process of standing too does not stand, because of the absurd consequence of two standings, and because the standing-in-process is non-existent apart from the stood and the non-stood. Moreover:

body.text: ko 'nutpannaśca tiṣṭhati |
body.translated_text: And what unarisen thing stands? /

body.text: ihotpādapratiṣedhātko 'sāvanutpannaḥ padārtho yastiṣṭhediti sarvathā nāsti sthitiḥ || 22 ||
body.translated_text: Here, since arising has been refuted, what unarisen entity could stand? Thus, duration does not exist in any way. // 22 //

body.text: api ca | iyaṃ sthitirnirudhyamānasya bhāvasya syādanirudhyamānasya vā? ubhayathā ca na yujyate iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, would this duration belong to an entity that is perishing, or to one that is not perishing? In both cases it is not tenable — demonstrating this, he says:

children.translated_text: Duration is not tenable for an entity that is perishing. /
And an entity that is not perishing — that entity is [itself] not tenable. // 23 //

body.text: nirudhyamānasya nirodhābhimukhasya tāvadbhāvasya virodhinī sthitirna saṃbhavati | yaścāpyanirudhyamānaḥ sa bhāva eva na bhavati, kutastasya sthitirbhaviṣyati || 23 ||
body.translated_text: The duration of a perishing entity — one that is facing destruction — is not possible, being contradictory. And one that is not perishing — that is not even an entity at all; how then could there be duration for it? // 23 //

body.text: api ca | jarasā maraṇena ca sarva eva bhāvāḥ kṣaṇamapi na tyajyante | yadā caitadevam tadā jarāmaraṇavirodhinyāḥ sthiterbhāveṣu pravṛttyavakāśa eva nāstīti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, all entities are never, not even for a moment, free from old age and death. And when this is so, there is simply no room for the operation of duration — which is contradictory to old age and death — in entities. Demonstrating this, he says:

children.translated_text: In all entities, which are subject to old age and death, always —

children.text: tiṣṭhanti katame bhāvā ye jarāmaraṇaṃ vinā || 24 ||
children.translated_text: What entities are there that are without old age and death? // 24 //

body.text: ke hi nāma jarāmaraṇarahitā bhāvā yeṣāṃ sthitiḥ syāt? tasmānnāstyeva sthitirityabhiprāyaḥ || 24 ||
body.translated_text: For what entities, devoid of old age and death, could there be persistence? Therefore, there is no persistence at all — this is the intent. // 24 //

body.text: yadi ca, asyāḥ sthiteranyā vā sthitiḥ sthityarthaṃ parikalpyeta, svayaṃ vā svātmānaṃ sthāpayet | ubhayathā ca na yujyate ityāha-
body.translated_text: And if for this persistence, either another persistence is imagined for the purpose of sustaining it, or it itself sustains itself — in both cases it is not justified. He says:

children.text: sthityānyayā sthiteḥ sthānaṃ tayaiva ca na yujyate |
children.translated_text: Persistence of persistence through another [persistence] is not justified, nor by itself. /
Just as arising does not [arise] by its own self, nor by another self — so too for arising. // 25 //

body.text: 'anutpanno 'yamutpādaḥ svātmānaṃ janayetkatham |'; ityādinā yathā utpāda ātmānaṃ na janayati ityuktam, evaṃ sthitirapi nātmānaṃ sthāpayatīti vaktavyam |
body.translated_text: Just as it was said 'This unarisen arising — how would it generate its own self?' and so forth, showing that arising does not generate itself — even so, it should be stated that persistence too does not sustain itself:

children.translated_text: 'If this persistence is itself unestablished, how would it sustain its own self?
And if it is [already] established and sustains, then what is to be sustained for something already established?'

body.text: iti yojyam | yathā ca-
body.translated_text: — thus it should be connected. And just as:

body.text: anya utpādayatyenaṃ yadyutpādo 'navasthitiḥ |
body.translated_text: 'If another generates this arising, then there would be an infinite regress' —

body.text: ityutpāde vyākhyātam, evaṃ sthitāvapi vyākhyeyam-
body.translated_text: was explained regarding arising, even so regarding persistence it should be explained:

body.text: athānyā sthāpayatyenāṃ sthitiryadyanavasthitiḥ |
body.translated_text: 'If another persistence sustains this one, then there would be an infinite regress.'

body.text: iti | evaṃ sthitirapi na yuktā | ata evoktaṃ bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: Thus persistence too is not justified. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said:

children.text: asthitā hi ime dharmāḥ sthitiścaiṣāṃ na vidyate |
children.translated_text: For these <s>dharmas</s> are unestablished, and no persistence is found in them. /
Non-persistence, by the word 'persistence,' does not exist by its own nature. //

body.text:
na sthitirnāpi co jātirlokanāthena deśitā
lokanāthaṃ viditvaivaṃ samādhiṃ tena jānathā || iti ||
body.translated_text:
Neither persistence nor birth was taught by the Protector of the World.
Having understood the Protector of the World thus, know the <s>samādhi</s> accordingly. //

body.text: uktaṃ ca āryasacaryagāthāsu-
body.translated_text: And it is said in the noble <s>Sancaryagāthā</s> (<s>Āryasancaryagāthās</s>):

children.text: ākāśaniśrita samāruta āpakhandho tanniśritā iya mahī pṛthivī jagacca |
children.translated_text: The mass of water rests upon the wind that rests upon space; this great earth and the world rest upon that. /

children.text: sattvāna karmaupabhoganidānamevaṃ ākāśathānu kṛta cittama etamartham ||
children.translated_text: The cause is the <s>karma</s> and enjoyment of beings — understand that like the nature of space is the mind, for this meaning. //

body.text: yāvat-
body.translated_text: Up to:

body.text: sthānammayānu ayu thānu jinena ukto ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Jina</s> (Victor) has declared that an abode is like an abode of life. //

body.text: iti vistaraḥ || 25 ||
body.translated_text: Thus the detailed exposition. // 25 //

body.text: atrāha- vidyete eva sthityutpādau tatsahacāridharmasadbhāvāt | iha utpādasthitilakṣaṇasahacāriṇī saṃskṛtānāmanityatāsti | tasmātsthityutpādāvapi staḥ iti | ucyate | syāta sthityutpādau, yadi anityataiva syāt | na tvasti | kathamiti? yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: Persistence and arising do indeed exist, because of the existence of their co-accompanying <s>dharma</s>. Here, impermanence, which co-accompanies the marks of arising, persistence, and cessation, belongs to conditioned things (<s>saṃskṛta</s>). Therefore persistence and arising also exist. We reply: Persistence and arising would exist if impermanence itself existed. But it does not. How so? Because:

children.translated_text: The unceased does not cease; the ceased does not cease. /
Likewise, the ceasing — does the unborn cease? // 26 //

body.text: yadi anityateti kācitsyāt, sā niruddhasya bhāvasya aniruddhasya vā nirudhyamānasya vā syāt | tatra niruddhaṃ nirudhyate iti na yuktam, atītavartamānayorvirodhāt | aniruddhamapi na yuktam, nirodhavirahitatvāt, yadaniruddhameva tatkathaṃ nirudhyata iti parasparavirodhācca | tathāpi nirudhyamānaṃ na nirudhyate ityanena saṃbandhaḥ | nirudhyamānamapi na nirudhyate nirudhyamānābhāvāt,
body.translated_text: If there were something called impermanence, it would belong either to a ceased entity, or to an unceased entity, or to one that is ceasing. Therein, it is not justified that the ceased ceases, because the past and the present are contradictory. The unceased too is not justified, because it is devoid of cessation, and because [saying] that what is unceased ceases involves mutual contradiction. 'Likewise, the ceasing does not cease' — the connection is with this. The ceasing too does not cease, because the ceasing as such does not exist

body.text: nirodhadvayaprasaṅgācca | yataścaivaṃ triṣvapi kāleṣu nirodhāsaṃbhavaḥ, tasmānnāstyeva nirodha iti kutastatsahacāristhityutpādasaṃbhavaḥ syāt? api ca | prāgutpādapratiṣedhādasaṃbhava eva nirodhasyetyāha-
body.translated_text: , and because the consequence of a double cessation would follow. And since cessation is thus impossible in all three times, there is no cessation at all — so how could persistence and arising, which accompany it, be possible? Moreover, from the prior refutation of arising, the impossibility of cessation follows — he says:

body.text: kimajātaṃ nirudhyate |
body.translated_text: Does the unborn cease?

body.text: api ca | ayaṃ nirodhaḥ sthitasya vā bhāvasya syādasthitasya vā? ubhayathā ca na yujyate ityāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, does this cessation belong to an entity that has persisted, or to one that has not persisted? In both cases it is not justified — he says:

body.text: sthitasya tāvadbhāvasya nirodho nopapadyate |
body.translated_text: First, the cessation of an entity that has persisted is not established. /

body.text: sthitasya nirodhaviruddhasya nāsti nirodhaḥ |
body.translated_text: The cessation of an entity that has persisted, which is opposed to cessation, does not exist.

body.text: nāsthitasyāpi bhāvasya nirodha upapadyate || 27 ||
body.translated_text: Nor is the cessation of an entity that has not persisted established. // 27 //

body.text: asthitasya abhāvasya avidyamānasya nirodho nāsti, iti sarvathā nāsti nirodhaḥ || 27 ||
body.translated_text: The cessation of what has not persisted — of what is non-existent, of what does not exist — does not obtain. Thus cessation does not exist in any way. // 27 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat | yadi iha nirodhaḥ syāt, sa tayaivāvasthayā tasyā evāvasthāyāḥ syādanyayā vā anyasyā avasthāyāḥ syāt | sarvathā ca nopapadyate iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: What further: if cessation existed here, would it be the cessation of that very state by that very state, or the cessation of one state by another? In no case is it established — demonstrating this, he says:

children.translated_text: A state does not cease by that very same state. /
Nor does one state cease by another state. // 28 //

body.text: tayaiva tāvatkṣīrāvasthayā saiva kṣīrāvasthā na nirudhyate, svātmani kriyāvirodhāt | nāpyanyayā dadhyavasthayā kṣīrāvasthā nirudhyate | yadi hi kṣīradadhyavasthayoryaugapadyaṃ syāt, syāttayorvināśyavināśakabhāvaḥ | na tu dadhyavasthāyāṃ kṣīrāvasthā asti | yadā ca nāsti, tadā kāmasatī vināśayet? yadi vināśayet, kharaviṣāṇatīkṣṇatāmapi vināśayet | tasmādanyayāpyavasthayā naivānyāvasthā nirudhyate || 28 ||
body.translated_text: First, the state of milk does not cease by that very same state of milk, because of the contradiction of an action operating upon itself. Nor does the state of milk cease by another state, namely the state of curds. For if the states of milk and curds existed simultaneously, there could be a relation of destroyer and destroyed between them. But the state of milk does not exist in the state of curds. And when it does not exist, how could it destroy it, even if it wished? If it could, it could also destroy the sharpness of a donkey's horn. Therefore, even by another state, one state does not cease. // 28 //

body.text: atrāha- yadyapi tayaivāvasthayā saivāvasthyā, anyayā vā avasthayā anyāvasthā na nirudhyate, tathāpi kṣīrāvasthāyāstāvannirodho 'sti, tataśca utpādo 'pi syāditi | ucyate | aho bata atijaḍatāmātmano bhavān prakaṭayati | nanu ca pūrvoktena nyāyena
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: Even though a state does not cease by that very same state, nor one state by another, nevertheless there is cessation of the state of milk, and from that there would also be arising. We reply: Alas, you are displaying your own extreme dullness! For by the reasoning stated above:

body.text: yadaivaṃ sarvadharmāṇāmutpādo nopapadyate |
body.translated_text: When the arising of all <s>dharmas</s> is not established in this way, /

body.text: ityuktam,
body.translated_text: it was said,

body.text: tadaivaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ nirodho nopapadyate || 29 ||
body.translated_text: then the cessation of all <s>dharmas</s> is [also] not established in this way. // 29 //

body.text: iti sphuṭatarameva pratipāditaṃ bhavati || 29 ||
body.translated_text: This is demonstrated most clearly. // 29 //

body.text: api ca | nirodho nāma yadi kaścit syāt, sa sato vā bhāvasya syādasato vā | tatra-
body.translated_text: Moreover, if cessation were something that destroys entities, does it now have another cessation, or not? If so, that is not justified.

body.text: sataśca tāvadbhāvasya nirodho nopapadyate |
body.translated_text: Cessation does not [come about] by its own self; cessation does not [come about] by another self. /

body.text: svabhāvādapracyutasya bhāvasya nirodho na yuktaḥ | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: The cessation of an entity that has not deviated from its own nature is not justified. Because:

body.text: ekatve na hi bhāvaśca nābhāvaścopapadyate || 30 ||
body.translated_text: In unity, neither entity nor non-entity is established. // 30 //

body.text: nirodho hi nāma abhāvaḥ | sa yasya bhavati, sa naiva bhavati | tataśca sato bhāvasya nirodha iti bruvatā bhāvābhāvayorekādhikaraṇatā abhyupagatā bhavati | ekatve sati ubhayaṃ na yujyate | yadi tadānīṃ bhāvaḥ syāt, tadā nirodhenābhāvenāveśādbhāvavyapadeśo 'yuktaḥ | atha abhāvaḥ, so 'pyasya na yujyate, abhāvavirodhinā bhāvarūpeṇāviyogāt | tasmādekatve sati bhāvābhāvayoḥ sa padārtho naiva bhāvo nāpyabhāva iti yujyate | athavā, parasparaviruddhatvādālokāndhakāravadekatve sati na hi bhāvaśca nābhāvaścopapadyate | evaṃ tāvatsato bhāvasya nirodho na yuktaḥ || 30 ||
body.translated_text: For cessation is precisely non-existence. That to which it pertains simply does not exist. Therefore, one who says 'there is cessation of an existent entity' has accepted the co-location of entity and non-entity in one substrate. When there is unity, both are not justified. If at that time it were an entity, then, through the intrusion of non-existence as cessation, the designation 'entity' would be unjustified. But if it were non-entity, that too is not justified for it, because it is inseparable from the form of entity, which is opposed to non-entity. Therefore, when there is unity, that thing is neither entity nor non-entity. Alternatively, because they are mutually contradictory — like light and darkness — when there is unity, neither entity nor non-entity is established. Thus, the cessation of an existent entity is not justified. // 30 //

body.text: idānīm-
body.translated_text: Now:

body.text: asato 'pi na bhāvasya nirodha upapadyate |
body.translated_text: The cessation of a non-existent entity too is not established. /

body.text: avidyamānasyābhāvasya na vināśo 'sti vandhyātanayasyeva, avidyamānatvāt | ata evāha-
body.translated_text: There is no destruction of what does not exist, of what is non-existent — like the son of a barren woman — because of its non-existence. Therefore he says:

body.text: na dvitīyasya śirasacchedanaṃ vidyate yathā || 31 ||
body.translated_text: Just as there is no cutting off of a second head. // 31 //

body.text: prasiddhāsattvasyaiva narāṇāṃ dvitīyasya śiraso dṛṣṭāntatvenopādānānnirdeśāpūrṇatvānnāstīti nopāttam | tadevamasato bhāvasya nirodho na saṃbhavati, sato 'pi na | yaścobhayathāpi na saṃbhavati, sa kenātmanā sthitaḥ? nāstyeva nirodha iti pratīyatām || 31 ||
body.translated_text: Since the non-existence of a second head of a person is well-established, its use as an example is [sufficient], and therefore the word 'does not exist' is not added, to avoid redundancy in the statement. Thus, the cessation of a non-existent entity is not possible; nor of an existent one. And what is not possible in either way — in what form does it stand? Let it be understood that cessation simply does not exist. // 31 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat | yadi nirodho nāma bhāvānāṃ nirodhaka iti kalpyate, tasyedānīṃ kimanyo nirodha iṣyate, uta na? yadi iṣyate tanna yujyate |
body.translated_text: Moreover, if cessation is conceived as the destroyer of entities, is another cessation now desired for it, or not? If so, that is not justified.

body.text: na svātmanā nirodho 'sti nirodho na parātmanā |
body.translated_text: Cessation does not [come about] by its own self; nor by another self. /

body.text: kathaṃ punarnāstīti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: How so? Demonstrating this, he says:

body.text: utpādasya yathotpādo nātmanā na parātmanā || 32 ||
body.translated_text: Just as arising does not [arise] by its own self, nor by another self. // 32 //

body.text: tatra yathā-
body.translated_text: Therein, just as:

body.text: anutpanno 'yamutpādaḥ svātmānaṃ janayetkatham |
body.translated_text: 'This unarisen arising — how would it generate its own self?' —

body.text: ityādinā utpādaḥ svātmānaṃ notpādayati, evaṃ nirodho 'pi svātmānaṃ na nirodhayati | kathamiti? ucyate-
body.translated_text: and so forth — arising does not generate itself. Even so, cessation too does not destroy itself. How? We reply:

children.translated_text: 'This unceased cessation — how would it destroy its own self?

children.text: atha naṣṭo nāśayati naṣṭe kiṃ nāśyate punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And if it is [already] destroyed and destroys, what is destroyed for something already destroyed?'

body.text: iti samamutpādena vaktavyam | evaṃ ca svātmanā na nirodho 'sti | nirodha idānīṃ parātmanāpi nāsti | katham? tatra yathā utpāde gaditam- 'anya utpādayatyenam'; ityādi, evaṃ nirodhe 'pi vaktavyam-
body.translated_text: — this should be stated on par with arising. Thus, cessation does not [come about] by its own self. Now, cessation does not [come about] by another self either. How? Therein, just as was said regarding arising — 'If another generates it...' and so forth — even so regarding cessation it should be stated:

children.translated_text: 'If another destroys it, then the destruction would involve an infinite regress. /

children.text: athāvināśo naṣṭo 'yaṃ sarvaṃ naśyatu te tathā ||
children.translated_text: And if it is [already] undestroyed and destroyed, then let everything be destroyed in that way for you.' //

body.text: iti | tadevaṃ parātmanāpi nirodho na saṃbhavatīti nāsti nirodhasya nirodhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus, cessation does not come about by another self either — therefore there is no cessation of cessation.

body.text: atha manyase- nāstyeva nirodhasya nirodha iti, tadayuktam | yadi hi nirodhasya nirodho na syāta, tadā nirodharahitatvātsaṃskṛtalakṣaṇamavahīyate | tadevaṃ yadi vināśasya vināśaḥ parikalpyate tathāpi na yukto vināśaḥ | atha na parikalpyate, tathāpi na yukta iti | kathaṃ tvidānīṃ vināśo yokṣyate parasya? atha syāt- tathāpi evameva vicāre sati vināśo bhavato 'pi na yujyate, tataḥ ya ubhayordoṣaḥ, na tenaikaścodyo bhavatīti | ucyate | naivedaṃ codyaṃ mamāpatati | kiṃ kāraṇam? ye svātmanā niḥsvabhāvā bhāvāḥ, te ca niḥsvabhāvā eva santo bālānāmidaṃsatyābhiniveśināṃ vyavahārapathamupayānti avicāraprasiddhenaiva nyāyeneti teṣu nāsti yathoditavicārāvatāro 'smākam māyāsvapnagandharvanagarādivattu laukikāḥ padārthā nirupapattikā eva santaḥ sarvalokasyāvidyātimiropahatamatinayanasya prasiddhimupagatā iti parasparāpekṣayaiva kevalaṃ prasiddhimupagatā bālairabhyupagamyante | yathoktaṃ śatake-
body.translated_text: If you think 'There is indeed no cessation of cessation' — that is not justified. For if there were no cessation of cessation, then, being devoid of cessation, the conditioned mark (<s>saṃskṛtalakṣaṇa</s>) would be forfeited. Thus, if the destruction of destruction is posited, even so destruction is not justified; and if it is not posited, even so it is not justified. How then will destruction be justified for the opponent? If it be said: 'Even so, upon such examination, destruction is not justified for you either; therefore, what is a defect for both cannot be raised by one party alone' — we reply: This objection does not apply to me. For what reason? Because entities that are without inherent nature by their own nature — those very entities, being without inherent nature, enter the path of conventional usage for foolish beings who cling to 'this is real,' through the very reasoning of being established without examination. There is no entry for the above-mentioned examination on our part regarding them. Rather, conventional things — like illusions, dreams, <s>gandharva</s>-cities, and so forth — while being devoid of rational establishment, have come to be accepted by the entire world whose mental vision is impaired by the darkness of ignorance. Through mere mutual dependence alone, they are accepted by the foolish. As stated in the <s>Catuḥśataka</s>:

children.translated_text: Existence is like a whirling firebrand, a magical creation, a dream, an illusion, the moon in water, /
a mist, an echo within, a mirage, and a cloud. //

body.text: tasmātsati utpāde utpādyam, sati utpādye utpādaḥ | sati nirodhe nirodhyam, sati nirodhye nirodhaḥ, ityevaṃ laukikasya vyavahārasyābhyupagamātkuto 'smatpakṣe samaprasaṅgitā bhavitumarhati |
body.translated_text: Therefore, when there is arising, there is that which is to arise; when there is that which is to arise, there is arising. When there is cessation, there is that which is to cease; when there is that which is to cease, there is cessation. Thus, from the acceptance of worldly convention, how can there be a parallel consequence in our position?

body.text: yastu vināśasya ahetukatvamabhyupetya kṣaṇikatāṃ saṃskārāṇāmāha, tasya nirhetukatvāt | khapuṣpavadvināśābhāvāt kutaḥ kṣaṇikatvaṃ bhāvānāṃ setsyati, kuto vināśarahitānāṃ saṃskṛtatvamapīti sarvameva asamañjasaṃ tasya jāyate | jātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ saṃskṛtalakṣaṇānāṃ ca saṃskāraskandhāntarbhāva varṇayatā bhagavatā nanu sahetukatvaṃ spaṣṭamādarśitaṃ vināśasya | jātimātrāpekṣatvāccāsya kṣaṇabhaṅgo 'pi sukhasādhya iti sarvaṃ susthaṃ jāyate ||
body.translated_text: But one who, having accepted the causelessness of destruction, asserts the momentariness of conditioned things — for him, since destruction is without cause and therefore, like a flower in the sky, non-existent, how will the momentariness of entities be established? And how will the conditioned nature of things devoid of destruction [be established]? Thus everything becomes inconsistent for him. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, in teaching that old age and death are conditioned by birth, and in explaining the inclusion within the aggregate of formations (<s>saṃskāraskandha</s>) of those that bear the conditioned marks, has clearly shown that destruction is causally conditioned. And since destruction depends merely on birth, its momentary destruction (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) too is easily established — thus everything is well.

body.text: atha syāt- vināśo hi nāma abhāvaḥ, yaśca abhāvaḥ, kiṃ tasya hetunā kartavyam | ato nirhetuko vināśa iti | nanu ca bhāve 'pi hetvabhāvaprasaṅgo bhavati | bhāvo hi nāma vidyamānaḥ, yaśca vidyamānaḥ tasya ca kiṃ hetunā prayojanam? na hi jātaṃ punarapi janyate | tasmātsarvatraiva hetvabhāvaprasaṅgādayuktametat ||
body.translated_text: If it be said: 'Destruction is non-existence, and what is non-existent — what is to be done with a cause for it? Therefore destruction is without a cause' — But the consequence of causelessness would apply to [positive] entity too! For entity means 'existent,' and what is existent — what purpose does a cause serve for it? For what has already arisen is not arisen again. Therefore, since the consequence of causelessness applies everywhere, this is not justified.

body.text: api ca | yathā utpādaḥ sahetukaḥ pūrvamabhāvātpaścācca bhāvāt, evaṃ vināśo 'pīṣyatām | vināśo hi na sarvadā bhavati, utpādātpūrvamabhāvātpaścācca bhāvāt | yaccocyate- yaścābhāvaḥ tasya
body.translated_text: Moreover, just as arising is causally conditioned — because of its prior non-existence and subsequent existence — even so, let destruction be accepted [as conditioned]. For destruction does not exist at all times — because of its prior non-existence and subsequent existence. And what is said — 'that which is non-existent, for it

body.text: kiṃ hetunā kartavyamiti, tadayuktam | yasmānna vayaṃ vināśasya hetunā kiṃcitkriyamāṇamicchāmaḥ, kiṃ tarhi vināśa eva kriyate iti varṇayāmaḥ | nanvevaṃ sati kriyamāṇatvādvināśo 'pi bhāvaḥ prāpnotīti cet, iṣyata evaitat | vināśo hi svarūpāpekṣayā bhāvaḥ, rūpādidharmanivṛttisvabhāvatvāttu na bhāvaḥ | api ca | maraṇamapi dvividhakāryapratyupasthāpanaṃ saṃskāravidhvaṃsanaṃ ca karoti | aparijñānānupacchedaṃ (?) cetyāgamāt kathaṃ na sahetuko vināśaḥ? api ca | kalpitābhāvalakṣaṇāyāśca śūnyatāyāḥ pareṇa bhāvarūpatāmabhyupagacchatā kathamabhāvasya bhāvatvaṃ nābhyupagataṃ bhavati? bhāvatvācca kathamasaṃskṛtatvaṃ śūnyatāyāḥ syāt? ataḥ sarvamabhyupetaṃ vihīyate bhavatā | ata eva vakṣyati-
body.translated_text: [that] something must be done by a cause of destruction — that is improper. For we do not maintain that anything whatsoever is brought about by a cause of destruction; rather, we explain that destruction itself takes place. If it be objected that, this being so, destruction too, being something brought about, would be an entity — this is indeed accepted. For destruction, with respect to its own form, is an entity; but since its nature is the cessation of properties such as form and so forth, it is not an entity. Moreover, death too accomplishes a twofold function: the presentation of a [future] effect and the dissolution of formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>). And from the scriptural statement that 'through non-comprehension, there is non-cessation,' how can destruction be without a cause? Moreover, when the opponent accepts the nature of an entity for <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), whose characteristic is an imagined non-existence, how does he not also accept that non-existence has the nature of existence? And if it has the nature of existence, how could the unconditioned nature of <s>śūnyatā</s> be maintained? Thus, everything accepted by you is undermined. For that very reason, it will be said —

children.translated_text: How could <s>nirvāṇa</s> be both an entity and a non-entity? /

children.text: na saṃskṛtaṃ hi nirvāṇaṃ bhāvābhāvau ca saṃskṛtau ||
children.translated_text: For <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not conditioned, while both entity and non-entity are conditioned. //

body.text: ityalaṃ prasaṅgena | prakṛtameva vyākhyāsyāmaḥ || 32 ||
body.translated_text: But enough of this digression. We shall explain the subject at hand. // 32 //

body.text: atrāha- yadi utpādasthitibhaṅgāḥ saṃskṛtasya niṣiddhāḥ, tathāpi saṃskṛtamasti viśeṣalakṣaṇayuktam | tathāhi kāṭhinyādikaṃ sāsnādikaṃ ca tasya viśeṣalakṣaṇamupadiśyate | tasmātsaṃskṛtasya sadbhāvāttallakṣaṇamapyastīti | ucyate | syādevaṃ yadi saṃskṛtameva vastu syāt | kutaḥ? yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: Even if arising, duration, and decay of the conditioned have been negated, the conditioned still exists, being endowed with specific characteristics. For hardness and so forth, dewlap and so forth, are taught as its specific characteristics. Therefore, since the conditioned exists, its characteristics too exist. It is replied: It would be so if the conditioned were an established entity. Whence? Because —

body.text: utpādasthitibhaṅgānāmasiddhernāsti saṃskṛtam |
body.translated_text: Since arising, duration, and decay are not established, there is no conditioned. /

body.text: yadā yathoktena nyāyena utpādasthitibhaṅgā eva niṣiddhāḥ, tadā kutaḥ saṃskṛtaṃ vastu tadviśeṣalakṣaṇamapyastīti ||
body.translated_text: When arising, duration, and decay have been negated by the reasoning stated above, then whence is the conditioned entity, or its specific characteristics?

body.text: atrāha- vidyata eva saṃskṛtam, tatpratipakṣāsaṃskṛtasadbhāvāt | ucyate | syādetadevam, yadi asaṃskṛtameva syāt | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: The conditioned does indeed exist, because of the existence of its opposite — the unconditioned. It is replied: This would be so if the unconditioned itself existed. Since —

body.text: saṃskṛtasyāprasiddhau ca kathaṃ setsyatyasaṃskṛtam || 33 ||
body.translated_text: And when the conditioned is not established, how will the unconditioned be established? // 33 //

body.text: atraike ākāśāpratisaṃkhyānirodhanirvāṇānyasaṃskṛtānīti kalpayanti | apare śūnyatāṃ tathatālakṣaṇāmasaṃskṛtāṃ parikalpayanti | tadetatsarvaṃ saṃskṛtasyāprasiddhau satyāṃ nāstyeveti spaṣṭamādarśitam || 33 ||
body.translated_text: Here, some imagine that space, <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> (cessation not through deliberation), and <s>nirvāṇa</s> are unconditioned. Others imagine <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), whose characteristic is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), to be unconditioned. All of this, when the conditioned is not established, simply does not exist — this has been clearly shown. // 33 //

body.text: atrāha- yadi utpādasthitibhaṅgā na santītyavadhāritam, yattarhi idamanāvaraṇajñāninā muninā-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: If it has been determined that arising, duration, and decay do not exist, then the following statement by the Sage whose knowledge is unobstructed —

body.text: "saṃskṛtasya bhikṣavaḥ utpādo 'pi prajñāyate, vyayo 'pi, sthityanyathātvamapi"
body.translated_text: 'Of the conditioned, monks, arising is discerned, decay is discerned, and the alteration of what persists is also discerned' —

body.text: ityudāhṛtam, tatkathaṃ veditavyamiti? ucyate-
body.translated_text: how is this to be understood? It is replied —

children.text: yathā māyā yathā svapno gandharvanagaraṃ yathā |
children.translated_text: Just as an illusion, just as a dream, just as a city of the <s>Gandharvas</s> — /
so arising has been declared, so duration, and so decay. // 34 //

body.text: yathā māyādayaḥ svabhāvenānutpannā avidyamānā māyādiśabdavācyā māyādivijñānagamyāśca lokasya, evamete 'pi lokaprasiddhimātreṇa utpādādayaḥ svabhāvena avidyamānā api bhagavatā tathāvidhavineyajanānugrahacikīrṣuṇā nirdiṣṭā iti | ata evoktam-
body.translated_text: Just as illusions and so forth, though unproduced by their own nature and non-existent, are designated by the words 'illusion' and so forth and are cognized by cognitions of illusions and so forth by worldly people — even so, these too — arising and the rest — though non-existent by their own nature, merely by worldly convention, have been taught by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who wished to benefit beings to be trained of such a type. Hence it is said —

children.text: tvaksnāyumāṃsāsthisamucchraye ca utpādya saṃjñāṃ mama patnireṣā |
children.translated_text: Having generated the notion 'this is my wife' regarding an assemblage of skin, sinew, flesh, and bone, /

children.text: mūḍhā hi balā janayanti rāgaṃ striyo na jānanti yathaiva māyām ||
children.translated_text: fools generate passion — they do not understand that women are like illusions. //

children.text: yathā kumārī supināntarasmiṃ sā putra jātaṃ ca mṛtaṃ ca paśyati |
children.translated_text: Just as a young woman in a dream sees a son who has been born and also who has died — /

children.text: jāte 'tituṣṭā mṛti daurmanasthitā tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān ||
children.translated_text: she is overjoyed at his birth and grief-stricken at his death — know that all <s>dharmas</s> are like that. //

children.text: yathaiva gandharvapuraṃ marīcikā yathaiva māyā supinaṃ yathaiva |
children.translated_text: Just as a <s>Gandharva</s>-city, just as a mirage, just as an illusion, just as a dream — /

children.text: svabhāvaśūnyā tu nimittabhāvanā tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān ||
children.translated_text: empty of intrinsic nature is the cultivation of signs — know that all <s>dharmas</s> are like that. //
Free from conditioned and unconditioned <s>dharmas</s>, there is no conceptualization for those sages. /
Having attained the unconditioned in all destinies, they are forever free from views and their courses. //

body.text:
nityamarakta aduṣṭa amūḍhāḥ tasya sabhāvasamāhitacittā |
eṣa samādhibalī balavanto yo imu jānati śūnyakadharmān || iti || 34 ||
body.translated_text:
Ever unattached, free from hatred, free from delusion, their minds composed in the nature of that —
this one of powerful <s>samādhi</s>, the mighty one, is he who knows these empty <s>dharmas</s>. // 34 //

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacittāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau saṃskṛtaparīkṣā nāma saptamaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh chapter, 'The Examination of the Conditioned,' in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary composed by <s>Ācārya Candrakīrtipāda</s>.

body.text: karmakārakaparīkṣā aṣṭamaṃ prakaraṇam |
body.translated_text: The Examination of Action and Agent (<s>Karmakārakaparīkṣā</s>), the Eighth Chapter.

body.text: atrāha- vidyanta eva saṃskṛtasvabhāvato vijñānādayaḥ saṃskṛtā dharmāḥ, taddhetukakarmakārakasadbhāvāt | uktaṃ hi bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: Conditioned <s>dharmas</s> such as consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) and so forth, of conditioned nature, do indeed exist, because of the existence of the action and agent that cause them. For the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said —

body.text: avidyānugato 'yaṃ bhikṣavaḥ puruṣapudgalaḥ puṇyānapi saṃskārānabhisaṃskaroti, apuṇyānapi, āniñjayānapi saṃskārānabhisaṃskaroti |
body.translated_text: 'This person-individual, monks, attended by ignorance, generates meritorious formations, demeritorious formations, and also imperturbable formations' —

body.text: ityādinā karmaṇāṃ kārako vyapadiṣṭaḥ, tatkarmaphalaṃ ca vijñānādikamupadiṣṭam | yasya ca kārako 'sti, tadasti, tadyathā ghaṭaḥ | yannāsti, na tasya kārakaḥ, tadyathā kūrmaromaprāvārasyeti | ucyate | syādvijñānādikaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ yadi tasya niṣpādakakarmakārakau syātām | na tu staḥ | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: — and so forth, whereby the agent of actions has been designated, and the fruit of that action, namely consciousness and so forth, has been taught. And that which has an agent exists — just as a pot [exists]. What does not exist has no agent — like a shawl made of tortoise-hair. It is replied: The conditioned, [namely] consciousness and so forth, would [exist] if there were an action and agent to produce it. But there are not. Because —

children.text: sadbhūtaḥ kārakaḥ karma sadbhūtaṃ na karotyayam |
children.translated_text: An agent that is existent does not perform an action that is existent. /
Nor does an agent that is non-existent undertake an action that is non-existent. // 1 //

body.text: tatra karotīti kārakaḥ kartā | kurvāṇasyaiva kiṃcit kārakavyapadeśo nākurvāṇasya | tacca karaṇaṃ sadbhūtasya vā kartuḥ parikalpyeta, asadbhūtasya vā, sadasadbhūtasya vā? kriyate iti karma karturīpsitatamam | tadapi trividham, sadbhūtamasadbhūtaṃ sadasadbhūtaṃ ca | tatra sadbhūtaḥ kārakaḥ kriyāyuktaḥ sadbhūtaṃ kriyāyuktaṃ karma na karotītyekā pratijñā | idānīmasadbhūto 'pi kriyākārakarahito 'sadbhutaṃ kriyārahitaṃ karma na karotītyaparā pratijñā || 1 ||
body.translated_text: Here, 'one who does' is the agent (<s>kāraka</s>) — the doer (<s>kartṛ</s>). The designation 'agent' applies to one who is actually doing something, not to one who is not doing. And that doing may be imagined either of an existent agent, or of a non-existent one, or of one both existent and non-existent. 'What is done' is the action (<s>karma</s>) — what is most desired by the agent. That too is threefold: existent, non-existent, and both existent and non-existent. Among these: an existent agent, possessed of action, does not perform an existent action, possessed of action — this is one proposition. Now: a non-existent agent, devoid of action, does not perform a non-existent action, devoid of action — this is another proposition. // 1 //

body.text: tatrādyāṃ prasādhayitumāha-
body.translated_text: In order to establish the first [proposition], he says —

body.text: sadbhūtasya kriyā nāsti karma ca syādakartṛkam |
body.translated_text: For an existent [agent], there is no action; and the action would be without an agent. /

body.text: kriyānibandhanatvātkārakavyapadeśasya, karoti kriyāyukta eva kaścitsadbhūtaḥ kārakavyapadeśaṃ labhate, tataśca tasyaivaṃvidhasya kriyāhetukalabdhakārakavyapadeśasya aparā kriyā nāsti yayā karma kuryāt | kriyābhāvācca yadā kārakaḥ karma na karoti, tadā kārakanirapekṣamakartṛkaṃ karma syāt | na cākartṛkaṃ karma saṃbhavati bandhyāsūnoriva ghaṭakaraṇamiti | evaṃ tāvat
body.translated_text: Since the designation 'agent' depends on an action, someone who is engaged in action — an existent [agent] — obtains the designation 'agent.' And for one of such a kind, who has obtained the designation 'agent' by virtue of action as the cause, there is no other action by which he would perform the deed. And since there is no action, when the agent does not perform the deed, the action would be without an agent — independent of the agent. But an action without an agent is impossible — like the making of a pot by a barren woman's son. Thus,

body.text: sadbhūtasya kriyā nāsti karma ca syādakartṛkam |
body.translated_text: for an existent [agent], there is no action; and the action would be without an agent —

body.text: iti doṣaprasaṅgāt sadbhūtaḥ kārakaḥ karma na karoti |
body.translated_text: because of this consequence of fault, an existent agent does not perform the action.

body.text: idānīṃ sadbhūtamapi karma kārako na karotīti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, in order to demonstrate that the agent also does not perform an existent action, he says —

body.text: sadbhūtasya kriyā nāsti kartā ca syādakarmakaḥ || 2 ||
body.translated_text: For an existent [agent], there is no action; and the agent would be without an action. // 2 //

body.text: sadbhūtaṃ nāma karma kriyāyuktam | tasyedānīṃ kriyānibandhanalabdhakarmavyapadeśasya aparā kriyā nāsti yayā karma kriyeteti | evaṃ tāvatsadbhūtasya karmaṇaḥ kriyā nāsti | yadā nāsti parā kriyā, tadā kārakastatsadbhūtaṃ karma naiva karoti | yadā ca na karoti karmaṇo dvitīyakriyābhāvāt, tadā
body.translated_text: 'Existent action' means action that is possessed of activity. For that [action], which has obtained the designation 'action' through the connection with activity as its cause — there is no other activity by which the action would be done. Thus, for an existent action, there is no activity. When there is no further activity, the agent simply does not perform that existent action. And when he does not perform it — because of the absence of a second activity of the action —

body.text: akarmaka eva avidyamānakarmaka eva tasya karmaṇaḥ kārakaḥ syāt | na caitadyaktam | na hi akṛtānantaryakarmaṇaḥ ānantaryakarmakārakatvaṃ dṛṣṭamiti || 2 ||
body.translated_text: the agent of that action would be without an action — one whose action does not exist. And this is not appropriate. For it has not been observed that one who has not committed an <s>ānantarya</s> (immediate retribution) action has the agency of an <s>ānantarya</s> action. // 2 //

body.text: evaṃ sadbhūtaḥ kārakaḥ sadbhūtaṃ karma na karoti iti saṃsādhya idānīṃ yathā asadbhūtamapi karma asadbhūtaḥ kārako na karoti tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Having thus established that an existent agent does not perform an existent action, now in order to demonstrate that a non-existent agent also does not perform a non-existent action, he says —

children.translated_text: If a non-existent agent were to perform a non-existent action, /
the action would be without a cause, and the agent too would be without a cause. // 3 //

body.text: asadbhūtaḥ kārako yaḥ kriyārahitaḥ | kriyā ca kārakavyapadeśe heturiti kriyārahita kārako 'pi nirhetukaḥ syāt | karmāpyasadbhūtaṃ nirhetukaṃ syāt || 3 ||
body.translated_text: A non-existent agent is one devoid of activity. And since activity is the cause of the designation 'agent,' an agent devoid of activity would also be without a cause. The action too, being non-existent, would be without a cause. // 3 //

body.text: sati ca ahetukavādābhyupagame kāryaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ ca sarvamapoditaṃ syādityāha-
body.translated_text: And if the doctrine of causelessness were accepted, then effect and cause — everything — would be negated. He says —

body.text: hetāvasati kāryaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ ca na vidyate |
body.translated_text: In the absence of a cause, neither effect nor cause exists. /

body.text: satyeva hi hetorabhyupagame hetunā yanniṣpādyate tat kāryam, tasya ca yo niṣpādakaḥ tatkāraṇamiti yujyate | tadyathā ghaṭasya mṛd hetuḥ, ghaṭaḥ kāryam, tasya ca cakrādayaḥ sahakārikāraṇam | ahetukavādābhyupagame tu hetvanapekṣatvānmaṇḍūkajaṭāśiromaṇimayaghaṭavanna syādayaṃ ghaṭaḥ | asati ghaṭe kutastatkāraṇamiti | evam-
body.translated_text: For only when a cause is accepted does it make sense that what is produced by the cause is the effect, and what produces it is the cause — just as clay is the cause of a pot, the pot is the effect, and the wheel and so forth are the cooperating causes. But if the doctrine of causelessness were accepted, then because of not depending on a cause, this pot would not exist — like a pot made of the crest-jewel on a frog's head-hair. And in the absence of the pot, whence its cause? Thus —

body.text: hetāvasati kāryaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ ca na vidyate |
body.translated_text: In the absence of a cause, neither effect nor cause exists. /

body.text: tataśca-
body.translated_text: And therefore —

body.text: tadabhāve kriyā kartā karaṇaṃ ca na vidyate || 4 ||
body.translated_text: In their absence, action, agent, and instrument do not exist. // 4 //

body.text: tadabhāve kāryakāraṇabhāve, kiṃ kurvāṇasya kriyā saṃbhavet, kasyāṃ vā kriyāyāṃ kumbhakārasya svātantryātkartṛtvaṃ syāt? na cāpi mṛdāṃ tādātmyapravṛttyā sādhakatamatvena karaṇatvaṃ yujyata iti evaṃ tāvat-
body.translated_text: In the absence of effect and cause, how could there be the action of one who performs? Or in what action would the potter have agency through his independent power? Nor would it be appropriate that the clay, through the operation of identity [with the pot], would have instrumentality as the most effective [factor]. Thus —

body.text: tadabhāve kriyā kartā karaṇaṃ ca na vidyate ||
body.translated_text: In their absence, action, agent, and instrument do not exist. //

body.text: tataśca-
body.translated_text: And therefore —

body.text: dharmādharmau na vidyete kriyādīnāmasaṃbhave |
body.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) do not exist when action and so forth are impossible. /

body.text: iha yadā devadattaḥ prāṇātipātaviratikriyāsvātantryātkartā san svatantrakāryeṇa karaṇabhūtena prāṇātipātaviratikriyāṃ karoti, tadāsya dharma upajāyate | evaṃ daśasvapi kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu kuśalakriyāniṣpādyeṣu ratnatrayamātāpitṛtadanyapūjyapūjādilakṣaṇeṣu ca kuśaladharmaprārambheṣu yojyam | evamadharme 'pi prāṇātipātādilakṣaṇe kuśalaviparyayeṇa kriyākartṛkaraṇānāmabhāve sati karmaṇāmabhāvaprasaṅga udbhāvanīyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Here, when <s>Devadatta</s>, being an agent through the independent power of the activity of refraining from taking life, performs the activity of refraining from taking life through the instrument that is the independent effect — then merit (<s>dharma</s>) arises for him. The same should be applied to all ten wholesome courses of action, the undertakings of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> characterized by worship of the Three Jewels, parents, and other worthy ones, and so forth. Likewise, with regard to demerit (<s>adharma</s>) — characterized by taking life and so forth, the opposite of the wholesome — the consequence of the non-existence of actions should be brought out from the non-existence of action, agent, and instrument.

body.text: yadā caivaṃ dharmādharmau na saṃbhavataḥ, tadā tatphalamapi nāstyeveti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And when merit and demerit are thus impossible, in order to demonstrate that their fruit too simply does not exist, he says —

body.text: dharme cāsatyadharme ca phalaṃ tajjaṃ na vidyate || 5 ||
body.translated_text: And when <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> do not exist, the fruit born from them does not exist. // 5 //

body.text: dharmādharmajanitamiṣṭāniṣṭaphalaṃ sugatidurgatyordharmādharmayorabhāve sati na syāt || 5 ||
body.translated_text: The desired and undesired fruit generated by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — in the good and bad destinations — would not exist in the absence of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. // 5 //

body.text: tataśca-
body.translated_text: And therefore —

body.text:
phale 'sati na mokṣāya na svargāyopapadyate |
mārgaḥ

body.translated_text: For if the desired and undesired fruit existed, then the worldly path — characterized by the <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), formless <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and attainment — would lead to heaven, and the cultivation of the worldly path for that purpose would be superior, and the refraining from the courses of action leading to bad destinations would be fruitful. And if the fruit characterized as liberation — <s>nirvāṇa</s> — existed, the cultivation of the noble supramundane eightfold path for that purpose would be fruitful. But when the fruit does not exist, then —

evamityanena anantarāṃ karmakārakaprajñaptiṃ darśayati | upāttirupādānam | anena copāttikriyāmāha | sā ca svasādhanaṃ kartāramupādātāraṃ karma copādānaṃ saṃnidhāpayati | tayośca upādeyopādātroḥ parasparāpekṣayoḥ karmakārakavadeva siddhirna svābhāvikī | kasmātpunaḥ svābhāvikī na bhavati ityāha- vyutsargāditi karmaṇaḥ, kartuśceti | itiśabdo hetuparāmarśī | vyutsargo vyudāsaḥ | tataśca ayamartha upapadyate- yaireva hetubhiḥ karmaṇaśca vyutsargo 'smābhiruktaḥ, taireva hetubhiḥ upādātā upādeyaṃ ca pratiṣiddhaṃ veditavyam | na ca kevalamanayoranyonyāpekṣikī siddhiḥ katurśca karmaṇaśca pratiṣedhenāvaseyā, api ca
karmakartṛbhyāṃ śeṣān bhāvān vibhāvayet || 13 ||
