kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmāt-

iha vidyamāna eva devadatto dhanopādānaṃ kurute nāvidyamāno vandhyātanayaḥ | evaṃ yadi tāvatpudgalo darśanādibhyaḥ pūrvaṃ vyavasthito na syāt, nāsau darśanādikasyopādānamakariṣyat | tasmādasti asau dhanātprāgeva sthitadevadattavat darśanādibhyaḥ pūrvaṃ pudgalo yo 'sya upādānaṃ kariṣyatīti || 2 ||
ucyate-

children.text: yaḥ prāgvyavasthito bhāvaḥ kena prajñapyate 'tha saḥ || 3 ||

body.text: yau 'sau pudgalo darśanādibhyaḥ pūrvamastīti vyavasthāpyate, sa kena prajñapyatām? pudgalaprajñapterhi darśanādikaṃ kāraṇam | sa yadi tebhyaḥ prāgvyavasthito 'stīti kalpyate, tadā darśananirapekṣaḥ syād ghaṭādiva paṭaḥ | yaśca svakāraṇanirapekṣaḥ sa nirhetuko dhanādinirapekṣaḥ dhanikavannāstītyabhiprāyaḥ || 3 ||
body.translated_text: When that person (<s>pudgala</s>) is posited as existing prior to seeing and so forth — by what is he to be designated? For seeing and so forth are the cause of the designation 'person.' If he is conceived as existing established prior to them, then he would be independent of seeing — like a pot is [independent] of cloth. And whatever is independent of its own cause is without cause — like one who is designated 'wealthy' without reference to wealth, he does not exist. This is the intent. // 3 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat-
body.translated_text: What is more —

children.translated_text: If he is established without seeing and so forth,

children.text: amūnyapi bhaviṣyanti vinā tena na saṃśayaḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: then these too will surely exist without him. // 4 //

body.text: yadi manyase- darśanādibhyaḥ pūrvaṃ pudgalo nāmāsti, sa darśanādikamupādānamupādatte iti | nanvevaṃ sati nirastasaṃśayamamūnyapi darśanādīni vinā pudgalena bhaviṣyanti | tathāhi devadatto dhanasaṃbandhātpūrvaṃ dhanavyatirikto vyavasthitaḥ san arthāntarabhūtameva pṛthaksiddhaṃ dhanamupādatte | evamupādāturapi svātmavyatirekeṇārthāntarabhūtaṃ darśanādikamupādānaṃ syāt || 4 ||
body.translated_text: If you think: 'Prior to seeing and so forth, there exists something called a person, and that [person] appropriates seeing and so forth as his substratum' — but in that case, without any doubt, these seeing and so forth too will exist without the person. For just as <s>Devadatta</s>, existing established as separate from wealth prior to the connection with wealth, appropriates wealth which is a separate thing, independently established — even so, the substratum of seeing and so forth, which is the appropriation [of the self], would be a different thing from the self's own nature. // 4 //

children.translated_text: But this is not possible — he says:
Something is made manifest by something; something is made manifest by something.
How can something [exist] without something, or something without something? // 5 //

body.text: iha bījākhyena kāraṇena kiṃcitkāryamabhivyajyate 'ṅkurākhyam, tena ca kāryeṇa kiṃcit kāraṇamabhivyajyate bījākhyam- asyedaṃ kāraṇamidamasya kāryamiti | evaṃ yadi kenaciddarśanādikenopādānena kaścidātmasvabhāvo 'bhivyajyate asyāyamupādāteti, kenaciccātmanā kiṃcidupādānaṃ darśanādikamabhivyajyate idamasyopādānamiti, tadānīṃ syātparasparāpekṣayorupādānopādātroḥ siddhiḥ yadā tu upādātāraṃ vinā pṛthak siddhaṃ darśanādikamabhyupagamyate, tadā tannirāśrayamasadeva tasmānnāstyubhayorapi siddhiḥ, iti na yuktametat- darśanādibhyaḥ pṛthagavasthita upādāteti || 5 ||
body.translated_text: Here, by a cause called 'seed,' some effect called 'sprout' is made manifest; and by that effect, some cause called 'seed' is made manifest — 'this is its cause, this is its effect.' In this way, if by some substratum, namely seeing and so forth, some self-nature is made manifest — 'this one is its appropriator' — and by some self, some substratum, namely seeing and so forth, is made manifest — 'this is its substratum' — then the establishment of the substratum and the appropriator would be through mutual dependence. But when seeing and so forth is accepted as independently established apart from the appropriator, then that, being without a substratum, is non-existent. Therefore neither of the two is established. Hence this is not correct — that the appropriator exists established separately from seeing and so forth. // 5 //

body.text: atrāha- yaduktaṃ darśanaśravaṇādibhya ityādi, atrocyate | yadi sarvebhyo darśanādibhya prāgavasthita ityabhyupagataṃ syāt, syādeṣa doṣaḥ | yadā tu-
body.translated_text: To this one says: regarding what was stated 'prior to seeing, hearing, and so forth' and so on, to this it is replied: if it were accepted that he exists established prior to all seeing and so forth, this fault would apply. But —

body.text: sarvebhyo darśanādibhyaḥ kaścitpūrvo na vidyate |
body.translated_text: No one exists prior to all seeing and so forth.

body.text: kiṃ tarhi ekaikasmātpūrvo vidyate | yadā caivam, tadā-
body.translated_text: Rather, he exists prior to each one. And when that is so —

body.text: ajyate darśanādīnāmanyena punaranyadā || 6 ||
body.translated_text: He is made manifest as different by a different one among seeing and so forth, at different times. // 6 //

body.text: yadā darśanena draṣṭetyabhivyajyate, na tadā śravaṇādīnyupādāya prajñapyate, tataśca pūrvoktadoṣānavasara iti || 6 ||
body.translated_text: When he is made manifest as 'seer' by seeing, he is not at that time designated in reference to hearing and so forth; and therefore the previously stated faults do not apply. // 6 //

body.text: ucyate | etadapi na yuktaṃ darśanādirahitasya nirupādānasya nirhetukasya nirañjanasyāstitvāsaṃbhavāt |
body.translated_text: It is replied: this too is not correct, because of the impossibility of the existence of one devoid of seeing and so forth, without a substratum, without a cause, without a characterizing mark.

body.text: sarvebhyo darśanādibhyo yadi pūrvo na vidyate |
body.translated_text: If he does not exist prior to all seeing and so forth,

body.text: iti parikalpyate, evamapi-
body.translated_text: this is conceived [by you]. Even so —

body.text: ekaikasmātkathaṃ pūrvo darśanādeḥ sa vidyate || 7 ||
body.translated_text: how does he exist prior to each one of seeing and so forth? // 7 //

body.text: yo hi sarvebhyaḥ pūrvo na bhavati, sa ekaikasmādapi na bhavati | tadyathā sarvebhyo vṛkṣebhya prāg vanaṃ nāsti, tadā ekaikasmādapi nāsti | sarvāsāṃ ca sikatānāṃ tailajananābhāve sati ekaikasyā api sikatāyāstailaṃ nāsti | api ca | yo hyekaikasmātpūrvo bhavati, nanu sa sarvebhyo 'pi pūrvaṃ evetyabhyupagataṃ bhavati | ekaikavyatirekeṇa sarvasyābhāvāt | tasmānna yuktamekaikasmātpūrvo vidyata iti || 7 ||
body.translated_text: For one who does not exist prior to all, does not exist prior to each one either. Just as, if a forest does not exist prior to all trees, it does not exist prior to each tree either. And when all grains of sand lack the capacity to produce oil, there is no oil from each individual grain of sand either. Moreover, one who exists prior to each one is thereby accepted as existing prior to all of them as well — since 'all' has no existence apart from 'each one.' Therefore it is not correct that he exists prior to each one. // 7 //

body.text: itaśca na yuktam- yasmāt-
body.translated_text: For this reason too it is not correct — because:

body.text: draṣṭā sa eva sa śrotā sa eva yadi vedakaḥ |
body.translated_text: If the seer is that very same one, and the hearer too is that same one, and the feeler too,

body.text: tadā-
body.translated_text: then —

body.text: ekaikasmādbhavetpūrvaṃ
body.translated_text: he would exist prior to each,

body.text: na ca yuktaṃ vaktuṃ sa eva draṣṭā sa eva śroteti | yadi syāt, tadā darśanakriyārahitasyāpi śroturdraṣṭṭatvaṃ syāt, śravaṇakriyārahitasyāpi draṣṭuḥ śrotṛtvaṃ syāt | na caivaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yaddarśanakriyārahito 'pi draṣṭā syāt, śravaṇakriyārahitaśca śroteti | ata evāha-
body.translated_text: but it is not correct to say 'the seer is the very same one who is the hearer.' If it were, then even one devoid of the activity of seeing would be a seer in virtue of being a hearer, and one devoid of the activity of hearing would be a hearer in virtue of being a seer. But it is not observed that one devoid of the activity of seeing is a seer, or that one devoid of the activity of hearing is a hearer. Hence he says:

body.text: evaṃ caitanna yujyate || 8 ||
body.translated_text: And thus this is not correct. // 8 //

body.text: iti | pratikriyaṃ ca kārakabhedātkuta etadevaṃ bhaviṣyatīti pratipādayannāha- evaṃ caitanna yujyata iti ||
body.translated_text: Since there is a difference in agents for each different action, how will this be so? Demonstrating this, he says: 'And thus this is not correct.'

body.text: ācāryabuddhapālitastu vyācaṣṭe- ekatve hi ātmanaḥ indriyāntaragamanaprasaṅgaḥ puruṣasya syāt, vātāyanāntaropagamanavaditi | asya ācāryabhāvaviveko dūṣaṇamāha- sarvagatasyātmano nendriyāntaragamanamastītyayuktaḥ prasaṅgadoṣa iti | tadetadayuktaṃ svayūthyaparikalpitapudgalavādanirāsasya prastutatvāt, tasya ca sarvagatatvāpratijñānāt | tasmād yukta eva prasaṅgadoṣa || 8 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Ācārya Buddhapālita</s> explains: 'For if the self were one, there would be the consequence that the person would pass from one sense-faculty to another, as if entering through a different window.' <s>Ācārya Bhāvaviveka</s> states a fault against this: 'For an all-pervading self, there is no passing from one sense-faculty to another — hence the absurd consequence is unjustified.' But this [objection] is incorrect, because what is at hand is the refutation of the person-doctrine devised by one's own school, and that [person] is not claimed to be all-pervading. Therefore the absurd consequence is entirely justified. // 8 //

body.text: athāpi yathoktadoṣaparijihīrṣayā-
body.translated_text: Even if, wishing to avoid the stated faults —

body.text: draṣṭānya eva śrotānyo vedako 'nyaḥ punaryadi |
body.translated_text: the seer is one, the hearer another, and the feeler yet another —

body.text: parikalpyate, tadapi na yuktam | evaṃ hīṣyamāṇe-
body.translated_text: is conceived, that too is not correct. For when this is desired —

body.text: sati syād draṣṭari śrotā bahutvaṃ cātmanāṃ bhavet || 9 ||
body.translated_text: when the seer exists, the hearer would exist [simultaneously], and there would be a multiplicity of selves. // 9 //

body.text: tadyathā goranyo 'śvaḥ na hi gavi sati na bhavati yaugapadyena, evaṃ yadi draṣṭuranyaḥ śrotā syāt, sadraṣṭaryapi sati syādyaugapadyena | na caivamiṣyate iti nāstyanyatvam | api ca | evaṃ sati bahava evātmānaḥ prāpnuvanti draṣṭṭaśrotṛvedakādīnāṃ pṛthak pṛthak siddhayupagamāt | tasmādekaikasmādapi darśanādeḥ pūrvaṃ nāsti pudgalo nāma kaścit || 9 ||
body.translated_text: Just as a horse is different from a cow — for when a cow exists, a horse does not fail to exist simultaneously — even so, if the hearer were different from the seer, then even when the seer exists, the hearer would exist simultaneously. But this is not desired — hence there is no difference. Moreover, in that case, there would be many selves, since the seer, hearer, feeler, and so forth would each be accepted as independently established. Therefore, there does not exist, prior to each one of seeing and so forth, anyone called a person. // 9 //

body.text: atrāha- vidyata eva pūrvaṃ sa sarvebhyo darśanādibhya ātmā | atha matam- yadyasti, kena prajñapyate sa iti yaducyate, iha darśanādibhyaḥ pūrvaṃ nāmarūpāvasthāyāṃ catvāri mahābhūtāni santi yataḥ kramānnāmarūpapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanamiti darśanaśravaṇādīnyutpadyante | tasmāddarśanādibhyaḥ pūrvaṃ caturmahābhūtopādānamevāstīti | evamapi-
body.translated_text: To this one says: the self does indeed exist prior to all seeing and so forth. And as for the question 'if he exists, by what is he designated?' — here, prior to seeing and so forth, in the state of name-and-form, the four great elements exist, from which, in sequence, the six sense-spheres arise, as [it is said]: 'Conditioned by name-and-form are the six sense-spheres.' Therefore, prior to seeing and so forth, the appropriation consisting of the four great elements does indeed exist. Even so —

children.translated_text: Seeing, hearing, and so forth, and feeling and so forth also —
in those elements from which they arise, he too does not exist. // 10 //

body.text: yebhyo mahābhūtebhyo darśanādikamutpadyate, teṣvapi mahābhūtopādānanimittako 'pyeṣa na yujyate pūrveṇaiva hetunetyabhiprāyaḥ | tatra yathā pūrvamuktam-
body.translated_text: In those great elements from which seeing and so forth arise, this one too — even as [supposedly] caused by the appropriation of great elements — is not justified, by the very same reason as before. This is the intent. As was stated earlier —

body.text: kutaḥ kiṃcidvinā kaścitkiṃcitkaṃcidvinā kutaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'How can something [exist] without something, or something without something?'

body.text: iti, ihāpi tathaiva vaktavyam | mahābhūtopādānādyaścātmā pūrvaṃ siddhaḥ syāt, sa mahābhūtānyupādāya syāt | na caivam, nirhetukatvāt | yaśca nāsti, sa kathaṃ mahābhūtānyupādāsyati? iti darśanopādānavadbhūtopādāne 'pi dūṣaṇamuktameveti na punarucyate || 10 ||
body.translated_text: The same should be said here. The self, which would supposedly be established prior to the appropriation of great elements, would exist in dependence on the great elements. But this is not so, because of being without a cause. And one who does not exist — how will he appropriate the great elements? Thus, the same refutation as stated for the appropriation of seeing applies to the appropriation of the elements as well — hence it is not repeated. // 10 //

body.text: atrāha- yadyapyevamātmā pratiṣiddhaḥ, tathāpi darśanādikamasti, apratiṣedhāt | na ca anātmasvabhāvānāṃ ghaṭādīnāṃ darśanādisaṃbandho 'sti | tasmātsaṃbandhī vidyata evātmeti | ucyate | syādātmā yadi darśanādīnyeva syuḥ | na tu santi | yasya darśanādīnyupādānaṃ sa yadā nāstīti
body.translated_text: To this one says: even though the self has been thus refuted, nevertheless seeing and so forth do exist, since they have not been refuted. And entities without a self-nature, like pots, do not have a connection with seeing and so forth. Therefore, a relatum — the self — does indeed exist. It is replied: the self would exist if seeing and so forth themselves were to exist. But they do not. When it has been demonstrated that the one whose seeing and so forth are the substratum does not exist,

body.text: pratipāditam, tadā tasminnātmani upādātari asati, kuto darśanādīnāmupādānabhūtānāmastitvamityāha-
body.translated_text: then, in the absence of that self as the appropriator, whence would the existence of seeing and so forth as the appropriated come? He says:

children.translated_text: And as for seeing, hearing, and so forth, and feeling and so forth also —

children.text: na vidyate cedyasya sa na vidyanta imānyapi || 11 ||
children.translated_text: if the one to whom they belong does not exist, then these too do not exist. // 11 //

body.text: yasya darśanādīni parikalpyante sa yadā nāstītyuktam, nanu tadaiva darśanādikamapi nāstīti spaṣṭamādarśitaṃ bhavati | tataśca darśanādyabhāvānnāstyevātmeti || 11 ||
body.translated_text: When it has been said that the one for whom seeing and so forth are conceived does not exist, surely it has thereby been clearly shown that seeing and so forth also do not exist. And therefore, from the non-existence of seeing and so forth, the self does not exist at all. // 11 //

body.text: atrāha- kiṃ khalu bhavato niścitametannāstyevātmeti? kena etaduktam? nanu ca anantaramevoktaṃ darśanādyabhāvādātmāpi nāstīti | uktametadesmābhiḥ | na tu asyārtho bhavatā samyagniścitaḥ | yato bhāvarūpa ātmeti parikalpitaḥ, sa svabhāvato na vidyate, tasya ca mayā svabhāvābhiniveśanivartakameva vacanamuktamasadviparyāsapratipakṣeṇa, na tu asya abhāvaḥ parikalpitaḥ | dvayaṃ hyetat parityājyaṃ yaśca bhāveṣvabhiniveśaḥ, yaśca abhāveṣu abhiniveśa iti | yathoktamāryadevena-
body.translated_text: To this one says: is it indeed your firm conclusion that the self does not exist at all? Who says so? Was it not just stated that from the non-existence of seeing and so forth, the self too does not exist? We have said this. But its meaning has not been correctly understood by you. For the self conceived as having the form of an existent entity does not exist by its own nature; and my statement was made only to turn away the clinging to its own-nature, as an antidote to the false perversion [of taking the non-existent for the existent] — but the non-existence of the self was not conceived [by me]. For both of these must be relinquished — the clinging to the existence of entities and the clinging to their non-existence. As <s>Āryadeva</s> has said:

children.translated_text: The one for whom there is both a self and a non-self — by that, the self is not determined to be such.
Surely, conceptual construction arises only with regard to impermanent entities. //

body.text: etadeva pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Demonstrating this very point, he says:

children.text: prāk ca yo darśanādibhyaḥ sāṃprataṃ cordhvameva ca |
children.translated_text: The one who, prior to seeing and so forth, at present, and after as well,
does not exist — regarding him, the conceptual constructions of 'exists' and 'does not exist' have ceased. // 12 //

body.text: prāk tāvaddarśanādibhya ātmā nāsti, tatra hi tasyāstitvābhāvāt | darśanādisahabhūto 'pi nāsti, pṛthakpṛthagasiddhayoḥ sahabhāvādarśanāt śaśaśṛṅgayoriva | ātmopādānayośca parasparanirapekṣayo pṛthakpṛthagasiddhatvāt sāṃpratamapi nāsti | urdhvamapi | yadi hi pūrvaṃ darśanādīni syuḥ, uttarakālamātmā syāt, tadānīmūrdhvaṃ saṃbhavet | na caivam, akartṛkasya karmaṇo 'siddhatvāt | yaścaivamātmā darśanādibhyaḥ prāk paścād yugapacca parīkṣyamāṇo nāsti, tasya idānīmanupalabdhasvabhāvasya astitvaṃ nāstitvaṃ vā kaḥ parikalpayetprājñaḥ? tasmātkarmakārakavadeva upādānopādātroḥ parasparāpekṣā siddhirna svābhāvikīti sthitam ||
body.translated_text: Prior to seeing and so forth, the self does not exist, for its existence is absent there. Co-existent with seeing and so forth, he also does not exist, because simultaneous existence of two things not independently established is not observed — like the horns of a rabbit. And since the self and its substratum, being mutually independent, are not independently established, he does not exist at present either. Nor after — for if first seeing and so forth were to exist, then later the self would exist, and then he would be possible 'after.' But this is not so, since action without an agent is not established. And for the self thus sought — prior to, simultaneously with, and after seeing and so forth — not found to exist, who, being wise, would now conceive either its existence or non-existence, for one whose own-nature is not apprehended? Therefore, just as with action and agent, the establishment of the appropriated and the appropriator is through mutual dependence, not inherent — this is established.

body.text: ata evoktaṃ bhagavatā āryasamādhirājabhaṭṭārake-
body.translated_text: Hence the <s>Bhagavān</s> has stated in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>:

children.text: tahi kāli so daśabalo anagho jinu bhāṣate imu samādhivaram |
children.translated_text: At that time, the faultless <s>Jina</s> of the ten powers speaks this supreme <s>samādhi</s>:

children.text: supinopamā bhagavatī sakalā na hi kaści jāyati na co mriyate ||
children.translated_text: 'All of the <s>Bhagavatī</s>'s [teachings] are like a dream — no one is born, nor does anyone die.

children.text: na ca sattvu labhyati na jīvu naro imi dharma phenakadalīsadṛśāḥ |
children.translated_text: No being is found, no life-principle, no person — these <s>dharmas</s> are like foam and plantain trees,
like illusions, like lightning in the sky, like the moon in water, like mirages.

children.text: na ca asmi loki mṛtu kaści naro paraloka saṃkramati gacchati vā |
children.translated_text: No person in this world dies, nor crosses over or goes to the other world.

children.text: na ca karma naśyati kadāci kṛtaṃ phalu deti kṛṣṇaśubha saṃsarato ||
children.translated_text: Nor does <s>karma</s> once performed ever perish — it yields fruit, dark and bright, as one transmigrates.

children.text: na ca śāśvataṃ na ca uccheda puno na ca karmasaṃcayu na cāpi sthitiḥ |
children.translated_text: It is neither eternal nor annihilation; there is neither accumulation of <s>karma</s> nor persistence.

children.text: na ca so 'pi kṛtva punarāspṛśati na ca anyu kṛtva puna vedayate ||
children.translated_text: Nor does the very one who performed it experience it again; nor does one experience [the result of] what another performed.

children.text: na ca saṃkramo na ca punāgamanaṃ na ca sarvamasti na ca nāsti punaḥ |
children.translated_text: There is neither transmigration nor return; neither does everything exist, nor does it not exist.

children.text: na ca dṛṣṭisthānagatiśuddhiriha na ca sattvacārasupaśāntagati ||
children.translated_text: Here there is no purification through views, positions, or destinations; nor is there a course of beings or a state of perfect peace.

children.text: anutpāda śānta animittapadaṃ sugatāna gocara jināna guṇā |
children.translated_text: Non-arising, peace, the signless state — the domain of the <s>Sugatas</s>, the virtues of the <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: bala dhāraṇī daśabalāna balaṃ buddhāniyaṃ vṛṣamitā paramā ||
children.translated_text: the powers, the <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, the strength of the ten-powered ones — this, the <s>Buddhas</s>' supreme bull-like measure.' //

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacitāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau pūrvaparīkṣā nāma navamaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the examination of the prior [entity], the ninth chapter, in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary, composed by the venerable <s>Ācārya Candrakīrti</s>.

body.text:
10
agnīndhanaparīkṣā daśamaṃ prakaraṇam |
body.translated_text:
10
The examination of fire and fuel, the tenth chapter.

body.text: atrāha- yadidamuktaṃ tasmātkarmakārakavadeva upādānopādātrorapi na svābhāvikī siddhiriti, tadayuktam, sāpekṣāṇāmapi padārthānāṃ sasvābhāvyadarśanāt | tathā hi agnirindhanamapekṣya bhavati | na ca niḥsvabhāvo 'gniḥ, tasya auṣṇyadāhakatvādisvabhāvakāryopalambhāt | evamagnimapekṣya indhanaṃ bhavati | na ca tanniḥsvabhāvam, bāhyamahābhūtacatuṣṭayasvabhāvatvāt | evamupādānasāpekṣo 'pyupādātā svabhāvato bhaviṣyati, upādātṛsāpekṣaṃ copādānamityagnīndhanavadetau bhaviṣyata upādānopādātārāviti | ucyate | syādetadevam, yadi agnīndhane eva syātām, na tu staḥ | katham? iha yadi agnīndhane syātām, niyataṃ te ekatvena vā syātāmanyatvena vā? ubhayathā tu na yujyata ityāha-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: 'What was stated — that just as with action and agent, the establishment of <s>upādāna</s> (the appropriated) and <s>upādātṛ</s> (the appropriator) is also not intrinsic — that is not correct, since even entities that are mutually dependent are observed to have their own nature. For fire exists in dependence on fuel. Yet fire is not without own-nature, since its own-nature functions of heat, burning capacity, and so forth are apprehended. Likewise, fuel exists in dependence on fire. Yet it is not without own-nature, since it has the nature of the four external great elements. Thus, even though the appropriator is dependent on <s>upādāna</s>, it will exist by own-nature, and <s>upādāna</s> will be dependent on the appropriator — just like fire and fuel, they will be <s>upādāna</s> and <s>upādātṛ</s>.' The reply is: This would be so if fire and fuel actually existed. But they do not. How so? If fire and fuel existed, they would necessarily exist either as identical or as different. But in both cases it is not appropriate — hence he says:

children.translated_text: If fuel were identical with fire, there would be identity of agent and object. /
If fire were other than fuel, it would exist even without fuel. // 1 //

body.text: tatra idhyate yat tadindhanam, dāhyaṃ kāṣṭhādikasaṃbhūtam | tasya dagdhā kartā agniḥ | tatra yadi tāvad yadindhanaṃ sa evāgniriti parikalpyate, tadā kartṛkarmaṇorekatvaṃ syāt | na caivaṃ dṛṣṭam, ghaṭakumbhakārayośchettṛcchettavyayoścaikatvaprasaṅgāt, tasya cānabhyupagamāt | atha anyatvam, evamapi yadi indhanādanyo 'gniḥ syāt, tadā indhananirapekṣasyāgnerupalabdhiḥ syāt | na hi ghaṭādanyaḥ paṭastannirapekṣo na dṛṣṭaḥ | na caivamindhananirapekṣo 'gniriti na yuktametat || 1 ||
body.translated_text: Here, 'fuel' (<s>indhana</s>) is that which is kindled — the combustible, consisting of wood and so forth. Its burner, the agent, is fire. Now, if it is first imagined that 'what is fuel is itself fire,' then there would be identity of agent and object. But this is not observed, since it would entail the identity of pot and potter, of cutter and what is cut — and that is not accepted. Alternatively, if there is difference — even so, if fire were other than fuel, then fire would be apprehended independently of fuel. For a cloth, being other than a pot, is indeed observed independently of it. But fire is not thus observed independently of fuel — hence this is not correct. // 1 //

body.text: api ca | yadi indhanādanyo 'gniḥ syāt, tadānīm-
body.translated_text: Moreover, if fire were other than fuel, then —

children.translated_text: It would be eternally ablaze, it would not require a cause of ignition, /
re-ignition would be pointless, and it would be without an object [of burning]. // 2 //

body.text: indhanātpṛthagbhūto 'gniriṣyamāṇo nityapradīpta eva syāt, apradīpanahetukaśca syāt punarārambhavaiyarthyaṃ ca syāt, evaṃ ca sati akarmaka eva syāt || 2 ||
body.translated_text: Fire, if conceived as separate from fuel, would be eternally ablaze, and it would not require a cause of ignition; re-ignition would be pointless; and being thus, it would be without an object. // 2 //

body.text: amumevārthaṃ pratipādayitukāma āha-
body.translated_text: Wishing to demonstrate this very point, he says:

children.translated_text: Because of not being dependent on anything other, it would not require a cause of ignition. /
Re-ignition would be pointless — and it would follow that it is eternally ablaze. // 3 //

body.text: iti | tatra pradīpyate taditi pradīpanamindhanam | pradīpanaṃ heturasyeti pradīpanahetuka, na pradīpanahetukaḥ apradīpanahetukaḥ | yadi pradīpanādanyo 'gniḥ syāt, tadā indhananirapekṣaḥ syāt | yo hi yasmādanyaḥ, sa tannirapekṣo dṛṣṭaḥ, ghaṭādiva paṭaḥ | tataśca paratra nirapekṣatvādapradīpanahetukaḥ syāt, pradīpanasāpekṣasya hi agneḥ tadabhāve syānnirvāṇam | yadā tu pradīpananirapekṣa, tadā nirvāṇapratyayavaikalyānnityapradīpta eva bhavet | nityapradīpte cāgnau sati agneraparinirvāṇārthaṃ
body.translated_text: Here, 'fuel' (<s>indhana</s>) is 'that which is kindled' (<s>pradīpana</s>). 'Possessing a cause of ignition' means that ignition is its cause. 'Not requiring a cause of ignition' means not possessing a cause of ignition. If fire were other than ignition [i.e. fuel], then it would be independent of fuel. For what is other than something is observed as independent of it — like a cloth from a pot. And because of not being dependent on anything other, it would not require a cause of ignition; for fire that depends on fuel would go out in its absence. But when it does not depend on fuel, then due to the absence of a condition for going out, it would be eternally ablaze. And if fire is eternally ablaze, then the act of feeding it

body.text: cāsya upādānasaṃdhukṣaṇādikaṃ vyarthameva syāt | evaṃ ca sati akarmako 'gniḥ kartā syāt | na ca avidyamānakarmakasya kartṛtvaṃ vandhyāsutasyeva | tasmādindhanādagneranyatvamiti na yujyate || 3 ||
body.translated_text: — the supplying of fuel and so forth for the non-extinction of fire — would be entirely pointless. And being thus, fire, the agent, would be without an object [of burning]. But there is no agenthood for what lacks an object — like the son of a barren woman. Therefore, the otherness of fire from fuel is not correct. // 3 //

body.text: atrāha- yadetaduktam-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: 'What was stated —

body.text: anyaścedindhanādagnirindhanādapyṛte bhavet |
body.translated_text: 'If fire were other than fuel, it would exist even without fuel' /

body.text: iti, tadayuktam | ihānyatve 'pi sati agnīndhanayorna vinaiva indhanena agnerastitvam | yasmājjvālāparigato 'rtho dāhyatvalakṣaṇaḥ indhanam | tadāśrayeṇa ca agnirupalabhyate na pṛthak | yadā caitadevam, agnisaṃbandhādevendhanavyapadeśo bhavati, indhanāśrayeṇa cāgnirupalabhyate na pṛthak, tadā anyaścedindhanādagnirityādidoṣaprasaṅgasya nāstyevāvasara iti | asya pakṣasyāṣyayuktatāmudbhāvayannāha-
body.translated_text: — that is not correct. For even when there is otherness, fire and fuel do not exist without fuel. For the combustible object surrounded by flames, characterized by being burnable, is fuel. And fire is apprehended dependent on that as its basis, not separately. And since this is so — since the designation "fuel" occurs because of the connection with fire, and fire is apprehended dependent on fuel as its basis, not separately — there is no scope for the consequence stated as "if fire were other than fuel" and so forth.' To bring out the incorrectness of this position, he says:

children.translated_text: If you say: 'By this [fire], that which is being kindled becomes fuel' — /
by what is that fuel kindled, when this alone is what [there is]? // 4 //

body.text: yadi manyase jvālāparigato 'rtho dāhyalakṣaṇaḥ indhanam, tadāśrayaścāgniriti, evamapi parikalpyamāne indhanamagnirdahatīti nopapadyate | yasmāt
body.translated_text: If you think: 'The combustible object surrounded by flames, characterized by being burnable, is fuel; and fire is its basis' — even when imagined thus, the statement 'fire burns fuel' is not tenable. For

body.text: kenedhyatāmindhanaṃ tattāvanmātramidaṃ yadā |
body.translated_text: 'By what is that fuel kindled, when this alone is what [there is]?'

body.text: ihendhanamagnirdahatīti parikalpyamāne jvālāparigataṃ dāhyamindhanamiti, na caitadvayatirekeṇāparamagniṃ paśyāmo yenendhanaṃ dahyeta | yasmādetāvanmātramidamupalabhyate yaduta jvālāparigataṃ dāhyamātram | yadā caitadvayatirikto nāstyagniḥ, tadā kena tadindhanaṃ dāhyatām? tāvanmātramidaṃ yadā, idhyamānamātramidaṃ yadetyarthaḥ | tasmānnāgnirindhanaṃ dahati tadvayatiriktāgnyabhāvāt | yadā caivam, tadā kutaḥ kasyacijjvālāparigatiriti sa eva doṣo na vepate || 4 ||
body.translated_text: When it is imagined that 'fire burns fuel,' the combustible surrounded by flames is fuel — yet we do not see any fire apart from this by which the fuel would be burned. For this alone is what is apprehended — namely, the combustible surrounded by flames alone. And when there is no fire apart from this, by what would that fuel be burned? 'When this alone is what [there is]' means: when what there is is merely the thing being kindled. Therefore, fire does not burn fuel, since there is no fire apart from [the fuel]. And when this is so, whence would anything be surrounded by flames? — hence that very problem remains unresolved. // 4 //

body.text: api ca | anyatvābhyupagame 'gnīndhanayoridhyamānavyapadeśābhāvātkuta idhyamānamindhanam, kuto vā indhanamagnirdhakṣyatīti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, if otherness of fire and fuel is accepted, then, since the designation 'being kindled' would be absent, whence would there be fuel being kindled, or whence would fire burn fuel? — demonstrating this, he says:

children.text: anyo na prāpsyate 'prāpto na dhakṣyatyadahan punaḥ |
children.translated_text: Being other, it will not reach [fuel]; not having reached, it will not burn; not burning, /
it will not go out; not going out, it will remain with its own mark. // 5 //

body.text: yadi indhanādanyo 'gniḥ syāt, so 'nyatvādandhakāramivendhanaṃ na prāpnuyāt | na ca dhakṣyati aprāptatvādviprakṛṣṭadeśāvasthitamivetyabhiprāyaḥ | evaṃ ca idhyamānamindhanaṃ bhavatīti nopapannameva | tataśca agnernirvāṇaṃ na syāt | anirvāṇaśca svaliṅgavāneva sthāsyati, pradīpta ityarthaḥ | vāśabdo 'vadhāraṇe draṣṭavyo vikalpārtho vā | svaliṅgavāneva agniḥ sthāsyati, yadi vā nāstyanyatvamagnerindhanāditi | samuccaye vā | anyo na prāpsyati na dhakṣyati na ca nirvāsyati svaliṅgavāṃśca sthāsyati | tasmādayuktamindhanādanyatvamagneḥ || 5 ||
body.translated_text: If fire were other than fuel, then, being other, it would not reach the fuel — like darkness. And it would not burn, because of not having reached it — like something situated at a distant place, is the intent. And thus, the statement 'fuel is being kindled' is simply not tenable. And consequently, the extinction of fire would not occur. And not being extinguished, it would remain with its own mark — meaning, ablaze. The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) should be understood as emphatic — or as expressing an alternative: fire will remain with its own mark; alternatively, fire is not other than fuel. Or as a conjunction: being other, it will not reach, it will not burn, it will not go out, and it will remain with its own mark. Therefore, the otherness of fire from fuel is not correct. // 5 //

body.text: atrāha- ayuktamagnīndhanayoranyatvam, yasmānna prāpsyate 'prāpto na dhakṣyatyadahan punarityādi, tadayuktam | dṛṣṭā hi anyatve strīpuruṣayoḥ prāptiḥ, evamagnīndhanayorapi bhaviṣyatīti | ucyate-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: 'The otherness of fire and fuel is not correct, since "being other, it will not reach; not having reached, it will not burn" and so forth — this is not correct. For the mutual contact of man and woman, which are other, is observed; even so, it will be the case for fire and fuel.' The reply is:

children.translated_text: If fire were indeed other than fuel, it could reach the fuel, /

children.text: strī saṃprāpnoti puruṣaṃ puruṣaśca striyaṃ yathā || 6 ||
children.translated_text: just as a woman reaches a man and a man reaches a woman. // 6 //

body.text: syādetadevam, yadi strīpuruṣavatparasparānapekṣā agnīndhanayoḥ siddhiḥ syāt || 6 ||
body.translated_text: This would be so if fire and fuel had an establishment independent of each other, as a man and a woman do. // 6 //

body.text: na tvastītyāha-
body.translated_text: But it is not so — hence he says:

children.translated_text: If fire were indeed other than fuel, it could by all means reach the fuel — /
if fire and fuel existed as mutually exclusive. // 7 //

body.text: na tvevaṃ saṃbhavati yadindhananirapekṣo 'gniḥ syāt, agninirapekṣaṃ cendhanamiti | tasmād dṛṣṭāntavaiyarthyam | anyonyāpekṣādhīnajanmanāṃ satyanyatve yeṣāṃ prāptiḥ siddhā, teṣāmeva dṛṣṭāntatvenopādānaṃ nyāyyaṃ syāt | te ca na saṃbhavantīti na yuktametadanyatve sati prāptirastīti || 7 ||
body.translated_text: But it is not possible that fire could exist independently of fuel, and fuel independently of fire. Therefore, the analogy is pointless. Only for those whose otherness is established while their arising depends on each other could contact be established — and only they could properly be adduced as an analogy. But those [entities] are not possible — hence it is not correct that there is contact when there is otherness. // 7 //

body.text: atrāha- yadyapi agnīndhanayoḥ strīpuruṣavatparasparanirapekṣā siddhirnāsti, tathāpi parasparāpekṣā tāvadasti | tataśca astyevāgnīndhanayoḥ svarūpasiddhiḥ parasparasāpekṣatvāt | na hi avidyamānayorvandhyāputraduhitroḥ parasparāpekṣatā dṛṣṭeti | ucyate | evamapi-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: 'Even though fire and fuel do not have an establishment independent of each other, as a man and a woman do, nevertheless there is at least mutual dependence. And hence there is indeed the own-nature establishment of fire and fuel, because of mutual dependence. For the mutual dependence of a barren woman's son and daughter, who are non-existent, is not observed.' The reply is: Even so —

children.translated_text: If fire exists in dependence on fuel, and if fuel exists in dependence on fire, /
which of the two is established first, in dependence on which fire and fuel [exist]? // 8 //

body.text: asyendhanasya ayamagnirdāhakaḥ kartā, ityevaṃ yadi indhanamapekṣyāgnirvyavasthāpyate, asyāgneridamindhanaṃ karmetyevamagnimapekṣya yadīndhanam, tat kataradanayoḥ pūrvaniṣpannam? kimindhanaṃ yadapekṣyāgni syāt, uta agniryamapekṣyendhanaṃ syāt? tatra yadi indhanaṃ pūrvaniṣpannamiti kalpyate, tadayuktam, agninirapekṣasya anidhyamānasyendhanatvābhāvāt, tṛṇādeḥ sarvasya caiva indhanatvaprasaṅgāt | atha pūrvamagniḥ paścādindhanamiti, tadapyayuktam, indhanātpūrvasiddhasyāgnerasaṃbhavāt, nirhetukatvaprasaṅgāt | paścāccāpekṣayā niṣprayojanatvāt | tasmānnāsti atra kiṃcitpūrvasiddhaṃ yadapekṣya itarasya siddhi syāt || 8 ||
body.translated_text: 'This fire is the burner — the agent — of this fuel' — if thus fire is established in dependence on fuel; and 'this fuel is the object of this fire' — if thus fuel is in dependence on fire — then which of these two is established first? Is it fuel, in dependence on which fire would exist? Or is it fire, in dependence on which fuel would exist? If fuel is imagined to be established first — that is not correct, since without dependence on fire, what is not being kindled does not have the status of fuel, and since all grass and everything else would absurdly become fuel. If fire first and fuel afterward — that too is not correct, since the prior establishment of fire before fuel is impossible, and since it would absurdly be without cause. And subsequently, the dependence would be purposeless. Therefore, there is nothing here that is established first, in dependence on which the other could be established. // 8 //

body.text: athāpi manyase- pūrvamindhanaṃ paścādagniriti, evamapi
body.translated_text: Even if you think: 'Fuel first, fire afterward' — even so,

body.text: yadīndhanamapekṣyāgniragneḥ siddhasya sādhanam |
body.translated_text: if fire exists in dependence on fuel, it would be the establishing of what is already established. /

body.text: bhaviṣyati | yadi indhanamapekṣyāgnirbhaviṣyatīti parikalpyate, evaṃ tarhi siddhasya sato 'gneḥ punarapi sādhanaṃ syāt | vidyamānasyaiva padārthasya siddharūpasyāpekṣā yujyate | na hi avidyamāno devadatto gṛhe kaṃcidapekṣate | evaṃ yadi agnirvidyamāno na syāt, nāsāvindhanamapekṣate | tasmādastitvamagne rambhupeyam | tadā ca kimasya indhanasyāpekṣayā punaḥ kartavyam? na hi siddho 'gniḥ punarindhanena
body.translated_text: If it is imagined that fire will exist in dependence on fuel, then there would be a re-establishing of fire that already exists. For the dependence of an entity that already exists in an established form is appropriate. For a non-existent <s>Devadatta</s> does not depend on anyone at home. Likewise, if fire did not already exist, it would not depend on fuel. Therefore, the existence of fire must be accepted. And in that case, what further is to be done by dependence on fuel? For an already-established fire does not need to be further

body.text: kartavyo yadarthamindhanāpekṣāsāphalyaṃ syāt | tasmādindhanamapekṣyāgnirbhavatīti na yuktam |
body.translated_text: made by fuel — for which purpose the dependence on fuel would be fruitful. Therefore, 'fire exists in dependence on fuel' is not correct.

body.text: api ca | yadi indhanamapekṣyāgnirbhavatīti parikalpyate-
body.translated_text: Moreover, if it is imagined that fire exists in dependence on fuel —

body.text: evaṃ satīndhanaṃ cāpi bhaviṣyati niragnikam || 9 ||
body.translated_text: that being so, fuel too will exist without fire. // 9 //

body.text: yadi indhanamasiddhaṃ syāt, naiva tadagninā apekṣyeta, asiddhasyāpekṣāyogāt | tasmānniragnikasyendhanasya siddhirabhyupeyā, na caivametaditi na yuktametaditi || 9 ||
body.translated_text: If fuel were unestablished, it would simply not be depended upon by fire, since dependence upon what is unestablished is not possible. Therefore, the establishment of fuel without fire must be accepted — but this is not so — hence this is not correct. // 9 //

body.text: atha matam- yaugapadyenaiva indhanasiddhayā agnisiddhiḥ, agnisiddhayā ca indhanasiddiḥ | tataśca ekasyāpi pūrvasiddhayanabhyupagamāt, tatra yaduktam-
body.translated_text: If it is thought: 'Simultaneously — by the establishment of fuel, fire is established, and by the establishment of fire, fuel is established. And hence, since neither is accepted as established first, the objection raised —

body.text: kataratpūrvaniṣpannaṃ yadapekṣyāgnirindhanam |
body.translated_text: 'Which of the two is established first, in dependence on which fire and fuel [exist]?' /

body.text: iti, tadayuktamiti | ucyate | evamapīṣyamāṇe ubhayasyāpi nāsti siddhiḥ | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: — is not correct.' The reply is: Even when desired in this way, the establishment of both is impossible. For —

children.translated_text: An entity that is established in dependence on something — that very thing is established in dependence on it. /

children.text: yadi yo 'pekṣitavyaḥ sa sidhyatāṃ kamapekṣya kaḥ || 10 ||
children.translated_text: If that which is to be depended upon is itself to be established, then depending on what is what established? // 10 //

body.text: tatra yadi yaḥ agnyākhyo bhāvaḥ yamindhanākhyaṃ bhāvamapekṣya sidhyati, indhanākhyaśca bhāvaḥ yo 'gninā ātmasiddhayarthamapekṣitavyaḥ, sa yadi tameva agnyākhyaṃ padārthamapekṣya sidhyati, kathyatāmidānīṃ sidhyatāṃ kamapekṣya kaḥ iti | yadā ca agnyabhāve sati indhanasya siddhireva nāsti, tadā akāraṇasyendhanasyābhāvāt kutastaddhetuko 'gniḥ prasetsyati? evaṃ ya indhanākhyo bhāvaḥ yamagnyākhyaṃ bhāvamapekṣya sidhyati, agnyākhyaśca bhāvo yaḥ indhanākhyena ātmasiddhayarthamapekṣitavyaḥ, sa yadi tamevendhanākhyaṃ bhāvamapekṣya sidhyati, kathyatāṃ kimidānīṃ sidhyatāṃ kamapekṣya kaḥ iti | yadā hi indhanābhāve sati agneḥ siddhirnāsti, tadā niṣkāraṇasyāgnerabhāvāt kutastaddhetukamindhanam? || 10 ||
body.translated_text: Therein, if the entity called fire is established in dependence on the entity called fuel, and if the entity called fuel, which must be depended upon by fire for its own establishment, is itself established in dependence on that very entity called fire — then let it now be stated: which is established in dependence on which? And when, in the absence of fire, there is no establishment of fuel at all, then, since fuel, which has no cause, is non-existent, how can fire, which is caused by it, be established? Likewise, the entity called fuel, which is established in dependence on the entity called fire — and the entity called fire, which must be depended upon by fuel for its own establishment — if it is itself established in dependence on that very entity called fuel, then let it be stated: which now is established in dependence on which? For when, in the absence of fuel, there is no establishment of fire, then, since fire, being without cause, is non-existent, how can fuel, which is caused by it, exist? // 10 //

body.text: itaśca agnīndhanayoḥ parasparāpekṣayāpi siddhirasatī, siddhāsiddhayorapekṣābhāvāditi pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And furthermore, showing that even through mutual dependence the establishment of fire and fuel is impossible, because there is no dependence between what is established and what is not established, he says:

children.translated_text: The entity that is established in dependence [on another] — how can it, being unestablished, depend [on that other]? /
And if it depends while being established, dependence is not appropriate for it. // 11 //

body.text: yo hi agnyākhyo bhāvaḥ indhanākhyaṃ bhāvamapekṣya sidhyati, saḥ asiddho vā indhanamapekṣate siddho vā? yadi asiddhaḥ, tadā asiddhatvāt kharaviṣāṇavannendhanamapekṣeta | atha siddhaḥ, siddhatvāt kimasyendhanāpekṣayā? na hi siddhaṃ punarapi sādhyate vaiyarthyāt | evamindhane 'pi vācyam | tasmānnāgnīndhanayoḥ parasparāpekṣayā yaugapadyena vā siddhiriti || 11 ||
body.translated_text: The entity called fire that is established in dependence on the entity called fuel — does it depend on fuel while being unestablished, or while being established? If unestablished, then, being unestablished like a donkey's horn, it could not depend on fuel. If established, then, being already established, what need has it of dependence on fuel? For what is established is not established again — that would be purposeless. The same should be said regarding fuel. Therefore, there is no establishment of fire and fuel through mutual dependence or simultaneously. // 11 //

body.text: yataścaivam, tasmāt-
body.translated_text: And since this is so, therefore:

body.text: apekṣyendhanamagnirna
body.translated_text: Fire does not exist in dependence on fuel. /

body.text: atha syāt- anapekṣyāgnistarhi bhaviṣyatīti | etadapi na yuktamityāha-
body.translated_text: Now, one might say: then fire will exist without dependence [on fuel]. This too is not correct — hence he says:

body.text: nānapekṣyāgnirindhanam |
body.translated_text: Nor does fire exist without dependence on fuel. /

body.text: anyatvapratiṣedhādahetukatvaprasaṅgācca | yathā ca agnirapekṣya vā anapekṣya vā indhanaṃ saṃbhavati, evamindhanamapītyāha-
body.translated_text: Because of the negation of otherness, and because of the absurd consequence of causelessness. And just as fire is impossible whether dependent on or independent of fuel, so too is fuel — hence he says:

body.text: apekṣyendhanamagniṃ na nānapekṣyāgnimindhanam || 12 ||
body.translated_text: Fuel does not exist in dependence on fire, nor does fuel exist without dependence on fire. // 12 //

body.text: etacca anantarameva gatārthatvānna punarucyate || 12 ||
body.translated_text: And this, because its meaning has just been stated, need not be repeated. // 12 //

body.text: atrāha- kimanayā asmākamatisūkṣmekṣikayā prayojanam, ye vayaṃ brūmaḥ- yasmādagninā idhyamānamindhanaṃ pratyakṣata upalabhyate, tasmātte eva agnīndhane iti | ucyate | syādetadevam, yadi agnirindhanaṃ dahet | yadi indhane 'gniḥ saṃbhavet, sa indhanaṃ dahet | na tu saṃbhavatītyāha-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: what is the purpose of this exceedingly subtle investigation of ours, when we say: since fire burning fuel is directly perceived, therefore fire and fuel do indeed exist? The reply is: this would be so if fire were to burn fuel. If fire existed in fuel, it could burn fuel. But it does not exist — hence he says:

body.text: āgacchatyanyato nāgnirindhane 'gnirna vidyate |
body.translated_text: Fire does not come from elsewhere; fire is not found in fuel. /

body.text: indhanavyatiriktāttāvatkutaścidanyato 'gnerāgamanaṃ nāsti, tasya adṛṣṭatvāt | nirindhanasya cāhetukasyāgnerāgamanābhāvāt, sendhanasya cāgamane prayojanābhāvāt, tatrāpi cendhane tulyaparyanuyogāt, anavasthāprasaṅgācca āgacchatyanyato nāgniḥ | tathā indhane 'pyagnirna saṃbhavati tatrānupalabhyamānatvāt |
body.translated_text: First, there is no coming of fire from anywhere else apart from fuel, because that has not been observed. And because a fireless, causeless fire cannot come, and because there is no purpose in the coming of fire that already has fuel, and because even there the same objection regarding fuel would apply equally, and because of the absurd consequence of infinite regress — fire does not come from elsewhere. Likewise, fire is not found in fuel, because it is not perceived there.

body.text: atha syāt- vidyamānasyāpi mūlodakādivadabhivyañjakapratyayavaikalyātpūrvamanupalabhyamānatvam, araṇinigharṣaṇādabhivyañjakapratyayasaṃbhavāttu paścādupalabdhiriti | idameva tāvatsaṃpradhāryate- kiṃ punarmūlodakādīnāmabhivyañjakaiḥ pratyayaiḥ kriyata iti | tatra svarūpaṃ tāvanna kriyate vidyamānatvāt abhivyaktiḥ kriyata iti cet, keyamabhivyaktirnāma? prakāśateti cet, evaṃ tarhi saiva kriyate pūrvamavidyamānatvādasyāḥ | satkāryavādatyāgaścaivaṃ jāyate abhivyakteḥ pūrvamavidyamānatvātpaścācca bhāvāt | svarūpasya cotpattipratyayanirapekṣatvātkhapuṣpavadabhivyaktipratyayasāpekṣatāpi na syāt | api ca iyamabhivyaktirabhivyaktasya vā bhāvasya parikalpyeta anabhivyaktasya vā? tatra tāvad yadabhivyaktaṃ tannābhivyajyate, tasyābhivyaktivaiyarthyāt aniṣṭadoṣaprasaṅgācca | anabhivyaktamapi nābhivyajyate khapuṣpavadanabhivyaktatvāt | ityevamabhivyaktirna saṃbhavati ||
body.translated_text: Now, one might say: even something that exists may be unperceived earlier due to the absence of the manifesting conditions, such as roots and water [for a plant], and is perceived later when the manifesting conditions — such as the friction of fire-sticks — come together. This is what must first be considered: what exactly do the manifesting conditions do to roots, water, and the like? Therein, they do not create the essential form, since it [already] exists. If it is said that manifestation (<s>abhivyakti</s>) is created — what is this thing called manifestation? If it is said: 'it becomes manifest' — then that very manifestation itself is being created, since it did not exist before. And thus the <s>satkāryavāda</s> (doctrine that the effect pre-exists in the cause) is abandoned, since the manifestation did not exist before and comes into being afterwards. And since the essential form is independent of productive conditions, there should be no dependence on manifesting conditions either, just as for a sky-flower. Moreover, would this manifestation be conceived of an entity that is already manifest or one that is unmanifest? Therein, what is already manifest is not manifested, because manifesting it would be purposeless and because undesired consequences would follow. What is unmanifest too is not manifested, because, like a sky-flower, it is unmanifest. Thus manifestation is impossible.

body.text: athāpi syāt- vidyamānasyaiva pratyayaiḥ sthaulyaṃ kriyate iti, evamapi yadeva sthaulyaṃ pūrvaṃ nāstīti tadeva kriyata iti kutaḥ sthaulyāpādanamabhivyaktiḥ? saukṣmyasya ca nirhetukasyāsaṃbhavāt kasya sthūlatāpādanādabhivyaktiḥ syāditi | tadevaṃ sarvathā indhane agnerna saṃbhava iti indhane 'gnirna vidyate | na cāvidyamānāgninā indhanasya dahanamupajāyate ityasatyamevaitadupalabhate bhavān |
body.translated_text: Now, one might further say: the conditions produce grossness (<s>sthaulya</s>) of what already exists. Even so, since that very grossness that did not exist before is what is being produced — how is the production of grossness a manifestation? And since subtlety (<s>saukṣmya</s>) without a cause is impossible, whose transformation into grossness would constitute manifestation? Thus, in every way, fire is not possible in fuel — hence 'fire is not found in fuel.' And fire that does not exist does not give rise to the burning of fuel — therefore what you perceive is indeed unreal.

body.text: api ca | yathā pūrvaṃ gatāgatagamyamānānāṃ dūṣaṇamuktam-
body.translated_text: Moreover, just as previously the refutation by means of the gone-to, being-gone-to, and not-yet-gone-to was stated:

body.text: atrendhane śeṣamuktaṃ gamyamānagatāgataiḥ || 13 ||
body.translated_text: The remainder regarding fuel here has been stated by means of the being-gone-to, gone-to, and not-yet-gone-to. // 13 //

body.text: agninā indhanaṃ dahyamānamupalabhyate ityatra indhanaprastāve śeṣaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ gamyamānagatāgatadūṣaṇena veditavyam, uktapāṭhaviparyayeṇa-
body.translated_text: Regarding the claim that 'fire is observed burning fuel' — in this context of fuel, the remaining refutation should be understood through the refutation by means of the being-gone-to, gone-to, and not-yet-gone-to, by transposing the stated formulation:

children.text: dagdhaṃ na dahyate tāvadadagdhaṃ naiva dahyate |
children.translated_text: What is burnt is not being burnt; what is unburnt is not being burnt. /
What is being burnt, distinct from the burnt and unburnt, is not being burnt. //

body.text: ityādinā | yata evam, ato nāstyagninā indhanasya dahanamiti veditavyam || 13 ||
body.translated_text: And so forth. Since this is so, it should be understood that fire does not burn fuel. // 13 //

body.text: idānīṃ yathopapāditamarthaṃ nigamayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, concluding the point that has been demonstrated, he says:

children.translated_text: Fuel, again, is not fire; nor is fire found apart from fuel. /
Fire does not possess fuel; fuel is not in fire; nor is fire in them. // 14 //

body.text: tatra
body.translated_text: Therein,

body.text: yadindhanaṃ sa cedagnirekatvaṃ kartṛkarmaṇoḥ |
body.translated_text: 'If fuel were fire, there would be an identity of agent and action' — /

body.text: bhavet, ityanena agnīndhanayorakatvapratiṣedhāt
body.translated_text: by this, the identity of fire and fuel has been negated, hence:

body.text:
indhanaṃ punaragnirna,
anyaścedindhanādagnirindhanādapyṛte bhavet |
body.translated_text:
Fuel, again, is not fire.
'If fire were other than fuel, it would exist even without fuel' — /

body.text: ityādinā anyatvasya pratiṣedhāt
body.translated_text: by this and such statements, their otherness has been negated, hence:

body.text: nāgniranyatra cendhanāt |
body.translated_text: Nor is fire found apart from fuel. /

body.text: tattvānyatvobhayapakṣapratiṣedhādeva tadvatpakṣādhārādheyapakṣāṇāmapyarthataḥ pratiṣiddhatvāttānapi nigamayannāha-
body.translated_text: Since the positions of identity and otherness and both have been negated, the positions of possession, container-and-contained are also implicitly negated. Concluding those as well, he says:

body.text: nāgnirindhanavānnāgnāvindhanāni na teṣu saḥ |
body.translated_text: Fire does not possess fuel; fuel is not in fire; nor is fire in them. /

body.text: iti | tatrāgnirindhanavānna bhavati | indhanamasyāsmin vā vidyata iti vyatirekeṇa vā vyutpādena avyatirekeṇa vā | tatra vyatirekeṇa- tadyathā gomān devadattaḥ | avyatirekeṇa- buddhimān devadatto rūpavānityādi | agnīndhanayośca pakṣadvayasyāpi pratiṣiddhatvādindhanavānagniriti pratiṣedho vihitaḥ | anyacca | kuṇḍaṃ dadhna ādhāratāṃ pratipadyate | na cendhanādanyatvamagnerastīti nāgnāvindhanānīti yujyate | nāpi indhane 'styagniḥ, anyatvapratiṣedhāditi | evamādhārādheyatāpratiṣedho 'pyarthata upapādita eva || 14 ||
body.translated_text: Therein, fire does not possess fuel. 'It has fuel' or 'fuel exists in it' — whether through separation or through non-separation. Therein, through separation — for example: '<s>Devadatta</s> possesses cows.' Through non-separation — for example: '<s>Devadatta</s> possesses intelligence,' '<s>Devadatta</s> possesses beauty,' and so forth. And since both positions regarding fire and fuel have been negated, the negation of 'fire possesses fuel' is established. Furthermore, a pot serves as the container for curds. But since fire is not other than fuel, 'fuel is in fire' is not tenable. Nor is there fire in fuel, because of the negation of otherness. Thus the negation of the container-and-contained relationship too has been effectively demonstrated. // 14 //

body.text: yathā cāgniḥ pañcadhā vicāryamāṇo na saṃbhavati, evamātmāpi, ityatidiśannāha-
body.translated_text: And just as fire, when examined in five ways, is impossible, so too is the self (<s>ātman</s>) — extending this analogy, he says:

body.text:
agnīndhanābhyāṃ vyākhyāta ātmopādānayoḥ kramaḥ |
sarvo niravaśeṣeṇa
body.translated_text:
By means of fire and fuel, the procedure regarding the self (<s>ātman</s>) and the appropriated (<s>upādāna</s>) has been explained /
in its entirety. /

body.text: tatra upādīyate ityupādānaṃ pañcopādānaskandhāḥ | yastānupādāya prajñapyate, sa upādātā grahītā niṣpādaka ātmetyucyate | ahaṃkāraviṣayatvādāhita utpādito 'haṃmāno 'sminniti | tadasyātmana upādānasya ca yaḥ kramaḥ siddhiḥ, sa sarvo 'gnīndhanābhyāṃ vyākhyāto 'vagantavyo niravaśeṣeṇa ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>upādāna</s> (appropriated) — 'that which is appropriated' — means the five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> (aggregates of clinging). He who is designated in dependence on appropriating them is the <s>upādātṛ</s> (appropriator), the grasper, the accomplisher, and is called the <s>ātman</s> (self) — because the sense of 'I' (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) is directed toward it, i.e., the conceit 'I am' is produced and established in it. The procedure — i.e., the establishment — of this self and the appropriated has been completely explained through fire and fuel, and should be so understood.

body.text: kaḥ punaḥ sarvasya niravaśeṣasya ca bhedaḥ? sarvagrahaṇenaiva pañca pakṣāḥ samanantaraprakrānta abhisaṃbadhyante | sarve ete pañcāpi pakṣāḥ agnīndhanavadātmopādānayorapyavikalā ḍhaukanīyāḥ | yaścaiyā pratipādane upapattikramaḥ prāgupavarṇitaḥ, tena niravaśeṣeṇa ātmopādānayoḥ pratiṣedho veditavyaḥ ityanena sarvātmanā pratiṣedhasāmyamagnīndhanābhyāmātmopādānayorveditavyamityupadarśanārthaṃ sarvo nirava śeṣeṇetyāha | tatra yadevopādānaṃ sa eva ātmā, ityevaṃ kartṛkarmaṇorekatvaprasaṅgānna yujyate nāpyanyadupādānamanya upādātā, skandhavyatirekeṇāpyātmopalabdhiprasaṅgāt, paratra nirapekṣatvādityādiprasaṅgācca | ekatvānyatvapratiṣedhācca skandhavānaṣyātmā na bhavati | anyatvābhāvācca nātmani skandhā na skandheṣvātmā | yata evaṃ pañcasu prakāreṣu ātmano na sattvam, tasmātkarmakārakavadeva ātmopādānayoḥ parasparāpekṣikī siddhiriti sthitam ||
body.translated_text: What then is the difference between 'all' and 'in its entirety'? By the word 'all,' the five positions that have just been set forth are connected. All these five positions should be applied, complete and without exception, to the self and the appropriated, just as with fire and fuel. And the sequence of reasoning that was described above in their demonstration — by that, in its entirety, the negation of the self and the appropriated should be understood. Thus, by the words 'all' and 'in its entirety,' it is shown that the negation of the self and the appropriated is in complete parity with fire and fuel. Therein, that the <s>upādāna</s> itself is the <s>ātman</s> — this is not tenable because of the absurd consequence of identity of agent and action. Nor is the <s>upādāna</s> one thing and the <s>upādātṛ</s> another, because of the absurd consequence that the <s>ātman</s> would be apprehended even apart from the <s>skandhas</s>, and because of consequences such as independence from what is other, and so forth. And because of the negation of both identity and otherness, the <s>ātman</s> does not possess the <s>skandhas</s>. And because of the absence of otherness, the <s>skandhas</s> are not in the <s>ātman</s>, nor is the <s>ātman</s> in the <s>skandhas</s>. Since in these five ways the <s>ātman</s> has no existence, therefore, just as with agent and action, it is established that the self and the appropriated are mutually dependent in their establishment.

body.text: yaścāyamātmopādānayoḥ kramaḥ, sa nānayoreva, kiṃ tarhi-
body.translated_text: And this procedure regarding the self and the appropriated applies not only to these two, but rather:

body.text: sārdhaṃ ghaṭapaṭādibhiḥ || 15 ||
body.translated_text: together with pots, cloths, and the like. // 15 //

body.text: niravaśeṣaiḥ padārthaiḥ sarvathā vyākhyāto veditavyaḥ | ghaṭādayo hi kāryakāraṇabhūta avayavāvayavibhūtā lakṣaṇalakṣyabhūtā guṇnaguṇibhūtā vā syuḥ | tatra mṛddaṇḍacakrasūtrasalilakulālakaravyāyāmādayo ghaṭasya kāraṇabhūtāḥ, ghaṭaḥ kāryabhūtaḥ | kapālādayo nīlādayo vā avayavabhūtāḥ ghaṭo 'vayavī | pṛthubudhnalambauṣṭhadīrghagrīvatvādīni lakṣaṇāni ghaṭo lakṣyaḥ| śyāmatvādayo guṇāḥ, ghaṭo guṇī | ityevaṃ vyavasthāpya agnīndhanavat kramo yojyaḥ | eṣāṃ ca ghaṭādīnāmātmopādānayośca madhyamakāvatāraprakaraṇād vyākhyānamavaseyam || 15 ||
body.translated_text: It should be understood as explained in every way with respect to all entities without exception. For pots and the like may be in the relation of effect and cause, whole and parts, characterized and characteristic, or quality and quality-possessor. Therein, clay, a stick, a wheel, string, water, the exertion of the potter's hand, and so forth are the causes of a pot; the pot is the effect. Potsherds, blue color, and so on are the parts; the pot is the whole. Having a broad base, a bulging lip, a long neck, and so forth are the characteristics; the pot is the characterized. Being dark in color and so forth are the qualities; the pot is the quality-possessor. Having thus established this, the procedure should be applied as with fire and fuel. And the explanation of these pots and the like, as well as the self and the appropriated, should be understood from the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s> treatise. // 15 //

body.text: tadevaṃ karmakārakavadātmopādānayorghaṭādīnāṃ ca parasparāpekṣikyāṃ siddhau vyavasthitāyāṃ tathāgatavacanāviparītārthāvabodhābhimānitayā tīrthyamatopakalpitapadārthavyavasthāṃ saugatapravacanārthatvenopanīya atimūḍhatayā-
body.translated_text: Thus, when it is established that the self and the appropriated, as well as pots and the like, are mutually dependent in their establishment — just as with agent and action — those who, with the conceit of understanding the meaning of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching unerringly, take up the system of entities fabricated by non-Buddhist doctrines as the meaning of the <s>Sugata</s>'s teaching, and out of extreme delusion:

children.text: ātmanaśca satattvaṃ ye bhāvānāṃ ca pṛthakpṛthak |
children.translated_text: Those who teach the real identity of the self and of entities severally — /
I do not consider them as knowers of the meaning of the teaching. // 16 //

body.text: tatra saha tena vartata iti satat, satato bhāvaḥ satattvam, apṛthaktvam, ananyatvam ekatvamityarthaḥ | tadetat satattvaṃ ye varṇayanti, na tānācāryaḥ śāsanārthapaṇḍitān manyate | tadyathā- ātmā upādānena prajñapyate yena, sahaiva tenopādānena saṃbhavati | sa na pṛthak | avyatirekeṇaiva bhavatītyarthaḥ | evaṃ yena kāraṇena mṛdādinā ghaṭaḥ prajñapyate, tadavyatirekeṇaiva sa bhavati, na pṛthak | evamātmano bhāvānāṃ ca satattvaṃ ye varṇayanti, na te paramagambhīrasya pratītyasamutpādastha śāśvatocchedarahitasya upādāyaprajñaptyabhidhānasya tattvaṃ paśyanti | pṛthak pṛthak ca ye nirdiśanti, pṛthagityātmānam, pṛthagupādānam, pṛthak kāryam, pṛthak kāraṇam, ityādinā anyatvaṃ paśyanti, amūnapi na śāsanasyārthakovidānācāryo manyate | yathoktam-
body.translated_text: Therein, 'existing together with' (<s>saha tena vartate</s>) is <s>satat</s>; the state of being <s>satat</s> is <s>satattva</s> — meaning non-separateness, non-otherness, identity. Those who describe this identity — the <s>Ācārya</s> does not consider them as learned in the meaning of the teaching. For instance: the self is designated by that <s>upādāna</s> by which [it is designated]; it exists together with that very <s>upādāna</s>; it is not separate — it exists only in non-separation. This is the meaning. Likewise, the pot that is designated by that cause — clay and the like — exists only in non-separation from them, not separately. Thus, those who describe the identity of the self and of entities — they do not see the truth of the supremely profound <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>, which is free from eternalism and annihilationism, and which is expressed by the term 'designation in dependence on that which is appropriated' (<s>upādāyaprajñapti</s>). And those who teach them as separate — 'separate' meaning: the self is separate, the appropriated is separate, the effect is separate, the cause is separate, and so forth — those who see otherness in this way, the <s>Ācārya</s> does not consider them to be knowers of the meaning of the teaching either. As it is said:

children.translated_text: The world, devoid of identity and otherness, is like an echo. /

body.text: evaṃ ca agnīndhanaparīkṣayā adhigatadharmatattvaparamasya yoginaḥ kalpenākālālipsitairapi naiva vapurdahyate rāgadveṣamohahutāśanairapi vā iti | yathoktaṃ bhagavatā-

gaganasama vijānamāna dharmān so 'pi na dahyati jātu sāgnimadhye ||
sarvi hi jvalamāṇi buddhakṣetre praṇidhi karoti samādhiye sthihitvā |
jvalata ayu praśāmyatāmaśeṣa pṛthivi vinaśyipi naivasyānyathātvam ||
araṇiṃ yatha cottarāraṇiṃ hastavyāyāmu trayebhi saṃgatiḥ |
iti pratyayato 'gni jāyate jātu kṛtu kārya laghū nirudhyate ||
atha paṇḍitu kaści mārgate kuta ayamāgatu kutra yāti vā |

skandhāyatanāni dhātavaḥ śūnya ādhyātmika śūnya bāhirāḥ |

anubuddha yatha tvayātmanā tatha bodhehi sadevamānuṣān ||
iti vistaraḥ ||

atrāha- vidyata eva ātmā, saṃsārasadbhāvāt | yadi hi ātmā na syāt, kasya pañcagatike ājavaṃjavībhāvena janmamaraṇaparaṃparayā saṃsaraṇaṃ syāt? uktaṃ hi bhagavatā- anavarāgro hi bhikṣavo jātijarāmaraṇasaṃsāraḥ iti | avidyānīvaraṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ tṛṣṇāsaṃyojanānāṃ tṛṣṇāgaṇḍurabaddhānāṃ saṃsaratāṃ saṃdhāvatāṃ pūrvā koṭirna prajñāyata iti | yadā ca bhagavadupadeśātsaṃsāro 'sti, tadā saṃsartāpyasti | sa ca ātmā ucyata iti | ucyate | syādātmā, yadā saṃsāra eva syāt | katham? yasmādasya-

koṭirbhāgo deśa iti paryāyāḥ | pūrvā koṭiḥ pūrvo deśa ityarthaḥ | yadi hi saṃsāro nāma kaścit syāt, niyataṃ tasya pūrvamapi syāt, paścimamapi, ghaṭādīnāmiva | uktaṃ ca bhagavatā- anavarāgro hi bhikṣavo jātijarāmaraṇasaṃsāra iti | yadeva avarāgre na staḥ, saṃsārasya anavarāgravacanāt, saṃsāra eva nāstīti nanu spaṣṭamādeśayāmāsa bhagavān | tasmānnāsti saṃsāraḥ, pūrvāparakoṭayanupalambhāt, alātacakravat, iti sthitam ||

atredaṃ vicāryate- yadi pūrvaṃ cāparaṃ ca saṃsārasya niṣiddhaṃ bhagavatā, kathaṃ punaridamāha- tasmāttarhi saṃsārakṣayāya pratipatsyāmaha ityevaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam, iti? ucyate | avidyānīvaraṇānāṃ sattvānāmityādiviśeṣaṇopādānātteṣāmevāyamanavarāgraḥ saṃsāra iti pratīyate, na punastattvajñānānilabalāt samunmūlitāvidyānīvaraṇatarūṇām | teṣāṃ tu lokottaramārgajñānāgninā dagdhāśeṣakleśavāsanāmūlaniḥśeṣapādapānāṃ bhavatyeva antaḥ iti vijñeyam ||
kathaṃ punarādirahitānāmantopadeśa iti yāvat | dṛṣṭametad bāhyeṣu vrīhyādiṣu ādyabhāve 'pi dahanādisaṃparkādantasadbhāvaḥ | yathoktamāryadevapādaiḥ-

yathā bījasya dṛṣṭo 'nto na cādistasya vidyate |
tathā kāraṇavaikalyājjanmano 'pi na saṃbhavaḥ || iti |

sa ca antopadeśo laukika eva vyavahāre sthitvā saṃsāracārakāvabaddhānāmutsāhanārthaṃ sattvānāṃ deśito laukikajñānāpekṣayā | vastukacintāyāṃ tu saṃsāra eva nāsti, tatkuto 'sya parikṣayaḥ? pradīpāvasthāyāṃ rajjūragaparikṣayavat ||
atrāha- yadyevaṃ laukikajñānāpekṣayā antavad ādirapi kiṃ nocyate? ucyate | ahetukadoṣaprasaṅgāt laukikajñānāpekṣayāpi saṃsārasyāderabhāva ityubhayathāpyāderabhāva eveti vijñeyam || 1 ||

atrāha- yadyāpi avarāgre na staḥ saṃsārasya, tathāpi madhyamasti, apratiṣedhāt | tataśca asti saṃsāro madhyasadbhāvāt | iha yannāsti, na tasya madhyamasti tadyathā kūrmaromaprāvaraṇasyeti | hāsyaḥ khalvasi | nanu ca bhoḥ,
naivāgraṃ nāvaraṃ yasya tasya madhyaṃ kuto bhavet |

agramiti ādiḥ, pūrvam, prathamam ucyate | avaramiti avasānam, antaḥ, vyavaccheda ucyate | yasya saṃsārasya ādirantaśca pratiṣiddhaḥ, tasya kuto madhyaṃ bhaviṣyati? tataśca saṃjñāmātrakameva viparyāsaparavaśamānasānāṃ saṃsāraḥ ādimadhyāvasānavirahitatvādākāśavadalātacakrādivaditi bhāvaḥ | saṃsārābhāvācca nāsti ātmeti | yata evaṃ saṃsārasyādimadhyāvasānāni na santi, ata eva saṃsārābhāvājjātijarāmaraṇādīnāṃ pūrvāparasahakramā api naiva santītyāha-
tasmānnātropapadyante pūrvāparasahakramāḥ || 2 ||
yathā ca nopapadyante tathā pratipādayannāha-

yadi pūrvaṃ jātirbhavet, tadā maraṇasahitā syāt | na ca jarādirahitā jātiryujyate, asaṃskṛtatvaprasaṅgāt | jarāmaraṇarahitasya bhāvasya jātau parikalpyamānāyāmanyatra amṛtasyaiva devadattasya prathamamiha jātiḥ parikalpyamānā syāt | tataśca ādimān saṃsāraḥ syādahetukadoṣaśca | abhūvamatītamadhvānam, ityevaṃ pūrvāntakalpanā ca na syāt | abhūtvā ca pūrvaṃ paścādihotpādaḥ syāt ||

atha syāt- āmrādīnāṃ yathā pūrvaṃ vināpi jarāmaraṇasaṃbandhāt prathamameva utpādo dṛṣṭaḥ, evamātmāno 'pīti | naivam | sādhyasamatvāt | āmrādīnāmapi hi svabījanirodhe samutpadyamānatvāt nānyatrāvinaṣṭānāmutpāda iti samametat pūrveṇa ||
atha syāt- anyadeva vṛkṣādbījam, ato 'nyatrāvināśapūrvaka eva vṛkṣasyotpāda iti naivam | kāryakāraṇayoranyatvasyāsiddhatvāt | tathā ca vakṣyati-

yadi sahabhāvo jātijarāmaraṇānāṃ syāt, tadā jāyamānasya maraṇaṃ syāt | na caitadyuktam | na ca parasparaviruddhatvādālokāndhakāravadekakālatā yuktā | na caivaṃ loke dṛṣṭaṃ yajjāyamāna eva mriyate iti | api ca | ahetukatvaṃ jātyādīnāṃ sahabhāvakalpanāyāṃ syāt | na hi sahabhūtayoḥ savyetaragoviṣāṇayoranyonyahetukatā dṛṣṭeti na yuktametat || 5 ||
tadevam-

tathā-

nityamasāraka māyasabhāvāḥ śuddha viśuddha nabhopama sarvi ||
yaṃ ca pabhāṣati dharma jinasya taṃ ca na paśyati so 'kṣayatāya |

children.translated_text: The limit that was characterless — [the question of] 'it existed before' or 'it will not come' is for the sake of conditionality. //

body.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> (action) and activity proceed thus; they arise as lower and higher. /

body.translated_text: Know all <s>dharmas</s> as always empty by nature, without self, O foolish ones! //
