body.translated_text: And so forth.

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacitāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau pūrvāparakoṭiparīkṣā nāmaikādaśamaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus concludes the eleventh chapter, titled 'The Examination of the Prior and Posterior Limits,' in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary composed by the venerable <s>Ācārya Candrakīrti</s>.

body.text:
12
duḥkhaparīkṣā dvādaśamaṃ prakaraṇam |
body.translated_text:
12
The Examination of Suffering — the twelfth chapter.

body.text: atrāha- vidyata eva ātmā, tatsaṃbandhiduḥkhasadbhāvāt | iha hi pañcopādānaskandhā duḥkhamityucyate, tacca asti, tena ca duḥkhena kasyacidbhavitavyaṃ na nirāśrayeṇeti, ato vidyata eva duḥkhasyāśrayaḥ, sa cātmeti | ucyate | syādātmā yadi duḥkhameva syāt | taddhi bhavet svayaṃ kṛtaṃ vā parakṛtaṃ vā ubhayakṛtaṃ vā heturahitaṃ vā | sarvathā ca iṣyamāṇaṃ tatkāryameva nāstīti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: 'The self does indeed exist, because the suffering related to it truly exists. For the five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> (aggregates of clinging) are said to be suffering, and that exists; and that suffering must belong to someone — it is not without a support. Therefore, the support of suffering does indeed exist, and that is the self.' The reply is: The self would exist if suffering itself existed. For that [suffering] would be either self-made, or made by another, or made by both, or without a cause. And in every case, that effect does not exist — demonstrating this, he says:

children.translated_text: Self-made, made by another, made by both, or without a cause — /

children.text: duḥkhamityeka icchanti tacca kāryaṃ na yujyate || 1 ||
children.translated_text: some hold suffering [to arise] thus; but that as an effect is not appropriate. // 1 //

body.text: tatraike vādinaḥ svayaṃ kṛtaṃ duḥkhamiti pratipannāḥ | apare punaḥ parakṛtam, anye ca ubhayakṛtam| kecidahetusamutpannameva duḥkhamiti pratipannāḥ | sarvathā ca tadduḥkhamiṣyamāṇaṃ kāryaṃ kartavyaṃ na yujyate, tadetatpratijñāmātrakamiti || 1 ||
body.translated_text: Therein, some proponents hold that suffering is self-made. Others hold it to be made by another. Others hold it to be made by both. Some hold that suffering has arisen without a cause. In every case, that suffering, however conceived, is not appropriate as an effect to be produced — this is merely a thesis-statement. // 1 //

body.text: tatpratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Demonstrating this, he says:

children.text: svayaṃ kṛtaṃ yadi bhavetpratītya na tato bhavet |
children.translated_text: If it were self-made, it would not exist dependently. /
For these aggregates arise in dependence on those aggregates. // 2 //

body.text: yasmādimān maraṇāntikān skandhān pratītya ime aupapattyāṃśikāḥ skandhā utpadyante tasmātsvayaṃ kṛtaṃ duḥkhamiti nopapadyate || 2 ||
body.translated_text: Since these aggregates of the rebirth-phase arise in dependence on those aggregates of the death-phase, therefore the statement 'suffering is self-made' is not tenable. // 2 //

body.text: idānīṃ parakṛtamapi duḥkhaṃ yathā na saṃbhavati, tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, demonstrating that suffering made by another is also impossible, he says:

children.text: yadyamībhya ime 'nye syurebhyo vāmī pare yadi |
children.translated_text: If these [aggregates] were other than those, or if those were other than these, /
suffering would be made by another — these would be made by those others. // 3 //

body.text: yadā amībhyo maraṇāntikebhyaḥ skandhebhyaḥ ime aupapattyāṃśikāḥ skandhā anye syuḥ, ebhyo vā aupapattyāṃśikebhyaḥ amī maraṇāntikā skandhāḥ pare syuḥ, syāttadānīṃ parakṛtaṃ duḥkham | na caiṣāmanyatvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ hetuphalasaṃbandhāvasthānāt | vakṣyati hi-

pratītya yadyadbhavati na hi tāvattadeva tat |
na cānyadapi tattasmānnocchinnaṃ nāpi śāśvatam || iti |

ataḥ parakṛtamapi duḥkhaṃ na saṃbhavati | yadi hi anyatvaṃ syāt, tadā sati anyatve etaiḥ parabhūtaiḥ skandhairamī parabhūtāḥ kṛtā iti yuktaṃ vaktuṃ syāt | na caitadevam| iti parakṛtamapi duḥkhaṃ na saṃbhavati || 3 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, suffering made by another is also impossible. For if there were otherness, then given the otherness, it would be appropriate to say: 'By these other aggregates, those other ones are made.' But this is not so. Hence suffering made by another is also impossible. // 3 //

body.text: atha syāt- na brūmo yasmādduḥkhenaiva duḥkhaṃ kṛtam, ataḥ svayaṃ kṛtamiti | kiṃ tarhi svapudgalena yasmātsvayameva kṛtam, nāpareṇa kṛtvā dattam, ityataḥ svayaṃ kṛtaṃ duḥkhamiti brūmaḥ | ucyate-
body.translated_text: Now one might say: 'We do not say that suffering is self-made because suffering itself creates suffering. Rather, it is made by one's own <s>pudgala</s> (person) — since it was made by oneself, not given having been made by another — hence we say suffering is self-made.' The reply is:

children.translated_text: If suffering is made by one's own <s>pudgala</s>, then apart from suffering, /

children.text: svapudgalaḥ sa katamo yena duḥkhaṃ svayaṃ kṛtam || 4 ||
children.translated_text: what <s>pudgala</s> is that by whom suffering is self-made? // 4 //

body.text: yadetanmanuṣyaduḥkhaṃ pañcopādānaskandhalakṣaṇaṃ svayaṃ pudgalena kṛtamiti parikalpyate, kalpyatāmasau pudgalo yena tadduḥkhaṃ svayaṃ kṛtam | yadi tāvadyena duḥkhena svapudgalaḥ prajñapyate, tadeva duḥkhaṃ tena kṛtamiti, sa bhedena kathyatāmidaṃ tadduḥkhamayamasya karteti | athāpi manuṣyaduḥkhopādānena pudgalena tadeva duḥkhaṃ kṛtaṃ syāt, na tarhi svapudgalakṛtaṃ tat, parapudgalakṛtameva syāt | athopādānabhede 'pi pudgalābheda iṣyate, etacca nāsti, upādānavyatiriktasya bhinnasya pudgalasya darśayitumaśakyatvāt | evaṃ tāvat svapudgalakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ na bhavati || 4 ||
body.translated_text: What is imagined is this: the human suffering characterized by the five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> is made by the <s>pudgala</s> himself. Let that <s>pudgala</s> be specified, by whom that suffering is self-made. If the very suffering by which the own-<s>pudgala</s> is designated is that which is made by him, let it be stated distinctly: 'This is that suffering; this is its maker.' Or if by the human-suffering-<s>upādāna</s>-<s>pudgala</s> that very suffering were made, then it would not be made by one's own <s>pudgala</s>; it would be made by another <s>pudgala</s>. Or if identity of the <s>pudgala</s> is desired even when the <s>upādāna</s> differs — this is not so, since a <s>pudgala</s> that is different and distinct from the <s>upādāna</s> cannot be shown. Thus, suffering made by one's own <s>pudgala</s> does not exist. // 4 //

body.text: atrāha- ka evamāha svapudgalakṛtaṃ duḥkhamiti? kiṃ tarhi parapudgalajaṃ duḥkham | anya eva devaduḥkhānmanuṣyapudgalaḥ, manuṣyapudgalaśca devaduḥkhaṃ kṛtvā yasmāddevapudgalāya dadāti, tena ca devaduḥkhena devapudgalaḥ prajñapyate, tasmāttasya pudgalasya tadduḥkhaṃ parapudgalajameva bhavati | ucyate-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: 'Who says suffering is made by one's own <s>pudgala</s>? Rather, suffering is produced by another <s>pudgala</s>. The human <s>pudgala</s> is entirely other than divine suffering, and the human <s>pudgala</s>, having created the divine suffering, gives it to the divine <s>pudgala</s>; and by that divine suffering, the divine <s>pudgala</s> is designated — therefore, that suffering of that <s>pudgala</s> is produced by another <s>pudgala</s>.' The reply is:

children.translated_text: If suffering is produced by another <s>pudgala</s>, to whom is it given? /

children.text: pareṇa kṛtvā tadduḥkhaṃ sa duḥkhena vinā kutaḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: Having made that suffering, if it is given by another — without that suffering, whence is he? // 5 //

body.text: yadi devaduḥkhaṃ manuṣyapudgalakṛtam, tena ca manuṣyapudgalena tadduḥkhaṃ kṛtvā parasmai devapudgalāya pradīyata iti sa devapudgalo devaduḥkhavinirmuktaḥ kuto yasmai pradīyeteti | evaṃ tāvadaparapudgalajasya duḥkhasya pratigrāhaka eva nāsti || 5 ||
body.translated_text: If divine suffering is made by the human <s>pudgala</s>, and that suffering, having been made by the human <s>pudgala</s>, is given to another — the divine <s>pudgala</s> — then where is that divine <s>pudgala</s>, freed from divine suffering, to whom it would be given? Thus, there is simply no recipient of suffering produced by another <s>pudgala</s>. // 5 //

body.text: idānīṃ yaśca dadāti, asāvapi nāstītyāha-
body.translated_text: Now, he who gives — he too does not exist, hence he says:

children.translated_text: If suffering is produced by another <s>pudgala</s> — who is that other <s>pudgala</s>? /

children.text: vinā duḥkhena yaḥ kṛtvā parasmai prahiṇoti tat || 6 ||
children.translated_text: Who, being without suffering, having made it, sends it to another? // 6 //

body.text: yenopādānena sa manuṣyapudgalaḥ prajñapyate, sa manuṣyopādānavyatiriktaḥ katamo yo devapudgalāya devaduḥkhaṃ kṛtvā praheṣyati? tasmātparapudgalajamapi duḥkhaṃ na saṃbhavati || 6 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>upādāna</s> by which the human <s>pudgala</s> is designated — apart from that human <s>upādāna</s>, what is he who would create divine suffering and send it to the divine <s>pudgala</s>? Therefore, suffering produced by another <s>pudgala</s> is also impossible. // 6 //

body.text: tataśca-
body.translated_text: And therefore —

children.translated_text: Since self-made [suffering] is not established, how can suffering be made by another? /

children.text: paro hi duḥkhaṃ yatkuryāttattasya syātsvayaṃ kṛtam || 7 ||
children.translated_text: For the suffering that another would make — that would be self-made for him. // 7 //

body.text: yadi devapudgaladuḥkhaṃ manuṣyapudgalena kṛtatvātparakṛtaṃ bhavati, nanu, manuṣyapudgalasya svayaṃkṛtameva tadbhavati | etacca nāstītyuktam | tataḥ svayaṃkṛtasyāprasiddheryadā manuṣyapudgalena svayaṃ tadduḥkhaṃ na kṛtam, tadā kutaḥ parapudgalasya devākhyasya tadduḥkhaṃ parakṛtaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | ato 'pi parakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ na saṃbhavati || 7 ||
body.translated_text: If the suffering of the divine <s>pudgala</s> is made by another because the human <s>pudgala</s> made it, surely that would be self-made for the human <s>pudgala</s>. And that is not so — as has been stated. Therefore, since self-made [suffering] is not established — when the human <s>pudgala</s> has not himself made that suffering — how then would that suffering of the other <s>pudgala</s> called divine be made by another? Hence, suffering made by another is also impossible. // 7 //

body.text: idānīṃ prakaraṇāntareṇāpi pakṣadvayāsaṃbhavaṃ pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, demonstrating the impossibility of both positions by yet another line of reasoning, he says:

children.text: na tāvatsvakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ na hi tenaiva tatkṛtam |
children.translated_text: Suffering is not, first, self-made — for it is not made by that very thing. /
If another is not self-made, how can suffering be made by another? // 8 //

body.text: itaśca svaparābhyāṃ duḥkhasya karaṇaṃ na yujyate, yasmānna tāvatsvakṛtaṃ duḥkham | kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmānna tenaiva hi tat kṛtam, svātmani vṛttivirodhāt, ataḥ svakṛtaṃ nāsti | na parakṛtamapi, yasmādyo 'sau paraḥ karotīti parikalpyate, sa eva tāvannātmanā kṛto nātmanā niṣpannaḥ tasyāpi hetvantarāpekṣaṇāt | yaśca svātmanā na niṣpannaḥ, sa kathamavidyamānasvabhāvaḥ san paraṃ kariṣyatīti na yuktametat || 8 ||
body.translated_text: For this further reason, the making of suffering by self and other is not appropriate: first, suffering is not self-made. Why? Because it is not made by that very thing — since action upon oneself is contradictory. Hence, self-made does not exist. Nor is it made by another — for that other who is imagined to make it is itself, first, not self-made, not self-accomplished, since it too requires dependence on another cause. And that which is not accomplished by its own self — how, being without own-nature, will it make another? Hence this is not correct. // 8 //

body.text: idānīmubhayakṛtamapi duḥkhamasadityāha-
body.translated_text: Now, he states that suffering made by both is also non-existent:

body.text: syādubhābhyāṃ kṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ syādekaikakṛtaṃ yadi |
body.translated_text: Suffering would be made by both only if it could be made by each separately. /

body.text: yadi hi ekaikena duḥkhasya karaṇaṃ syāt syāttadānīmubhābhyāṃ kṛtaṃ duḥkham | na caikaikakṛtaṃ tat, uktadoṣāt | na caikaikena prāṇātipāte kṛte dvābhyāṃ kṛta iti vyapadeśo dṛṣṭaḥ ||
body.translated_text: For if the making of suffering by each individually were possible, then suffering made by both would be possible. But it is not made by each individually, because of the faults already stated. Nor is it observed that when two individuals commit a murder, it is designated as done by both.

body.text: idānīṃ nirhetukamapi duḥkhaṃ yathā nāsti, tathā pratipadayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, demonstrating that suffering without a cause is also impossible, he says:

body.text: parākārāsvayaṃkāraṃ duḥkhamahetukaṃ kutaḥ || 9 ||
body.translated_text: Suffering that is neither made by another nor self-made — how could it be causeless? // 9 //

body.text: pareṇa akāro akaraṇaṃ yasyeti parākāram | na svayaṃkāro 'syetyasvayaṃkāram | yadi duḥkhaṃ svayaṃkṛtaṃ nāsti, parakṛtamapi nāsti yathoktena nyāyena, tadidānīṃ kuta eva nirhetukaṃ bhaviṣyati khapuṣpasaugandhyavat? duḥkhābhāvātkutastasyāśrayabhūta ātmā || 9 ||
body.translated_text: 'Non-making by another' (<s>parākāra</s>) means that which has no making by another. 'Non-self-making' (<s>asvayaṃkāra</s>) means that which has no self-making. If suffering is not self-made and not made by another, by the reasoning stated, then how could it be causeless — like the fragrance of a sky-flower? And in the absence of suffering, whence the self that would be its support? // 9 //

body.text: yathā ca caturdhā vicāryamāṇaṃ duḥkhamasat, evaṃ bāhyā api bījāṅkuraghaṭapaṭādayo bhāvā veditavyāḥ, iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And just as suffering, when examined fourfold, is non-existent, so too external entities such as seeds, sprouts, pots, cloths, and so forth should be understood — demonstrating this, he says:

body.text: na kevalaṃ hi duḥkhasya cāturvidhyaṃ na vidyate |
body.translated_text: It is not only of suffering that the fourfold [analysis] is not found. /

body.text: sarveṣāṃ
body.translated_text: Of all

body.text: bāhyānāmapi bhāvānāṃ cāturvidhyaṃ na vidyate || 10 ||
body.translated_text: external entities as well, the fourfold [analysis] is not found. // 10 //

body.text: pūrvavatsarva samaṃ yojyam | yadi khalveṣāṃ duḥkhādīnāṃ cāturvidhyāsaṃbhavaḥ, tatkatamena tarhi idānīṃ prakāreṇa eṣāṃ siddhiriti | ucyate | svabhāvato yadi etāni duḥkhādīni syuḥ, niyatameṣāṃ caturṇāṃ prakārāṇāmanyatamena prakāreṇa siddhiḥ syāt | na tvasti | tasmātsvabhāvato na santi duḥkhādīnītyavasīyate | atha viparyāsamātralabdhātmasattākāyā duḥkhādisaṃvṛteḥ pratītyasamutpādavyavasthā
body.translated_text: Everything should be connected as before. Now if the fourfold [analysis] is impossible for suffering and so forth, then by what mode is their establishment? The reply is: If suffering and so forth existed by own-nature, then their establishment would necessarily be by one of the four modes. But it is not so. Therefore, it is concluded that suffering and so forth do not exist by own-nature. But if the establishment of conventional suffering and so forth — whose entity-status is obtained merely through perversion — is sought through <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination),

body.text: mṛgyate, tadā karmakārakaparīkṣāprakaraṇavihitavidhinā yathoditapakṣacatuṣṭayatiraskāreṇa idaṃpratyayatāmātrārthapratītyasamutpādasiddhayā siddhirabhyupeyā | yathoktam-
body.translated_text:
then, by the method laid down in the chapter on the Examination of Action and Agent, by setting aside the fourfold position as stated, the establishment should be accepted through the establishment of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> as having the meaning of mere conditionality. As stated:
'Self-made, made by another, made by both, or causeless —
such is suffering according to the dialecticians; but you have declared it to be dependently arisen.' //

children.text: tārkikairiṣyate duḥkhaṃ tvayā tūktaṃ pratītyajam || iti ||

body.text: uktaṃ ca bhagavatā āryopālipṛcchāyām-
body.translated_text: And the <s>Bhagavān</s> has stated in the noble <s>Upāliparipṛcchā</s>:

body.text: tathā
body.translated_text: Thus,

children.text: saṃvṛti bhāṣitu dharma jinena saṃskṛta 'saṃskṛta paśyatha eva |
children.translated_text: The <s>Dharma</s> has been spoken by the Conqueror conventionally — behold the conditioned and the unconditioned! /

children.text: nāstiha bhūtatu ātma naro vā ettaku lakṣaṇa sarvajagasya ||
children.translated_text: There is no self here in reality, nor a person — this is the characteristic of the entire world. //

children.text: kṛṣṇaśubhaṃ ca na naśyati karma ātmana kṛtva ca vedayitavyam |
children.translated_text: Black and wholesome <s>karma</s> does not perish; having done it oneself, it must be experienced. /

children.text: no 'pi tu saṃkrama karmaphalasya no ca ahetuka pratyanubhoti ||
children.translated_text: Yet there is no transference of <s>karma</s>'s fruit, nor is anything experienced without a cause. //

children.text: sarvi bhavā alikā vasikāśca riktaka tucchaka phenasamāśca |
children.translated_text: All existences are false, like reeds — empty, hollow, and like foam. /

children.text: māyamarīcisamā sada śūnyā deśituḥ saṃvṛtu te ca viviktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Like illusions and mirages, always empty — taught conventionally, they are [in reality] isolated. //
Just as in mountain-caves, mountains, gorges, and rivers, an echo arises dependently, /

children.text: evimu saṃskṛta sarvi vijāna māyamarīcisamaṃ jagu sarvam ||
children.translated_text: so too know all conditioned things — the entire world is like illusions and mirages. //

body.text: ityādi || 10 ||
body.translated_text: And so forth. // 10 //

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacitāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau duḥkhaparīkṣā nāma dvādaśamaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus concludes the twelfth chapter, titled 'The Examination of Suffering,' in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary composed by the venerable <s>Ācārya Candrakīrti</s>.

body.text:
13
saṃskāraparīkṣā trayodaśamaṃ prakaraṇam |
body.translated_text:
13
The Examination of <s>Saṃskāras</s> (Conditioned Things) — the thirteenth chapter.

body.text: yataścaivaṃ samanantarātikrāntaprakaraṇavidhinā svaparobhayakṛtatvamahetusamutpanatvaṃ ca nirūpyamāṇaṃ bhāvānāmasat, anyaścotpādako vidhirasan, utpannarūpatvena caite bhāvā avidyātimiropahatamatinayanānāṃ bālapṛthagjanānāṃ khyānti, tasmānniḥsvabhāvā eva santo bālānāṃ visaṃvādakā māyākarituragādivat tadanabhijñānāṃ na tu vijñānām | ata eva sarvadharmasvābhāvāvyāparokṣadhīnayanaḥ samunmūlitāśeṣāvidyāvāsanaḥ caturviparyāsaviparyastātrāṇasattvaparitrāṇāya aviparītanaiḥ svābhāvyopadeśatatparo buddho jagadvibodhako mahākāruṇikaḥ-
body.translated_text: Since in this way, as set forth in the immediately preceding chapter, the self-made, other-made, both-made, and causeless nature of entities, when examined, is non-existent, and since other modes of arising are also non-existent, and since these entities appear to foolish ordinary beings — whose eye of intelligence is impaired by the cataract of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — as having the form of what has arisen, therefore, being without own-nature, they are deceptive to the foolish, like the horses and elephants of a magician, to those who do not understand them — but not to those who do. For this very reason, the <s>Buddha</s>, the great compassionate one, the awakener of the world — whose eye of understanding is direct and unobstructed in [perceiving] the non-intrinsic-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, who has completely uprooted the residual impressions of all <s>avidyā</s> — devoted to the instruction of the non-perverted true nature for the rescue of beings who are unprotected and perverted by the four perversions —

children.translated_text: 'That is false, of deceptive nature' — so the <s>Bhagavān</s> declared. /

children.text: sarve ca moṣadharmāṇaḥ saṃskārāstena te mṛṣā || 1 ||
children.translated_text: 'And all conditioned things (<s>saṃskāras</s>) are of deceptive nature — therefore they are false.' // 1 //

body.text: sūtre uktam- tanmṛṣā moṣadharma yadidaṃ saṃskṛtam | etaddhi khalu bhikṣavaḥ paramaṃ satyaṃ yadidamamoṣadharma nirvāṇam | sarvasaṃskārāśca mṛṣā moṣadharmāṇaḥ iti | tathā- nāstyatra tathatā avitathatā vā | moṣadharmakamapyetat | pralopadharmakamapyetat iti | tadanena nyāyena yanmoṣadharma tanmṛṣetyevaṃ yasmāduktavāṃstathāgato bhagavān, sarve ca moṣadharmāṇaḥ saṃskārāḥ, tasmānmoṣadharmakatvena te saṃskārā mṛṣā bhavanti citrakarayantradārikāvat, lakṣaṇopetayantramayavāraṇavañcitodayanavatsarājavat | tatra visaṃvādakaṃ moṣadharmakaṃ vitathakhyātyālātacakravat | ato niḥsvabhāvatvena mṛṣā sarvasaṃskārāḥ moṣadharmakatvāt marīcikādijalavat | yattu satyaṃ na tanmoṣadharmakam, tadyathā nirvāṇamekam | tataśca vihitayā upapattyā asmāccāgamāt siddhaṃ sarvabhāvānāṃ naiḥsvābhāvyam | śūnyāḥ sarvadharmā niḥsvabhāvayogena iti ca prajñāpāramitā- ardhaśatikāpāṭhāt || 1 ||

atrāha- yadyevaṃ moṣadharmakatvena sarvasaṃskārāṇāṃ mṛṣātvaṃ pratipāditaṃ bhavatā, nanvevaṃ sati na santi sarve bhāvā iti sarvapadārthāpavādinī mithyādṛṣṭireva syāt | ucyate | satyaṃ moṣadharmakāḥ sarvasaṃskārāḥ, ye 'dyāpi bhavantaṃ muṣṇanti | nanu ca bhoḥ,
tanmṛṣā moṣadharma yadyadi kiṃ tatra muṣyate |

yadā asmābhiḥ tanmṛṣā moṣadharmakam ityuktam, tadā kiṃ tatra muṣyate? kiṃ tatrābhāvo bhavati? kaścidyadi padārtho 'bhaviṣyat, syāttasyāpavādādabhāvadarśanānmithyādṛṣṭiḥ | yadā tu padārthameva kaṃcinna paśyāmaḥ, tadā kiṃ tatra muṣyate? naiva kiṃcidabhāvo bhavatītyayukto 'yamupālambho bhavataḥ |
atrāha- yadi abhāvadarśanamapi na pratipādyate, kiṃ punaranenāgamena pratipādyata iti? ucyate-
etattūktaṃ bhagavatā śūnyatāparidīpakam || 2 ||
yadetaduktaṃ bhagavatā, tanna bhāvānāmabhāvaparidīpakam kiṃ tarhi śūnyatāparidīpakam svabhāvānutpādaparidīpakamityarthaḥ | yathoktamanavataptahradāpasaṃkramaṇasūtre-

children.text: yaḥ pratyayairjāyati sa hyajāto no tasya utpādu sabhāvato 'sti |
yaḥ pratyayādhīnu sa śūnya ukto yaḥ śūnyatāṃ jānati so 'pramattaḥ ||

body.text: atrāha- nāyamāgamo bhāvasvabhāvānutpādaṃ paridīpayati, kiṃ tarhi niḥsvabhāvatvam, svabhāvasyānavasthāyitvam, vināśitvam, iti | kuta etaditi cet,
bhāvānāṃ niḥsvabhāvatvamanyathābhāvadarśanāt |

vicāryamāṇānāmanyathātvaṃ vipariṇāmadarśanāt ityarthaḥ | etaduktaṃ bhavati- yadi bhāvānāṃ svabhāvo na syāt, tadānīṃ naivaiṣāmanyathātvamupalabhyeta | upalabhyate ca pariṇāmaḥ | tasmātsvabhāvānava sthāyitvameva sūtrārtha iti vijñeyam ||
itaścaitadevam | yasmāt-
asvabhāvo bhāvo nāsti bhāvānāṃ śūnyatā yataḥ || 3 ||

yo hyasvabhāvo bhāvaḥ, sa nāsti | bhāvānāṃ ca śūnyatā dharma iṣyate | na ca asati dharmiṇi tadāśrito dharma upapadyate | na hi asati vandhyātanaye tacchayāmatopapadyata iti | tasmādastyeva bhāvānāṃ svabhāva iti || 3 ||
api ca-
kasya syādanyathābhāvaḥ svabhāvaścenna vidyate |
yadi bhāvānāṃ svabhāvo na syāt, yo 'yaṃ vipariṇāmalakṣaṇaḥ anyathābhāvaḥ, sa kasya syāditi? atrocyate | evamapi parikalpyamāne
kasya syādanyathābhāvaḥ svabhāvo yadi vidyate || 4 ||

iha yo dharmo yaṃ padārthaṃ na vyabhicarati, sa tasya svabhāva iti vyapadiśyate, aparapratibaddhatvāt | agnerauṣṇyaṃ hi loke tadavyabhicāritvāt svabhāva ityucyate | tadeva auṣṇyamapsūpalabhyamānaṃ parapratyayasaṃbhūtatvātkṛtrimatvānna svabhāva iti | yadā caivamavyabhicāriṇā svabhāvena bhavitavyam, tadā asya avyabhicāritvādanyathābhāvaḥ syādabhāvaḥ | na hi agniḥ śaityaṃ pratipadyate | evaṃ bhāvānāṃ sati svabhāvābhyupagame 'nyathātvameva na saṃbhavet | upalabhyate caiṣāmanyathātvam | ato nāsti svabhāvaḥ || 4 ||
api ca | ayamanyathābhāvo bhāvānāṃ naiva saṃbhavati, yaddarśanātsasvabhāvatā syāt | yathā ca na saṃbhavati, tathā pratipādayannāha-

children.text: yuvā na jīryate yasmādyasmājjīrṇo na jīryate || 5 ||

body.text: tasyaiva tāvat prāgvat prāgavasthāyāṃ vartamānasya bhāvasyānyathātvaṃ nopapadyate | tathā hi yūno yuvāvasthāyāmeva vartamānasya nāsti anyathātvam | athāpi avasthāntaraprāptasyaiva anyathātvaṃ parikalpyate, tadapi nopapadyate | anyathātvaṃ nāma jarāyāḥ paryāyaḥ | tadyadi yūno neṣyate, anyasyaiva jīrṇasya bhavatīti, tadapi na yujyate | yasmānna hi jīrṇasya punarjarayā saṃbandhaḥ, niṣprayojanatvāt | kiṃ hi jīrṇasya punarjarayā saṃbandhaḥ kuryāt? tadāgamanāntareṇa jīrṇatābhāvājjīrṇo jīryata iti na yujyate | atha yūna evānyathābhāvaḥ, tadayuktam, aprāptajarāvasthasya yuveti vyapadeśāt, avasthādvayasya ca parasparaviruddhatvāt || 5 ||
api ca |
tasya cedanyathābhāvaḥ kṣīrameva bhaveddadhi |
atha syāt- kṣīrāvasthāparityāgena dadhyavasthā bhavati, ataḥ na kṣīrameva dadhi bhavatīti | ucyate | yadi kṣīraṃ dadhi bhavatīti neṣyate parasparavirodhāt-
kṣīrādanyasya kasyātha dadhibhāvo bhaviṣyati || 6 ||

kimudakasya dadhibhāvo bhavatu? tasmādasaṃbaddhameva tadanyasya dadhibhāvo bhaviṣyatīti | tadevamanyathātvāsaṃbhavāt kutastaddarśanāt sasvabhāvatā bhāvānāṃ prasetsyatīti na yuktametat | yathoktamāryaratnākaramahāyānasūtre-

children.text: yo na pi jāyati no cupapadyī no cyavate na pi jīryati dharmaḥ |
taṃ jinu darśayatī narasiṃha tatra nideśayi sattva maharṣī ||
yasya svabhāva na vidyati kaści no 'parabhāvatu kenaci labdhaḥ |
nāntarato na pi bāhirato vā labhyati tatra niveśayi nāthaḥ ||
śānta gatī kathitā sugatena no ca gatī upapadyati kāci |
tatra ca vyoharasī gatimukto muktaku mocayasī bahusattvān ||
sarvi vadesi nirātmaka dharmān sattvatu grāhatu mocasi lokam |
mukta svayaṃ gatito gatimukto tenasi pāragato na ca tīrṇaḥ ||
pāragato 'si bhavārṇavatīrṇaḥ pāragato na ca labhyati kaści |
pāru na vidyati nāpi apāru pāragato 'smi vadesi ca vākyam ||
vāca na vidyati yāṃ ca vadesi yaṃ pi vadesi na vidyati taṃ pi |
yasya vadesi na vidyati so 'pi yo 'pi vijānati so 'pi asanto ||
tatra praṇaṣṭu jagaṃ imu sarvaṃ vitathavikalpaniveśavaśena |
śānta vijānati yo naru dharmāṃ stehi tathāgatu dṛṣṭa svayaṃbhūḥ ||

so bhavatī jinu jitvena kleśān ātma ............ |

yaccoktam- asvabhāvo bhāvo naivāsti, śūnyatā ca bhāvānāmiṣyate, tasmādasti śūnyatāaśrayo bhāvasvabhāva iti, etadapi na yujyate ityāha-

children.text: na kiṃcidastyaśūnyaṃ ca kutaḥ śūnyaṃ bhaviṣyati || 7 ||

body.text: yadi śūnyatā nāma kācit syāt, tadā tadāśrayo bhāvasvabhāvaḥ syāt | na tvevam | iha hi śūnyatā nāmeti sarvadharmāṇāṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇamityabhyupagamāt aśūnyadharmābhāvādaśūnyataiva nāsti | yadā ca aśūnyāḥ padārthā na santi, aśūnyatā ca nāsti, tadā pratipakṣanirapekṣatvācchūnyatāpi
khapuṣpamālāvannāstītyavasīyatām | yadā ca śūnyatā nāsti, tadātadāśrayā api padārthā na santīti sthitamavikalam || 7 ||

atrāha- trīṇi vimokṣamukhāni śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitākhyāni vimuktaye vineyebhyo bhagavatā nirdiṣṭāni sarvatīrthikasamayāsādhāraṇāni saugata eva pravacane samupalabhyante | yeṣāmupadeśārthameva buddhā bhagavanto 'śeṣatīrthyavādamahāmohāndhakārānugatajagati jagadekapradīpā nairātmyopadeśāvicchinnaśikhā utpadyante | sa bhavāṃstathāgatapravacanavyākhyānavyājena idānīṃ tāmeva śūnyatāṃ pratikṣeptumārabdhavān, ityalaṃ bhavatā svargāpavargamārgasamucchedakeneti | ucyate | aho vata bhavānatyunmukha iva atyantaviparyāsānnirvāṇapuragāminaṃ śivamṛjuṃ paramaṃ panthānamavadhūya bhāvābhiniveśavyā, kulitaṃ saṃsārakāntārānugameva mārgaṃ mokṣapuragāmitvena samāśrito nirmumukṣuḥ san saṃsārāṭavīkāntāraḥ sadbhirupālabhya eva san abhimānābhiniveśagrahapavaraśatayā tānevopālabhate | nanu bhoḥ, niravaśeṣakleśavyādhicikitsakairmahāvaidyarājaiḥ-

iha sarveṣāmeva dṛṣṭikṛtānāṃ sarvagrahābhiniveśānāṃ yaniḥsaraṇamapravṛttiḥ sā śūnyatā | na ca dṛṣṭikṛtānāṃ nivṛttimātraṃ bhāvaḥ | ye tu tasyāmapi śūnyatāyāṃ bhāvābhiniveśinaḥ, tān prati avācakā vayamiti kuto 'smadupadeśāt sakalakalpanāvyāvṛttyā mokṣo bhaviṣyati? yaḥ nakiṃcidapi te paṇyaṃ dāsyāmītyuktaḥ, sa cet 'dehi bhostadeva mahyaṃ nakiṃcinnāma paṇyam,'; iti brūyāt, sa kenopāyena śakyaḥ paṇyābhāvaṃ grāhayitum? evaṃ yeṣāṃ śūnyatāyāmapi bhāvābhiniveśaḥ, kenedānīṃ sa teṣāṃ tasyāṃ bhāvābhiniveśo niṣidhyatāmiti? ato mahābhaiṣajye 'pi doṣasaṃjñitvāt paramacikitsakairmahāvaidyaistathāgataiḥ pratyākhyātā eva te | yathoktaṃ bhagavatā āryaratnakūṭasūtre-
body.translated_text: Here, that which is the escape from all view-based clinging and attachment to all grasping — that non-engagement — is emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). And [it is said that] view-based —

body.text: yanna śūnyatayā dharmān śūnyān karoti, api tu dharmā eva śūnyāḥ | yannānimittena dharmānanimittān karoti, api tu dharmā evānimittāḥ | yannāpraṇihitena dharmānapraṇihitān karoti, api tu dharmā evāpraṇihitāḥ | yaivaṃ pratyavekṣā, iyamucyate kāśyapa madhyamā pratipaddharmāṇāṃ bhūtapratyavekṣā | ye hi kāśyapa śūnyatopalambhena śūnyatāṃ pratisaranti, tānahaṃ naṣṭapraṇaṣṭāniti vadāmi ||
body.translated_text: it is not that emptiness makes <s>dharmas</s> empty, but rather <s>dharmas</s> themselves are empty. It is not that signlessness makes <s>dharmas</s> signless —

body.text: iti pravacanāt ||
body.translated_text: Thus from the teaching.

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: And also —

body.text: varaṃ khalu kāśyapa sumerumātrā pudgaladṛṣṭirāśritā, na tveva abhāvābhiniveśikasya śūnyatādṛṣṭiḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvadṛṣṭikṛtānāṃ hi kāśyapa śūnyatā niḥsaraṇam | yasya khalu punaḥ śūnyataiva dṛṣṭiḥ, tamahamacikitsyamiti vadāmi | tadyathā kāśyapa glānaḥ puruṣaḥ syāt | tasmai
body.translated_text: 'Better indeed, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is a view of a person as large as Mount <s>Sumeru</s> than the view of emptiness held by one who clings to non-existence.'

body.text: vaidyo bhaiṣajyaṃ dadyāt | tasya tadbhaiṣajyaṃ sarvadoṣānuccārya svayaṃ koṣṭhagataṃ na niḥsaret | tatkiṃ manyase kāśyapa api tu sa puruṣastato glānyānmukto bhavet? no hīdaṃ bhagavan | gāḍhataraṃ tasya puruṣasya glānyaṃ bhavet, yasya tadbhaiṣajyaṃ sarvadoṣānuccārya koṣṭhagataṃ na niḥsaret | bhagavānāha- evameva kāśyapa sarvadṛṣṭikṛtānāṃ śūnyatā niḥsaraṇam | yasya khalu punaḥ śūnyataiva dṛṣṭiḥ, tamahamacikitsyamiti vadāmi || iti || 8 ||
body.translated_text: 'A physician might give medicine. That medicine, having expelled all the ailments, might itself remain lodged in the stomach and not come out.'

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacitāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau saṃskāraparīkṣā nāma trayodaśamaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the examination of formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>), the thirteenth chapter, in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary, composed by the venerable <s>Ācārya Candrakīrti</s>.

body.text:
14
saṃsargaparīkṣā caturdaśamaṃ prakaraṇam |
body.translated_text:
14
The examination of contact (<s>saṃsarga</s>), the fourteenth chapter.

body.text: atrāha- astyeva bhāvasvabhāvaḥ, tatsaṃsargopadeśāt | iha yannāsti, na tasya saṃsargaḥ, tadyathā vandhyāsutaduhitroḥ | asti ca saṃskārāṇāṃ saṃsargopadeśaḥ | cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpāṇi cotpadyate cakṣurvijñānam, trayāṇāṃ saṃnipātaḥ sparśaḥ, sparśasahajā vedaneti vistaraḥ | tathā saṃjñā ca vedanā ca saṃsṛṣṭāvetau dharmau nāsaṃsṛṣṭāviti saṃskārāṇāṃ saṃsargopadeśaḥ | tadevaṃ saṃsargopadeśādvidyata eva bhāvasvabhāva iti | ucyate | syādetadevam, yadi saṃsarga eva bhavato bhavet, na tvasti, yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Here one says: the intrinsic nature of entities does indeed exist, because of the teaching of their mutual contact. For what does not exist has no contact — just as the barren woman's [son] does not come into contact with anything. And form, seeing, and so forth do come into contact. Hence they do exist. It is replied:

children.text: draṣṭavyaṃ darśanaṃ draṣṭā trīṇyetāni dviśo dviśaḥ |
children.translated_text: The visible (<s>draṣṭavya</s>), seeing (<s>darśana</s>), and the seer (<s>draṣṭā</s>) — these three, in pairs,
and altogether — do not come into contact with each other. // 1 //

body.text: tatra draṣṭavyaṃ rūpam,darśanaṃ cakṣuḥ, draṣṭā vijñānam | eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ dviśo dviśaḥ saṃsargo nāsti | cakṣuṣo rūpasya ca, cakṣuṣo vijñānasya ca, vijñānasya rūpasya ca saṃsargo nāsti | ityevaṃ dviśo dviśaḥ saṃsargo na bhavati | sarvaśo 'pi trayāṇāmapyeṣāṃ yugapacca saṃsargo nāsti || 1 ||
body.translated_text: Here, the 'visible' is form; 'seeing' is the eye; the 'seer' is consciousness. The contact of these three, in pairs, does not exist;

body.text: yathā ca draṣṭavyadarśanadraṣṭaṇāṃ dviśo dviśaḥ sarvaśaśca saṃsargābhāvaḥ,
body.translated_text: and just as the contact of the visible, seeing, and the seer does not exist in pairs or altogether,

body.text: evaṃ rāgaśca raktaśca rañjanīyaṃ ca dṛśyatām |
body.translated_text: so too should passion (<s>rāga</s>), the passionate one (<s>rakta</s>), and the object of passion (<s>rañjanīya</s>) be viewed.

body.text: rāgasya raktasya ca saṃsargo nāsti, rāgasya rañjanīyasya ca, trayāṇāmapi yugapatsaṃsargo nāsti | yathā caiṣām, evam-
body.translated_text: There is no contact between passion and the passionate one, no contact between passion and the object of passion, and no simultaneous contact of all three either.

body.text: traidhena śeṣāḥ kleśāśca śeṣāṇyāyatanāni ca || 2 ||
body.translated_text: The remaining afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) and the remaining sense-spheres (<s>āyatanas</s>), by the threefold [analysis], // 2 //

body.text: anyonyena saṃsargaṃ na vrajanti | trayaḥ prakārāstridhā, tridhābhāvastraidham | tena traidhena śeṣāḥ kleśā dveṣamohādayaḥ, te ete dveṣadviṣṭadveṣaṇīyādinā traidhena śrotraśrotṛśrotavyādinā ca || 2 ||
body.translated_text: do not come into mutual contact. Three modes constitute the threefold; the threefold non-existence constitutes the 'threefold.' By that threefold [analysis], the remaining [afflictions and sense-spheres]

body.text: kasmātpunareteṣāṃ saṃsargo nāstītyāha-
body.translated_text: Why is there no contact among these? He says:

children.translated_text: Contact is of one with another; but that otherness does not exist
in the case of the visible and so forth — therefore they do not come into contact. // 3 //

body.text: yadityayaṃ yasmādarthe | yadi draṣṭavyādīnāṃ parasparamanyatvaṃ syāt, tadā kṣīrodakayoriva anyena anyasya saṃsargaḥ syāt | taccānyatvaṃ yasmādeṣāṃ draṣṭavyaprabhṛtīnāṃ na saṃbhavati, ato naite saṃsarga brajanti || 3 ||
body.translated_text: 'Since' (<s>yat</s>) here has the meaning of 'because.' If there were mutual otherness among the visible and so forth, then, like milk and water, one would come into contact with another.

body.text: api ca |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.translated_text: And it is not only the visible and so forth that do not possess otherness;
the otherness of anything whatsoever with anything whatsoever is not possible. // 4 //

body.text: na ca kevalaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvasthitānāṃ draṣṭavyādīnāmanyatvaṃ na saṃbhavati, ghaṭapaṭādīnāmapi padārthānāṃ sarveṣāṃ naiva saṃbhavatītyavasīyatām || 4 ||
body.translated_text: It is not only the visible and so forth, situated in a cause-effect relationship, for which otherness is not possible — even for entities like pots and cloths,

body.text: yathā caiṣāṃ draṣṭavyaprabhṛtīnāṃ parasparato 'nyatvamasat, tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Just as the otherness of the visible and so forth from one another is non-existent, demonstrating this he says:

children.translated_text: 'Other' is other dependent on another; the other is not other apart from another.
And that which depends on that — it is not possible for that to be other than that. // 5 //

body.text: iha yadetad ghaṭākhyaṃ vastu paṭādanyaditi vyapadiśyate, tadetadanyadanyatpratītya anyadbhavati | anyavastunaḥ ṛte, ṛte 'nyataḥ, vinā anyat, anyadanyanna bhavati | yacca paṭākhyaṃ vastu anyad ghaṭākhyaṃ vastu pratītya anyadbhavati, tasmātpaṭākhyādvastunaḥ tad ghaṭākhyaṃ vastu nānyadbhavatītyavasīyatām | yasmāt, yatpratītya yadbhavati, tasmāttadanyanna bhavati, sāpekṣatvād bījāṅkuravat hrasvadīrghavacceti | tathā ca vakṣyati-
body.translated_text: Here, this entity called 'pot' is designated as other than cloth — and this 'other' is other dependent on another, i.e. it becomes other [only in relation to another].

children.text: pratītya yadyadbhavati na hi tāvattadeva tat |
children.translated_text: Whatever comes to be dependent on whatever — that indeed is not that very thing;
nor is it other than that — therefore it is neither annihilated nor eternal. //

body.text: atrāha- yadi ghaṭādanyaḥ paṭaḥ syāt, taṃ ca pṛthagbhūtaṃ paṭamapekṣya anyo ghaṭaḥ syāt, tadā ko doṣa iti | ucyate-
body.translated_text: To this one says: if a cloth were other than a pot, and a pot were other in dependence on that separately existing cloth, then what is the fault?

children.translated_text: If the other were other than another, it would exist even apart from another;
but the other does not exist apart from another — hence it does not exist. // 6 //

body.text: eko 'tra anyaśabda upadarśane, aparaśca arthāntaraparāmarśī, anyaśca prasiddhoccāraṇam, iti anyaśabdatrayopādānam | yadi hi etad ghaṭākhyaṃ vastu paṭādanyasmādanyat syāt, tad ghaṭākhyaṃ vastu anyasmādapi paṭākhyādṛte anyadbhavet, tadā ca paṭanirapekṣasyaiva ekaikasya ghaṭasya anyatvaṃ bhavet | yaddhi yasmādanyat, tattena vināpi siddhayati | tadyathā | sa eva ghaṭo na svarūpaniṣpattāvanyaṃ paṭamapekṣate | evamanyatvamapi yadi ghaṭasya anyasmātpaṭādṛte bhavet, tadānīṃ paṭanirapekṣasya ghaṭasya paratvaṃ syāt | na tu ekaikasya paṭanirapekṣasya ghaṭasyānyatvaṃ dṛṣṭam| tasmādanyadbhavatīti bruvatā yadapekṣya yadanyat, tatastadanyanna bhavatīti sphuṭamabhyupetaṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Here, one [occurrence of] the word 'other' is for indication; another is for reference to a different entity; and the third is the commonly used pronunciation. Thus the word 'other' [is used in three senses].

body.text: atrāha- yadi khalu anyatvamevaṃ kutaścitkasyacinnāsti, nanu idamapi tadā na saṃbhavati vaktum- yasmādanyatpratītya anyadanyadbhavatīti, tasmādeva tadanyadanyanna bhavatīti | ucyate | yata eva hi parasparāpekṣikī bhāvānāmanyatvasiddhiḥ, ata eva anyadityucyate laukike vyavahāre sthitvā | vastutastu parīkṣyamāṇamanyatvaṃ na saṃbhavatīti brūmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: To this one says: if indeed otherness does not exist in this way for anything from anything, then surely it is also not possible to say 'therefore that is not other than —'

body.text: yadi tarhi evamapyavidyamāne 'pyanyatve lokasaṃvṛtyā paṭādanyo ghaṭa iti vyapadiśyate, atha kasmād bījāṅkurayorapi evamanyatvaṃ na vyapadiśyate? ucyate | naiva hi loko ghaṭapaṭayoriva bījāṅkurayoranyatvaṃ pratipadyate, ghaṭapaṭayoriva janyajanakatvābhāvaprasaṅgāt, yaugapadyabhāvaprasaṅgāt | api ca | yasmādbījamātramu tvā bījakāryaṃ vṛkṣamupadarśayati pumān loke- ayaṃ vṛkṣo mayopta iti, tasmālloke 'pi kāryakāraṇabhūtānāṃ nāstyeva paratvamiti vyavasthāpyate || 6 ||
body.translated_text: If then, even though otherness does not exist in this way, conventionally a pot is designated as other than cloth — then why not also [accept that] —

body.text: atrāha- yadi padārthāntare padārthāntarasāpekṣā parabuddhiḥ syāt, syādeṣa doṣaḥ- tasmāttadanyanna bhavatīti | na tvevaṃ brūmaḥ | kiṃ tarhi iha anyatvaṃ nāma sāmānyaviśeṣo 'sti, tadyatra samavetam sa padārthaḥ padārthāntaranirapekṣayāpi para ityucyate, tasmāduktadoṣānavasaro 'smatpakṣe iti | ucyate syādetadevam, yadi anyatvameva syāt, na tvasti | ihedamanyatvaṃ kalpyamānamanyasmin vā kalpyeta ananyasmin vā? ubhayathā ca nopapadyata iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: To this one says: if the cognition 'other' with reference to one entity depended on another entity, this fault would apply — 'therefore that is not other than —'

body.text: nānyasmin vidyate 'nyatvamananyasminna vidyate |
body.translated_text: Otherness does not exist in the other, nor does it exist in the non-other.

body.text: tatra anyasminnanyatvamastīti kalpyate, kiṃ tadānīmanyatvaparikalpanayā? anyavyapadeśasiddhayarthaṃ hi bhavatā anyatvaṃ parikalpyate | sa ca anyavyapadeśo vināpyanyatvena siddha eva, yasmāllabdhānyavyapadeśa eva padārthe 'nyasmin anyatvaṃ kalpyate, ityevaṃ tāvadanyasminnanyatvaṃ na saṃbhavati idānīmananyasminnapi anyatvaṃ nāsti, yasmādananya ucyate ekaḥ, tatra ca anyatvaviruddhamekatvamastīti yataḥ virodhādananyasminnapi anyatvaṃ na saṃbhavati | yacca idānīṃ nānyasminnananyasmin vidyate tadvayatiriktasya padārthāntarasyāsaṃbhavād etadvayatirikte 'pi padārthe na saṃbhavati, tatraivāsti | yadā caivamanyatvameva nāsti, tadā anyatvasamavāyanibandhanaḥ anyabuddhidhvanipravṛttiheturanyo 'pi padārtho nāstīti siddham ||
body.translated_text: There, otherness is conceived as existing in the other — but then what is the purpose of conceiving otherness? It is for the sake of establishing the designation 'other.'

body.text: atrāha- yadyapi anyatvaṃ nāsti, tathāpi anyastāvadasti | na ca asati anyatve anyo bhavitumarhati, ato 'nyatvaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | ucyate-
body.translated_text: To this one says: even though otherness does not exist, nevertheless 'other' does exist. But in the absence of otherness, one cannot be other. Hence:

body.text: avidyamāne cānyatve nāstyanyadvā tadeva vā || 7 ||
body.translated_text: And in the absence of otherness, there is neither 'another' nor 'that very same thing.' // 7 //

body.text: yadā anyatvameva nāstīti prāk pratipāditam, tadā kutaḥ asati anyatve anyadvā tadeva vā bhaviṣyati? tadeveti ananyatvamityarthaḥ | tasmānnāsti anyadvā tadeva vā || 7 ||
body.translated_text: When it has already been demonstrated that otherness itself does not exist, then whence, in the absence of otherness, will either 'another' or 'that very same thing' come to be?

body.text: atrāha- vidyanta eva darśanādayaḥ, saṃsargasadbhāvāt | iha darśanādīnāṃ yadyapi anyatvaṃ nāstīti pratipāditam, tathāpi trayāṇāṃ saṃnipātaḥ saṃgatiḥ sparśa iti saṃsargo 'sti | tataśca saṃsargasadbhāvād vidyanta eva darśanādaya iti | ucyate | syurevam, yadi teṣāṃ saṃsarga eva syāt | na tvasti | yathā ca nāsti, tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: seeing and so forth do indeed exist, because of the existence of conjunction. Here, although it has been demonstrated that seeing and so forth do not have otherness, nevertheless there is conjunction — the coming together, meeting, and contact of the three. And therefore, because of the existence of conjunction, seeing and so forth do indeed exist. It is replied: It would be so, if there were indeed conjunction among them. But there is not. And to demonstrate how there is not, he says —

body.text: na tena tasya saṃsargo nānyenānyasya yujyate |
body.translated_text: Neither the conjunction of that with that, nor of one different with another different, is tenable. /

body.text: iha yadi darśanādīnāṃ saṃsargaḥ syāt, sa ekatvena vā parikalpyeta anyatvena vā? tatra ekatve nāsti saṃsargaḥ | na hi ekakaṃ kṣīramudakanirapekṣamudakena saṃsṛjyata ityucyate | pṛthaktve 'pi saṃsargo nāsti | na hi udakātpṛthagavasthitaṃ kṣīramudakena saṃsṛjyata iti kathyate | evaṃ darśanādīnāṃ yadi ekatve sati saṃsargaḥ parikalpyate, so 'nupapannaḥ | ekakasyāpi cakṣuṣaḥ saṃsṛṣṭiprasaṅgāt | atha pṛthaktvam, evamapyanupapannaḥ | ekakasyāpi cakṣuṣo rūpādibhyaḥ pṛthagbhūtasya saṃsṛṣṭiprasaṅgāt | asati saṃsarge nāsti darśanādikamiti siddham ||
body.translated_text: Here, if there were conjunction of seeing and so forth, would it be conceived through identity or through otherness? In the case of identity, there is no conjunction. For one does not say that milk alone, without dependence on water, is conjoined with water. Even in the case of separateness, there is no conjunction. For one does not say that milk, existing separately from water, is conjoined with water. Thus, if conjunction of seeing and so forth is conceived in the case of identity, it is untenable — because there would be the absurd consequence that even the eye alone would be conjoined [with itself]. And if otherness [is maintained], even so it is untenable — because there would be the absurd consequence that even the eye alone, being separate from form and the rest, would be conjoined [with them]. When there is no conjunction, it is established that seeing and so forth do not exist.

body.text: atrāha- yadyapi saṃsargo nāsti, tathāpi saṃsṛjyamānaṃ saṃsṛṣṭaṃ saṃsraṣṭā cāsti, tadapratiṣedhāt | na ca saṃsargamantareṇa saṃsṛjyamānaṃ saṃsṛṣṭaṃ saṃsraṣṭā ca saṃbhavati | tasmātsaṃsargo 'pi bhaviṣyatīti | ucyate | etadapi na yuktam | yasmādyadā saṃsarga eva nāstīti pratipāditam, asati ca
body.translated_text: Here one objects: Even if there is no conjunction, nevertheless the thing being conjoined, the conjoined, and the conjoiner exist, since they have not been negated. And without conjunction, the thing being conjoined, the conjoined, and the conjoiner are not possible. Therefore, conjunction too will exist. It is replied: This too is not correct. Because when it has been demonstrated that conjunction itself does not exist, and when

body.text: saṃsarge tadā kutaḥ saṃsṛjyamānādikam? tatra vartamānasaṃsargakriyāsādhanakarmabhūtaṃ saṃsṛjyamānam, saṃsṛṣṭaṃ niṣpannasaṃsargakriyam, saṃsraṣṭā kartā kriyāniṣpattau svātantryeṇāvasthitaḥ | tadatra saṃsargābhāvādeva saṃsṛjyamānādikamapaśyaṃstatpratiṣedhaṃ nigamayannāha-
body.translated_text: conjunction does not exist, then whence the thing being conjoined and so forth? Therein, the thing being conjoined is what serves as the object-of-action of the present activity of conjoining; the conjoined is that whose activity of conjoining is completed; the conjoiner is the agent who is independently engaged in the accomplishment of the activity. Now here, not seeing the thing being conjoined and so forth precisely because of the absence of conjunction, concluding their negation, he says —

body.text: saṃsṛjyamānaṃ saṃsṛṣṭaṃsaṃsraṣṭā ca na vidyate || 8 ||
body.translated_text: The thing being conjoined, the conjoined, and the conjoiner do not exist. // 8 //

body.text: iti | yathoktaṃ bhagavatā [upāliparipṛcchāyām]
body.translated_text: Thus. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said [in the <s>Upāliparipṛcchā</s>] —

children.text: sarvasayogi tu paśyati cakṣustatra na paśyati pratyayahīnam |
children.translated_text: Everything is seen when in conjunction; the eye does not see when devoid of conditions. /
The eye itself does not see form — therefore [arises]
the conceptualization of conjunction and disjunction. //

children.text: ālokasamāśrita paśyati cakṣu rūpa manorama citravicitram |
children.translated_text: Dependent on light, the eye sees form — delightful, variegated, and excellent. /

children.text: yena ca yogasamāśrita cakṣustena na paśyati cakṣu kadāci ||
children.translated_text: But by that very conjunction on which the eye depends, the eye never sees. //

children.text: te parinirvṛta laukika śūrā yehi svabhāvata jñātibhi dharmāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those worldly heroes have attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — those by whom <s>dharmas</s> have been known by their intrinsic nature. /

children.text: kāmaguṇairhi caranti asaṅgāḥ saṅga vivarjiya sattva vinenti ||
children.translated_text: They move unattached to the qualities of sense-desire; having abandoned attachment, they discipline beings. //

children.text: no pi ca sattva na jīviha kaści sattvahitaṃ ca karonti jinendrāḥ |
children.translated_text: There is no being whatsoever and no living entity here, yet the <s>Jinendras</s> (conquerors) act for the benefit of beings. /

children.text: ............. sattvu na asti karonti ca artham ||
children.translated_text: ............. beings do not exist, yet they accomplish their purpose. //
Conjunction is never found here .............. /
............. feeling in the world does not exist for that one. //

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise —

children.text: bhāvitu mārga pavartitu jñāna śūnyaka dharma nirātmaka sarvi |
children.translated_text: Having cultivated the path and set in motion knowledge — all <s>dharmas</s> are empty and without self. /
One by whom entities have been discerned as <s>dharmas</s> — for that one, there will be infinite <s>pratibhāna</s> (eloquence). //

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacitāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau saṃsargaparīkṣā nāma caturdaśamaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, 'The Examination of Conjunction,' in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary composed by <s>Ācārya Candrakīrtipāda</s>.

body.text:
15
svabhāvaparīkṣā pañcadaśamaṃ prakaraṇam |
body.translated_text:
15
The Examination of Intrinsic Nature (<s>Svabhāvaparīkṣā</s>), the Fifteenth Chapter.

body.text: atrāha- vidyata eva bhāvānāṃ svabhāvaḥ, tanniṣpādakahetupratyayopādānāt | iha yannāsti na tasya niṣpādakahetupratyayopādānamasti yathā khapuṣpasya | upādīyante ca bījāvidyādayo hetupratyayā aṅkarasaṃskārādīnāṃ niṣpādakāḥ, ityato vidyata eva bhāvasvabhāva iti | ucyate | yadi bhāvānāṃ saṃskārāṅkurādīnāṃ svabhāvo 'sti, kimidānīṃ vidyamānānāṃ hetupratyayaiḥ prayojanam | yathā vartamānībhūtānāṃ saṃskārāṅkurādīnāṃ bhūyoniṣpattaye avidyābījādīnāmupādānaṃ kriyate evamanyadapi tadutpattaye na kartavyaṃ syāt, tatsvabhāvasya vidyamānatvāditi pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: The intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of entities does indeed exist, because of the employment of causes and conditions that produce it. Here, that which does not exist — for that, there is no employment of productive causes and conditions, just as for a sky-flower. But causes and conditions such as ignorance, seeds, and so forth are employed as producers of formations, sprouts, and so forth. Therefore, the intrinsic nature of entities does indeed exist. It is replied: If the intrinsic nature of entities such as formations, sprouts, and so forth exists, then what now is the purpose of causes and conditions for things that already exist? Just as causes and conditions such as ignorance, seeds, and so forth are employed for the further production of formations, sprouts, and so forth that have already come into being — even so, nothing else would need to be done for their arising, since their intrinsic nature already exists. Demonstrating this, he says —

body.text: na saṃbhavaḥ svabhāvasya yuktaḥ pratyayahetubhiḥ |
body.translated_text: The arising of intrinsic nature from conditions and causes is not tenable. /

body.text: atha syāt- naivotpādātpūrvaṃ kasyacidbhāvasya svabhāvo 'sti yato 'sya vidyamānatvādutpattivaiyarthyaṃ syāt, kiṃ tarhi utpādātpūrvamavidyamānasyaiva svabhāvasya hetupratyayān pratītya paścādutpādo bhavatīti | evamapīḥyamāṇe-
body.translated_text: Now one might say: it is not the case that the intrinsic nature of any entity exists prior to arising, such that the pointlessness of its arising would follow from its already existing; rather, the arising occurs afterwards, when the intrinsic nature that did not exist prior to arising comes into being in dependence on causes and conditions. Even when pressed in this way —

body.text: hetupratyayasaṃbhūtaḥ svabhāvaḥ kṛtako bhavet || 1 ||
body.translated_text: An intrinsic nature that has arisen from causes and conditions would be fabricated. // 1 //

body.text: atha syāt- iṣyata eva hetupratyayasaṃbhūtatvātsvabhāvasya kṛtakatvam, tasmātkṛtakasyaiva svabhāvasyābhyupagamāt kṛtakatvaprasaṅgo nāsmākaṃ bādhaka iti, etadapi na yuktamityāha-
body.translated_text: Now one might say: it is indeed accepted that intrinsic nature is fabricated, because of arising from causes and conditions; therefore, since we accept a fabricated intrinsic nature, the objection of fabricatedness does not damage us. This too is not correct — he says —

body.text: svabhāvaḥ kṛtako nāma bhaviṣyati punaḥ katham |
body.translated_text: How could what is called 'intrinsic nature' be fabricated? /

body.text: kṛtakaśceti svabhāvaśceti parasparaviruddhatvādasaṃgatārthametat | iha hi svo bhāvaḥ svabhāva iti vyutpatteḥ, yaḥ kṛtakaḥ padārthaḥ, sa loke naiva svabhāva iti vyapadiśyate, tadyathā apāmauṣpyaṃ dhātupiśācapratyayaniṣpāditaḥ karkeṭanādīnāṃ padmarāgādibhāvaśca | yastu akṛtakaḥ sa svabhāvaḥ, tadyathā agnerauṣṇyaṃ jātānāṃ padmarāgādīnāṃ padmarāgādisvabhāvaśca | sa hi teṣāṃ padārthāntarasaṃparkājanitatvātsvabhāva ityucyate | tadevamakṛtakaḥ svabhāva iti lokavyavahāre vyavasthite vayamidānīṃ brūmaḥ- yadetadauṣṇyaṃ tadaṣyagneḥ svabhāvo na bhavatīti gṛhyatāṃ kṛtakatvāt, iha maṇīndhanādityasamāgamādaraṇinirdharṣaṇādeśca agnerhetupratyayasāpekṣataiva upalabhyate | na ca agnivyatiriktamauṣṇyaṃ saṃbhavati | tasmādauṣṇyamapi hetupratyayajanitam, tataśca kṛtakam, kṛtakatvāccāpāmauṣṇyavat svabhāvo naiva bhavatīti sphuṭamavasīyate ||
body.translated_text: 'Fabricated' and 'intrinsic nature' — this is an incoherent expression, because the two are mutually contradictory. For here, from the etymological derivation that <s>svabhāva</s> means 'one's own being,' that which is a fabricated thing is never in the world designated as 'intrinsic nature' — for example, the heat of water, and the ruby-like appearance of crystals produced by the conditions of minerals and coloring agents. But what is unfabricated — that is intrinsic nature — for example, the heat of fire, and the ruby-nature of naturally occurring rubies and the like. For that [heat] is called their intrinsic nature because it is not produced through contact with other things. Having thus established that unfabricated [alone] is intrinsic nature according to worldly convention, we now say: let it be understood that this heat is also not the intrinsic nature of fire, because of being fabricated. For the dependence of fire on causes and conditions — such as the conjunction of jewel, fuel, and sun, the friction of fire-sticks, and so forth — is indeed observed. And heat apart from fire is not possible. Therefore, heat too is produced by causes and conditions, and hence is fabricated; and because of being fabricated, it is clearly ascertained that, like the heat of water, it is simply not intrinsic nature.

body.text: nanu ca gopālāṅganājanaprasiddhametad agnerauṣṇyaṃ svabhāva iti | kiṃ khalu asmābhiruktaṃ na prasiddhamiti? etattu vayaṃ brūmaḥ- nāyaṃ svabhāvo bhavitumarhati svabhāvalakṣaṇaviyuktatvāt | avidyāviparyāsānugamāttu loko niḥsvabhāvameva bhāvajātaṃ sasvabhāvatvena pratipannaḥ | yathā hi
body.translated_text: But surely it is well-known even among cowherd women and common folk that the heat of fire is its intrinsic nature! Have we indeed said that it is not well-known? But what we say is this: this cannot be intrinsic nature, because it is devoid of the defining characteristic of intrinsic nature. It is only because of conformity with the ignorance of perversion that the world apprehends the totality of entities, which are devoid of intrinsic nature, as possessing intrinsic nature. For just as

body.text: taimirikāḥ timirapratyayādasantameva keśādisvabhāvaṃ sasvabhāvatvenābhiniviṣṭāḥ, evamavidyātimiropahatamatinayanatayā bālā niḥsvabhāvaṃ bhāvajātaṃ sasvabhāvatvenābhiniviṣṭā yathābhiniveśaṃ lakṣaṇamācakṣate agnerauṣṇyaṃ svalakṣaṇam | tato 'nyatrānupalambhādasādhāraṇatvena svameva lakṣaṇamiti kṛtvā | bālajanaprasiddhayaiva ca bhagavatā tadevaiṣāṃ sāṃvṛtaṃ svarūpamabhidharme vyavasthāpitam | sādhāraṇaṃ tvanityatvādikaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇamiti coktam | yadā tu vigatāvidyātimirāvadātaprajñācakṣuṣāṃ darśanamapekṣyate, tadā vitimiraiḥ taimirikopalabdhakeśādarśanavat bālajanamatiparikalpitānupalabdhasvabhāvairāryaiḥ pura ucyate parahitavyāpāraiḥ, nāyaṃ svabhāvo bhāvānāmiti | yathoktamāryalaṅkāvatārasūtre-
body.translated_text: those afflicted with eye-disease, due to the condition of the eye-disease, are attached to a nature of hair-strands and so forth that does not exist at all, taking it as possessing intrinsic nature — even so, the childish, whose cognitive eyes are impaired by the eye-disease of ignorance, being attached to the totality of entities devoid of intrinsic nature as possessing intrinsic nature, declare a defining characteristic in accordance with their attachment: 'the heat of fire is its own-characteristic' — because it is not apprehended elsewhere, and hence, being uncommon, it is its own characteristic. And by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in accordance with the conventions of the childish, that very conventional nature of theirs has been established in the <s>Abhidharma</s>. And the common [characteristic] such as impermanence and so forth has been declared the general characteristic. But when the vision of the noble ones whose eyes of wisdom are purified, free from the eye-disease of ignorance, is taken into account, then — just as those with clear eyes say regarding the hair-strands perceived by those with eye-disease — so too the noble ones, for whom the intrinsic nature fabricated by the cognition of the childish is not found, have previously said, engaged in benefiting others: 'This is not the intrinsic nature of entities.' As stated in the noble <s>Laṅkāvatārasūtra</s> —

children.translated_text: Just as a mass of hairs is falsely apprehended by people with eye-disease, /
so this conceptual construction of entities is falsely constructed by the childish. //

body.text:
na svabhāvo na vijñaptirna ca vastu na cālayaḥ |
bālairvikalpitā hyete śavabhūtaiḥ kutārkikaiḥ || iti |
body.translated_text:
There is no intrinsic nature, no representation, no substance, and no repository. /
These are fabricated by the childish, who are like corpses, [mere] sophists. //

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise —

body.text: svabhāvānutpattiṃ saṃdhāya mahāmate mayā sarvadharmā anutpannā ityuktāḥ || iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Intending the non-arising of intrinsic nature, <s>Mahāmati</s>, I have declared that all <s>dharmas</s> are unarisen.' Thus in detail.

body.text: atrāha- yadi khalu idamagnyāderauṣṇyādikaṃ hetupratyayasaṃbhūtatvena kṛtakatvānniḥsvabhāvamityucyate, kimidānīṃ tatsvabhāvasya lakṣaṇaṃ kaścāsau svabhāva iti vaktavyam | ucyate-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: If this heat of fire and so forth is said to be devoid of intrinsic nature because of being fabricated, having arisen from causes and conditions, then what is the defining characteristic of that intrinsic nature, and what is that intrinsic nature? It is replied —

body.text: akṛtrimaḥ svabhāvo hi nirapekṣaḥ paratra ca || 2 ||
body.translated_text: For intrinsic nature is unfabricated and independent of anything else. // 2 //

body.text: iha svo bhāvaḥ svabhāva iti yasya padārthasya yadātmīyaṃ rūpaṃ tattasya svabhāva iti vyapadiśyate | kiṃ ca kasyātmīyaṃ yadyasyākṛtrimam, yattu kṛtrimaṃ na tattasyātmīyaṃ tadyathā apāmauṣṇyam | yacca yasyāyattaṃ tadapi tadātmīyaṃ tadyathā sve bhṛtyāḥ, svāni dhanāni | yattu yasya parāyattaṃ na tattasyātmīyaṃ tadyathā tāvatkālikāyācitakamasvatantram | yataścaivaṃ kṛtrimasya parasāpekṣasya ca svabhāvatvaṃ neṣṭam, ata eva auṣṇyamagnerhetupratyayapratibaddhatvātpūrvaṃmabhūtvā paścādutpādena kṛtakatvānna svabhāva iti yujyate | yataścaitadevam, ato yadevāgneḥ kālatraye 'pyavyabhicāri nijaṃ rūpamakṛtrimam, pūrvamabhūtvā paścādyanna bhavati, yacca hetupratyayasāpekṣaṃ na bhavati apāmauṣṇyavat pārāvāravat dīrghahrasvavadvā, tat svabhāva iti vyapadiśyate | kiṃ khalu agneḥ taditthaṃ svarūpamasti? na tadasti, na cāpi nāsti svarūpataḥ | yadyapi evam, tathāpi śrotṛṇāmuttrāsaparivarjanārthaṃ saṃvṛtyā samāropya tadastīti brūmaḥ | yathoktaṃ bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: Here, 'one's own being' is <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature). That form which belongs to a thing itself — that is designated as its intrinsic nature. Moreover, what belongs to what? That which is unfabricated for that thing. But what is fabricated does not belong to that thing — for example, the heat of water. And that which is dependent on something else also does not belong to it — for example, borrowed servants, borrowed wealth. But that which is not dependent on another does belong to it — for example, one's own servants and one's own wealth. And since the intrinsic-nature-hood of what is fabricated and dependent on others is thus not accepted, for this very reason it is correct that the heat of fire is not intrinsic nature, because of being bound to causes and conditions, because of not existing before and arising afterwards — i.e., because of being fabricated. And since this is so, whatever is the genuine form of fire that is invariable across the three times and unfabricated — what does not come into being having not existed before, and what does not depend on causes and conditions, like the heat of water, like the ocean, or like long and short — that is designated as intrinsic nature. But does fire indeed have such a form? It does not have it, nor does it not have it intrinsically. Although this is so, nevertheless, in order to avert the alarm of listeners, we say by conventional superimposition that it exists. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said —

body.text:
anakṣarasya dharmasya śrutiḥ kā deśanā ca kā |
śrūyate deśyate cāpi samāropādanakṣaraḥ || iti |
body.translated_text:
For the <s>Dharma</s> that is without syllables — what hearing and what teaching can there be? /
Yet it is heard and taught through superimposition upon what is without syllables. //

body.text: ihāpi ca vakṣyati-
body.translated_text: And here too it will be said —

children.translated_text: 'Empty' should not be said, nor 'non-empty,' /

children.text: ubhayaṃ nobhayaṃ ceti prajñaptyarthaṃ tu kathyate ||
children.translated_text: nor both, nor neither — it is spoken for the purpose of designation. //

body.text: yadi khalu tadadhyāropādbhavadbhirastītyucyate, kīdṛśaṃ tat? yā sā dharmāṇāṃ dharmatā nāma, saiva tatsvarūpam | atha keyaṃ dharmāṇāṃ dharmatā? dharmāṇāṃ svabhāvaḥ | ko 'yaṃ svabhāvaḥ? prakṛtiḥ | kā ceyaṃ prakṛtiḥ? yeyaṃ śūnyatā | keyaṃ śūnyatā? naiḥsvābhāvyam | kimidaṃ naiḥsvābhāvyam? tathatā | keyaṃ tathatā? tathābhāvo 'vikāritvaṃ sadaiva sthāyitā | sarvathānutpāda eva hyagnyādīnāṃ paranirapekṣatvādakṛtrimatvātsvabhāva ityucyate ||
body.translated_text: If indeed it is said by you through superimposition that it exists — what is it like? That which is the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of <s>dharmas</s> — that itself is their essential form. Now what is this <s>dharmatā</s> of <s>dharmas</s>? The intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s>. What is this intrinsic nature? <s>Prakṛti</s> (original nature). And what is this <s>prakṛti</s>? It is <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). What is this <s>śūnyatā</s>? The absence of intrinsic nature (<s>naiḥsvābhāvya</s>). What is this absence of intrinsic nature? <s>Tathatā</s> (suchness). What is this <s>tathatā</s>? The state of being thus, unalterable, always abiding. For it is the complete non-arising of fire and so forth that, because of independence from others and unfabricatedness, is called intrinsic nature.

body.text:
etaduktaṃ bhavati- avidyātimiraprabhāvopalabdhaṃ bhāvajātaṃ yenātmanā vigatāvidyātimirāṇāmāryāṇāmadarśanayogena viṣayatvamupayāti, tadeva svarūpameṣāṃ svabhāva iti vyavasthāpyate | tasya cedaṃ lakṣaṇam-
akṛtrimaḥ svabhāvo hi nirapekṣaḥ paratra ca |
iti vyavasthāpayāṃbabhūvurācāryā iti vijñeyam | sa caiṣa bhāvānāmanutpādātmakaḥ svabhāva akiṃcittvena abhāvamātratvādasvabhāva eveti kṛtvā nāsti bhāvasvabhāva iti vijñeyam | yathoktaṃ bhagavatā-
body.translated_text:
What has been said amounts to this: the totality of entities perceived through the power of the eye-disease of ignorance — by which nature it serves as the object of the noble ones, free from the eye-disease of ignorance, through the mode of non-perception — that alone is established as their essential form, their intrinsic nature. And its defining characteristic is:
'For intrinsic nature is unfabricated and independent of anything else' —
thus the <s>Ācāryas</s> have established it — this should be understood. And this intrinsic nature of entities, whose nature is non-arising, because it is nothing at all, being mere non-existence, is itself non-intrinsic-nature — therefore it should be understood that the intrinsic nature of entities does not exist. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said —

children.text: bhāvānabhāvāniti yaḥ prajānati sa sarvabhāveṣu na jātu sajjate |
children.translated_text: He who knows entities and non-entities does not become attached to any entities whatsoever. /

children.text: yaḥ sarvabhāveṣu na jātu sajjate sa ānimittaṃ spṛśate samādhim ||
children.translated_text: He who does not become attached to any entities whatsoever touches the signless <s>samādhi</s>. //

body.translated_text: Thus. // 2 //

body.text: atrāha- yadyapi svabhāvo nāsti bhāvānām, tathāpi parabhāvastāvadasti, tadapratiṣedhāt sati ca parabhāve svabhāvo 'pi bhaviṣyati | svabhāvamantareṇa parabhāvāprasiddheriti | ucyate-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: even though <s>svabhāva</s> (own-nature) does not exist for entities, at least <s>parabhāva</s> (other-nature) exists, since it has not been negated. And if <s>parabhāva</s> exists, <s>svabhāva</s> too will exist, because <s>parabhāva</s> cannot be established without <s>svabhāva</s>. The reply is:

children.translated_text: In the absence of <s>svabhāva</s>, how can <s>parabhāva</s> exist? /
For the <s>svabhāva</s> of a <s>parabhāva</s> is called <s>parabhāva</s>. // 3 //

body.text: iha svabhāva eva hi loke kaścitsvabhāvāntarāpekṣayā para iti vyapadiśyate | yadi hi agnerauṣṇyaṃ svabhāvaḥ syāt, dravasvabhāvasalilasāpekṣayā parabhāva iti vyapadiśyeta | yadā tu mumukṣubhirvicāryamāṇasya kasyacitsvabhāva eva nāsti, tadā kutaḥ paratvaṃ syāt? parabhāvācca svabhāvo 'pi nāsti iti siddham || 3 ||
body.translated_text: Here in the world, it is <s>svabhāva</s> (own-nature) itself that, in relation to another <s>svabhāva</s>, is designated as 'other' (<s>para</s>). For if the heat of fire were its <s>svabhāva</s>, it would be designated as <s>parabhāva</s> in relation to water, whose <s>svabhāva</s> is fluidity. But when, for those who examine [things] desiring liberation, nothing whatsoever has <s>svabhāva</s>, how could there be otherness? And since <s>parabhāva</s> does not exist, <s>svabhāva</s> too does not exist — this is established. // 3 //

body.text: atrāha- yadyapi svabhāvaparabhāvau na staḥ, tathāpi bhāvastāvadasti, apratiṣedhāt | sa ca bhāvo bhavan svabhāvo vā bhavet, parabhāvo vā | tasmātsvabhāvaparabhāvāvapi bhaviṣyata iti | ucyate-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: even though <s>svabhāva</s> and <s>parabhāva</s> do not exist, at least <s>bhāva</s> (entity, existence) exists, since it has not been negated. And that <s>bhāva</s>, being existent, would be either <s>svabhāva</s> or <s>parabhāva</s>. Therefore <s>svabhāva</s> and <s>parabhāva</s> too will exist. The reply is:

children.translated_text: Apart from <s>svabhāva</s> and <s>parabhāva</s>, how can <s>bhāva</s> exist? /

children.text: svabhāve parabhāve vā sati bhāvo hi sidhyati || 4 ||
children.translated_text: For <s>bhāva</s> is established only when <s>svabhāva</s> or <s>parabhāva</s> exists. // 4 //

body.text: bhāvo hi parikalpyamānaḥ svabhāvo vā bhavet, parabhāvo vā | tau ca pūrvoktavidhinā na staḥ, iti tayorabhāvādbhāvo 'pi nāstītyavadhāryatām || 4 ||
body.translated_text: A <s>bhāva</s>, when conceived, would be either <s>svabhāva</s> or <s>parabhāva</s>. And these two, by the method stated above, do not exist. Therefore, from their non-existence, let it be ascertained that <s>bhāva</s> too does not exist. // 4 //

body.text: atrāha- yadyapi bhavatā bhāvaḥ pratiṣiddhaḥ, tathāpyabhāvo 'sti, pratiṣedhābhāvāt | tataśca bhāvo 'pi bhaviṣyati pratidvandvisadbhāvāt, abhāvavaditi | ucyate | syādbhāvaḥ, yadi abhāva eva syāt | na tvastītyāha-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: even though you have negated <s>bhāva</s>, <s>abhāva</s> (non-existence) still exists, since it has not been negated. And from that, <s>bhāva</s> too will exist, because its opposite exists — just like <s>abhāva</s>. The reply is: <s>bhāva</s> would exist if <s>abhāva</s> itself existed. But it does not — hence he says:

children.translated_text: If <s>bhāva</s> is not established, <s>abhāva</s> too is certainly not established. /
For people call the becoming-otherwise of a <s>bhāva</s> its <s>abhāva</s>. // 5 //

body.text: iha hi yadi bhāvo nāma kaścidabhaviṣyat, syāttasyānyathābhāvādabhāvaḥ | ghaṭādayo hi vartamānāvasthāyāḥ pracyutāḥ santaḥ anyathābhāvamāpannāḥ abhāvadhvanivācyā bhavanti loke | yadā tvamī ghaṭādayo bhāvarūpatvenaivāsiddhāḥ, tadā kuto 'vidyamānasvabhāvānāmanyathātvamiti | ataḥ abhāvo 'pi nāsti || 5 ||
body.translated_text: Here, if some entity called <s>bhāva</s> existed, there would be <s>abhāva</s> through its becoming-otherwise. For pots and the like, having fallen from their present state, having undergone becoming-otherwise, become expressible by the term <s>abhāva</s> in the world. But when these pots and the like are not established even as having the nature of <s>bhāva</s>, then how can there be becoming-otherwise for things whose own nature is non-existent? Therefore <s>abhāva</s> too does not exist. // 5 //

body.text: tadevaṃ sarvathā svabhāvaparabhāvabhāvābhāveṣu anupapadyamāneṣu avidyātimiropahatamatinayanatayā viparītam-
body.translated_text: Thus, when <s>svabhāva</s>, <s>parabhāva</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and <s>abhāva</s> are in every way untenable, those whose mental vision is impaired by the darkness of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) see things in a distorted manner:

children.text: svabhāvaṃ parabhāvaṃ ca bhāvaṃ cābhāvameva ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Svabhāva</s> and <s>parabhāva</s>, <s>bhāva</s> and <s>abhāva</s> — /

children.text: ye paśyanti na paśyanti te tattvaṃ buddhaśāsane || 6 ||
children.translated_text: those who see these do not see the truth in the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching. // 6 //

body.text: ye hi tathāgatapravacanāviparītavyākhyānābhimānitayā pṛthivyāḥ kāṭhinyaṃ svabhāvaḥ, vedanāyā viṣayānubhavaḥ, vijñānasya viṣayaprativijñaptiḥ svabhāvaḥ, ityevaṃ svabhāvaṃ bhāvānāṃ varṇayanti, anyadvijñānam, anyadrūpam, anyaiva ca vedanā, ityevaṃ parabhāvaṃ varṇayanti, vartamānāvasthaṃ ca vijñānādikaṃ bhāvatvena ye varṇayanti, vijñānādikameva ca atītatāmāpannamabhāva iti, na te paramagambhīrasya pratītyasamutpādasya tattvaṃ varṇayanti | yasmādyathoditopapattiviruddhaṃ svabhāvaparabhāvādīnāmastitvam, na copapattiviruddhaṃ padārthasvabhāvamanuvarṇayanti tathāgatāḥ | svayamaviparītāśeṣapadārthatattvasaṃbodhāt | ata eva buddhānāmeva bhagavatāṃ vacanaṃ pramāṇamityupavarṇayanti vicakṣaṇāḥ, sopapattikatvenāvisaṃvādakatvāt | ata eva ca āptebhyaḥ prahīṇāśeṣadoṣebhya āgatatvāt, āgamayatīti samantāt tattvaṃ gamayatīti vā, āmimukhyādgamanādvā tadāśrayeṇa lokasya nirvāṇagamanāt saṃbuddhavacanasyaiva āgamatvaṃ vyavasthāpyate | tadanyamatānāṃ tu upapattiviyuktatvānna prāmāṇyam, āgamābhāsatvaṃ ca vyavasthāpyate || 6 ||
body.translated_text: Those who, with the conceit of explaining the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching without distortion, describe the <s>svabhāva</s> of entities — saying 'hardness is the <s>svabhāva</s> of earth, the experience of objects is the <s>svabhāva</s> of <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), the cognition of objects is the <s>svabhāva</s> of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness)' — and who describe <s>parabhāva</s> thus: 'consciousness is one thing, form is another, and feeling is yet another' — and who describe consciousness and the rest in their present state as <s>bhāva</s>, and consciousness and the rest that have reached the past as <s>abhāva</s> — they do not describe the truth of the supremely profound <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>. Because the existence of <s>svabhāva</s>, <s>parabhāva</s>, and so forth is contradicted by the reasoning set forth above, and the <s>Tathāgatas</s> do not describe the nature of entities as contradicted by reasoning — because of their own unerring realization of the true nature of all entities without exception. For this very reason, the discerning declare that only the word of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, is authoritative — because it is non-deceptive, being supported by reasoning. And for this very reason, because it comes from trustworthy ones (<s>āpta</s>) who have abandoned all faults without remainder, and because it 'imparts' (<s>āgamayati</s>), i.e., conveys the truth in all respects, or because beginning with the going forth (<s>āmimukhyāt gamanāt</s>), and because the world goes to <s>nirvāṇa</s> by relying on it — only the word of the perfectly awakened ones is established as <s>āgama</s> (authoritative scripture). But the doctrines of others, being devoid of reasoning, are not authoritative and are established as mere semblances of <s>āgama</s>. // 6 //

body.text: yasmācca etāni svabhāvaparabhāvabhāvābhāvadarśanāni yuktividhuratvānna tattvāni, ata eva mumukṣūṇāṃ vineyajanānām-
body.translated_text: And since these views of <s>svabhāva</s>, <s>parabhāva</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and <s>abhāva</s> are not truths because they are devoid of reasoning, for this very reason, for those who desire liberation among beings to be guided:

children.translated_text: In the <s>Kātyāyanāvavāda</s>, both 'it exists' and 'it does not exist' /
were negated by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who discerns <s>bhāva</s> and <s>abhāva</s>. // 7 //

body.text: uktaṃ hi bhagavatā āryakātyāyanāvavādasūtre-
body.translated_text: For the <s>Bhagavān</s> said in the <s>Āryakātyāyanāvavāda-sūtra</s>:

body.text: yadbhūyasā kātyāyana ayaṃ loko 'stitāṃ vā abhiniviṣṭo nāstitāṃ ca | tena na parimucyate | jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsebhyo na parimucyate | pāñcagatikātsaṃsāracārakāgārabandhanānna parimucyate | mātṛmaraṇasaṃtāpaduḥkhānna parimucyate | pitṛmaraṇasaṃtāpaduḥkhāditi vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'For the most part, <s>Kātyāyana</s>, this world is attached to existence and to non-existence. Because of that, it is not liberated. It is not liberated from birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and agitation. It is not liberated from the prison-house of the round of five-destinied <s>saṃsāra</s>. It is not liberated from the sorrow and suffering of the death of a mother. It is not liberated from the sorrow and suffering of the death of a father' — and so forth in detail.

body.text: idaṃ ca sūtraṃ sarvanikāyeṣu paṭhayate | tadasmādāgamāt yathopavarṇitāyāścopapatternārhati prājñasvabhāvaparabhāvabhāvābhāvadarśanaṃ tathāgatavacanādatyantaviruddhamāsthātum | bhagavatā pratiṣiddhatvāt | kiṃviśiṣṭena bhagavatā? bhāvābhāvavibhāvinā | bhāvābhāvau vibhāvayituṃ śīlamasyeti bhāvābhāvavibhāvī | yathāvasthitabhāvābhāvāviparītasvabhāvaparijñānād bhāvābhāvavibhāvīti bhagavānevocyate | tena bhagavatā bhāvābhāvavibhāvinā yasmādastitvaṃca nāstitvaṃ ca ubhayametat pratiṣiddham, tasmānna yuktaṃ bhāvābhāvadarśanaṃ tattvamityāsthātum ||
body.translated_text: And this <s>sūtra</s> is recited in all the <s>nikāyas</s> (schools). Therefore, from this <s>āgama</s> and from the reasoning described above, a wise person should not adopt the view of <s>svabhāva</s>, <s>parabhāva</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and <s>abhāva</s> — which is utterly contradictory to the word of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — because it has been negated by the <s>Bhagavān</s>. By what kind of <s>Bhagavān</s>? By one who discerns <s>bhāva</s> and <s>abhāva</s> — one whose nature it is to discern <s>bhāva</s> and <s>abhāva</s>. Because of his knowledge of the unerring, true nature of <s>bhāva</s> and <s>abhāva</s> as they actually are, the <s>Bhagavān</s> alone is called 'the discerner of <s>bhāva</s> and <s>abhāva</s>.' Since by that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the discerner of <s>bhāva</s> and <s>abhāva</s>, both existence and non-existence have been negated, therefore it is not correct to adopt the view of <s>bhāva</s> and <s>abhāva</s> as the truth.

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise:

body.text: astīti kāśyapa ayameko 'ntaḥ | nāstīti kāśyapa ayameko 'ntaḥ | yadenayorantayormadhyam, tadarūpyamanidarśanamapratiṣṭhamanābhāsamaniketamavijñaptikam | iyamucyate kāśyapa madhyamāṃ pratipad bhūtapratyavekṣā iti ||
body.translated_text: '"It exists," <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is one extreme. "It does not exist," <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is another extreme. That which is the middle of these two extremes — that is formless, without appearance, without foundation, without manifestation, without abode, without cognizability. This, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is called the Middle Path, the true examination of entities.'

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: astīti nāstīti ubhe 'pi antā śuddhī aśuddhīti ime 'pi antā |
children.translated_text: 'It exists' and 'it does not exist' — both of these are extremes; 'purity' and 'impurity' — these too are extremes. /

children.text: tasmādubhe anta vivarjayitvā madhye 'pi sthānaṃ na karoti paṇḍitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, having abandoned both extremes, the wise one does not take a stand even in the middle. //

body.text:
astīti nāstīti vivāda eṣaḥ śuddhī aśuddhīti ayaṃ vivādaḥ |
vivādaprāptyā na duḥkhaṃ praśāmyati avivādaprāptyā ca duḥkhaṃ nirudhyate || iti |
body.translated_text:
'It exists' and 'it does not exist' — this is a dispute; 'purity' and 'impurity' — this is a dispute. /
Through the attainment of dispute, suffering is not pacified; through the attainment of non-dispute, suffering ceases. //

body.text: atrāha- yadi punarevamagnyādīnāṃ svabhāvata evāstitvaṃ syāt, ko doṣaḥ syāt? uktadoṣaḥ-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: if entities such as fire and the like existed by their very own nature, what fault would there be? The fault that has been stated:

body.text: hetupratyayasaṃbhūtaḥ svabhāvaḥ kṛtako bhavet |
body.translated_text: A <s>svabhāva</s> produced from causes and conditions would be fabricated. /

body.text: ityādinā || 7 ||
body.translated_text: And so forth. // 7 //

body.text: api ca | yadi ayameṣāmagnyādīnāṃ svabhāvaḥ syāt, tasya vidyamānasya sato na syāt punaranyathātvamiti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, if this were the <s>svabhāva</s> of fire and the like, then, since it exists, it could not again become otherwise — demonstrating this, he says:

body.text: yadyastitvaṃ prakṛtyā syānna bhavedasya nāstitā |
body.translated_text: If existence were by nature, its non-existence would not be possible. /

body.text: yadi agnyāderbhāvasya prakṛtyā svabhāvato 'stitvam, tadā asya svabhāvasya prakṛtyā vidyamānasya punaranyathātvaṃ na syāt | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: If the existence of an entity such as fire were by nature, by <s>svabhāva</s>, then the becoming-otherwise of this <s>svabhāva</s>, which exists by nature, would not be possible. Because:

body.text: prakṛteranyathābhāvo na hi jātūpapadyate || 8 ||
body.translated_text: The becoming-otherwise of [one's own] nature is never tenable. // 8 //

body.text: yadi eṣāmagnyādīnāmiyameva prakṛtiḥ syāt, svabhāvaḥ syāt, tadā prakṛteravikāriṇītvānna kadācitpunaranyathābhāva upapadyeta | na hi ākāśasyānāvaraṇatvaṃ kadācidapyanyathātvaṃ pratipadyate | evamagnyādīnāmapi prakṛtyā vidyamānānāṃ punaranyathātvaṃ na syāt | upalabhate ca bhavāneṣāmanyathātvaprabandhoparamalakṣaṇaṃ vināśam | tasmādvipariṇāmadharmitvādapāmauṣṇyavat nāyameṣāṃ svabhāva iti pratīyatām || 8 ||
body.translated_text: If this were the nature, the <s>svabhāva</s>, of fire and the like, then, since nature is unchangeable, a later becoming-otherwise would never be tenable. For the non-obstructive nature of space never undergoes becoming-otherwise. Likewise, if fire and the like existed by nature, their becoming-otherwise would not be possible. But you do observe their destruction, characterized by the cessation of the continuum of their becoming-otherwise. Therefore, because they are subject to transformation, this is not their <s>svabhāva</s> — just as warmth is not [the <s>svabhāva</s>] of water. Let this be understood. // 8 //

body.text: atrāha- yadi prakṛtyā vidyamānasyānyathātvāsaṃbhavādanyathātvasya ca upalabhyamānatvāt prakṛtireṣāṃ bhāvānāṃ nāstītyucyate, nanu ca evamapi-
