body.translated_text: Here one objects: if it is said that the nature of these entities does not exist because becoming-otherwise is impossible for what exists by nature, and because becoming-otherwise is observed — then surely even so:

body.text: prakṛtau kasya cāsatyāmanyathātvaṃ bhaviṣyati |
body.translated_text: In the absence of nature, of what will there be becoming-otherwise? /

body.text: kasya idānīṃ prakṛtyā svarūpeṇāvidyamānasya khapuṣpasyeva anyathātvaṃ bhaviṣyati? tasmādavidyamānaprakṛtikasya anyathātvānupalambhāt, anyathātvasya ca darśanāt, astyeva svabhāva iti | ucyate | yadi tāvakena matena prakṛtyā svabhāvena asaṃvidyamānasya anyathātvābhāvād anyathātvasya ca darśanātprakṛtirityucyate, evamapi-
body.translated_text: Of what, now — of that which, like a sky-flower, does not exist in its own form, by nature — will there be becoming-otherwise? Therefore, since becoming-otherwise is not observed for something whose nature is non-existent, and since becoming-otherwise is observed, <s>svabhāva</s> does indeed exist. The reply is: if, according to your view, becoming-otherwise is impossible for something that does not exist by nature, by <s>svabhāva</s>, and since becoming-otherwise is observed, this is called nature — even so:

body.text: prakṛtau kasya ca satyāmanyathātvaṃ bhaviṣyati || 9 ||
body.translated_text: In the presence of nature, of what will there be becoming-otherwise? // 9 //

body.text: kasyedānīṃ prakṛtyā svabhāvena vidyamānasya vartamānasyaiva anyathātvaṃ bhaviṣyati? tasmāt prakṛtyā vidyamānasya anyathātvaṃ nāstīti sarvathā anyathātvāsaṃbhava eva | tataśca nāsti prakṛtirbhāvānāmioti vijñeyam || 9 ||
body.translated_text: Of what, now — of that which exists by nature, by <s>svabhāva</s>, i.e., that which is present — will there be becoming-otherwise? Therefore, for what exists by nature, there is no becoming-otherwise — thus, in every way, becoming-otherwise is impossible. And from this, let it be understood that the nature of entities does not exist. // 9 //

body.text: yaccāpyuktam- anyathātvasya darśanānnāsti prakṛtiriti, tadapi paraprasiddhayā anyathātvadarśanamadhikṛtyoktam, na tvasmābhiḥ kadācidapi kasyacidanyathātvamabhyupetam | tadevamatyantataḥ prakṛtāvasaṃvidyamānāyāṃ sarvadharmeṣu asaṃvidyamāneṣu asvabhāveṣu tadanyathātve ca asaṃvidyamāne yo hi idānīmastitvaṃ nāstitvaṃ ca bhāvānāṃ parikalpayati, tasya evaṃ parikalpayato niyatameva-
body.translated_text: And as for what was said — 'since becoming-otherwise is observed, nature does not exist' — that too was said with reference to the other party's accepted view of becoming-otherwise; but we ourselves never accept becoming-otherwise of anything at any time. Thus, when nature utterly does not exist in all <s>dharmas</s>, and all <s>dharmas</s> are non-existent and without <s>svabhāva</s>, and their becoming-otherwise too is non-existent — whoever now conceives the existence and non-existence of entities, for such a conceiver, certainly:

body.text: astīti śāśvatagrāho nāstītyucchedadarśanam |
body.translated_text: 'It exists' is the grasping of eternalism; 'it does not exist' is the view of annihilationism. /

body.text: prasajyata iti vākyaśeṣaḥ | taccaitat śāśvatocchedadarśanaṃ svargāpavargamārgāntarāyakaratvād yasmānmahānarthakaram,
body.translated_text: — this is the remainder of the sentence. And since this view of eternalism and annihilationism is greatly harmful, being an obstacle to the paths to heaven and liberation:

body.text: tasmādastitvanāstitve nāśrīyeta vicakṣaṇaḥ || 10 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore a discerning person should not resort to existence or non-existence. // 10 //

body.text: kasmātpunarbhāvābhāvadarśane sati śāśvatocchedadarśanaprasaṅgo bhavatīti? yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Why is it that, when entities and non-entities are viewed, the consequence of eternalism and annihilationism follows? Because:

children.text: asti yaddhi svabhāvena na tannāstīti śāśvatam |
children.translated_text: That which exists by <s>svabhāva</s> — that it does not exist [later] implies eternalism. /
'It does not exist now but existed before' — annihilationism follows. // 11 //

body.text: yat svabhāvena astītyucyate, svabhāvasyānapāyitvānna tat kadācidapi nāstīti, evaṃ bhāvasyāstitvābhyupagame sati śāśvatadarśanamāpadyate | pūrvaṃ ca vartamānāvasthāyāṃ bhāvasvarūpamabhyupetya idānīṃ tadvinaṣṭatvānnāstiti paścādabhyupagacchataḥ ucchedadarśanaṃ prasajyate | yasya tu bhāvasvabhāva eva nopapadyate, na tasya śāśvatocchedadarśanaprasaṅgaḥ, bhāvasvabhāvānupalambhāt ||
body.translated_text: That which is said to exist by <s>svabhāva</s> — since <s>svabhāva</s> does not depart, it never does not exist. Thus, when the existence of <s>bhāva</s> is accepted, the view of eternalism ensues. And having first accepted the entity's own form in its present state, and then later accepting that it does not exist because it has perished — the view of annihilationism follows. But for one for whom the <s>svabhāva</s> of <s>bhāva</s> itself is not tenable, there is no consequence of eternalism or annihilationism — because of the non-apprehension of <s>bhāvasvabhāva</s>.

body.text: nanu ca bhāvānāṃ svabhāvo nāstītyabhyupagacchato mā bhūdbhāvadarśanābhāvācchāśvatadarśanam, ucchedadarśanaṃ tu niyataṃ prasajyate iti | naivamabhāvadarśanaṃ bhavati | yo hi pūrvaṃ bhāvasvabhāvamabhyupetya paścāt tannivṛttimālambate, tasya pūrvopalabdhasvabhāvāpavādāt syādabhāvadarśanam | yastu taimirikopalabdhakeśeṣviva vitaimiriko na kiṃcidupalabhate, sa nāstīti bruvan kiṃcinnāstīti brūyāt pratiṣedhyābhāvāt | viparyastānāṃ tu mithyābhiniveśanivṛttyarthamataimirikā iva vayaṃ brūmaḥ- na santi sarvabhāvāḥ iti | na caivaṃ bruvatāmasmākaṃ parahitavyāpāraparāyaṇānāmucchedadarśanaprasaṅgaḥ | yathoktaṃ sūtre-
body.translated_text: Now, one who accepts that entities have no inherent nature — for him, the view of eternalism may not arise due to the absence of seeing entities [as real], but the view of annihilationism would certainly follow. [Reply:] This is not so — it is not a view of non-existence. For one who first accepts the inherent nature of entities and later apprehends the cessation of that — for him, since he denies the inherent nature previously apprehended, there would be a view of non-existence. But one who, like a person free from cataracts regarding the hairs perceived by one with cataracts, does not apprehend anything at all — when he says 'it does not exist,' what would he be saying does not exist, since there is nothing to be negated? Rather, like those free from cataracts, we say — for the purpose of removing the wrong attachments of the deluded — 'all entities do not exist.' And for us who speak thus, devoted as we are to activity for the benefit of others, there is no consequence of the view of annihilationism. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>:

body.text: yo hi bhagavan pūrvaṃ rāgadveṣamohabhāvābhyupagamaṃ kṛtvā paścānna santi rāgadveṣamohabhāvā iti bravīti, sa bhagavan vai nāstiko bhavati | iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'One who, <s>Bhagavān</s>, having first accepted the existence of the states of passion, hatred, and delusion, later says "the states of passion, hatred, and delusion do not exist" — he, <s>Bhagavān</s>, indeed becomes a nihilist.' Thus the detailed [exposition]. //

body.text: yastu paratantracittacaittavastumātramabhyupetya tasya parikalpitasvabhāvābhāvādastitvadarśanaṃ pariharati, saṃkleśavyavadānanibandhanasya ca paratantravastumātrasadbhāvānnāstitvadarśanaṃ pariharati, tasya parikalpitasyāvidyamānatvāt paratantrasya ca vidyamānatvād astitvanāstitvadarśanadvayasyāpi upanipātāt kuto 'ntadvayaparihāraḥ? hetupratyayajanitasya ca sasvabhāvenāyuktatvapratipādanādayuktamevāsya vyākhyānam | tadevaṃ madhyamakadarśane eva astitvanāstitvadvayadarśanasyāprasaṅgaḥ, na vijñānavādidarśanādiṣviti | vijñeyam | ata evoktamāryaratnāvalyām-
body.translated_text: But one who, having accepted the mere reality of mind and mental factors as other-dependent (<s>paratantra</s>), avoids the view of existence through the non-existence of the imagined nature (<s>parikalpitasvabhāva</s>), and avoids the view of non-existence through the real existence of the mere other-dependent reality that is the basis of affliction and purification — for him, since the imagined is non-existent and the other-dependent is existent, both the views of existence and non-existence impinge [upon him]. How then can there be avoidance of the two extremes? And since it has been demonstrated that what is produced from causes and conditions is not tenable as having inherent nature, his [the <s>Vijñānavādin</s>'s] interpretation is indeed unjustified. Thus, only in the <s>Madhyamaka</s> view is there no consequence of the dual view of existence and non-existence — not in the <s>Vijñānavāda</s> view and others. This should be understood. Hence it is said in the noble <s>Ratnāvalī</s>:

children.translated_text: Ask the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, <s>Jainas</s>, and proponents of <s>pudgala</s> and <s>skandha</s> /
whether the world [they teach] proclaims the transcendence of existence and non-existence. //
Therefore, know that the nectar of the <s>Buddhas</s>' teaching, which transcends existence and non-existence, /
is called 'the dowry of the <s>Dharma</s>' — and it is said to be profound. //

body.text: tathāvidhavineyajanabodhānurodhāttu paramārthadarśanasya upāyabhūtatvāt neyārthatvena bhagavatā mahākaruṇāparatantratayā vijñānādivādo deśitaḥ sāṃmitīyapudgalavādavat, na nītārthaḥ iti vijñeyam | yathoktamāryasamādhirājabhaṭṭārake-
body.translated_text: However, because of the need to guide disciples of that type to awakening, and because the teaching of ultimate reality serves as a means [to that end], the <s>Bhagavān</s>, out of his great compassion and being governed by it, taught the doctrine of consciousness and the like (<s>vijñānādivāda</s>) as having a provisional meaning (<s>neyārtha</s>) — like the <s>Sāṃmitīya</s> doctrine of the <s>pudgala</s> — not as having a definitive meaning (<s>nītārtha</s>). This should be understood. As stated in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>:

children.translated_text: One knows the distinction of the <s>sūtras</s> of definitive meaning, and knows <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) as taught by the <s>Sugata</s>. /

children.text: yasmin punaḥ pudgala sattva pūruṣo neyārthato jānati sarvadharmān ||
children.translated_text: But wherever a person, a being, or a <s>puruṣa</s> [is mentioned], one knows all those <s>dharmas</s> as having a provisional meaning. //

body.text: etacca āryākṣayamatinirdeśādiṣu vistareṇa boddhavyamiti | bhāvābhāvadarśanadvayaprasaṅgo yāvat tāvatsaṃsāra ityavetya mumukṣubhiretaddarśanadvayanirāsena sadbhirmadhyamā pratipad bhāvanīyā yathāvaditi | etaccoktaṃ bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: And this should be understood in detail from the noble <s>Akṣayamatinirdeśa</s> and other [<s>sūtras</s>]. Having understood that the consequence of the dual view of existence and non-existence extends as far as <s>saṃsāra</s>, those who seek liberation should, through the elimination of this dual view, cultivate the Middle Path (<s>madhyamā pratipad</s>) properly, as the noble ones [teach]. And this was said by the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

children.text: bhāva abhāva vibhāvayi jñānaṃ sarvi acintiya sarvi abhūtaṃ |
children.translated_text: The knowledge that discriminates existence and non-existence — all is inconceivable, all is unreal. /

children.text: ye puna cittavaśānuga bālāḥ te dukhitā bhavakoṭiśateṣu ||
children.translated_text: Those fools who follow the power of [their] minds are tormented in hundreds of world-ages (<s>bhavokoṭi</s>). //

body.text:
bhāvānabhāvāniti yaḥ prajānatī sa sarvabhāveṣu na jātu sajjate |
yaḥ sarvabhāveṣu na jātu sajjate sa ānimittaṃ spṛśate samādhim || iti |
body.translated_text:
One who understands [things] as neither existent entities nor non-existent — he is never attached to any entity.
One who is never attached to any entity — he attains the signless <s>samādhi</s>. //

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: smarāmyahaṃ pūrvamatīta adhvani acintiye kalpi narāṇamuttamaḥ |
children.translated_text: I recall in the past, in a bygone age, in inconceivable <s>kalpas</s>, the supreme among men, /
a great <s>ṛṣi</s> who arose for the benefit of the world — his name was '<s>Abhāvasamudgata</s>' (Arisen from Non-existence). //

children.text: sa jātamātro gagane sthihitvā sarvāṇa dharmāṇabhāva deśayi |
children.translated_text: As soon as he was born, standing in the sky, he taught all <s>dharmas</s> as non-existent (<s>abhāva</s>). /

children.text: tadānurūpaṃ kṛta nāmadheyaṃ śabdena sarvaṃ trisahasra vijñayī ||
children.translated_text: A name was given to him accordingly — by that sound the entire trichiliocosm was made aware. //

children.text: devāpi sarve pramumocu śabdaṃ abhāvanāmeti jino bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: Even all the <s>devas</s> uttered the cry: 'The one named <s>Abhāva</s> (Non-existence) will be a <s>Jina</s> (Victor)!' /

children.text: yo jātamātraḥ pada sapta prakraman abhāva dharmāṇa samaṃ prakāśayī ||
children.translated_text: He who, as soon as born, taking seven steps, illuminated the <s>dharmas</s> of non-existence equally. //

children.text: buddho yadā bheṣyati dharmarājaḥ sarvāṇa dharmāṇa prakāśako muniḥ |
children.translated_text: When the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>-king, the <s>Muni</s> who illuminates all <s>dharmas</s>, will come to be, /
there will be the sound of the <s>dharma</s> of non-existence upon the grasses, bushes, trees, herbs, rocks, and mountains. //

body.text:
yāvanti śabdāstahi lokadhātau sarve hyabhāvā na hi kaści bhāvaḥ |
tāvanti kho tasya tathāgatasya ravu niścarī lokavināyakasya || iti |
body.translated_text:
As many sounds as there are in that world-system — all are non-existent, for there is nothing existent;
so many sounds will issue forth from that <s>Tathāgata</s>, the guide of the world. //

body.text: bhavatīti bhāvaḥ sattā | na vidyate sattā svabhāvaḥ sarvabhāvānāmityabhāvāḥ sarvadharmāḥ, śūnyāḥ sarvadharmā niḥsvabhāvayogeneti prajñāpāramitāpāṭhāt bhāvasvabhāvasyānupapatteḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Bhāva</s> (entity) means 'existence' (<s>sattā</s>). There is no existence — no inherent nature — of all entities; therefore all <s>dharmas</s> are non-existent (<s>abhāva</s>). [As stated in the] <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> reading: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are empty by the method of being without inherent nature' — because the inherent nature of entities is impossible.

body.text: abhāva dharmāṇa ravo bhaviṣyati
body.translated_text: 'There will be the sound of the <s>dharma</s> of non-existence' —

body.text: ityādinā sūtrārtho 'vagantavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: and so forth — by this the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> should be understood. //

body.text:
yāvanti śabdāstahi lokadhātau
sarve hyabhāvā na hi kaści bhāvaḥ | ityādi |
body.translated_text:
'As many sounds as there are in that world-system —
all are non-existent, for there is nothing existent.' And so forth. //

body.text: bhūtvā abhāvapratiṣedhavivakṣitatvād bhāvābhāvārtha eva svabhāvābhāvārthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Since what is intended is the negation of non-existence after [an entity] has existed, the meaning of 'non-existence of entities' (<s>bhāvābhāva</s>) is precisely 'non-existence of inherent nature' (<s>svabhāvābhāva</s>). //

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacitāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau svabhāvaparīkṣā nāma pañcadaśamaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, 'Examination of Inherent Nature' (<s>Svabhāvaparīkṣā</s>), in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary composed by the venerable <s>Ācārya Candrakīrti</s>. //

body.text:
16
bandhamokṣaparīkṣā ṣoḍaśamaṃ prakaraṇam |
body.translated_text:
16
'Examination of Bondage and Liberation' (<s>Bandhamokṣaparīkṣā</s>), the sixteenth chapter.

body.text: atrāha- vidyata eva bhāvānāṃ svabhāvaḥ, saṃsārasadbhāvāt | iha saṃsaraṇaṃ saṃsṛtiḥ gatergatyantaragamanaṃ saṃsāra ityucyate | yadi bhāvānāṃ svabhāvo na syāt, kasya gatergatyantaragamanaṃ saṃsāraḥ syāt? na hi avidyamānānāṃ vandhyāsūnusaṃskārāṇāṃ saṃsaraṇaṃ dṛṣṭam | tasmāt saṃsārasadbhāvāt vidyata eva bhāvānāṃ svabhāva iti | ucyate | syādbhāvānāṃ svabhāvaḥ, yadi saṃsāra eva bhavet | na tvasti | iha yadi saṃsāraḥ syāt, sa niyataṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ vā bhavet sattvasya vā? kiṃ cātaḥ? ubhayathā ca doṣa ityāha-
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: The inherent nature of entities does indeed exist, because of the reality of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Here, 'transmigrating' (<s>saṃsaraṇa</s>) is <s>saṃsṛti</s> — the passage from one state of existence to another is called <s>saṃsāra</s>. If entities had no inherent nature, whose passage from one state to another would constitute <s>saṃsāra</s>? For one does not observe the transmigration of non-existent formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) such as the son of a barren woman. Therefore, because of the reality of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the inherent nature of entities does indeed exist. [Reply:] The inherent nature of entities would [exist] if <s>saṃsāra</s> itself were to exist. But it does not. Here, if there were <s>saṃsāra</s>, it would necessarily belong either to formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) or to a being (<s>sattva</s>). And what follows from this? In both cases there is a fault — hence he says:

children.text: saṃskārāḥ saṃsaranti cenna nityāḥ saṃsaranti te |
children.translated_text: If formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) transmigrate — [do they transmigrate as] permanent? Then permanent [things] do not transmigrate. /

children.text: saṃsaranti ca nānityāḥ sattve 'pyeṣa samaḥ kramaḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: Nor do impermanent [things] transmigrate. The same procedure applies to the being (<s>sattva</s>) as well. // 1 //

body.text: tatra yadi saṃskārāḥ saṃsarantīti parikalpyate, kiṃ te nityāḥ saṃsaranti uta anityāḥ? tatra na nityāḥ saṃsaranti niṣkriyatvāt, anityānāṃ ca ghaṭādīnāṃ sakriyatvopalambhāt | atha anityāḥ, ye hi akriyāḥ, te utpādasamanantarameva vinaṣṭāḥ | ye ca vinaṣṭāḥ, kutasteṣāmavidyamānatvādvandhyāsūnusaṃskārāṇāmiva kvacid gamanam? ityevamanityānāmapi nāsti saṃsāraḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, if it is imagined that formations transmigrate — do they transmigrate as permanent or as impermanent? Therein, permanent [things] do not transmigrate, because of their inactivity, and because impermanent things like pots and the like are observed to have activity. But if impermanent — those that are without activity perish immediately upon arising. And those that have perished — whence could they, being non-existent like the formations [that are the sons] of a barren woman, go anywhere? Thus, even for impermanent [things] there is no <s>saṃsāra</s>. //

body.text: athāpi syāt- anityā eva santo hetuphalasaṃbandhaparaṃparayā avicchinnakramāḥ saṃtānena ca pravartamānāḥ saṃskārāḥ saṃsarantīti | etadapi nopapadyate | kutaḥ? yat tāvadutpadyate kāryam, tasya saṃsāro nāsti, kutaścidanāgamanāt kvaciccāgamanāt | yacca kāraṇaṃ naṣṭam, tasyāpi saṃsāro nāsti, kutaścidanāgamanāt kvaciccāgamanāt | saṃskāramātravyatirekeṇa atītānāgatayorasiddhatvāt, naṣṭājātatvena avidyamānatvāt ||
body.translated_text: Now one might say: the formations, being impermanent, transmigrate precisely through the continuity of the unbroken succession of the cause-effect relationship, proceeding as a <s>saṃtāna</s> (continuum). This too is not tenable. Why? First, regarding the effect that arises — there is no <s>saṃsāra</s> for it, because it does not come from anywhere and does not go anywhere. And regarding the cause that has perished — there is no <s>saṃsāra</s> for it either, because it does not come from anywhere and does not go anywhere. Since, apart from the formations themselves, the past and future are not established — because they are non-existent, being perished and not-yet-born. //

body.text: uttarasmin kṣaṇe utpanne pūrvaḥ saṃsaratīti cet, yadi pūrvottarayoḥ kṣaṇayorekatvaṃ syāt, syādetadevam | na tu ekatvamasti kāryakāraṇabhāvāt, cakṣūrūpacakṣurvijñānānāṃ nāsti ca | kiṃ ca ekatve sati pūrvottarakṣaṇavācyataiva na syāt | na hi eko devadattaḥ ekadā pūrvaścottaraśceti vyapadiśyate | evamihāpi ekatvāt pūrvottarakṣaṇavyapadeśa eva na syāt | api ca pūrvakṣaṇo naṣṭa iti na syāduttarakṣaṇavadavyatiriktatvāt | uttarakṣaṇa utpanna iti na syāt, pūrvakṣaṇavadavyatiriktatvāt | atha anyatve sati saṃsaraṇaṃ syāt, evaṃ sati arhatāmapi saṃsaraṇaṃ syāt | anyasya pṛthagjanasya saṃsārotpattisadbhāvāt | nirvṛtaśca pradīpaḥ pradīpāntare jvalatīti syāt | kiṃ cānyat | naṣṭādvā pūrvakṣaṇāduttarasya kṣaṇasyodayaḥ syādanaṣṭānnaśyamānādvā? tatra yadi naṣṭādiṣyate, vahnidagdhādapi bījādaṅkurodayaḥ syāt, tataśca nirhetukaḥ syāt | atha anaṣṭāt, evamapi avikṛte 'pi bīje 'ṅkurodayaḥ syāt, kāryakāraṇayośca yaugapadyaṃ syāt, nirhetukaścotpādaḥ syāt | naśyamānāditi cet | naṣṭānaṣṭavyatirekeṇa naśyamānābhāvāt, naṣṭānaṣṭayośca
body.translated_text: If one says 'when the subsequent moment arises, the prior [moment] transmigrates' — if there were identity between the prior and subsequent moments, this could be so. But there is no identity, because of the cause-effect relationship — just as with eye, form, and visual consciousness [which are distinct]. Moreover, if there were identity, the very designation 'prior moment' and 'subsequent moment' would not be possible. For one <s>Devadatta</s> is not designated at one and the same time as both 'prior' and 'subsequent.' Even so here, because of identity, the designation of prior and subsequent moments would not be possible. Furthermore, the prior moment has perished — [yet] this should not be so, since it would be non-different from the subsequent moment. The subsequent moment has arisen — [yet] this should not be so, since it would be non-different from the prior moment. Now, if there were transmigration on the basis of otherness, then even <s>Arhats</s> would transmigrate, since the <s>saṃsāra</s>-arising of another, an ordinary person, exists. And an extinguished lamp would burn in another lamp. Moreover: does the subsequent moment arise from the prior moment that has perished, or from one that has not perished, or from one that is perishing? Therein, if it is maintained that it arises from one that has perished, then even from a seed burnt by fire a sprout should arise, and consequently it would be without a cause. But if from one that has not perished — even so, a sprout should arise even when the seed is unmodified, and cause and effect would be simultaneous, and the arising would be without a cause. If from one that is perishing — since there is no 'perishing' apart from 'perished' and 'not-yet-perished,' and since

body.text: vihitadoṣatvānnaśyamānādapi nāstyutpattiriti, kutaḥ kāryakāraṇavyavasthā pūrvottarakṣaṇavyavasthā vā bhaviṣyati? yadā ca pūrvottarakṣaṇavyavasthā kāryakāraṇavyavasthā ca nāsti, tadā saṃtāno 'pi nāsti, tadabhāvānnāsti bhavatāṃ saṃsāra iti anityānāmapi saṃskārāṇāṃ nāsti saṃsāra iti ||
body.translated_text: the faults have already been stated for both the perished and not-yet-perished — from the perishing too there is no arising. So how will the establishment of the cause-effect [relationship] or the establishment of prior and subsequent moments be possible? And when there is no establishment of prior and subsequent moments and no establishment of the cause-effect relationship, then there is no continuum (<s>saṃtāna</s>) either. And because of its non-existence, there is no <s>saṃsāra</s> for you. Thus, even for impermanent formations there is no <s>saṃsāra</s>. //

body.text: atraike varṇayanti- satyaṃ saṃskārā na saṃsaranti utpattividhuratvāt, kiṃ tarhi sattvaḥ saṃsaratīti | ucyate | sattve 'pyeṣa samaḥ kramaḥ | sattvaḥ saṃsaratītyucyamāne kimasau nityaḥ saṃsarati, uta anityaḥ, iti vicāryamāṇe ya eva saṃskārāṇāṃ saṃsaraṇānupapattikramaḥ, sa samatvātsattve 'pi samo nipatati | tasmātsattvo 'pi na saṃsarati || 1 ||
body.translated_text: Here some [i.e., the <s>Pudgalavādins</s>] explain: It is true that formations do not transmigrate, because they lack arising; rather, it is the being (<s>sattva</s>) that transmigrates. [Reply:] 'The same procedure applies to the being as well.' When it is said that the being transmigrates — does it transmigrate as permanent or as impermanent? — when this is examined, the very same sequence showing the impossibility of transmigration for formations applies equally to the being as well, because it is the same. Therefore the being too does not transmigrate. // 1 //

body.text: atrāha- naiva hi sattvasaṃskārāṇāṃ saṃsārānupapattikramaḥ samo bhavitumarhati, yasmādiha saṃskārāṇāṃ nityānityabhūtānāṃ saṃsaraṇaṃ nāstītyuktam | na caivamātmā nityānityabhūtaḥ | tasya hi skandhebhyastattvānyatvāvaktavyatāvat nityatvenānityatvenāpyavaktavyatā vyavasthāpyate | tasmādātmaiva saṃsaratīti na coktadoṣaprasaṅga iti | ucyate-
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: The sequence showing the impossibility of <s>saṃsāra</s> for the being and for formations cannot be the same, because here it was said that formations, being permanent or impermanent, do not transmigrate. But the self (<s>ātman</s>) is not [either] permanent or impermanent. For its inexpressibility (<s>avaktavyatā</s>) as either identical with or different from the <s>skandhas</s> is established — just as its inexpressibility as either permanent or impermanent is established. Therefore the self alone transmigrates, and there is no consequence of the stated faults. [Reply:]

children.translated_text: If the <s>pudgala</s> (person) transmigrates — when sought in the five ways among the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>dhātus</s>, /
it does not exist. What then will transmigrate? // 2 //

body.text: yadi pudgalo nāma kaścit syāt, sa saṃsaret | na tvasti | yasmāt skandhāyatanadhātuṣu pañcadhā mṛgyamāṇo nāsti | kathaṃ kṛtvā?
body.translated_text: If there were some entity called the <s>pudgala</s>, it would transmigrate. But it does not exist. Because when sought in the five ways among the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>dhātus</s>, it is not found. How so?

children.translated_text: Fuel, again, is not fire; nor is fire found apart from fuel. /
Fire does not possess fuel; fuel is not in fire; nor is fire in them. //

body.text: agnīndhanābhyāṃ vyākhyāta ātmopādānayoḥ kramaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The procedure regarding the self (<s>ātman</s>) and the appropriated (<s>upādāna</s>) has been explained through fire and fuel. //

body.text: ityevaṃ skandhāyatanadhātusvabhāva ātmā na bhavati | nāpi tebhyo vyatiriktaḥ | na skandhāyatanadhātumān | na skandhāyatanadhātuṣvātmā | nātmani skandhāyatanadhātavaḥ | ityevaṃ pañcadhā mṛgyamāṇa ātmā na saṃbhavati pūrvoditena nyāyena | yaścedānīṃ skandhāyatanadhātuṣvevaṃ vicāryamāṇaḥ pañcadhā na saṃbhavati, sa kathamavidyamānaḥ san saṃsariṣyatīti? evamātmano 'pi nāsti saṃsāraḥ, vandhyāsutasyeva avidyamānatvāt || 2 ||
body.translated_text: Thus the self (<s>ātman</s>) is not of the nature of the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>dhātus</s>. Nor is it something different from them. Nor does it possess the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>dhātus</s>. The self is not in the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>dhātus</s>. Nor are the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>dhātus</s> in the self. Thus, when sought in the five ways, the self is impossible, by the reasoning stated above. And one who, when examined in the five ways among the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>dhātus</s>, is not possible — how could he, being non-existent, transmigrate? Thus, even for the self there is no <s>saṃsāra</s>, because of its non-existence, like the son of a barren woman. // 2 //

body.text: api ca | ayamātmā-
body.translated_text: Moreover, this self —

children.translated_text: Transmigrating from appropriation (<s>upādāna</s>) to appropriation — he would be without [real] existence (<s>vibhava</s>). /
And being without [real] existence and without appropriation — who is he, and what will transmigrate? // 3 //

body.text: bhavatu kāmamātmanaḥ saṃsāraḥ, yadi anupādānasya sato 'sya saṃsāro yuktaḥ syāt | kathaṃ punarasya anupādānatā prasajyata iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Let there be <s>saṃsāra</s> for the self if you wish — if <s>saṃsāra</s> were justified for one who is without appropriation. But how does the consequence of being without appropriation arise for him? — demonstrating this, he says:

body.text: upādānādupādānaṃ saṃsaran vibhavo bhavet iti |
body.translated_text: 'Transmigrating from one set of appropriated [aggregates] to another, there would be destruction' — thus it is said.

body.text: iha hi manuṣyopādānāddevopādānaṃ gacchan parityajya vā manuṣyopādānaṃ devopādānaṃ gacchedaparityajya vā? yadi tāvatparityajya gacchatītyucyate, tadā pūrvopādānasya parityāgāduttarasya cānupādānāttadantarāle vibhavaḥ syāt | vigato bhavo vibhavaḥ | bhavaḥ pañcopādānaskandhāḥ, tadrahitaḥ syāt | yaśca vibhavo 'nupādānaḥ, sa skandharahitatvāt prajñaptyupādānakāraṇarahitatvānnirhetukaḥ syāt | yaśca anupādāno nirañjano 'vyakto nirhetukaḥ, kaḥ saḥ? na kaścit saḥ | nāstyeva sa ityarthaḥ | tasmiṃścāsati tadabhāvādeva upādānamapi nirupādātṛkaṃ nāstīti kiṃ saṃsariṣyati? nāstyeva tat, yatsaṃsariṣyatītyarthaḥ | athavā, kimityetat saṃsaraṇakriyāviśeṣaṇam | tataśca avidyamānatvāt naiva saṃsaraṇakriyāṃ kariṣyati | evaṃ tāvatpūrvopādānaparityāgena saṃsaraṇamayuktam | atha aparityāgena, tathāpi nopapadyate | kiṃ kāraṇam? pūrvasyāparityāgāduttarasya ca grahaṇād yasmādekasyātmano dvayātmakatā syāt | na caitadiṣyata iti | tasmādaparityāgenāpi saṃsaraṇaṃ nāsti ||
body.translated_text: For here, in going from the human appropriated [aggregates] to the divine appropriated [aggregates] — does one go to the divine appropriated [aggregates] having abandoned the human appropriated [aggregates], or without abandoning them? If one first abandons them,

body.text: atha pūrvottarayorbhavayormadhye āntarābhavikaskandhasaṃbhavāt, taiśca sopādānatvāt sopādānaṃ saṃsarato 'pi na vibhavatāprasaṅga iti | tadapi na yuktam, pūrvabhavaparityāgāparityāgābhyāmāntarāmavikaskandhasaṃsāre 'pi tulyaprasaṅgatvāt ||
body.translated_text: But since between the prior and subsequent existences there arise the aggregates of the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>), and since by them one possesses appropriation — even for one who transmigrates with appropriation, there is no destruction.

body.text: yugapattyāgopādānādadoṣa iti cet, ucyate | kimekadeśena pūrvopādānaṃ tyajate ekadeśenāntarābhavopādānaṃ saṃcarati, atha sarvātmanā? tatra yadi avayaveneti parikalpyate, tadā dvayātmakatāprasaṅgādityuktadoṣaḥ | atha sarvātmanā, evamapi sa eva vibhavatāprasaṅga āpadyate | etāvāṃstu viśeṣaḥ yadantarābhavasaṃcāre 'tisāmīpyāt sūkṣmaṃ kālamanupādānaḥ syāt | na ca sarvātmanā ekasya padārthasya abhinnapadārthasya viṣaye yugapat tyāgopādāne dṛṣṭe | na hi ekasya devadattasya sarvātmanā gṛhādgṛhaṃ saṃcarataḥ ekadā tyāgopādānakriye dve saṃbhavataḥ | atha ekena pādena ekasya parityāgādaparasya copādānād yugapattyāgopādāne parikalpyete, nanu evaṃ sati pādadvayavad dvayātmakatā ātmanaḥ syāt | aṃśena pūrvatrāvasthānādaṃśena cottaratrāvasthānādanekāvayavatā prasajyeta | tasmād yaugapadyenāpi tyāgopādāne na saṃbhavataḥ ityaparihāra evāyam | tasmādantarābhavopādāne 'pi sa eva doṣaprasaṅga iti sarvathā ātmano 'pi nāsti saṃsāraḥ ||
body.translated_text: If [one says:] 'There is no fault, since the abandonment and appropriation are simultaneous' — it is replied: does one abandon the prior appropriation with one part and transmigrate to the intermediate-existence appropriation with another part, or with the whole? [In each case, contradictions follow.]

body.text: yadā ca saṃskārāṇāmātmanaśca saṃsāro nāsti, tadā nāstyeva saṃsāra iti sthitam || 3 ||
body.translated_text: And when there is no <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) either of the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) or of the self — then <s>saṃsāra</s> simply does not exist. This is established. // 3 //

body.text: atrāha- vidyata eva saṃsāraḥ, pratidvandvisadbhāvāt | iha yo nāsti, na tasya pratidvandvī vidyate, tadyathā vandhyāsūnoriti | asti ca saṃsārasya pratidvandvi nirvāṇam | tasmādasti saṃsāra iti | ucyate | syātsaṃsāraḥ, yadi tatpratidvandvi nirvāṇaṃ syāt | na tvastītyāha-
body.translated_text: To this one says: <s>saṃsāra</s> does indeed exist, because of the existence of its counterpart. For what does not exist has no counterpart — just as the barren woman's son has no enemy. But <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the counterpart of <s>saṃsāra</s>, exists. Therefore <s>saṃsāra</s> too exists. It is replied:

children.translated_text: <s>Nirvāṇa</s> of the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) is in no way possible.
<s>Nirvāṇa</s> of a being (<s>sattva</s>) is also in no way possible. // 4 //

body.text: yadi nirvāṇaṃ nāma kiṃcit syāt, tat parikalpyamānaṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ nityānāṃ vā parikalpyeta anityānāṃ vā? tatra nityānāmavikāriṇāṃ kiṃ nirvāṇaṃ kuryāt? anityānāmapi asaṃvidyamānānāṃ kiṃ nirvāṇaṃ kuryāditi sarvaṃ pūrveṇa tulyam | na kathaṃciditi na kenāpi prakāreṇetyarthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: If <s>nirvāṇa</s> were something, then when examined, it would be conceived either of permanent <s>saṃskāras</s> or of impermanent ones. In the case of permanent ones, it is not possible, because the cessation of permanent entities is impossible.

body.text: atha sattvasya nirvāṇaṃ parikalpyate, tadapi nityasya vā anityasya vā pūrvavannopapadyate ||
body.translated_text: And if <s>nirvāṇa</s> is conceived for a being, that too, whether [the being is] permanent or impermanent, is not possible, as before.

body.text: atha nityānityatvenāvācyasya parikalpyate, nanvevaṃ sati nirvāṇe 'pyātmāstītyabhyupeta bhavati saṃsāra iva | api ca | sopādānasyaivātmanaḥ avācyatā yujyate | na ca nirvāṇe upādānamastīti kuto 'sya avācyatā? bhavatu vā tattvānyatvāvācyatā ātmanaḥ, api tu kimasau nirvāṇe 'sti uta nāsti? yadi asti, tadā mokṣe 'pi tasya sadbhāvānnityatā syāt | atha nāsti, tadā anitya ātmā syāt | tataśca tattvānyatvāvācyatāvannityānityatvenāpi ātmanaḥ avaktavyateti na syāt | atha nirvāṇe 'pi ātmanaḥ astitvanāstitvenāvācyataiva iṣyate, evamapi kimasau vijñeyaḥ, atha na? yadi vijñeyaḥ, na tarhi nirupādāno 'sāvātmā nirvāṇe vijñeyatvāt saṃsāra iva | atha na vijñāyate, tatrāsau avijñeyasvarūpatvāt khapuṣpavannāstyeveti kuto 'sya avācyatā? tadevaṃ nirvāṇamapi nāsti | tadabhāvānnāsti saṃsāra iti | ata evoktaṃ bhagavatyāmaṣṭasāhasrikāyām-
body.translated_text: And if it is conceived for one who is inexpressible as either permanent or impermanent — but in that case, even in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, it is accepted that there is a self, just as in <s>saṃsāra</s>. Moreover,

body.text: nirvāṇamapyāyuṣman subhūte māyopamaṃ svapnopamam | buddhadharmā āyuṣman subhūte māyopamāḥ svapnopamā ityādi | saceta kulaputra nirvāṇādapyadhikataro 'nyo dharmo 'bhaviṣyat, tamapyahaṃ māyopamaṃ svapnopamamiti vadāmi ||
body.translated_text: '<s>Nirvāṇa</s> too, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is illusion-like, dream-like. The qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, are illusion-like, dream-like.' And so forth. If, son of good family, —

body.text: tathā āryasamādhirājabhaṭṭārake-
body.translated_text: And also in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>:

children.translated_text: 'The ultimate truth is equal to a dream; <s>nirvāṇa</s> is equal to a dream; one crosses over as in a dream.'

children.text: mana evamotarati yena vidu manasaṃvaraḥ kathitu śreṣṭhu ayam ||
children.translated_text: 'The mind thus crosses over — whereby the wise one is said to have the supreme restraint of mind.' //

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: And also —

children.text: nirodhasatyaṃ supinaṃ yathaiva svapnasvabhāvāmatha nirvṛtiṃ ca |
children.translated_text: 'The truth of cessation is just like a dream; and cessation (<s>nirvṛti</s>) has the nature of a dream.'

children.text: yeneha vācottari bodhisattvo ayaṃ khu so vuccati vācasaṃvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who here by speech crosses over — he indeed is called one who has restraint of speech.' //

body.text: atrāha- yadyapi tvayā saṃsāranirvāṇe pratiṣiddhe, tathāpi bandhamokṣau vidyete | na cāvidyamānasya bhāvasvabhāvasya bandhamokṣau saṃbhavataḥ | tasmād bandhamokṣasadbhāvād vidyata eva bhāvānāṃ svabhāva iti | ucyate | syādbhāvānāṃ svabhāvaḥ, yadi bandhamokṣāveva syātām | na tu staḥ ityāha-
body.translated_text: To this one says: even though <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s> have been refuted by you, nevertheless bondage and liberation do exist. And the bondage and liberation of a non-existent entity-nature is not possible.

children.translated_text: The <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), being subject to arising and passing away, are neither bound nor freed.

children.text: saṃskārāḥ pūrvavatsattvo badhyate na na mucyate || 5 ||
children.translated_text: A being, as before, is neither bound nor freed. // 5 //

body.text: iha ya ime rāgādayaḥ kleśāḥ baddhānāmasvatantrīkaraṇe bandhanamiti vyapadiśyate, yaiśca baddhāḥ pṛthagjanāḥ traidhātukaṃ nātikramantīti vyavasthāpyate, tadetadrāgādikaṃ bandhanatvena parikalpyamānamudayavyayadharmiṇāṃ tāvat kṣaṇikānāṃ saṃskārāṇāmutpādānantaradhvaṃsināṃ naṣṭānāmasattvānna saṃbhavati | rāgādibandhanavicchedalakṣaṇo 'pi mokṣaḥ anityānāṃ saṃskārāṇāmavidyamānatvānnaiva saṃbhavati | pūrvavat pūrvoktavidhinetyarthaḥ | yathā ca pūrvoktavidhinā saṃskārāṇāṃ bandhamokṣau na saṃbhavataḥ, evaṃ pūrvavadeva sattvo 'pi na badhyate nāpi mucyate, ityevaṃ bandhamokṣāvapi na staḥ || 5 ||
body.translated_text: Here, these afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) such as passion (<s>rāga</s>) and so forth, which are designated as 'bondage' in the sense of making the bound ones unfree — and by which ordinary persons, being bound, do not transcend the triple world —

body.text: atrāha- yadyapi saṃskārāṇāṃ sattvasya vā bandho nāsti, tathāpi rāgādikamupādānākhyaṃ bandhanabhūtamasti, tatsadbhāvādbandho 'pi bhaviṣyatīti | ucyate | syādupādānam, bandhanaṃ yadi kaṃcitpadārthaṃ badhnīyāt, na tu badhnāti | yathā ca na badhnāti, tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: To this one says: even though there is no bondage of the <s>saṃskāras</s> or of a being, nevertheless the appropriation (<s>upādāna</s>), consisting of passion and so forth, designated as bondage, does exist. Since it exists, bondage exists. It is replied:

children.translated_text: If bondage is appropriation, one with appropriation is not bound.
One without appropriation is not bound — in what state, then, is one bound? // 6 //

body.text: tatra vidyamānopādānaḥ sopādānaḥ, sa tāvadbhāvo na badhyate | yo hi sopādānaḥ, sa baddha eva | tasya punarapi bandhanayogaḥ kiṃ kuryāt? yaścāpi anupādānaḥ bandhanarahitaḥ, asāvapi bandhanarahitatvāt tathāgatavanna badhyate | anupādānaḥ bandhanarahitaḥ badhyata iti parasparaviruddhatvāccāyuktametat | yaścaivaṃ nirūpyamāṇaḥ sopādāno nirupādāno vā na badhyate, sa idānīṃ kimavastho badhyatām? nāstyevāsau kācidaparā asyāvasthā, yasyāṃ badhyetetyabhiprāyaḥ | yadā caivaṃ nirūpyamāṇaṃ bandhanaṃ na kaṃcidapi badhnāti, tadā kaṃcidapyabadhnata upādānasya rāgādeḥ kuto bandhanatvamiti | tasmād bandhanamapi nāsti || 6 ||
body.translated_text: Here, one who has existing appropriation is 'one with appropriation' — he is not bound. For one who has appropriation is already bound. To bind him again with bondage

body.text: api ca |
body.translated_text: Moreover:

body.text:
badhnīyādbandhanaṃ kāmaṃ bandhyātpūrvaṃ bhavedyadi |
na cāsti tat
body.translated_text: Bondage would bind, if only what is to be bound existed prior [to bondage]. But it does not exist.

body.text: iha bandhyavyatirekeṇa bandhanaṃ nigaḍādikaṃ pūrvasiddhaṃ sat bandhyaṃ devadattaṃ badhnātīti dṛṣṭam | evaṃ yadi bandhyebhyaḥ saṃskārebhyaḥ pudgalādvā bandhyātpūrvaṃ rāgādikaṃ bandhanaṃ siddhaṃ syāt, tena pūrvasiddhena bandhanaṃ syāt saṃskārāṇāṃ pudgalasya vā | taccaitanna saṃbhavati nirāśrayasya rāgādikasya asiddhatvāt | pūrvasiddhasya ca bandhanasya paścād bandhyena saha saṃbandhasya niṣprayojanatvāt |
body.translated_text: Here, it is observed that a fetter, such as a chain, existing established prior to and separately from the one to be bound, binds the person <s>Devadatta</s> who is to be bound. In the same way, if before the one to be bound —

body.text: bandhyasya ca bandhanātpṛthaksiddhasya pūvabandhanāpekṣāniṣprayojanatvācca nāsti bandhyādbandhanasya pūrvasiddhiḥ | tasmānnaiva bandhanaṃ kaṃcidapi badhnāti | na ca kaṃcidapyabadhnato bandhanatvaṃ yuktamiti nāsti bandhanam| bandhanābhāvācca bandhyo 'pi nāstīti siddham | yatpunaratra śeṣaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ tat-
body.translated_text: and since bondage established prior to the one to be bound would serve no purpose without reference to a prior object of bondage — the prior establishment of bondage apart from the one to be bound does not exist.

body.text: śeṣamuktaṃ gamyamānagatāgataiḥ || 7 ||
body.translated_text: The remainder is stated by [the analysis of] the being-gone-to, the gone-to, and the not-yet-gone-to. // 7 //

body.text: iti veditavyam | ślokapāṭhaparivartanena-
body.translated_text: This should be understood. By transposing the verse reading:

children.text: baddho na badhyate tāvadabaddho naiva badhyate |
children.translated_text: The bound one is not bound; the unbound one is certainly not bound.
One freed from both bound and unbound — the one being bound is not bound. //

body.text: ityādinā yojyam || 7 ||
body.translated_text: And so forth, this should be applied. // 7 //

body.text: atrāha- yadyapi bhavatā bandhanaṃ pratiṣiddham, tathāpi saṃsāracārakāgārāvabaddhānāmatrāṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ mahākāruṇikaistathāgataiḥ śīlasamādhiprajñātmakarakandhatrayopadeśo yadarthamuktaḥ, sa tāvanmokṣo 'sti | na ca abaddhasya puṃso mokṣaḥ | tasmād bandho 'pyastīti | ucyate | syādbandhayadi mokṣa eva syāt | ihāyaṃ mokṣaḥ parikalpyamānaḥ baddhasya vā parikalpyeta abaddhasya vā? kicātaḥ? ubhayathā ca na yujyata ityāha-
body.translated_text: To this one says: even though bondage has been refuted by you, nevertheless, for beings who are confined in the prison of <s>saṃsāra</s>'s wandering, without protection — liberation by the great compassionate ones

children.text: baddho na mucyate tāvadabaddho naiva mucyate |
children.translated_text: The bound one is not freed; the unbound one is certainly not freed.
If the bound one were being freed, bondage and liberation would be simultaneous. // 8 //

body.text: tatra baddhasya mokṣo na saṃbhavati baddhatvāt | atha baddhasya paścādupāyena mokṣa iti kṛtvā baddha eva mucyate iti syāt, na tarhi baddho mucyata iti vaktavyam, kiṃ tarhi mokṣyata iti | vartamānasāmīpyādeva mucyata iti cet, yadi kadācidapi mokṣaḥ saṃbhavet, tadā samīpe syāt yadā tu kasyāṃcidapyavasthāyāṃ mokṣe iṣyamāṇe baddhasya mokṣāsaṃbhavena mokṣābhāvaḥ pratipipādayiṣita tadā kuto vartamānasamīpatā? evaṃ tāvad baddho na mucyate iti sthitam ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the liberation of one who is bound is not possible, because of being bound. If one were to say: 'The bound one is subsequently liberated through a means' — and so the bound one is indeed liberated — then one should not say 'is liberated' but rather 'will be liberated.' If [it is said] 'is liberated' because of proximity to the present — if liberation were possible at some time, then it would be proximate. But when the impossibility of liberation for the bound one is being demonstrated in any state whatsoever, [thereby showing] the non-existence of liberation, then whence the proximity to the present? Thus it is established: the bound one is not liberated.

body.text: idānīmabaddho 'pi na mucyate | sa hi mukta eva | tasya punarapi mokṣaḥ kiṃ kuryāt | muktānāṃ cārhatāṃ punarapi mokṣāpekṣatvād baddhataiva syāt, tataścārhato 'pi bandhaḥ syāt ||
body.translated_text: Now, the unbound one is also not liberated. For he is already liberated. What would a further liberation do for him? And if even <s>Arhats</s> who are liberated had a further need of liberation, they would be still bound — and hence even the <s>Arhat</s> would be in bondage.

body.text: atha syāt- abaddhasya mokṣāsaṃbhavād baddha eva mucyate iti, evaṃ sati baddhe mucyamāne parikalpyamāne baddhatvānmucyamānatvācca yaugapadyena bandhamokṣaṇe syātām | na ca parasparaviruddhatvādālokāndhakāravadekasmin kāle bandhamokṣaṇe upapadyete | yataścaivaṃ baddhābaddhayormokṣāsaṃbhava, tasmānmokṣo 'pi nāsti, tadabhāvācca bandhanamapi nāstīti siddham ||
body.translated_text: If one were to say: 'Since liberation is impossible for the unbound, it is the bound one who is liberated' — in that case, when the bound one is imagined as being liberated, since he is simultaneously bound and being liberated, bondage and liberation would occur at the same time. But since they are mutually contradictory — like light and darkness — bondage and liberation cannot occur at a single time. And since liberation is impossible for both the bound and the unbound, liberation too does not exist; and in its absence, bondage too does not exist — this is established.

body.text: atrāha- yadi bhavataiva saṃsāranirvāṇe niṣiddhe, bandhamokṣau ca pratiṣiddhau, ya eṣa saṃsāravinirmumukṣūṇāmavidyāsāndrāndhakāravividhakudarśanakaṭhinātidīrghalatāsaṃchāditasatpathaṃ jātyādivividhā paryantavyasanāniṣṭataravipulavipākaphaladānuśayaviṣavṛkṣasaṃkulaṃ viṃśatiśikharasamunnatatarātipṛthusatkāyadṛṣṭimahāśailapariveṣṭitasarvadiṅmukhaṃ
body.translated_text: Here one objects: 'If <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s> have been refuted by you, and bondage and liberation have been refuted — then the great wholesome desire for the <s>Dharma</s>, which provides supreme solace to those who wish to escape <s>saṃsāra</s> and wish to cross beyond the great wilderness-thicket of <s>saṃsāra</s> — [a wilderness] whose good path is covered by the thick and extremely long creepers of various harmful views [grown from] the dense darkness of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), crowded with trees of evil tendency bearing the undesirable and vast fruits of ripening of various disasters at every boundary of birth and so forth, encircled on all sides by the great mountain of the towering and exceedingly broad <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the existing body) with its twenty peaks,

body.text: viṣayasukhāśātipicchilavipulamahātaṭavivaravāhitṛṣṇānadīmahāparikhaṃ saṃsāramahāṭavīkāntāraṃ nistitīrṣūṇāṃ paramāśvāsakaraḥ kuśalo mahādharmacchandaḥ, kadā nu khalvahamanupādāno nirvāsyāmi, kadā nu me nirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyatīti, nanu sa vyarthaka eva saṃjāyate, yaścāpyevamutpāditakuśalāmalavipuladharmacchandānāṃ kalyāṇamitrasaṃsevādānaśīlaśrutacintābhāvanādikramo nirvāṇaprāptaye, nanu tamyāpi vaiyarthyaṃ syāditi ucyate | yo hyevaṃ niḥsvabhāveṣu sarvabhāveṣu pratibimbamarīcikājalālātacakrasvapnamāyendrajālasadṛśeṣu ātmātmīyasvabhāvarahiteṣu viparyāsamātrānugamāt tāmeva satkāyadṛṣṭim ahaṃ mametyahaṃkāramamakārasamudācāraparigraheṇotpādya manyate-
body.translated_text: with the great moat of the river of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) flowing through vast gaps in the extremely slippery great cliffs of attachment to sense-pleasure — [that wholesome desire which says:] "When will I, without clinging, attain <s>nirvāṇa</s>? When will <s>nirvāṇa</s> come to me?" — surely that becomes entirely pointless! And the sequence for attaining <s>nirvāṇa</s> — attending upon virtuous friends, morality, learning, reflection, meditation, and so forth — for those who have generated such wholesome, pure, and vast desire for the <s>Dharma</s>, surely that too would be pointless!' The reply is: He who, with regard to all entities that are without own-nature — resembling reflections, mirages, water-trails, whirling firebrands, dreams, illusions, and magic — devoid of self, mine, and own-nature, merely following perversion, generating that very <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> through the engagement of 'I' and 'mine' — of I-making and mine-making — thinks:

children.translated_text: 'I shall attain <s>nirvāṇa</s>, being free from clinging; /
<s>nirvāṇa</s> will be mine' — those who have this grasping have a great grasping at clinging. // 9 //

body.text: ahamanupādānaḥ sarvopādānarahito nirvāsyāmi, mama caivaṃ pratipannasya nirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyatīti, evaṃ yeṣāṃ mumukṣūṇāṃ grāho bhavati, nanu tadeva ahaṃkāramamakārākhyaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭayupādānameṣāṃ mahāgraho bhavati, na caivaṃvidhamahāgrahābhiniviṣṭānāṃ śāntiḥ saṃbhāvyate | niravaśeṣagrahaprahāṇenaiva mokṣāvāptaye yāvadahaṃmameti grāhābhiniveśaḥ, yāvacca nirvāṇaṃ nāma astīti grāhābhiniveśaḥ, yāvacca upādānatyāgābhiniveśaḥ, tāvanniyatameva anupāyena nirvāṇaṃ prārthayatāṃ sarva evārambhā vyarthā bhavanti | tasmānmumukṣuṇā sarvametat parityājyam | yathoktaṃ bhagavatā āryadhyāyitamuṣṭisūtre-
body.translated_text: 'I, without clinging, free from all clinging, shall attain <s>nirvāṇa</s>; and for me, having thus practiced, <s>nirvāṇa</s> will come about.' Those who desire liberation and have such grasping — that very I-making and mine-making, called <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>-clinging, becomes their great grasping. And for those attached to such great grasping, peace is not conceivable. Since liberation is attained only through the abandonment of all grasping without remainder — as long as there is clinging to the fixation of 'I' and 'mine,' as long as there is clinging to the fixation that 'something called <s>nirvāṇa</s> exists,' and as long as there is clinging to the abandonment of clinging — so long, indeed, all efforts of those who seek <s>nirvāṇa</s> by wrong means are entirely fruitless. Therefore, one who desires liberation must abandon all of this. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> stated in the noble <s>Dhyāyitamuṣṭisūtra</s>:

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat- caturṇāmāryasatyānāṃ yathābhūtārthādarśanāccaturbhirviparyāsairviparyastacittāḥ satvāḥ evamimamabhūtaṃ saṃsāraṃ nātikrāmanti | evamukte mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto bhagavantametadavocat- deśayatu bhagavān kasyopalambhataḥ sattvāḥ saṃsāraṃ nātikrāmanti | bhagavānāha- ātmātmīyopalambhānmañjuśrīḥ sattvāḥ saṃsāraṃ nātikrāmanti | tat kasya hetoḥ? yo hi mañjuśrīrātmānaṃ paraṃ ca samanupaśyati, tasya karmābhisaṃskārā bhavanti | bālo mañjuśrīraśrutavān pṛthagjanaḥ atyantāparinirvṛtān sarvadharmānaprajānānaḥ ātmānaṃ paraṃ ca upalabhate | upalabhya abhiniviśate | abhiniviṣṭaḥ san rajyate duṣyate muhyate | sa rakto duṣṭo mūḍhaḥ san trividhaṃ karma abhisaṃskaroti kāyena vācā manasā | saḥ asatsamāropeṇa vikalpayati- ahaṃ raktaḥ, ahaṃ dviṣṭaḥ, ahaṃ mūḍhaḥ iti | tasya tathāgataśāsane pravrajitasya evaṃ bhavati- ahaṃ śīlavān, ahaṃ brahmacārīti | ahaṃ saṃsāraṃ samatikramiṣyāmi | ahaṃ nirvāṇamanuprāpsyāmi | ahaṃ duḥkhebhyo mokṣyāmi | sa vikalpayati- ime kuśalā dharmāḥ, ime 'kuśalā dharmāḥ, ime dharmāḥ prahātavyāḥ, ime dharmāḥ sākṣātkartavyāḥ, duḥkhaṃ parijñātavyam, samudayaḥ prahātavyaḥ, nirodhaḥ sākṣātkartavyaḥ, mārgo bhāvayitavyaḥ | sa vikalpayati- anityāḥ sarvasaṃskārāḥ, ādīptāḥ sarvasaṃskārāḥ, yannvahaṃ sarvasaṃskārebhyaḥ palāyeyam | tasya evamavekṣamāṇasya utpadyate nirvitsahagato manasikāraḥ animittapurogataḥ | tasyaivaṃ bhavati- eṣā sā duḥkhaparijñā
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the youth <s>Mañjuśrī</s>: 'Because of not seeing the four noble truths as they really are, beings whose minds are perverted by the four perversions do not cross beyond this unreal <s>saṃsāra</s>.' Thus addressed, the youth <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> teach — through the apprehension of what do beings not cross beyond <s>saṃsāra</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Through the apprehension of self and what belongs to self, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, beings do not cross beyond <s>saṃsāra</s>. For what reason? He who sees a self and another, <s>Mañjuśrī</s> — for him, <s>karmic</s> formations come into being. The foolish, unlearned ordinary person, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, not understanding that all <s>dharmas</s> are utterly beyond <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, apprehends a self and another. Having apprehended, he clings. Being attached, he is passionate, hateful, and deluded. Being passionate, hateful, and deluded, he constructs the threefold <s>karma</s> — by body, speech, and mind. He constructs through false superimposition: "I am passionate; I am hateful; I am deluded." For that one, having gone forth in the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching, the thought arises: "I am moral; I am a practitioner of the holy life. I shall cross beyond <s>saṃsāra</s>. I shall attain <s>nirvāṇa</s>. I shall be freed from suffering." He constructs: "These <s>dharmas</s> are wholesome; these are unwholesome. These <s>dharmas</s> are to be abandoned; these <s>dharmas</s> are to be directly realized. Suffering is to be fully known; the origin is to be abandoned; cessation is to be directly realized; the path is to be cultivated." He constructs: "All formations are impermanent; all formations are ablaze — may I flee from all formations!" For that one, examining thus, a mental application accompanied by revulsion arises, preceded by signlessness. The thought arises in him: "This is that full knowledge of suffering —

body.text: yeyameṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ parijñā | tasyaivaṃ bhavati- yannvahaṃ samudayaṃ prajaheyam | sa ebhyo dharmebhya ārtīyate jehrīyate vitarati vijugupsate uttrasyati saṃtrasyati saṃtrāsamāpadyate | tasyaivaṃ bhavati- iyameṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ sākṣātkriyā | idaṃ samudayaprahāṇaṃ yadidamebhyo dharmebhyo 'rtīyanā vijugupsanā | tasyaiva bhavati- nirodhaḥ sākṣātkartavyaḥ | samudayaṃ kalpayitvā nirodhe saṃjānāti | tasyaivaṃ bhavati- eṣā sā nirodhasākṣātkriyā | tasyaivaṃ bhavati- yannūnamahaṃ mārgaṃ bhāvayeyam | sa eko rahogataḥ tān dharmān manasi kurvan śamathaṃ pratilabhate | tasya tena nirvitsahagatena manasikāreṇa śamatha utpadyate | tasya sarvadharmeṣu cittaṃ pratilīyate prativahati pratyudāvartate, tebhyaścārtīyate jehrīyate, anabhinandanācittamutpadyate | tasyaivaṃ bhavati- mukto 'smi sarvaduḥkhebhyaḥ | na mama bhūya uttariṃ kiṃcitkaraṇīyam | arhannasmi | ityātmānaṃ saṃjānāti | samaraṇakālasamaye utpattimātmanaḥ samanupaśyati | tasya kāṅkṣā ca vicikitsā ca bhavati buddhabodhau | sa vicikitsāpatitaḥ kālagato mahānirayeṣu prapatati | tatkasya hetoḥ? yathāpīdamanutpannān sarvadharmān vikalpayitvā tathāgate vicikitsāṃ vimatiṃ cotpādayati ||
body.translated_text: namely, this full knowledge of these <s>dharmas</s>." The thought arises in him: "May I abandon the origin." He feels repulsion, aversion, disgust, and revulsion toward these <s>dharmas</s>; he is frightened, alarmed, and falls into alarm. The thought arises in him: "This is the direct realization of these <s>dharmas</s>. This is the abandonment of the origin — namely, this repulsion and revulsion toward these <s>dharmas</s>." The thought arises in him: "Cessation is to be directly realized." Having constructed the origin, he perceives cessation. The thought arises in him: "This is that direct realization of cessation." The thought arises in him: "May I cultivate the path." He, alone and secluded, attending to those <s>dharmas</s> in his mind, attains calm. Through that mental application accompanied by revulsion, calm arises for him. His mind withdraws, retreats, and turns back from all <s>dharmas</s>; he feels repulsion and aversion toward them. A mind of non-delight arises. The thought arises in him: "I am liberated from all suffering. There is nothing further for me to do. I am an <s>Arhat</s>." He perceives himself thus. At the approach of death, he sees [further] arising for himself. Doubt and uncertainty arise in him regarding the <s>Buddha</s>'s awakening. Fallen into doubt, having died, he falls into the great hells. For what reason? Because, having constructed these <s>dharmas</s>, which are [in reality] unarisen, he generates doubt and uncertainty regarding the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto bhagavantametadavocat- kathaṃ punarbhagavaṃścatvāri āryasatyāni draṣṭavyāni? bhagavānāha- yena mañjuśrīranutpannāḥ sarvasaṃskārā dṛṣṭāḥ, tena duḥkhaṃ parijñātam | yena asamutthitāḥ sarvadharmā dṛṣṭāḥ, tasya samudayaḥ prahīṇaḥ | yena atyantaparinirvṛtāḥ sarvadharmā dṛṣṭāḥ, tena nirodhaḥ sākṣātkṛtaḥ | yena atyantaśūnyāḥ sarvadharmā dṛṣṭāḥ, tena mārgo bhāvitaḥ | yena mañjuśrīrevaṃ catvāri āryasatyāni dṛṣṭāni, sa na kalpayati na vikalpayati- ime kuśalā dharmāḥ, ime 'kuśalā dharmāḥ | ime dharmāḥ prahātavyāḥ, ime dharmāḥ sākṣātkartavyāḥ | duḥkhaṃ parijñātavyam | samudayaḥ prahātavyaḥ, nirodhaḥ sākṣātkartavyaḥ, mārgo bhāvayitavya iti | tatkasya heto? tathāhi sa taṃ dharmaṃ na samanupaśyati yaṃ parikalpayet | bālapṛthagjanāstu etān dharmān kalpayanto rajyanti ca dviṣanti ca muhyanti ca | sa na kaṃciddharmamāvyūhati nirvyūhati | tasya evamanāvyūhato 'nirvyūhataḥ traidhātuke citta na sajjati, ajāta sarvatraidhātukaṃ samanupaśyati || iti vistaraḥ || 9 ||
body.translated_text: Then the youth <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'How then, <s>Bhagavān</s>, should the four noble truths be seen?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'He by whom, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, all formations have been seen as unarisen — by him suffering has been fully known. He by whom all <s>dharmas</s> have been seen as not having arisen — for him the origin has been abandoned. He by whom all <s>dharmas</s> have been seen as utterly beyond <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — by him cessation has been directly realized. He by whom all <s>dharmas</s> have been seen as utterly empty — by him the path has been cultivated. He by whom, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the four noble truths have been seen in this way — he neither constructs nor discriminately constructs: "These <s>dharmas</s> are wholesome; these are unwholesome. These <s>dharmas</s> are to be abandoned; these are to be directly realized. Suffering is to be fully known. The origin is to be abandoned; cessation is to be directly realized; the path is to be cultivated." For what reason? He does not see any <s>dharma</s> that he would construct. But foolish ordinary beings, constructing these <s>dharmas</s>, are passionate, hateful, and deluded. He neither adds to any <s>dharma</s> nor removes from it. For him, who neither adds nor removes, his mind does not become attached in the three realms — he sees the entirety of the three realms as unborn.' Thus in detail. // 9 //

body.text: ata eva asmādāgamāt paramārthasatya ucyate-
body.translated_text: For this very reason, from this scripture, the ultimate truth is stated:

children.translated_text: There is neither the superimposition of <s>nirvāṇa</s> nor the removal of <s>saṃsāra</s>. /

children.text: yatra kastatra saṃsāro nirvāṇaṃ kiṃ vikalpyate || 10 ||
children.translated_text: Where there is no <s>saṃsāra</s>, what <s>nirvāṇa</s> is conceived? // 10 //

body.text: yatra hi nāma paramārthasatye naivaṃ na nirvāṇasamāropaḥ na nirvāṇādhyāropaḥ saṃbhavati, anupalabhyamānatvāt, nāpi saṃsārāpakarṣaṇaṃ saṃsāraparikṣayo na saṃbhavati, kastatra saṃsāraḥ yo vikalpyate kṣayārtham, kiṃ vā tatra nirvāṇaṃ yatprāpyarthaṃ vikalpyate? athavā | yatra nirvāṇe kasyacit sattvasya saṃsārādapakarṣaṇamapanayanaṃ nirvāṇe ca samāropaṇaṃ prayatnavatāpi na śakyate kartuṃ saṃsāranirvāṇayorapyanupalabhyamānatvāt, tatra kiṃ nirvāṇaṃ vikalpyate? naiva hi kiṃcidvikalpayituṃ
body.translated_text: In the ultimate truth, neither the superimposition of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — the attribution of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — is possible, since it is not apprehended, nor is the removal of <s>saṃsāra</s> — the destruction of <s>saṃsāra</s> — possible. What <s>saṃsāra</s> is there that would be conceived for the purpose of destroying? Or what <s>nirvāṇa</s> is there that would be conceived for the purpose of attaining? Alternatively: in a <s>nirvāṇa</s> where one cannot accomplish — even with great effort — either the removal of some being from <s>saṃsāra</s> or the superimposition [of that being] upon <s>nirvāṇa</s>, since both <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s> are not apprehended — what <s>nirvāṇa</s> is conceived there? Indeed, it is not appropriate to conceive of anything at all.

body.text: yuktam | avikalpayataśca niyataṃ yathoditasaṃsārāṭavīkāntārātikramo nirvāṇapuraprāptiśca bhaviṣyatīti | ata evoktamāryamāradamanasūtre-
body.translated_text: And for one who does not conceive, there will certainly be the crossing beyond the wilderness-thicket of <s>saṃsāra</s> as described and the attainment of the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Hence it is said in the noble <s>Māradamanasūtra</s>:

body.text: atha mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ tasyāṃ velāyāṃ tathārūpaṃ samanvāhāraṃ samanvāharati sma, yanmāraḥ pāpīyānindrakīlabandhanabaddho dharaṇītalaprapatitaḥ utkrośati sma- gāḍhabandhanabaddho 'smi | mañjuśrīrāha- asti pāpīyannetasmādbandhanādgāḍhataraṃ bandhanaṃ yena tvaṃ nityabaddho na punarbadhyase? tatpunaḥ katamat? yadidamasmimānaviparyāsabandhanaṃ tṛṣṇādṛṣṭibandhanam, idaṃ pāpīyan bandhanam | ato bandhanād gāḍhataraṃ bandhanaṃ na saṃvidyate | tena tvaṃ nityabaddho na punarbadhyase | peyālam | āha- kiṃ tvaṃ pāpīyannāttamanā bhūyāḥ yadi mucyethāḥ | āha- āttamanā bhaveyam, paramāttamanā bhaveyam ||
body.translated_text: Then the youth <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, at that time, exercised such a power of concentration that <s>Māra</s> the evil one, bound by the bondage of the <s>indrakīla</s> (Indra's pillar), fallen to the surface of the earth, cried out: 'I am tightly bound!' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'Is there not, evil one, a bondage tighter than this one, by which you are eternally bound and not bound again? And what is that? Namely, the bondage of the perversion of the conceit "I am" — the bondage of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) and <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (views). This, evil one, is bondage. No bondage tighter than this bondage is found. By that you are eternally bound and not bound again.' And so forth in brief. He said: 'Would you not, evil one, be delighted if you were freed?' He said: 'I would be delighted — supremely delighted!'

body.text: atha khalu suyāmo devaputro mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat- utsṛja mañjuśrīrmāraṃ pāpīyāṃsam | gacchatu svabhavanam | atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto māraṃ pāpīyāṃsametadavocat- kenāsi pāpīyan baddho yadātmānamutsṛjasi? āha- na jāne mañjuśrīḥ- kenāsmi baddhaḥ iti | āha- yathā tvaṃ pāpīyan abaddho baddhasaṃjñī, evameva sarvabālapṛthagjanā anitye nityasaṃjñinaḥ, duḥkhe 'duḥkha saṃjñinaḥ, aśubhe śubhasaṃjñinaḥ, anātmani ātmasaṃjñinaḥ, arūpe rūpasaṃjñinaḥ, avedanāyāṃ vedanāsaṃjñinaḥ, asaṃjñāyāṃ saṃjñāsaṃjñinaḥ, asaṃskāre saṃskārasaṃjñinaḥ, avijñāne vijñānasaṃjñinaḥ | api tu khalu punaḥ pāpīyan, yastvaṃ mokṣyase, kuto mokṣyase? āha- nāhaṃ jāne kutaścinmokṣye | āha- evameva pāpīyan ye 'pi mokṣyante, nate kutaścidvimokṣyante, anyatra yā asau asadbhūtasaṃjñā | tāṃ parijānanti, tāṃ parijñāya vimuktā ityucyante || iti ||
body.translated_text: Then the divine prince <s>Suyāma</s> said to the youthful <s>Mañjuśrī</s>: 'Release <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>! Let him go to his own abode.' Then the youthful <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said to <s>Māra</s> the Evil One: 'By whom are you bound, Evil One, that you would release yourself?' He said: 'I do not know, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, by whom I am bound.' He said: 'Just as you, Evil One, are unbound yet have the perception of being bound — even so, all foolish ordinary beings have the perception of permanence in what is impermanent, the perception of happiness in what is suffering, the perception of beauty in what is impure, the perception of self in what is not-self, the perception of form in what is formless, the perception of feeling in what is not feeling, the perception of perception in what is not perception, the perception of formations in what is not formations, the perception of consciousness in what is not consciousness. But tell me further, Evil One — you who will be freed, from what will you be freed?' He said: 'I do not know from what I will be freed.' He said: 'Even so, Evil One, those who will be freed are not freed from anything whatsoever, except from that which is the unreal perception. They fully understand it, and having fully understood it, they are said to be liberated.'

body.text: ata eva āgamād asadviparyāsakalpanāmātralatābandhanavicchedo vimokṣo nirvāṇamityucyate svapnopalabdhadahanajvālānirvāpaṇavat tadanilasalilairiti || 10 ||
body.translated_text: For this very reason, from this scriptural authority, the severance of the creeper-bond of mere unreal, perverted conceptual construction is called 'liberation' and '<s>nirvāṇa</s>' — like the extinguishing of the blaze of a fire apprehended in a dream by the wind and water of that [dream]. // 10 //

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacitāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau bandhamokṣaparīkṣā nāma ṣoḍaśamaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus concludes the sixteenth chapter, the Examination of Bondage and Liberation, in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary composed by the venerable <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Candrakīrti</s>.

body.text:
17
karmaphalaparīkṣā saptadaśamaṃ prakaraṇam |
body.translated_text:
Chapter 17
The Examination of <s>Karma</s> (Action) and Its Fruit — the seventeenth chapter.

body.text: atrāha- vidyata eva saṃsāraḥ, karmaphalasaṃbandhāśrayatvāt | yadi iha saṃtānāvicchedakrameṇa janmamaraṇaparaṃparayā hetuphalabhāvapravṛttyā saṃskārāṇāmātmano vā saṃsaraṇaṃ syāt, syāttadānīṃ karmaphalasaṃbandhaḥ | yathāvarṇite saṃsārābhāve tu utpattyanantaravināśitvāccittasya karmākṣepakāle ca vipākasyāsadbhāvāt karmaphalasaṃbandhābhāva eva syāt | saṃsārasadbhāve tu sati iha kṛtasya karmaṇe janmāntare 'pi vipākaphalasaṃbandhāt karmaṇāṃ phalasaṃbandho na virodhito bhavati | tasmādvidyata eva saṃsāraḥ karmaphalasaṃbandhāśrayatvāditi | kāni punastāni karmāṇi kiṃ vā tatphalamiti tatprabheda vivakṣayedamucyate-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: <s>saṃsāra</s> does indeed exist, because it is the basis of the connection between <s>karma</s> (action) and its fruit. If here, through the unbroken succession of the continuum, through the sequence of birth and death, through the operation of the cause-and-effect relation, there were transmigration of the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) or of the self, then there would be a connection between <s>karma</s> and its fruit. But when <s>saṃsāra</s> is absent as you have described — since the mind perishes immediately after arising, and since at the time when <s>karma</s> projects [a result] the maturation does not yet exist — there would simply be no connection between <s>karma</s> and its fruit. But when <s>saṃsāra</s> does exist, the connection of actions with their fruit is not contradicted, since <s>karma</s> done here is connected with its maturation-fruit even in another birth. Therefore <s>saṃsāra</s> does indeed exist, because it is the basis of the connection between <s>karma</s> and its fruit. What then are these actions, and what is their fruit? Wishing to state their classification, he says:

children.translated_text: The mind that restrains oneself and that benefits others, /

children.text: maitraṃ sa dharmastadbījaṃ phalasya pretya ceha ca || 1 ||
children.translated_text: and that which is friendly — that is <s>dharma</s>; that is the seed of fruit both hereafter and here. // 1 //

body.text: tatra āhitaḥ utpāditaḥ ahaṃmāno 'sminnityātmā | skandhānupādāya prajñapyamānaḥ pudgalaātmetyucyate | cinoti upacinoti śubhamaśubhaṃ karma vipākadānasāmarthye niyamayatīti cetaḥ | cittaṃ manaḥ vijñānamiti tasyaiva paryāyāḥ | ātmānaṃ saṃyamayati viṣayeṣvasvatantrayati rāgādikleśavaśena pravṛttiṃ nivārayatītyātmasaṃyamakam | tadetadātmasaṃyamakaṃ kuśalaṃ cetaḥ prāṇātipātādiṣu pravṛttividhārakaṃ durgatigamanāddhārayatīti dharma ityucyate ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the self (<s>ātman</s>) is that in which the conceit 'I am' is established, i.e., produced. It is the <s>pudgala</s> (person), designated in dependence on appropriating the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), and is called <s>ātman</s>. <s>Cetas</s> (mind) is that which accumulates and heaps up wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s> and determines the capacity for giving maturation. <s>Citta</s> (mind), <s>manas</s> (thought), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) are its synonyms. 'Self-restraining' (<s>ātmasaṃyamaka</s>) means: it restrains the self, makes it unfree with respect to sense-objects, prevents activity under the control of afflictions such as passion and the rest. This self-restraining wholesome mind, which holds back from engagement in killing and the like, is called <s>dharma</s> because it 'holds' (<s>dhārayati</s>) — it holds one back from going to lower destinies.

body.text: dharmaśabdo 'yaṃ pravacane tridhā vyavasthāpitaḥ | svalakṣaṇadhāraṇārthena kugatigamanavidhāraṇārthena pāñcagatikasaṃsāravidhāraṇārthena | tatra svalakṣaṇadhāraṇārthena sarve sāsravā anāsravāśca dharmā ityucyante | kugatigamanavidhāraṇārthena daśakuśalādayo dharmā ityucyante |
body.translated_text: The word <s>dharma</s> is established in the teaching in three senses: in the sense of maintaining one's own characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇadhāraṇa</s>), in the sense of holding back from going to lower destinies, and in the sense of holding back from wandering in the five-destinied <s>saṃsāra</s>. Therein, in the sense of maintaining one's own characteristic, all <s>dharmas</s>, both with and without <s>āśravas</s> (defilements), are called <s>dharmas</s>. In the sense of holding back from going to lower destinies, the ten wholesome courses of action and the like are called <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: dharmacārī sukhaṃ śete asmiṃlloke paratra ca ||
body.translated_text: One who practices <s>dharma</s> sleeps happily, in this world and the next. //

body.text: pāñcagatikasaṃsāragamanavidhāraṇārthena nirvāṇe dharma ityucyate, dharmaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchatītyatra| iha tu kugatigamanavidhāraṇārthenaiva dharmaśabdo 'bhipretaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the sense of holding back from wandering in the five-destinied <s>saṃsāra</s>, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is called <s>dharma</s> — as in 'I go for refuge to the <s>Dharma</s>.' But here, the word <s>dharma</s> is intended only in the sense of holding back from going to lower destinies.

body.text: kiṃ punarātmasaṃyamakamevaikaṃ cetaḥ dharma iti? netyāha | kiṃ tarhi parānugrāhakaṃ ca maitraṃ ca yaccetaḥ, asāvapi dharmaḥ | maitramityatra caśabdo luptanirdiṣṭo veditavyaḥ | tatra paramanugṛhṇātīti parānugrāhakaṃ cetaḥ, catuḥsaṃgrahavastupravṛttaṃ bhayaparitrāṇapravṛttaṃ ca yaccetaḥ, asāvapi dharmaḥ | mitre bhavamaviruddhaṃ sattveṣu yaccetaḥ, tanmaitraṃ cetaḥ | maitraṃ yaccetaḥ, tanmaitracetaḥ, maitramevaṃ vā | yaccaitat trividhaṃ ceto nirdiṣṭam, sa dharma ityucyate| viparyayādadharmo yojyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Is it then only self-restraining mind that is <s>dharma</s>? No, he says. What then? The mind that benefits others and that which is friendly — that too is <s>dharma</s>. In the word 'friendly' (<s>maitra</s>), a conjunctive particle 'and' (<s>ca</s>) should be understood as elided. Therein, the mind that benefits others — that which operates through the four means of attraction (<s>catuḥsaṃgrahavastu</s>) and that which operates for the protection from fear — that too is <s>dharma</s>. The mind that is friendly, non-hostile toward beings, as befits a friend — that is friendly mind. And this threefold mind that has been described is called <s>dharma</s>. By reversal, <s>adharma</s> (non-virtue) should be understood.

body.text: yaccaitannirdiṣṭaprabhedaṃ cetaḥ, tadbījaṃ phalasya | asādhāraṇaṃ phalābhinirvṛttau yatkāraṇam, tadeva bījamityucyate | tadyathā śālyaṅkurasya śālibījam | yattu sādhāraṇaṃ kṣityādi na tadbījaṃ kāraṇametat | yathaitadevam, ihāpi iṣṭasya vipākasyābhinirvṛttau trividhaṃ ceto bhavati bījam | puruṣakārādayastu kāraṇameva ||
body.translated_text: This mind of the described classification — that is the seed of the fruit. What is the exclusive cause for the production of the fruit is called the seed — just as the rice seed is [the seed] of the rice sprout. But what is common, such as earth and the like, is not the seed; that is [merely] a condition. Just so, here too, the threefold mind is the seed for the production of the desired maturation. But effort (<s>puruṣakāra</s>) and the like are merely conditions.

body.text: kasmin punaḥ kāle bījasya phalaniṣpattirityāha- pretya ceha ca | pretyeti adṛṣṭe janmani, iheti dṛṣṭe janmanītyarthaḥ | etacca āgamādvistareṇa boddhavyam || 1 ||
body.translated_text: At what time does the seed produce its fruit? He says: 'hereafter and here.' 'Hereafter' (<s>pretya</s>) means in an unseen birth; 'here' (<s>iha</s>) means in a seen birth — this is the meaning. And this should be understood in detail from the <s>āgama</s> (scripture). // 1 //

body.text: evaṃ tāvat cittātmakamevaikaṃ dharmaṃ vyavasthāpya punarapi dvividhaṃ bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: Having thus established <s>dharma</s> as being of the nature of mind alone, furthermore, by the <s>Bhagavān</s> it has been divided in two:

body.text: cetanā cetayitvā ca karmoktaṃ paramarṣiṇā |
body.translated_text: <s>Cetanā</s> (volition) and what is done after deliberation (<s>cetayitvā</s>) — thus has <s>karma</s> been declared by the supreme sage. /

body.text: paramārthadarśanādṛṣiḥ | paramaścāsau ṛṣiśceti paramarṣiḥ sarvākāratayā paramārthagamanāt śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhyo 'pi utkṛṣṭatvāt paramarṣiḥ saṃbuddho bhagavān | tena paramarṣiṇā cetanā karma, cetayitvā ca karmetyuktaṃ sūtre ||
body.translated_text: Because of his vision of ultimate reality, he is a sage (<s>ṛṣi</s>). He is the supreme (<s>parama</s>) and also a sage — hence <s>paramarṣi</s> (supreme sage), because of his going to ultimate reality in all its aspects, and because of his superiority even to <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. The <s>paramarṣi</s> is the fully awakened <s>Bhagavān</s>. By that supreme sage, <s>cetanā</s> (volition) is <s>karma</s>, and what is done after deliberation is <s>karma</s> — thus it has been declared in the <s>sūtra</s>.

body.text: yaccaitad dvividhaṃ karmoktam-
body.translated_text: Of this twofold <s>karma</s> that has been declared:

body.text: tasyānekavidho bhedaḥ karmaṇaḥ parikīrtitaḥ || 2 ||
body.translated_text: The manifold classification of that <s>karma</s> has been proclaimed. // 2 //

body.text: kathaṃ kṛtvā?
body.translated_text: How?

children.translated_text: Therein, what has been called <s>cetanā</s> (volition) — that <s>karma</s> is considered mental. /
And what has been called 'done after deliberation' — that is bodily and verbal. // 3 //

body.text: manasi bhavaṃ mānasam | manodvāreṇaiva niṣṭhāgamanāt kāyavākpravṛttinirapekṣatvācca manovijñānasaṃprayuktaiva cetanā mānasaṃ karmetyucyate | tatraśabdo nirdhāraṇe | yattu dvitīyaṃ cetayitvā ca karmetyuktam, tatpunaḥ kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ ca veditavyam | evaṃ ca evaṃ ca kāyavāgbhyāṃ pravartiṣye ityevaṃ cetasā saṃcintya yat kriyate, taccetayitvā karmetyucyate | tatpunardvividham, kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ ca | kāyavācorbhavatvāt taddvāreṇa ca niṣṭhāgamanāt | evaṃ ca trividham- kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ mānasaṃ ca || 3 ||
body.translated_text: What arises in the mind is mental. Because it reaches completion through the mind-door alone and is independent of bodily and verbal activity, <s>cetanā</s> associated with mind-consciousness alone is called mental <s>karma</s>. The word 'therein' (<s>tatra</s>) serves for specification. And the second kind — 'what has been called "done after deliberation" is <s>karma</s>' — that should be understood as bodily and verbal. Thus: 'I shall act in such and such a way with body and speech' — having deliberated with the mind and then acting, that is called '<s>karma</s> done after deliberation.' That is further twofold: bodily and verbal — because it belongs to body and speech, and because it reaches completion through their doors. Thus it is threefold: bodily, verbal, and mental. // 3 //

body.text: etadapi trividhaṃ karma punarbhidyamānaṃ saptavidhaṃ saṃjāyate, ityevaṃ tasya karmaṇo bhagavatā bahuprakāro bhedo 'nuvarṇitaḥ | kathaṃ kṛtvā?
body.translated_text: This threefold <s>karma</s>, when further subdivided, becomes sevenfold — thus the <s>Bhagavān</s> has described its manifold classification. How?

children.translated_text: Speech, bodily movement, and those that are designated as non-restraints of the <s>avijñapti</s> (non-informative) class, /
and other <s>avijñaptis</s> that are the restraints, likewise — // 4 //
merit that follows from enjoyment, and demerit of the same kind, /

children.text: cetanā ceti saptaite dharmāḥ karmāñjanāḥ smṛtāḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: and <s>cetanā</s> (volition) — these seven <s>dharmas</s> are considered to be the types of <s>karma</s>. // 5 //

body.text: tatra vyaktavarṇoccāraṇaṃ vāk | viṣpandaḥ śarīraṃceṣṭā | tatra kuśalākuśalā vā vāk sarvaiva viratyaviratilakṣaṇā vijñaptisamutthāpikā sāmānyena vāgiti gṛhyate | evaṃ kuśalo 'kuśalo vā viratyaviratilakṣaṇo vijñaptisamutthāpako viṣpandaḥ sāmānyena gṛhyate || yathā caitadvijñapterdvidhā bhedaḥ,
body.translated_text: Therein, speech is the utterance of distinct sounds. Bodily movement (<s>viṣpanda</s>) is bodily gesticulation. Therein, speech, whether wholesome or unwholesome, which has the character of restraint or non-restraint and gives rise to informative action (<s>vijñapti</s>), is generally understood as speech. Likewise, bodily movement, whether wholesome or unwholesome, having the character of restraint or non-restraint and giving rise to informative action, is generally understood [as bodily action]. And just as there is this twofold division of the informative (<s>vijñapti</s>),

body.text: evamavijñapterapi | aviratilakṣaṇā avijñaptayaḥ viratilakṣaṇāśceti kṛtvā | tatra aviratilakṣaṇā avijñaptayaḥ tadyathā adyaprabhṛti mayā prāṇinaṃ hatvā cauryaṃ kṛtvā jīvikā parikalpayitavyeti pāpakarmābhyupagamātprabhṛti tadakāriṇo 'pi akuśalakarmābhyupagamahetukāḥ satatasamitamavijñaptayaḥ samupajāyante | kaivartādīnāṃca jālādiparikarmakālātprabhṛti tadakāriṇāmapi yā avijñaptaya upajāyante, tā etā aviratilakṣaṇā avijñaptaya ityucyante | yathā caitāstathā anyāḥ viratilakṣaṇāḥ kuśalasvabhāvā avijñaptayaḥ | tadyathā- adyaprabhṛti prāṇātipātādibhyaḥ prativiramāmīti kāyavāgvijñaptiparisamāptikālakṣaṇātprabhṛti taduttarakālaṃ pramattādyavasthasyāpi yāḥ kuśalopacayasvabhāvā avijñaptaya upajāyante, tā etā viratilakṣaṇā avijñaptaya ityucyante | etā rūpakriyāsvabhāvā api satyo vijñaptivat parānna vijñāpayantītyavijñaptayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: so too of the non-informative (<s>avijñapti</s>). This is because of the division into non-restraint-characterized <s>avijñaptis</s> and restraint-characterized ones. Therein, non-restraint-characterized <s>avijñaptis</s> are: for instance, from the time of undertaking evil action such as 'From today I shall make my living by killing beings and stealing' — even when not performing that action, <s>avijñaptis</s> that are caused by the undertaking of unwholesome action continuously and uninterruptedly arise. And for fishermen and the like, <s>avijñaptis</s> that arise from the time of preparing nets and such implements, even when not performing that action — these are called non-restraint-characterized <s>avijñaptis</s>. And just as these, so too there are other <s>avijñaptis</s> that are restraint-characterized and wholesome in nature. For instance: from the time of completing the bodily and verbal informative action of saying 'From today I shall refrain from killing and the like' — from that time onwards, even for one in a heedless state and the like, <s>avijñaptis</s> that are wholesome in nature of accumulating merit arise — these are called restraint-characterized <s>avijñaptis</s>. These, though having the nature of material form and activity, do not inform (<s>vijñāpayanti</s>) others like informative action — hence they are <s>avijñaptis</s>.

body.text: tathā paribhogānvayaṃ puṇyam, kuśalamityarthaḥ | paribhogena anvayaḥ asyeti paribhogānvayam | paribhogaḥ parityaktasya vastunaḥ saṃghādibhirupabhogaḥ | anvayaḥ anugamaḥ | dāyakasaṃtānajaḥ kuśalopacaya ityarthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, 'merit that follows from enjoyment' (<s>paribhogānvaya</s>) — meaning wholesome [<s>karma</s>]. 'Following from enjoyment' means: it has a following from enjoyment.
