'Enjoyment' is the use of a donated object by the <s>Saṃgha</s> and others. 'Following' is continuation. The meaning is: the accumulation of merit arising in the continuum of the donor.

body.text: apuṇyaṃ ca tathāvidham, paribhogānvayamityarthaḥ | tadyathā devakulādipratiṣṭhāpanam, yatra sattvā hanyante | yathā yathā hi tatkīrtau prāṇino hanyante, tathā tathā taddevakulādyupabhogāt tatkartṛṇāṃ saṃtāne paribhogānvayamapuṇyamapi jāyate, ityevamapuṇyaṃ ca tathāvidhaṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: 'Demerit of the same kind' — meaning following from enjoyment. For instance, the establishment of temples and the like where beings are killed. For insofar as living beings are killed because of the renown of that [establishment], to that extent demerit following from enjoyment also arises in the continuum of the builders, through the use of those temples and the like. Thus demerit too is 'of the same kind.'

body.text: cittābhisaṃskāramanaskarmalakṣaṇā cetanā ceti ||
body.translated_text: And <s>cetanā</s> (volition), which has the characteristic of mental action (<s>manaskarma</s>), i.e., the mental formation of mind (<s>cittābhisaṃskāra</s>).

body.text: saṃkṣepeṇa etatsaptavidhaṃ karma bhavati- kuśalākuśalā vāk, kuśalākuśalo viṣpandaḥ, kuśalamavijñaptilakṣaṇam, akuśalamavijñaptilakṣaṇam, paribhogānvayaṃ puṇyam, paribhogānvayamapuṇyam, cetanā ceti ||
body.translated_text: In summary, this sevenfold <s>karma</s> is: wholesome and unwholesome speech; wholesome and unwholesome bodily movement; wholesome <s>avijñapti</s>-characterized [<s>karma</s>]; unwholesome <s>avijñapti</s>-characterized [<s>karma</s>]; merit following from enjoyment; demerit following from enjoyment; and <s>cetanā</s>.

body.text: ete ca sapta dharmāḥ karmāñjanāḥ karmatvenābhivyaktāḥ karmalakṣaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ || 5 ||
body.translated_text: And these seven <s>dharmas</s>, identified as <s>karma</s>, expressed as having the nature of <s>karma</s>, having the defining mark of <s>karma</s>, are considered [thus]. // 5 //

body.text: atraike paricodayanti- yadetat karma bahuvidhamuktam, tat kimā vipākakālādavatiṣṭhate, atha na tiṣṭhati utpattyanantaravināśitvāt? yadi tāvat-
body.translated_text: Here some raise an objection: this <s>karma</s> that has been described as manifold — does it persist until the time of maturation, or does it not persist because it perishes immediately after arising? If indeed:

children.translated_text: If <s>karma</s> persists until the time of maturation, it would become permanent. /
And if it has ceased — having ceased, how will it produce a fruit? // 6 //

body.text: yadi utpannaṃ sat karma āvipākakālaṃ svarūpeṇāvatiṣṭhate iti parikalpyate, tad iyantaṃ kālamasya nityatā āpadyate vināśarahitatvāt | paścādvināśasadbhāvānna nityatvamiti cet, naitadevam, pūrvaṃ vināśarahitasya ākāśādivat paścādapi vināśena saṃbandhābhāvāt | vināśarahitasya ca asaṃskṛtatvaprasaṅgāt, asaṃskṛtānāṃ ca vipākādarśanāt, avipākatvena sadaivāvasthānāt nityatābhyupagama eva karmaṇāmupapadyate | ityevaṃ tāvannityatve doṣaḥ | atha utpādānantaravināśitvameva karmaṇāmabhyupetam, nanu evaṃ sati-
body.translated_text: If it is conceived that <s>karma</s>, once arisen, persists in its own form until the time of maturation, then for that entire duration it would be permanent, because it is devoid of destruction. If it is said that it is not permanent because of the subsequent existence of destruction — this is not so, because what was previously devoid of destruction, like space and the like, cannot have a connection with destruction later. And because what is devoid of destruction would have the consequence of being unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>), and because maturation is not observed for unconditioned things, and because of its permanent abiding due to not maturing — it follows that the acceptance of the permanence of actions is tenable. Thus, this is the defect if permanence is accepted. Now, if it is accepted that actions perish immediately after arising, then surely in that case:

body.text: niruddhaṃ cenniruddhaṃ sat kiṃ phalaṃ janayiṣyati |
body.translated_text: And if it has ceased — having ceased, how will it produce a fruit? /

body.text: abhāvībhūtaṃ sat karma avidyamānasvabhāvatvānnaiva phalaṃ janayiṣyatītyabhiprāyaḥ || 6 ||
body.translated_text: The intention is: <s>karma</s> that has become non-existent, having an existent non-nature, will certainly not produce a fruit. // 6 //

body.text: tatraike nikāyāntarīyāḥ parihāraṃ varṇayanti- utpattyanantaravināśitvātsaṃskārāṇām, anityatvadoṣastāvadasmākaṃ nopapadyate | yaccāpyuktam-
body.translated_text: Therein, certain members of other schools offer a defense: Since formations are destroyed immediately after arising, the fault of impermanence does not apply to us. And as for what was said —

body.text: niruddhaṃ cenniruddhaṃ sat kiṃ phalaṃ janayiṣyati |
body.translated_text: 'If what has ceased has ceased, being [already] ceased, what fruit will it produce?' /

body.text: iti, atrāpi parihāraṃ brūmaḥ-
body.translated_text: — to this too we state a defense:

children.translated_text: The continuum that proceeds from the seed, beginning with the sprout — /
from that, fruit [arises]; and without the seed, that [continuum] does not proceed. // 7 //

body.text: iha bījaṃ kṣaṇikamapi sat svajātīyabhāviphalaviśeṣaniṣpattisāmarthyaviśeṣayuktasyaiva saṃtānasya aṅkurakāṇḍanālapatrādyabhidhānasya hetubhāvamapyupagamya nirudhyate | yaścāyamaṅkuraprabhṛtirbījātsaṃtānaḥ pravartate, tasmāt krameṇa sahakārikāraṇavaikalye sati svalpādapi hetorvipulaphalapracaya upajāyate | ṛte bījāt vinā bījāt sa ca aṅkurādisaṃtānaḥ nābhipravartate | tadevaṃ tadbhāve bhāvitvena tadabhāve ca abhāvitvena bījahetukatvamaṅkurādisaṃtānasya phalasyopadarśitaṃ bhavati || 7 ||
body.translated_text: Here, the seed, even though momentary, ceases only after having also assumed the role of being a cause for a continuum — designated as sprout, stalk, stem, leaf, and so forth — that is endowed with a specific capacity for producing a particular fruit belonging to its own kind. And this continuum, beginning with the sprout, that proceeds from the seed — from that, gradually, when the cooperating conditions are not lacking, an abundant accumulation of fruit arises even from a small cause. And without the seed — apart from the seed — that continuum of sprout and so forth does not proceed. Thus, by its existing when that [seed] exists and not existing when that [seed] does not exist, the seed's causal status for the fruit, which is the continuum of sprout and so forth, has been demonstrated. // 7 //

body.text: tadevam-
body.translated_text: Thus indeed —

children.translated_text: Since from the seed [there is] a continuum, and from the continuum [there is] the arising of fruit, /
the fruit, being preceded by the seed, is therefore neither annihilated nor eternal. // 8 //

body.text: yadi iha bījamaprasūya aṅkurādisaṃtānaṃ jvālāṅgārādivirodhipratyayasāṃnidhyānnirudhyeta, tadā tatra kāryasaṃtānapravṛttyadarśanāt syāducchedadarśanam | yadi ca bījaṃ na nirudhyeta, aṅkurādisaṃtānaśca pravarteta, tadā bījasyānirodhābhyupagamācchāśvatadarśanaṃ syāt, na caitadevam, ityato nāsti bījasya śāśvatocchedadarśanaprasaṅgaḥ || 8 ||
body.translated_text: Here, if the seed were to cease — due to the presence of an opposing condition such as flame, ember, and the like — without having generated the continuum of sprout and so forth, then, because no procession of the effect-continuum would be observed there, there would be the view of annihilation. And if the seed did not cease, yet the continuum of sprout and so forth proceeded, then, because of accepting the non-cessation of the seed, there would be the view of eternalism. But this is not the case — therefore there is no consequence of the views of eternalism and annihilation for the seed. // 8 //

body.text: yathā ca bīje ayaṃ kramo 'nuvarṇitaḥ, evam-
body.translated_text: And just as this procedure has been described regarding the seed, even so —

children.translated_text: The mental continuum that proceeds from the mind — /
from that, fruit [arises]; and without the mind, that [continuum] does not proceed. // 9 //

body.text: tasmāt kuśalākuśalacetanāviśeṣasaṃprayuktāccittād yaḥ cittasaṃtānastaddhetukaḥ pravartate, tasmāt kuśalākuśalacetanāparibhāvitāccittasaṃtānāt sahakārikāraṇasaṃnidhānāvaikalye sati iṣṭamaniṣṭaṃ phalamupajāyate sugatidurgatiṣu | ṛte tu taccitāt cittamantareṇa sa ca nābhipravartate || 9 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, from the mind that is conjoined with a particular volition (<s>cetanā</s>) — whether wholesome or unwholesome — the mental continuum that proceeds, having that [mind] as its cause — from that mental continuum, perfumed by wholesome or unwholesome volition, when the cooperating conditions are not lacking, desired and undesired fruit arises in the good and bad destinations. But without that mind — in the absence of that mind — that [continuum] does not proceed. // 9 //

body.text: tadevam-
body.translated_text: Thus indeed —

children.translated_text: Since from the mind [there is] a continuum, and from the continuum [there is] the arising of fruit, /
the fruit, being preceded by action, is therefore neither annihilated nor eternal. // 10 //

body.text: yadi arhaccaramacittamiva taddhetuphalapāraṃparyāvicchinnakramavartino bhāvinaścittasaṃtānasya hetubhāvamanupagamya kuśalaṃ cittaṃ nirudhyeta, tadā ucchinnaṃ tatkarma syāt | athāpi anāgatasaṃtānasya hetubhāvamupagamya svarūpādapracyutaṃ syāt, syāttadānīṃ karma śāśvatam | na caitadevamiti | tasmāt kṣaṇikakarmābhyupagame 'pi nāsti ucchedaśāśvatadarśanadvayaprasaṅga iti || 10 ||
body.translated_text: If the wholesome mind were to cease without assuming the role of being a cause for the future mental continuum that proceeds in unbroken successive sequence of cause and fruit — like the final mind-moment of an <s>Arhat</s> — then that action would be annihilated. And if, having assumed the role of being a cause for the future continuum, it were to remain without departing from its own form, then that action would be eternal. But this is not the case. Therefore, even when accepting momentary action, there is no consequence of the twofold view of annihilation and eternalism. // 10 //

body.text: tadatra yathoditakarmaprabhedavyākhyāne daśa kuśalāḥ karmapathā vyākhyātāḥ | te ca-
body.translated_text: Now here, in the exposition of the classifications of action as described above, the ten wholesome courses of action have been explained. And they —

children.translated_text: The ten wholesome courses of action are the means of accomplishing <s>dharma</s> (merit); /

children.text: phalaṃ kāmaguṇāḥ pañca dharmasya pretya ceha ca || 11 ||
children.translated_text: the five qualities of sense-desire are the fruit of <s>dharma</s>, both hereafter and here. // 11 //

body.text: ta ete daśa kuśalāḥ karmapathā dharmasya sādhanopāyā niṣpattihetubhūtā ityarthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: These ten wholesome courses of action are the means of accomplishing <s>dharma</s> — meaning, they are the causes of its production.

body.text: kaḥ punarasau kuśalakarmapathavyatirikto dharmo nāma, yasyaite sādhanopāyatvena vyavasthāpyante? ucyate | cittaviśeṣa eva kaścit dharmaśabdenoktaḥ ||
body.translated_text: What, then, is that <s>dharma</s> distinct from the wholesome courses of action, for which these are established as the means of accomplishment? It is replied: a certain specific state of mind has been designated by the word '<s>dharma</s>' —

body.text:
ātmasaṃyamakaṃ cetaḥ parānugrāhakaṃ ca yat |
maitraṃ sa dharmaḥ
body.translated_text:
That mind which is self-restraining and which benefits others,
benevolent — that is <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: ityanena | athavā | pariniṣṭhitarūpā ete daśa kuśalāḥ karmapathā dharmaśabdavācyā bhavanti, kriyamāṇarūpāstu kuśalakarmapathavācyā bhavanti | tadasya uktalakṣaṇasya ete daśa kuśalāḥ karmapathā niṣpattau hetutvena vyavasthāpyante | kathaṃ punaratra prakrānte karmavibhāge daśa kuśalāḥ karmapathā iti? ucyate-
body.translated_text: — by this [statement]. Alternatively, these ten wholesome courses of action, in their completed form, are designated by the word '<s>dharma</s>,' while in their form of being performed, they are designated as wholesome courses of action. Thus these ten wholesome courses of action are established as causes for the production of <s>dharma</s> of the described characteristics. But how are the ten wholesome courses of action [classified] in this context of the classification of action being discussed? It is replied —

body.text: vāgviṣpando 'viratayo yāścāvijñaptisaṃjñitāḥ |
body.translated_text: Vocal expression, non-restraints, and those designated as <s>avijñapti</s> (unmanifest action) — /

body.text: ityādinā kāyikāsrayaḥ karmapathāḥ vācikāścatvāro vyākhyātāḥ| cetanā cetyanena abhidhyāvyāpādasamyagdṛṣṭayākhyāsrayo mānasā vyākhyātāḥ | ityevaṃ daśāpi kuśalāḥ karmapathā atra vyākhyātāḥ | te ca yathoditasya dharmasya niṣpattihetavo bhavanti | asya ca dharmasya rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyalakṣaṇāḥ pañca kāmaguṇāḥ | pretya ca adṛṣṭe paraloke ityarthaḥ, iha ceti ihaloke ityarthaḥ, phalamupabhujyate iti || 11 ||
body.translated_text: — by this and so forth, three courses of action based on the body and four based on speech have been explained. And by 'volition,' the three mental ones — designated as covetousness, malice, and right view — have been explained. Thus all ten wholesome courses of action have been explained here. And they are the causes for the production of <s>dharma</s> as described above. And the fruit of this <s>dharma</s> is the five qualities of sense-desire, characterized by form, sound, smell, taste, and touch. And 'hereafter' means in the unseen next world; 'here' means in this world — [the fruit] is enjoyed. // 11 //

body.text: evaṃ tāvadaikanikāyikairākṣepaparihāre varṇite sati, tān prati apare doṣamudbhāvya anyākṣepaparihāraṃ varṇayantaḥ āhuḥ-
body.translated_text: Now, when this defense against the objection has been described by members of one school, others, pointing out faults in their position and describing a defense against a different objection, say —

children.translated_text: Many and great faults would follow from that theory; /
therefore that theory is not tenable here. // 12 //

body.text: yadi bījāṅkurasādharmyeṇa cittasaṃtāne śāśvatocchedadarśanadvayadoṣaprasaṅgaparihāraḥ syāt, tadā bahavaśca doṣāḥ saṃkhyābahutvena mahāntaśca dṛṣṭādṛṣṭavirodhena parapakṣe prāpruvanti | kathaṃ kṛtvā? yadi hi bījasaṃtānadṛṣṭāntena śālibījāt śālyaṅkurādisaṃtāna eva pravartate, na vijātīyaḥ, śālyaṅkurādisaṃtānācca śāliphalameva upajāyate, na bilvaphalam, bhinnajātīyatvāt, evamihāpi kuśalacittāt kuśalacittasaṃtāna eva syāt, samānajātīyatvāt, na akuśalāvyākṛtacittasaṃtānaḥ, vijātīyatvāt | evamakuśalāvyākṛtacittādakuśalāvyākṛtacittasaṃtāna eva syānnānyaḥ, bhinnajātīyatvāt | kāmarūpārūpyāvacarānāsravacittebhyaḥ sadṛśānāmeva cittānāṃ kāmarūpārūpyāvacarānāsravāṇāmutpādaḥ
body.translated_text: If, by analogy with the seed-sprout, the defense against the consequence of the twofold fault of the views of eternalism and annihilation were [to be maintained] through the mental continuum, then many faults in number and great faults through contradiction with what is seen and unseen would befall the other's position. How so? For if, by the illustration of the seed-continuum, only a rice-sprout continuum proceeds from a rice-seed and not a dissimilar one, and from a rice-sprout continuum only rice-fruit arises and not <s>bilva</s>-fruit because of being of a different kind — even so here, from a wholesome mind there would be only a wholesome mental continuum, because of being of the same kind, and not an unwholesome or indeterminate mental continuum, because of being of a different kind. Likewise, from an unwholesome or indeterminate mind there would be only an unwholesome or indeterminate mental continuum and no other, because of being of a different kind. From minds belonging to the desire-realm, form-realm, formless-realm, and uncontaminated [spheres], only similar minds — of the desire-realm, form-realm, formless-realm, and uncontaminated [type] — would arise

body.text: syāt, na bhinnajātīyānām | manuṣyacittānmanuṣyacittameva syānna devanārakatiryagādyanyacittam | tataśca yo devaḥ sa deva eva syāt, yo manuṣyaḥ sa manuṣya eva syādityādi | tataśca akuśalamapi kurvatāṃ devamanuṣyāṇāṃ gatiyonivarṇabuddhīndriyabalarūpabhogādi vaicitryaṃ na syādapāyapatanaṃ ca | iṣyate caitatsarvamiti | evaṃ bahavaśca mahāntaśca doṣā yasmādbījasaṃtānasādharmyakalpanāyāṃ prasajyante, tasmānnaiṣā kalpanā atropapadyate || 12 ||
body.translated_text: , not those of a different kind. From a human mind there would be only a human mind, not the mind of a god, hell-being, animal, or other being. And consequently, whoever is a god would always be a god; whoever is a human would always be a human — and so forth. And consequently, even for gods and humans who perform unwholesome deeds, there would be no diversity of destiny, birth-type, caste, intelligence, faculties, powers, form, enjoyments, and so forth, nor would there be falling into bad destinations. But all of this is indeed accepted. Thus, since many and great faults follow from the theory of analogy with the seed-continuum, this theory is not tenable here. // 12 //

children.text: imāṃ punaḥ pravakṣyāmi kalpanāṃ yātra yojyate |
children.translated_text: I shall now set forth the theory that is applicable here, /
which has been described by <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Śrāvakas</s>. // 13 //

body.text: kā cāsau kalpanetyāha-
body.translated_text: And what is that theory? He says —

children.translated_text: Just as a promissory note is the <s>avipraṇāśa</s> (non-destruction), so too action is like a debt. /
It is fourfold by realm, and by nature it is indeterminate. // 14 //

body.text: iha kuśalaṃ karma kṛtaṃ sat utpādānantarameva nirudhyate, na ca tasminniruddhe phalābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ | yasmād yadaiva tatkarma utpadyate, tadā etasya karmaṇo 'vipraṇāśo nāma viprayukto dharmaḥ kartuḥ saṃtāne samupajāyate ṛṇapatrasthānīyaḥ | tadevaṃ patraṃ yathā avipraṇāśaḥ tathā veditavyaḥ | yasya ca asau avipraṇāśākhyo dharma utpadyate, ṛṇamiva tatkarma veditavyam | yathā ca ṛṇapatrāvasthānāt prayukte 'pi dhane dhanino na dhananāśo bhavati, saṃbadhyata eva sa kālāntareṇa pañcamena dhanaskandhena, tathā vinaṣṭe 'pi karmaṇi avipraṇāśākhyadharmāntarāvasthānāt tannimittakena phalena abhisaṃbadhyata eva kartā | yathā ca ṛṇapatraṃ dāturdhanābhyāgamaṃ kṛtvā nirmuktaṃ sat punarapi vidyamānaṃ vā avidyamānaṃ vā na dhanābhyāgame samartham, evamavipraṇāśo 'pi dattavipākaḥ san vidyamāno vā avidyamāno vā na śaknoti nirmuktapatravat kartuḥ punarapi vipākasaṃbandhaṃ kartum ||
body.translated_text: Here, a wholesome action, having been performed, ceases immediately after arising, and yet when it has ceased, there is no consequence of the absence of fruit. Because at the very moment when that action arises, a <s>dharma</s> (factor) called <s>avipraṇāśa</s> (non-destruction), dissociated [from mind], arises in the continuum of the doer — analogous to a promissory note. Thus, the <s>avipraṇāśa</s> should be understood as being like a promissory note. And the action for which this <s>dharma</s> called <s>avipraṇāśa</s> arises should be understood as being like a debt. And just as, due to the existence of a promissory note, even when the wealth has been spent, the destruction of the wealth-owner's wealth does not occur — for he is connected, after some time, with a fifth aggregate of wealth — so too, even when the action has perished, due to the existence of the <s>dharma</s>-factor called <s>avipraṇāśa</s>, the doer is indeed connected with the fruit occasioned by it. And just as a promissory note, having been discharged upon the creditor's receipt of wealth, whether existing or non-existing, is no longer capable of [effecting] the receipt of wealth — even so, the <s>avipraṇāśa</s> too, having yielded its result, whether existing or non-existing, is unable, like a discharged note, to again effect the connection of the doer with a result.

body.text: yaścāyamavipraṇāśo 'smābhiruktaḥ sūtrāntaroktaḥ, caturvidho dhātutaḥ sa kāmarūpārūpyāvacarānāsravabhedāt, prakṛtyā avyākṛtaśca saḥ | kuśalākuśalatvena avyākaraṇādavyākṛta evāvipraṇāśaḥ | yadi asau akuśalānāṃ karmaṇāmakuśalaḥ syāt, tadā kāmaṃ vītarāgāṇāṃ na syāt | yadi ca kuśalānām, kuśalaḥ syāt, samucchinnakuśalamūlānāṃ sa na syāt | tasmāt prakṛtyavyākṛta evāsau || 14 ||
body.translated_text: And this <s>avipraṇāśa</s> stated by us, which is stated in other <s>sūtras</s>, is fourfold by realm — by the division into desire-realm, form-realm, formless-realm, and uncontaminated. And by nature it is indeterminate. The <s>avipraṇāśa</s> is indeterminate because it is not declared as either wholesome or unwholesome. For if it were unwholesome for unwholesome actions, then it would not exist for those who have become free from desire. And if it were wholesome for wholesome actions, it would not exist for those whose wholesome roots have been completely severed. Therefore, it is by nature indeterminate. // 14 //

body.text: kiṃ ca |
body.translated_text: Moreover —

body.text: prahāṇato na praheyo bhāvanāheya eva vā |
body.translated_text: It is not to be abandoned through abandonment, but is to be abandoned through cultivation alone. /

body.text: sa cāyamavipraṇāśaḥ prahāṇato na praheyaḥ | pārthagjanikāni karmāṇi darśanamārgeṇaiva prahīyante mā bhūdāryaḥ pṛthagjanakarmasamanvāgata iti | avipraṇāśastu tatkarmaprahāṇe 'pi darśanamārgeṇa na prahīyate, kiṃ tu bhāvanāmārgeṇa vā tasyā prahāṇaṃ bhavati | dhātusamatikramaṇapraheya eveti vāśabdo vikalpārthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: And this <s>avipraṇāśa</s> is not to be abandoned through abandonment. Actions of ordinary beings are abandoned by the path of seeing alone, lest a noble one be possessed of ordinary-being actions. But the <s>avipraṇāśa</s>, even when that action has been abandoned through the path of seeing, is not abandoned; rather, its abandonment occurs through the path of cultivation. Or [it is] to be abandoned through transcending the realm — the word 'or' indicates an alternative.

body.text: yataścaivamavipraṇāśaḥ karmavināśe 'pi na naśyati, karmaprahāṇe 'pi na prahīyate,
body.translated_text: And since the <s>avipraṇāśa</s> does not perish even when the action perishes, and is not abandoned even when the action is abandoned,

body.text: tasmādavipraṇāśena jāyate karmaṇāṃ phalam || 15 ||
body.translated_text: therefore, through the <s>avipraṇāśa</s>, the fruit of actions is born. // 15 //

body.text: yadi punarapi asya avipraṇāśasya karmaṇaḥ prahāṇena prahāṇātprahāṇataḥ prahāṇaṃ syāt karmaṇaśca saṃkrameṇa karmaṇo vināśena karmāntarasaṃmukhībhāvena vināśaḥ syāt, ko doṣaḥ syāditi? ucyate-
body.translated_text: If, further, this <s>avipraṇāśa</s> were abandoned through the abandonment of the action — abandonment through abandonment — and if it were destroyed through the transference of the action, through the destruction of the action, through the coming to face another action — what fault would there be? It is replied —

children.translated_text: If it were to be abandoned through abandonment, or through the transference of the action, /
faults such as the destruction of action would follow. // 16 //

body.text: yadi darśanamārgeṇa pārthagjanikakarmavadavipraṇāśaḥ prahīyeta, tadā karmaṇo vināśa eva syāt | karmavināśācca āryāṇāmiṣṭāniṣṭakarmaphalavipākaḥ pūrvakarmaphalahetuko na syāt | akṛtasyaiva karmaṇaḥ phalodayaḥ syāt | karmaphalābhāvadarśanācca mithyādarśanaṃ syāditi | evaṃ karmavadhādayo doṣāḥ prasajyante prahāṇataḥ praheyatvābhyupagame sati avipraṇāśasya | evaṃ karmaṇaḥ saṃkrame 'pi yojyam || 16 ||
body.translated_text: If the <s>avipraṇāśa</s> were abandoned through the path of seeing, like the actions of ordinary beings, then there would be the very destruction of action. And from the destruction of action, the ripening of the fruit of desired and undesired actions for the noble ones, caused by former actions, would not occur. There would be the arising of fruit of action not performed. And from seeing the absence of the fruit of action, there would be wrong view. Thus, faults such as the destruction of action follow when the <s>avipraṇāśa</s> is accepted as being abandoned through abandonment. The same should be applied regarding the transference of action. // 16 //

children.translated_text: Of all dissimilar and similar actions, /
of those belonging to the same realm, a single one arises at the moment of rebirth-linking. // 17 //

body.text: bhinnajātīyāni karmāṇi viṣabhāgāni | sadṛśāni sabhāgāni | teṣāṃ sarveṣāmeva sabhāgānāṃ ca viṣabhāgānāṃ ca karmaṇāṃ kāmarūpārūpyadhātupratisaṃdhiṣu sarvakarmāpamardanaḥ eka eva avipraṇāśa utpadyate | sa cāpi sadhātūnāṃ samānadhātukānāmeva utpadyate na viṣabhāgadhātukānām || 17 ||
body.translated_text: Actions of different kinds are dissimilar. Similar ones are of the same kind. Of all these — both similar and dissimilar — actions, at the rebirth-linkings in the desire-realm, form-realm, and formless-realm, a single <s>avipraṇāśa</s> arises that neutralizes all actions. And it arises only for those of the same realm, not for those of dissimilar realms. // 17 //

children.text: karmaṇaḥ karmaṇo dṛṣṭe dharma utpadyate tu saḥ |
children.translated_text: For each and every action, this <s>dharma</s> (factor) arises in the seen [realm]; /
and it persists even in the ripening of both types of all [actions]. // 18 //

body.text: sa cāyamavipraṇāśākhyo dharmaḥ sarvasyaiva karmaṇaḥ cetanācetayitvāsvabhāvasya sāsravānāsravabhedena vā dviprakārabhinnasya dṛṣṭe dharme ihaiva janmani karmaṇaḥ karmaṇaḥ ekaiko 'vipraṇāśa utpadyate | sa cāyamavipraṇāśo vipakke 'pi vipāke nāvaśyaṃ nirudhyate, nirbhuktapatravacca vidyamāno 'pi san na śaknoti punarapi vipaktum || 18 ||
body.translated_text: And this <s>dharma</s> (factor) called 'non-perishing' (<s>avipraṇāśa</s>) pertains to every action whatsoever — whether of the nature of volition (<s>cetanā</s>) or of the nature of what is willed (<s>cetayitva</s>) — differentiated into two kinds according to the division of with-defilements and without-defilements.

children.translated_text: It ceases either by the transcendence of the fruit, or by death.

children.text: anāsravaṃ sāsravaṃ ca vibhāgaṃ tatra lakṣayet || 19 ||
children.translated_text: One should discern therein the distinction of without-defilements and with-defilements. // 19 //

body.text: tatra phalavyatikramānnirudhyate | yathoktam- bhāvanāheya eveti | maraṇānnirudhyate | yathoktam-
body.translated_text: Therein, it ceases by the transcendence of the fruit. As stated: 'It is to be abandoned only by the path of meditation.' It ceases by death. As stated:

body.text: pratisaṃdhau sadhātūnāmeka utpadyate tu saḥ | iti |
body.translated_text: 'At the moment of recon­nection (<s>pratisaṃdhi</s>), among those with the same elements, that single one arises.' //

body.text: sa cāyaṃ sāsravāṇāṃ sāsravaḥ, anāsravāṇāmanāsravaḥ ityevaṃ vibhāgaṃ lakṣayet || 19 ||
body.translated_text: And this [non-perishing factor] is with-defilements for [actions] with-defilements, and without-defilements for those without-defilements — thus one should discern the distinction. // 19 //

body.text: tadevam-
body.translated_text: Thus indeed —

children.text: śūnyatā ca na cocchedaḥ saṃsāraśca na śāśvatam |
children.translated_text: Emptiness, yet not annihilation; <s>saṃsāra</s>, yet not eternalism;
the non-perishing of <s>karma</s> — this <s>dharma</s> was taught by the <s>Buddha</s>. // 20 //

body.text: yasmāt karma kṛtaṃ sat nirudhyate, na svabhāvenāvatiṣṭhate, tasmāt karmaṇaḥ svabhāvenāvasthānāt śūnyatā copapadyate | na caivaṃ karmaṇo 'navasthānāducchedadarśanaprasaṅgaḥ, avipraṇāśaparigraheṇa karmavipākasadbhāvāt | vipākābhāve hi karmaṇaḥ ucchedadarśanaṃ syāt | avipraṇāśadharmasadbhāvāt
body.translated_text: Since <s>karma</s>, having been performed, ceases, and does not remain by its own nature — therefore, from the non-remaining of <s>karma</s> by its own nature, emptiness [follows];

body.text: bījasaṃtānasādharmyaparikalpanābhāvācca nānāgatijātiyonidhātubhedabhinnaśca pāñcagatikaḥ saṃsāro vicitraḥ siddho bhavati | na ca śāśvatavādaprasaṅgaḥ, karmaṇaḥ svarūpeṇāvasthānānabhyupagamāt | karmaṇāṃ ca avipraṇāśaḥ, avipraṇāśasadbhāvāt, iti | evaṃ niravaśeṣāvidyānidrāpagamādvibuddhena bhagavatā yasmādayaṃ dharmo deśitaḥ, tasmād yatpūrvaṃmuktaṃ pareṇa-
body.translated_text: and since there is no imagined analogy with a seed-continuum, <s>saṃsāra</s>, differentiated by the divisions of various destinies, births, modes of origin, and elements, proceeding through the five destinies, is also

children.translated_text: 'If <s>karma</s> persists until the time of ripening, it would become permanent;

children.text: niruddhaṃ cenniruddhaṃ sat kiṃ phalaṃ janayiṣyati || iti,
children.translated_text: and if it has ceased, having ceased, what fruit will it produce?' //

body.text: tadasmatpakṣe nopapadyate iti | tasmādasmābhirupavarṇitakalpanaiva nyāyyā iti || 20 ||
body.translated_text: — this [objection] does not apply in our position. Therefore the formulation described by us alone is correct. // 20 //

body.text: atrocyate- kimiha bhavanto gandharvanagaraprākārapatanātiśaṅkitayā atīvodvignāḥ tatparirakṣāpariśramāyāsamāpannāḥ, ye nāma yūyaṃ karmaṇyanupapadyamāne tatphalanimittaṃ vipravadadhvam? yadi hi karmaṇaḥ svarūpeṇaivotpādaḥ syāt, tasya āvipākamavasthānānnityatvaṃ syāt, vināśāducchedaḥ syāt | yadā tu karma naivotpadyate svabhāvaśūnyatvāt, tadā tasya kuto 'vasthānaṃ vināśo vā, yata eṣā cintā syāt? atrāha-
body.translated_text: Here it is replied: why are you so exceedingly alarmed, as if fearing the collapse of the walls of a city of <s>Gandharvas</s> (a mirage-city), and exerting yourselves so much to protect them?

body.text: karma notpadyate kasmāt
body.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> does not arise — why?

body.text: ācārya āha-
body.translated_text: The <s>Ācārya</s> says:

body.text: niḥsvabhāvaṃ yatastataḥ |
body.translated_text: Because it is without own-nature.

body.text: yasmānniḥsvabhāvaṃ karma tasmānnotpadyate | yadi khalvevaṃ niḥsvabhāvatvātkarma notpadyate, tat kathamevamuktaṃ bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: Since <s>karma</s> is without own-nature, therefore it does not arise. But if <s>karma</s> does not arise because of being without own-nature, then how [do you interpret the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s statement]:

children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even after hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām || iti?
children.translated_text: when they meet with the right conditions and time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings.' //?

body.text: ucyate-
body.translated_text: It is replied:

body.text: yasmācca tadanutpannaṃ na tasmādvipraṇaśyati || 21 ||
body.translated_text: And since that [<s>karma</s>] has not arisen, therefore it does not perish. // 21 //

body.text: ityevaṃ bhagavato 'bhiprāya iti | ato nāyamasmākaṃ bādhako vidhiriti |21 ||
body.translated_text: This is the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s intent. Therefore this scripture does not contradict us. // 21 //

body.text: avaśyaṃ caitadevaṃ vijñeyam- niḥsvabhāvaṃ karmeti | anyathā hi-
body.translated_text: And this must certainly be understood in this way — that <s>karma</s> is without own-nature. For otherwise —

children.translated_text: If <s>karma</s> existed by its own nature, it would undoubtedly be permanent;

children.text: akṛtaṃ ca bhavetkarma kriyate na hi śāśvatam || 22 ||
children.translated_text: and <s>karma</s> would be unperformed — for what is permanent is not performed. // 22 //

body.text: yadi hi karma svabhāvataḥ syāt, muktasaṃśayaṃ tacchāśvataṃ syāt, svabhāvasyānyathābhāvābhāvāt | tataśca akṛtameva karma bhavet | kartuḥ svatantrasya kriyayā yadīpsitatamaṃ tatkarma | etacca na yujyate | kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmāt kriyate na hi śāśvatam | śāśvataṃ hi nāma tad yadvidyamānasattākam | yacca vidyamānaṃ tasya karaṇānupapatteḥ tannaiva kāraṇamapekṣata iti || 22 ||
body.translated_text: For if <s>karma</s> existed by its own nature, it would undoubtedly be permanent, since own-nature cannot become otherwise. And then

body.text: śubhāśubhe karmaṇi akṛta eva sakalasya lokasya vipāko yasmāt, tataśca-
body.translated_text: since for wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s>, ripening would exist for the entire world even without being performed — therefore:

children.translated_text: There would be the fear of encountering [the fruit of] what was not done, if <s>karma</s> were unperformed;
and the fault of not living the holy life would follow. // 23 //

body.text: yadi hi akṛtaṃ karma bhavet, tadā akṛtābhyāgamabhayaṃ syāt | yenāpi hi prāṇātipātādikaṃ na kṛtam, tasyāpi akṛtamapi sat tat karma astyeveti tenāpyasya saṃbandhādakṛtābhyāgamabhayaṃ syāt | abrahmacaryavāsaśca tatra pakṣe prāpnoti | kiṃ kāraṇam? pariśuddhabrahmacaryavāsānna kasyacinnirvāṇena bhavitavyaṃ syāt || 23 ||
body.translated_text: For if <s>karma</s> were unperformed [yet bearing fruit], then there would be the fear of encountering [the fruit of] what was not done. Even one who has not committed killing of living beings and so forth

body.text: kiṃ cātaḥ?
body.translated_text: What further follows from this?

children.text: vyavahārā virudhyante sarva eva na saṃśayaḥ |
children.translated_text: All conventional dealings would be contradicted, without doubt;
and even the distinction between one who has done merit and one who has done sin would not be justified. // 24 //

body.text: ye hi ete kṛṣivāṇijyagorakṣādayaḥ kriyārambhāḥ phalārthamārabhyante, teṣāṃ sarveṣāmakṛtānāmeva vidyamānatvāt prārambhavaiyarthyaṃ syāt | ghaṭaṃ kuru, paṭaṃ kuru, ityevamādayaśca sarva eva laukikavyavahārā virudhyante, ghaṭādīnāṃ sarveṣāmeva vidyamānatvāt | puṇyakṛdayam, pāpakṛdayam, iti ca pravibhāgo na prāpnoti, ubhayorapi puṇyapāpakṛtoḥ akṛtayorapi puṇyapāpayoḥ pratyekaṃ vidyamānatvāt || 24 ||
body.translated_text: For all these enterprises of agriculture, commerce, cattle-herding, and so forth, which are undertaken for the sake of their results — all of them, even though unperformed, would be known [to bear fruit].

body.text: kiṃ ca-
body.translated_text: What is more —

children.translated_text: That [<s>karma</s>] whose fruit has [already] ripened would ripen again;
since <s>karma</s> is established [as permanent], if it were inherent. // 25 //

body.text: vipakvavipākasyāpi karmaṇaḥ punarvipākadānamāpadyate svarūpādapracyutatvāt, avipakvavipākāvasthāyāmiva | tadevaṃ yadi karma svābhāvikamiti manyase, yasmāt tatkarma vyavasthitamasti tasmānniḥsaṃśayaṃ yathopavarṇitā doṣāḥ prāpnuvanti sasvabhāvatve | tasmānniḥsvabhāvaṃ karma, yataśca niḥsvabhāvaṃ karma, tasmācchāśvatocchedadarśanaprasaṅgo naivāsmākamevaṃ vyācakṣamāṇānāmāpadyate iti || 25 ||
body.translated_text: Even <s>karma</s> whose fruit has ripened would incur the giving of fruit again, since it has not fallen from its own nature — just as in the state when the fruit has not ripened.

body.text: atrāha- vidyata eva svabhāvataḥ karma, tatkāraṇasadbhāvāt | iha yannāsti, na tasya kāraṇamasti [kūrma] romakūpaprāvārasyeva | asti ca karmaṇaḥ kāraṇaṃ kleśāḥ | avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ, ..... upādānapratyayo bhavaḥ, iti vacanāt | tasmādvidyata eva karma svabhāvataḥ iti | ucyate | ayuktameva | kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmāt-
body.translated_text: To this one says: <s>karma</s> does indeed exist by its own nature, because of the existence of its cause. For what does not exist has no cause — like [the hair of] a tortoise.

children.text: karma kleśātmakaṃ cedaṃ te ca kleśā na tattvataḥ |
children.translated_text: If this <s>karma</s> is of the nature of afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>), those afflictions do not exist in reality.

children.text: na cette tattvataḥ kleśāḥ karma syāttattvataḥ katham || 26 ||
children.translated_text: If the afflictions do not exist in reality, how will <s>karma</s> exist in reality? // 26 //

body.text: ihedaṃ karma kleśātmakaṃ kleśahetukam | te ca kleśāstattvato na santi | vakṣyati hi-
body.translated_text: Here, this <s>karma</s> is of the nature of afflictions, having afflictions as its cause. And those afflictions do not exist in reality. For he will say:

body.text:
śubhāśubhaviparyāsān saṃbhavanti pratītya ye |
te svabhāvānna vidyante tasmātkleśā na tattvataḥ || iti |
body.translated_text: 'Those [afflictions] which arise dependent on the perversions of good and bad — they do not exist by their own nature; therefore the afflictions do not exist in reality.' //

body.text: tadevaṃ tāvat na tattvataḥ kleśāḥ, taddhetukaṃ karma tadānīṃ kutastattvato bhaviṣyati? tasmānnāsti karma svabhāvataḥ || 26 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, when the afflictions do not exist in reality, then <s>karma</s> which has them as its cause — how will it exist in reality at that time? Therefore <s>karma</s> does not exist in reality.

body.text: atrāha- vidyanta eva kleśā karmāṇi ca, tatkāryasadbhāvāt | iha hi kleśakarmaṇāṃ dehākhyaṃ kāryamupalabhyate | yasya ca kāryamupalabhyate tadasti, avidyamānasya khapuṣpādeḥ kāryādarśanāt iti | ucyate | syuḥ kleśāḥ karmāṇi ca, yadi tatkāryaṃ dehā vidyeran | na tu vidyante ityāha-
body.translated_text: To this one says: afflictions and <s>karma</s> do indeed exist, because their effect exists. For the effect of afflictions and <s>karma</s> — namely, the body — is apprehended.

children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> and afflictions are declared to be the conditions for bodies.

children.text: karma kleśāśca te śūnyā yadi deheṣu kā kathā || 27 ||
children.translated_text: If <s>karma</s> and afflictions are empty, what can be said about bodies? // 27 //

body.text: yathā karma kleśāśca śūnyāḥ, tathā pratipāditam | tataśca karma kleśā yadā na santi, tadā tatkāryāṇāṃ dehānāmasattve kā kathā bhaviṣyati? nāstitvaṃ teṣāṃ pūrvameva siddhaṃ yasmāt, tasmānnānna kaścidvaktavyaviśeṣo 'stītyabhiprāyaḥ || 27 ||
body.translated_text: That <s>karma</s> and afflictions are empty — this has been demonstrated. And therefore, when <s>karma</s> and afflictions do not exist, then of bodies which are their effects,

body.text: atrāha- vidyata eva svabhāvataḥ karma, tatphalabhoktṛsadbhāvāt | yannāsti, na tasya phalopabhoktāsti, tadyathā gaganacūtaphalasyeti | asti ca karmaṇaḥ phalopabhoktā-
body.translated_text: To this one says: <s>karma</s> does indeed exist by its own nature, because of the existence of one who experiences its fruit. What does not exist has no one who experiences its fruit.

children.translated_text: The being, enveloped by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), fettered by <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) —

children.text: sa bhoktā sa ca na karturanyo na ca sa eva saḥ || 28 ||
children.translated_text: he is the experiencer, and he is neither other than the doer nor identical with him. // 28 //

body.text: tatra avidyā ajñānaṃ tamaḥ saṃmoha iti paryāyāḥ | avidyayā nivṛtaśchāditaḥ | pāñcagatikasaṃsāre punaḥ punarjāyata iti jantuḥ | sattvaḥ pudgalaḥ prāṇīti tasyaiva paryāyāḥ | tṛṣṇā rāgaḥ saktirvisaktiśceti paryāyāḥ | saṃyojanaṃ bandhanam | tṛṣṇā saṃyojanamasyeti tṛṣṇāsaṃyojanaḥ tṛṣṇābandhana ityarthaḥ | yathoktaṃ sūtre- avidyānivṛtāḥ sattvāstṛṣṇāsaṃyojanāḥ iti | atha ca punaridaṃ pāpaṃ karma svayameva kṛtam, asya svayameva vipākaḥ pratyanubhavitavyaḥ iti vacanāt | sa ca bhoktā karmaphalasya | sa ca na karturanyaḥ, na ca sa eva saḥ | tattvānyatvāvācyatvāt | tasmāt phalopabhoktṛsadbhāvādastyeva karmeti || 28 ||
body.translated_text: Here, <s>avidyā</s> — ignorance, darkness, and delusion are its synonyms. 'Enveloped by <s>avidyā</s>' means covered [by it]. In the <s>saṃsāra</s> of the five destinies, again

body.text: atrocyate- syātkarmaṇaḥ kartā karmaphalasya copabhoktā yadi karmaiva syāt | na tvasti | kathaṃ kṛtvā?
body.translated_text: Here it is replied: there would be a doer of <s>karma</s> and an experiencer of <s>karma</s>'s fruit, if <s>karma</s> itself were to exist. But it does not. How so?

children.translated_text: Neither arisen from conditions, nor arisen without conditions —
since this <s>karma</s> does not exist, therefore the doer too does not exist. // 29 //

children.text: karma cennāsti kartā ca kutaḥ syātkarmajaṃ phalam |
children.translated_text: If <s>karma</s> does not exist, and the doer does not exist, whence would the fruit born of <s>karma</s> come?

children.text: asatyatha phale bhoktā kuta eva bhaviṣyati || 30 ||
children.translated_text: And if the fruit does not exist, whence will the experiencer come to be? // 30 //

body.text: yadi karma nāma kiṃcitsyāt, tat pratyayasamutpannaṃ vā bhavet, apratyayasamutpannaṃ vā? yadi tāvat pratyayasamutpannamiṣyate, tanna yuktam, pratyayaparīkṣāyāmuktadoṣatvāt | atha apratyayajanitaṃ nirhetukam, tadapi- hetāvasati kāryaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ ca ityādinā karmakārakaparīkṣāyāṃ vistareṇa pratipāditam | yataścaivaṃ pratyayasamutpannaṃ vā apratyayasamutpannaṃ vā karmedaṃ na saṃbhavati, tasmādasya karmaṇaḥ kartāpi na saṃbhavati | yadā caivaṃ karma ca kartā ca nāsti, tadā nirhetukaṃ karmajaṃ phalaṃ kuto bhaviṣyatīti, asati ca phale kuta eva phalabhoktā bhaviṣyatīti, sarvametat svabhāvato 'saṃvidyamānameveti vijñeyam ||
body.translated_text: If something called <s>karma</s> were to exist, it would either be arisen from conditions or arisen without conditions. If it is arisen from conditions,

body.text: atrāha- yadi evaṃ naiḥsvābhāvyaṃ bhāvānāṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ bhavati, yattarhi etaduktaṃ bhagavatā- svayaṃ kṛtasya karmaṇaḥ svayameva vipākaḥ pratyanubhavitavyaḥ iti, tadetat sarvamamunā nyāyena apākṛtaṃ bhavati | karmaphalāpavādācca pradhānanāstiko bhavāniti | ucyate | na vayaṃ nāstikāḥ | astitvanāstitvadvayavādanirāsena tu vayaṃ nirvāṇapuragāminamadvayapathaṃ vidyotayāmaḥ | na ca karmakartṛphalādikaṃ nāstīti brūma, kiṃ tarhi niḥsvabhāvametaditi vyavasthāpayāmaḥ | atha manyase- niḥsvabhāvānāṃ bhāvānāṃ vyāpārakaraṇānupapatteḥ tadavastha eva doṣa iti, etadapi nāsti | sasvabhāvānāmeva vyāpārādarśanāt | niḥsvabhāvānāmeva vyāpāradarśanāt | tathāhi niḥsvabhāvā eva santo ghaṭādayaḥ loke svakāryakṛt upalabhyante || 30 ||
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: If the absence of inherent nature of entities has been established in this way, then what the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said — 'One must experience the fruit of self-made <s>karma</s> oneself' — all of this would be invalidated by the above reasoning. And since you deny <s>karma</s> and its fruit, you would be a great nihilist. [Reply:] We are not nihilists. Rather, by eliminating the dual doctrine of existence and non-existence, we illuminate the non-dual path leading to the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. And we do not say that <s>karma</s>, the agent, the fruit, and so forth do not exist; rather, we establish that these are without inherent nature. Now, if you think: 'the fault remains as before, since for entities without inherent nature, the performance of activity is impossible' — this too is not so. Because activity is not observed for things that have inherent nature; activity is observed precisely for things that are without inherent nature. For thus, pots and the like, being without inherent nature, are observed in the world to accomplish their respective functions. // 30 //

body.text: api ca | amuṣmād dṛṣṭāntāt spaṣṭatarādayamartho 'vasīyatām-
body.translated_text: Moreover, let this matter be ascertained from this even more vivid example:

children.translated_text: Just as the Teacher, through the power of supernatural accomplishment (<s>ṛddhisaṃpad</s>), creates a magical creation (<s>nirmitaka</s>), /

children.text: nirmito nirmimītānyaṃ sa ca nirmitakaḥ punaḥ || 31 ||
children.translated_text: and that created being in turn creates another — that too is a magical creation. // 31 //

body.text: tadyathā- ekaṃ nirmitakaṃ śāstā buddho bhagavān ṛddhisaṃpadā ṛddhiprabhāveṇa nirmimīta, sa cāpi nirmitakaḥ punaḥ yo 'yaṃ buddhena bhagavatā nirmitaḥ, sa punarbhūyo 'nyamaparaṃ nirmitakaṃ nirmimīta | tatra ya eṣa nirmitakaḥ aparasya nirmitakasya nirmātā, sa śūnyaḥ niḥsvabhāvaḥ, tathāgatasvabhāvarahita ityarthaḥ | yaścāyamaparo nirmitakaḥ, yonirmitakena nirmitaḥ, asāvapi śūnyo nisvabhāvaḥ, tathāgatasvabhāvarahita ityarthaḥ | yathātra niḥsvabhāvānāṃ nisvabhāvakāryakṛttvaṃ karmakartṛvyapadeśaśca bhavati,
body.translated_text: For example: the Teacher, the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>, by the power of supernatural accomplishment, creates one magical being. And that magical being — the one created by the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s> — in turn creates yet another magical being. Therein, this magical being that is the creator of the other magical being is empty, without inherent nature — meaning devoid of the inherent nature of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And this other magical being that was created by the [first] magical being — that too is empty, without inherent nature — meaning devoid of the inherent nature of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Just as here there is, for those without inherent nature, the accomplishment of functions by those without inherent nature, and the designation of <s>karma</s> and agent —

children.text: tathā nirmitakākāraḥ kartā karma ca tatkṛtam |
children.translated_text: so too the agent has the form of a magical creation, and the <s>karma</s> performed by him [is likewise]. /
Just as one magical creation creates another — so should it be understood. // 32 //

body.text: yo hyatra karmaṇaḥ kartā sa nirmitakākāraḥ svabhāvaśūnyaḥ | tena ca svabhāvaśūnyena svatantrakartrā yat kiṃcit karma kriyate, tadapi svabhāvaśūnyam | tadyathā nirmitakena anyo nirmitako nirmitaḥ tathā veditavyam | yathoktamāgame-
body.translated_text: For here, the agent of <s>karma</s> has the form of a magical creation — empty of inherent nature. And whatever <s>karma</s> is performed by this agent, who is empty of inherent nature and autonomous — that too is empty of inherent nature. Just as one magical being creates another magical being — so should it be understood. As stated in the <s>Āgama</s>:

children.translated_text: When one [magical creation] speaks, all the magical creations speak; /
and when one falls silent, all indeed fall silent. //

body.text: tasmādadvayavādināṃ mādhyamikānāṃ kuto mithyādarśanam? uktaṃ ca āryasamādhirāje-
body.translated_text: Therefore, how could there be a false view for the <s>Mādhyamikas</s>, who are proponents of non-duality? And it is said in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>:

children.text: yada sugatu kathāṃ katheti nātho vīthigatān manujān kṛpāyamānaḥ |
children.translated_text: When the <s>Sugata</s>, the Protector, teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, having compassion for people in the streets, /

children.text: nirmita jinu tatra nirminitva vicarati teṣu praṇītabuddhadharmān ||
children.translated_text: he creates a <s>Jina</s>-creation there, and [that creation] goes about [teaching] to them the excellent <s>Buddhadharmas</s>. //

body.text: prāṇiśatasahasra taṃ śruṇitvā praṇidadhayiṃsu varāgrabuddhajñāne |
body.translated_text: Hundreds of thousands of beings, having heard that, set their aspirations upon the supreme, foremost <s>Buddhajñāna</s> (Buddha-knowledge). /

body.text: kada vaya labhi jñānamevarūpaṃ āśaya jñātva jino 'sya vyākaroti ||
body.translated_text: When shall we obtain such knowledge? — knowing [their] intention, the <s>Jina</s> gives them the prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>). //

children.text: raśmi śatasahasra aprameyān avasiri pādatalehi dharmarājā |
children.translated_text: Innumerable hundreds of thousands of rays the <s>Dharma</s>-king emits from the soles of his feet; /

children.text: sarvi niraya śītalā bhavanti dukhamapanīya sukhaṃ ca vedayanti ||
children.translated_text: all the hells become cool, and [beings there], having their suffering removed, experience happiness. //

body.text: dharma daśabalaprabhāṣite 'tra marumanujāna viśuddha bhoti cakṣuḥ |
body.translated_text: In the <s>Dharma</s> proclaimed by the Ten-Powered One, the eye of <s>devas</s> and humans becomes purified. /

body.text: ityādi |
body.translated_text: And so forth.

children.text: keci spṛha janenti tatra kāle parama acintya tehi labdhalābhā |
children.translated_text: Some at that time generate aspiration — supreme, inconceivable, by them a great gain was obtained, /

children.text: yehi jinu nimantrito narendro na ca pariyanta teṣu dakṣiṇāyā ||
children.translated_text: by whom the <s>Jina</s>, the Lord of Men, was invited — and there is no limit to their gift (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>). //

body.text: ityādi vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: And so forth, in detail. //

body.text: tathā āryavimalakīrtinirdeśe-
body.translated_text: Likewise in the noble <s>Vimalakīrtinirdeśa</s>:

body.text: tannirmitabodhisattvena gandhasugandhāyāṃ lokadhātau samantabhadratathāgatopabhuktaśeṣaṃ bhojanamānītaṃ nānāvyañjanakhādyādisaṃprayuktaṃ pṛthakpṛthagvividharasamekabhojanena sarvaṃ tacchrāvakabodhisattvasaṃgharājarājāmātyapurohitāntaḥ puradauvārikasārthavāhādijanapadaṃ saṃtarpya prītyākāraṃ nāma mahāsamādhiṃ lambhayāmāsa | iti ||
body.translated_text: That <s>Bodhisattva</s> created by magical transformation brought from the world-system <s>Gandhasugandhā</s> the food left over after being enjoyed by the <s>Tathāgata Samantabhadra</s>, endowed with various condiments, eatables, and the like, and with a single serving of various tastes, satisfied the entire assemblage of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, kings, royal ministers, chief priests, doorkeepers of the inner city, caravan leaders, and country folk, and caused them to attain the great <s>samādhi</s> named 'Appearance of Joy' (<s>Prītyākāra</s>). //

body.text: vinaye ca paṭhayate-
body.translated_text: And it is read in the <s>Vinaya</s>:

body.text: pāpabhikṣurapratirūpako bhagavatā bhikṣurabhinirmitaḥ | tadvacanena śīlavato 'pi viśuddhipratijñāsaṃvāsaḥ prajñaptaḥ iti || 32 ||
body.translated_text: A monk who was a counterfeit of the evil monk was magically created by the <s>Bhagavān</s>. By his [the created monk's] word, the communal living with declaration of purity was prescribed even for one of good conduct. // 32 //

body.text: na ca kevalaṃ nirmāṇadṛṣṭāntena naiḥsvabhāvyadarśanamupapadyamānarūpam, api ca amībhyo dṛṣṭāntebhyaḥ sphuṭaṃ naiḥsvabhāvyaṃ bhāvānāṃ pratīyatāmiti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And the view of absence of inherent nature is established not only through the example of magical creation, but also — [<s>Nāgārjuna</s>], demonstrating that the absence of inherent nature of entities should be clearly understood from these further examples as well, says:

children.text: kleśāḥ karmāṇi dehāśca kartāraśca phalāni ca |
children.translated_text: Afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>), <s>karmas</s>, bodies, agents, and fruits — /
are like a <s>gandharva</s>-city in form, resembling a mirage and a dream. // 33 //

body.text: tatra kleśā rāgādayaḥ, kliśnanti sattvacittasaṃtānānīti kṛtvā | karmāṇi kuśalākuśalāneñjyāni | dehāḥ śarīrāṇi | kartāraḥ ātmānaḥ | phalāni vipākādhipatyaniṣyandādīni | ta ete kleśādayo 'rthāḥ gandharvanagarādivanniḥsvabhāvāḥ veditavyāḥ | tasmānmādhyamikānāmeva bhāvānāṃ svabhāvānabhyupagamācchāśvatocchedadarśanadvayaprasaṅgo nāstīti vijñeyam ||
body.translated_text: Therein, afflictions are passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the rest — because they afflict the mental continua of beings. <s>Karmas</s> are meritorious, demeritorious, and imperturbable. Bodies are physical forms. Agents are selves. Fruits are the ripening (<s>vipāka</s>), the dominant (<s>adhipatya</s>), the outflow (<s>niṣyanda</s>), and so forth. These things — afflictions and the rest — should be understood as without inherent nature, like a <s>gandharva</s>-city and the rest. Therefore, it should be understood that only for the <s>Mādhyamikas</s>, who do not accept the inherent nature of entities, is there no consequence of the dual view of eternalism and annihilationism. //

body.text: atra ca karmaphalasaṃbandhavicāre kucodyaśeṣākṣepaparihāro madhyamakāvatārādvistareṇāvaseyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: And regarding the investigation of the relationship between <s>karma</s> and its fruit, the resolution of the remaining subtle objections should be understood in detail from the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s>. //

body.text: yathoktamāryaratnakūṭasūtre-
body.translated_text: As stated in the noble <s>Ratnakūṭa Sūtra</s>:

body.text: pañca ca bhikṣuśatāni dhyānalābhīni utthāyāsanebhyaḥ prakrāntāni imāṃ gambhīrāṃ dharmadeśanāmanavabudhyamānāni anavataranti anavagāhamānāni anadhimucyamānāni | bhagavānāha- tathā hyete kāśyapa bhikṣavaḥ ābhimānikāḥ imāmanāsravāṃ śīlaviśuddhiṃ nāvataranti nāvagāhante nādhimucyante uttrasyanti saṃtrasyanti saṃtrāsamāpadyante | gambhīraḥ kāśyapa gāthābhinirhāro gambhīrā ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ bodhiḥ | sā na śakyā anavaropitakuśalamūlaiḥ sattvaiḥ pāpamitraparigṛhītairanadhimuktibahulairadhimoktum | api ca | etāni kāśyapa pañca bhikṣuśatāni kāśyapasya tathāgatasya pravacane 'nyatīrthikaśrāvakā abhūvan | taireva tasya kāśyapasya tathāgatasyāntikādupālambhābhiprāyaireṣā dharmadeśanā śrutā | śrutvā ca ekacittaprasādo labdhaḥ | evaṃtairvāg bhāṣitā- āścaryaṃ yāvat madhurapriyamāṇī kāśyapastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha iti | ta etenaikacittaprasādena pratilabdhena kālagatāḥ trāyastriṃśeṣu deveṣūpapannāḥ | te tataścyutāḥ samānāḥ ihopapannāḥ | tenaiva ca hetunā iha mama śāsane pravrajitāḥ | tānyetāni kāśyapa pañca bhikṣuśatāni dṛṣṭipraskandhāni imāṃ gambhīrāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ nāvataranti nāvagāhante nādhimucyante uttrasyanti saṃtrasyanti saṃtrāsamāpadyante kṛtaṃ punareṣāmanayā dharmadeśanayā parikarma | na bhūyo durgativinipātaṃ gamiṣyanti | ebhireva ca skandhaiḥ parinirvāsyanti ||
body.translated_text: And five hundred monks who had attained <s>dhyāna</s> rose from their seats and departed, not comprehending this profound <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, not entering into it, not fathoming it, not being receptive to it. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Thus indeed, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, these monks are conceited (<s>ābhimānika</s>). They do not enter into, do not fathom, do not embrace this stainless purity of moral discipline; they are frightened, terrified, and fall into terror. Profound, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is the purport of the verses, and profound is the awakening of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>. It cannot be embraced by beings who have not planted roots of merit, who are associated with evil friends, and who are deficient in faith. Moreover, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, these five hundred monks were, in the dispensation of the <s>Tathāgata Kāśyapa</s>, disciples of other sects. By them, in the presence of that <s>Tathāgata Kāśyapa</s>, this <s>Dharma</s>-teaching was heard with the intention of finding fault. And having heard it, they obtained a single moment of faith. They uttered these words: "How wonderful! How sweet and pleasing is <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One!" By this single moment of faith so obtained, they died and were reborn among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods. Having fallen from there, they were reborn here. And by that very cause, they have gone forth in my dispensation here. These five hundred monks, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are prone to [wrong] views. They do not enter into, do not fathom, do not embrace this profound <s>Dharma</s>-teaching; they are frightened, terrified, and fall into terror. Yet this <s>Dharma</s>-teaching has already served as their preparation. They will no longer go to the lower realms of misfortune. And with these very <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) they will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimāmantrayate sma- gaccha subhūte, etān bhikṣūn saṃjñapatha | subhūtirāha- bhagavata eva tāvadete bhāṣitaṃ vilomayanti, kaḥ punarvādo mama? atha bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ yena mārgeṇaite bhikṣāvo gacchanti sma, tasmin mārge drau bhikṣū nirmimīte sma | atha tāni pañca bhikṣuśatāni yena mārgeṇa tau dvau bhikṣū nirmitakau tenopasaṃkrāmanti sma | upasaṃkramya etadavocan- kutra āyuṣmantau gamiṣyathaḥ? tāvavocatām- gamiṣyāva āvāmaraṇyāyataneṣu | tatra dhyānasukhasaṃsparśavihārairvihariṣyāvaḥ || ..... tānyapi pañca bhikṣuśatānyetadavocan- vayamapyāyuṣmantau bhagavato dharmadeśanāṃ nāvatarāmo nāvagāhāmahe nādhimucyāmahe uttrasyāmaḥ saṃtrasyāmaḥ saṃtrāsamāpadyāmahe | tena vayamaraṇyāyataneṣu dhyānasukhasaṃsparśavihārairvihariṣyāma iti | nirmitakāvavocatām- tena hi āyuṣmantaḥ saṃgāsyāmo na vivadiṣyāmaḥ | avivādaparamo hi śramaṇadharmaḥ | yadidamāyuṣmanta ucyate parinirvāṇamiti, katamaḥ sa dharmo yaḥ parinirvāsyati? kaścitpunaratra kāyaḥ ātmā vā sattvo vā jīvo vā janturvā poṣo vā puruṣo vā pudgalo vā manujo vā mānavo va, yaḥ parinirvāsyati? kasya vā kṣayāt parinirvāṇam? te 'vocan rāgadveṣamohakṣayāt parinirvāṇam | nirmitakāvavocatām- kiṃ punarāyuṣmatāṃ saṃvidyante rāgadveṣamohā yān kṣayiṣyatha? te 'vocan- na te adhyātmaṃ na bahirdhā nobhayamantareṇopalabhyante, nāpi te aparikalpitā utpadyante .... |
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'Go, <s>Subhūti</s>, and admonish those monks.' <s>Subhūti</s> replied: 'They reject even the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s own words — what need to speak of mine?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> at that moment, on the path by which those monks were going, magically created two monks. Then those five hundred monks approached the path where the two magical monks were, and having approached, said: 'Where will you go, Venerables?' They replied: 'We will go to forest hermitages. There we shall dwell enjoying the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s>.' ... Those five hundred monks also said: 'We too, Venerables, do not enter into, do not fathom, do not embrace the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>Dharma</s>-teaching; we are frightened, terrified, and fall into terror. Therefore we shall dwell in forest hermitages enjoying the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s>.' The magical monks replied: 'Then, Venerables, let us dwell together and not quarrel. For the highest quality of an ascetic's practice is non-dispute. That which, Venerables, is called <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — which <s>dharma</s> is it that will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>? Is there here any body, or self, or being, or life-force, or creature, or nurture, or person, or individual, or human, or youth, that will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>? Or through whose destruction is there <s>parinirvāṇa</s>?' They said: 'Through the destruction of passion, hatred, and delusion there is <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.' The magical monks replied: 'Do you, Venerables, have passion, hatred, and delusion that you will destroy?' They said: 'They are found neither internally, nor externally, nor in between — nor do they, being unimagined, arise...'

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacitāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau karmaphalaparīkṣā nāma saptadaśamaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, 'Examination of <s>Karma</s> and Fruit' (<s>Karmaphalaparīkṣā</s>), in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary composed by the venerable <s>Ācārya Candrakīrti</s>. //

body.text:
18
ātmaparīkṣā aṣṭādaśamaṃ prakaraṇam |
body.translated_text:
18
'Examination of the Self' (<s>Ātmaparīkṣā</s>), the eighteenth chapter.

body.text: atrāha- yadi kleśāḥ karmāṇi ca dehāśca kartāraśca phalāni ca sarvametanna tattvam, kevalaṃtu gandharvanagarādivadattatvameva sat tattvākāreṇa pratibhāsate bālānām, kiṃ punaratra tattvam, kathaṃ vā tattvasyāvatāraḥ iti? ucyate | ādhyātmikabāhyāśeṣavastvanupalambhena adhyātmaṃ bahiśca yaḥ sarvathā ahaṃkāramamakāraparikṣayaḥ, idamatra tattvam | tattvāvatāraḥ punaḥ-
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: If afflictions, <s>karmas</s>, bodies, agents, and fruits — all of this is not reality, but, like a <s>gandharva</s>-city and the like, merely non-reality that appears in the form of reality to the foolish — then what is reality here, and how does one enter into reality? [Reply:] Through the non-apprehension of all internal and external things without exception — the complete dissolution of the sense of 'I' (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) and 'mine' (<s>mamakāra</s>) with respect to what is internal and external in every way — this is reality here. As for entering into reality:

children.translated_text: Seeing with wisdom all the afflictions and faults that arise from the view of the real body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), /

children.text: ātmānamasyā viṣayaṃ ca buddhā yogī karotyātmaniṣedhameva ||
children.translated_text: and [seeing] the self as the object of this [view] — the yogin undertakes the very negation of the self. //

body.text: ityādinā madhyamakāvatārādvistareṇāvaseyaḥ | kāyadṛṣṭimūlakameva saṃsāramanupaśyan ātmānupalambhācca satkāyadṛṣṭiprahāṇaṃ tatprahāṇācca sarvakleśavyāvṛttiṃ samanupaśyan prathamataramātmānamevopaparīkṣate, ko 'yamātmā nāmeti, yo 'haṃkāraviṣayaḥ | sa cāyamahaṃkārasya viṣayaḥ parikalpyamānaḥ skandhasvabhāvo vā bhavetskandhavyatirikto vā? ādhārādheyatadvatpakṣāṇāmapi ekatvānyatvapakṣe eva antarbhāvāt saṃkṣepeṇaiva ca vivakṣitatvādekatvānyatvapakṣadvayapratiṣedhenaiva ātmaniṣedhamārabdhukāma ācārya āha-
body.translated_text: And so forth — this should be understood in detail from the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s>. Seeing that <s>saṃsāra</s> has the view of the real body as its root, and seeing that through the non-apprehension of the self there is the abandonment of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, and through its abandonment there is the cessation of all afflictions — one first of all examines the self: 'What is this thing called the self?' — which is the object of the sense of 'I.' And this object of the sense of 'I,' when imagined, would either be of the nature of the <s>skandhas</s> or different from the <s>skandhas</s>. Since the positions of container-contained and possessor-possessed are subsumed under the positions of identity and otherness, and since [the author] wishes to be concise, the <s>Ācārya</s>, wishing to undertake the negation of the self through the negation of just these two positions of identity and otherness, says:

children.translated_text: If the self were the <s>skandhas</s>, it would be subject to arising and passing away. /
If it were other than the <s>skandhas</s>, it would have the characteristic of being non-<s>skandha</s>. // 1 //

body.text: kimartha punaranyatra tathāgataparīkṣāyāmagnīndhanaparīkṣāyāṃ ca pañca pañca pakṣā upanyastāḥ, iha tu punaḥ pakṣadvayameveti? ucyate | yenaiva tatra prakaraṇadvaye pañca pañca pakṣā nirdiṣṭāḥ, ata eva anyatra nirdiṣṭatvānna punariha nirdiśyante | saṃkṣepeṇa tu pakṣadvayamupanyasyate iti ||
body.translated_text: Why, then, were five positions each set forth elsewhere in the Examination of the <s>Tathāgata</s> and in the Examination of Fire and Fuel, while here only two positions [are examined]? [Reply:] Precisely because those five positions each were set forth in those two other chapters, they are not set forth here again, since they have already been stated elsewhere. But in brief, only two positions are set forth. //

body.text: tatra yadi skandhā ātmeti parikalpyate, tadā udayavyayabhāg utpādī ca vināśī ca ātmā prāpnoti, skandhānāmudayavyayabhāktvāt | na caivamiṣyate, ātmāneka[tva]doṣaprasaṅgāt vakṣyati hi-
body.translated_text: In this regard, if the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) are conceived as the self, then the self would be subject to arising and passing away, being one that arises and perishes — since the <s>skandhas</s> are subject to arising and passing away. And this is not accepted, because of the consequence of the fault of the self having multiple [selves]. For it will be said —

body.text:
nāpyabhūtvā samutpanno doṣo hyatra prasajyate |
kṛtako vā bhavedātmā saṃbhūto vāpyahetukaḥ || iti |
body.translated_text:
'Nor has it arisen having not existed before — for the fault follows here: /
either the self would be fabricated, or it would have arisen without a cause.' //

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise —

body.text:
na copādānamevātmā vyeti tatsamudeti ca |
kathaṃ hi nāmopādānamupādātā bhaviṣyati || iti |
body.translated_text:
'And the self is not the <s>upādāna</s> (appropriation) itself — it perishes and arises again. /
How could the appropriation become the appropriator?' //

body.text: kiṃ ca-
body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: skandhā ātmā cedatastadbahutvāt ātmānaḥ syuste 'pi bhūyāṃsa eva |
children.translated_text: If the <s>skandhas</s> were the self, then, since they are many, the selves would be many — indeed very numerous. /

children.text: dravyaṃ cātmā prāpnuyāttādṛśaśca dravye vṛttau vaiparītye ca na syāt ||
children.translated_text: And the self would be a substance; and one of such a kind — there would be no operation regarding substance, nor would there be in the opposite case. //

children.text: ātmocchedo nirvṛtau syādavaśyaṃ nāśotpādau nirvṛteḥ prāk kṣaṇeṣu |
children.translated_text: The annihilation of the self at <s>nirvāṇa</s> would necessarily follow; arising and destruction in the moments prior to <s>nirvāṇa</s> [would also follow]. /
From the destruction of the agent, there would be the very non-existence of its fruit; and one person would enjoy the action accumulated by another. //

body.text: ityādinā madhyamakāvatāre vistareṇa vihitavicārādapi pakṣo boddhavya iti neha punarvistaraprapañca ārabhyate ||
body.translated_text: — and so forth. The position should also be understood from the investigation conducted at length in the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s>; therefore a further elaborate discussion is not undertaken here.

body.text: evaṃ tāvat skandhā ātmā na bhavati | skandhavyatirikto 'pi na yujyate | yadi hi skandhebhyo 'nya ātmā bhavet, askandhalakṣaṇo bhavet | yathā hi goranyo 'śvaḥ na golakṣaṇe bhavati, evamātmāpi skandhavyatiriktaḥ parikalpyamānaḥ askandhalakṣaṇo bhavet | tatra skandhāḥ saṃskṛtatvād hetupratyayasaṃbhūtā utpādasthitibhaṅgalakṣaṇāḥ | tatra askandhalakṣaṇa ātmā bhavan bhavanmatena utpādasthitibhaṅgalakṣaṇāyuktaḥ syāt | yaścaivaṃ bhavati, saḥ avidyamānatvādasaṃskṛtatvādvā khapuṣpavannirvāṇabadvā naiva ātmavyapadeśaṃ pratilabhate, nāpyahaṃkāraviṣayatvena yujyate, iti skandhavyatirikto 'pyātmā na yujyate ||
body.translated_text: Thus, the <s>skandhas</s> are not the self. Nor is [the self] separate from the <s>skandhas</s> tenable. For if the self were other than the <s>skandhas</s>, it would have non-<s>skandha</s> characteristics. For just as a horse, being other than a cow, does not have the characteristics of a cow — even so the self, being conceived as separate from the <s>skandhas</s>, would have non-<s>skandha</s> characteristics. Now the <s>skandhas</s>, being conditioned, having arisen from causes and conditions, have the characteristics of arising, duration, and destruction. The self, having non-<s>skandha</s> characteristics, would in your view be devoid of the characteristics of arising, duration, and destruction. And one that is of such a kind — because of non-existence, or because of being unconditioned — like a sky-flower or like <s>nirvāṇa</s>, simply does not obtain the designation 'self,' nor is it tenable as being the object of the sense of 'I.' Thus, the self as separate from the <s>skandhas</s> is also not tenable.

body.text: athavā | ayamanyo 'rthaḥ- yadi ātmā skandhavyatiriktaḥ syāt, saḥ askandhalakṣaṇa syāt | rūpaṇānubhavanimittodgahaṇābhisaṃskaraṇaviṣayaprativijñaptilakṣaṇāḥ pañca skandhāḥ | ātmā ca rūpādiva vijñānaṃ skandhebhyo vyatirikta iṣyamāṇaḥ pṛthaglakṣaṇasiddhaḥ syāt, pṛthaglakṣaṇasiddhaśca gṛhyeta rūpādiva cittam| na ca gṛhyate | tasmāt skandhavyatirikto 'pi nāsti ||
body.translated_text: Alternatively, this is another meaning: if the self were separate from the <s>skandhas</s>, it would have non-<s>skandha</s> characteristics. The five <s>skandhas</s> have the characteristics of materialization, experiencing, apprehension of signs, formation, and cognition of objects. And the self, being posited as separate from the <s>skandhas</s> like consciousness is [separate] from form and so forth, would be established with a distinct characteristic; and being established with a distinct characteristic, it would be apprehended like the mind [is apprehended as distinct] from form and so forth. But it is not apprehended. Therefore, [the self] as separate from the <s>skandhas</s> also does not exist.

body.text: nanu ca tīrthikāḥ skandhebhyo vyatiriktamātmānaṃ pratipannā bhinnalakṣaṇamācakṣate, tasmātteṣāmabādhaka evāyaṃ vidhiriti | yathā ca tīrthikā ātmano bhinnalakṣaṇamācakṣate tathoktaṃ madhyamakāvatāre-
body.translated_text: But surely the non-Buddhists, who accept a self separate from the <s>skandhas</s>, declare it to have a distinct characteristic — therefore this procedure is simply not damaging to them! And the way in which non-Buddhists declare the distinct characteristic of the self has been stated in the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s> —

children.text: ātmā tīrthyaiḥ kalpyate nityarūpo 'kartā bhoktā nirguṇo niṣkriyaśca |
children.translated_text: The self is conceived by the non-Buddhists as permanent in nature, non-agent, enjoyer, without qualities, without activity. /

children.text: kaṃcitkaṃcidvedamāśritya tasya bhedaṃ yātā prakriyā tīrthikānām ||
children.translated_text: Depending on one or another doctrine, the non-Buddhists have diverged into different systems regarding it. //

body.text: ityanena | ucyate | satyaṃ bruvanti tīrthikāḥ skandhavyatiriktasya lakṣaṇam, na punaste svarūpata ātmānamupalabhya tasya lakṣaṇamācakṣate, kiṃ tarhi yathāvadupādāyaprajñaptyanavagamena nāmamātrakamevātmānaṃ trāsādapratipadyamānāḥ saṃvṛtisatyādapi paribhraṣṭā mithyākalpanayaiva kevalamanumānābhāsamātravipralabdhāḥ santaḥ mohāt parikalpayanti ātmānam, tasya ca lakṣaṇamācakṣate | teṣāṃ ca karmakārakaparīkṣādiṣu ātmopādānayoḥ parasparāpekṣikīṃ siddhiṃ bruvatā saṃvṛtyāpi pratiṣedho vihita eva | uktaṃ ca-
body.translated_text: — by this. It is replied: It is true that the non-Buddhists state the characteristic of [a self] separate from the <s>skandhas</s>; but they do not perceive the self by its own form and then declare its characteristic. Rather, through their failure to understand designation-in-dependence-on-that (<s>upādāyaprajñapti</s>) as it truly is, not accepting even the mere name 'self' out of fear [of its non-existence], having fallen even from conventional truth, being deceived merely by what has the semblance of inference alone through false construction, they fabricate the self out of delusion, and declare its characteristic. And even their [position] has been conventionally refuted by the one who, in the Examination of Action and Agent and so forth, states the mutually dependent establishment of self and the appropriated. And it has been said —

children.translated_text: Just as, depending on a mirror, the reflection of one's own face /

children.text: dṛśyate nāma taccaiva na kiṃcidapi tattvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: is seen, so to speak — yet that very thing is not anything at all in reality. //
Even so, the sense of 'I' is apprehended in dependence on the <s>skandhas</s>, /
but it is nothing at all in reality — like the reflection of one's own face. //
Just as, without taking up a mirror, the reflection of one's own face /
is not seen — even so, without taking up the <s>skandhas</s>, the thought 'I' [does not arise]. //
Having heard the meaning of this kind, the noble <s>Ānanda</s> obtained the eye of <s>Dharma</s>, /
and he himself also repeatedly told the monks. //

body.text: ato na punastatpratipādanārthaṃ yatna ārabhyate | upādāya prajñapyamāna eva avidyāviparyāsānugatānāmātmābhiniveśāspadabhūto mumukṣubhirvicāryate, yasyedaṃ skandhapañcakamupādānatvena pratibhāsate kimasau skandhalakṣaṇaḥ uta askandhalakṣaṇaḥ iti | sarvathā ca vicārayanto mumukṣavo nainamupalabhante bhāvasvabhāvataḥ | tadā eṣām-
body.translated_text: Therefore no further effort is undertaken to demonstrate that. [The self] as designated in dependence — which for those conforming to the perversion of ignorance has become the basis for the attachment to self — is examined by those who seek liberation, for whom this fivefold aggregate appears as the appropriated: is it of <s>skandha</s>-characteristic or of non-<s>skandha</s>-characteristic? And those seeking liberation, examining in every way, do not find it as having the nature of an entity. Then for them —

body.text: ātmanyasati cātmīyaṃ kuta eva bhaviṣyati |
body.translated_text: And when the self does not exist, how will what belongs to the self (<s>ātmīya</s>) come to be? /

body.text: ātmānupalambhādātmaprajñaptyupādānaṃ skandhapañcakamātmīyamiti sutarāṃ nopalabhante | yathaiva hi dagdhe rathe tadaṅgānyapi dagdhatvānnopalabhyante, evaṃ yogino yadaiva ātmanairātmyaṃ pratipadyante, tadaiva ātmīyaskandhavastunairātmyamapi niyataṃ pratipadyante | yathoktaṃ ratnāvalyām-
body.translated_text: From the non-apprehension of the self, they do not find the fivefold aggregate — which is the basis of designation for the self — as 'belonging to the self' all the more. For just as, when a chariot has been burned, its parts too, being burned, are not found — even so, at the very moment when yogins realize the selflessness of the self, they necessarily also realize the selflessness of the things that belong to the self, namely the <s>skandhas</s>. As stated in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s> —

children.translated_text: The <s>skandhas</s> arise from the sense of 'I'; that sense of 'I' is in reality false. /

children.text: bījaṃ yasyānṛtaṃ tasya prarohaḥ satyataḥ kutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the seed is false, how can its sprout be true? //
Having seen the <s>skandhas</s> as unreal, the sense of 'I' is abandoned. /
From the abandonment of the sense of 'I,' the <s>skandhas</s> do not arise again. //

body.text: yathaiva hi grīṣme madhyāhnakālāvasānamāsāditasya vidhananabhomadhyadeśamācikraṃsorīṣatparibhramyamānapaṭutarahutabhugvitatasphuliṅgāniva virūkṣataramahīmaṇḍalottāpanaparān pradīptakiraṇasya kiraṇān pratītya virūkṣataramavanideśaṃ cāsādya viparītaṃ ca darśanamapekṣya salilākārā marīcaya upalabhyamānā vidūradeśāvasthitānāṃ janmavatāmatiprasannābhinīlajalākāraṃ pratyayamādadhati
body.translated_text: For just as, in summer, at the end of the midday hour, when the sun's blazing rays — that seem like the widespread sparks of a sharp, swift fire whirling slightly as it ascends toward the middle region of the cloudless sky — reach a parched expanse of earth that is extremely dry, and depending on those rays, and arriving at an extremely dry stretch of ground, and with a mistaken perception, mirages appearing in the form of water provide, for beings standing at a great distance, a cause for [perceiving] water that appears as extremely clear and blue

body.text: na tu tatsamīpagatānām, evamihāpi yathāvasthitātmātmīyapadārthatattvadarśanavidūradeśāntarasthitānāṃ saṃsārādhvani vartamānānāmavidyāviparyāsānugamānmṛṣārtha eva skandhasamāropaḥ satyataḥ pratibhāsamānaḥ padārthatattvadarśanasamīpasthānāṃ na pratibhāsate | yathoktamācāryapādaiḥ-
body.translated_text: — but not for those who have come near to it — even so here, for those who are far removed from seeing the reality of the self and what belongs to the self, who are traversing the road of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and who are conforming to the perversion of ignorance, the superimposition of the <s>skandhas</s>, though its meaning is false, appears as true; but it does not appear to those who stand near to seeing the reality of things. As stated by the <s>Ācāryapāda</s> (<s>Nāgārjuna</s>) —

children.translated_text: A form seen from afar is seen clearly by those who are near. /

children.text: marīciryadi vāri syādāsannaiḥ kiṃ na gṛhyate ||
children.translated_text: If a mirage were water, why is it not apprehended by those who are near? //
Just as this world, as it truly is, is seen by those who are far away, /
it is not seen thus by those who are near — signless, like a mirage. //
Just as a mirage resembles water but is not water and not [water] in reality, /
so the <s>skandhas</s> resemble a self but are not a self, nor are they [a self] in reality. //

body.text: ata eva ca ātmātmīyānupalambhātparamārthadarśanasamīpastho yogī niyataṃ bhavati-
body.translated_text: And for this very reason — from the non-apprehension of self and what belongs to the self — the yogin who stands near to the vision of ultimate reality necessarily becomes —

body.text: nirmamo nirahaṃkāraḥ śamādātmātmanīnayoḥ || 2 ||
body.translated_text: free from 'mine' and free from 'I' — from the cessation of the self and what pertains to the self. // 2 //

body.text: ātmani hitamātmanīnam, skandhapañcakam, ātmīyamityarthaḥ | ātmano 'haṃkāraviṣayasya ātmanīnasya ca skandhādervastunaḥ mamakāraviṣayasya śamādanutpādādanupalambhānnirmamo nirahaṃkāraśca jāyate yogī || 2 ||
body.translated_text: 'What pertains to the self' (<s>ātmanīna</s>) means what is beneficial to the self — the fivefold aggregate, meaning: what belongs to the self. From the cessation — the non-arising, the non-apprehension — of the self, which is the object of the sense of 'I,' and of what pertains to the self, namely the <s>skandhas</s> and other things, which are the object of the sense of 'mine,' the yogin becomes free from 'mine' and free from 'I.' // 2 //

body.text: nanu ca yo 'sāvevaṃ nirmamo nirahaṃkāraśca yogī bhavati, sa tāvadasti | sati ca tasmin siddha ātmā skandhāśceti naitadevam | yasmāt-
body.translated_text: But surely, the yogin who is thus free from 'mine' and free from 'I' — he at least exists! And if he exists, then the self and the <s>skandhas</s> are established. This is not so. Because —

children.text: nirmamo nirahaṃkāro yaśca so 'pi na vidyate |
children.translated_text: One who is free from 'mine' and free from 'I' — even he does not exist. /

children.text: nirmamaṃ nirahaṃkāraṃ yaḥ paśyati na paśyati || 3 ||
children.translated_text: One who sees [a being] free from 'mine' and free from 'I' does not [truly] see. // 3 //

body.text: ātmani skandheṣu ca sarvathānupalabhyamānasvarūpeṣu kutastadvayatirikto 'parapadārtho bhaviṣyati yo 'sau nirmamo nirahaṃkāraśceti | yastu evamasaṃvidyamānasvarūpaṃ nirmamaṃ nirahaṃkāraṃ ca paśyati, sa tattvaṃ na paśyatīti vijñeyam | yathoktaṃ bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: When the self and the <s>skandhas</s> have in every way a nature that is not found, whence would there be another entity separate from both — the one who is said to be free from 'mine' and free from 'I'? And whoever sees what is free from 'mine' and free from 'I' as having such a non-existent nature — that one does not see reality. This should be understood. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said —

children.translated_text: See the internal as empty; see the external as empty. /

children.text: na vidyate so 'pi kaścidyo bhāvayati śūnyatām ||
children.translated_text: There does not exist even that one who cultivates emptiness. //

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise —

children.text: yo 'pi ca cintayi śūnyaka dharmān so 'pi kumārgapapannaku bālaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who reflects on empty <s>dharmas</s> — even that one is a childish person who has entered a wrong path. /

children.text: akṣara kīrtita śūnyaka dharmāḥ te ca anakṣara akṣara uktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The indestructible <s>dharmas</s> are declared as empty — and those empty ones are declared as indestructible. //

body.text:
śānta paśānta ya cintayi dharmān so 'pi ca cittu na jātu na bhūtaḥ |
cittavitarkiṇa sarvi papañcāḥ tasya acintiya budhyatha dharmān || iti |
body.translated_text:
One who reflects on <s>dharmas</s> as 'ceased' or 'not ceased' — even that mind has never been, and is not existent. /
All conceptual proliferations belong to one who deliberates with the mind — understand those <s>dharmas</s> as inconceivable. //

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise —

children.text: skandha sabhāvatu śūnya vivikta bodhi sabhāvatu śūnya vivikta |
children.translated_text: The <s>skandhas</s> are empty by their own nature, isolated; enlightenment is empty by its own nature, isolated. /
