children.text: yo 'pi caretsa pi śūnyasabhāvo jñānavato na tu bālajanasya ||
children.translated_text: One who practices this — that one too is of empty nature; [this is] for the one who has knowledge, but not for the childish. //

body.text: tadevam-
body.translated_text: Thus indeed —

children.translated_text: When 'mine' and 'I' have been exhausted, both externally and internally, /
appropriation ceases; from the exhaustion of that, there is the exhaustion of birth. // 4 //

body.text: satkāyadṛṣṭimūlakāḥ satkāyadṛṣṭisamudayāḥ satkāyadṛṣṭihetukāḥ sarvakleśāḥ sūtre uktāḥ | sā ca satkāyadṛṣṭirātmātmīyānupalambhātprahīyate, tatprahāṇācca kāmadṛṣṭiśīlavratātmavādopādānacatuṣṭayaṃ prahīyate, upādānakṣayācca janmanaḥ punarbhavalakṣaṇasya kṣayo bhavati || 4 ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>sūtra</s>, all afflictions have been said to have the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) as their root, to have <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> as their origin, and to have <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> as their cause. And that <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> is abandoned through the non-apprehension of self and what belongs to the self. And from its abandonment, the fourfold appropriation (<s>upādāna</s>) — of desire, views, rules-and-vows, and self-doctrine — is abandoned. And from the exhaustion of appropriation, there is the exhaustion of birth, characterized by renewed existence. // 4 //

body.text: yataśca ayaṃ janmanivṛttikramaḥ evaṃ vyavasthāpitaḥ, tasmāt-
body.translated_text: And since this sequence of the cessation of birth has been thus established, therefore —

body.text: karmakleśakṣayānmokṣaḥ
body.translated_text: Liberation is through the exhaustion of action and afflictions. /

body.text: iti sthitam | upādāne hi kṣīṇe tatpratyayo bhavo na bhavati | bhave niruddhe kuto jātijarāmaraṇādikasya saṃbhava iti | evaṃ karmakleśakṣayānmokṣo bhavatīti sthitam |
body.translated_text: — this is established. For when appropriation has been exhausted, becoming (<s>bhava</s>), which is conditioned by it, does not occur. When becoming has ceased, whence the arising of birth, old age, death, and the rest? Thus it is established that liberation comes about through the exhaustion of action and afflictions.

body.text: karmakleśānāṃ tarhi kasya kṣayātparikṣaya iti vaktavyam || ucyate-
body.translated_text: Then from the exhaustion of what do actions and afflictions undergo complete exhaustion? This must be stated. It is replied —

children.translated_text: Actions and afflictions [arise] from conceptual construction. /
Those [arise] from conceptual proliferation (<s>prapañca</s>); but <s>prapañca</s> ceases in emptiness. // 5 //

body.text: ayoniśo hi rūpādikaṃ vikalpayato bālapṛthagjanasya kleśa upajāyate rāgādikaḥ vakṣyati hi-
body.translated_text: For the childish ordinary person who inappropriately constructs form and so forth, the affliction of passion (<s>rāga</s>) and so forth arises. For it will be said —

children.translated_text: 'Passion, hatred, and delusion are said to arise from conceptual construction; /
for they arise in dependence on the pleasant, the unpleasant, and the perverted.' //

body.text: uktaṃ ca sūtre-
body.translated_text: And it has been said in the <s>sūtra</s> —

children.text: kāma jānāmi te mūlaṃ saṃkalpātkila jāyase |
children.translated_text: 'O desire, I know your root — you arise from conceptual construction. /

children.text: na tvāṃ saṃkalpayiṣyāmi tato me na bhaviṣyasi || iti ||
children.translated_text: I shall not construct you [in thought] — then you will not exist for me.' //

body.text: evaṃ tāvat karmakleśā vikalpataḥ pravartante | te ca vikalpāḥ anādimatsaṃsārābhyastād jñānajñeyavācyavācakakartṛkarmakaraṇakriyāghaṭapaṭamukuṭaratharūpavedanāstrīpuruṣalābhālābhasukhaduḥkhayaśo 'yaśonindāpraśaṃsādilakṣaṇādvicitrātprapañcādupajāyate | sa cāyaṃ laukikaḥ prapañco niravaśeṣa śūnyatāyāṃ sarvasvabhāvaśūnyatādarśane sati nirudhyate | kathaṃ kṛtvā? yasmātsati hi vastunaṃ upalambhe syād yathoditaprapañcajālam | na hi anupalabhya vandhyāduhitaraṃ rūpalāvaṇyayauvanavatīṃ tadviṣayaṃ prapañcamavatārayanti rāgiṇaḥ | na ca anavatārya prapañcaṃ tadviṣayamayoniśo vikalpamavatārayanti | na ca anavatārya kalpanājālam ahaṃmametyabhiniveśāt satkāyadṛṣṭimūlakān kleśagaṇānutpādayanti | na ca anutpādya satkāyadṛṣṭayātmakān kleśagaṇān karmāṇi śubhāśubhāniñjyāni kurvanti | na ca akurvāṇāḥ karmāṇi jātijarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasya[upāyāsādirūpaṃ] ekajālībhūtaṃ saṃsārakāntāramanubhavanti | evaṃ yogino 'pi śūnyatādarśanāvasthā niravaśeṣaskandhadhātvāyatanāni svarūpato nopalabhante | na ca anupalabhamānā vastusvarūpaṃ tadviṣayaṃ prapañcamavatārayanti | na ca anavatārya tadviṣayaṃ prapañcaṃ vikalpamavatārayanti | na ca anavatārya vikalpam ahaṃmametyabhiniveśāt satkāyadṛṣṭimūlakaṃ kleśagaṇamutpādayanti | na ca anutpādya satkāyadṛṣṭayādikaṃ kleśagaṇaṃ karmāṇi kurvanti | na ca akurvāṇāḥ jātijarāmaraṇākhyaṃ saṃsāramanubhavanti | tadevam aśeṣaprapañcopaśamaśivalakṣaṇāṃ śūnyatāmāgamya yasmādaśeṣakalpanājālaprapañcavigamo bhavati, prapañcavigamācca vikalpanivṛtiḥ, vikalpanivṛttyā ca aśeṣakarmakleśanivṛtti, karmakleśanivṛttyā ca janmanivṛttiḥ, tasmāt śūnyataiva sarvaprapañcanivṛttilakṣaṇatvānnirvāṇamityucyate yathoktaṃ śatake-
body.translated_text: Thus, first, <s>karma</s> (action) and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) proceed from conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>). And those conceptual constructions arise from manifold conceptual proliferation (<s>prapañca</s>) — characterized by knowledge and knowable, word and referent, agent and action, instrument and act, pot, cloth, turban, chariot, form, feeling, woman, man, gain, loss, happiness, suffering, fame, infamy, blame, praise, and so forth — which has been habituated since beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>. And this worldly <s>prapañca</s> ceases when there is the vision of complete emptiness (<s>niravaśeṣa-śūnyatā</s>) — the emptiness of all <s>svabhāva</s>. How so? Because if there were apprehension of entities, there would be the net of <s>prapañca</s> as described. For lustful persons do not project the net of <s>prapañca</s> concerning a barren woman's daughter endowed with beauty, charm, and youth without first apprehending her. And without projecting <s>prapañca</s>, they do not engage in unwise conceptual construction (<s>ayoniśo vikalpa</s>) regarding her. And without engaging in the net of conceptual construction, they do not produce the host of <s>kleśas</s> rooted in <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (the view of the transitory collection) through the clinging 'I' and 'mine.' And without producing the host of <s>kleśas</s> rooted in <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, they do not perform wholesome, unwholesome, or imperturbable actions. And without performing actions, they do not experience the jungle of <s>saṃsāra</s>, which has the form of birth, old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and agitation — all woven into a single net. Even so, yogins in the state of the vision of emptiness do not apprehend the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) in their own form, without remainder. And not apprehending the own-form of entities, they do not project <s>prapañca</s> regarding them. And without projecting <s>prapañca</s> regarding them, they do not engage in conceptual construction. And without engaging in conceptual construction, they do not produce the host of <s>kleśas</s> rooted in <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> through the clinging 'I' and 'mine.' And without producing the host of <s>kleśas</s> beginning with <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, they do not perform actions. And without performing actions, they do not experience <s>saṃsāra</s> called birth, old age, and death. Thus, since there is the complete cessation of the entire net of conceptual proliferation through arriving at emptiness — characterized by the auspicious pacification of all <s>prapañca</s> without remainder — and since from the cessation of <s>prapañca</s> there is the cessation of conceptual construction, and from the cessation of conceptual construction there is the cessation of all <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> without remainder, and from the cessation of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> there is the cessation of birth — therefore <s>śūnyatā</s> itself, because it has the character of the cessation of all <s>prapañca</s>, is called <s>nirvāṇa</s>. As stated in the <s>Śataka</s> (Catuḥśataka):

children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgatas</s> describe the <s>Dharma</s> in brief as non-harm. /
<s>Śūnyatā</s> alone is <s>nirvāṇa</s> — only these two [are taught] here. //

body.text: ācāryabhāvavivekastu śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ yathoditaśūnyatādhigamamapratipadyamānaḥ evaṃ varṇayati- aparotpannapratikṣaṇavinaśvarasaṃskārakalāpamātramanātmānātmīyamavalokayataḥ āryaśrāvakasyāpi ātmātmīyavastvabhāvād dharmamātramidaṃ jāyate mriyate ceti darśanamutpadyate | ahaṃkāraviṣayo hyātmā, [tadabhāvāttasyāpyabhāvaḥ], tadabhāvādeva na kvacidādhyātmikaṃ bāhyaṃ vā vastu astīti mamakārānutpatteḥ nirmamo nirahaṃkāro 'hamiti na svarūpaviniścitirupajāyate, anyatra vyavahārasaṃketāt | prāgeva ajātasarvasaṃskāradarśināṃ nirvikalpaprajñācāravihāriṇāṃ mahābodhisattvānāmiti | ata āha-
body.translated_text: But <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Bhāvaviveka</s>, not accepting the realization of emptiness as described above for <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, describes it thus: 'For the noble <s>Śrāvaka</s> too, who, contemplating nothing other than the mere aggregate-mass of <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) — momentarily perishing, arisen from other [causes] — as without self and without what belongs to self, the vision arises: "Since there is no real self or what belongs to self, only <s>dharmas</s> arise and die" — this is due to the absence of a real self or what belongs to self. From this, because of the very absence [of self], since nothing whatsoever is "mine" — neither internal nor external — the determination "I am without mine, without self" does not arise as a determination of own-nature, except through conventional designation. How much more so for the great <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who see all <s>saṃskāras</s> as unborn and who abide in the conduct of non-conceptual <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom)!' Therefore he says:

body.text: nirmamo nirahaṃkāro yaśca so 'pi na vidyate || iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Without mine, without self' — even he is not found. //

body.text: tadayamācāryo yathaivaṃvidhe viṣaye nācāryapādamatānuvartī tathā pratipāditaṃ madhyamakāvatāre-
body.translated_text: This <s>Ācārya</s>, in that he does not follow the position of the venerable <s>Ācārya</s> [<s>Candrakīrti</s>] on this subject, has been demonstrated in the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s> —

body.text: dūraṃgamāyāṃ tu dhiyādhikaḥ
body.translated_text: 'On the Far-Going [stage], the one who excels in wisdom...' —

body.text: ityatreti na punastaddūṣaṇe yatna āsthīyate | ata evoktaṃ bhagavatā āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāṃ bhagavatyām-
body.translated_text: at that point. Therefore, no effort is made here again to refute it. For this very reason the <s>Bhagavān</s> said in the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>:

body.text: śrāvakabodhimabhisaṃboddhukrāmena subhūte asyāmeva prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitavyam | pratyeka bodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmena subhūte asyāmeva prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitavyam | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmena subhūte bodhisattvena mahāsattvena asyāmeva prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitavyamityādi ||
body.translated_text: 'One who wishes to realize the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-awakening, <s>Subhūti</s>, should train in precisely this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. One who wishes to realize the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-awakening, <s>Subhūti</s>, should train in precisely this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. One who wishes to realize unsurpassed, perfect awakening, <s>Subhūti</s> — a <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>mahāsattva</s> should train in precisely this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' And so forth.

body.text: āha ca-
body.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: yo icchatī sugataśrāvaku haṃ bhaveyaṃ pratyekabuddhu bhavijā tatha dharmarājo |
children.translated_text: 'He who wishes: "May I become a disciple of the <s>Sugata</s>, or a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, or a king of <s>Dharma</s>" — /

children.text: imu kṣānti nāgatya na śakyati pāpuṇotuṃ yatha ārapāragamanīyaṃ atīradarśī ||
children.translated_text: without resorting to this patience [i.e., the acceptance of the profound <s>Dharma</s>], it is impossible to attain [any of these] — like one who sees no shore while crossing to the far bank.' //

body.translated_text: Thus. // 5 //

body.text: atrāha- yadyevamādhyātmikabāhyavastvanupalambhādadhyātmaṃ bahiśca ahaṃmametikalpanājālānāmanutpādastattvamiti vyavasthāpitam, yattarhi etaduktaṃ bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: if it has been established that the truth is the non-arising of the nets of 'I' and 'mine' conceptual construction, because of the non-apprehension of internal and external entities — then how is it that the <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

children.text: ātmā hi ātmano nāthaḥ ko nu nāthaḥ paro bhavet |
children.translated_text: 'The self is indeed one's own protector — who else could be a protector? /

children.text: ātmanā hi sudāntena svargaṃ prāpnoti paṇḍitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For with a well-disciplined self, the wise one attains heaven.' //

children.text: ātmā hi ātmano nāthaḥ ko nu nāthaḥ paro bhavet |
children.translated_text: 'The self is indeed one's own protector — who else could be a protector? /

children.text: ātmā hi ātmanaḥ sākṣī kṛtasyāpakṛtasya ca ||
children.translated_text: The self is indeed one's own witness of what has been done and what has not been done.' //

body.text: tathā āryasamādhirāje-
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the Noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>:

children.text: kṛṣṇaśubhaṃ ca na naśyati karma ātmana kṛtva ca vedayitavyam |
children.translated_text: 'Dark and bright <s>karma</s> does not perish; having done it oneself, one must experience [the result]. /

children.text: no pi ca saṃkrama karmaphalasya no ca ahetuka pratyanubhoti ||
children.translated_text: There is no transference of the fruit of action, nor does one experience it without a cause.' //

body.text: iti vistaraḥ | tatkathaṃ na virudhyata iti? ucyate | idamapi kiṃ noktaṃ bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: And so forth in detail. How then is there no contradiction? The reply is: has not this too been said by the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text: nāstīha sattva ātmā vā dharmāstvete sahetukāḥ | iti?
body.translated_text: 'There is no being here, no self — these <s>dharmas</s> exist with their causes.' //

body.text: tathā hi- rūpaṃ nātmā rūpavānnāpi cātmā rūpe nātmā nātmani rūpaṃ .... | evaṃ yāvat vijñānaṃ nātmā, vijñānavānnātmā vijñāne nātmā nātmani vijñānam iti | tathā- anātmānaḥ sarvadharmā iti | tatkathamidānīmanenāgamena pūrvakasyāgamasya virodho na syāt? tasmāddeśanābhiprāyo bhagavato 'nveṣyaḥ |
body.translated_text: For thus: 'Form is not the self; the self does not possess form; the self is not in form; form is not in the self... Likewise up to: consciousness is not the self; the self does not possess consciousness; the self is not in consciousness; consciousness is not in the self.' Likewise: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are without self.' How then can there be no contradiction between this scripture and the former? Therefore the teaching-intention of the <s>Bhagavān</s> must be investigated.

body.text: sāmānyena tu bhagavadbhirbuddhaiḥ pravacane neyanītārthavistaraprabhede 'śeṣajagadvineyabuddhipadmākaravibodhana parairādityakalpairanastaṃgatairmahākaruṇopāyavijñānagabhastivistaraiḥ-
body.translated_text: But in general, by the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, the <s>Buddhas</s>, in the teaching — with its division into interpretable (<s>neyārtha</s>) and definitive (<s>nītārtha</s>) meanings — like suns that never set, incomparable, who with the far-reaching rays of their wisdom of great compassion and skillful means cause the lotus-beds of the intellects of all beings to be guided throughout the entire universe to blossom:

children.translated_text: 'Self' too has been designated, and 'non-self' too has been taught; /
the <s>Buddhas</s> have also taught that neither self nor non-self whatsoever [truly exists]. // 6 //

body.text: atra cāyamabhiprāyaḥ- iha ye [ātmābhāvaviparyāsa] kudarśanadhanatimirapaṭalāvacchāditāśeṣabuddhinayanatayā laukikāvadātadarśanaviṣayānatikrāntamapi bhāvajātamapaśyanto vyavahārasatyāvasthitā eva santaḥ kṣitisalilajvalanapavanābhidhānatattvamātrānuvarṇanaparā mūlaudanodakakiṇvādidravyaviśeṣaparipākamātrapratyayotpannamadamurcchādisāmarthyaviśeṣānugatamadyapānopalambhavat kalalādimahābhūtaparipākamātrasaṃbhūtā eva buddhīranuvarṇayantaḥ pūrvāntāparāntāpavādapravṛttāḥ santaḥ paralokamātmānaṃ cāpavadante- nāstyayaṃ lokaḥ, nāsti paralokaḥ, nāsti sukṛtaduṣkṛtānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalavipākaḥ, nāsti sattva upapādukaḥ, ityādinā | tadapavādācca svargāpavargaviśiṣṭeṣṭaphalaviśeṣākṣepaparāṅmukhāḥ satatasamitamakuśalakarmābhisaṃskaraṇapravṛttā narakādimahāprapātapatanābhimukhāḥ | teṣāṃ tadasadṛṣṭinivṛttyartha caturaśīticittacaritasahasrabhedabhinnasya sattvadhātoryathāśayānuvartakairaśeṣasattvadhātūttāraṇākṣiptapratijñāsaṃpādanatatparaiḥ prajñopāyamahākaruṇāsaṃbhārapuraḥ sarairnirupamairekajagadbandhubhirniravaśeṣakleśamahāvyādhicikitsakairmahāvaidyarājabhūtairhīnamadhyotkṛṣṭavineyajanānujidhṛkṣayā hīrnānāṃ vineyānāmakuśalakarmakāriṇāmakuśalādi nivartayituṃ buddhairbhagavadbhiḥ kvacidātmetyapi prajñapitaṃ loke vyavasthāpitam | ahetuvādapratiṣedhopapattiśca karmakārakaparīkṣātaḥ, nāpyahetutaḥ ityataḥ, madhyamakāvatārācca vistareṇa veditavyeti tatpratiṣedhārtha neha punaryatna āsthīyate ||
body.translated_text: And herein is the intention: those who, because their entire mental vision is obscured by the thick cataract of the dark mis-vision of the distorted view of the non-existence of self — not seeing even the realm of things visible to correct worldly sight, and being situated in conventional truth alone — describe nothing more than the truth of the mere elements called earth, water, fire, and wind, and describe intellects as arising solely from the maturation of specific material substances such as roots, grain, water, and yeast — like the observation of intoxication and the like arising from the specific power of the maturation of mere specific material substances of liquor — and who, proceeding with the denial of past and future lives, deny the next world and the self: 'There is no this world, no next world, no fruit and maturation of good and bad deeds, no spontaneously born being,' and so forth — and who, because of that denial, turn away from the attraction to the special desired fruits of heaven and liberation, constantly engage in the performance of unwholesome actions, and head toward falling into the great abyss of the hells and the like — for them, in order to turn them away from that false view, by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, who are eager to benefit beings to be guided, and who follow the dispositions of the realm of beings divided into eighty-four thousand types of mental conduct, whose vow is impelled by the task of rescuing the entire realm of beings, who are preceded by the accumulations of wisdom, skillful means, and great compassion, who are the incomparable sole kinsmen of the entire world, the supreme physician-kings who cure the great disease of all <s>kleśas</s> without remainder — for the sake of the inferior beings to be guided, wishing to turn the performers of unwholesome actions from unwholesome deeds and the like, 'self' (<s>ātman</s>) too has been designated, established in the world. And the reasoning for the refutation of the doctrine of no cause should be understood from the Examination of Agent and Action (<s>karmakārakaparīkṣā</s>), from the statement 'nor from no cause,' and in detail from the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s> — therefore no effort is made here for that refutation.

body.text: ye tu sadbhūtātmadṛṣṭikaṭhinātidīrghaśithilamahāsūtrabaddhā vihaṃgamā iva sudūramapi gatāḥ kuśalakarmakāriṇo 'kuśalakarmapathavyāvṛttā api na śaknuvanti traidhātukabhavopapattimativāhya śivamajaramamaraṇaṃ nirvāṇapuramabhigantum, teṣāṃ madhyānāṃ vineyānāṃ satkāyadarśanābhiniveśaśithilīkaraṇāya nirvāṇābhilāṣasaṃjananārthaṃ buddhairbhagavadbhirvineyajanānugrahacikīrṣubhiranātmetyapi deśitam ||
body.translated_text: But those who, like birds bound by the hard, exceedingly long, loose, great string of the view of a truly existent self — even though they have gone far, performing wholesome actions and having turned away from unwholesome courses of action — are unable to pass beyond the occurrence of existence in the triple world and reach the auspicious, ageless, deathless city of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — for them, the middling beings to be guided, in order to loosen the grip of their clinging to the view of the transitory collection (<s>satkāyadarśana</s>) and to generate the aspiration for <s>nirvāṇa</s>, 'non-self' (<s>anātman</s>) too has been taught by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, who wish to benefit beings to be guided.

body.text: ye tu pūrvābhyāsaviśeṣānugatagambhīradharmādhimokṣalabdhabījaparipākāḥ pratyāsannavartini nirvāṇe teṣāmutkṛṣṭānāṃ vineyānāṃ vigatātmasnehānāṃ paramagambhīramaunīndrapravacanārthatattvāvagāhanasamarthānāmadhimuktiviśeṣamavadhārya-
body.translated_text: But those who, having attained the ripening of the seed of devotion to the profound <s>Dharma</s> through the specific power of prior practice — for whom <s>nirvāṇa</s> is near at hand — for them, the superior beings to be guided, who are free from attachment to the self, who are capable of plunging into the truth of the meaning of the supremely profound teaching of the Lord of Sages — having ascertained their specific devotion:

body.text: buddhairātmā na cānātmā kaścidityapi deśitam ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s> have also taught that neither self nor non-self whatsoever [truly exists]. //

body.text: yathaiva hi ātmadarśanamatattvam, evaṃ tatpratipakṣabhūtamapi anātmadarśanaṃ naiva tattvamiti | evaṃ nāstyātmā kaścit, na cāpyanātmā kaścidastīti deśitam | yathoktamāryaratnakūṭe-
body.translated_text: For just as the view of self is not the truth, even so the view of non-self, which is its counterpart, is not the truth either. Thus it has been taught: there is no self whatsoever, and there is no non-self whatsoever either. As stated in the Noble <s>Ratnakūṭa</s>:

body.text: ātmeti kāśyapa ayameko 'ntaḥ | nairātmyamityayaṃ dvitīyo 'ntaḥ | yadetadanayorantayormadhyaṃ tadarūpyamanidarśanamapratiṣṭhamanābhāsamavijñaptikamaniketam | iyamucyate | kāśyapa madhyamā pratipada dharmāṇāṃ bhūtapratyavekṣā iti ||
body.translated_text: '"Self," <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is one extreme. "Non-self" is the second extreme. That which is the middle of these two extremes — that is formless, without appearance, without foundation, without manifestation, without cognizability, without abode. This, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is called the Middle Path, the true examination of <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: uktaṃ cāryaratnāvalyām-
body.translated_text: And it is said in the Noble <s>Ratnāvalī</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Neither self nor non-self is found as it truly is. /
The Great Sage turned away from views made by [the concepts of] self and non-self.' //

body.text:
dṛṣṭaśrutādyaṃ muninā na satyaṃ na mṛṣoditam |
pakṣāddhi pratipakṣaḥ syādubhayaṃ tacca nārthataḥ || iti |
body.translated_text:
'What is seen, heard, and so forth was said by the Sage to be neither true nor false. /
From a thesis, indeed, an antithesis would follow — and both are not real in the ultimate sense.' //

body.text: yataścaivaṃ hīnamadhyotkṛṣṭavineyajanāśayanānātvena ātmānātmatadubhayapratiṣedhena buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ dharmadeśanā pravṛttā, tasmānnāsti āgamabādho mādhyamikānām | ata evoktamāryadevapādaiḥ-
body.translated_text: And since, through the diversity of the dispositions of inferior, middling, and superior beings to be guided, the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, proceeds by negating self, non-self, and both — therefore there is no contradiction with scripture for the <s>Mādhyamikas</s>. For this very reason, the venerable <s>Āryadeva</s> has said:

children.translated_text: 'First, the turning away from demerit; in the middle, the turning away from self; /

children.text: sarvasya vāraṇaṃ paścādyo jānīte sa buddhimān || iti ||
children.translated_text: at the end, the turning away from all [views] — he who knows this is wise.' //

body.text: tathā ācāryapādairuktam-
body.translated_text: Likewise, the venerable <s>Ācārya</s> [<s>Nāgārjuna</s>] has said:

children.translated_text: 'Just as a grammarian would teach even the alphabet, /
the <s>Buddha</s> taught the <s>Dharma</s> to beings to be guided according to their capacity.' //
'To some he taught the <s>Dharma</s> for turning away from evil; /
to some for the accomplishment of merit; to some, what is based on the duality.' //
'To some, what is not based on duality — the profound, terrifying to the fearful, /
whose essence is emptiness and compassion — to some, the means of awakening.' //

body.text: athavā- ayamanyo 'rthaḥ- ātmetyapi prajñapitaṃ sāṃkhyādibhiḥ pratikṣaṇavinaśvarāṇāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ karmaphalasaṃbandhābhāvamutprekṣya | anātmetyapi prajñapitaṃ lokāyatikaiḥ upapattyā ātmānaṃ saṃsartāramapaśyadbhiḥ-
body.translated_text: Alternatively, another meaning is this: 'Self' has been designated by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> and others, who imagine that there is no connection between <s>karma</s> and its fruit for momentarily perishing <s>saṃskāras</s>. 'Non-self' has been designated by the <s>Lokāyatikas</s> (materialists), who through reasoning do not see a self that transmigrates:

children.translated_text: 'A person is only as much as the range of the senses. /
Good lady, this is a wolf's footprint — what the learned ones say.' //

body.text: ityādinā | taimirikopalabdhakeśamaśakādiṣviva vitaimirikairiva bālajanaparikalpitātmānātmādivastusvarūpaṃ sarvathaivāpaśyadbhiḥ-
body.translated_text: And so forth. By those who, like the clear-sighted regarding hair, flies, and so on apprehended by one with an eye-disease (<s>taimirika</s>), do not see in any way whatsoever the own-nature of entities such as self, non-self, and the like, which are constructed by foolish people —

body.text: buddhairnātmā na cānātmā kaścidityapi deśitam ||
body.translated_text: Neither self nor non-self has been taught as something by the <s>Buddhas</s>. //

body.text: yathoktamāryatathāgataguhyasūtre-
body.translated_text: As stated in the noble <s>Tathāgataguhyasūtra</s> —

body.text: atha khalu śāntamatirbodhisattvo bhagavantametadavocat- upaśama upaśama iti bhagavannucyate, ka eṣa upaśamo nāma? kasya copaśamādupaśama ityucyate? bhagavānāha- upaśama iti kulaputra
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Śāntamati</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Pacification, pacification — so it is said, <s>Bhagavān</s>. What is this called pacification? And through the pacification of what is it called pacification?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Pacification, O son of good family

body.text: ucyate, kleśopaśamasyaitadadhivacanam | kleśopaśama iti saṃkalpavikalpaparikalpopaśamasyaitadadhivacanam | saṃkalpavikalpaparikalpopaśama iti saṃjñāmanasikāropaśamasyaitadadhivacanam | saṃjñāmanasikāropaśama iti viparyāsopaśamasyaitadadhivacanam | viparyāsopaśama iti hetvārambaṇopaśamasyaitadadhivacanam | hetvārambaṇopaśama iti avidyābhavatṛṣṇopaśamasyaitadadhivacanam | avidyābhavatṛṣṇopaśama iti ahaṃkāramamakāropaśamasyaitadadhivacanam | ahaṃkāramamakāropaśama iti ucchedaśāśvatadṛṣṭayupaśamasyaitadadhivacanam | ucchedaśāśvatadṛṣṭayupaśama iti satkāyadṛṣṭayupaśamasyaitadadhivacanam iti śāntamate ye kecidārambaṇahetudṛṣṭisaṃyuktāḥ saṃkleśāḥ pravartante, sarve te satkāyadṛṣṭerutpadyante, satkāyadṛṣṭayupaśamātsarvadṛṣṭayupaśama iti | sarvadṛṣṭayupaśamātsarvapraṇidhānopaśama iti | sarvaprāṇi dhānopaśamātsarvakleśopaśamaḥ | tadyathāpi nāma śāntamate vṛkṣasya mūle chinne sarvaśākhāpatraphalāni śuṣyanti, evameva śāntamate satkāyadṛṣṭayupaśamātsarvakleśā upaśāmyante | satkāyadṛṣṭau śāntamate aparijñātāyāṃ sarvopādānopakleśā utpadyante | satkāyadṛṣṭiparijñāto 'pi sarvopādānopakleśā notpadyante na bādhante ||
body.translated_text: — so it is said — this is a designation for the pacification of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). The pacification of afflictions — this is a designation for the pacification of conceptualization, differentiation, and imaginative construction. The pacification of conceptualization, differentiation, and imaginative construction — this is a designation for the pacification of perception and mental attention. The pacification of perception and mental attention — this is a designation for the pacification of perversions. The pacification of perversions — this is a designation for the pacification of causes and objects. The pacification of causes and objects — this is a designation for the pacification of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>bhava</s> (existence), and <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving). The pacification of ignorance, existence, and craving — this is a designation for the pacification of I-making and mine-making. The pacification of I-making and mine-making — this is a designation for the pacification of the views of annihilation and eternalism. The pacification of the views of annihilation and eternalism — this is a designation for the pacification of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the existing body).' '<s>Śāntamati</s>, whatever afflictions arise that are conjoined with the view of objects, causes, and [wrong] views — all of them arise from <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>. Through the pacification of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, there is the pacification of all views. Through the pacification of all views, there is the pacification of all aspirations. Through the pacification of all aspirations, there is the pacification of all afflictions. Just as, <s>Śāntamati</s>, when the root of a tree is cut, all its branches, leaves, and fruits wither — even so, <s>Śāntamati</s>, through the pacification of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, all afflictions are pacified. When <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, <s>Śāntamati</s>, is not fully comprehended, all the secondary afflictions of clinging arise. When <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> is fully comprehended, all the secondary afflictions of clinging do not arise and do not afflict.'

body.text: śāntamatirāha- kā punarbhagavan satkāyadṛṣṭiparijñā? bhagavānāha- ātmāsamutthānaṃ śāntamate satkāyadṛṣṭiparijñā sattvāsamutthānaṃ jivāsamutthānaṃ pudgalāsamutthānaṃ dṛṣṭayasamutthānaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiparijñā na khalu punaḥ śāntamate sā dṛṣṭiradhyātmaṃ pratiṣṭhitā, na bahirdhā pratiṣṭhitā | sā dṛṣṭiḥ sarvato 'pratiṣṭhitā | yattasyā apratiṣṭhitāyā dṛṣṭerapratiṣṭhiteti jñānam, iyaṃ śāntamate satkāyadṛṣṭiparijñā | satkāyadṛṣṭiparijñeti śāntamate śunyatāyā etadadhivacanam | yacchūnyatānulomikyā kṣāntyā tāṃ dṛṣṭi nodgṛhṇāti, iyamapi śāntamate satkāyadṛṣṭiparijñā | satkāya iti śāntamate śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitānabhisaṃskārājātānutpādadṛṣṭayā tāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ nodgṛhṇāti, iyamapi śāntamate satkāyadṛṣṭiparijñā | satkāya iti śāntamate akāya eṣaḥ, na kasati na vikasati na cinoti nopacinoti, ādita eva tadabhūtaṃ parikalpitam | yacca abhūtaṃ parikalpitam, tanna parikalpitaṃ na parikalpyate na vikalpyate, tanna kriyate na viṭhapyate, notthāpyate nādhyavasyate | taducyate upaśama iti ||
body.translated_text: <s>Śāntamati</s> said: 'What, then, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the full comprehension of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'The non-arising of self, <s>Śāntamati</s>, is the full comprehension of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>. The non-arising of a being, the non-arising of a life-force, the non-arising of a <s>pudgala</s> (person), the non-arising of views — that is the full comprehension of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>. Moreover, <s>Śāntamati</s>, that view is not established internally, nor is it established externally. That view is entirely without establishment. The knowledge that it is unestablished when that view is unestablished — this, <s>Śāntamati</s>, is the full comprehension of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>. The full comprehension of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>, <s>Śāntamati</s>, is a designation for <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). That which, by the patient acceptance conforming to emptiness, does not grasp that view — this too, <s>Śāntamati</s>, is the full comprehension of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>. The existing body (<s>satkāya</s>), <s>Śāntamati</s> — [one who] through the views of emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, non-construction, and non-arising does not grasp that view — this too, <s>Śāntamati</s>, is the full comprehension of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>. The existing body (<s>satkāya</s>), <s>Śāntamati</s>, is [in truth] a non-body — it does not expand, does not spread, does not accumulate, does not pile up. From the very beginning, it was imagined as unreal. And what is imagined as unreal — that is not imagined, is not being imagined, is not discriminated; it is not made, not established, not raised up, not determined. That is called pacification.'

body.text:
śāntamatirāha- upaśānta upaśānta iti bhagavannucyate, kasyopaśamādupaśānta ityucyate |
bhagavānāha- ārambaṇataḥ śāntamate cittaṃ jvalati | yanna bhūya ālambanīkaroti tanna jvalati, ajvalan upaśānta ityucyate | tadyathāpi nāma śāntamate agnirupādānato jvalati, anupādānataḥ śāmyati, evameva ālambanataścittaṃ jvalati anālambanataḥ śāmyati | tatra śāntamate upāyakuśalo 'yaṃ bodhisattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāpariśuddhaḥ ālambanasamatāṃ ca prajānāti, kuśalamūlālambanaṃ ca śamayati | ityādi || 6 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Śāntamati</s> said: 'Pacified, pacified — so it is said, <s>Bhagavān</s>. Through the pacification of what is it called pacified?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'From its object, <s>Śāntamati</s>, the mind blazes. When it no longer takes as an object, it does not blaze; not blazing, it is called pacified. Just as, <s>Śāntamati</s>, fire blazes from fuel and is extinguished without fuel — even so, the mind blazes from its object and is pacified without an object. Therein, <s>Śāntamati</s>, this <s>Bodhisattva</s>, skillful in means, purified through <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, understands the equality of objects and pacifies the taking of wholesome roots as objects.' And so forth. // 6 //

body.text: atrāha- yadi buddhairbhagavadbhirnātmeti deśitam, nānātmeti, kiṃ tarhi deśitamiti? ucyate-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: 'If by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, neither self has been taught, nor non-self — then what has been taught?' The reply is:

children.translated_text: What is to be expressed has ceased, the domain of thought having ceased. /
For <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of things), like <s>nirvāṇa</s>, is unarisen and unceased. // 7 //

body.text: iha yadi kiṃcidabhidhātavyaṃ vastu syāt, taddeśyeta | yadā tu abhidhātavyaṃ nivṛttam, vācāṃ viṣayo nāsti, tadā kiṃcidapi naiva deśyate buddhaiḥ | kasmātpunarabhidhātavyaṃ nāstītyāha- nivṛtte cittagocare iti | cittasya gocaraḥ cittagocaraḥ | gocaro viṣayaḥ | ārambaṇamityarthaḥ | yadi cittasya kaścid gocaraḥ syāt, tatra kiṃcinnimittamadhyāropya syād vācāṃ pravṛttiḥ | yadā tu cittasya viṣaya evānupapannaḥ, tadā kva nimittādhyāropaḥ, yena vācāṃ pravṛttiḥ syāt? kasmāt punaścittaviṣayo nāstīti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Here, if there were some entity to be expressed, it would be taught. But when what is to be expressed has ceased — when there is no domain for words — then nothing whatsoever is taught by the <s>Buddhas</s>. Why, then, is there nothing to be expressed? He says: 'the domain of thought having ceased.' The domain of thought is the object of thought — the domain, object, support — this is the meaning. If there were some domain of thought, then by superimposing some sign there, there would be the operation of words. But when the very domain of thought is impossible, then where is the superimposition of a sign by which there would be the operation of words? Why, moreover, is there no domain of thought? Explaining this, he says —

body.text: anutpannāniruddhā hi nirvāṇamiva dharmatā |
body.translated_text: For <s>dharmatā</s>, like <s>nirvāṇa</s>, is unarisen and unceased. /

body.text: yasmādanutpannāniruddhā nirvāṇamiva dharmatā dharmasvabhāvaḥ dharmaprakṛtiḥ vyavasthāpitā, tasmānna tatra cittaṃ pravartate | cittasyāpravṛttau ca kuto nimittādhyāropaḥ? tadabhāvāt kuto vācāṃ pravṛttiḥ? ataśca na kiṃcid buddhairbhagavadbhirdeśitamiti sthitamavikalam | ata eva ca vakṣyati-
body.translated_text: Since <s>dharmatā</s> — the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>, the intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s> — has been established as unarisen and unceased, like <s>nirvāṇa</s>, therefore the mind does not operate there. And when the mind does not operate, whence the superimposition of a sign? In its absence, whence the operation of words? Therefore, it is established fully and without deficiency that nothing whatsoever has been taught by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>. And for this very reason, he will say later —

body.text:
sarvopalambhopaśamaḥ prapañcopaśamaḥ śivaḥ |
na kvacitkasyacitkaściddharmo buddhena deśitaḥ || iti |
body.translated_text: 'The pacification of all apprehension, the pacification of <s>prapañca</s> (conceptual proliferation), is auspicious. / No <s>dharma</s> whatsoever has been taught by the <s>Buddha</s> to anyone, anywhere.' //

body.text: evaṃ caitat ||
body.translated_text: And so it is. //

body.text: athavā | ayamanyaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ- yaduktaṃ prapañcaḥ śūnyatāyāṃ nirudhyate iti, kathaṃ punaḥ prapañcasya śūnyatāyāṃ nirodha iti? ucyate | yasmānnivṛttamabhidhātavyamityādi pūrvavad vyākhyeyam ||
body.translated_text: Alternatively, here is another objection: What was stated — 'conceptual proliferation ceases in emptiness' — how, then, does conceptual proliferation cease in emptiness? The reply is: Since what is to be expressed has ceased — and so forth, which should be explained as before. //

body.text: athavā yadetaduktaṃ prāgādhyātmikabāhyavastvanupalambhena adhyātmaṃ bahiśca yaḥ sarvadā ahaṃkāramamakāraparikṣayaḥ, idamatra tattvamiti | kīdṛśaṃ tat kiṃvat, vaktuṃ vā śakyate, tasmāt
body.translated_text: Alternatively, what was stated earlier — that through the non-apprehension of internal and external entities, the complete destruction of I-making and mine-making, both internally and externally and at all times, is the truth herein — what is the nature of that? What is it like? Can it be expressed? Therefore —

body.text: nivṛttamabhidhātavyaṃ nivṛtte cittagocare |
body.translated_text: What is to be expressed has ceased, the domain of thought having ceased. /

body.text: tatra tattvataḥ iti vākyaśeṣaḥ | kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ tatra tattve nivṛttamabhidhātavyaṃ nivṛtte cittagocare ityāha-
body.translated_text: There, 'in ultimate truth' is the completion of the sentence. What, moreover, is the reason that there, in the ultimate truth, what is to be expressed has ceased and the domain of thought has ceased? He says —

body.text: anutpannāniruddhā hi nirvāṇamiva dharmatā ||
body.translated_text: For <s>dharmatā</s>, like <s>nirvāṇa</s>, is unarisen and unceased. //

body.text: iti pūrvakameva vyākhyānaṃ yojyam || ata evoktamāryatathāgataguhyasūtre-
body.translated_text: The earlier explanation should be applied here. // For this very reason, it is stated in the noble <s>Tathāgataguhyasūtra</s> —

body.text: yāṃ ca śāntamate rātriṃ tathāgato 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ, yāṃ ca rātrimanupādāya parinirvāsyati, asminnantare tathāgatena ekākṣaramapi nodāhṛtaṃ na pravyāhṛtaṃ na pravyāhariṣyati | kathaṃ tarhi bhagavatā sakalasurāsuranarakiṃnarasiddhavidyādharoragaprabhṛtivineyajanebhyo vividhaprakārebhyo dharmadeśanā deśitā? ekakṣaṇavāgudāhāreṇaiva tattajjanamanastamoharaṇī bahuvidhabuddhinalinīvanavibodhinī jarāmaraṇasaritsāgarocchoṣiṇī kalpakālānalasaptārkaraśmivisarahrepiṇī śaradaruṇamahāprabheti ||
body.translated_text: On the night, <s>Śāntamati</s>, when the <s>Tathāgata</s> fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect awakening, and on the night when he will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without clinging — in this interval, not a single syllable has been uttered by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, nor spoken, nor will be spoken. How, then, has a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> of various kinds been taught by the <s>Bhagavān</s> to the assembly of beings to be trained — consisting of all <s>devas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>narakas</s>, <s>kiṃnaras</s>, <s>siddhas</s>, <s>vidyādharas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, and others? By a single-moment vocal utterance alone — [a speech that] dispels the mental darkness of each respective being, that opens the varied lotus-groves of <s>Buddha</s>-intelligence, that dries up the rivers and oceans of old age and death, that melts away the seven rays of the fires of the end of the <s>kalpa</s>, and that is like the great radiance of the autumn dawn.

body.text: tadevaṃ sūtre-
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, in the <s>sūtra</s> —

children.translated_text: Just as a mechanical instrument produces music when stirred by the wind, /

children.text: na cātra vādakaḥ kaścinniścarantyatha ca svarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and there is no musician there, yet sounds come forth; //

body.text:
evaṃ pūrvasuśuddhatvātsarvasattvāśayeritā |
vāgniścarati buddhasya na cāsyāstīha kalpanā |
pratiśrutkādayaḥ śabdā nādhyātmaṃ na bahiḥ sthitāḥ |
vāgapyevaṃ narendrasya nādhyātmaṃ na bahiḥ sthitāḥ || iti |
body.translated_text: even so, because of prior complete purity, stirred by the dispositions of all beings, / the speech of the <s>Buddha</s> comes forth, yet he has no conceptualization herein. / Sounds such as echoes are not established internally or externally; / even so, the speech of the Lord of Men is not established internally or externally. //

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise —

children.text: devata codani dundubhi divya karmavipāka nivṛtta marūṇaṃ |
children.translated_text: The <s>devas</s> caused a divine drum to sound — the result of the <s>karma</s> of the gods; /

children.text: deva pamattavihāriṇa ñātvā dundubhighoṣa pamuñci nabhāto ||
children.translated_text: knowing the <s>devas</s> to be dwelling in heedlessness, it released its drum-sound from the sky. //

children.text: sarva anitya aśāśvata kāmā itvara adhruva phenasabhāvāḥ |
children.translated_text: All pleasures are impermanent, non-eternal, transient, unstable, of the nature of foam; /
like illusions and mirages, like reflections in water — all existences are of the nature of dreams. /

children.text: dundubhi vādita śakramarudbhiḥ sārddhaya saṃkrami dharmasabhāyām |
children.translated_text: The drum was sounded by <s>Śakra</s> together with the <s>Maruts</s>, and it moved to the <s>Dharma</s>-assembly; /

children.text: dharmakathāṃ pakaroti marūṇāṃ yā katha śānta virāganukūlā ||
children.translated_text: it delivered a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> to the gods — a discourse that accords with peace and dispassion. //

body.text: tathā āryasamādhirāje-
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the noble <s>Samādhirājasūtra</s> —

children.text: buddho yadā bheṣyati dharmarājaḥ sarvāṇa dharmāṇa pakāśako muniḥ |
children.translated_text: When the <s>Buddha</s> will be the <s>Dharma</s>-king, the <s>Muni</s> who illuminates all <s>dharmas</s>, /

children.text: tṛṇagulmavṛkṣauṣadhi śaila parvata abhāva dharmāṇa ravo bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: from grass, shrubs, trees, herbs, mountains, and peaks, the sound of the non-existence of <s>dharmas</s> will arise. //

children.text: yāvanti śabdāstahi lokadhātau sarve hyabhāvā na hi kaści bhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: However many sounds there are in that world-realm — all are non-existent, for nothing truly exists; /

children.text: tāvantu kho tasya tathāgatasya svaru niścarī lokavināyakasya ||
children.translated_text: just so many sounds come forth from that <s>Tathāgata</s>, the guide of the world. //

body.text: iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: And so forth in detail. //

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise —

children.text: ekasvarā tu tava lokahito nānādhimukti svaru niścarati |
children.translated_text: Your single voice, O benefactor of the world, comes forth in accord with the varied dispositions; /

children.text: ekaikamanvimamabhāṣi jino brūhi smitaṃ prakṛtakasya kṛte || iti ||
children.translated_text: the Conqueror spoke to each one individually — tell me, for whose sake was the smile? //

body.text: atraike paricodayanti- nāstikāviśiṣṭā mādhyamikāḥ, yasmāt kuśalākuśalaṃ karma kartāraṃ ca phalaṃ ca sarvaṃ ca lokaṃ bhāvasvabhāvaśūnyamiti bruvate | nāstikā api hi etannāstīti bruvate | tasmānnāstikāviśiṣṭā mādhyamikā iti | naivam | kutaḥ? pratītyasamutpādavādino hi mādhyamikāḥ hetupratyayān prāpya pratītya samutpannatvāt sarvameva ihalokaparalokaṃ niḥsvabhāvaṃ varṇayanti | yathāsvarūpavādino naiva nāstikāḥ pratītyasamutpannatvād bhāvasvabhāvaśunyatvena na paralokādyabhāvaṃ
body.translated_text: Here some raise the objection: 'The <s>Mādhyamikas</s> are no different from nihilists, since they declare wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s>, the agent, the fruit, and the entire world to be empty of intrinsic nature. For nihilists too say "this does not exist." Therefore the <s>Mādhyamikas</s> are no different from nihilists.' This is not so. Why? Because the <s>Mādhyamikas</s> are proponents of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination). They describe everything — this world and the next — as without own-nature, precisely because it is dependently arisen. Those who speak in accordance with the true nature of things are certainly not nihilists — since, because of [things] being dependently arisen and therefore empty of intrinsic nature, they do not maintain the non-existence of the next world and so forth

body.text: pratipannāḥ | kiṃ tarhi aihalaukikaṃ vastujātamupalabhya svabhāvataḥ tasya paralokādihāgamanam, ihalokācca paralokagamanapaśyantuḥ ihalokopalabdhapadārthasadṛśapadārthāntarāpavādaṃ kurvanti | tathāpi vastusvarūpeṇa avidyamānasyaiva te nāstitvaṃ pratipannāḥ ityamunā tāvaddarśanena sāmyamastīti cet, na hi | kutaḥ? saṃvṛtyā mādhyamikairastitvenābhyupagamānna tulyatā | vastutastulyateti cet, yadyapi vastuto 'siddhistulyā, tathāpi pratipatṛbhedādatulyatā | yathā hi kṛtacaurya puruṣamekaḥ samyagaparijñāyaiva tadamitrapreritaḥ taṃ mithyā vyācaṣṭe cauryamanena kṛtamiti, aparastu sākṣād dṛṣṭvā dūṣayati, tatra yadyapi vastuto nāsti bhedaḥ, tathāpi parijñātṛbhedādekastatra mṛṣāvādītyucyate, aparastu satyavādīti, ekaśca ayaśasā ca apuṇyena ca samyak parīkṣyamāṇo yujyate nāparaḥ, evamihāpi yathāvadviditavastusvarūpāṇāṃ mādhyamikānāṃ bruvatāmavagacchatāṃ ca vastusvarūpābhede 'pi yathāvadaviditavastusvarūpairnāstikaiḥ saha jñānābhidhānayornāsti sāmyam | yathaiva hi upekṣāsāmānye 'pi apratisaṃkhyāya pratisaṃkhyāya upekṣakayoriva pṛthagjanārhatoḥ jātyandhacakṣuṣmatośca viṣamaprapātapradeśaviniścitasāmānye 'pi yathāsti mahān viśeṣaḥ, tathā nāstikānāṃ mādhyamikānāṃ ca viśeṣo bhaviṣyatīti pūrvācāryāḥ | ityalaṃ prasaṅgenaḥ prakṛtameva vyākhyāsyāmaḥ || 7 ||
body.translated_text: . Rather, nihilists, having perceived the entities of this world as real, deny the existence of other entities similar to the entities perceived in this world — [they deny] the coming [of beings] from the next world to this world, and the going from this world to the next world. Even so, they maintain the non-existence of what does not in fact exist in its own real nature — if one says 'then there is similarity through this view,' no, that is not so. Why? Because the <s>Mādhyamikas</s> accept [things] as existent conventionally, there is no equivalence. 'But there is equivalence in terms of reality' — even if the non-establishment in terms of reality is equivalent, nevertheless, because of the difference in the knowers, there is non-equivalence. For just as when one man is falsely accused of theft — one person, without truly knowing, prompted by an enemy, falsely accuses him, saying 'theft was committed by this one,' while another denounces him having directly witnessed it — there, even though in reality there is no difference, nevertheless, because of the difference in the knowers, one is called a liar and the other a truth-teller; and one, when properly examined, is liable to disgrace and demerit, but not the other. Even so here, there is no equivalence in knowledge and expression between the <s>Mādhyamikas</s>, who know the true nature of things as it really is — whether speaking or understanding — and the nihilists, who do not know the true nature of things as it really is, even though there is no difference in the true nature of things. For just as, even though there is similarity in equanimity between an ordinary person and an <s>Arhat</s> who is equanimous with and without deliberate reflection — or between a person born blind and one with sight in their identical determination regarding a place with a precipitous drop — there is nevertheless a great difference, even so there will be a difference between nihilists and <s>Mādhyamikas</s> — so say the earlier masters. But enough of this digression — we shall explain the subject at hand. // 7 //

body.text: atrāha- yadyapi evam
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: Even though thus

body.text: anutpannāniruddhā hi nirvāṇamiva dharmatā |
body.translated_text: the nature of things (<s>dharmatā</s>), like <s>nirvāṇa</s>, is unarisen and unceased, /

body.text: tasyāṃ ca nāsti vākcittayoḥ pravṛttiḥ, tathāpi naivāsau adeśyamānā śakyā janairvijñātumiti avaśyaṃ tasyāmavatāraṇārthaṃ vineyajanānāṃ saṃvṛtisatyāpekṣayā kadāciddeśanānupūrvyā bhavitavyam, ityataḥ sā kathyatāmiti | ucyate | iyamatra buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ tattvāmṛtāvatāradeśanānupūrvī vijñeyā, yaduta-
body.translated_text: and there is no operation of speech and mind regarding it — nevertheless, since it cannot be known by people without being taught, there must necessarily be a gradual order of teaching for guiding disciples, with reference to conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>), for the purpose of leading them into it. Therefore, let that be stated. [Reply:] Here the following should be understood as the gradual order of teaching by which the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, lead [beings] into the nectar of reality (<s>tattvāmṛta</s>), namely:

children.text: sarvaṃ tathyaṃ na vā tathyaṃ tathyaṃ cātathyameva ca |
children.translated_text: Everything is real; or not real; both real and not real; /
neither not real nor real — this is the graded teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s>. // 8 //

body.text: tatra-
body.translated_text: Therein:

body.text:
yadyadyasya priyaṃ pūrvaṃ tattattasya samācaret |
na hi pratihataḥ pātraṃ saddharmasya kathaṃcana || iti |
body.translated_text:
Whatever is dear to whomever at first — that should be practiced for them.
For a vessel of the true <s>Dharma</s> is never rejected under any circumstances. //

body.text: tathā ca bhagavatoktam-
body.translated_text: And thus the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said:

body.text: loko mayā sārdhaṃ vivadati | nāhaṃ lokena sārdhaṃ vivadāmi | yalloke 'sti saṃmatam, tanmamāpyasti saṃmatam | yalloke nāsti saṃmatam, mamāpi tannāsti saṃmatam |
body.translated_text: 'The world disputes with me; I do not dispute with the world. What is accepted in the world, that is accepted by me too. What is not accepted in the world, that is not accepted by me either.'

body.text: ityāgamācca ||
body.translated_text: And from the <s>Āgama</s>:

children.text: nānyayā bhāṣayā mlecchaḥ śakyo grāhayituṃ yathā |
children.translated_text: Just as a barbarian (<s>mleccha</s>) cannot be made to understand by means of another language, /

children.text: na laukikamṛte lokaḥ śakyo grāhayituṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: so too the world cannot be made to understand except through the worldly [conventions]. //

body.text: ityādita eva tāvadbhagavatā svaprasiddhapadārthamedasvarūpavibhāgaśravaṇasaṃjātābhilāṣasya vineyajanasya yadetat skandhadhātvāyatanādikamavidyātaimirikaiḥ satyataḥ parikalpitamupalabdham, tadeva tāvat satyamityupavarṇitaṃ bhagavatā taddarśanāpekṣayā, ātmani lokasya gauravotpādanārtham | viditaniravaśeṣalokavṛttānto 'yaṃ bhagavān sarvajñaḥ sarvadarśī, yaḥ evaṃ bhavāgraparyantasya vāyumaṇḍalāderākāśadhātuparyavasānasya bhājanalokasya sattvalokasya ca aviparītaṃ sthityutpādapralayādikaṃ sātivicitraprabhedaṃ sahetukaṃ saphalaṃ sāsvādaṃ sādīnavaṃ copadiṣṭavāniti | tadevaṃ bhagavati utpannasarvajñabuddhivineyajanasya uttarakālaṃ tadeva sarvaṃ na vā tathyamityupadeśitam | tatra tathyaṃ nāma yasya anyathātvaṃ nāsti | vidyate ca pratikṣaṇavināśitvāt saṃskārāṇāmanyathābhāvaḥ, tasmādanyathābhāvasadbhāvānna vā tathyam | vāśabdaścakārārtho deśanāsamuccaye draṣṭavyaḥ | sarvaṃ tathyaṃ na ca tathyamiti ||
body.translated_text: Thus, at the very outset, for the disciple who has developed eagerness from hearing the classification of the essential forms of the categories well-known to him — the <s>Bhagavān</s> has described as 'real' that very thing which — namely the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and so forth — has been imagined as real and apprehended by those afflicted with the cataract of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). The <s>Bhagavān</s> described it thus with respect to their viewpoint, for the purpose of generating reverence for himself in the world. [They think:] 'This <s>Bhagavān</s>, the omniscient one, the all-seeing one, who knows the ways of the entire world without remainder — he has taught, without error, the persistence, arising, destruction, and the rest of the world-vessel from the wind-circle up to the realm of space, and of the world of beings, with their marvelously diverse classifications, together with their causes, fruits, pleasures, and dangers.' Then, at a later time, for the disciple in whom the conviction that the <s>Bhagavān</s> is omniscient has arisen, all that very same [teaching] was taught as 'not real.' Therein, 'real' (<s>tathya</s>) means that of which there is no alteration. And there is indeed alteration of the formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>), because of their momentary destruction. Therefore, because alteration does exist, [everything is] 'not real.' The particle 'vā' (or) should be understood as having the sense of 'ca' (and), indicating a combination of teachings: 'everything is real and not real.'

body.text: keṣāṃcit sarvametat tathyaṃ ca atathyaṃ ceti deśitam | tatra bālajanāpekṣayā sarvametat tathyam | āryajñānāpekṣayā tu sarvametanmṛṣā, tairevamanupalambhāditi ||
body.translated_text: To some it was taught that all this is both real and not real. Therein, with respect to foolish beings, all this is real; but with respect to the knowledge of the noble ones, all this is false — because they do not apprehend it in that way. //

body.text: keṣāṃcittu aticirābhyastatattvadarśanānāṃ kiṃcinmātrānutkhātāvaraṇatarūmūlānāṃ naivātathyaṃ naiva tathyaṃtaditi deśitam | tasyāpi kiṃcinmātrasyāvaraṇasya prahāṇārthaṃ vandhyāsutasya avadātaśyāmatāpratiṣedhavadubhayametat pratiṣiddham ||
body.translated_text: But to some — those who have practiced the vision of reality for a very long time, whose roots of the tree of obscurations have been slightly loosened — it was taught: 'this is neither not real nor real.' For the purpose of abandoning even that slight remaining obscuration, both [positions] are negated — like negating both fairness and darkness of the son of a barren woman. //

body.text: etacca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmanuśāsanam- unmārgādapanīya samyaṅmārgapratiṣṭhāpanaṃ śāsanam | evamānupūrvyā śāsanamanuśāsanam | vineyajananurūpyeṇa vā śāsanamanuśāsanam ||
body.translated_text: And this is the teaching (<s>anuśāsana</s>) of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>: instruction (<s>śāsana</s>) is leading away from the wrong path and establishing on the right path. And graduated instruction is <s>anuśāsana</s>. Or, instruction suited to the disciples is <s>anuśāsana</s>. //

body.text: sarvāścaitā deśanā buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākaruṇopāyajñānavatāṃ tattvāmṛtāvatāropāyatvena vyavasthitāḥ | na hi tathāgatāḥ tattvāmṛtāvatārānupāyabhūtavākyamudāharanti | vyādhyanurūpabhaiṣajyopasaṃhāravat te vineyajanānujighṛkṣayā yathānurūpaṃ dharmaṃ deśayanti | yathoktaṃ śatake-
body.translated_text: All these teachings of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, who possess great compassion, skillful means, and knowledge, are established as methods for leading [beings] into the nectar of reality. For the <s>Tathāgatas</s> do not utter a single word that is not a method for leading into the nectar of reality. Like the application of medicine suited to the disease, they teach the <s>Dharma</s> as appropriate, out of the desire to benefit the disciples. As stated in the <s>Śataka</s> (<s>Catuḥśataka</s>):

children.translated_text: It is taught as existent, non-existent, both existent and non-existent, and neither. /
Is not wholesome medicine, by its very name, born in accordance with the disease? //

body.text: kiṃlakṣaṇaṃ punaḥ tat tattvaṃ yasyaitā deśanā avatārārthamupadiśante bhagavantaḥ? uktametadasmābhiḥ-
body.translated_text: What, then, is the characteristic of that reality for entry into which the <s>Bhagavāns</s> give these teachings? We have already stated this:

body.text: nivṛttamabhidhātavyaṃ nivṛtte cittagocare | iti |
body.translated_text: 'That which is to be expressed has ceased, the domain of the mind having ceased.' //

body.text: yadā caitadevam, tadā kimaparaṃ pṛcchayate? yadyapyevam, tathāpi vyavahārasatyānurodhena laukikatathyādyabhyupagamavat tasyāpi samāropato lakṣaṇamucyatāmiti | taducyate-
body.translated_text: And when this is so, why do you ask further? Although this is so, nevertheless, just as there is acceptance of worldly truth and the like in accordance with conventional truth, let the characteristic of that [reality] too be stated by way of superimposition. That is stated:

children.translated_text: Not dependent on another, peaceful, not elaborated by conceptual proliferations (<s>prapañca</s>), /
free from conceptual construction (<s>nirvikalpa</s>), without diverse meaning — this is the characteristic of reality (<s>tattva</s>). // 9 //

body.text: tatra nāsmin parapratyayo 'stīti aparapratyayam | paropadeśāgamyam | svayamevādhigantavyamityarthaḥ | yathā hi taimirikā vitathaṃ keśamaśakamakṣikādirūpaṃ paśyanto vitimiropadeśenāpi na śaknuvanti keśānāṃ yathāvadavasthitaṃ svarūpamadarśananyāyena adhigantavyamataimirikā ivādhigantum, kiṃ tarhi ataimirikopadeśānmithyaitadityetāvanmātrakameva pratipadyante | yadā tu timiropaghātyaviparītaśūnyatādarśanāñjanāñjitabuddhinayanāḥ santaḥ samutpannatattvajñānā bhavanti, tadā tat tattvamanadhigamanayogena svayamadhigacchantīti | evamaparapratyayaṃ bhāvānāṃ yat svarūpaṃ tat tattvam | etacca śāntasvabhāvamataimirikakeśādarśanavat svabhāvavirahitamityarthaḥ | ata eva tat prapañcairaprapañcitam| prapañco hi vāk, prapañcayati arthāniti kṛtvā | prapañcairaprapañcitaṃ vāgbhiravyāhṛtamityarthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, 'not dependent on another' (<s>aparapratyaya</s>) — in it there is no dependence on another. It is not accessible through the instruction of another. The meaning is: it is to be realized by oneself alone. For just as those with cataracts, seeing false forms such as hairs, insects, flies, and so forth, are unable — even through the instruction of one free from cataracts — to realize the true nature of the hairs as they actually are (which is to be realized through the method of non-seeing), as one free from cataracts does; rather, from the instruction of one free from cataracts, they understand only this much: 'this is false.' But when, having their affliction of cataracts dispelled, with the eye of their intellect anointed with the eye-salve of the undistorted vision of emptiness, they come to possess the knowledge of reality — then they realize that reality by themselves, through the method of non-realization. Thus, the own-nature of entities that is not dependent on another — that is reality. And this is of a peaceful nature — like the non-seeing of hairs by one free from cataracts — meaning it is devoid of inherent nature. For this very reason it is 'not elaborated by conceptual proliferations.' For <s>prapañca</s> (proliferation) is speech — because it elaborates objects. 'Not elaborated by proliferations' means not uttered by speech. //

body.text: nirvikalpaṃ ca tat | vikalpaścittapracāraḥ | tadrahitatvāt tat tattvaṃ nirvikalpam | yathoktaṃ sūtre-
body.translated_text: And it is free from conceptual construction (<s>nirvikalpa</s>). <s>Vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) is the operation of the mind. Because it is free from that, reality is <s>nirvikalpa</s>. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>:

body.text: paramārthasatyaṃ katamat? yatra jñānasyāpyapracāraḥ, kaḥ punarvādo 'kṣarāṇāmiti |
body.translated_text: 'What is ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>)? That in which even knowledge does not operate — what need to speak of words (<s>akṣara</s>)?' //

body.text: evaṃ nirvikalpam ||
body.translated_text: Thus it is free from conceptual construction. //

body.text: nānārtho 'syeti nānārthaṃ bhinnārtham, na nānārthaḥ anānārtham, abhinnārthamityarthaḥ | yathoktamāryasatyadvayāvatārasūtre-
body.translated_text: '<s>Nānārtha</s>' — having diverse meaning; 'not <s>nānārtha</s>' is '<s>anānārtha</s>' — without diverse meaning, meaning undifferentiated. As stated in the noble <s>Satyadvayāvatāra Sūtra</s>:

body.text: devaputra āha- katamaḥ punarmañjuśrīḥ samyakprayogaḥ? mañjuśrīrāha- yatsamā devaputra paramārthatastathatā dharmadhātuḥ atyantājātiśca, tatsamāni paramārthataḥ pañcānantaryāṇi, yatsamāni pañcānantaryāṇi tatsamāni dṛṣṭikṛtāni, yatsamāni dṛṣṭikṛtāni tatsamāḥ pṛthagjanadharmāḥ, yatsamāḥ pṛthagjanadharmāḥ tatsamāḥ śaikṣadharmāḥ, yatsamāḥ śaikṣadharmāḥ tatsamā aśaikṣadharmāḥ, yatsamā aśaikṣadharmāḥ tatsamāḥ samyaksaṃbuddhadharmāḥ, yatsamāḥ samyaksaṃbuddhadharmāḥ tatsamaṃ nirvāṇam, yatsamaṃ nirvāṇaṃ tatsamaḥ saṃsāraḥ, yatsamaḥ saṃsāraḥ tatsamaḥ paramārthataḥ saṃkleśaḥ, yatsamaḥ paramārthataḥ saṃkleśaḥ tatsamaṃ paramārthato vyavadānam, yatsamaṃ paramārthato vyavadānaṃ tatsamāḥ paramārthataḥ sarvadharmāḥ | evaṃ paramārthataḥ sarvadharmasamatāprayukto devaputra bhikṣuḥ samyakprayukta ityucyate ||
body.translated_text: The <s>devaputra</s> said: 'What, then, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is right practice?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'That which in ultimate reality, O <s>devaputra</s>, is the sameness of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), and absolute non-arising — that same is, in ultimate reality, the five heinous acts (<s>ānantarya</s>). That which is the sameness of the five heinous acts — that same is the sameness of [acts] produced by [wrong] views. That which is the sameness of acts produced by views — that same is the sameness of the qualities of ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>). That which is the sameness of the qualities of ordinary persons — that same is the sameness of the qualities of those in training (<s>śaikṣa</s>). That which is the sameness of the qualities of those in training — that same is the sameness of the qualities of those beyond training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>). That which is the sameness of the qualities of those beyond training — that same is the sameness of the qualities of the Perfectly Awakened Ones. That which is the sameness of the qualities of the Perfectly Awakened Ones — that same is the sameness of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. That which is the sameness of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — that same is, in ultimate reality, the sameness of <s>saṃsāra</s>. That which is, in ultimate reality, the sameness of <s>saṃsāra</s> — that same is, in ultimate reality, the sameness of affliction (<s>saṃkleśa</s>). That which is, in ultimate reality, the sameness of affliction — that same is, in ultimate reality, the sameness of purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>). That which is, in ultimate reality, the sameness of purification — that same is, in ultimate reality, the sameness of all <s>dharmas</s>. Thus, a monk who is engaged in the sameness of all <s>dharmas</s> in ultimate reality, O <s>devaputra</s>, is said to be rightly practicing.' //

body.text: devaputra āha- katamayā punarmañjuśrīḥ samatayā yāvat paramārthato yatsamaṃ vyavadānaṃ tatsamāḥ sarvadharmāḥ paramārthata iti? mañjuśrīrāha- paramārthataḥ sarvadharmānutpādasamatayā paramārthataḥ sarvadharmātyantājātisamatayā paramārthataḥ samāḥ sarvadharmāḥ | tat kasmāddhetoḥ? paramārthato nirvāṇānānākaraṇā hi devaputra sarvadharmā atyantanirutpādatāmupādāya | tadyathāpi nāma devaputra yacca mṛddhājanasyāmyantaramākāśam, yacca ratnabhājanasyākāśam, ākāśadhātureva eṣaḥ | tat paramārthato na kiṃcinnānākaraṇam | evameva devaputra yaḥ saṃkleśaḥ, sa paramārthato 'tyantānutpādatā | yadapi vyavadānaṃ tadapi paramārthato 'tyantānutpādatā | saṃsāro 'pi paramārthato 'tyantānutpādatā | yāvannirvāṇamapi
body.translated_text: The <s>devaputra</s> said: 'By what sameness, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is it that in ultimate reality, as you say, that which is the sameness of purification is the sameness of all <s>dharmas</s>?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'In ultimate reality, through the sameness of the non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s>, through the sameness of the absolute non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s> — in ultimate reality, all <s>dharmas</s> are the same. For what reason? Because, O <s>devaputra</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> in ultimate reality are not different from <s>nirvāṇa</s>, on account of their absolute non-arising. Just as, O <s>devaputra</s>, the space within a vessel of clay and the space within a vessel of jewels — [both are] just the element of space. In ultimate reality, there is no differentiation whatsoever. Even so, O <s>devaputra</s>, that which is affliction — that, in ultimate reality, is absolute non-arising. And that which is purification — that too, in ultimate reality, is absolute non-arising. Even <s>saṃsāra</s>, in ultimate reality, is absolute non-arising. And even <s>nirvāṇa</s>

body.text: paramārthato 'tyantānutpādatā | nātra kiṃcitparamārthato nānākaraṇam | tat kasmāddhetoḥ? paramārthato 'tyantānutpādatvātsarvadharmāṇāmiti ||
body.translated_text: , in ultimate reality, is absolute non-arising. There is no differentiation whatsoever here in ultimate reality. For what reason? Because all <s>dharmas</s> in ultimate reality are absolutely unarisen.' //

body.text: tadevamanānārthatā tattvasya lakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam, śūnyataikarasatvāt | uttarottaravyākhyānaṃ cātra veditavyam || 9 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, the non-differentiation of reality should be understood as the characteristic of <s>tattva</s>, because of the single taste of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). And herein, each successive explanation should be understood [as progressively deeper]. // 9 //

body.text: evaṃ tāvadāryāṇāṃ jātijarāmaraṇasaṃsāraparikṣayāya kṛtakāryāṇāṃ tattvalakṣaṇam | laukikaṃ tu tattvalakṣaṇamadhikṛtyocyate-
body.translated_text: Thus, such is the characteristic of reality for the noble ones who have accomplished their task of exhausting birth, old age, death, and <s>saṃsāra</s>. But regarding the worldly characteristic of reality, it is said:

children.text: pratītya yadyadbhavati na hi tāvattadeva tat |
children.translated_text: Whatever arises in dependence on something — that is indeed not that very thing; /
nor is it something other than that — therefore it is neither annihilated nor eternal. // 10 //

body.text: yat kāraṇaṃ pratītya yat kāryamutpadyate, tadyathā śālibījaṃ pratītya pṛthivyādisāmagrīṃ ca śālyaṅkura upajāyate, na hi tāvat tadeva taditi śakyate vaktum | naiva yadeva bījaṃ sa eva aṅkuraḥ, janyajanakayorekatvaprasaṅgāt | tataśca pitāputrayorapi ekatvaṃ syāt | ananyatvācca aṅkurāvasthāyāmaṅkuravadbījagrahaṇamapi syāt, bījavacca aṅkurasyāpi grahaṇaṃ syāt | nityatvaṃ caivaṃ bījasya syāt, avināśābhyupagamāt | tataśca śāśvatavādaprasaṅgānmahādoṣarāśiḥ syāt karmaphalādyabhāvaprasaṅgāt | evaṃ tāvad yadeva bījaṃ sa eva aṅkuraḥ iti na yujyate | na ca anyadapi tattasmāt | nāpi bījādaṅkurasyānyatvam, bījamantareṇāpi aṅkurodayaprasaṅgāt |
body.translated_text: Whatever effect arises in dependence on whatever cause — for example, a rice sprout arises in dependence on a rice seed together with the aggregate of earth and the rest — it cannot be said that 'it is that very thing.' The seed itself is not the sprout, because of the absurd consequence that the produced and the producer would be identical. And from that, father and son too would be identical. And because of non-otherness, at the stage of the sprout there would be the grasping of the seed just as of the sprout, and the grasping of the sprout just as of the seed. And the seed would thus be permanent, because of the acceptance of its non-destruction. And from that, because of the consequence of eternalism, there would be a great mass of faults, including the consequence of the non-existence of <s>karma</s>, its fruit, and so forth. Thus, 'the seed itself is the sprout' is not justified. 'Nor is it something other than that' — nor is the sprout other than the seed, because of the consequence that even without the seed a sprout could arise.

body.text: yadyanyadanyadanyasmādanyasmādapyṛte bhavet |
body.translated_text: 'If what is other were [truly] other, it would exist even without the other' — /

body.text: iti vacanādaṅkurāvasthāne'pi bījānucchedaprasaṅgāt | tataśca satkāryavādadoṣaḥ syāt | yataścaivaṃ yat kāraṇaṃ pratītya yat kāryamutpadyate, naiva tat kāraṇaṃ kāryaṃ bhavati, na ca tasmātkāraṇāttat kāryamanyat | tasmānna kāraṇamucchinnaṃ nāpi śāśvatamiti śakyate vyavasthāpayitum | yathoktamāryadevapādaiḥ-
body.translated_text: by this statement, [and] because of the consequence that even at the stage of the sprout the seed would not be annihilated — from that there would be the defect of the <s>satkāryavāda</s> (doctrine that the effect pre-exists in the cause). And since thus whatever effect arises in dependence on whatever cause — the cause does not become the effect, nor is the effect other than that cause — therefore it can be established that the cause is neither annihilated nor eternal. As stated by the venerable <s>Āryadeva</s>:

body.text:
yasmātpravartate bhāvastenocchedo na jāyate |
yasmānnivartate bhāvastena nityo na jāyate || iti |
body.translated_text:
'From that out of which an entity proceeds — by that, annihilation does not arise;
from that out of which an entity ceases — by that, permanence does not arise.' //

body.text: uktaṃ ca āryalalitavistarasūtre-
body.translated_text: And it is said in the noble <s>Lalitavistara Sūtra</s>:

children.text: bījasya sato yathāṅkuro na ca yo bīja sa caiva aṅkuro |
children.translated_text: 'Just as when the seed exists, there is the sprout — yet the seed is not the sprout; /

children.text: na ca anyu tato na caiva tadevamanuccheda aśāśvata dharmatā ||
children.translated_text: nor is it other than that, nor is it that very thing — thus the nature of things (<s>dharmatā</s>) is neither annihilation nor permanence.' //

body.text: tadevaṃ yathopavarṇitena nyāyena-
body.translated_text: Thus, by the reasoning as described above:

children.translated_text: Not of manifold meaning, not of uniform meaning, not annihilation, not permanence — /
this is the nectar of the teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the protectors of the world. // 11 //

body.text: mahākaruṇopāyamahāmeghapaṭalanirantarāvacchāditākāśadhātuparyantadiṅmaṇḍalānāṃ rāgādikleśagaṇasamudācārātitīkṣṇatarādityamaṇḍalopatāpitajagajjātijarāmaraṇaduḥkhadahanasaṃtāpopaśamatatparāṇāṃ satatāviratayathānurūpacaritapratipakṣasaddharmadeśanāmṛtadhārāpātaiḥ yathānurūpavineyajanakuśalamūlaśasyauṣadhiphalaphullalatotpannātivṛddhayanujidhṛkṣūṇāṃ saddharmāmṛtamahāvarṣavarṣiṇāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhamahānāgānāmatrāṇālaukikatrāṇānāmanāthanāthānāṃ sakalalokanāthānāmetat tatsaddharmāmṛtaṃ sakalatraidhātukabhavaduḥkhakṣayasvabhāvaṃ yathopavarṇitena nyāyena ekatvānyatvarahitaṃ śāśvatocchedavādavigataṃ ca vijñeyam | etaddharmatattvāmṛtapratipannānāṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ śrutacintābhāvanākramāt pravartamānānāṃ śīlasamādhiprajñātmakaskandhatrayāmṛtarasasya upayogānniyatameva jarāmaraṇakṣayasvabhāvanirvāṇādhigamo bhavati | athāpi kathaṃcidiha aparipakvakuśalamūlatayā śrutvāpyetat saddharmāmṛtam, dṛṣṭa eva dharme na mokṣamāsādayanti, tathāpi janmāntare 'pi avaśyameṣāṃ pūrvahetubalādeva niyatā siddhiḥ saṃpadyate | yathoktaṃ śatake-
body.translated_text: Of those <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> Great <s>Nāgas</s> (supreme beings) — who are the unworldly refuge of the refugeless, the protectors of the unprotected, the lords of all the worlds — whose canopy of clouds of great compassion and skillful means continuously covers the expanse of the sky-realm in all directions, who are intent upon alleviating the burning torment of the suffering of birth, old age, and death afflicting the world scorched by the sun-disc of the defilements of passion and so forth, fiercer than any [ordinary sun], who, through the constant and unceasing outpouring of the nectar-streams of the true <s>Dharma</s>-teaching as the appropriate antidote practiced according to suitability, wish to nurture and sustain the abundant crops, herbs, fruits, and blossoming vines of the wholesome roots of the trainable beings appropriate [to each teaching], who rain the great rain of the nectar of the true <s>Dharma</s> — that nectar of their true <s>Dharma</s>, whose nature is the destruction of all suffering of existence in the three realms, should be understood, by the method described above, as devoid of unity and otherness, and free from the doctrines of eternalism and annihilationism. For <s>Śrāvakas</s> who have realized this nectar of the truth of <s>dharmas</s>, proceeding through the stages of hearing, reflection, and meditation, through the partaking of the nectar-essence of the three aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) consisting of moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> whose nature is the destruction of old age and death certainly occurs. Moreover, even if some, due to the immaturity of their wholesome roots, having heard this nectar of the true <s>Dharma</s>, do not attain liberation in this very life, nevertheless even in a future birth their definite accomplishment is certainly achieved by the very force of their prior causes. As stated in the <s>Śataka</s>:

children.translated_text: Even if the knower of truth does not attain <s>nirvāṇa</s> here [in this life],
he will certainly obtain it effortlessly in the next birth, like [the fruit of] <s>karma</s>. //

body.text: athāpi kathaṃcit-
body.translated_text: Moreover, even if somehow —

body.text: saṃbuddhānāmanutpāde śrāvakāṇāṃ punaḥ kṣaye |
body.translated_text: When perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s> have not arisen, and when <s>Śrāvakas</s> have ceased to exist,

body.text: sati, āryamārgopadeśakakalyāṇamitrapratyayavaikalyāt na syād dharmatattvāmṛtādhigamaḥ, tathāpi pūrvajanmāntaradharmatattvaśravaṇahetubalādeva aihalaukikopadeśanirapekṣāṇāmapi pravivekasevāmātropanatapratyayānāṃ svāyaṃbhuvaṃ-
body.translated_text: due to the absence of the condition of a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) who teaches the noble path, there would be no attainment of the nectar of the truth of <s>dharmas</s> — even so, by the very force of having heard the truth of <s>dharmas</s> in a previous birth, for those who do not depend on worldly instruction, for whom the condition has arisen merely through the pursuit of solitude, the self-arisen —

body.text: jñānaṃ pratyekabuddhānāmasaṃsargātpravartate || 12 ||
body.translated_text: knowledge of the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> arises from seclusion (<s>asaṃsarga</s>). // 12 //

body.text: kāyacetasoḥ praviveko 'saṃsargaḥ, kalyāṇamitrāparyeṣaṇaṃ vā | tasmādasaṃsargāddhetoḥ pratyekabuddhānāmasaṃbuddhake 'pi kāle yasmādbhavatyeva dharmatattvādhigamaḥ, tasmādabandhyā siddhirasya saṃbuddhamahāvaidyarājapraṇītasya saddharmatattvāmṛtabhaiṣajyasyeti vijñeyam | yataśca etadevam, ato 'rhati prājñaḥ prāṇānapi parityajya saddharmatattvaṃ paryeṣitumiti | yathoktaṃ bhagavatā āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāṃ bhagavatyām-
body.translated_text: Seclusion (<s>asaṃsarga</s>) is the solitude of body and mind, or the non-seeking of a spiritual friend. From that cause of seclusion, because even in a <s>Buddha</s>-less age the attainment of the truth of <s>dharmas</s> does occur for <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, therefore the efficacy of this nectar-medicine of the truth of the true <s>Dharma</s> prescribed by the <s>Sambuddha</s> great physician-king is not barren — this should be understood. And since this is so, therefore the wise person should seek the truth of the true <s>Dharma</s> even at the cost of abandoning life itself. As stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Bhagavatī</s>:

body.text: kathaṃ ca bhagavan sadāpraruditena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā paryeṣitā? evamukto bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ subhūtiṃ sthavirametadavocat- sadāpraruditena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena pūrvaṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ paryeṣamāṇena kāye 'narthikena jīvitanirapekṣeṇa lābhasatkāraślokeṣvaniśritena paryeṣamāṇena paryeṣitā | tena prajñāpāramitāṃ paryeṣamāṇena araṇyagatena antarīkṣānnirghoṣaḥ śruto 'bhūt- gaccha kulaputra pūrvasyāṃ diśi | tatra prajñāpāramitāṃ śroṣyasi | tathā ca gaccha yathā na kāyaklamathamanasikāramutpādayasi, na styānamiddhamanasikāramutpādayasi, na bhojanamanasikāramutpādayasi, yāvat mā kvaciccittaṃ praṇidhā adhyātmaṃ vā bahirdhā vā | mā ca kulaputra vāmenāvalokayan
body.translated_text: 'And how, <s>Bhagavān</s>, did the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita</s> (Ever-Weeping) seek this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?' Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the Elder, the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'The <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sadāprarudita</s>, when formerly seeking the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, sought it without regard for the body, without concern for life, without attachment to gain, honor, and fame. While seeking the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, having gone to the wilderness, a voice was heard from the sky: "Go, son of good family, to the eastern direction. There you will hear the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And go in such a way that you do not give rise to attention to bodily fatigue, do not give rise to attention to torpor and drowsiness, do not give rise to attention to food — and do not direct the mind anywhere, internally or externally. And, son of good family, do not go looking

body.text: gāḥ, mā dakṣiṇena, [mā pūrveṇa], mā paścimena, mā uttareṇa, mā urdhvaṃ mā adhaḥ, mā ca anuvidiśamavalokayan gāḥ | tathā ca kulaputra gaccha yathā [nātmato] na satkāyataścalasi na rūpato na vedanāto na saṃjñāto na saṃskārebhyo na vijñānataścalasi | yo hi ataścalati sa vitiṣṭhate | [kuto vitiṣṭhate?] buddhadharmebhyo vitiṣṭhate | yo buddhadharmebhyo vitiṣṭhate, sa saṃsāre carati | yaḥ saṃsāre carati, sa prajñāpāramitāyāṃ na carati, na ca tāmanuprāpnotīti ||
body.translated_text: to the left, not to the right, [not to the front], not behind, not to the north, not upward, not downward, and do not go looking to the intermediate directions. And go, son of good family, in such a way that [you do not move away from the self,] you do not move away from the body-view (<s>satkāya</s>), you do not move away from form, from feeling, from perception, from formations, from consciousness. For whoever moves away from these, deviates. [From what does he deviate?] He deviates from the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. Whoever deviates from the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> wanders in <s>saṃsāra</s>. Whoever wanders in <s>saṃsāra</s> does not practice the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and does not attain it."'
