body.text: saṃbhavaṃ vinā kathaṃ nāma vibhavo vināśo bhaviṣyati? kathaṃ nāmetyanena prasiddhamatyantāsaṃbhavaṃ darśayati | kathaṃ nāma bhaviṣyati, naiva etatsaṃbhavatītyabhiprāyaḥ | yadi punarvinaiva saṃbhavaṃ vibhavaḥ syāt, ko doṣaḥ syāt? ucyate | vinaiva janma maraṇaṃ syāt, ajātasya maraṇaṃ syāt | na ca ajātasya maraṇaṃ dṛṣṭamiti | tasmādvibhavo nodbhavaṃ vinā bhavitumarhati | ādyenātra ślokasyārdhena pratijñā, madhyena pādena prasaṅgāpādanam, antyena nigamanamiti vijñeyam || 2 ||
body.translated_text: How could there possibly be destruction without arising? By 'how could there possibly,' he shows that it is well-known to be utterly impossible. How could it possibly be — the intent is: this simply cannot occur. If, however, destruction were to exist without arising, what fault would there be? [Reply:] There would be death without birth — there would be the death of the unborn. But the death of the unborn is not observed. Therefore destruction cannot exist without coming-into-being. In this [verse], the first half-verse is the thesis, the middle quarter is the absurd consequence, and the final [quarter] is the conclusion — this should be understood. // 2 //

body.text: evaṃ tāvadvinā saṃbhavena vibhavo na yuktaḥ iti pratipādya idānīṃ saha saṃbhavenāpi vibhavo na saṃbhavati tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Having thus demonstrated that destruction without arising is not justified, now demonstrating that destruction does not occur even together with arising, he says:

children.translated_text: How could destruction exist simultaneously with arising? /

children.text: na janmamaraṇaṃ caivaṃ tulyakālaṃ hi vidyate || 3 ||
children.translated_text: For birth and death do not exist at the same time. // 3 //

body.text: yadi hi saṃbhavena saha yugapat tulyakālaṃ vibhavaḥ syāt, evaṃ sati janmamaraṇe yugapat syātām | na caivaṃ parasparaviruddhe ālokāndhakāravadekasmin kāle vidyete iti | tasmāt sahāpi saṃbhavena vibhavasya nāsti siddhiriti sthitam || 3 ||
body.translated_text: For if destruction were to exist simultaneously, at the same time, with arising, then birth and death would be simultaneous. But these two, being mutually contradictory — like light and darkness — do not exist at one time. Therefore, even together with arising, the establishment of destruction is impossible — this is established. // 3 //

body.text: yadā caivaṃ saṃbhavena vinā vā saha vā vibhavasya nāsti siddhiḥ, evaṃ saṃbhavasyāpi vinā vā saha vā vibhavena nāsti siddhiriti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And since thus the establishment of destruction is impossible either without or together with arising, demonstrating that likewise the establishment of arising is also impossible either without or together with destruction, he says:

body.text: bhaviṣyati kathaṃ nāma saṃbhavo vibhavaṃ vinā

children.text: anityatā hi bhāveṣu na kadācinna vidyate || 4 ||
children.translated_text: For impermanence is never absent in entities. // 4 //

body.translated_text: How could there possibly be arising without destruction? /

body.text: naiva hi saṃbhavo vibhavena vinā yujyate | yasmādanityatā hi bhāveṣu bhavanadharmakeṣu utpāda dharmakeṣu na kadācinna vidyate, kiṃ tarhi sarvadaiva vidyate | uktaṃ hi-
body.translated_text: Arising without destruction is indeed not justified. Because impermanence is never absent in entities — in things that are subject to becoming, that are subject to arising — but rather is present at all times. For it has been said:

body.text:
jarāmaraṇadharmeṣu sarvabhāveṣu sarvadā |
tiṣṭhanti katame bhāvā ye jarāmaraṇaṃ vinā || iti |
body.translated_text:
'Among all entities that are subject to old age and death, always —
which entities persist that are without old age and death?' //

body.text: yadā caivaṃ nityamanityatānugatāḥ sarve bhāvāḥ, tadā kutaḥ sā kācidavasthā yā vināśarahitā syāditi? ato nāsti vibhavena vinā utpāda iti | evaṃ tāvadvinā vibhavena nāsti saṃbhavaḥ | śeṣamatra saṃskṛtaparīkṣāyāṃ vicāritattvānna vicāryate ||
body.translated_text: And when thus all entities are always accompanied by impermanence, then how could there be any state that would be free from destruction? Therefore arising does not exist without destruction. Thus, arising does not exist without destruction. The remainder here is not examined, since it was already investigated in the Examination of the Conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaparīkṣā</s>). //

body.text: yastu sahetuko vināśaḥ, saṃskṛtalakṣaṇatvāt, utpādavat, iti sādhanamutkṣipya antyacittacaittakṣaṇairanaikāntikatāmāha, sa na yuktamāha, tadvināśasyāpi jātipratyayatvena sahetukatvāt sādhyasamatvācca anaikāntikatābhāvāt | yadapi nirdiṣṭam- bhāvātmabhāva eva abhūtvā bhāvādutpāda ucyate, tasmād dravyasadutpādasiddhervyavahārato dṛṣṭāntabhāva iti, tadapi na yuktam, adravyasatāṃ pratibimbādīnāṃ sahetukatvābhyupagamāt | yathoktamācāryapādaiḥ-
body.translated_text: As for the one who puts forward the proof: 'Destruction is causally produced, because of being a conditioned mark, like arising' — and [the opponent] objects that it is inconclusive because of the counter-instance of the final moment of consciousness and mental factors — he does not speak correctly, since destruction too is causally produced (having birth as its condition), and because the inconclusiveness does not hold due to the equal status of the thesis [and the counter-example]. And as for what was stated — 'It is from the essential nature of the entity itself that arising, which was not [there] before, is said to arise from the entity; therefore, from the establishment of arising as substantially real (<s>dravyasat</s>), the example is [established] conventionally' — this too is not correct, because even things that are not substantially real, such as reflections and the like, are accepted as having causes. As stated by the <s>Ācārya</s> [<s>Nāgārjuna</s>]:

body.text:
hetutaḥ saṃbhavo yeṣāṃ tadabhāvānna santi ye |
kathaṃ nāma na te spaṣṭaṃ pratibimbasamā matāḥ || iti |
body.translated_text:
'Those whose arising is from causes, and which do not exist in the absence of those [causes] —
how are they not clearly regarded as being like reflections?' //

body.text: asmādā[gamāt] kuto vyavahārato dṛṣṭāntāsiddhiḥ? yadi ca bhāvāt, yat tattvānyatvena na śakyate vaktum, tat saṃvṛtyāpi nāstītyucyate | nīlādikamapi nāstītyucyate | yathoktaṃ ratnāvalyām-
body.translated_text: Given this <s>āgama</s> (scriptural authority), how can there be non-establishment of the example conventionally? Moreover, if [it is argued] from [substantial] entity — that which cannot be stated as either identical with or different from [its cause] — that too is said not to exist even conventionally. Even blue and the like are said not to exist [ultimately]. As stated in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Since form is nothing but non-existence, space is mere name. /
Without the elements, whence form? Therefore it too is mere name.' //

body.text: api ca | kuto mādhyamikānāṃ svabhāvarūpaṃ siddhasattākaṃ yasya avasthāviśeṣa utpādaḥ syāt? ataḥ ayuktameva dṛṣṭāntāsiddhatodbhāvanam | yaccoktam- na sahetuko vināśaḥ, avināśavattvāt, yathā asaṃskṛtamiti, tasyaivaṃ bruvato mahāntaṃ virodhamayaṃ heturābhavati | yathā hi ayaṃ heturvināśasya nirhetukatvaṃ sādhayati, evaṃ saṃskṛtalakṣaṇatvābhāvamapi sādhayati | tathā saṃskāraskandhasaṃgrahapratītyasamutpādāṅgasaṃgrahādikamapi sarvaṃ virodhayatīti na yuktametanmatam | tathā | na vijñānaṃ viṣayasvarūpacchedakam, avijñānavattvāt, asaṃskṛtavat, ityādinā sarvaniṣedhānmahatī aniṣṭāpattirupapadyate 'sya, iti nāstheyametat || 4 ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, how could the <s>Mādhyamikas</s> have a form of inherent nature with established existence, of which a particular state would be 'arising'? Therefore, the raising of the objection of non-establishment of the example is indeed unjustified. And as for what was stated — 'Destruction is not causally produced, because of being without destruction, like the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>)' — for one who speaks thus, this reason (<s>hetu</s>) brings about a great contradiction. For just as this reason establishes the causelessness of destruction, so too it establishes the absence of the conditioned mark. And likewise it contradicts everything — inclusion in the aggregate of formations (<s>saṃskāraskandha</s>), inclusion as a limb of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), and so forth. Therefore this view is not justified. Likewise, [the argument that] 'consciousness does not cut off the own-form of the object, because of being without consciousness, like the unconditioned' — and so forth: by such universal negations, great undesired consequences arise for him. Therefore this should not be relied upon. // 4 //

body.text: idānīṃ vibhavena saha yathā saṃbhavasya nāsti siddhiḥ, tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, demonstrating that the establishment of arising together with destruction is impossible, he says:

children.translated_text: How could arising exist simultaneously with destruction? /

children.text: na janmamaraṇaṃ caiva tulyakālaṃ hi vidyate || 5 ||
children.translated_text: For birth and death do not exist at the same time. // 5 //

body.text: yadi hi saṃbhavo vibhavenaiva saha syāt, tadā janmamaraṇayostulyakālatā syāt | na ca [sā] saṃbhavati | tasmāt sahabhāvenāpi saṃbhavavibhavayornāsti siddhiḥ || 5 ||
body.translated_text: For if arising were to exist simultaneously with destruction, then birth and death would be simultaneous. But this is not possible. Therefore, even through co-existence, the establishment of arising and destruction is impossible. // 5 //

body.text: atha syāt- yadyapi janmamaraṇayorekībhāvena vā nānābhāvena vā nāsti siddhiḥ, tathāpi vidyete eva saṃbhavavibhavau, vācyatvāt, vijñānavat, iti | ucyate | yadi vācyatvena anayoḥ siddhiriṣyate, vandhyāputrasyāpi iṣyatām ||
body.translated_text: Now one might say: even though the establishment of birth and death is not possible either through identity or through difference, nevertheless arising and destruction do indeed exist, because they are expressible, like consciousness. [Reply:] If you wish the establishment of these two through expressibility, then let it be [equally] wished for the son of a barren woman. //

body.text: api ca-
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.translated_text: Those two, of which establishment together with each other or without each other /

children.text: na vidyate, tayoḥ siddhiḥ kathaṃ nu khalu vidyate || 6 ||
children.translated_text: is not found — how indeed could their establishment be found? // 6 //

body.text: sahabhāvāsahabhāvarahitaṃ nāsti pakṣāntaraṃ yataḥ saṃbhavavibhavayoḥ siddhiḥ syāt | avācyatayā siddhirbhaviṣyatīti cet, keyamavācyatā nāma? yadi miśrībhāvaḥ, so 'nupapannaḥ, pṛthakpṛthagasiddhayo miśrībhāvābhāvāt | anirdhāryamāṇau svarūpatvāt bandhyāputraśyāmagauratādivanna staḥ eva saṃbhavavibhavāviti | yadā caivaṃ saṃbhavavibhavau na staḥ, tadā taddheturapi kālo nāstīti siddham || 6 ||
body.translated_text: Since there is no alternative position apart from co-existence and non-co-existence from which the establishment of arising and destruction could follow — [one might say:] 'their establishment will be through inexpressibility (<s>avācyatā</s>).' What is this 'inexpressibility'? If it is a mixture [of both], that is untenable, because what is individually unestablished cannot be mixed. When they cannot be determined [as either co-existent or separately existent], they simply do not exist, because of being without own-nature — like the darkness or fairness of the son of a barren woman. And when arising and destruction do not exist in this way, then time too, which is their cause, does not exist — this is established. // 6 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat- ihemau saṃbhavavibhavau parikalpyamānau kṣayadharmiṇo vā bhāvasya parikalpyeyātāmakṣayadharmiṇo vā? ubhayathā ca nopapadyate iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: What more: here, when arising and destruction are imagined, would they be imagined of an entity that is subject to decay, or of one that is not subject to decay? In both cases it is untenable — demonstrating this, he says:

children.translated_text: There is no arising of what is subject to decay; nor is there arising of what is not subject to decay. /

children.text: kṣayasya vibhavo nāsti vibhavo nākṣayasya ca || 7 ||
children.translated_text: There is no destruction of what is subject to decay; nor is there destruction of what is not subject to decay. // 7 //

body.text: tatra kṣayasya kṣayalakṣaṇasya bhāvasya virodhidharmasadbhāvāt saṃbhavo na yuktaḥ | akṣayasyāpi bhāvalakṣaṇaviyuktatvāt kharaviṣāṇasyeva saṃbhavo na yuktaḥ | evaṃ kṣayasya vibhavo nāsti | kṣayadharmo hi avidyamānaḥ, tasya nirāśrayo vibhavo na yuktaḥ | tathā vibhavo nākṣayasya ca | akṣayadharmo hi bhāvābhāvalakṣaṇavilakṣaṇaḥ | tasya avidyamānasya kuto vibhavo bhaviṣyati? yau ca saṃbhavavibhavau na kṣayadharmiṇo nākṣayadharmiṇo bhāvasya saṃbhavataḥ, tau na saṃbhavataḥ | iti na staḥ saṃbhavavibhavau |7 ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the arising of what is subject to decay — of an entity possessing the characteristic of decay — is not justified, because of the presence of a contradictory property. And the arising of what is not subject to decay is also not justified — because it is devoid of the characteristic of entity, like the horn of a donkey. Likewise, the destruction of what is subject to decay does not exist. For what is subject to decay is non-existent; destruction without a substrate is not justified. And likewise, destruction does not exist for what is not subject to decay. For what is not subject to decay is dissimilar from the characteristics of both entity and non-entity. How could there be destruction of that which is non-existent? And since arising and destruction do not occur for an entity that is either subject to decay or not subject to decay — they do not occur. Therefore arising and destruction do not exist. // 7 //

body.text: atrāha- vidyete eva bhāvānāṃ saṃbhavavibhavau, tadāśrayidharmisadbhāvāt | iha bhāvāśrayau saṃbhavavibhavau, sa ca tāvad bhāvo 'sti, tatsadbhāvāt tadāśritāvapi dharmau bhaviṣyataḥ iti | ucyate | syātāṃ bhāvāśritāvetau dharmau, yadi bhāvaḥ syāt | yadā tu bhāvo nāsti, tadā-
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: Arising and destruction of entities do indeed exist, because of the existence of their substratum — the entity on which they depend. Here, arising and destruction depend on an entity; and that entity does exist. Because of its existence, the two properties that depend on it will also exist. [Reply:] These two properties would depend on an entity, if the entity existed. But when the entity does not exist, then:

body.text: saṃbhavo vibhavaścaiva vinā bhāvaṃ na vidyate |
body.translated_text: Arising and destruction do not exist without an entity. /

body.text: kasmātpunarbhāvo nāstīti cet, yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Why, then, does the entity not exist? Because:

body.text: saṃbhavaṃ vibhavaṃ caiva vinā bhāvo na vidyate || 8 ||
body.translated_text: Without arising and destruction, the entity does not exist. // 8 //

body.text: bhāvasya hi lakṣaṇabhūtau saṃbhavavibhavau, tau ca svarūpato na staḥ iti pratiṣiddhau | yadā ca tau bhāvataḥ pratiṣiddhau, tadā bhāvalakṣaṇaṃ saṃbhavaṃ vibhavaṃ ca vinā kuto bhāvalakṣaṇavilakṣaṇo bhāvo bhaviṣyati? bhāvaṃ ca vinā na staḥ saṃbhavavibhavau ||
body.translated_text: For arising and destruction are the defining marks of an entity, and these two have been negated as not existing by their own nature. And when these two have been negated with respect to entity, then — without the defining marks of arising and destruction — how could an entity, dissimilar from the defining marks of entity, exist? And without the entity, arising and destruction do not exist. //

body.text: apare tu pūrvārdhaṃ paścimaṃ kṛtvā vyācakṣate | staḥ eva saṃbhavavibhavau, bhāvadharmatvāt | iha yannāsti, na tasyāsti bhāvadharmatvam, tadyathā maṇḍūkajaṭāśiromaṇeḥ | bhāvadharmau ca saṃbhavavibhavau,
body.translated_text: Others, however, reversing the order of the half-verses, explain: Arising and destruction do indeed exist, because they are properties of entity. Here, what does not exist has no property of being a property of entity — just as the crest-jewel of a frog's matted hair [does not]. And arising and destruction are properties of entity

body.text: tasmāt staḥ eva tau iti | yadi kasyacit paramārthataḥ saṃbhavavibhavau syātām, sa bhāva iti yuktaṃ syādabhidhātum | tau ca na staḥ, iti
body.translated_text: — therefore they do exist. [Reply:] If someone had arising and destruction in ultimate reality, it would be justified to call that an 'entity.' But they do not exist. Therefore:

body.text: saṃbhavaṃ vibhavaṃ caiva vinā bhāvo na vidyate |
body.translated_text: Without arising and destruction, the entity does not exist. /

body.text: bhāvasya saṃbhavavibhavasattve vidyamānatvāt, iti bhāvaḥ | tadasattve ca hetorasiddhārthatā | tathā-
body.translated_text: [The word] 'entity' [is used] because of the existence of arising and destruction [as qualities] of the entity, [i.e.] because they are present. And if they are non-existent, the reason is unestablished in its meaning. Likewise:

body.text: saṃbhavo vibhavaścaiva vinā bhāvaṃ na vidyate ||
body.translated_text: Arising and destruction do not exist without an entity. //

body.text: āśrayasyābhāvādāśritasya asiddhiḥ ityabhisaṃdhiriti || 8 ||
body.translated_text: The intent is: because of the non-existence of the substratum, what depends on it is unestablished. // 8 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat- ihemau saṃbhavavibhavau parikalpamānau śūnyasya vā bhāvasya parikalpyeyātāmaśūnyasya vā? ubhayathā ca nopapadyate iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: What more: here, when arising and destruction are imagined, would they be imagined of an entity that is empty, or of one that is non-empty? In both cases it is untenable — demonstrating this, he says:

body.text: saṃbhavo vibhavaścaiva na śūnyasyopapadyate |
body.translated_text: Arising and destruction are not tenable for what is empty. /

body.text: avidyamānāśrayatvādākāśacitravadityabhiprāyaḥ | tathā-
body.translated_text: The intent is: because of the non-existence of a substratum — like a painting in the sky.

body.text: saṃbhavo vibhavaścaiva nāśūnyasyopapadyate || 9 ||
body.translated_text: Likewise: Arising and destruction are not tenable for what is non-empty. // 9 //

body.text: aśūnyasya asattvāt nirāśrayau saṃbhavavibhavau nopapadyataḥ || 9 ||
body.translated_text: For what is non-empty — because of its non-existence — arising and destruction, being without a substratum, are not tenable. // 9 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat- iha yadi saṃbhavavibhavau syātām, tau ekatvena vā syātāmanyatvena vā? ubhayathā ca nopapadyate ityāha-
body.translated_text: What more: here, when arising and destruction are imagined — would they be imagined as identical or as different? In both cases it is untenable — hence he says:

body.text: saṃbhavo vibhavaścaiva naika ityupapadyate |
body.translated_text: It is not tenable that arising and destruction are one. /

body.text: parasparaviruddhayorālokāndhakārayorivaikatvānupapatteḥ |
body.translated_text: Because of the impossibility of identity between mutually contradictory things, like light and darkness.

body.text: saṃbhavo vibhavaścaiva na nānetyupapadyate || 10 ||
body.translated_text: It is not tenable that arising and destruction are different. // 10 //

body.text: ubhayoḥ parasparamavyabhicāritvāt | na hi saṃbhavarahitasya vināśaḥ, na vibhavarahitasya saṃbhavo dṛṣṭa iti | evamubhayoḥ parasparamavyabhicāritvāt
body.translated_text: Because the two are invariably concomitant with each other. For destruction of what is devoid of arising is not observed, nor is the arising of what is devoid of destruction. Thus, because the two are invariably concomitant with each other,

body.text: saṃbhavo vibhavaścaiva na nānetyupapadyate ||
body.translated_text: it is not tenable that arising and destruction are different. //

body.text: atha syāt- kimanayā sūkṣmekṣikayā? āgopālāṅganādiko hi janaḥ yasmāt saṃbhavaṃ vibhavaṃ ca paśyati, tasmāt staḥ saṃbhavavibhavau | na hi avidyamāno vandhyātanayaḥ śakyo draṣṭumiti | evamapi-
body.translated_text: Now one might say: 'What is the use of this subtle examination? For the common people — cowherd women and the like — see arising and destruction. Therefore, arising and destruction do exist. For a non-existent barren woman's son cannot be seen.' Even so —

body.text: dṛśyate saṃbhavaścaiva vibhavaścaiva te bhavet |
body.translated_text: Arising and also destruction would exist for you because they are seen. /

body.text:
ucyate | anaikāntikametat | na hi yad yad lokenopalabhyate tasya tasya astitvam |
tathā hi āgopālāṅganādiko jano gandharvanagaramāyāsvapnālātacakramarīcikāsalilādikamavidyamānamapi paśyati indriyopaghātāt, evamimāvapi saṃbhavavibhavau asantau mohādeva paśyatītyāha-
body.translated_text: It is replied: This is inconclusive. For it is not the case that whatever is perceived by the world truly exists. For the common people — cowherd women and the like — see even non-existent things such as <s>gandharva</s>-cities, illusions, dreams, whirling firebrands, mirages, water [in a desert], and so forth, due to the impairment of the senses. Even so, they see these two — arising and destruction — which are non-existent, through delusion alone. Hence he says —

body.text: dṛśyate saṃbhavaścaiva mohādvibhava eva ca || 11 ||
body.translated_text: Arising and also destruction are seen through delusion alone. // 11 //

body.text: atha kasmāt punaretadevaṃ niścīyate- avidyamānasvarūpāvimau saṃbhavavibhavau mohādeva vāralokena dṛśyete iti | yuktyā hyetadevaṃ niścīyate | kā punaratra yuktiḥ? iha yadi kaścid bhāvo nāma bhavet, niyataṃ sa bhāvādvā jāyeta abhāvādvā | tathā yadi abhāvo nāma kaścit, so 'pi bhāvādvā jāyeta abhāvādvā | ubhayathā ca ubhayorapyasaṃbhavaḥ ityāha-
body.translated_text: Now, for what reason is this determined thus — that these two, arising and destruction, whose own nature is non-existent, are seen by the deluded world through delusion alone? This is determined by reasoning. And what is the reasoning here? Here, if there were some entity, it would necessarily arise either from an entity or from a non-entity. Likewise, if there were some non-entity, it too would arise either from an entity or from a non-entity. And in both cases, both are impossible. Hence he says —

children.translated_text: An entity does not arise from an entity; an entity does not arise from a non-entity. /
A non-entity does not arise from a non-entity; a non-entity does not arise from an entity. // 12 //

body.text: bhāvāt tāvat saṃbhavākhyād bhāvasya saṃbhavākhyasya utpādo na vidyate, kāryakāraṇayoryaugapadyābhāvāt, utpādasya ca labdhajanmanaḥ punarutpādavaiyarthyāt | abhāvādapi bhāvo na jāyate | kiṃ kāraṇam? abhāvo hi nāma vibhavo vināśaḥ | sa ca bhāvaviruddhaḥ | tasmādbhāvaviruddhāt kathaṃ bhāvaḥ syāt? yadi syāt, tadā vandhyāduhiturapi putraḥ syāt | na caitadevamiti | tasmādabhāvādapi bhāvo na bhavati | idānīmabhāvo 'pyabhāvānna bhavati | bhāvanivṛttirūpo hi abhāvaḥ, tata kuto 'sya kāryakaraṇasāmarthyam? yadi syāt, nirvāṇasyāpi kāryakaraṇasāmarthyaṃ syāt | yadi ca abhāvādabhāvaḥ syāt, tadā vandhyāduhiturapi putraḥ syāt | na caitadevamiti | tasmādabhāvādapyabhāvo na bhavati | idānīṃ bhāvādapyabhāvo na bhavati | bhāvaviruddho hyabhāvaḥ | sa kathaṃ bhāvādbhavet | yadi bhavet, pradīpādandhakāraḥ syāt | yataścaivaṃ vicāryamāṇau saṃbhavavibhavau na staḥ, tasmānmohādeva lokena dṛśyete iti vijñeyam ||
body.translated_text: First, the arising of an entity called arising from an entity called arising does not exist, because of the impossibility of the simultaneity of cause and effect, and because of the pointlessness of the re-arising of what has already been born. Nor does an entity arise from a non-entity. For what reason? For a non-entity is indeed destruction, dissolution. And that is contradictory to an entity. Therefore, how could an entity arise from what is contradictory to an entity? If it could, then even a son from a barren woman's daughter would be possible. But this is not so. Therefore, an entity does not arise from a non-entity either. Now, a non-entity too does not arise from a non-entity. For a non-entity is of the nature of the cessation of an entity — whence, then, would it have the capacity to produce an effect? If it had, then even <s>nirvāṇa</s> would have the capacity to produce an effect. And if a non-entity arose from a non-entity, then even a son from a barren woman's daughter would be possible. But this is not so. Therefore, a non-entity does not arise from a non-entity either. Now, a non-entity does not arise from an entity either. For a non-entity is contradictory to an entity. How could it arise from an entity? If it did, darkness would arise from a lamp. And since, when examined thus, arising and destruction do not exist, therefore it should be understood that they are seen by the world through delusion alone. //

body.text: athavā | ayamanyaḥ pūrvapakṣaḥ- iha hi yadi saṃbhavavibhavau syātām, tau bhāvāśrayau vā syātāmabhāvāśrayau vā | tau ca bhāvābhāvau sarvathā vicāryamāṇau na saṃbhavataḥ | tataśca kuto nirāśrayau saṃbhavavibhavāviti? ataḥ-
body.translated_text: Alternatively, here is another objection: If arising and destruction were to exist, they would have either an entity as their basis or a non-entity. And these two — entity and non-entity — when examined in every way, are not possible. Whence, then, would there be arising and destruction without a basis? Therefore —

body.text: dṛśyate saṃbhavaścaiva mohādvibhava eva ca |
body.translated_text: Arising and also destruction are seen through delusion alone. /

body.text: iti vijñeyam | yathā ca bhāvābhāvau na saṃbhavataḥ, tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: — this should be understood. And how entity and non-entity are not possible — demonstrating this, he says —

children.translated_text: An entity does not arise from an entity; an entity does not arise from a non-entity. /
A non-entity does not arise from a non-entity; a non-entity does not arise from an entity. //

body.text: asyārthaḥ pūrvavat || 12 ||
body.translated_text: The meaning of this is as before. // 12 //

body.text: api ca | yadi kaścid bhāvo nāma syāt, tasya udayavyayavattvāt saṃbhavavibhavau syātām | na ca kaścid bhāvaḥ svarūpato 'sti kharaviṣāṇavat svabhāvānutpannatvāt | anutpannatvamasiddhamiti cet, tat siddham, yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Moreover, if there were some entity, because of its having arising and destruction, arising and destruction would exist. But no entity exists by its own nature — like a donkey's horn — because its own-nature has not arisen. If it is objected that non-arising is not established, that is established, because —

children.text: na svato jāyate bhāvaḥ parato naiva jāyate |
children.translated_text: An entity does not arise from itself, nor does it arise from another. /

children.text: na svataḥ parataścaiva jāyate, jāyate kutaḥ || 13 ||
children.translated_text: Nor does it arise from both itself and another — whence, then, does it arise? // 13 //

body.text: etacca ādya eva prakaraṇe vyākhyātattvānna punarvyākhyāyate | yaścaivaṃ yathoktaprakāreṇa jāyate sa idānīṃ kuto jāyate? naiva kutaścijjāyate ityabhiprāyaḥ | avaśyaṃ caitadevamabhyupeyam- sarvathā nāsti bhāvasyotpāda iti || 13 ||
body.translated_text: And this has been explained in the very first chapter, hence it is not explained again. And that which arises in the manner described — whence does it now arise? It does not arise from anything whatsoever — this is the intended meaning. And this must necessarily be accepted — that in every way, there is no arising of an entity. // 13 //

body.text:
bhāvasadbhāvatābhyupagame ca bhavataḥ śāśvatocchedadarśanamāpadyate bauddhamatānugasyetyāha-
bhāvamabhyupapannasya śāśvatocchedadarśanam |
prasajyate
body.translated_text: And when the real existence of an entity is accepted, the view of eternalism and annihilationism befalls you, the follower of the Buddhist doctrine — hence he says: For one who has accepted the [real existence of an] entity, the view of eternalism and annihilationism / follows,

body.text: yasmāt,
body.translated_text: because

body.text: sa bhāvo hi nityo 'nityo 'tha vā bhavet || 14 ||
body.translated_text: that entity would be either permanent or impermanent. // 14 //

body.text: yo hi yathoditapadārthavyavasthāmatikramya bhāvasadbhāvadarśanamabhyupaiti, tasya avaśyaṃ pravacanātyantaviruddhaṃ śāśvatocchedadarśanadvayamāpadyate | kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmāt sa bhāvaḥ parikalpyamānaḥ nityo vā bhavedanityo vā | yadi nityaḥ, tadā niyataṃ śāśvatavādaḥ | atha anityaḥ, tadā niyatamuccheda iti || 14 ||
body.translated_text: For one who, transgressing the arrangement of meanings as stated, accepts the view of the real existence of an entity — for him, the twofold view of eternalism and annihilationism, utterly opposed to the [Buddha's] teaching, necessarily follows. For what reason? Because that entity, when imagined, would be either permanent or impermanent. If permanent, then certainly the doctrine of eternalism [follows]. If impermanent, then certainly annihilationism [follows]. // 14 //

body.text: atrāha-
body.translated_text: Here one objects —

body.text: bhāvamabhyupapannasya naivocchedo na śāśvatam |
body.translated_text: For one who has accepted the [real existence of an] entity, there is neither annihilation nor permanence. /

body.text: kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmāt-
body.translated_text: For what reason? Because —

body.text: udayavyayasaṃtānaḥ phalahetvorbhavaḥ sa hi || 15 ||
body.translated_text: The continuum of arising and destruction of fruit and cause — that is existence (<s>bhava</s>). // 15 //

body.text: yo hi hetuphalayorudayavyayānuprabandhaḥ, sa hi asmākaṃ bhavaḥ saṃsāraḥ | tatra yadi heturnirudhyeta, taddhetukaṃ phalaṃ notpadyeta, tadā syāducchedavādadoṣaḥ | yadi ca heturna nirudhyeta, svarūpeṇāvatiṣṭhet, tadā syācchāśvatavādadarśanadoṣaḥ | na caitadevamiti | tasmād bhāvābhyupagame 'pi nāsti śāśvatocchedadarśanadoṣadvayaprasaṅgaḥ | sa eva saṃsāraḥ yo 'yaṃ hetuphalāvicchinnakramavartī utpādavyayānuprabandhaḥ saṃskārāṇāmiti | ato nāsti asmākamayaṃ doṣa iti || 15 ||
body.translated_text: The unbroken succession of the arising and destruction of cause and fruit — that is our existence, <s>saṃsāra</s>. Therein, if the cause were to cease and the fruit caused by it were not to arise, then there would be the fault of the doctrine of annihilationism. And if the cause were not to cease but were to persist in its own form, then there would be the fault of the view of the doctrine of eternalism. But this is not the case. Therefore, even when accepting entities, there is no consequence of the twofold fault of the views of eternalism and annihilationism. That very <s>saṃsāra</s> is this unbroken succession of arising and destruction, proceeding in uninterrupted sequence of cause and fruit, of conditioned things (<s>saṃskāras</s>). Therefore, this fault does not apply to us. // 15 //

body.text: ucyate-
body.translated_text: It is replied —

body.text: udayavyayasaṃtānaḥ phalahetvorbhavaḥ sa cet |
body.translated_text: If that existence is the continuum of arising and destruction of fruit and cause, /

body.text: nanu evamapi-
body.translated_text: then surely even so —

body.text: vyayasyāpunarutpatterhetūcchedaḥ prasajyate || 16 ||
body.translated_text: the view of annihilationism follows from the non-re-arising of what has been destroyed as a cause. // 16 //

body.text: yo hi hetukṣaṇaḥ phalasyotpattau hetubhāvamupetya nirudhyate, nanu tasya vyayavato hetukṣaṇasya punaranutpādāducchedadarśanamāpadyate | tavāyaṃ kathaṃ na doṣa iti cet, bhāvamabhyupapannasya ayaṃ doṣaḥ | na ca mayā bhāvo 'bhyupagataḥ, svabhāvānutpannatvāt sarvadharmāṇām | yatrāpi mayā-
body.translated_text: The causal moment that, having assumed the role of cause for the arising of the fruit, ceases — surely, from the non-re-arising of that causal moment that has been destroyed, the view of annihilationism follows. [Objection:] How is this not a fault for you? [Reply:] This fault belongs to one who has accepted the real existence of an entity. But I have not accepted an entity, because all <s>dharmas</s> are without arising of own-nature. Even where I have stated —

children.text: pratītya yadyadbhavati na hi tāvattadeva tat |
children.translated_text: Whatever arises dependent on something — it is not identical with that; /
nor is it different from it — therefore it is neither annihilation nor permanence. //

body.text: ityuktam, tatrāpi amunā nyāyena naiḥsvābhāvyameva bhāvānāṃ pratipāditam | anyathā hi sati bhāvasvarūpe bījāṅkurayoḥ kathamanyatvaṃ na syāt? tasmānnāyaṃ prasaṅgo 'smākaṃ bādhaka iti || 16 ||
body.translated_text: — even there, by this very reasoning, only the absence of own-nature of entities has been demonstrated. For otherwise, if there were the own-nature of an entity, how could there not be otherness between the seed and the sprout? Therefore this consequence does not refute us. // 16 //

body.text: evaṃ tāvad bhāvamabhyupapannasya hetoḥ punaranutpādāducchedadarśanaprasaṅgamudbhāvya idānīṃ śāśvatavāde doṣaprasaṅgamudbhāvayannāha-
body.translated_text: Having thus brought out the consequence of the view of annihilationism from the non-re-arising of the cause for one who accepts the real existence of an entity, now bringing out the consequence of the fault regarding the view of eternalism, he says —

body.text: sadbhāvasya svabhāvena nāsadbhāvaśca yujyate |
body.translated_text: The non-existence of what truly exists by own-nature is not possible. /

body.text: yadi hi hetoḥ sadbhāvaḥ svabhāvataḥ syāt, tasya paścādasadbhāvo na syāt svabhāvasyā napāyitvāt | tataśca śāśvatadarśanaprasaṅgaḥ tadavastha eva ||
body.translated_text: For if the true existence of the cause were by own-nature, its subsequent non-existence would not be possible, since own-nature does not pass away. And consequently, the consequence of the view of eternalism remains as it is. //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat-
body.translated_text: Moreover —

body.text: nirvāṇakāle cocchedaḥ praśamādbhavasaṃtateḥ || 17 ||
body.translated_text: And at the time of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, annihilationism [follows] from the cessation of the continuum of existence. // 17 //

body.text: yadyapi hetuphalayorudayavyayasaṃtānapravṛttyā śāśvatocchedadarśanaprasaṅgaḥ parihriyate, tathāpi yatrāsya saṃtānasya punarapyapravṛttiḥ, tatra nirvāṇe niyatamucchedadarśanamāpadyate | ucchedadarśanaṃ ca prahātavyamityuktaṃ bhagavatā | evaṃvidhamucchedadarśanaṃ na bhaviṣyatīti cet, anyadapi kimarthaṃ bhavatā bhaviṣyatīti bhāvavicchedālambanatvāt, nirvāṇakāle bhāvavicchedālambanavadityabhiprāyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Even if the consequence of the views of eternalism and annihilationism is avoided through the continuum of arising and destruction of cause and fruit, nevertheless, where this continuum no longer proceeds — there, in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the view of annihilationism necessarily follows. And the view of annihilationism is to be abandoned — so the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said. [Objection:] 'This kind of view of annihilationism will not apply.' [Reply:] What other [view] will you have and for what purpose? — since it has the cessation of existence as its object; at the time of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, like [any view] having the cessation of existence as its object — this is the intent. //

body.text: yaccoktam-
body.translated_text: And what was stated —

body.text: udayavyayasaṃtānaḥ phalahetvorbhavaḥ sa hi |
body.translated_text: The continuum of arising and destruction of fruit and cause — that is existence /

body.text: iti, tadapi nopapadyate | kathaṃ kṛtvā? iha hi caramo bhavo nivṛttilakṣaṇaḥ, prathamo gatipratisaṃdhilakṣaṇaḥ | tatra caramo bhavo nirudhyamāno hetutvenāvatiṣṭhate | upapattilakṣaṇastu prathamo bhavaḥ phalarūpatvena vyavatiṣṭhate | anayośca bhavayoḥ saṃsāra iti saṃjñā kṛtā || 17 ||
body.translated_text: — that too is not tenable. How so? Here, the last existence has the characteristic of cessation, and the first existence has the characteristic of rebirth-linking in a destination. Therein, the last existence, while ceasing, persists as a cause. And the first existence, having the characteristic of rebirth, is established as having the nature of a fruit. And these two existences are designated as <s>saṃsāra</s>. // 17 //

body.text: atra ca idaṃ vicāryate- ya eṣa prathamo bhavaḥ phalarūpatvena vyavasthāpyate, sa kiṃ carame bhave niruddhe upajāyate, athāniruddhe, uta nirudhyamāne, yato hetuphalānuprabandhāt saṃsāraḥ syāt? sarvathā ca vicāryamāṇo na saṃbhavatīti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And here this is examined: This first existence that is established as having the nature of a fruit — does it arise when the last existence has ceased, or when it has not ceased, or while it is ceasing — such that through the succession of cause and fruit, <s>saṃsāra</s> would exist? And when examined in every way, it is not possible — demonstrating this, he says —

children.text: carame na niruddhe ca prathamo yujyate bhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: Neither when the last [existence] has ceased does the first existence obtain, /

children.text: carame nāniruddhe ca prathamo yujyate bhavaḥ || 18 ||
children.translated_text: nor when the last [existence] has not ceased does the first existence obtain. // 18 //

body.text: tatra yadi carame bhave niruddhe prathamo bhavo jāyate iti parikalpyate, tadā nirhetuka syāt | dahanadagdhabījādapi aṅkurodayaḥ syāt | na caitadiṣṭam | tasmāccarame niruddhe prathamo bhavo na yujyate ||
body.translated_text: Therein, if it is imagined that the first existence arises when the last existence has ceased, then it would be without a cause. Even from a seed burned and destroyed by fire, a sprout would arise. But this is not accepted. Therefore, when the last has ceased, the first existence does not obtain. //

body.text: idānīmaniruddhe 'pi carame bhave prathamo bhavo na yujyate | yadi syāt, nirhetukaḥ syāt, dvirūpatā ca ekasya sattvasya syāt, apūrvasattvaprādurbhāvaśca, pūrvasya ca nityatā syāt, avinaṣṭe ca bīje aṅkurodayaḥ syāt | na caitadevamiṣṭamiti | ataḥ-
body.translated_text: Now, even when the last existence has not ceased, the first existence does not obtain. If it did, it would be without a cause; and there would be a dual form of a single being; and the appearance of a new being [would follow]; and the prior [being] would be permanent; and from an undestroyed seed, a sprout would arise. But this is not accepted. Therefore —

body.text: carame nāniruddhe ca prathamo yujyate bhavaḥ |
body.translated_text: Nor when the last [existence] has not ceased does the first existence obtain. /

body.text: iti sthitam || 18 ||
body.translated_text: — this is established. // 18 //

body.text: idānīṃ nirudhyamāne 'pi carame bhave prathamo bhavo yathā nopapadyate tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, demonstrating how even when the last existence is in the process of ceasing, the first existence is not tenable, he says —

children.translated_text: If the first [existence] arises while the last is in the process of ceasing, /
the one ceasing would be one [existence], and the one arising would be another. // 19 //

body.text: tatra nirudhyamāno vartamāno vartamānapratyayāntavācyatvāt, jāyate ityapi vartamāna evocyate vartamānaśabdavācyatvāt | athavā nirudhyamāno nirodhakriyākārakaḥ | yaścāpi jāyate, asāvapi janikriyākārakaḥ, tau ca ekakālāviṣyamāṇau yaugapadyenaiva staḥ | tataśca nirudhyamānaḥ eko bhavaḥ syāt, jāyamānaścāpara iti yaugapadyenaiva dvau bhavau prāpnutaḥ | na caikasya yugapad dvau bhavau saṃbhavataḥ ityuktametat || 19 ||
body.translated_text: Therein, 'ceasing' (<s>nirudhyamāna</s>) is said to be present, because it is expressible by a word denoting the present [tense]; 'arises' (<s>jāyate</s>) is also said to be in the present, because it is expressible by a word denoting the present [tense]. Alternatively, 'ceasing' means the agent of the action of cessation. And the one who 'arises' too is the agent of the action of arising. And these two, occurring at the same time, are simultaneous. And consequently, the one ceasing would be one existence, and the one arising would be another — thus two existences would obtain simultaneously. But it is not possible for a single [being] to have two existences simultaneously — this has been stated. // 19 //

body.text: tadevaṃ yathoktena vicārakameṇa-
body.translated_text: Thus, by the method of examination as described —

children.translated_text: If it is not possible that [a being] is simultaneously ceasing and arising, /

children.text: sārdhaṃ ca mriyate yeṣu teṣu skandheṣu jāyate || 20 ||
children.translated_text: then is it born in those very aggregates in which it dies? // 20 //

body.text: caśabdaḥ samuccayārthaḥ | pṛthakpṛthak ceti etatsaṃnidhāpayati | yadā evaṃ yathoditanyāyena niruddhe carame prathamo bhavo na saṃbhavati, aniruddhe 'pi carame prathamo bhavo na saṃbhavati, sārdhaṃ caikasmiśca kāle caramena bhavena saha prathamo bhavo na saṃbhavati, tat kimidānīṃ yeṣu eva skandheṣu mriyate teṣu eva jāyate iti syāt | yeṣu skandheṣu sthito mriyate, teṣveva jāyate iti atyantaviruddhametat | na hi mriyamāṇo jāyate iti dṛṣṭam || 20 ||
body.translated_text: The word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) is used in the sense of conjunction. 'Separately and individually' — this is what it indicates. When, by the reasoning as described, the first existence is not possible when the last existence has ceased; and the first existence is not possible when the last existence has not ceased; and the first existence is not possible simultaneously, at a single time, together with the last existence — then, would it be the case that one is born in those very aggregates in which one dies? [The idea that] one dies in [certain] aggregates and is born in those very same aggregates — this is utterly contradictory. For it is not observed that one who is dying is [simultaneously] being born. // 20 //

body.text: tat-
body.translated_text: Therefore —

body.text: evaṃ triṣvapi kāleṣu na yuktā
body.translated_text: thus, in all three times, the continuum of existence

body.text: bhavadabhimatā
body.translated_text: as you maintain

body.text: bhavasaṃtatiḥ |
body.translated_text: is not possible. /

body.text: carame bhave niruddhe 'niruddhe nirudhyamāne yasmāt prathamo bhavo na saṃbhavati, tasmāt triṣvapi kāleṣu bhavasaṃtirnāsti |
body.translated_text: Since, when the final existence has ceased, has not ceased, or is ceasing, the first existence is not possible — therefore, in all three times, there is no continuity of existence.

body.text: triṣu kāleṣu yā nāsti sā kathaṃ bhavasaṃtatiḥ || 21 ||
body.translated_text: That which does not exist in the three times — how can it be a continuity of existence? // 21 //

body.text: yā ca idānīṃ triṣu kāleṣu nāsti, kutaḥ sā anyenātmanā bhaviṣyatīti sarvathā nāsti bhavanmatā bhavasaṃtatiḥ | tataśca yaduktam-
body.translated_text: And that which now does not exist in the three times — how will it come to be with another nature? Thus, the continuity of existence maintained by you does not exist in any way. And therefore, what was said —

body.text: udayavyayasaṃtānaḥ phalahetvorbhavaḥ sa hi |
body.translated_text: 'That which is a continuum of arising and decay for effect and cause — that is existence' /

body.text: iti, tanna yuktam | tataśca bhāvābhyupagame sati sa eva śāśvatocchedavādaprasaṅgo durnivāro bhavatām, ityato nāstyeva bhāvānāṃ svabhāvata utpattiriti siddham | yathoktamāryasamādhirājabhaṭṭārake-
body.translated_text: — that is not justified. And therefore, given the acceptance of entities, that very same consequence of the views of eternalism and annihilationism is unavoidable for you. Thus, it is established that there is simply no arising of entities by their own nature. As stated in the noble <s>Samādhirāja</s> —

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise —

children.text: bījasya sato yathāṅkuro na ca yo bīju sa caiva aṅkuro |
children.translated_text: 'Just as, when the seed exists, there is a sprout — yet the seed itself is not the sprout, /

children.text: na ca anyu tato na caiva tadevamanuccheda aśāśvata dharmatā ||
children.translated_text: nor is it something other than it, nor is it identical with it — thus the nature of <s>dharmas</s> is neither annihilation nor eternalism.' //
'From a seal, an impression is seen; but the transference of the seal is not found. /

children.text: na ca tatra na caiva sānyato evaṃ saṃskāra anucchedaśāśvatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is neither in that [impression] nor is it other than it — thus formations are neither annihilated nor eternal.' //

body.text:
ata evoktamāryanāgārjunapādaiḥ
svādhyāyadīpamudrādarpaṇaghoṣārkakāntabījāmraiḥ |
skandhapratisaṃdhirasaṃkramaśca vidvadbhiravadhāryau || iti |
body.translated_text:
For this very reason, the noble <s>Nāgārjuna</s> has said:
'Through recitation, lamp, seal, mirror, echo, sun-stone, seed, and sour fruit — /
the rebirth-linking of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and its non-transference should be ascertained by the learned.' //

body.text: tathā bhagavān-
body.translated_text: Likewise, the <s>Bhagavān</s> —

body.text:
jāyate cyavate cāpi na ca jātirna ca cyutiḥ |
yasya vijānata eṣa samādhirnāsya durlabhaḥ || iti|
body.translated_text:
'It is born and it dies — yet there is neither birth nor death. /
For one who knows this, that <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) is not hard to attain.' //

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise —

children.text: sūsukhitā sada te nara loke yehi acintiya jñātibhi dharmāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Well and truly happy always are those people in the world by whom <s>dharmas</s> have been known as inconceivable. /

children.text: na ca dharma adharma vikalpo cittapapañca vibhāvita sarvi ||
children.translated_text: There is no conceptualization of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — all conceptual proliferations of the mind have been discerned [as empty].' //

children.text: bhāva abhāva vibhāvayi jñānaṃ sarvamacintayi sarvamabhūtam |
children.translated_text: 'Existence and non-existence have been discerned through knowledge — everything is inconceivable, everything is unreal. /

children.text: ye puna cittavaśānuga bālāste dukhitā bhavakoṭiśateṣu ||
children.translated_text: But those who are childish, following the power of the mind — they suffer through hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of existences.' //

children.text: yo 'pi ca cintayi śūnyakadharmān so 'pi kumārgapapannaku bālaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'One who reflects on empty <s>dharmas</s> — even that one is a childish person who has entered a wrong path. /

children.text: akṣara kīrtita śūnyaka dharmāste ca anakṣara akṣara uktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The indestructible <s>dharmas</s> are declared as empty — and those empty ones are declared as indestructible.' //

children.text: śānta paśānta ya cintayi dharmān so 'pi ca cittu na jātu na bhūtaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'One who reflects on <s>dharmas</s> as "ceased" or "not ceased" — even that mind has never been, and is not existent. /

children.text: cittavitarkaṇa sarvi papañcāḥ sūkṣma acintiya budhyatha dharmān ||
children.translated_text: All conceptual proliferations belong to one who deliberates with the mind — understand those <s>dharmas</s> as subtle and inconceivable.' //

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacitāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau saṃbhavavibhavaparīkṣā nāma ekaviṃśatitamaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, 'The Examination of Arising and Destruction,' in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary composed by <s>Ācārya Candrakīrtipāda</s>.

body.text:
22
tathāgataparīkṣā dvāviṃśatitamaṃ prakaraṇam |
body.translated_text:
22
The Examination of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the Twenty-Second Chapter.

body.text: atrāha- vidyata eva bhavasaṃtatiḥ, tathāgatasadbhāvāt | iha hi bhagavatā mahākaruṇopāyaprajñādvayadhāriṇā sakalatraidhātukāśeṣasattvajātyādiduḥkhavyupaśamaikamanasā tribhiḥ kalpāsaṃkhyeyaiḥ saptabhirvā nairantaryakrameṇodyacchatā taistairniratiśayairativicitraiḥ puṇyakriyāprārambhaiḥ sakalajagaddhitodayaikakriyālakṣaṇaiḥ priyaikaputrādapyadhikataraniravaśeṣajagadanugrahatatpareṇa mahākaruṇāparavaśena tatratatropapattyāyatane kṣitisalilajvalanapavanasādhāraṇabhaiṣajyamahāmahīruhavajjanānāṃ svecchāta upabhogyatāmātmānamupagamayatā mahākālena sārvajñaṃ sarvākāraparicchedi padamadhigatam | sa evamadhigatasarvajñajñāno bhagavān yathā dharmāṇāṃ tattvaṃ vyavasthitaṃ tathaiva aśeṣato gatatvād buddhatvāt tathāgata ityucyate | yadi bhavasaṃtatirna syāt, tadā tathāgato 'pi na syāt | na hi ekena janmanā śakyaṃ tathāgatatvamanuprāptum | tasmādvidyata eva bhavasaṃtatiḥ, tathāgatasadbhāvāditi | ucyate | bhavadīyameva hi idamatimahadajñānaṃ bhavasaṃtānasya avicchedavartitāṃ ca atidīrghakālaṃ ca gamayati, yasya nāma bhavataḥ atimahadajñānadhanāndhakārameva vicitrairupapattiśaraccandrajñānālokairvidhvasyamānamapi aticiratarakālābhyāsavāsanāvistarābhivṛddhamadyāpi na vidhvasyate na nivartate | yadi hi tathāgato nāma kaścit syāt svabhāvataḥ, tadā tasya mahatā kālenābhiniṣpatterbhavasaṃtatiḥ syāt | na ca tathāgato nāma kaścid bhāvasvabhāvata upalabhyate | kevalaṃ tu bhavānavidyātimiropahatamatinayanatayā dvicandrakeśamaśakādivanmithyā tathāgataṃ nāma svabhāvata upalabhate | yathā ca tathāgato nāsti svabhāvataḥ, tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: the continuity of existence does indeed exist, because of the existence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. For here, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who holds the dual [qualities] of great compassion, skillful means, and wisdom, who is singularly intent on the pacification of the sufferings of birth and so forth for all beings without exception in the entire triple world, who — striving continuously through three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), or seven, by means of various unsurpassed and exceedingly diverse undertakings of meritorious activity, whose sole defining activity is the arising of benefit for the entire world, and who, being supremely devoted to the welfare of all beings without exception even more than an only beloved child, being under the power of great compassion, in one birth-place after another transformed himself into the common great medicinal trees of earth, water, fire, and wind, and like the wish-fulfilling tree-of-diamond, offered himself voluntarily for the enjoyment of beings — over a great length of time attained the state of omniscience, which discerns everything in every way. That <s>Bhagavān</s>, having thus attained omniscient knowledge, because he has gone (<s>gata</s>) to the reality (<s>tathā</s>) of <s>dharmas</s> exactly as it is established, completely and without remainder — hence he is called '<s>Tathāgata</s>.' If the continuity of existence did not exist, then the <s>Tathāgata</s> too would not exist. For it is not possible to attain <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood in a single lifetime. Therefore, the continuity of existence does indeed exist, because of the existence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. It is replied: it is indeed this exceedingly great ignorance of yours that demonstrates the unbroken continuation and exceedingly long duration of the continuity of existence — [your ignorance,] the dense darkness of whose exceedingly great wealth of ignorance, even though being dispelled by the diverse lights of knowledge [shining like] autumn moons of various kinds of rebirth, through exceedingly long habitual practice and augmented latent impressions, is even now not dispelled, does not turn back. For if there were someone called a <s>Tathāgata</s> by intrinsic nature, then through his accomplishment over a great length of time, there would be a continuity of existence. But no one called a <s>Tathāgata</s> is found by the nature of an entity. Rather, you, because your cognitive eyes are impaired by the eye-disease of ignorance, falsely perceive someone called a <s>Tathāgata</s> by intrinsic nature — like a double moon, or hairs, or flies. And to demonstrate how the <s>Tathāgata</s> does not exist by intrinsic nature, he says —

children.text: skandhā na nānyaḥ skandhebhyo nāsmin skandhā na teṣu saḥ |
children.translated_text: He is not the <s>skandhas</s>, not other than the <s>skandhas</s>; the <s>skandhas</s> are not in him, nor he in them. /
The <s>Tathāgata</s> does not possess the <s>skandhas</s> — then what <s>Tathāgata</s> is there? // 1 //

body.text: yadi hi tathāgato nāma kaścit padārtho 'malo niṣprapañcaḥ syāt, sa skandhasvabhāvo vā bhavet, rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānākhyaskandhapañcakasvabhāvo vā bhavet | yadi vā śīlasamādhiprajñāvimuktivimuktijñānadarśanākhyapañcaskandhasvabhāvaḥ, tadvayatirikto vā bhavet | pūrvakā eva pañca skandhāḥ sattvaprajñaptinimittatvādiha vicāre parigṛhyante nottare, avyāpakatvādeṣāṃ pūrvakairantarbhāvita tvāditi ||
body.translated_text: If indeed there were some thing called the <s>Tathāgata</s>, stainless and free from conceptual proliferation, it would either have the nature of the <s>skandhas</s> — the fivefold aggregate designated as form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — or it would have the nature of the fivefold aggregate designated as morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge-and-vision of liberation — or it would be distinct from them. It is the former five <s>skandhas</s> that are taken up here for examination, because of being the basis for the designation of a being; the latter ones are not [taken up] separately, because of their non-pervasiveness and because they are subsumed under the former.

body.text: yadi vā pañcaskandhavyatirikto bhavet, tatra tathāgate vā skandhāḥ syuḥ, skandheṣu vā sa bhavet, tathāgato vā skandhavān bhavet dhanavāniva devadattaḥ? sarvathā ca vicāryamāṇo na saṃbhavati | kathaṃ kṛtvā? tatra tāvat skandhā eva na tathāgataḥ | kiṃ kāraṇam? uktaṃ hi-
body.translated_text: Or, if it were distinct from the five <s>skandhas</s>, then either the <s>skandhas</s> would be in the <s>Tathāgata</s>, or he would be in the <s>skandhas</s>, or the <s>Tathāgata</s> would possess the <s>skandhas</s>, like <s>Devadatta</s> possessing wealth? And when examined in every way, [none of these] is possible. How so? First, the <s>skandhas</s> themselves are not the <s>Tathāgata</s>. For what reason? For it has been said —

body.text: yadindhanaṃ sa cedagnirekatvaṃ kartṛkarmaṇoḥ |
body.translated_text: 'If fuel were fire, there would be the identity of agent and action' /

body.text: bhavediti, tadihāpi yojyam,
body.translated_text: — this should be applied here too:

body.text: sa buddho yo hyupādānamekatvaṃ kartṛkarmaṇoḥ |
body.translated_text: 'If the <s>Buddha</s> were the <s>upādāna</s> (appropriated), there would be the identity of agent and action.' /

body.text: bhavediti | tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise —

body.text: ātmā skandhā yadi bhavedudayavyayabhāgbhavet |
body.translated_text: 'If the self were the <s>skandhas</s>, it would be subject to arising and passing away' /

body.text: ityuktam, tadihāpi yojyam,
body.translated_text: — it has been said, and this should be applied here too:

body.text: buddhaḥ skandhā yadi bhavedudayavyayabhāgbhavet | iti |
body.translated_text: 'If the <s>Buddha</s> were the <s>skandhas</s>, he would be subject to arising and passing away.' //

body.text: evaṃ tāvat skandhā na tathāgataḥ || idānīṃ nānyaḥ skandhebhyastathāgata iti | kiṃ kāraṇam? uktaṃ hi-
body.translated_text: Thus, the <s>skandhas</s> are not the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Now: nor is the <s>Tathāgata</s> other than the <s>skandhas</s>. For what reason? For it has been said —

body.text: anyaścedindhanādagnirindhanādaṣyṛte bhavet |
body.translated_text: 'If fire were other than fuel, it would exist without fuel.' /

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise —

children.translated_text: 'Because of independence from what is other, because of being without a cause of kindling, /
because of the purposelessness of further undertaking, and because it would be without action.' //

body.text: tathā ihāpi yojyam,
body.translated_text: Likewise, here too this should be applied:

body.text: buddho 'nyaścedupādānādupādānaṃ vinā bhavet |
body.translated_text: 'If the <s>Buddha</s> were other than the <s>upādāna</s>, he would exist without the <s>upādāna</s>.' /

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise —

children.translated_text: 'Because of independence from what is other, because of being without the cause of <s>upādāna</s>, /
because of the purposelessness of further undertaking, and because he would be without action.' //

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise —

body.text: skandhebhyo 'nyo yadi bhavedbhavedaskandhalakṣaṇaḥ |iti |
body.translated_text: 'If he were other than the <s>skandhas</s>, he would have non-<s>skandha</s> characteristics.' //

body.text: anyatvābhāvācca skandhādīnāṃ tathāgatasya ca, tathāgate skandhā nopapadyante ||
body.translated_text: And because of the absence of otherness between the <s>skandhas</s> and so forth and the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>skandhas</s> in the <s>Tathāgata</s> are not tenable.

body.text: nāpi skandheṣu tathāgata iti upapadyate | uktaṃ caitanmadhyamakāvatāre pakṣadvayavyākhyānam-
body.translated_text: Nor is it tenable that the <s>Tathāgata</s> is in the <s>skandhas</s>. And the explanation of these two positions has been stated in the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s> —

children.text: skandheṣvātmā vidyate naiva cāmī santi skandhā ātmanītīha yasmāt |
children.translated_text: 'The self does not exist in the <s>skandhas</s>, nor are these <s>skandhas</s> in the self — because, /

children.text: satyanyatve syādiyaṃ kalpanā vai taccānyatvaṃ nāstyataḥ kalpanaiṣā ||
children.translated_text: if there were otherness, this conception would hold; but there is no such otherness, hence this is [mere] conception.' //

body.text: skandhavānapi tathāgato yathā na bhavati, tathā tatraivoktam-
body.translated_text: And that the <s>Tathāgata</s> does not possess the <s>skandhas</s> — this has been stated there as well —

body.text: iṣṭo nātmā rūpavānnāsti yasmādātmā vattvārthopayogo hi nātaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'The self is not accepted as possessing form, because the self does not exist; hence there is no application of the meaning of "possessing." /

body.text: bhede gomān rūpavānaṣyabhede tattvānyatve 'rūpato nātmanaḥ staḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the case of difference, [it would be] like possessing cows and possessing form would not apply; in the case of non-difference, neither identity nor otherness from form exists for the self.' //

body.text: tattvānyatvapakṣe eva tu pañcāpi pakṣā antargatā vastutaḥ | satkāyadṛṣṭipravṛttyapekṣayā tu pañca pakṣāḥ samupavarṇyante ācāryeṇeti vijñeyam | yaścaivaṃ skandheṣu pañcadhā vicāryamāṇo nāsti tathāgataḥ, sa kenānyena ātmanā bhaviṣyatīti, sarvathā na saṃbhavatyeva tathāgata iti bhāvasvabhāvādapaśyanta ācāryapādāḥ prāhuḥ- katamo 'tra tathāgata iti | nāstyeva sa kaścit sakalatrailokyavastuvipaścidbhāvasvabhāva ityabhiprāyaḥ | tathāgatābhāvācca bhavasaṃtatirapi dravyasaṃtatirnāstīti siddham || 1 ||
body.translated_text: But in reality, all five positions are included within the two positions of identity and otherness. It should be understood that the <s>Ācārya</s> describes the five positions with reference to the operation of the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>). And the <s>Tathāgata</s> who, when examined in the five ways among the <s>skandhas</s>, does not exist — with what other nature will he come to be? Thus, the <s>Ācāryapādas</s>, not seeing the <s>Tathāgata</s> at all by the nature of an entity, said: 'Then what <s>Tathāgata</s> is there?' — the meaning being: there is simply nothing, knowing all things in the entire triple world, that has the nature of an entity. And from the non-existence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, it is established that the continuity of existence too — as a substantial continuum — does not exist. // 1 //

body.text: atraike vadanti- naiva hi skandhāstathāgata iti brūmaḥ, yathoktadoṣaprasaṅgāt | nāpi skandhavyatiriktaḥ | nāpi tathāgate anāsravān skandhān varṇayāmaḥ, himavati parvate iva tarukhaṇḍam | nāpi skandheṣu, tarukhaṇḍe eva siṃham | nāpi skandhavantaṃ varṇayāmaḥ, lakṣaṇavantamiva cakravartinam, ekatvānyatvānabhyupagamādeva | kiṃ tarhi skandhānamalānupādāya tattvānyatvādyavācyaṃ tathāgataṃ vyavasthāpayāmaḥ | tasmānnāyaṃ vidhirasmākaṃ bādhaka iti | atrocyate-
body.translated_text: Here some say: we do not say that the <s>skandhas</s> themselves are the <s>Tathāgata</s>, because of the consequence of the stated faults. Nor [do we say he is] distinct from the <s>skandhas</s>. Nor do we describe the uncontaminated <s>skandhas</s> as being in the <s>Tathāgata</s>, like a grove of trees on Mount <s>Himavat</s>. Nor [do we describe] the <s>Tathāgata</s> in the <s>skandhas</s>, like a lion in a grove of trees. Nor do we describe him as possessing the <s>skandhas</s>, like a <s>Cakravartin</s> possessing the marks — precisely because of not accepting either identity or otherness. Rather, we establish the <s>Tathāgata</s> as inexpressible as either identical with or different from the stainless <s>skandhas</s>, in dependence on those <s>skandhas</s>. Therefore, this procedure is not damaging to us. To this it is replied —

children.translated_text: If the <s>Buddha</s> does not exist by intrinsic nature in dependence on the <s>skandhas</s>, /

children.text: svabhāvataśca yo nāsti kutaḥ sa parabhāvataḥ || 2 ||
children.translated_text: and one who does not exist by intrinsic nature — how will he come to be through other-nature? // 2 //

body.text: yadi hi buddho bhagavānamalān skandhānupādāya tattvānyatvenāvaktavyaḥ prajñapyate, na tarhi svabhāvataḥ so 'stīti vyaktamāpadyate, pratibimbavadupādāya prajñapyamānatvāt | yaśca idānīṃ svabhāvato nāsti ātmīyena svarūpeṇa, sa kathamavidyamānaḥ svabhāvataḥ skandhānupādāya parabhāvato bhaviṣyatīti? na hi avidyamāno vandhyātanayaḥ parabhāvamapekṣya bhavatīti yujyate || 2 ||
body.translated_text: If the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> is designated as inexpressible in terms of identity or difference in dependence on the stainless <s>skandhas</s>, then clearly it follows that he does not exist by intrinsic nature — because of being designated in dependence, like a reflection. And one who now does not exist by intrinsic nature, by his own form — how will he, being non-existent by intrinsic nature, come to be through other-nature, in dependence on the <s>skandhas</s>? For it is not justified that a non-existent son of a barren woman comes to be by depending on other-nature. // 2 //

body.text: atha syāt- yathaiva hi pratibimbakaṃ svabhāvato 'saṃvidyamānamapi parabhāvaṃ mukhādarśādikamapekṣya bhavati, evaṃ ca tathāgato 'pi svabhāvato 'saṃvidyamānaḥ anāsravān pañca skandhānupādāya parabhāvato bhaviṣyatīti, evamapi-
body.translated_text: Now one might say: just as a reflection, even though non-existent by intrinsic nature, comes to be by depending on other-nature — the face, the mirror, and so forth — even so, the <s>Tathāgata</s> too, being non-existent by intrinsic nature, will come to be through other-nature in dependence on the five uncontaminated <s>skandhas</s>. Even so —

children.translated_text: One who depends on other-nature — it follows that he is without self (<s>anātman</s>). /

children.text: yaścānātmā sa ca kathaṃ bhaviṣyati tathāgataḥ || 3 ||
children.translated_text: And how could one who is without self be a <s>Tathāgata</s>? // 3 //

body.text: yadi pratibimbavat parabhāvaṃ pratītya tathāgataḥ iṣyate, evaṃ sati pratibimbavadeva sa tathāgato 'nātmetyupapadyate | na tu svabhāvata iti yujyate | ātmaśabdo 'yaṃ svabhāvaśabdaparyāyaḥ | yaśca anātmā niḥsvabhāvaḥ pratibimbavadeva, sa kathaṃ tathāgataḥ svabhāvarūpato bhaviṣyati? aviparītamārgagato na bhaviṣyatītyabhiprāyaḥ || 3 ||
body.translated_text: If the <s>Tathāgata</s> is accepted as depending on other-nature, like a reflection, then — this being so — that <s>Tathāgata</s> follows to be without self, like a reflection. But it is not justified [to say he exists] by intrinsic nature. Here, the word '<s>ātman</s>' is a synonym for '<s>svabhāva</s>' (intrinsic nature). And one who is without self (<s>anātman</s>), without intrinsic nature, like a reflection — how will he be a <s>Tathāgata</s> in the form of intrinsic nature? The meaning is: one who follows the undeluded path will not [accept this]. // 3 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat- iha yadi tathāgatasya kaścit svabhāvaḥ syāt, tadā tatsvabhāvāpekṣayā skandhasvabhāvaḥ parabhāva iti syāt, taṃ ca parabhāvaṃ pratītya tathāgataḥ syāt | yadā tu tathāgatasya svabhāva eva nāsti, tadā kutaḥ skandhānāṃ paratvaṃ syāditi pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And what else: here, if the <s>Tathāgata</s> had some intrinsic nature, then the intrinsic nature of the <s>skandhas</s>, with reference to that intrinsic nature, would be other-nature; and in dependence on that other-nature, there would be a <s>Tathāgata</s>. But when the <s>Tathāgata</s> has no intrinsic nature at all, then whence would there be the otherness of the <s>skandhas</s>? Demonstrating this, he says —

body.text: yadi nāsti svabhāvaśca parabhāvaḥ kathaṃ bhavet |
body.translated_text: If intrinsic nature does not exist, how could other-nature come to be? /

body.text: yadā caivaṃ svabhāvaparabhāvau na staḥ, tadā
body.translated_text: And when thus intrinsic nature and other-nature do not exist, then —

body.text: svabhāvaparabhāvābhyāmṛte kaḥ sa tathāgataḥ || 4 ||
body.translated_text: Apart from intrinsic nature and other-nature, what <s>Tathāgata</s> is there? // 4 //

body.text: padārtho hi bhavan svabhāvo bhavet, parabhāvo vā | tābhyāṃ tu vinā ko 'sau aparaḥ padārtho 'sti, yastathāgata iti vyavasthāpyate? tasmānnāsti svabhāvatastathāgata iti || 4 ||
body.translated_text: For a thing, if it existed, would be either intrinsic nature or other-nature. But apart from these two, what other thing is there that would be established as a <s>Tathāgata</s>? Therefore, the <s>Tathāgata</s> does not exist by intrinsic nature. // 4 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat-
body.translated_text: And what else —

children.translated_text: If some <s>Tathāgata</s> were to exist without depending on the <s>skandhas</s>, /
he would now appropriate, and then, having appropriated, he would come to be. // 5 //

body.text: yadi manyase- skandhebhyastattvānyatvena avaktavyastathāgataḥ skandhānupādāya prajñapyate iti, tat kadā yujyate? yadi skandhānanupādāya agṛhītvā pūrvaṃ kaścittathāgato nāma bhavet, sa skandhānupādadyāt | vyatirikta eva hi pūrvasiddho dhanād devadatto dhanasyopādānaṃ kurute, tadvadetān skandhānanupādāya yadi kaścit tathāgataḥ syāt, sa idānīṃ skandhānupādadyāt, tataśca tān skandhānupādāya tato bhavet || 5 ||
body.translated_text: If you think that the <s>Tathāgata</s>, being inexpressible as either identical with or different from the <s>skandhas</s>, is designated in dependence on appropriating the <s>skandhas</s> — when would that be tenable? If, without having first appropriated the <s>skandhas</s> — without grasping them — there were some <s>Tathāgata</s>, then he would appropriate the <s>skandhas</s>. For just as <s>Devadatta</s>, being already established separately from wealth, undertakes the appropriation of wealth — so too, if there were some <s>Tathāgata</s> without having appropriated these <s>skandhas</s>, he would now appropriate the <s>skandhas</s>, and then, having appropriated those <s>skandhas</s>, he would thereby come to be. // 5 //

body.text: vicāryamāṇastu sarvathā-
body.translated_text: But when examined in every way:

body.text: skandhāṃścāpyanupādāya nāsti kaścittathāgataḥ |
body.translated_text: Without having appropriated the <s>skandhas</s>, there is no <s>Tathāgata</s> whatsoever. /

body.text: nirhetukatvaprasaṅgāt |
body.translated_text: Because of the consequence of being without cause.

body.text: yaśca nāstyanupādāya sa upādāsyate katham || 6 ||
body.translated_text: And he who does not exist without appropriation — how can he appropriate? // 6 //

body.text: avidyamānatvādityabhiprāyaḥ | yadā caivaṃ na kiṃcidapyupādatte, tadā skandhānupādāya tathāgato nāma bhaviṣyatīti nopapadyate || 6 ||
body.translated_text: Because he is non-existent — this is the intended meaning. And when he does not appropriate anything whatsoever, 'the <s>Tathāgata</s> comes to be by appropriating the <s>skandhas</s>' is not tenable. // 6 //

body.text: yadā caivaṃ tathāgataḥ upādānātpūrvamavidyamānatvāt na kiṃcidupādatte, tadā tadupādānasyāpi kenacidapi anupādīyamānasya upādānatvaṃ na saṃbhavatyeveti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And when the <s>Tathāgata</s>, being non-existent prior to appropriation, does not appropriate anything, then even that appropriation, not being appropriated by anyone whatsoever, cannot have the status of appropriation — demonstrating this, he says:

body.text: na bhavatyanupādattamupādānaṃ ca kiṃcana |
body.translated_text: There is nothing whatsoever that is not appropriated and [yet has the status of] appropriation. /

body.text: yadā caivamupādānaṃ kenacidapyanupādīyamānatvādupādānaṃ na bhavatīti, tadā upādānābhāvādupādātāpi kaścinnāstīti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And when appropriation does not exist as such, because it is not appropriated by anyone — then, from the non-existence of appropriation, there is no appropriator either — demonstrating this, he says:

body.text: na cāsti nirupādānaḥ kathaṃcana tathāgataḥ || 7 ||
body.translated_text: Nor is there in any way a <s>Tathāgata</s> without appropriation. // 7 //
Thus. // 7 //

body.text: tadevaṃ yathopapāditanyāyena-
body.translated_text: Thus, by the reasoning as demonstrated:

children.translated_text: He who does not exist through identity or otherness, and who is sought in five ways — /
how can that <s>Tathāgata</s> be designated through appropriation? // 8 //

body.text: yo hi tathāgato vicāryamāṇo mṛgyamāṇaḥ tattvenaskandhebhya ekatvena nāsti, anyatvena skandhebhyaḥ pṛthaktvena ca yo nāsti, evaṃ tattvānyatvāsatvādādhārādheyatadvatpakṣapañcaprakārairmṛgyamāṇo
body.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> who, when examined and sought, does not exist through identity — through oneness with the <s>skandhas</s> — and does not exist through otherness — through separateness from the <s>skandhas</s> — and thus, because of the non-existence of identity and otherness, is sought through the five modes of container-and-contained and possessor

body.text: yo nāsti, sa kathamatyanto 'saṃvidyamānastathāgataḥ upādānena śakyaḥ prajñapayitum? ityato 'pi nāsti tathāgato nāma svabhāvataḥ || 8 ||
body.translated_text: and does not exist — how can that utterly non-existent <s>Tathāgata</s> be designated through appropriation? Therefore, from this too, there is no such thing as a <s>Tathāgata</s> by its own nature. // 8 //

body.text: na kevalamanena vicāreṇa tathāgata eva nāsti,
body.translated_text: It is not only through this examination that the <s>Tathāgata</s> alone does not exist —

body.text: yadapīdamupādānaṃ tatsvabhāvatvānna vidyate |
body.translated_text: Even this appropriation does not exist by its own nature. /

body.text: yadapi idamupādānaṃ rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānākhyaṃ skandhapañcakam, tadapi svabhāvena na vidyate, pratītyasamutpannatvāt, skandhaparīkṣāyāṃ ca vistareṇa pratiṣiddhatvāt ||
body.translated_text: This appropriation too — the fivefold aggregate called form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — does not exist by <s>svabhāva</s> (inherent nature), because it is dependently arisen, and because it has been extensively refuted in the Examination of the <s>Skandhas</s>.

body.text: athāpi syāt- yadyapi svabhāvataḥ upādānaṃ nāsti, tathāpi hetupratyayātmakāt parabhāvā dbhaviṣyatīti, tadāpi nopapadyate iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, one might say: even though the appropriation does not exist by <s>svabhāva</s>, it will exist through <s>parabhāva</s> (other-nature), having the nature of causes and conditions. Even so, it is not tenable — demonstrating this, he says:

body.text: svabhāvataśca yannāsti kutastatparabhāvataḥ || 9 ||
body.translated_text: And that which does not exist by its own nature — how can it exist through other-nature? // 9 //

body.text: na hi bandhyāsūnuḥ svabhāvato 'saṃvidyamānaḥ śakyaḥ parabhāvena prajñapayitumiti | ataḥ upādānamapi nāsti ||
body.translated_text: For a barren woman's son, not existing by <s>svabhāva</s>, cannot be designated through <s>parabhāva</s>. Therefore the appropriation too does not exist.

body.text: athavā-
body.translated_text: Alternatively:

body.text: yadapīdamupādānaṃ tatsvabhāvānna vidyate |
body.translated_text: Even this appropriation does not exist by its own nature — /

body.text: upādātṛsāpekṣatvādupādātṛnirapekṣasya ca upādānatvābhāvānnāsti svabhāvasiddhamupādānam | atha yadyapi upādātṛnirapekṣamupādānaṃ svabhāvasiddhaṃ na saṃbhavati, evaṃ tadupādātrapekṣameva bhavatviti | ucyate | evamapi-
body.translated_text: because it depends on an appropriator, and because without being independent of an appropriator it cannot have the status of appropriation — there is no appropriation established by <s>svabhāva</s>. Now, even though appropriation independent of an appropriator is not possible as established by <s>svabhāva</s>, let it be dependent on the appropriator. The reply is: even so —

body.text: svabhāvataśca yannāsti kutastatparabhāvataḥ ||
body.translated_text: And that which does not exist by its own nature — how can it exist through other-nature? //

body.text: svabhāvato yadupādānaṃ na siddham, tadavidyamānasvabhāvaṃ kathamupādātuḥ parabhāvato bhaviṣyatīti | tasmādupādānamapi nāstīti || 9 ||
body.translated_text: That appropriation which is not established by <s>svabhāva</s> — being of non-existent <s>svabhāva</s>, how will it exist through the <s>parabhāva</s> of the appropriator? Therefore the appropriation too does not exist. // 9 //

body.text: idānīṃ yathāprasādhitamevārthamupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, displaying the very point that has been demonstrated, he says:

body.text: evaṃ śūnyamupādānamupādātā ca sarvaśaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus, the appropriation is empty in every way, and so is the appropriator. /

body.text: sarveṇa prakāreṇa vicāryamāṇaṃ śūnyamupādānaṃ niḥsvabhāvam, upādātā ca śūnyaḥ svabhāvarahitaḥ | tenedānīmupādānena-
body.translated_text: The appropriation, when examined in every way, is empty — without <s>svabhāva</s>; and the appropriator too is empty — devoid of <s>svabhāva</s>. Now, by that empty appropriation —

body.text: prajñapyate ca śūnyena kathaṃ śūnyastathāgataḥ || 10 ||
body.translated_text: how can an empty <s>Tathāgata</s> be designated by what is empty? // 10 //

body.text: naiva tatsaṃbhavati yadavidyamānena avidyamānasya tathāgatasya prajñaptiḥ syāditi | tasmāt skandhānupādāya tathāgataḥ prajñapyate iti nopapadyate ||
body.translated_text: That is simply not possible — that there should be a designation of a non-existent <s>Tathāgata</s> by what is non-existent. Therefore, 'the <s>Tathāgata</s> is designated by appropriating the <s>skandhas</s>' is not tenable.

body.text: atrāhuḥ- aho vata hatā pratyāśā asmākam, ye hi nāma vayaṃ svavikalpavikalpitātikaṭhinakudarśanamālutālatājālāvabaddheṣu nirvāṇapuragāmyaviparītamārgagamanaparibhraṣṭeṣu anatikrāntasaṃsārāṭavīkāntāradurgeṣu kaṇabhakṣākṣapādadigambarajaimininaiyāyikaprabhṛtiṣu tīrthakareṣu aviparītasvargāpavargamārgopadeśābhimāniṣu spṛhāṃ parityajya niravaśeṣānyatīrthyamatāndhakāropaghātakaṃ svargāpavargānugāmyaviparītamārgasaṃprakāśakaṃ saddharmadeśanātipaṭutarakiraṇavyāptāśeṣāśāmukhaṃ vividhavineyajanamatikamalakuṅmalavibodhanatatparaṃ
body.translated_text: Here they say: Alas, our hope is destroyed! For we — having abandoned the desire for the non-Buddhist teachers such as <s>Kaṇabhakṣa</s> (<s>Kaṇāda</s>), <s>Akṣapāda</s> (<s>Gautama</s>), the <s>Digambaras</s> (<s>Jainas</s>), <s>Jaimini</s>, the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>, and others, who are bound by the net of creepers of exceedingly hard mis-vision conceptually constructed by their own conceptual constructions, who have fallen from the correct path leading to the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, who have not crossed beyond the difficult passages of the jungle of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and who have the conceit of teaching the correct path to heaven and liberation — having taken refuge, seeking liberation and seeking unsurpassed perfect awakening, in the <s>Tathāgata</s>-sun: the singular eye — stainless, the vessel for the truth of the nature of entities as they actually are — for the entire world to take refuge in, the incomparable, the stainless maṇḍala of the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, and the unique <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, the supreme charioteer of the great vehicle and the great path, yoked with the lofty steeds and infantry of the seven limbs of awakening, intent on drying up the river of birth, old age, death, and <s>saṃsāra</s> of all beings in the three worlds, the victor in the rain of arrows in the battle against the enemy <s>Māra</s> of the four armies, the dispeller of the seizure of the <s>Rāhu</s>-planet of wrong grasping of the entire world

body.text: yathāvadavasthitapadārthatattvārthabhājanānāmamalaikacakṣurbhūtaṃ sakalajagaccharaṇyabhūtamadvitīyaṃ daśabalavaiśāradyāveṇikabuddhadharmāmalamaṇḍalaṃ mahāyānamahānayasārathivaraṃ saptabodhyaṅgottuṅgaturaṃgapadātiyojitaṃ sakalatribhuvanajanajātijarāmaraṇasaṃsārakāntārasariducchoṣaṇatatparaṃ caturasamamārārātisamaraśarasaṃpātavijayinaṃ sakalajagadasadgrāharāhugrahavigrahodgrahanirāsinaṃ tathāgatasavitāramajñānadhanagahanāndhakāranirākaraṇāya mokṣārthino 'tuttarasamyaksaṃbodhyarthinaḥ śaraṇaṃ pratipannāḥ, tasya ca tvayā-
body.translated_text: — for the dispelling of the darkness of the dense forest of ignorance — and now, by you, in declaring the non-existence by <s>svabhāva</s> with such words as:

children.translated_text: 'Thus, the appropriation is empty in every way, and so is the appropriator. /
How can an empty <s>Tathāgata</s> be designated by what is empty?' //

body.text: ityādinā svabhāvato 'sattvaṃ vruvatā bhavatā hatā asmākaṃ mokṣapratyāśā anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhyāgamābhilāṣaḥ iti | tadalaṃ bhavatā tathāgatamahādityapracchādakena ākālikadhanadhanāvalīvisaraṇena jagadandhakāropameneti | ucyate | asmākameva hatā pratyāśā bhavadvidheṣvabudhajaneṣu ye hi nāma bhavantaḥ mokṣakāmatayā anyatīrthyamatāni parityajya bhagavantaṃ tathāgatamapi aviparītaṃ paramaśāstāraṃ pratipadya paramagambhīramanuttaraṃ sarvatīrthyavādāsādhāraṇaṃ nairātmyasiṃhanādamasahamānāḥ kuraṅgamā iva svādhimuktidaridratayā vividhakudṛṣṭivyālamālākulaṃ viparyastajanānuyātaṃ tameva mahāghorasaṃsārāṭavīkāntāracārakānugamārgamavagāhante | na hi tathāgatāḥ kadācidapyātmanaḥ skandhānāṃ vā astitvaṃ prajñapayanti | yathoktaṃ bhagavatyām-
body.translated_text: — our hope for liberation and our aspiration for the approach of unsurpassed perfect awakening have been destroyed. Enough of you, who obscure the great sun of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — who are like an untimely cloud-mass spreading [darkness] over the world! The reply is: it is our hope that is destroyed — regarding unenlightened persons such as yourselves — who, having abandoned non-Buddhist doctrines out of desire for liberation and having arrived at the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, the correct supreme teacher, are unable to bear the supremely profound, unsurpassed lion-roar of <s>nairātmya</s> (non-self), unshared by all non-Buddhist doctrines, and like deer, because of the poverty of your own devotion, plunge into that very path through the dense jungle of <s>saṃsāra</s> — terrifying, swarming with garlands of various wrong views and followed by perverted people.
