For the <s>Tathāgatas</s> never designate the existence of either the self or the <s>skandhas</s>. As stated in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>:

body.text: buddho 'pyāyuṣman subhūte māyopamaḥ svapnopamaḥ | buddhadharmā apyāyuṣman subhūte māyopamāḥ svapnopamāḥ || iti ||
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Buddha</s> too, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is like an illusion, like a dream. The <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> too, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, are like illusions, like dreams.'

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise:

body.text:
dharma svabhāvatu śūnya vivikto bodhi svabhāvatu śūnya viviktā |
yo hi caretsa pi śūnyasvabhāvo jñānavato na tu bālajanasya || iti |
body.translated_text:
'<s>Dharmas</s> are by nature empty and secluded; awakening is by nature empty and secluded. /
Whoever practices thus — he too is empty by nature; this is for the one with knowledge, not for the foolish.' //

body.text: na ca vayaṃ sarvathaiva niṣprapañcānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ nāstitvaṃ brūmaḥ, yadasmākaṃ tadapavādakṛto doṣaḥ syāt || 10 ||
body.translated_text: And we do not say that the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, who are in every way beyond conceptual proliferation, are non-existent — for then we would have the fault of that denial. // 10 //

body.text: api ca | niḥsvabhāvaṃ hi tathāgataṃ vyācakṣāṇena aviparītārthābhidhitsunā yogināṃ satā sarvathā-
body.translated_text: Moreover, for one who, wishing to express the correct meaning, describes the <s>Tathāgata</s> as without <s>svabhāva</s>, being a true yogin, in every way:

body.text:
śūnyamiti na vaktavyamaśūnyamiti vā bhavet |
ubhayaṃ nobhayaṃ ceti
body.translated_text:
One should not say 'empty,' nor should one say 'non-empty,' /
nor both, nor neither —

body.text: sarvametanna vaktavyamasmābhiḥ | kiṃ tu anukte yathāvadavasthitaṃ svabhāvaṃ pratipattā pratipattuṃ na samartha ityato vayamapi āropato vyavahārasatye eva sthitvā vyavahārārthaṃ vineyajanānurodhena
body.translated_text: none of this should be said by us. But since, without its being said, a person situated in things as they actually are is unable to comprehend [their] <s>svabhāva</s> — therefore we too, placing ourselves through superimposition in conventional truth alone, for the sake of convention, in accordance with beings to be guided,

body.text: śūnyamityapi brūmaḥ, aśūnyamityapi, śūnyāśūnyamityapi, naiva śūnyaṃ nāśūnyamityapi brūmaḥ | ata evāha
body.translated_text: say 'empty,' and also 'non-empty,' and also 'both empty and non-empty,' and also 'neither empty nor non-empty.' For this very reason he says:

body.text: prajñaptyarthaṃ tu kathyate || 11 ||
body.translated_text: but it is said for the purpose of designation. // 11 //

body.text: iti | yathoktaṃ bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: As stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text: śūnyāḥ sarvadharmā niḥsvabhāvayogena | nirnimittāḥ sarvadharmā nirnimittatāmupādāya | apraṇihitāḥ sarvadharmā apraṇidhānayogena | prakṛtiprabhāsvarāḥ sarvadharmāḥ prajñāpāramitāpariśuddhayā | iti ||
body.translated_text: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are empty by the connection of being without <s>svabhāva</s>. All <s>dharmas</s> are signless by taking signlessness. All <s>dharmas</s> are without aspiration by the connection of non-aspiration. All <s>dharmas</s> are luminous by nature through the purification of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

body.text: anyatra aśūnyamuktam-
body.translated_text: Elsewhere, 'non-empty' has been stated:

body.text: atītaṃ cedbhikṣavo rūpaṃ nābhaviṣyanna śrutavānāryaśrāvako 'tītaṃ rūpamabhyanandiṣyat | yasmāttarhi bhikṣavaḥ asti atītaṃ rūpam, tasmādāryaśrāvakaḥ śrutavānatītaṃ rūpamabhinandatīti | anāgataṃ cedbhikṣavaḥ- ityādi | evaṃ yāvat atītaṃ cedbhikṣavo vijñānaṃ nābhaviṣyat- ityādi pūrvavat ||
body.translated_text: 'If, monks, past form did not exist, the learned noble disciple would not have turned away from past form. Because, monks, past form does exist, therefore the learned noble disciple turns away from past form. If, monks, future [form] —' and so forth. 'If, monks, past consciousness did not exist —' and so forth, as before.

body.text:
tathā sautrāntikamate atītānāgataṃ śūnyam, anyadaśūnyam | viprayuktā vijñaptiḥ śūnyā |
vijñānavāde 'pi kalpitasvabhāvasya śūnyatvam, apratītyasamutpannatvāt, taimirikadvicandrādi darśanavat |
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the <s>Sautrāntika</s> view, the past and future are empty, but other things are non-empty. Dissociated cognition is empty. In the <s>Vijñānavāda</s> (mind-only) view too, the imagined nature (<s>parikalpitasvabhāva</s>) is empty, because it is not dependently arisen — like the vision of two moons by one with an eye-disease.

children.text: na śūnyaṃ nāpi cāśūnyaṃ tasmātsarvaṃ vidhīyate |
children.translated_text: Neither empty nor non-empty — therefore everything is established. /
From existence and non-existence — that is the middle path. //

body.text:
yena tvabhiprāyeṇa śūnyatvādikamupadiśyate, sa ātmaparīkṣāto boddhavyaḥ |
yathoktaṃ sūtre-
body.translated_text: And the intention with which emptiness and the like are taught should be understood from the Examination of the Self. As stated in a <s>sūtra</s>:

children.translated_text: 'This world has been declared by you to be like an illusion, like the dancing of an actor, like a dream. /

children.text: nātmā na sattva na ca jīvagatī dharmā marīcidakacandrasamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is no self, no being, no life-force — <s>dharmas</s> are like mirages and reflections of the moon in water.' //
'Empty, peaceful, without appropriation — yet the world wanders about, not knowing. /
Out of compassion, you lead them by hundreds of skillful means and methods.' //
'You see the entire world terrified by hundreds of diseases of passion and the like. /
Like a physician you move about, incomparable, liberating hundreds of beings, O <s>Sugata</s>.' //

body.text:
rathacakravad bhramati sarvajagat tiryakṣu pretanirayeṣu gatāḥ |
mūḍhā adeśika anāthagatāḥ teṣāṃ pradarśayasi mārgavaram || iti |
body.translated_text:
'The entire world revolves like the wheel of a chariot — gone to animals, <s>pretas</s>, and hells. /
Deluded, without a guide, without a protector — to them you show the supreme path.' //

body.text: sarvāstvetāḥ kalpanā niṣprapañce tathāgate na saṃbhavanti || 11 ||
body.translated_text: But all these conceptual designations are impossible with respect to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who is beyond conceptual proliferation. // 11 //

body.text: na ca kevalaṃ śūnyatvādikameva catuṣṭayaṃ tathāgate na saṃbhavati, api ca-
body.translated_text: And it is not only the fourfold [designation] of emptiness and the like that is impossible with respect to the <s>Tathāgata</s>; moreover:

children.translated_text: How can the fourfold [designation] of eternal, non-eternal, and so forth apply to what is at peace? /
And how can the fourfold [designation] of finite, infinite, and so forth apply to what is at peace? // 12 //

body.text: iha caturdaśa avyākṛtavastūni bhagavatā nirdiṣṭāni | tadyathā- śāśvato lokaḥ, aśāśvato lokaḥ, śāśvataśca aśāśvataśca lokaḥ, naiva śāśvato nāśāśvataśca lokaḥ, iti catuṣṭayam | antavān lokaḥ, anantavān lokaḥ, antavāṃśca anantavāṃśca lokaḥ, naiva antavān na anantavāṃśca lokaḥ, iti dvitīyam | bhavati tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāt, na bhavati tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāt, bhavati ca na bhavati ca tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāt, naiva bhavati na na bhavati ca tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāt, iti tṛtīyam | sa jīvastaccharīram, anyo jīvo 'nyaccharīram, iti | tānyetāni caturdaśa vastūni avyākṛtatvādavyākṛtavastūni ityucyante | tatra yathopavarṇitena nyāyena yathā śūnyatvādikaṃ catuṣṭayaṃ prakṛtyā śānte niḥsvabhāve tathāgate na saṃbhavati, evaṃ śāśvatāśāśvatādikamapi catuṣṭayamatra na saṃbhavati | asaṃbhavādeva ca catuṣṭayaṃ vandhyāputrasya śyāmagauratvādivat na vyākṛtaṃ bhagavatā lokasya | yathā ca etaccatuṣṭayaṃ tathāgate na saṃbhavati, evamantānantādikamapi śānte tathāgate na saṃbhavati || 12 ||
body.translated_text: Here, fourteen indeterminate matters (<s>avyākṛtavastu</s>) have been indicated by the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Namely: the world is eternal; the world is not eternal; the world is both eternal and not eternal; the world is neither eternal nor not eternal — this is the first tetrad. The world is finite; the world is infinite; the world is both finite and infinite; the world is neither finite nor infinite — this is the second. The <s>Tathāgata</s> exists after death; the <s>Tathāgata</s> does not exist after death; the <s>Tathāgata</s> both exists and does not exist after death; the <s>Tathāgata</s> neither exists nor does not exist after death — this is the third. The life-force (<s>jīva</s>) is identical with the body; the life-force is different from the body — thus [the fourth]. These fourteen matters are called 'indeterminate matters' because they are not determined. Therein, by the reasoning as described above, just as the tetrad of emptiness and so forth is not possible in the case of the <s>Tathāgata</s> who is quiescent by nature and without inherent nature, so too the tetrad of eternality, non-eternality, and so forth is also not possible here. And precisely because the tetrad is impossible, it was not determined by the <s>Bhagavān</s> for the world — like the dark or fair complexion of a barren woman's son. And just as this tetrad is not possible in the case of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, so too the [tetrad] of finitude, infinitude, and so forth is not possible in the case of the quiescent <s>Tathāgata</s>. // 12 //

body.text: idānīṃ bhavati tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāt ityādikasyāpi kalpanācatuṣṭayasya pravṛttyasaṃbhava mudbhāvayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, demonstrating the impossibility of the application of even the conceptual tetrad beginning with 'the <s>Tathāgata</s> exists after death,' he says:

children.translated_text: He by whom the dense grasping has been grasped [thinking] 'the <s>Tathāgata</s> exists' —
he, imagining 'does not exist,' would conceptualize even about one who has passed beyond (<s>nirvṛta</s>). // 13 //

body.text: yena hi ghanataro mahatābhiniveśena asti tathāgataḥ iti grāho gṛhītaḥ, parikalpa utpāditaḥ, saḥ niyataṃ parinirvṛte tathāgate, na bhavati tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāt, maraṇāduttarakālaṃ na bhavati, ucchinnastathāgataḥ, na saṃvidyate, iti parikalpayet | tasya evaṃ vikalpayataḥ syād dṛṣṭikṛtam || 13 ||
body.translated_text: For he by whom, through a dense, great attachment, the grasping has been grasped, the conceptual construction generated — 'the <s>Tathāgata</s> exists' — that person would certainly conceptualize about the <s>Tathāgata</s> who has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> does not exist after death; after death, at a subsequent time, [he] does not exist; the <s>Tathāgata</s> is annihilated; [he] is not found.' For such a one who conceptualizes thus, there would be a view-based [wrong] action. // 13 //

body.text: yasya tu na kasyāṃcidapyavasthāyāṃ svabhāvaśūnyatvāt tathāgatasya astitvanāstitvam, tasya pakṣe-
body.translated_text: But for one in whose position the <s>Tathāgata</s> has neither existence nor non-existence in any state whatsoever, due to being empty of inherent nature —

children.translated_text: Regarding that which is empty by inherent nature, the thought simply does not arise:

children.text: paraṃ nirodhādbhavati buddho na bhavatīti vā || 14 ||
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Buddha</s> exists after cessation' or 'does not exist.' // 14 //

body.text: ākāśe citrarūpakalpanāvadeṣā kalpanā nāstītyabhiprāyaḥ || 14 ||
body.translated_text: Such conceptualization does not exist — like imagining colorful pictures in the sky. This is the intended meaning. // 14 //

body.text: tadevaṃ prakṛtiśānte niḥsvabhāve tathāgate sarvaprapañcātīte mandabuddhitayā śāśvatāśāśvatādikayā nityānityāstināstiśūnyāśūnyasarvajñāsarvajñādikayā kalpanayā-
body.translated_text: Thus, regarding the <s>Tathāgata</s> who is quiescent by nature, without inherent nature, and beyond all conceptual elaboration (<s>prapañca</s>) — through dull-wittedness, by means of conceptual constructions such as eternal and non-eternal, permanent and impermanent, existent and non-existent, empty and non-empty, omniscient and non-omniscient, and so forth —

children.translated_text: Those who conceptually elaborate upon the <s>Buddha</s>, who is beyond conceptual elaboration and imperishable —

children.text: te prapañcahatāḥ sarve na paśyanti tathāgatam || 15 ||
children.translated_text: they, struck down by conceptual elaboration, do not see the <s>Tathāgata</s>. // 15 //

body.text: vastunibandhanā hi prapañcāḥ syuḥ, avastukaśca tathāgataḥ | kutaḥ prapañcānāṃ pravṛttisaṃbhava iti? ataḥ prapañcātītastathāgataḥ | anutpādasvabhāvāvācca svabhāvāntarāgamanādavyayaḥ | tamitthaṃvidhaṃ tathāgataṃ svotprekṣitamithyāparikalpamalamalinamānasatayā vividhairabhūtaiḥ parikalpaviśeṣaiḥ ye buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ prapañcayanti, te svakaireva prapañcairhatāḥ santaḥ tathāgataguṇasamṛddheratyantaparokṣavartino bhavanti | tataśca śavabhūtāḥ etasmin pravacane na paśyanti tathāgataṃ jātyandhā ivādityam | ata evāha bhagavān-
body.translated_text: For conceptual elaborations would be based on [real] entities, but the <s>Tathāgata</s> is without [real] entity. Whence could there be the possibility of the application of conceptual elaborations? Therefore the <s>Tathāgata</s> is beyond conceptual elaboration. And because of the nature of non-arising, and because of the impossibility of the coming-to-be of another inherent nature, he is imperishable. Those who, with minds stained by the impurity of false conceptual constructions imagined by themselves, conceptually elaborate upon the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s> with various unreal conceptual distinctions — they, being struck down by their own conceptual elaborations, become utterly remote from the wealth of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s qualities. And thus, being like corpses in this teaching, they do not see the <s>Tathāgata</s> — like those born blind [who do not see] the sun. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said:

children.text: ye māṃ rūpeṇa adrākṣurye māṃ ghoṣeṇa anvayuḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who saw me by form, those who followed me by voice —

children.text: mithyāprahāṇaprasṛtā na māṃ drakṣyanti te janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those people, engaged in wrong abandonment, will not see me.

children.text: dharmato buddhā draṣṭavyā dharmakāyā hi nāyakāḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s> are to be seen through the <s>Dharma</s>, for the guides have the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body).

children.text: dharmatā cāpyavijñeyā na sā śakyā vijānitum ||
children.translated_text: And the true nature of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmatā</s>) is unknowable — it cannot be known. //

body.text: tadatra tathāgataparīkṣāyāṃ sattvalokaḥ sakalaḥ sasurāsuranarādiḥ parīkṣitaḥ | yathā cāyaṃ sattvaloko niḥsvabhāvaḥ, tathā bhājanalokasyāpi vāyumaṇḍalāderakaniṣṭhavitānabhavanaparyantasya naiḥsvābhāvyamudbhāvayannāha-
body.translated_text: Thus, here in the Examination of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the entire world of beings together with <s>devas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, humans, and the rest has been examined. And just as this world of beings is without inherent nature, so too, demonstrating the absence of inherent nature of the world as receptacle (<s>bhājanāloka</s>) — from the wind-disc up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> dome of heaven — he says:

body.text: tathāgato yatsvabhāvastatsvabhāvamidaṃ jagat |
body.translated_text: Whatever is the inherent nature of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, that is the inherent nature of this world.

body.text: idaṃ jagaditi ayaṃ bhājanaloka ityarthaḥ | kiṃsvabhāvastathāgataḥ punarityāha-
body.translated_text: 'This world' means this world as receptacle — this is the meaning. And what is the inherent nature of the <s>Tathāgata</s>? He says:

body.text: tathāgato niḥsvabhāvo niḥsvabhāvamidaṃ jagat || 16 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> is without inherent nature; this world is without inherent nature. // 16 //

body.text: iti | yathā ca jagato naiḥsvābhāvyam, tathā pratyayaparīkṣādibhiḥ pratipāditam | ata evoktaṃ sūtre-
body.translated_text: And the absence of inherent nature of the world has been demonstrated by the Examination of Conditions and so forth. Therefore it is stated in a <s>sūtra</s>:

children.text: anupādadharmaḥ satataṃ tathāgataḥ sarve ca dharmāḥ sugatena sādṛśāḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> is constantly of the nature of non-grasping; and all <s>dharmas</s> are similar to the <s>Sugata</s>.

children.text: nimittagrāheṇa tu bālabuddhayaḥ asatsu dharmeṣu caranti loke ||
children.translated_text: But those of childish understanding, through grasping at signs, act in the world regarding <s>dharmas</s> that do not [truly] exist. //

body.text:
tathāgato hi pratibimbabhūtaḥ kuśalasya dharmasya anāsravasya |
naivātra tathatā na tathāgato 'sti bimbaṃ ca saṃdṛśyati sarva loke || iti |
body.translated_text: For the <s>Tathāgata</s> is like a reflection of wholesome, undefiled <s>dharma</s>. Neither <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) nor the <s>Tathāgata</s> exists herein — yet the reflection is seen in the entire world. //

body.text: uktaṃ ca bhagavatyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyām-
body.translated_text: And it is stated in the <s>Bhagavatī Prajñāpāramitā</s>:

body.text: atha khalu te devaputrāḥ āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtiṃ sthavirametadavocan- kiṃ punarāryasubhūte māyopamāste sattvāḥ, na te māyā? evamukte āyuṣmān subhūtistān devaputrānetadavocat- māyopamāste devaputrāḥ sattvāḥ, svapnopamāste devaputrāḥ sattvāḥ | iti hi māyā ca sattvāśca advayameta dadvaidhīkāram | iti hi svapnaśca sattvāśca advayametadadvaidhīkāram |sarvadharmā api devaputrā māyopamāḥ svapnopamāḥ | strotaāpanno 'pi māyopamaḥ svapnopamaḥ | strotaāpattiphalamapi māyopamaṃ svapnopamam | evaṃ sakṛdāgāmyapi sakṛdāgāmiphalamapi | anāgāmyapi anāgāmiphalamapi | arhannapi māyopamaḥ svapnopamaḥ | arhattvaphalamapi māyopamaṃ svapnopamam | pratyekabuddho 'pi māyopamaḥ svapnopamaḥ | pratyekabuddhatvamapi māyopamaṃ svapnopamam | samyaksaṃbuddho 'pi māyopamaḥ svapnopamaḥ iti | samyaksaṃbuddhatvamapi māyopamaṃ svapnopamamiti vadāmi ||
body.translated_text: Then those <s>devaputras</s> said to the Elder, the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'Are those beings, Noble <s>Subhūti</s>, like a magical illusion, [or] are they not illusions?' Thus addressed, the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to those <s>devaputras</s>: 'Those beings, <s>devaputras</s>, are like a magical illusion; those beings, <s>devaputras</s>, are like a dream. For illusion and beings are non-dual, without duality. For dream and beings are non-dual, without duality. All <s>dharmas</s> too, <s>devaputras</s>, are like an illusion, like a dream. A stream-enterer too is like an illusion, like a dream. The fruit of stream-entry too is like an illusion, like a dream. Likewise a once-returner and the fruit of once-returning. A non-returner too and the fruit of non-returning. An <s>Arhat</s> too is like an illusion, like a dream. The fruit of <s>Arhatship</s> too is like an illusion, like a dream. A <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> too is like an illusion, like a dream. <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s> too is like an illusion, like a dream. A perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s> too is like an illusion, like a dream. Perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbuddhatva</s>) too, I say, is like an illusion, like a dream.'

body.text: atha khalu devaputrā āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimetadavocan- samyaksaṃbuddho 'pi māyopamaḥ svapnopama iti, samyaksaṃbuddhatvamapi māyopamaṃ svapnopamamiti āryasubhūte vadasi? subhūtirāha- nirvāṇamapi devaputrā māyopamaṃ svapnopamamiti vadāmi, kiṃ punaranyaṃ dharmam? devaputrā āhuḥ- nirvāṇamapyāryasubhūte māyopamaṃ svapnopamamiti vadasi? subhūtirāha- yadyapi devaputrā nirvāṇādapyanyaḥ kaściddharmo viśiṣṭataraḥ syāt, tamapyahaṃ māyopamaṃ svapnopamamiti vadeyam | iti hi māyā ca nirvāṇaṃ ca advayametadadvaidhīkāramiti ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>devaputras</s> said to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'You say, Noble <s>Subhūti</s>, that even a perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s> is like an illusion, like a dream, and that perfect awakening too is like an illusion, like a dream?' <s>Subhūti</s> replied: 'Even <s>nirvāṇa</s>, <s>devaputras</s>, I say is like an illusion, like a dream — how much more so any other <s>dharma</s>?' The <s>devaputras</s> said: 'You say, Noble <s>Subhūti</s>, that even <s>nirvāṇa</s> is like an illusion, like a dream?' <s>Subhūti</s> replied: 'Even if, <s>devaputras</s>, there were some <s>dharma</s> more distinguished than <s>nirvāṇa</s>, even that I would say is like an illusion, like a dream. For illusion and <s>nirvāṇa</s> are non-dual, without duality.'

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacitāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau tathāgataparīkṣā nāma dvāviṃśatitamaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, 'Examination of the <s>Tathāgata</s>' (<s>Tathāgataparīkṣā</s>), in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary composed by the venerable <s>Ācārya Candrakīrti</s>. //

body.text:
23
viparyāsaparīkṣā trayoviṃśatitamaṃ prakaraṇam |
body.translated_text:
23
'Examination of Perversions' (<s>Viparyāsaparīkṣā</s>), the twenty-third chapter.

body.text: atrāha- vidyata eva bhavasaṃtatiḥ, tatkāraṇasadbhāvāt | iha hi kleśebhyaḥ karma pravartate | karmakleśahetukā janmamaraṇaparaṃparā upajāyate | sā ca bhavasaṃtatirvyapadiśyate | tasyāśca pradhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ kleśāḥ, prahīṇakleśānāṃ bhavasaṃtaterabhāvāt | te ca rāgādayaḥ kleśāḥ santi | tasmāt kāryabhūtāpi janmamaraṇaparaṃparā avicchedaprabandhena bhavasaṃtatirapi bhaviṣyatīti | ucyate | syād bhavasaṃtatiḥ, yadi taddhetubhūtāḥ kleśāḥ syuḥ | na tu santi | kathaṃ kṛtvā? iha bhagavadbhirbuddhaiḥ sakalatribhuvanajanasaṃkleśaśatruvidhvaṃsibhiścaturmārārātisamaraparājayaiḥ-
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: The continuum of existence (<s>bhavasaṃtati</s>) does indeed exist, because its cause exists. For here, <s>karma</s> proceeds from the afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>). The succession of birth and death arises from <s>karma</s> and the afflictions as its causes. And that is designated as the continuum of existence. And its primary cause is the afflictions, since for those who have eliminated the afflictions, the continuum of existence is absent. And those afflictions — passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the rest — do exist. Therefore the succession of birth and death, which is the effect, will also exist as the continuum of existence in an unbroken stream. [Reply:] The continuum of existence would exist, if the afflictions that are its cause were to exist. But they do not. How so? Here, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, the <s>Buddhas</s>, who destroy the enemy of the defilements of all beings in the three worlds, who are victorious in the battle with the four <s>Māra</s>-foes —

children.translated_text: Passion (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>) are said to originate from conceptual thought (<s>saṃkalpa</s>).
For they arise dependent on the perversions of pleasant and unpleasant. // 1 //

body.text: saṃkalpo vitarkaḥ | saṃkalpāt prabhavatīti saṃkalpaprabhavaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃkalpa</s> is discursive thought (<s>vitarka</s>). 'Originating from <s>saṃkalpa</s>' means arising from conceptual thought.

children.text: kāma jānāmi te mūlaṃ saṃkalpātkila jāyase |
children.translated_text: 'O desire, I know your root — you are born from conceptual thought.

children.text: na tvāṃ saṃkalpayiṣyāmi tato me na bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: I shall not conceptualize you; therefore you shall not exist for me.' //

body.text: iti gāthābhidhānāt
body.translated_text: — because of this verse declaration.

body.text: saṃkalpaprabhavo rāgo dveṣo mohaśca kathyate |
body.translated_text: Passion, aversion, and delusion are said to originate from conceptual thought.

body.text: etanmūlakatvādanyeṣāṃ kleśānāṃ mukhyatvādeṣāmevopādānaṃ trayāṇām | ete ca trayaḥ kleśāḥ-
body.translated_text: Because these are the root [of the others], and because of the pre-eminence of the other afflictions, only these three are taken up [for analysis]. And these three afflictions —

body.text: śubhāśubhaviparyāsān saṃbhavanti pratītya hi |
body.translated_text: arise dependent on the perversions of pleasant and unpleasant.

body.text: tatra hi śubhamākāraṃ pratītya rāga utpadyate, aśubhaṃ pratītya dveṣaḥ, viparyāsān pratītya moha utpadyate | saṃkalpastu eṣāṃ trayāṇāmapi sādhāraṇakāraṇamutpattau | kathaṃ punarmohaḥ saṃkalpaprabhavaḥ? ucyate | uktaṃ hi pratītyasamutpāde bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: For therein, passion arises dependent on the appearance of the pleasant, aversion dependent on the unpleasant, and delusion arises dependent on the perversions. And conceptual thought is the common cause for the arising of all three. But how is delusion (<s>moha</s>) 'originating from conceptual thought'? [Reply:] For it has been stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the [teaching on] dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>):

body.text: avidyāpi bhikṣavaḥ sahetukā sapratyayā sanidānā | kaśca bhikṣavaḥ avidyāyā hetuḥ? ayoniśo bhikṣavo manaskāro 'vidyāyā hetuḥ | āvilo mohajo manaskāro bhikṣavo 'vidyāyā hetuḥ || ityataḥ avidyā saṃkalpaprabhavā bhavati || 1 ||
body.translated_text: 'Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) too, monks, has a cause, has a condition, has an origin. And what, monks, is the cause of ignorance? Improper attention (<s>ayoniśo manaskāra</s>), monks, is the cause of ignorance. Attention that is turbid and born of delusion, monks, is the cause of ignorance.' Therefore ignorance originates from conceptual thought. // 1 //

body.text: tataśca-
body.translated_text: And from that —

children.translated_text: Those which arise dependent on the perversions of pleasant and unpleasant —

children.text: te svabhāvānna vidyante tasmāt kleśā na tattvataḥ || 2 ||
children.translated_text: they do not exist by their own nature; therefore the afflictions do not exist in reality. // 2 //

body.text: iti | yadi rāgādayaḥ svabhāvasiddhāḥ syuḥ, naiva te śubhāśubhaviparyāsān pratītya saṃbhaveyuḥ, svabhāvasya akṛtrimatvāt paranirapekṣatvācca | bhavanti ca śubhāśubhaviparyāsān pratītya, tasmānniḥsvabhāvā eva te | tattvato na vidyante, paramārthataḥ svabhāvato na vidyante ityarthaḥ || 2 ||
body.translated_text: If passion and the rest were established by their own nature, they would never arise dependent on the perversions of pleasant and unpleasant, since own-nature is uncreated and independent of others. But they do arise dependent on the perversions of pleasant and unpleasant — therefore they are simply without inherent nature. They do not exist in reality, meaning they do not exist ultimately, by their own nature. // 2 //

body.text: api ca-
body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.translated_text: The existence and non-existence of the self are not established in any way;
without that [self], how will the existence and non-existence of the afflictions be established? // 3 //

body.text: ātmano yathā astitvanāstitve na staḥ, tathā uktaṃ vistareṇa | tataśca- tadāśritasya dharmasya kuto 'stitvanāstitve bhaviṣyataḥ? || 3 ||
body.translated_text: That the existence and non-existence of the self are not established has been stated in detail. And therefore — for the <s>dharma</s> that is dependent on that [self], whence will existence and non-existence come to be? // 3 //

body.text: atha syāt- yadi astitvanāstitve ātmano na staḥ, tadā kimatra kleśānāmāyātam, yatasteṣāmapi astitvanāstitve na staḥ iti? ucyate-
body.translated_text: Now one might say: if the existence and non-existence of the self are not established, then what does this have to do with the afflictions here, such that their existence and non-existence too are not established? [Reply:]

children.text: kasyaciddhi bhavantīme kleśāḥ sa ca na sidhyati |
children.translated_text: For these afflictions belong to someone, and that [someone] is not established.

children.text: kaścidāho vinā kaṃcitsanti kleśā na kasyacit || 4 ||
children.translated_text: Can the afflictions exist apart from someone? They do not belong to anyone [else]. // 4 //

body.text: iha amī rāgādayaḥ kuḍayaṃ citravat phalaṃ pakvatādivacca utpattau āśrayamapekṣante | tataśca kasyacidete bhavanti, na vinā kaṃcidāśrayam | sa ca āśrayaḥ parikalpyamānaḥ ātmā vā cittaṃ vā bhavet | sa caiṣāmāśrayaḥ pūrvameva pratiṣiddhatvānnāsti | taṃ ca kaṃcidāśrayaṃ vinā kasya kleśā bhavantu? naiva kasyacidbhavanti, tasyāvidyamānatvāt, āho vinā kaṃcit santi kleśā na kasyacit || 4 ||
body.translated_text: Here, these [afflictions] of passion and the rest require a support for their arising — like a painting on a wall, or like the ripening of fruit. And therefore these belong to someone, not apart from some support. And that support, when imagined, would be either the self or the mind. And that support of these [afflictions] does not exist, since it has already been refuted. And apart from some support, whose afflictions would they be? They do not belong to anyone at all, since that [support] is non-existent — or, apart from someone, the afflictions do not belong to anyone. // 4 //

body.text: atrāha- naiva hi kleśānāṃ kaścidāśrayaḥ pūrvaṃ siddho 'bhyupagamyate | na ca ātmā nāma kaścidasti, yaḥ āśrayatvena vyavasthāpyeta, nirhetukatvād vyomacūtataruvat | kiṃ tarhi kliṣṭaṃ cittaṃ pratītya kleśā upajāyante, tacca cittaṃ sahaiva kleśairupajāyata iti | etadapi na yuktamityāha-
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: No substratum of the afflictions is accepted as established beforehand. Nor is there any entity called a 'self' that would be established as the substratum — because it would be without a cause, like a mango tree in the sky. Rather, the afflictions arise in dependence on the afflicted (<s>kliṣṭa</s>) mind, and that mind arises together with the afflictions. This too is not justified — hence he says:

children.text: svakāyadṛṣṭivat kleśāḥ kliṣṭe santi na pañcadhā |
children.translated_text: Like the view of the real body (<s>svakāyadṛṣṭi</s>), the afflictions do not exist in the afflicted [mind] in the five ways. /
Like the view of the real body, the afflicted [mind] does not exist in the afflictions in the five ways either. // 5 //

body.text: svakāyo hi nāma rūpādilakṣaṇasaṃhatiḥ | svakāyadṛṣṭiḥ svakāye ātmadṛṣṭiḥ ātmīyākāragrahaṇapravṛttā | yatheyaṃ pañcadhā vicāryamāṇā svakāye na saṃbhavati,
body.translated_text: The 'own body' (<s>svakāya</s>) is the aggregate characterized by form and the rest. The 'view of the own body' (<s>svakāyadṛṣṭi</s>) is the view of self in the own body — operating through the apprehension of 'mine.' Just as this [view], when examined in the five ways, does not obtain in the own body —

children.text: skandhā na nānyaḥ skandhebhyo nāsmin skandhā na teṣu saḥ |
children.translated_text: [The <s>Tathāgata</s>] is not the <s>skandhas</s>, nor other than the <s>skandhas</s>; the <s>skandhas</s> are not in him, nor he in them. /
The <s>Tathāgata</s> does not possess the <s>skandhas</s> — which, then, is the <s>Tathāgata</s>? //

body.text: ityanena | evaṃ kliṣṭe 'pi kleśā vicāryamāṇāḥ pañcadhā na saṃbhavanti | tatra kliśyantīti kleśā kliśyate iti kliṣṭam | tatra yadeva kliṣṭaṃ tadeva kleśā iti na yujyate dagdhṛdāhyayorapyekatvaprasaṅgāt | anyat kliṣṭam, anye kleśā iti na yujyate | paratra nirapekṣatvāt, akliṣṭahetuka kleśaprasaṅgāt | ata eva ca ekatvānyatvābhāvādādhārādheyatadvatpakṣāṇāṃ ca abhāvānna kleśeṣu kliṣṭam, na kliṣṭe kleśāḥ, nāpi kleśavat kliṣṭam | ityevaṃ kliṣṭe pañcadhā vicāryamāṇāḥ kleśā na saṃbhavanti | yathā ca kliṣṭahetukāḥ kleśā na saṃbhavanti, evaṃ kleśahetukamapi kliṣṭaṃ kleśeṣu vicāryamāṇaṃ pañcadhā na saṃbhavati | na hi kleśā eva kliṣṭam, kartṛkarmaṇorekatvaprasaṅgāt, nānye kleśā anyat kliṣṭam, nirapekṣatvaprasaṅgāt, na ca kliṣṭe kleśāḥ na ca kleśeṣu kliṣṭam, na kliṣṭavantaḥ
body.translated_text: — by this [verse]. Even so, the afflictions, when examined in the afflicted [mind], do not obtain in the five ways. Therein, 'they afflict' — hence 'afflictions' (<s>kleśas</s>); 'it is afflicted' — hence 'the afflicted' (<s>kliṣṭa</s>). Therein, that the afflicted is identical with the afflictions is not justified, because of the absurd consequence that the burner and the burnt would also be identical. That the afflicted is one thing and the afflictions another is not justified, because of the [consequent] independence from the other, and because of the absurd consequence that the afflictions would have a non-afflicted cause. And precisely because of the absence of identity and otherness, the positions of container-contained and possessor-possessed are also absent — the afflictions are not in the afflicted, the afflicted is not in the afflictions, nor is the afflicted a possessor of afflictions. Thus, when the afflictions are examined in the afflicted in the five ways, they do not obtain. And just as the afflictions caused by the afflicted do not obtain, so too the afflicted that is caused by the afflictions, when examined in the afflictions in the five ways, does not obtain. For the afflictions are not identical with the afflicted, because of the absurd consequence that agent and action would be identical; nor are the afflictions one thing and the afflicted another, because of the consequence of independence; the afflicted is not in the afflictions, the afflictions are not in the afflicted, and the afflictions do not possess the afflicted

body.text: kleśāḥ | ityevaṃ svakāyadṛṣṭivadeva kliṣṭaṃ kleśeṣvapi pañcadhā nāsti | yataścaivam, ataḥ parasparāpekṣayāpi kleśākliṣṭayornāsti siddhiḥ || 5 ||
body.translated_text: . Thus, just as with the view of the real body, the afflicted does not exist in the afflictions in the five ways either. And since this is so, even through mutual dependence, the establishment of the afflictions and the afflicted is impossible. // 5 //

body.text: atrāha- yadyapi tvayā kleśāḥ pratiṣiddhāḥ, tathāpi kleśahetavaḥ śubhāśubhaviparyāsāstāvat santi, tatsadbhāvācca kleśāḥ santīti | ucyate | syuḥ kleśāḥ, yadi śubhāśubhaviparyāsā eva syuḥ, yāvatā ete 'pi pratītya sasutpannatvādvakṣyamāṇapratiṣedhācca | yadā ca te na santi svabhāvataḥ, tadā-
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: Even though the afflictions have been refuted by you, nevertheless the perversions (<s>viparyāsas</s>) regarding the attractive and unattractive, which are the causes of afflictions, at least exist; and because of their existence, the afflictions exist. [Reply:] The afflictions would exist if the perversions regarding the attractive and unattractive themselves existed. But even these, because of being dependently originated and because of the refutation to be stated — and when they do not exist by their own nature, then:

body.text: svabhāvato na vidyante śubhāśubhaviparyayāḥ |
body.translated_text: The perversions regarding the attractive and unattractive do not exist by their own nature. /

body.text: pratītyasamutpannatvādvakṣyamāṇapratiṣedhācca | yadā ca te na santi svabhāvataḥ, tadā-
body.translated_text: Because of being dependently originated and because of the refutation to be stated. And when they do not exist by their own nature, then:

body.text: pratītya katamān kleśāḥ śubhāśubhaviparyayān || 6 ||
body.translated_text: In dependence on which perversions regarding the attractive and unattractive do the afflictions [arise]? // 6 //

body.text: naiva santi kleśāḥ, taddhetuśubhāśubhaviparyayābhāvādityabhiprāyaḥ || 6 ||
body.translated_text: The afflictions simply do not exist — because of the non-existence of their causes, the perversions regarding the attractive and unattractive — this is the intent. // 6 //

body.text: atrāha- vidyanta eva kleśāḥ, tadālambanasadbhāvāt | iha hi yannāsti, na tasyālambana masti, tadyathā vandhyāsūnoḥ | asti ca rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyadharmākhyaṃ ṣaḍvidhamālambanam | tasmādālambanasadbhāvādvidyanta eva kleśā iti | ucyate | astyetat, yad bhavadbhiḥ-
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: The afflictions do indeed exist, because of the existence of their objects (<s>ālambana</s>). Here, what does not exist has no object — for example, the son of a barren woman. But the sixfold object — called form, sound, smell, taste, touch, and <s>dharmas</s> — does exist. Therefore, because of the existence of the object, the afflictions do indeed exist. [Reply:] This is so; it is as you [maintain]:

children.translated_text: Form, sound, taste, touch, smell, and <s>dharmas</s> — the sixfold /

children.text: vastu rāgasya dveṣasya mohasya ca vikalpyate || 7 ||
children.translated_text: object of passion, hatred, and delusion is imagined. // 7 //

body.text: tatra vastu ālambanam, vasatīti vā asmin rāgādikam, tadutpatteḥ iti kṛtvā | tacca tadālambanaṃ ṣoḍhā bhavati, indriyāṇāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ paricchedakarāṇāmanyonyabhedāt | rūpaṃ śabdā gandhā rasāḥ spraṣṭavyāni dharmāśceti | tatra idamihāmutreti nirūpaṇāt, rūpaṇācca rūpam | tena śabdena śabdyante prakāśyante padārthā iti śabdaḥ | gandhyante hiṃsyante yatra prāptāḥ tato 'nyatrāgamanād gandhāḥ | rasyate āsvādyate iti rasaḥ | spṛśyate iti sparśaḥ | svalakṣaṇāsādhāraṇānnirvāṇāgradharmādhāraṇāddharmāḥ | tadetat ṣaḍvidhaṃ vastu bhavati | kasya? rāgasya dveṣasya mohasya | tatra rañjanaṃ rāgo raktiradhyavasānam | rajyate vā anena cittamiti rāgaḥ | dūṣaṇaṃ doṣaḥ, āghātaḥ sattvaviṣayo 'sattvaviṣayo vā dūṣyate vā anena citamiti doṣaḥ | mohanaṃ mohaḥ saṃmohaḥ padārthasvarūpāparijñānam | muhyate vā anena cittamiti mohaḥ | tadeṣāṃ kleśānāṃ rūpādikaṃ ṣaḍvidhaṃ vastu ālambanaṃ bhavati | tatra śubhākārādhyāropeṇa yathā rūpādibhyo rāga upajāyate, aśubhākārādhyāropeṇa dveṣaḥ, nityātmādyadhyāropeṇa mohaḥ saṃbhavatīti || 7 ||
body.translated_text: Therein, 'object' (<s>vastu</s>) means support (<s>ālambana</s>) — or: passion and the rest 'dwell' (<s>vasati</s>) in it, because they arise there. And that object is sixfold, due to the mutual distinction of the six sense faculties that delimit [their respective objects]: form, sounds, smells, tastes, tangibles, and <s>dharmas</s>. Therein: it is 'form' (<s>rūpa</s>) because it delineates 'this is here, this is there,' and because it 'forms.' Things are made known and revealed by 'sound' (<s>śabda</s>) — hence 'sound.' 'Smells' (<s>gandha</s>) — because those who arrive where [they are] are impelled (<s>gandhyante</s>) to move away from there. 'Taste' (<s>rasa</s>) — because it is savored (<s>rasyate</s>). 'Touch' (<s>sparśa</s>) — because it is touched (<s>spṛśyate</s>). '<s>Dharmas</s>' — because of their bearing (<s>dhāraṇa</s>) the uncommon own-characteristics, up to the supreme <s>dharmas</s> including <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Thus this object is sixfold. Of what? Of passion, hatred, and delusion. Therein, 'passion' (<s>rāga</s>) is coloring, attachment, fixed determination — or: the mind is 'colored' (<s>rajyate</s>) by it, hence <s>rāga</s>. 'Hatred' (<s>dveṣa</s>) is a defect (<s>doṣa</s>), hostility — whether directed at beings or non-beings — or: the mind is 'defiled' (<s>dūṣyate</s>) by it, hence <s>doṣa</s>. 'Delusion' (<s>moha</s>) is bewilderment, confusion — non-comprehension of the own-nature of things — or: the mind is 'bewildered' (<s>muhyate</s>) by it, hence <s>moha</s>. Thus, for these afflictions, the sixfold object beginning with form serves as the support. Therein, passion arises from form and the rest through the superimposition of the aspect of attractiveness; hatred through the superimposition of the aspect of unattractiveness; and delusion through the superimposition of permanence, self, and so forth. // 7 //

body.text: satyaṃ vikalpyate etadbālajanaiḥ ṣaḍvidhaṃ vastu | kiṃ tu avidyamānasvabhāvasattākametad rāgādīnāmālambanatvena parikalpyate bhavatā taimirikairiva asatkeśamaśakamakṣikādvicandrādikamiti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: It is true that this sixfold object is imagined by foolish beings. However, this, being without existent inherent nature, is imagined by you as the object of passion and the rest — like the non-existent hairs, insects, flies, double moons, and so forth [imagined] by those with cataracts. Demonstrating this, he says:

body.text: rūpaśabdarasasparśā gandhā dharmāśca kevalāḥ |
body.translated_text: Form, sound, taste, touch, smell, and <s>dharmas</s> — are mere [constructs]. /

body.text: kevalā iti parikalpitamātrā niḥsvabhāvā ityarthaḥ | yadi niḥsvabhāvāḥ, kathaṃ tarhi upalabhyante iti? ucyate-
body.translated_text: 'Mere' (<s>kevala</s>) — meaning merely imagined, without inherent nature. If they are without inherent nature, how then are they apprehended? [Reply:]

body.text: gandharvanagarākārā marīcisvapnasaṃnibhāḥ || 8 ||
body.translated_text: They are like a <s>gandharva</s>-city in form, resembling a mirage and a dream. // 8 //

body.text: iti ete upalabhyante || 8 ||
body.translated_text: Thus they are apprehended. // 8 //

body.text: yathā gandharvanagarādiprakhyā ete kevalaṃ viparyāsādupalabhyante, tadā-
body.translated_text: Since, like a <s>gandharva</s>-city and the rest, these are apprehended merely through perversion, then:

children.text: aśubhaṃ vā śubhaṃ vāpi kutasteṣu bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: How could the unattractive or the attractive exist /
in those that are like illusory persons and equal to reflections? // 9 //

body.text: tadanena mithyāśrayasamutpannatvācchubhāśubhayorapi nimittayormṛṣātvameva bhavati | yathoktam-
body.translated_text: By this, since the attractive and unattractive — the two causes — arise from a false substratum, their falsity too is [established]. As stated:

children.translated_text: 'The <s>skandhas</s> arise from the sense of "I" (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>); that sense of "I" is in reality false. /

children.text: bījaṃ yasyānṛtaṃ tasya prarohaḥ satyataḥ kutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the seed is false, how could its sprout be real? //
Having seen the <s>skandhas</s> as unreal in this way, the sense of "I" is abandoned. /
From the abandonment of the sense of "I," the <s>skandhas</s> no longer arise.' //

body.text: na ca kevalamāśrayamithyātve śubhāśubhayornimittayormithyātvam, api ca anayāpyupapattyā anayormithyātvamiti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And it is not only through the falsity of the substratum that the two causes — the attractive and unattractive — are false; but also by this further reasoning their falsity is demonstrated — hence he says:

children.translated_text: Without reference to the attractive, we would not designate the unattractive. /
That in dependence on which we designate the attractive — therefore the attractive itself is not tenable. // 10 //

body.text: iha yadi śubhaṃ nāma kiṃcit syāt, niyataṃ tadaśubhamapekṣya bhavet, pārāvāravat, bījāṅkuravat, hrasvadīrghavadvā, śubhasya saṃbandhyantarapadārthasāpekṣatvāt | taccāpyapekṣaṇīyamaśubhaṃ śubhena vinā nāsti | [anapekṣya śubhaṃ nāstyaśubhaṃ] śubhaṃ nirapekṣyāśubhaṃ nāstītyabhiprāyaḥ | yadaśubhaṃ pratītya yadaśubhamapekṣya śubhaṃ prajñapayemahi vyavasthāpayemahi | yacchabdena anantarasyāśubhasya parāmarśaḥ | prajñapayemahītyanena uttarasya śubhasya saṃbandhaḥ | yataśca evaṃ śubhasya prajñaptau saṃbandhyantaramapekṣaṇīyamaśubhākhyaṃ padārthāntaraṃ nāsti, tasmācchubhaṃ naivopapadyate hrasvāsaṃbhavādiva dīrgham, pārāsaṃbhavādiva avāramityabhiprāyaḥ || 10 ||
body.translated_text: Here, if something called 'the attractive' existed, it would necessarily exist in dependence on the unattractive — like the near and far shores, like the seed and sprout, or like short and long — because the attractive requires reference to another relational term. And that very unattractive thing to which reference must be made does not exist without the attractive. 'Without reference to the attractive, the unattractive does not exist' — the intent is: setting aside the attractive, the unattractive does not exist. That in dependence on the unattractive — that in reference to the unattractive — we would designate, we would establish, the attractive. By the word 'that' (<s>yat</s>), there is reference back to the immediately preceding [term] 'unattractive.' By 'we would designate,' the connection is with the subsequent [term] 'attractive.' And since thus, for the designation of the attractive, the other relational term called 'the unattractive' does not exist, therefore the attractive itself is not tenable — like the long without the short, or the near shore without the far — this is the intent. // 10 //

body.text: idānīmaśubhamapi yathā na saṃbhavati, tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, demonstrating that the unattractive too does not obtain, he says:

children.translated_text: Without reference to the unattractive, the attractive does not exist — [thus] we would not designate [it]. /
That in dependence on which we would designate the unattractive — therefore the unattractive does not exist at all. // 11 //

body.text: yadi hi aśubhaṃ nāma kiṃcit syāt, niyatameva tacchubhamapekṣya bhavet, pārāvāravat, hrasvadīrghavadvā, aśubhasya saṃbandhyantarapadārthasāpekṣatvāt | taccāpyapekṣaṇīyaṃ śubhamaśubhena vinā nāsti, anapekṣyāśubhaṃ nāsti śubham | aśubhaṃ nirapekṣya śubhaṃ na saṃbhavatītyabhiprāyaḥ | yacchubhaṃ pratītya yacchubhamapekṣya aśubhaṃ prajñapayemahi, aśubhaṃ vyavasthāpayemahi | atrāpi yacchabdena anantarasya
body.translated_text: For if something called 'the unattractive' existed, it would necessarily exist in dependence on the attractive — like the near and far shores, or like short and long — because the unattractive requires reference to another relational term. And that very attractive thing to which reference must be made does not exist without the unattractive: 'without reference to the unattractive, the attractive does not exist.' Setting aside the unattractive, the attractive does not obtain — this is the intent. That in dependence on the attractive — that in reference to the attractive — we would designate the unattractive, we would establish the unattractive. Here too, by the word 'that' (<s>yat</s>), there is reference back to the immediately preceding

body.text: śubhasya parāmarśaḥ | prajñapayemahītyanena ca uttarasyāśubhasya saṃbandhaḥ | yataścaivamaśubhasya prajñaptau saṃbandhyantaramapekṣaṇīyaṃ śubhākhyaṃ padārthāntaraṃ nāsti, tasmādaśubhaṃ naiva vidyate || 11 ||
body.translated_text: 'attractive.' And by 'we would designate,' the connection is with the subsequent 'unattractive.' And since thus, for the designation of the unattractive, the other relational term called 'the attractive' does not exist, therefore the unattractive does not exist at all. // 11 //

body.text: yataścaivaṃ śubhāśubhayorasaṃbhavaḥ, ataḥ-
body.translated_text: And since thus the attractive and unattractive are impossible, therefore:

children.text: avidyamāne ca śubhe kuto rāgo bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: When the attractive does not exist, whence will passion arise? /
When the unattractive does not exist, whence will hatred arise? // 12 //

body.text: śubhāśubhanimittakayo rāgadveṣayoḥ śubhāśubhanimittābhāve sati nirhetukatvānnāsti saṃbhava ityabhiprāyaḥ || 12 ||
body.translated_text: Since passion and hatred have the attractive and unattractive as their causes — when the causes, the attractive and unattractive, are absent, they are without cause and therefore do not arise — this is the intent. // 12 //

body.text: tadevaṃ śubhāśubhanimittābhāvena rāgadveṣayorabhāvamupapādya viparyāsasvabhāvābhāvapratipādanena mohasyāpyadhunā svabhāvābhāvaṃ pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Having thus established the non-existence of passion and hatred through the non-existence of their causes, the attractive and unattractive, now demonstrating the non-existence of the inherent nature of delusion as well, through demonstrating the non-existence of the inherent nature of perversion (<s>viparyāsa</s>), he says:

children.translated_text: If the grasping 'permanent' with respect to the impermanent is perversion, /

children.text: nānityaṃ vidyate śūnye kuto grāho viparyayaḥ || 13 ||
children.translated_text: then since the impermanent does not exist in what is empty, how could there be the grasping of perversion? // 13 //

body.text: iha catvāro viparyāsā ucyante | tadyathā- anitye pratikṣaṇavināśini skandhapañcake yo nityamiti grāhaḥ, sa viparyāsaḥ | tathā-

children.text: anityasya dhruvā pīḍā pīḍā yasya na tatsukham |
children.translated_text: 'What is impermanent is certainly painful; what is painful is not happiness. /
Therefore, whatever is impermanent — all of that is suffering' — thus it arises. //

body.translated_text: Here, four perversions are taught. Namely: in the fivefold <s>skandhas</s>, which are impermanent, perishing every moment, the grasping 'permanent' — that is perversion. Likewise:

body.text: ityamunā nyāyena yadanityaṃ tadduḥkham, sarvasaṃskārāśca anityāḥ, tasmādduḥkhātmake skandhapañcake yaḥ sukhamiti viparīto grāhaḥ, so 'paro viparyāsaḥ | tathā-
body.translated_text: By this reasoning: what is impermanent is suffering; and all conditioned things (<s>saṃskāras</s>) are impermanent; therefore, in the fivefold <s>skandhas</s> whose nature is suffering, the perverted grasping 'this is happiness' — that is another perversion. Likewise:

children.translated_text: 'The seed born from the union of semen and blood, nourished by feces and urine, /
of impure form — knowing this, why are you, through desire for the body, attached to it? //

body.text:
amedhyapuñjapracchanne tatkledārdreṇa carmaṇā |
yaḥ śayīta sa nārīṇāṃ śayīta jaghanodare || ityādi |
body.translated_text:
One who would lie upon a heap of filth covered by skin moistened with its secretions —
that one would lie upon the belly of women.' And so forth. //

body.text: evamidaṃ śarīraṃ sarvātmanā satatamaśucisvabhāvam | tatra yo mohācchucitvena grāho 'bhiniveśaḥ, sa viparyāsaḥ | tathā pañcaskandhakamātmalakṣaṇavilakṣaṇamasthiratvādudayavyayadharmitvācca nirātmakamātmasvabhāvaśūnyam, tasmin ya ātmagrāho 'bhiniveśaḥ anātmani ātmābhiniveśaḥ, sa viparyāsaḥ | ityete catvāro viparyāsāḥ saṃmohasya hetubhūtāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus this body is in every way, always, of an impure nature. Therein, the grasping, the clinging, to purity through delusion — that is perversion. Likewise, the fivefold <s>skandhas</s>, dissimilar from the characteristic of a self, without self, empty of self-nature — because of their instability, because of being subject to arising and passing away — therein, the grasping of a self, the clinging to a self in what is without self — that is perversion. Thus these four perversions are the causes of delusion. //

body.text: atredānīṃ vicāryate- yadi nityatvaṃ nityadarśanaṃ svabhāvaśūnyeṣu nityagrāho viparyāsa ityevaṃ vyavasthāpyate, nanu ca svabhāvaśūnyeṣu skandheṣu anityatvamapi nāsti, iti
body.translated_text: Now here this is examined: if permanence — the view of permanence — is established as perversion, namely the grasping 'permanent' with respect to what is empty of inherent nature, then indeed in the <s>skandhas</s> that are empty of inherent nature, impermanence too does not exist. Therefore:

body.text: nānityaṃ vidyate śūnye kuto grāho viparyayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Since the impermanent does not exist in what is empty, how could there be the grasping of perversion? /

body.text: anityatvaṃ hi viparītamapekṣya nityatvaṃ viparyāsa iti vyavasthāpyate | na ca anityatvaṃ vidyate śūnye | yadā anityatvasyābhāvaḥ, tadā kutastadvirodhi nityatvaṃ nityadarśanaviparyāso bhaviṣyatīti bhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: For impermanence is established as perversion with reference to its opposite, permanence. But impermanence does not exist in what is empty. When impermanence is absent, then how could its opposite — permanence, the perversion of the view of permanence — exist? This is the meaning.

body.text: tasmānnāsti viparyāsaḥ | yathā ca anityatvaṃ śūnye na saṃbhavati bhāvasvabhāvarahite sasvabhāvena anutpanne, evaṃ duḥkhatvamapi na saṃbhavati, aśucitvamapi nāsti | anātmakatvamapi nāsti | yadā ca svabhāvaśūnyatvādduḥkhatvādikaṃ nāsti, tadā kutastadvipakṣabhūtā nityasukhaśucyātmaviparyāsā bhaviṣyanti? tasmāt santi viparyāsāḥ svarūpataḥ | tadabhāve kuto bhaviṣyatyavidyā? hetvabhāvāt | yathoktaṃ bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: Therefore, perversion does not exist. And just as impermanence is not possible in what is empty — in what is devoid of the own-nature of an entity, in what has not arisen with own-nature — so too suffering is not possible, nor is impurity, nor is non-selfhood. And when, because of emptiness of own-nature, suffering and so forth do not exist, then whence would the perversions — [the notions of] permanence, pleasure, purity, and self, which are the opposite of those — come about? Therefore, the perversions do exist in their own nature. In their absence, whence would <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) come about? — since the cause is absent. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> has stated —

children.text: avidyayā naiva kadāci vidyate avidyata pratyayasaṃbhavaśca |
children.translated_text: <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) never exists as something real; and arising occurs through conditions for the non-existent. /

children.text: avidyamāneyamavidya loke tasmānmayā ukta avidya eṣā ||
children.translated_text: Since this <s>avidyā</s> is non-existent in the world, therefore I have called it <s>avidyā</s> (non-knowledge). //

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise —

body.text: kathaṃ bhagavan moho dhāraṇīpadam? bhagavānāha- atyantamukto hi mañjuśrīḥ mohaḥ, tenocyate mohaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'How, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is delusion a syllable of <s>dhāraṇī</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Delusion is utterly liberated, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>; hence it is called delusion.'

body.text: ityādinā viparyaya iti vyavasthāpyate || 13 ||
body.translated_text: — and so forth, [the term] 'perversion' is established [as a designation]. // 13 //

body.text: nanu evaṃ sati svabhāvena avidyamāne padārthe anityamityapi grāho na saṃbhavati iti asāvapi kasmānna viparyāsa iti vyavasthāpyate iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, if this is so — when the object does not exist by own-nature — the grasping 'it is impermanent' too is not possible; then why is that too not established as a perversion? Demonstrating this, he says —

children.translated_text: If the grasping 'permanent' with regard to what is impermanent is a perversion, /

children.text: anityamityapi grāhaḥ śūnye kiṃ na viparyayaḥ || 14 ||
children.translated_text: then the grasping 'impermanent' with regard to what is empty — why is it not a perversion? // 14 //

body.text: yadā ca ubhayasyāpi vaiparītyaṃ nityasya anityasya ca, tadā tadvayatiriktaṃ tṛtīyamaparaṃ nāsti yanna viparyayaḥ syāt | yadā ca aviparyāso nāsti, tadā kimapekṣo viparyāsaḥ syāditi | tasmādamunāpi nyāyena nāsti viparyayaḥ | tasyābhāvācca nāstyavidyā svarūpataḥ | yathā ca anitye nityamityevaṃ grāho viparyāso na saṃbhavati, evaṃ śeṣaviparyāsāsaṃbhave 'pi yojyam | ata evoktaṃ bhagavatā āryadṛḍhāśayaparipṛcchāyām-
body.translated_text: And when both are perverted — both permanence and impermanence — then apart from these two, there is no third [option] that would not be a perversion. And when there is no non-perversion, then with reference to what would there be perversion? Therefore, by this reasoning too, perversion does not exist. And because it does not exist, <s>avidyā</s> does not exist in its own nature. And just as the grasping 'permanent' with regard to what is impermanent is not possible as a perversion, so too it should be applied to the non-possibility of the remaining perversions. For this very reason, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has stated in the noble <s>Dṛḍhāśayaparipṛcchā</s> —

body.text: bhagavānāha- kimetat kulaputra tasya bhavati yo mārgeṇa niḥsaraṇaṃ paryeṣate? na kulaputra tathāgatena rañjanīyān dharmān parivarjya rāgaprahāṇaṃ prajñaptam, evaṃ na doṣaṇīyān mohanīyāna dharmān parivarjya tathāgatena doṣamohaprahāṇaṃ prajñaptam | tat kasmāddhetoḥ? na kulaputra tathāgatāḥ kasyaciddharmasya utsargāya vā pratilambhāya vā dharmaṃ deśayanti na parijñāyai na prahāṇāya na sākṣātkriyāyai nābhisamayāya na saṃsāracaraṇatāyai na nirvāṇagamanatāyai notkṣepāya na prabhedāya | na hi kulaputra dvayaprabhāvitā tathāgatadharmatā | tatra ye dvaye caranti, na te samyakprayuktāḥ | mithyāprayuktāste vaktavyāḥ | katamacca kulaputra dvayam? ahaṃ rāgaṃ prahāsyāmīti dvayametat | ahaṃ dveṣaṃ prahāsyāmīti dvayametat | ahaṃ mohaṃ prahāsyāmīti dvayametat | ye evaṃprayuktāḥ, na te samyakprayuktā | mithyāprayuktāste veditavyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What does this amount to, son of good family, for one who seeks escape through the path? The <s>Tathāgata</s>, son of good family, has not prescribed the abandonment of passion by setting aside <s>dharmas</s> that cause passion; likewise, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has not prescribed the abandonment of aversion and delusion by setting aside <s>dharmas</s> that cause aversion and delusion. For what reason? The <s>Tathāgatas</s>, son of good family, do not teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the sake of relinquishing or attaining any <s>dharma</s> whatsoever — not for full knowledge, not for abandonment, not for direct realization, not for actualization, not for the sake of wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s>, not for the sake of going to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, not for casting off, not for breaking apart. For the <s>dharmatā</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, son of good family, is not established through duality. Those who engage in duality are not rightly applied; they should be called wrongly applied. And what, son of good family, is this duality? "I shall abandon passion" — this is duality. "I shall abandon aversion" — this is duality. "I shall abandon delusion" — this is duality. Those who are thus applied are not rightly applied; they should be known as wrongly applied.'

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra kaścideva puruṣo māyākāranāṭake pratyupasthite māyākāranirmitāṃ striyaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāgacittamutpādayet | sa rāgaparītacittaḥ parṣacchāradyabhayena utthāyāsanādapakramet | so 'pakramya tāmeva striyamaśubhato manasi kuryādanityato duḥkhataḥ śūnyato 'nātmato manasi kuryāt | bhagavānāha- evameva kulaputra ihaike bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā draṣṭavyāḥ, ye 'nutpannān dharmānajātānaśubhato manasi kurvanti, anityato duḥkhato 'nātmato manasi kurvanti | nāhaṃ teṣāṃ mohapuruṣāṇāṃ mārgabhāvanāṃ vadāmi | mithyāprayuktāste veditavyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as, son of good family, some man, when a magician-actor has appeared, having seen a woman created by the magician, would generate a mind of passion — he, with a mind overcome by passion, out of fear and shame before the audience, would rise from his seat and depart. Having departed, he would attend to that very woman as impure, attend to her as impermanent, as suffering, as empty, as non-self.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Even so, son of good family, some monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen should be seen here — those who attend to <s>dharmas</s> that are unarisen and unborn as impure, who attend to them as impermanent, as suffering, as non-self. I do not call their cultivation the path of those deluded persons; they should be known as wrongly applied.'

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra kaścideva puruṣaḥ suptaḥ svapnāntare svagṛhe rājabhāryāṃ paśyet | sa tayā sārdhaṃ śayyāṃ kalpayet | smṛtisaṃmoṣāccaivaṃ kalpayet- viruddho 'smīti | sa bhītasrastaḥ palāyet, mā māṃ rājā vidhyet, sa mā māṃ jīvitād vyavaropayet | tat kiṃ manyase kulaputra api nu sa puruṣo bhītasrastaḥ palāyamānastato rājabhāryānidānabhayātparimucyeta? āha- no bhagavan | tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi bhagavaṃstena puruṣeṇa astriyāṃ strīsaṃjñā utpāditā, abhūtaṃ ca parikalpitam | bhagavānāha- evameva kulaputra ihaike bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā draṣṭavyāḥ, ye arāge rāgasaṃjñāmutpādya rāgabhayabhītā rāganiḥsaraṇaṃ paryeṣante | evamadoṣe doṣasaṃjñāmutpādya doṣabhayabhītā doṣaniḥsaraṇaṃ paryeṣante | amohe mohasaṃjñāmutpādya mohabhayabhītā mohaniḥsaraṇaṃ paryeṣante | nāhaṃ teṣāṃ mohapuruṣāṇāṃ mārgabhāvanāṃ vadāmi | mithyāprayuktāste veditavyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as, son of good family, some man, while asleep, would see in a dream the king's wife in his own house. He would prepare a bed with her. And through the loss of mindfulness, he would imagine thus: "I am in transgression." Frightened and alarmed, he would flee: "May the king not strike me! May he not deprive me of life!" What do you think, son of good family — would that man, frightened and alarmed and fleeing, be freed from the fear occasioned by the king's wife?' He said: 'No, <s>Bhagavān</s>. For what reason? For that man generated the perception of a woman with regard to what is not a woman, and imagined what is unreal.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Even so, son of good family, some monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen should be seen here — those who, having generated the perception of passion with regard to what is free from passion, seek escape from passion out of fear of passion; who, having generated the perception of aversion with regard to what is free from aversion, seek escape from aversion out of fear of aversion; who, having generated the perception of delusion with regard to what is free from delusion, seek escape from delusion out of fear of delusion. I do not call their cultivation the path of those deluded persons; they should be known as wrongly applied.'

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra sa puruṣaḥ abhaye bhayasaṃjñāmutpādayedasatsamāropeṇa | evameva kulaputra sarvabālapṛthagjanā rāgakoṭiṃ virāgakoṭimaprajānanto rāgakoṭibhayabhītā virāgakoṭiṃ niḥsaraṇaṃ paryeṣante | doṣakoṭimakiṃcanakoṭimaprajānanto doṣakoṭibhayabhītā akiṃcanakoṭiṃ niḥsaraṇaṃ paryeṣante | mohakoṭiṃ śūnyatākoṭimaprajānanto mohakoṭibhayabhītāḥ śūnyatākoṭiṃ niḥsaraṇaṃ paryeṣante | nāhaṃ teṣāṃ kulaputra mohapuruṣāṇāṃ mārgabhāvanāṃ vadāmi | mithyāprayuktāste veditavyāḥ || iti vistaraḥ || 14 ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as, son of good family, that man would generate the perception of fear with regard to what is free from fear, through the false superimposition of what does not exist — even so, son of good family, all foolish ordinary persons, not understanding the limit of passion and the limit of dispassion, seek escape to the limit of dispassion out of fear of the limit of passion. Not understanding the limit of aversion and the limit of non-possession, they seek escape to the limit of non-possession out of fear of the limit of aversion. Not understanding the limit of delusion and the limit of emptiness, they seek escape to the limit of emptiness out of fear of the limit of delusion. I do not call their cultivation the path, son of good family, of those deluded persons; they should be known as wrongly applied.' And so forth in detail. // 14 //

body.text: atrāha- yadyapi anitye nityamityevaṃ grāho viparyayo na saṃbhavati, tathāpi eṣa tāvat grāho 'sti | grāhaśca nāma saṃgrahaṇaṃ bhāvarūpaḥ | tasya ca avaśyaṃ sādhanena karaṇena bhavitavyaṃ sādhakatamena nityatvādinā | kartrā ca bhavitavyaṃ svatantreṇa nityātmanā cittena vā | karmaṇā ca karturīpsitatamena viṣayeṇa rūpādinā | satyāṃ ca bhāvakaraṇakartṛkarmaṇāṃ siddhau sarvasiddheriṣṭasiddhiḥ syādasmākamiti | ucyate | alīkeyaṃ pratyāśā | nanu ca yathopavarṇitena nyāyena-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: 'Even if the grasping "permanent" with regard to what is impermanent is not possible as a perversion, nevertheless this grasping at least exists. And grasping is indeed a seizing, a thing of real nature. And it must necessarily have an instrument — the most effective means, such as permanence and so forth. And it must have an agent — an independent, permanent self or a mind. And it must have an object — the thing most desired by the agent, such as form and so forth. And when the existence of the thing, the instrument, the agent, and the object is established, the establishment of everything we wish [to prove] would follow.' It is replied: This is a vain expectation. For indeed, by the reasoning as described —

children.text: yena gṛhṇāti yogrāho grahītā yacca gṛhyate |
children.translated_text: That by which one grasps, the grasping, the grasper, and that which is grasped — /
all are pacified; therefore grasping does not exist. // 15 //

body.text: iha hi kaścid grahītā yena viśeṣeṇa nityatvādinā karaṇabhūtena kiṃcit karmabhūtaṃ rūpaśabdādikaṃ vastu gṛhṇāti, tadyathā na saṃbhavati tathā pūrvaṃ pratipāditam | kathaṃ kṛtvā?
body.translated_text: Here, some grasper, by means of some particular instrument such as permanence and so forth, grasps some object such as form, sound, and so forth — that this is not possible has been demonstrated earlier. How so?

body.text: anitye nityamityevaṃ yadi grāho viparyayaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'If the grasping "permanent" with regard to what is impermanent is a perversion' /

body.text: ityādinā yathā nityatvādikaṃ karaṇaṃ na saṃbhavati, tathā pratipāditam | grahītāpi yathā nāsti, tathā-
body.translated_text: — and so forth: how permanence and so forth are not possible as an instrument has been demonstrated by this. That the grasper too does not exist has been demonstrated by —

body.text: ātmano 'stitvanāstitve na kathaṃcicca sidhyataḥ |
body.translated_text: 'The existence and non-existence of the self are in no way established' /

body.text: ityanena pratipāditam| yacca gṛhyate tadapi nāsti tathā-
body.translated_text: — by this. And that which is grasped also does not exist — by —

body.text: rūpaśabdarasasparśā gandhā dharmāśca kevalāḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Form, sound, taste, touch, smell, and <s>dharmas</s> alone' /

body.text: ityanena pratipāditam | yadā caivaṃ kartṛkaraṇakarmāṇi na siddhāni, tadā kuto nirhetuko grāho bhaviṣyati? tataśca-
body.translated_text: — by this it has been demonstrated. And when agent, instrument, and object are not established, whence would grasping without a cause come about? Therefore —

body.text:
yena gṛhṇāti yo grāho grahītā yacca gṛhyate |
upaśāntāni sarvāṇi
body.translated_text: That by which one grasps, the grasping, the grasper, and that which is grasped — / all are pacified,

body.text: svabhāvena anutpannatvānirvṛtāni sarvāṇītyarthaḥ | yataśca evamevam-
body.translated_text: meaning: all are quiescent because of not having arisen by own-nature. And since this is so —

body.text: tasmād grāho na vidyate ||
body.translated_text: therefore grasping does not exist. //

body.text: athavā | pratyayaparīkṣādibhiḥ prakaraṇairyasmāt sarveṣāmeva karaṇakartṛkarmaṇāṃ sarvathānutpādaḥ pratipāditaḥ, tasmāt sarvāṇyetāni bhāvasvarūpavirahādupaśāntāni | ataśca grāho na vidyate || 15 ||
body.translated_text: Alternatively, since in the chapters on the Examination of Conditions and so forth, the non-arising of all instruments, agents, and objects has been demonstrated in every way, therefore all of these are pacified, being devoid of the own-nature of entities. And hence, grasping does not exist. // 15 //

body.text: atrāha- vidyanta eva viparyayāḥ, viparītasadbhāvāt | iha hi viparyāsānugato devadatto nāma vidyate | na ca vinā viparyāsaiḥ sa viparyāsānugataḥ saṃbhavati | tasmāt santi viparyāsāḥ viparyastasadbhāvāditi | ucyate | iha asmābhiḥ karaṇakartṛkarmaṇāmabhāvāt sarvathā grāha eva nāstīti pratipāditam | tataśca-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: 'Perversions do indeed exist, because of the real existence of the perverted. For a perverted person named <s>Devadatta</s> is known to exist. And without perversions, he who is subject to perversions cannot exist. Therefore, perversions exist, because of the real existence of the perverted.' It is replied: Here, by us, because of the non-existence of instrument, agent, and object, it has been demonstrated that grasping does not exist in any way. And therefore —

children.text: avidyamāne grāhe ca mithyā vā samyageva vā |
children.translated_text: When grasping does not exist, whether false or true, /
whose would there be perversion? Whose would there be non-perversion? // 16 //

body.text: samyagvā mithyā vā kasyacit kiṃcidapyagṛhṇataḥ kuto viparītatvamaviparītatvaṃ veti | tasmānna santi viparyayāḥ || 16 ||
body.translated_text: For one who does not grasp anything whatsoever, whether correctly or falsely, whence would there be the state of being perverted or unperverted? Therefore, perversions do not exist. // 16 //

body.text: api ca | ime viparyayāḥ kasyacidiṣyamāṇāḥ viparītasya parikalpyeran, aviparītasya vā, viparyasyamānasya vā? sarvathā ca nopapadyante iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, these perversions, if posited for someone, would be imagined for the perverted, or for the unperverted, or for one being perverted. And in every case they are not tenable — demonstrating this, he says —

children.translated_text: Perversions do not arise for the perverted; /
perversions do not arise for the unperverted. // 17 //
Perversions do not arise for one being perverted. /
Examine for yourself — for whom do perversions arise? // 18 //

body.text: tatra tāvadviparītasya viparyayā na saṃbhavanti | kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmāt, yo hi viparīta, sa viparīta eva | kiṃ tasya punarapi viparyayasaṃbandhaḥ kuryāt? niṣprayojanatvāt | aviparītasyāpi viparyayā na yujyante, vibuddhabuddhinayanānāmapi ajñānanidrātimiropaśamād buddhānāṃ viparyayaprasaṅgāt ||
body.translated_text: Therein, first, perversions do not arise for the perverted. For what reason? Because one who is perverted is already perverted. What would a further connection with perversion accomplish for him? — since it would be purposeless. Perversions are also not appropriate for the unperverted — because there would be the consequence that perversions [apply] even for <s>Buddhas</s>, whose eye of awakened intelligence has been freed from the darkness of the sleep of ignorance. //

body.text: tathā viparyasyamānasyāpi na santi viparyayāḥ, viparyasyamānasya bhāvasya abhāvāt | ko hi nāma asāvaparaḥ padārthaḥ, yo viparītāviparītavinirmukto viparyasyamāno nāma bhaviṣyati? ardhaviparīto viparyasyamāna iti cet, ardhaviparīto hi nāma yasya kiṃcidviparītaṃ kiṃcidaviparītam | tatra yadasya kiṃcidviparītaṃ tadviparyāso na viparyāsayati, viparyastatvāt | yadapyasya aviparītam, tadapi viparyāso na viparyāsayati, aviparyastatvāt | tasmādviparyasyamānasyāpi kasyacidviparyāsā na saṃbhavanti | yadā caivaṃ viparītāviparītaviparyasyamānā na saṃbhavanti, bhavānidānīṃ vimṛśatu svayaṃ prajñayā madhyasthaḥ san kasya saṃbhavanti viparyāsā iti | tadevamāśrayasyābhāvānna santi viparyayāḥ || 17-18 ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, perversions do not exist even for one being perverted, because a thing that is 'being perverted' does not exist. For what other entity is that, which, free from [being] perverted and [being] unperverted, would be called 'being perverted'? [Objection:] 'The half-perverted is the one being perverted.' [Reply:] The half-perverted is one of whom something is perverted and something unperverted. Therein, that which is perverted in him — perversion does not make that perverted, since it is already perverted. And that which is unperverted in him — perversion does not make that perverted either, since it is unperverted. Therefore, perversions do not arise even for anyone being perverted. And when thus perversions are not possible for the perverted, the unperverted, or one being perverted, let the reader now examine for himself with wisdom, being impartial — for whom do perversions arise? Thus, because of the absence of a basis, perversions do not exist. // 17-18 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat-
body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.translated_text: How can perversions that are unarisen come to exist? /
When perversions are unborn, whence is one subject to perversion? // 19 //

body.text: tatra
body.translated_text: In that regard,

children.text: na svato jāyate bhāvaḥ parato naiva jāyate |
children.translated_text: an entity does not arise from itself, nor does it arise from another. /
Nor from both itself and another — whence, then, is one subject to perversion? // 20 //

body.text: kuto viparīta ityarthaḥ | tataśca yaduktam- santi viparyayāḥ viparyayagatasadbhāvāditi, tanna yuktam || 19-20 ||
body.translated_text: — meaning: whence is one perverted? Therefore, what was stated — 'perversions exist because of the real existence of one subject to perversion' — that is not correct. // 19-20 //

body.text: yasyāpi kathaṃcidviparyāsacatuṣṭayamastyevetyabhyupagamyate, tathāpi tasya viparītatvamaśakyamāsthātum | kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Even for one who somehow accepts that the fourfold group of perversions does indeed exist, nevertheless his perverted state cannot be maintained. For what reason? Because —

children.text: ātmā ca śuci nityaṃna sukhaṃ ca yadi vidyate |
children.translated_text: If self, purity, permanence, and pleasure do exist, /

children.text: ātmā ca śuci nityaṃ ca sukhaṃ ca na viparyayaḥ || 21 ||
children.translated_text: then self, purity, permanence, and pleasure are not perversions. // 21 //

body.text: yadi etāni ātmaśucinityasukhāni viparyāsā iti vyavasthāpyante, kimetāni santi, atha na santi? yadi vidyante, na tarhi viparyāsāḥ, vidyamānatvādanātmādivat || 21 ||
body.translated_text: If these — self, purity, permanence, and pleasure — are established as perversions, are they existent or non-existent? If they exist, then they are not perversions, because they exist — just like non-self and so forth. // 21 //

body.text: atha na vidyante, tadā eṣāmavidyamānatvānna kevalaṃ nāsti viparyāsatvam, viparyāsapratibandhyabhāvādanātmādīnāmapi aviparyāsādīnāṃ nāsti sadbhāva iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: If they do not exist, then, because of their non-existence, not only do they not have the status of perversions, but also — because of the absence of what the perversions are counterparts to — the non-self and so forth too, which are the non-perversions, do not have real existence. Demonstrating this, he says:

children.text: nātmā ca śuci nityaṃ ca sukhaṃ ca yadi vidyate |
children.translated_text: If self, purity, permanence, /

children.text: anātmāśucyanityaṃ ca naiva duḥkhaṃ ca vidyate || 22 ||
children.translated_text: and pleasure do not exist, then non-self, impurity, impermanence, and suffering too do not exist. // 22 //

body.text: yadi ātmā ca śuci nityaṃ ca na vidyate iti manyase, viparyāsāsaṃbhavāt, evaṃ sati ātmādīnāmapyabhāvād yadi etadanātmādikamaviparyāsatvena gṛhītam, tadapi tarhi tyajyatām, pratiṣedhyābhāve pratiṣedhasyābhāvāt | yadā caivamanātmādikaṃ na saṃbhavati, tadā tadapi svarūpato 'vidyamānatvāt ātmādivat kathaṃ na viparyāsaḥ syāt? tasmāt jātijarāmaraṇasaṃsāracārakāgārabandhanānmumukṣubhiraṣṭāvapyete viparyāsāstyājyāḥ || 22 ||
body.translated_text: If you think that self, purity, permanence, and pleasure do not exist — because perversions are impossible — then, when this is the case, since the self and the rest too would be non-existent, if this non-self and the rest has been grasped as non-perversion, then let even that be abandoned, because in the absence of what is to be negated, the negation too is absent. And when non-self and the rest do not exist in this way, then, since they too, like self and the rest, do not exist in their own form, how would they not be perversions? Therefore, for those who desire liberation from the prison of wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s> with its births, old ages, and deaths, all eight of these perversions should be abandoned. // 22 //

body.text: asya ca yathopavarṇitaviparyāsavicārasya avidyādiprahāṇahetutvena mahārthatāṃ pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And demonstrating the great significance of this examination of perversion as described, by showing it to be the cause for the abandonment of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and the rest, he says:

children.translated_text: Thus, <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) ceases through the cessation of perversion. /
When <s>avidyā</s> has ceased, the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) and the rest cease. // 23 //

body.text: yadā ayaṃ yogī yathoditena nyāyena viparyāsān nopalabhate, tadā evaṃ viparyāsānupalambhanena taddhetukā avidyā nirudhyate | tannirodhācca saṃskārādayaḥ avidyāhetukā jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaparyantā dharmā nirudhyante ||
body.translated_text: When this yogin, by the reasoning as stated, does not apprehend perversions, then through this non-apprehension of perversions, <s>avidyā</s> — which is caused by them — ceases. And through its cessation, the <s>saṃskāras</s> and the rest — which are caused by <s>avidyā</s> — the <s>dharmas</s> ending with old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and agitation — cease.

body.text: avidyā hi sakalasyaiva saṃkleśagaṇasya jātyādiduḥkhasya ca hetubhūtā | yathā hi kāyendriyahetukāni sarvāṇi rūpīndriyāṇi kāyendriye nirudhyamāne nirudhyante, evamavidyāhetukāni saṃskārādīni bhavāṅgāni pravartamānāni niyatamavidyāyāṃ niruddhāyāṃ nirudhyante iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: For <s>avidyā</s> is the cause of the entire mass of affliction and of suffering beginning with birth. Just as all material sense-faculties, which are caused by the body-faculty, cease when the body-faculty ceases — even so, the <s>saṃskāras</s> and the other limbs of existence, which are caused by <s>avidyā</s> and which proceed [in the twelve-fold chain], certainly cease when <s>avidyā</s> has ceased. Demonstrating this, he says:

body.text: avidyāyāṃ niruddhāyāṃ saṃskārādyaṃ nirudhyate |iti ||
body.translated_text: When <s>avidyā</s> has ceased, the <s>saṃskāras</s> and the rest cease. //

body.text: atrāha- yadi viparyāsanirodhādavidyā nirudhyate, asti tarhi avidyā yasyā evaṃ viparyāsanirodhānnirodho bhavati | na tarhi avidyamānāyā gaganacūtalatāyāḥ prahāṇopāyānveṣamasti | tasmādvidyate eva avidyā, tannirodhopāyānveṣaṇasadbhāvāt | tataśca santi taddhetukā rāgādayaḥ kleśāḥ | kleśāsadbhāvācca astyeva saṃsāre bhavasaṃtatiḥ | ucyate | atra hi nāma atimahadanarthapāṇḍityaṃ parasya, yo hi nāma sarvātmanā atyantaduḥkhāyāsakleśāsamañjase saṃsāre nirantaraphullaphalapradasaṃkleśaviṣavṛkṣe parārthodayasaṃbaddhakakṣaiḥ sādhubhiḥ prajñopāyamahānilabalairniḥśeṣaṃ tadunmūlyamānairna kevalaṃ na sāhāyyenāvatiṣṭhante, api khalu tadunmūlakānāmatimahānilabalānāmiva bhāvasadbhāvavādamahāśailāyamāna ivātivirodhitayā avasthito bhavān āhopuruṣikayā tasyaiva kleśaviṣavṛkṣasya jātijarāmaraṇaśokāyāsavisaraduḥkhaikaphalasya sutarāṃ bhāvābhiniveśatoyāsravairāropaṇamādriyate ||
body.translated_text: Here one objects: if <s>avidyā</s> ceases through the cessation of perversions, then <s>avidyā</s> does exist — that very <s>avidyā</s> whose cessation occurs through the cessation of perversions. For one does not seek means of abandoning the creeper growing from a sky-cuckoo-tree, which does not exist. Therefore <s>avidyā</s> does indeed exist, because of the existence of the search for the means of its cessation. And from that, the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) such as <s>rāga</s> (passion) and the rest, which are caused by it, exist. And because of the existence of <s>kleśas</s>, the continuum of existence in <s>saṃsāra</s> does indeed exist. The reply is: here indeed is the other's great skill in misfortune! For one who, regarding <s>saṃsāra</s> — which is utterly discordant because of extreme suffering, misery, and affliction, which is a poison-tree of affliction ceaselessly bearing fruit — while good persons, whose interests are bound up with the welfare of others, with the great wind-force of wisdom and skillful means, are thoroughly uprooting it entirely — not only does not stand by assisting, but rather, standing as if a great mountain-obstacle of the doctrine of the real existence of entities against the supremely great wind-force of those who uproot, heroically takes delight in the further irrigation of that very poison-tree of <s>kleśas</s> — whose sole fruit is the outpouring of sufferings of birth, old age, death, sorrow, and misery — with the waters of attachment to existence.
