body.text: api ca | yadi avidyādīnāṃ saṃkleśānāṃ prahāṇaṃ saṃbhavet, syāt tatprahāṇopāyānveṣaṇam | na ca teṣāṃ prahāṇaṃ saṃbhavati | yadi syāt, tadā tattvarūpato vidyamānānāṃ vā syāt, avidyamānānāṃ vā? kiṃ cātaḥ? tatra yadi svarūpataḥ sadbhatānāṃ kleśānāṃ prahāṇamiṣyate, tannopapadyate| kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Moreover, if the abandonment of <s>avidyā</s> and the other afflictions were possible, there would be a search for the means of their abandonment. But their abandonment is not possible. If it were, would it be [the abandonment] of <s>kleśas</s> that are existent in their true form, or of non-existent ones? What follows from this? Therein, if the abandonment of <s>kleśas</s> that are real in their own form is desired, that is not tenable. Why? Because:

children.text: yadi bhūtāḥ svabhāvena kleśāḥ keciddhi kasyacit |
children.translated_text: If the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are real in their own nature for some person, /

children.text: kathaṃ nāma prahīyeran kaḥ svabhāvaṃ prahāsyati || 24 ||
children.translated_text: how indeed could they be abandoned? Who can abandon <s>svabhāva</s> (inherent nature)? // 24 //

body.text: svabhāvato vidyamānānāṃ bhāvānāṃ na śakyaḥ svabhāvo vinivartayitum | na hi kṣityādīnāṃ kaṭhinatvādisvabhāvo nivartate | evaṃ yadi ime kleśāḥ svabhāvataḥ sadbhūtāḥ syuḥ | kecidityavidyādayaḥ | kasyaciditi pudgalasya | kathaṃ nāma prahīyeran? naiva te kasyacit kathaṃcinnāma prahīyeran | kasmātpunaḥ na te prahīyante ityāha- kaḥ svabhāvaṃ prahāsyatīti | svabhāvasya vinivartayitumaśakyatvāt | ākāśānāvaraṇavinivartanāsaṃbhavavadityabhiprāyaḥ || 24 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>svabhāva</s> of entities that exist by <s>svabhāva</s> cannot be made to disappear. For the hardness and the like that is the <s>svabhāva</s> of earth and the rest does not disappear. Thus, if these <s>kleśas</s> were real by <s>svabhāva</s> — 'some' means <s>avidyā</s> and the rest; 'for some person' means for a <s>pudgala</s> (person) — how indeed could they be abandoned? They could in no way be abandoned by anyone whatsoever. Why can they not be abandoned? He says: 'Who can abandon <s>svabhāva</s>?' — because <s>svabhāva</s> cannot be made to disappear, just as the non-obstructive nature of space cannot be caused to disappear. This is the intended meaning. // 24 //

body.text: atha svabhāvena asadbhūtā iti vikalpyate, evamapi prahāṇāsaṃbhava evetyāha-
body.translated_text: If, on the other hand, they are conceived as unreal by <s>svabhāva</s>, even so, the impossibility of abandonment is the same — hence he says:

children.translated_text: If the <s>kleśas</s> are unreal in their own nature for some person, /
how indeed could they be abandoned? Who can abandon what is non-existent? // 25 //

body.text: abhūtā api kleśāḥ svabhāvena avidyamānāḥ aśakyā eva prahātum | na hi agneḥ śaityamasaṃvidyamānaṃ śakyamapākartum | evamime 'pi kleśāḥ kecid yadi kasyacit svabhāvato na vidyante, kastān prahāsyati? naiva kaścit prahāsyati | tadevamubhayapakṣe 'pi prahāṇāsaṃbhavānnāsti prahāṇaṃ kleśānām | prahāṇābhāvācca kutaḥ kleśaprahāṇopāyānveṣaṇamiti | ato yaduktam- vidyanta eva avidyādayaḥ kleśāḥ, tatprahāṇopāyānveṣaṇāditi, tadayuktamiti | yathoktamāryasamādhirāje-
body.translated_text: Even <s>kleśas</s> that are unreal — that do not exist by <s>svabhāva</s> — cannot be abandoned. For the coldness of fire, which does not exist, cannot be removed. Thus, if these <s>kleśas</s> — some — do not exist for some person by <s>svabhāva</s>, who will abandon them? No one will abandon them. Thus, since abandonment is impossible in both cases, the abandonment of <s>kleśas</s> does not exist. And in the absence of abandonment, whence would there be a search for the means of abandoning <s>kleśas</s>? Therefore what was stated — '<s>avidyā</s> and the other <s>kleśas</s> do indeed exist, because of the existence of the search for the means of their abandonment' — that is untenable. As stated in the Noble <s>Samādhirāja</s>:

body.text: yo rajyeta, yatra vā rajyeta, yena vā rajyeta | yo duṣyeta, yatra vā duṣyeta, yena vā duṣyeta | yo muhyeta yatra vā muhyeta, yena vā muhyeta | sa taṃ dharma na samanupaśyati, taṃ dharmaṃ nopalabhate | sa taṃ dharmamasamanupaśyan anupalabhamāno 'rakto 'duṣṭo 'mūḍho 'viparyastacittaḥ samāhita ityucyate | tīrṇaḥ pāraga ityucyate | kṣemaprāpta ityucyate || iti vistaraḥ |
body.translated_text: 'He who would be passionate, or regarding what he would be passionate, or by what he would be passionate; he who would be averse, or regarding what he would be averse, or by what he would be averse; he who would be deluded, or regarding what he would be deluded, or by what he would be deluded — he does not truly see that <s>dharma</s>, he does not apprehend that <s>dharma</s>. He, not truly seeing that <s>dharma</s>, not apprehending it, is called unattached, without aversion, undeluded, of unperverted mind, concentrated. He is called one who has crossed over, one who has reached the far shore. He is called one who has attained safety.' And so forth in detail.

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: ādarśapṛṣṭhe tatha tailapātre nirīkṣate nārimukhaṃ svalaṃkṛtam |
children.translated_text: 'On the surface of a mirror or in a bowl of oil, he gazes at a woman's face, beautifully adorned. /

children.text: so tatra rāgaṃ janayitva bālo pradhāvito kāmi gaveṣamāṇo ||
children.translated_text: Having generated passion for it, the fool, lustful, runs about searching.' //

body.text:
mukhasya saṃkrānti yadā na vidyate bimbe mukhaṃ naiva kadāci labhyate |
mūḍho yathā so janayeta rāgaṃ tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān || ityādi |
body.translated_text:
'When there is no transference of the face, the face is never found in the reflection. /
Just as that fool would generate passion — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like this.' // And so forth.

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: rūpeṇa darśitā bodhī bodhaye rūpa darśitam |
children.translated_text: 'Awakening has been shown by form; form has been shown for the sake of awakening. /
The supreme <s>Dharma</s> has been taught by means of speech that is of a different kind.' //

children.text: śabdena uttaraṃ rūpaṃ gambhīraṃ ca svabhāvataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Speech is supreme [in its capacity to point to] form, yet profound by its own nature. /

children.text: samaṃ rūpaṃ ca bodhiśca nānātvaṃ na sa labhyate ||
children.translated_text: Form and awakening are equal — their duality is not found.' //
'Just as profound <s>nirvāṇa</s> has been illuminated by speech, /

children.text: labhyate na ca nirvāṇaṃ sa ca śabdo na labhyate |
children.translated_text: yet <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not found, and that speech too is not found.' //

children.text: śabdaścāpi nirvāṇaṃ ca ubhayaṃ tanna labhyate |
children.translated_text: 'Speech and <s>nirvāṇa</s> — both are not found. /
Thus, among empty <s>dharmas</s>, <s>nirvāṇa</s> has been illuminated.' //

children.text: nirvāṇaṃ nivṛttireva nirvāṇaṃ ca na labhyate |
children.translated_text: '<s>Nirvāṇa</s> is cessation itself, and <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not found. /
For the non-operation of <s>dharmas</s> is the same afterwards as before.' //
'All <s>dharmas</s> by their own nature are equal, similar to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. /
This is known by those whose essence is renunciation, who are devoted to the awakening of the <s>Buddha</s>.' //

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: jñānena jānāmyahu skandhaśūnyatāṃ jñātvā ca kleśehi na saṃvasāmi |
children.translated_text: 'By knowledge I know the emptiness of the <s>skandhas</s>; and having known, I do not dwell with the <s>kleśas</s>. /

children.text: vyāhāramātreṇa hi vyāharāmi parinirvṛto lokamimaṃ carāmi ||
children.translated_text: By mere expression alone I make utterances — I wander in this world, having attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.' //

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: parinirvṛta loki te śūrā yehi svabhāvata jñātibhi dharmāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Those heroes are <s>parinirvṛta</s> (fully liberated) in the world — those by whom <s>dharmas</s> are known in their own nature. /

children.text: kāmaguṇairhi caranti asaṅgāḥ saṅgu vivarjiya sattva vinenti ||
children.translated_text: They move among sense-pleasures without attachment; having abandoned attachment, they guide beings.' //

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacitāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau viparyāsaparīkṣā nāma trayoviṃśatitamaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus concludes the twenty-third chapter, the Examination of Perversion, in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary composed by the venerable <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Candrakīrti</s>.

body.text:
24
āryasatyaparīkṣā caturviṃśatitamaṃ prakaraṇam |
body.translated_text:
Chapter 24
The Examination of the Noble Truths — the twenty-fourth chapter.

body.text: atrāha-
body.translated_text: Here one objects:

children.text: yadi śūnyamidaṃ sarvamudayo nāsti na vyayaḥ |
children.translated_text: If all this is empty, there is no arising and no destruction. /
It follows for you that the four noble truths are non-existent. // 1 //

body.text: yadi yuktyā nopapadyate iti kṛtvā sarvamidaṃ bāhyamādhyātmikaṃ bhāvajātaṃ śūnyamiti pratipāditam, nanu ca evaṃ sati bahavaśca mahāntaśca doṣā bhavata āpadyante | kathaṃ kṛtvā? yadi sarvamidaṃ śūnyaṃ syāt, tadā yacchūnyaṃ tannāsti, yacca nāsti, tadavidyamānatvād vandhyāputravannaivotpadyate na cāpi nirudhyate, iti na kasyacitpadārthasya udayo vyayaśca | tadabhāvācca caturṇāmāryasatyānāmabhāvaḥ te śūnyavādinaḥ prasajyate | kathaṃ kṛtvā? iha hi pūrvahetujanitāḥ pratītyasamutpannāḥ pañcopādānaskandhāḥ duḥkhaduḥkhatayā vipariṇāmaduḥkhatayā saṃskāraduḥkhatayā ca pratikūlavartitvācca pīḍātmakatvena duḥkhamityucyate | etacca duḥkhamāryā eva viparyāsaprahāṇe sati duḥkhamiti saṃjānate, na anāryāḥ, viparyāsānugatatvāt, yathādarśanaṃ ca padārthasvabhāvavyavasthānāt | yathā hi viparyastendriyāṇāṃ madhurasvabhāvamapi guḍaśarkarādikaṃ tiktatayā upalabhamānānāṃ jvarādirogāturāṇāṃ tiktataiva satyaṃ tajjñānāpekṣayā, mādhuryam, tenātmanā tasya vastuno 'nupalabhyamānatvāt, evamihāpi yadyapi pañcopādānaskandhā duḥkhasvabhāvā bhavanti, tathāpi ye etān duḥkhātmakān paśyanti, teṣāmeva duḥkhaṃ vyavasthāpyate, na viparyāsānugamādanyathopalabhamānānāmiti | ataḥ āryāṇāmeva duḥkhātmatā satyamiti kṛtvā duḥkhamāryasatyamityucyate | nanu ca anāryairduḥkhā vedanā duḥkhamiti paricchidyate iti, evaṃ tatkathaṃ duḥkhamāryāṇāmeva satyam? satyam | na hi duḥkhaiva vedanā kevalaṃ duḥkhasatyam, kiṃ tarhi pañcāpyupādānaskandhāḥ, ityataḥ āryāṇāmeva tat satyamiti kṛtvā āryasatyamiti vyavasthāpyate | yathoktam-
body.translated_text: If all this — external and internal — has been demonstrated to be empty on the grounds that it is not tenable by reasoning, then surely many and great faults befall you. How so? If all this were empty, then what is empty does not exist, and what does not exist, being non-existent like a barren woman's son, neither arises nor ceases. Thus there is neither arising nor destruction of any entity. And because of their non-existence, the non-existence of the four noble truths follows for you, the proponent of emptiness. How so? Here, the five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> (aggregates of clinging), produced by prior causes, dependently arisen, are called suffering — because of being of the nature of the suffering of suffering, the suffering of change, and the suffering of formations, and because of being adverse and of the nature of affliction. And this suffering is recognized as suffering only by the noble ones, when the perversions have been abandoned — not by the ignoble, because they are subject to perversions, and because entities are established as they are seen in their own nature. For just as for those afflicted with fever and other diseases, whose sense-faculties are perverted, even what is sweet by nature, such as jaggery and sugar, is apprehended as bitter — the bitterness alone is true with reference to their knowledge, while the sweetness [is not], since that entity is not apprehended by them in that form — even so here, although the five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> are of the nature of suffering, nevertheless, suffering is established only for those who see them as having the nature of suffering, not for those who apprehend them otherwise due to their being subject to perversions. Therefore, since the nature of suffering is true only for the noble ones, suffering is called a noble truth. But surely painful feeling is discerned as suffering even by the ignoble — how then is suffering true only for the noble ones? True. But not painful feeling alone constitutes the truth of suffering — rather, all five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> do. Therefore, since it is true only for the noble ones, it is established as a noble truth. As stated:

children.text: ūrṇāpakṣma yathaiva hi karatalasaṃsthaṃ na vi(ve?)dyate puṃbhiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Just as a hair from a woolen thread, when placed on the palm, is not felt by people — /

children.text: akṣigataṃ tu tadeva hi janayatyaratiṃ ca pīḍāṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: yet that very same thing, when placed on the eye, generates discomfort and pain.' //

body.text:
karatalasadṛśo bālo na vetti saṃskāraduḥkhatāpakṣma |
akṣisadṛśastu vidvān tenaivodvejate gāḍham || iti |
body.translated_text:
'The fool, like the palm, does not perceive the hair-thread of the suffering of formations. /
But the wise one, like the eye, is deeply distressed by it.' //

body.text: tasmādāryāṇāmeva tadduḥkhasatyamiti duḥkhamāryasatyamiti vyavasthāpyate ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, since it is the truth of suffering only for the noble ones, suffering is established as a noble truth.

body.text: kadā ca tadduḥkhamāryasatyaṃ yujyate? yadā saṃskārāṇāmudayavyayau saṃbhavataḥ | yadā tu śūnyatvānna kiṃcidutpadyate nāpi kiṃcinnirudhyate, tadā nāsti duḥkham ||
body.translated_text: And when is that suffering a noble truth? When the arising and destruction of <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) are possible. But when, because of emptiness, nothing arises and nothing ceases, then suffering does not exist.

body.text: asati ca duḥkhe kutaḥ samudayasatyam? yato hi hetorduḥkham, samudeti samutpadyate sa hetuḥ tṛṣṇākarmakleśalakṣaṇaḥ samudaya ityucyate | yadā tu phalabhūtaṃ duḥkhasatyaṃ nāsti, tadā phalarahitasya hetukatvānupapatteḥ samudayo 'pi nāsti ||
body.translated_text: And when suffering does not exist, whence is the truth of origination? For the cause from which suffering originates — arises — that cause, characterized by <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), <s>karma</s> (action), and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), is called <s>samudaya</s> (origination). But when the truth of suffering, which is the fruit, does not exist, then — since it is untenable for what lacks a fruit to have the status of a cause — <s>samudaya</s> too does not exist.

body.text: duḥkhasya ca vigamaḥ apunarutpādaḥ nirodha ityucyate | yadā tu duḥkhameva nāsti, tadā kasya nirodhaḥ syāditi? ato duḥkhanirodho 'pi na saṃbhavati | asati hi duḥkhe nirodhasatyasyāpyabhāvaḥ | asati ca duḥkhanirodhe kuto duḥkhanirodhagāminī āryāṣṭāṅgamārgānugā pratipad bhaviṣyatīti mārgasatyamapi nāstīti | tadevaṃ śūnyatvaṃ bhāvānāṃ bruvataḥ caturṇāmāryasatyānāmabhāvaḥ prasajyate || 1 ||
body.translated_text: And the removal, the non-re-arising, of suffering is called cessation. But when suffering itself does not exist, whose cessation would there be? Therefore, the cessation of suffering too is not possible. For when suffering does not exist, the truth of cessation also does not exist. And when the cessation of suffering does not exist, whence will there be the practice that follows the noble eightfold path leading to the cessation of suffering? — hence the truth of the path too does not exist. Thus, for one who asserts the emptiness of entities, the non-existence of the four noble truths follows. // 1 //

body.text: tataśca ko doṣa iti? ucyate-
body.translated_text: And from that, what fault [follows]? It is said —

children.text: parijñā ca prahāṇaṃ ca bhāvanā sākṣikarma ca |
children.translated_text: Full knowledge, abandonment, cultivation, and direct realization — /
because of the non-existence of the four noble truths, these are not tenable. // 2 //

body.text: caturṇāmāryasatyānāmabhāvaprasaṅge sati yadetadanityādibhirākārairduḥkhasatyaparijñānaṃ duḥkhasamudayasya ca prahāṇaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminyāśca pratipado bhāvanā duḥkhanirodhasya ca sākṣikarma sākṣātkaraṇam, tannopapadyate || 2 ||
body.translated_text: When the consequence of the non-existence of the four noble truths follows, then the following are not tenable: the full knowledge (<s>parijñā</s>) of the truth of suffering through its aspects such as impermanence and so forth, the abandonment (<s>prahāṇa</s>) of the origin of suffering, the cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) of the practice leading to the cessation of suffering, and the direct realization (<s>sākṣikarma</s>) — the making face-to-face — of the cessation of suffering. // 2 //

body.text: yadi duḥkhādīnāmāryasatyānāmabhāve sati parijñānādikaṃ nāsti, tadā ko doṣa iti? ucyate-
body.translated_text: If, when the noble truths of suffering and so forth do not exist, full knowledge and so forth do not exist — then what fault follows? It is said —

children.translated_text: Because of the non-existence of those, the four noble fruits too are not found. /

children.text: phalābhāve phalasthā no na santi pratipannakāḥ || 3 ||
children.translated_text: In the absence of the fruits, those abiding in the fruits do not exist, nor do the practitioners. // 3 //

children.text: saṃgho nāsti na cetsanti te 'ṣṭau puruṣapudgalāḥ |
children.translated_text: If those eight person-individuals do not exist, the <s>Saṅgha</s> does not exist. /
And because of the non-existence of the noble truths, the True <s>Dharma</s> too is not found. // 4 //

body.text: dharme cāsati saṃghe ca kathaṃ buddho bhaviṣyati |
body.translated_text: And when the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Saṅgha</s> do not exist, how will the <s>Buddha</s> come to be? /

body.text: yadā caivaṃ duḥkhaparijñānādikaṃ nāsti, tadā, asminnasati srotaāpattisakṛdāgāmyanāgāmyarhatphalākhyaṃ phalacatuṣṭayaṃ nopapadyate | kathaṃ kṛtvā? iha kleśānāṃ prahāṇaṃ saṃpiṇḍitaṃ phalākhyaṃ pratilabhate | tadyathā- saṃyojanatrayaprahāṇe sati ṣoḍaśe mārge anvayajñānakṣaṇe yat kleśaprahāṇaṃ tat srotaāpattiphalam | kāmāvacarāṇāṃ bhāvanāprahātavyānāṃ kleśānāmadhimātramadhyamṛdūnāṃ prakārāṇāṃ punaradhimātramadhyamṛduprakārabhedena pratyekaṃ bhidyamānānāṃ nava prakārā bhavanti | tatra kāmāvacaraṣaṣṭhakleśaprakāraparikṣaye vimuktimārge yat prahāṇaṃ tat sakṛdāgāmiphalam | teṣāmeva kāmāvacarāṇāṃ navamaprakārakleśaparikṣaye vimuktimārge yat kleśaprahāṇaṃ tadanāgāmiphalam | rūpārūpyāvacarāṇāṃ kleśānāṃ bhāvanāprahātavyānāṃ bhūmau bhūmau navaprakārabhedabhinnānāṃ yāvannaivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanabhūmikanavamakleśaprakāraparikṣaye vimuktimārge yat prahāṇaṃ tadarhatphalam | ityetāni catvāri phalāni | tānyetāni kathaṃ yujyante? yadi duḥkhasya parijñānaṃ saṃbhavati, samudayasya prahāṇam, nirodhasya sākṣātkaraṇam, āryamārgasya ca bhāvanā bhavati | yadā tu duḥkhādīnāmāryasatyānāmabhāve sati duḥkhaparijñānādikaṃ nāsti, tadā na santi tāni catvāri phalāni | caturṇā ca phalānāmabhāve sati ye teṣu vyavasthitāḥ phalasthāścatvāra āryapudgalāḥ, te na santi | ata eva ca pratipannakā api catvāra āryapudgalā na saṃvidyante ||
body.translated_text: And when the full knowledge of suffering and so forth does not exist thus, then — in the absence of this — the four fruits designated as the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpatti</s>), once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>), non-returning (<s>anāgāmin</s>), and <s>Arhat</s>-ship are not tenable. How so? Here, the abandonment of afflictions, taken collectively, obtains the designation 'fruit.' Namely: when the three fetters have been abandoned, at the sixteenth moment of the path — the moment of consequent knowledge (<s>anvayajñāna</s>) — the abandonment of afflictions is the fruit of stream-entry. Of the afflictions to be abandoned through cultivation belonging to the desire-realm, the gross, medium, and subtle types — when further subdivided into gross, medium, and subtle for each type — become nine types. Therein, at the moment of the liberation-path upon the exhaustion of the sixth type of desire-realm affliction, the abandonment is the fruit of once-returning. At the moment of the liberation-path upon the exhaustion of the ninth type of those very desire-realm afflictions, the abandonment of afflictions is the fruit of non-returning. Of the afflictions to be abandoned through cultivation belonging to the form and formless realms, which are divided into nine types on each level — up to the moment of the liberation-path upon the exhaustion of the ninth type of affliction belonging to the level of neither-perception-nor-non-perception — the abandonment is the fruit of <s>Arhat</s>-ship. These are the four fruits. How are they tenable? [Only] if the full knowledge of suffering, the abandonment of the origin, the direct realization of cessation, and the cultivation of the noble path take place. But when, because of the non-existence of the noble truths of suffering and so forth, the full knowledge of suffering and so forth does not exist, then those four fruits do not exist. And when the four fruits do not exist, the four noble individuals who are established in them — who abide in the fruits — do not exist. And for this very reason, the four noble individuals who are practitioners also do not exist.

body.text: iha hi ṣoḍaśāt mārge 'nvayajñānakṣaṇāt pūrve ye pañcadaśa kṣāntijñānakṣaṇāḥ, tadyathā- traidhātukaduḥkhābhisamaye duḥkhasatyālambanāścatvāraḥ kṣāntijñānakṣaṇāḥ | tatra katame traidhātukaduḥkhābhisamaye catvāraḥ kṣāntijñānakṣaṇāḥ? tadyathā- kāmāvacaraduḥkhadarśanaprahātavyasatkāyāntagrāhamithyādṛṣṭidṛṣṭiparāmarśaśīlavrataparāmarśavicikitsārāgapratighamānāvidyākhyadaśānuśayapratipakṣaḥ anityaduḥkhaśūnyānātmākārotpannaḥ kāmāvacaraduḥkhasatyālambanaḥ ānantaryamārgalakṣaṇaḥ duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntikṣaṇaḥ ekaḥ | tadālambanākāra eva ca vimuktimārgalakṣaṇaḥ duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣaṇaḥ dvitīyaḥ | evaṃ rūpārūpyāvacaraduḥkhasatyālambanaḥ pratighavarjitānantaroktāṣṭādaśānuśayapratipakṣaḥ duḥkhādyākārotpannaḥ ānantaryamārgalakṣaṇaḥ duḥkhe anvayajñānakṣāntikṣaṇastṛtīyaḥ | tadālambanākāra eva ca vimuktimārgalakṣaṇaḥ duḥkhe 'nvayajñānakṣaṇaścaturthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Here, prior to the sixteenth moment of the path — the moment of consequent knowledge — there are fifteen moments of acceptance and knowledge. Namely: in the comprehension of suffering across the three realms, there are four moments of acceptance and knowledge pertaining to the truth of suffering. Therein, what are the four moments of acceptance and knowledge in the comprehension of suffering across the three realms? Namely: (1) the acceptance-moment of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge regarding suffering (<s>duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣānti</s>), which is the antidote to the ten latent afflictions (<s>anuśaya</s>) — the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), extreme views (<s>antagrāha</s>), wrong views (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), clinging to views (<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s>), clinging to rules and vows (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>), doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), passion (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>pratigha</s>), conceit (<s>māna</s>), and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) — that are to be abandoned through seeing the desire-realm truth of suffering, having the desire-realm truth of suffering as its object, arisen through the aspects of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self, having the character of the uninterrupted path — this is the first. (2) The knowledge-moment of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge regarding suffering (<s>duḥkhe dharmajñāna</s>), having the same object and aspect, having the character of the liberation-path — this is the second. (3) Similarly, the acceptance-moment of consequent knowledge regarding suffering (<s>duḥkhe anvayajñānakṣānti</s>), having the truth of suffering in the form and formless realms as its object, being the antidote to the eighteen latent afflictions as just stated minus aversion, arisen through the aspects of suffering and so forth, having the character of the uninterrupted path — this is the third. (4) The knowledge-moment of consequent knowledge regarding suffering (<s>duḥkhe anvayajñāna</s>), having the same object and aspect, having the character of the liberation-path — this is the fourth.

body.text: yathā caite traidhātukāvacaraduḥkhasatyābhisamaye kṣāntijñānakṣaṇāścatvāraḥ, evaṃ kāmāvacarasamudayadarśanaprahātavyamithyādṛṣṭidṛṣṭiparāmarśavicikitsārāgapratighamānāvidyākhyasaptānuśayapratipakṣaḥ hetusamudayaprabhavapratyayākārotpannaḥ kāmāvacarasamudayasatyālambanaḥ ānantaryamārgalakṣaṇaḥ samudaye dharmajñānakṣāntikṣaṇaḥ ekaḥ | tadālambanākāra eva ca vimuktimārgalakṣaṇaḥ samudaye dharmajñānakṣayo dvitīyaḥ | evaṃ rūpārūpyāvacarasamudayasatyālambanaḥ pratighavarjitānantaroktadvādaśānuśayapratipakṣaḥ samudayasatyākārotpannaḥ ānantaryamārgalakṣaṇaḥ samudaye 'nvayajñānakṣāntikṣaṇastṛtīyaḥ | tadālambanākāra eva ca vimuktimārgalakṣaṇaḥ samudaye 'nvayajñānakṣaṇaścaturthaḥ | ityete traidhātukāvacaraduḥkhasamudayasatyābhisamaye catvāraḥ kṣaṇāḥ ||
body.translated_text: And just as these four moments of acceptance and knowledge pertain to the comprehension of the truth of suffering across the three realms, so too: (1) the acceptance-moment of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge regarding the origin (<s>samudaye dharmajñānakṣānti</s>), which is the antidote to the seven latent afflictions — wrong views, clinging to views, doubt, passion, aversion, conceit, and ignorance — that are to be abandoned through seeing the desire-realm truth of the origin, having the desire-realm truth of the origin as its object, arisen through the aspects of cause, origin, production, and condition, having the character of the uninterrupted path — this is the first. (2) The knowledge-moment of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge regarding the origin (<s>samudaye dharmajñāna</s>), having the same object and aspect, having the character of the liberation-path — this is the second. (3) Similarly, the acceptance-moment of consequent knowledge regarding the origin (<s>samudaye anvayajñānakṣānti</s>), having the truth of the origin in the form and formless realms as its object, being the antidote to the twelve latent afflictions as just stated minus aversion, arisen through the aspects of the truth of the origin, having the character of the uninterrupted path — this is the third. (4) The knowledge-moment of consequent knowledge regarding the origin (<s>samudaye anvayajñāna</s>), having the same object and aspect, having the character of the liberation-path — this is the fourth. These are the four moments pertaining to the comprehension of the truths of suffering and the origin across the three realms.

body.text: yathā caite catvāraḥ kṣaṇāḥ traidhātukaduḥkhasamudayasatyābhisamaye, evaṃ kāmāvacaraduḥkhanirodhadarśanaprahātavyasamudayoktasaptānuśayapratipakṣaḥ nirodhaśāntapraṇītaniḥsaraṇākārotpannaḥ kāmāvacaraduḥkha nirodhasatyālambanaḥ ānantaryamārgalakṣaṇaḥ nirodhe dharmajñānakṣāntikṣaṇaḥ ekaḥ | tadālambanākāra eva ca vimuktimārgalakṣaṇaḥ nirodhe dharmajñānakṣaṇaḥ dvitīyaḥ | etaireva ākāraiḥ rūpārūpyāvacaraduḥkhanirodhasatyālambanaḥ pratighavarjitadvādaśānuśayapratipakṣaḥ ānantaryamārgalakṣaṇaḥ nirodhe anvayajñānakṣāntikṣaṇastṛtīyaḥ | tadālambanākāra eva ca vimuktimārgalakṣaṇaḥ nirodhe anvayajñānakṣaṇaścaturthaḥ | ityete traidhātukāvacaraduḥkhanirodhasatyābhisamaye catvāraḥ kṣaṇāḥ ||
body.translated_text: And just as these four moments pertain to the comprehension of the truths of suffering and the origin across the three realms, so too: (1) the acceptance-moment of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge regarding cessation (<s>nirodhe dharmajñānakṣānti</s>), which is the antidote to the seven latent afflictions stated above regarding the origin, that are to be abandoned through seeing the desire-realm truth of cessation, having the desire-realm truth of cessation as its object, arisen through the aspects of cessation, peace, excellence, and escape, having the character of the uninterrupted path — this is the first. (2) The knowledge-moment of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge regarding cessation (<s>nirodhe dharmajñāna</s>), having the same object and aspect, having the character of the liberation-path — this is the second. (3) The acceptance-moment of consequent knowledge regarding cessation (<s>nirodhe anvayajñānakṣānti</s>), having the truth of cessation in the form and formless realms as its object, being the antidote to the twelve latent afflictions minus aversion, with the same aspects, having the character of the uninterrupted path — this is the third. (4) The knowledge-moment of consequent knowledge regarding cessation (<s>nirodhe anvayajñāna</s>), having the same object and aspect, having the character of the liberation-path — this is the fourth. These are the four moments pertaining to the comprehension of the truth of cessation across the three realms.

body.text: evaṃ kāmāvacaraduḥkhanirodhagāmimārgadarśanaprahātavyanirodhoktānuśayeṣu śīlavrataparāmarśamaṣṭamaṃ prakṣipya aṣṭānuśayapratipakṣaḥ mārganyāyapratiopannairyāṇikākārotpannaḥ kāmāvacaraduḥkhanirodhagāmimārgālambanaḥ ānantaryamārgalakṣaṇaḥ mārge dharmajñānakṣāntikṣaṇaḥ ekaḥ | tadālambanākāra eva ca vimuktimārgalakṣaṇaḥ mārge dharmajñānakṣaṇaḥ dvitīyaḥ | etairevākāraiḥ rūpārūpyāvacaraduḥkhanirodhagāmimārgālambanaḥ pratighavarjitacaturdaśānuśayapratipakṣaḥ ānantaryamārgalakṣaṇo mārge 'nvayajñānakṣāntikṣaṇaḥ tṛtīyaḥ | ityete pañcadaśa kṣaṇāḥ darśanamārgābhidhānāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Similarly, (1) the acceptance-moment of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge regarding the path (<s>mārge dharmajñānakṣānti</s>), which is the antidote to the eight latent afflictions — those stated above regarding cessation plus clinging to rules and vows as the eighth — that are to be abandoned through seeing the desire-realm truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering, having the desire-realm truth of the path as its object, arisen through the aspects of path, method, practice, and deliverance, having the character of the uninterrupted path — this is the first. (2) The knowledge-moment of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge regarding the path (<s>mārge dharmajñāna</s>), having the same object and aspect, having the character of the liberation-path — this is the second. (3) The acceptance-moment of consequent knowledge regarding the path (<s>mārge anvayajñānakṣānti</s>), having the truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering in the form and formless realms as its object, being the antidote to the fourteen latent afflictions minus aversion, with the same aspects, having the character of the uninterrupted path — this is the third. These are the fifteen moments designated as the path of seeing.

body.text: evaṃ vyavasthitaḥ āryaḥ srotaāpattiphalasākṣātkriyāyai pratipannakaḥ ityucyate | ṣoḍaśe tu mārge 'nvayajñānasthitaḥ sa srotaāpanna ityucyate ||
body.translated_text: A noble one thus established is said to be a practitioner for the direct realization of the fruit of stream-entry. But one who abides at the sixteenth moment of the path — the moment of consequent knowledge — is called a stream-enterer.

body.text: ta ete aṣṭāśītiranuśayāḥ satyānāṃ darśanamātreṇa bhāvanāmanapekṣyaiva prahīyante iti kṛtvā darśanaprahātavyā ityucyante | yathādṛṣṭasatyākārabhāvanayā tu ye paścātprahīyante te bhāvanāprahātavyāḥ | te ca daśānuśayā bhavanti | kāmāvacarā rāgapratighamānāvidyāḥ | rūpāvacarā eva pratighavarjitāsrayaḥ | ārūpyāvacarāśca trayaḥ ete eveti daśa bhavanti | ete ca yathoktena nyāyena bhūmau bhūmau navadhā bhidyante, kāmadhātau caturṣu dhyāneṣu, caturṣvārūpyeṣu | ekaikasya ca kleśaprakārasya prahāṇārthamānantaryavimuktimārgabhedena dvau dvau jñānakṣaṇau vyavasthāpyete kleśakṣaṇaviparyayeṇa | adhimātrādhimātro hi kleśaprakāraḥ mṛdumṛdubhyāmānantaryavimuktimārgābhyāṃ prahīyate | yāvanmṛdumṛdukleśaprakāro 'dhimātrādhimātrābhyāṃ jñānakṣaṇābhyāṃ prahīyate | sthūlaṃ hi malamalpaprayatnasādhyam, sūkṣmaṃ tu mahāyatnasādhyaṃ rajakavastradhāvanasādharmyeṇeti vijñeyam ||
body.translated_text: These eighty-eight latent afflictions are abandoned through the mere seeing of the truths, without recourse to cultivation — hence they are called 'to be abandoned through seeing.' But those that are subsequently abandoned through the cultivation of the aspects of the truths as already seen are 'to be abandoned through cultivation.' And they are ten latent afflictions: in the desire-realm — passion, aversion, conceit, and ignorance; in the form-realm — the same three minus aversion; and in the formless-realm — the same three. Thus there are ten. And these, by the method stated above, are divided into nine on each level — in the desire-realm, in the four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), and in the four formless [attainments]. And for the abandonment of each type of affliction, two knowledge-moments are established — by the division into uninterrupted path and liberation path — in reverse order to the affliction-moments. For the grossest type of affliction is abandoned by the subtlest uninterrupted and liberation paths. Up to: the subtlest type of affliction is abandoned by the grossest knowledge-moments. For gross impurity is removed with little effort, while subtle impurity requires great effort — this should be understood by analogy with a washerman washing cloth.

body.text: tatra darśanamārgādūrdhvaṃ kāmāvacarabhāvanāprahātavyaṣaṣṭhakleśaprakārapratipakṣavimuktimārgākhyajñānakṣaṇādarvāg jñānakṣaṇāvasthitaḥ āryaḥ sakṛdāgāmiphalapratipannaka ityucyate | sakṛdimaṃ lokamāgatya parinirvāṇāt sakṛdāgāmītyucyate, tatphalārthaṃpratipannakaḥ prayogasthaḥ sakṛdāgāmiphalapratipannaka ityucyate | ṣaṣṭhe tu kṣaṇe sakṛdāgāmītyucyate ||
body.translated_text: Therein, from above the path of seeing, a noble one who abides in the knowledge-moments up to but not including the knowledge-moment designated as the liberation-path that is the antidote to the sixth type of desire-realm affliction to be abandoned through cultivation is called a practitioner for the fruit of once-returning. Because of attaining <s>parinirvāṇa</s> after coming once more to this world, he is called a once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>). A practitioner for that fruit, one who is in the preparatory stage, is called a practitioner for the fruit of once-returning. At the sixth moment, he is called a once-returner.

body.text: ṣaṣṭhāt kṣaṇādūrdhva navamakleśaprakāraprahāṇavimuktimārgakṣaṇādarvāgjñānakṣaṇeṣu vartamānaḥ āryaḥ anāgāmiphalapratipannaka ityucyate | anāgatya imaṃ lokaṃ tatraiva parinirvāṇādanāgāmītyucyate | tatphalārthaṃ pratipannakaḥ prayogasthaḥ anāgāmiphalapratipannaka ityucyate | navame tu kṣaṇe anāgāmītyucyate ||
body.translated_text: From above the sixth moment, a noble one who abides in the knowledge-moments up to but not including the liberation-path moment of the abandonment of the ninth type of affliction is called a practitioner for the fruit of non-returning. Because of attaining <s>parinirvāṇa</s> right there without coming to this world, he is called a non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>). A practitioner for that fruit, one who is in the preparatory stage, is called a practitioner for the fruit of non-returning. At the ninth moment, he is called a non-returner.

body.text: kāmāvacaranavamavimuktimārgakṣaṇādūrdhvaṃ naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñātayanabhūmikanavamakleśaprakāraprahāṇavimuktimārgakṣaṇādarvāgjñānakṣaṇeṣu vartamānaḥ āryaḥ arhatphalapratipannakaḥ ityucyate | sadevamānuṣāsurāllokāt pūjārhatvādarhannityucyate | tatphalārthaṃ pratipannakaḥ prayogasthaḥ arhatphalapratipannakaḥ ityucyate | bhavāgrikanavamakleśaprakāraprahāṇāttu navamavimuktimārge vyavasthitaḥ arhan bhavati ||
body.translated_text: From above the ninth liberation-path moment in the desire-realm, a noble one who abides in the knowledge-moments up to but not including the liberation-path moment of the abandonment of the ninth type of affliction belonging to the level of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is called a practitioner for the fruit of <s>Arhat</s>-ship. Because of being worthy of worship (<s>pūjārhā</s>) from the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>, he is called an <s>Arhat</s>. A practitioner for that fruit, one who is in the preparatory stage, is called a practitioner for the fruit of <s>Arhat</s>-ship. But one who is established at the ninth liberation-path upon the abandonment of the ninth type of affliction belonging to the peak of existence is an <s>Arhat</s>.

body.text: ta ete catvāraḥ pratipannakāḥ pudgalāḥ, catvāraśca phalasthāḥ ityete aṣṭau mahāpuruṣapudgalā bhavanti | paramadakṣiṇārhā uktā bhagavatā | yathoktaṃ sūtre-
body.translated_text: These four person-individuals who are practitioners, and the four who abide in the fruits — these are the eight great person-individuals. They have been declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> to be supremely worthy of offerings. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s> —

children.translated_text: Asked by <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, the ruler — /
'For those who farm and sacrifice, for living beings who desire merit, /
for those who act with faith, always creating merit with a material basis — /

children.text: sukṣetraṃ te pravakṣyāmi yatra dattaṃ mahatphalam ||
children.translated_text: I shall declare to you the good field where what is given yields great fruit.' //

body.text:
pratipannakāścatvāraścatvāraśca phalasthitāḥ |
eṣa saṃgho dakṣiṇīyo vidyācaraṇasaṃpadā || iti |
body.translated_text:
'Four who are practitioners and four who abide in the fruits — /
this <s>Saṅgha</s> is worthy of offerings, through the accomplishment of knowledge and conduct.' //

body.text: yadi catvāri āryasatyāni na santi teṣāṃ ca parijñānāni, tadā satyadarśanabhāvanālabhyānāṃ phalānāmabhāvāt pratipannakaphalasthapudgalānāmabhāva eva | ataśca saṃgho nāsti | tatra
body.translated_text: If the four noble truths do not exist and the full knowledge of them [does not exist], then — because of the non-existence of the fruits that are attainable through seeing and cultivating the truths — there is simply the non-existence of the person-individuals who are practitioners and who abide in the fruits. And consequently, the <s>Saṅgha</s> does not exist. Therein

body.text: adhigamadharmeṇa pratyakṣadharmatayā sarvamārairapi buddhe bhagavati abhedyatvādavetya prasādalābhena saṃghaḥ, sa na syāt | na cet santi te 'ṣṭau puruṣapudgalāḥ ||
body.translated_text: through the <s>dharma</s> of attainment, by the direct presence of <s>dharmatā</s>, since he is unshakeable even by all <s>Māras</s> — the <s>Saṃgha</s>, [obtained] through gaining confidence (<s>prasāda</s>) in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing him [to be such] — that would not exist. And those eight <s>puruṣapudgalas</s> (types of noble persons) would not exist. //

body.text: āryasatyānāṃ ca abhāvāt saddharmo 'pi na saṃbhavati | satāmāryāṇāṃ dharmaḥ saddharmaḥ | tatra nirodhasatyaṃ phaladharmaḥ, mārgasatyaṃ tu phalāvatāradharmaḥ | eṣa tāvadadhigamadharmaḥ | tatsaṃprakāśikā deśanā āgamadharmaḥ | sarva eṣa āryasatyānāmabhāve sati nāstīti-
body.translated_text: And because of the non-existence of the noble truths, the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharma</s>) too would not exist. The <s>Dharma</s> of those who are noble — that is the true <s>Dharma</s>. Therein, the truth of cessation is the <s>Dharma</s> as fruit; and the truth of the path is the <s>Dharma</s> as the means of access to the fruit. This, first, is the <s>Dharma</s> of attainment. The teaching that illuminates that [attainment] is the <s>Dharma</s> of scripture. All of this, when the noble truths are absent, does not exist. Hence —

children.translated_text: And because of the non-existence of the noble truths, the true <s>Dharma</s> is also not found. /

children.text: dharme cāsati saṃghe ca kathaṃ buddhao bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: And when the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Saṃgha</s> do not exist, how will there be a <s>Buddha</s>? //

body.text: yadi hi yathokto dharmaḥ syāt, tadā taddharmapratipattyā sarvākārasarvadharmābhisaṃbodhād buddho bhavatīti yuktaṃ syāt | yadi ca saṃghaḥ syāt, tadā tadupadeśairupacīyamānajñānasaṃbhāraḥ taddānamānaśaraṇagamanādibhiśca upacīyamānapuṇyasaṃbhāraḥ kramād buddho bhavet ||
body.translated_text: For if the <s>Dharma</s> as described were to exist, then it would be appropriate that through the practice of that <s>Dharma</s>, one becomes a <s>Buddha</s> through the complete awakening to all <s>dharmas</s> in all aspects. And if the <s>Saṃgha</s> were to exist, then, with the accumulation of knowledge increased through its instructions and the accumulation of merit increased through giving, honor, going for refuge, and so forth to it, one would gradually become a <s>Buddha</s>. //

body.text: athavā | asati saṃghe srotaāpattiphalapratipannakādīnāmabhāvaḥ syāt | na ca pratipannakāditvamaprāpya buddhatvamāpyate | avaśyaṃ hi pūrvaṃ bhagavatā kasmiṃścit phale vyavasthātavyam | tatra ca phale vyavasthitaḥ saṃghāntaḥpātyeva bhagavān bhavati | saṃghe cāsati niyataṃ nāsti bhagavān buddhaḥ | atha bhagavānapi aśaikṣāntarbhāvāt saṃghāntargata eva | tathā ca buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃghaḥ ityabhidhānāt saṃghāntargata eva bhagavān iti kecidvarṇayanti | teṣāṃ matena spaṣṭamevaitat-
body.translated_text: Alternatively, if the <s>Saṃgha</s> did not exist, there would be the non-existence of those who have entered the path of the fruit of stream-entry and so forth. And without first attaining the status of one who has entered the path and so forth, <s>Buddhahood</s> is not attained. For the <s>Bhagavān</s> must necessarily have been established in some [prior] fruit. And being established in that fruit, the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself falls within the <s>Saṃgha</s>. And when the <s>Saṃgha</s> does not exist, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>, certainly does not exist. Moreover, since the <s>Bhagavān</s>, being included within the non-learners, is within the <s>Saṃgha</s> itself — and as it is stated: 'the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>' — the <s>Bhagavān</s> is indeed within the <s>Saṃgha</s>; so some explain. According to their view, this is plainly evident —

body.text:
dharme cāsati saṃghe ca kathaṃ buddho bhaviṣyati |iti |
madhyoddeśikāśca mahāvastūpadiṣṭabhūmivyavasthayā prathamabhūmisthitaṃ bodhisattvamutpannadarśanamārgaṃ vyācakṣāṇāḥ saṃghāntaḥpātinaṃ vyācakṣate | tadā saṃghe cāsati bodhisattvo 'pi nāstīti kathaṃ buddho bhaviṣyatīti spaṣṭamevaitat | tad-
body.translated_text: 'And when the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Saṃgha</s> do not exist, how will there be a <s>Buddha</s>?' // And the <s>Madhyoddeśikas</s>, explaining a <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the first <s>bhūmi</s> (stage) as one who has generated the path of seeing — according to the arrangement of stages taught in the <s>Mahāvastu</s> — explain him as falling within the <s>Saṃgha</s>. Then, when the <s>Saṃgha</s> does not exist, even the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not exist — how, then, will there be a <s>Buddha</s>? This is plainly evident. Therefore —

body.text: evaṃ trīṇyapi ratnāni bruvāṇaḥ pratibādhase || 5 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, by asserting [emptiness], you contradict all three jewels. // 5 //

body.text: śūnyatāmityevaṃ vadan buddhadharmasaṃghākhyāni trīṇyapi durlabhatvāt kadācideva utpattitaḥ alpapuṇyānāṃ ca tadaprāpteḥ mahārghamūlyatvād ratnāni pratibādhase || 5 ||
body.translated_text: Speaking of emptiness in this way, you contradict the three jewels called <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s> — which are called 'jewels' because of their rarity, arising only occasionally, and because of their unattainability by those of little merit, hence being of great value. // 5 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat-
body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.translated_text: The real existence of emptiness, of fruits, /
of <s>adharma</s> and <s>dharma</s>, and all worldly conventions — you contradict. // 6 //

body.text: śūnyatāṃ bruvāṇa ityanena saṃbandhaḥ | yadi sarvamidaṃ śūnyam, yadā sarvameva nāsti, tadā sarvāntaḥ pātitvāt dharmādharmau saha taddhetukena iṣṭāniṣṭaphalena na saṃbhavataḥ | sarva eva cāmī laukikā vyavahārāḥ- kuru, paca, khāda, tiṣṭha, gaccha, āgaccha ityevamādayo 'pi sarvāntargatatvāt sarvadharmāṇāṃ ca śūnyatvānnaiva yujyante iti | ato nāyaṃ yathopavarṇito nyāyo jyāyāniti || 6 ||
body.translated_text: This connects with 'by asserting emptiness.' If all this is empty — when everything simply does not exist — then, being included within everything, <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, together with their causes, the desired and undesired fruits, are not possible. And all these worldly conventions — 'do,' 'cook,' 'eat,' 'stay,' 'go,' 'come,' and so forth — are also not appropriate, since they are included within everything and all <s>dharmas</s> are empty. Therefore, the reasoning as described is not the better [view]. // 6 //

children.text: atra brūmaḥ śūnyatāyāṃ na tvaṃ vetsi prayojanam |
children.translated_text: To this we say: In [regard to] emptiness, you do not understand its purpose, /

children.text: śūnyatāṃ śūnyatārthaṃ ca tata evaṃ vihanyase || 7 ||
children.translated_text: nor emptiness [itself], nor the meaning of emptiness — therefore you are thus frustrated. // 7 //

body.text: sa bhavān svavikalpanayaiva nāstitvaṃ śūnyatārtha ityevaṃ viparītamadhyāropya "yadi sarvamidaṃ śūnyamudayo nāsti na vyayaḥ" ityādinopālambhaṃ bruvāṇo 'smāsu mahāntaṃ khedamāpanno 'tīva vihanyate vividhairbhūtaiḥ parikalpairhanyate ityarthaḥ | na tvayamasmābhiratra śāstre śūnyatārthaṃ upavarṇito yastvayā parigṛhītaḥ, śūnyatārthaṃ cājānānaḥ śūnyatāmapi na jānāsi | na cāpi śūnyatāyā yatprayojanaṃ tadvijānāsi | tataśca yathāvasthitavastusvarūpāparijñānena etat tvayā bahucāyuktamasmadvayākhyānāsaṃbaddhamevopavarṇitam ||
body.translated_text: You, sir, by your own misapprehension alone, having falsely superimposed the distorted [notion that] non-existence is the meaning of emptiness — and raising objections with 'if all this is empty, there is no arising and no destruction' and so forth — have brought great distress upon yourself and are greatly frustrated, meaning: you are tormented by various imagined entities. But the meaning of emptiness that has been described by us in this treatise is not what you have grasped. And not knowing the meaning of emptiness, you do not know emptiness either. Nor do you understand the purpose of emptiness. And therefore, through your failure to comprehend the true nature of things as they really are, all this that you have described is quite inappropriate and utterly unconnected with our exposition. //

body.text: atha kiṃ punaḥ śūnyatāyāṃ prayojanam? uktameva tadātmaparīkṣāyām-
body.translated_text: Now, what then is the purpose of emptiness? That has already been stated in the Examination of the Self —

children.translated_text: Liberation is from the destruction of <s>karma</s> (action) and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions); <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> are from conceptualization. /
Those [conceptualizations] are from <s>prapañca</s> (conceptual proliferation); and <s>prapañca</s> ceases in emptiness. //

body.text: ato niravaśeṣaprapañcopaśamārthaṃ śūnyatopadiśyate, tasmātsarvaprapañcopaśamaḥ śūnyatāyāṃ prayojanam | bhavāṃstu nāstitvaṃ śūnyatārthaṃ parikalpayan prapañcajālameva saṃvardhayamāno na śūnyatāyāṃ prayojanaṃ vetti ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, emptiness is taught for the purpose of the pacification of all <s>prapañca</s> without remainder; hence the pacification of all <s>prapañca</s> is the purpose of emptiness. But you, imagining non-existence to be the meaning of emptiness, are merely nourishing the net of <s>prapañca</s> and do not understand the purpose of emptiness. //

body.text: atha kā punaḥ śūnyatā? sāpi tatraivoktā |
body.translated_text: Now, what then is emptiness? That too has been stated there [in the Examination of the Self]:

body.text: aparapratyayaṃ śāntaṃ prapañcairaprapañcitam ||
body.translated_text: Not dependent on another, peaceful, not elaborated by <s>prapañca</s>, //

body.text: nirvikalpamanānārthametattatvasya lakṣaṇam || iti |
body.translated_text: free from conceptual construction, without manifold meaning — this is the characteristic of reality (<s>tattva</s>). //

body.text: ataḥ prapañcanivṛttisvabhāvāyāṃ śūnyatāyāṃ kuto nāstitvamiti śūnyatāmapina jānāti bhavān | yaṃ cārthamupādāya śūnyatāśabdaḥ pravartate, tamapīhaiva pratipādayiṣyāmaḥ-
body.translated_text: Therefore, since emptiness is of the nature of the cessation of <s>prapañca</s>, whence is non-existence in it? — thus you do not know emptiness either. And the meaning on account of which the word '<s>śūnyatā</s>' (emptiness) operates — that too we shall demonstrate right here:

children.translated_text: That which is <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) — we declare that to be <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). /
That is a dependent designation; that itself is the middle path. //

children.text: yaḥ pratyayairjāyati sa hyajāto na tasya utpādu svabhāvato 'sti |
children.translated_text: That which arises from conditions — that is indeed unborn; the arising of that does not exist by own-nature. /

children.text: yaḥ pratyayādhīnu sa śūnyu ukto yaḥ śūnyatāṃ jānati so 'pramattaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That which depends on conditions is called empty; one who knows emptiness is heedful. //

body.text: iti bhagavato gāthāvacanāt | evaṃ pratītyasamutpādaśabdasya yo 'rthaḥ, sa eva śūnyatāśabdasyārthaḥ, na punarabhāvaśabdasya yo 'rthaḥ sa śūnyatāśabdasyārthaḥ | abhāvaśabdārthaṃ ca śūnyatārthamityadhyāropya bhavānasmānupālabhate | tasmācchūnyatāśabdārthamapi na jānāti | ajānānaśca tvamevamupālambhaṃ kurvan niyataṃ vihanyase || 7 ||
body.translated_text: — so says the <s>Bhagavān</s> in verse. Thus the meaning of the word '<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>' (dependent origination) is the very meaning of the word '<s>śūnyatā</s>' (emptiness); but the meaning of the word '<s>abhāva</s>' (non-existence) is not the meaning of the word '<s>śūnyatā</s>.' And having falsely superimposed the meaning of the word 'non-existence' as the meaning of emptiness, you reproach us. Therefore, you do not know even the meaning of the word 'emptiness.' And not knowing it, you, by thus raising objections, are certainly frustrated. // 7 //

body.text: kaścāsmākaṃ yathoktamupālambhaṃ karoti? yo bhagavatpravacanopadiṣṭāviparītasatyadvayavibhāgaṃ na jānāti, kevalaṃ granthamātrādhyayanapara eveti | ata ācāryaḥ karuṇayā parasya mithyāpravacanārthāvabodhanirāsārthaṃ bhagavatpravacanopadiṣṭāviparītasatyadvayavyavasthāmeva tāvadadhikṛtyāha-
body.translated_text: And who makes the objections as described against us? One who does not know the non-distorted distinction of the two truths as taught in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching — one who is merely devoted to the study of texts alone. Therefore, the <s>Ācārya</s>, out of compassion, for the purpose of removing the other's wrong understanding of the meaning of the teaching, first takes up the very establishment of the two truths as taught without distortion in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching, and says —

children.translated_text: The <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s> is based on two truths: /
the truth of worldly convention (<s>lokasaṃvṛtisatya</s>) and the truth in the ultimate sense (<s>paramārthasatya</s>). // 8 //

body.text: iha hi bhagavatāṃ buddhānāṃ satyadvayamāśritya dharmadeśanā pravartate | katamatsatyadvayam? lokasaṃvṛtisatyaṃ ca paramārthasatyaṃ ca | tatra
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddhas</s> proceeds based on two truths. What are the two truths? The truth of worldly convention (<s>lokasaṃvṛtisatya</s>) and the ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>). Therein,

body.text: skandhātmā loka ākhyātastatra loko hi niśritaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'The world is declared to be the self of the aggregates; the world indeed depends on them.' /

body.text: iti vacanātpañca skandhānupādāya prajñapyamānaḥ pudgalo loka ityucyate | samantādvaraṇaṃ saṃvṛtiḥ | ajñānaṃ hi samantātsarvapadārthatattvāvacchādanātsaṃvṛtirityucyate | parasparasaṃbhavanaṃ vā saṃvṛtiranyonyasamāśrayeṇetyarthaḥ | athavā saṃvṛtiḥ saṃketo lokavyavahāra ityarthaḥ | sa cābhidhānābhidheyajñānajñeyādilakṣaṇaḥ | loke saṃvṛtirlokasaṃvṛtiḥ | kiṃ punaralokasaṃvṛtirapyasti yata evaṃ viśiṣyate lokasaṃvṛtiriti? yathāvasthitapadārthānuvāda eṣaḥ, nātraiṣā cintāvatarati | athavā | timirakāmalādyupahatendriyaviparītadarśanāvasthānāste 'lokāḥ, teṣāṃ yā saṃvṛtirasāvalokasaṃvṛtiḥ | ato viśiṣyate lokasaṃvṛtiriti | etacca madhyamakāvatāre vistareṇoktaṃ tato veditavyam | lokasaṃvṛtyā satyaṃ lokasaṃvṛtisatyam | sarva evāyamabhidhānābhidheyajñānajñeyādivyavahāro 'śeṣo lokasaṃvṛtisatyamityucyate | na hi paramārthata ete vyavahārāḥ saṃbhavanti | tatra hi-
body.translated_text: — by this statement, the <s>pudgala</s> (person), designated in dependence on the five aggregates, is called 'the world.' <s>Saṃvṛti</s> (convention) is covering on all sides. For <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance) is called <s>saṃvṛti</s> because it covers the reality of all objects on all sides. Or <s>saṃvṛti</s> is mutual origination — meaning, through mutual dependence. Or <s>saṃvṛti</s> means convention, worldly usage — this is the meaning. And that has the characteristics of expression and what is expressed, knowledge and what is known, and so forth. <s>Saṃvṛti</s> in the world is <s>lokasaṃvṛti</s>. [Objection:] Is there also a non-worldly <s>saṃvṛti</s>, that it is thus specified as '<s>lokasaṃvṛti</s>'? [Reply:] This is merely a statement conforming to the actual state of things; the objection does not apply here. Alternatively, those whose senses are impaired by conditions such as cataracts and the like, resulting in a distorted perception — they are the 'non-worldly' (<s>alokas</s>); their <s>saṃvṛti</s> is 'non-worldly convention.' Hence '<s>lokasaṃvṛti</s>' is specified as distinct. And this has been stated in detail in the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s>, from which it should be understood. What is true by worldly convention is <s>lokasaṃvṛtisatya</s>. The entire range of conventional usage — expression and what is expressed, knowledge and what is known, and so forth — without remainder, is called <s>lokasaṃvṛtisatya</s> (conventional truth). For these conventions are not possible in the ultimate sense. For therein —

children.translated_text: 'What is to be expressed has ceased, the domain of thought having ceased. /
For <s>dharmatā</s>, like <s>nirvāṇa</s>, is unarisen and unceased.' //

body.text: iti kṛtvā kutastatra paramārthe vācāṃ pravṛttiḥ kuto vā jñānasya? sa hi paramārtho 'parapratyayaḥ śāntaḥ pratyātmavedya āryāṇāṃ sarvaprapañcātītaḥ | sa nopadiśyate na cāpi jñāyate | uktaṃ hi pūrvam-
body.translated_text: — given this, whence would there be the operation of words in the ultimate, or of knowledge? For the ultimate is not dependent on another, is peaceful, is to be known individually by the noble ones, and transcends all <s>prapañca</s>. It is not taught, nor is it known. For it was stated earlier —

body.text:
aparapratyayaṃ śāntaṃ prapañcairaprapañcitam |
nirvikalpamanānārthametattattvasya lakṣaṇam || iti |
body.translated_text: 'Not dependent on another, peaceful, not elaborated by <s>prapañca</s>, / free from conceptual construction, without manifold meaning — this is the characteristic of reality.' //

body.text: paramaścāsāvarthaśceti paramārthaḥ | tadeva satyaṃ paramārthasatyam | anayośca satyayorvibhāgo vistareṇa madhyamakāvatārādavaseyaḥ | tadetatsatyadvayamāśritya buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ dharmadeśanā pravartate | evaṃ vyavasthite deśanākrame-
body.translated_text: It is the supreme (<s>parama</s>) and it is the meaning (<s>artha</s>) — hence '<s>paramārtha</s>' (the ultimate meaning). That itself as truth is <s>paramārthasatya</s> (ultimate truth). And the distinction between these two truths should be ascertained in detail from the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s>. Based on these two truths, the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, proceeds. When the order of teaching is thus established —

children.translated_text: Those who do not know the distinction between these two truths /

children.text: te tattvaṃ na vijānanti gambhīraṃ buddhaśāsane || 9 ||
children.translated_text: do not know the profound reality in the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching. // 9 //

body.text: atrāha- yadi tarhi paramārtho niṣprapañcasvabhāvaḥ sa evāstu, tatkimanayā aparayā skandhadhātvāyatanāryasatyapratītyasamutpādādideśanayā prayojanamaparamārthayā? atatvaṃ hi parityājyam | yacca parityājyaṃ kiṃ tenopadiṣṭena? ucyate | satyametadevam | kiṃ tu laukikaṃ vyavahāramanabhyupagamya abhidhānābhidheyajñānajñeyādilakṣaṇam, aśakya eva paramārtho deśayitum, adeśitaśca na śakyo 'dhigantum, anadhigamya ca paramārthaṃ na śakyaṃ nirvāṇamadhigantumiti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: 'If the ultimate is of the nature of the cessation of <s>prapañca</s>, let that alone be [taught]. Then what is the purpose of this other teaching of the aggregates, elements, sense-bases, noble truths, dependent origination, and so forth, which is not ultimate? For what is not the truth is to be abandoned. And what is the use of teaching what is to be abandoned?' It is replied: This is indeed true. However, without accepting worldly convention — characterized by expression and what is expressed, knowledge and what is known, and so forth — the ultimate simply cannot be taught. And when not taught, it cannot be realized. And without realizing the ultimate, <s>nirvāṇa</s> cannot be attained. Demonstrating this, he says —

children.translated_text: Without relying on convention, the ultimate is not taught. /
Without arriving at the ultimate, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not attained. // 10 //

body.text: tasmānnirvāṇādhigamopāyatvādavaśyameva yathāvasthitā saṃvṛtirādāvevābhyupeyā bhājanamiva salilārthineti || 10 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, since it is the means for attaining <s>nirvāṇa</s>, conventional [truth] as it really is must necessarily be accepted at the very outset — like a vessel for one who desires water. // 10 //

body.text: tadevaṃ yaḥ saṃvṛtiparamārthalakṣaṇasatyadvayasya vyavasthāmapākṛtya śūnyatāṃ varṇayati, taṃ tathāvidhaṃ pudgalam-
body.translated_text: Thus, one who, having set aside the establishment of the two truths characterized by conventional and ultimate, expounds emptiness — such a person of that kind —

children.translated_text: Emptiness wrongly understood destroys one of weak intelligence, /

children.text: sarpo yathā durgṛhīto vidyā vā duṣprasādhitā || 19 ||
children.translated_text: like a snake wrongly grasped, or a spell wrongly practiced. // 19 //

body.text: saṃvṛtisatyaṃ hi ajñānamātrasamutthāpitaṃ niḥsvabhāvaṃ buddhā tasya paramārthalakṣaṇāṃ śūnyatāṃ pratipadyamāno yogī nāntadvaye patati | kiṃ tadāsīdyadidānīṃ nāstītyevaṃ pūrvaṃ bhāvasvabhāvānupalambhāt paścādapi nāstitāṃ na pratipadyate | pratibimbākārāyāśca lokasaṃvṛterabādhanāt karmakarmaphaladharmādharmādikamapi na bādhate | na cāpi paramārthaṃ bhāvasvabhāvatvena samāropayati | niḥsvabhāvānāmeva padārthānāṃ karmaphalādidarśanāt sasvabhāvanāṃ cādarśanāt ||
body.translated_text: For conventional truth, which is without own-nature, arisen merely from ignorance — when a yogin realizes its ultimate-characterized emptiness — he does not fall into either extreme. [He does not think:] 'What existed before that now does not exist' — because of the non-apprehension of the own-nature of an entity even previously, he does not adopt the position of non-existence even afterward. And because of not undermining worldly convention, which has the nature of a reflection, he does not undermine <s>karma</s>, the fruit of <s>karma</s>, <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, and so forth either. Nor does he superimpose upon the ultimate as being the own-nature of an entity — because of seeing <s>karma</s> and its fruit and so forth only for entities without own-nature, and because of not seeing [them] for entities with own-nature. //

body.text: yastu evaṃ satyadvayavibhāgamapaśyan śūnyatāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ paśyati, sa śūnyatāṃ paśyan mumukṣurnāstitāṃ vā saṃskārāṇāṃ parikalpayed, yadi vā śūnyatāṃ kāṃcidbhāvataḥ satīm, tasyāścāśrayārthaṃ bhāvasvabhāvamapi parikalpayet | ubhayathā cāsya durdṛṣṭā śūnyatā niyataṃ vināśayet | kathaṃ kṛtvā? yadi tāvatsarvamidaṃ śūnyaṃ sarvaṃ nāstīti parikalpayet, tadāsya mithyādṛṣṭirāpadyate | yathoktam-
body.translated_text: But one who, not seeing the distinction of the two truths (<s>satyadvaya</s>), sees the emptiness of conditioned things — he, seeing emptiness and seeking liberation, would either imagine the non-existence of conditioned things, or imagine emptiness as something truly existent, and would also imagine inherent nature of entities as the substratum of that [emptiness]. In both ways, emptiness wrongly apprehended would certainly destroy him. How so? If he were to imagine that all this is empty, that everything does not exist, then a wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) would befall him. As stated:

children.translated_text: This teaching, wrongly apprehended, destroys the unwise person, /
since he sinks into the stain of the view of non-existence. //

body.text: atha sarvāpavādaṃ kartuṃ necchati, tadā niyatamasya śūnyatāyāḥ pratikṣepa āpadyate- kathaṃ hi nāma amī bhāvāḥ sakalasurāsuranaralokairupalabhyamānā api śūnyā bhaviṣyanti? tasmānna niḥsvabhāvārthaḥ śūnyatārthaḥ, ityevaṃ pratikṣipya saddharmavyasanasaṃvartanīyena pāpakena karmaṇā niyatamapāyānvayāt | yathoktamāryaratnāvalyām-
body.translated_text: But if he does not wish to repudiate everything, then a rejection of emptiness necessarily befalls him: 'How indeed could these entities, perceived by the entire world of <s>devas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, and humans, be empty? Therefore the meaning of emptiness is not the meaning of absence of inherent nature.' Having thus rejected [emptiness], because of the evil <s>karma</s> tending toward the ruin of the true <s>Dharma</s>, he would necessarily follow the lower realms of existence. As stated in the noble <s>Ratnāvalī</s>:

body.text:
aparo 'pyasya durjñānānmūrkhaḥ paṇḍitamānikaḥ |
pratikṣepavinaṣṭātmā yātyavīcimadhomukhaḥ || iti |
body.translated_text:
'Another too, a fool with wrong knowledge, a mere pretender to learning,
his self destroyed by rejection, goes headlong to <s>Avīci</s> [hell].' //

body.text: evaṃ tāvadabhāvena gṛhyamāṇā śūnyatā grahītāraṃ vināśayati | athāyaṃ bhāvena śūnyatāṃ parikalpayet, tadāśrayāṇāṃ ca saṃskārāṇāmastitvam, evamapi nirvāṇagāmini mārge vipratipannatvācchūnyatopadeśavihvalo jāyeta | tadevaṃ bhāvarūpeṇāpi śūnyatā gṛhyamāṇā grahītāraṃ vināśayati ||
body.translated_text: Thus, when grasped as non-existence, emptiness destroys the grasper. Now, if he were to imagine emptiness as a [real] entity, and [consequently] the existence of the conditioned things that are its substratum — even so, being on the wrong path with respect to the path leading to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, he would be confused by the teaching of emptiness. Thus, even when grasped as entity, emptiness destroys the grasper. //

body.text: nanu ca yadupakārakaṃ tadanyathā [kriyamāṇamakāloptamiva bījaṃ na phalāya kalpate, kāloptaṃ ca mahate phalalābhāya jāyate, evameva maṇimantrauṣadhādibhi] rgṛhyamāṇaḥ [sarpaḥ] mahāntaṃ dhanaskandhamāvahati śiromaṇigrahaṇāt, tena ca vyālagrāhakāṇāṃ jīvikākalpanāt | yathoddeśatiraskāreṇa
body.translated_text: Now, just as what is beneficial, when used wrongly — [like a seed sown at the wrong time, which does not serve to bear fruit, but sown at the right time yields a great harvest; even so, a serpent] grasped [with the help of] jewels, mantras, and herbs brings a great treasure of wealth through the seizing of its crest-jewel, and by that, the livelihood of snake-charmers is ensured. But

body.text: tu gṛhyamāṇo grahītārameva vināśayati | yathā ca yathopadeśaṃ prasādhitā vidyā sādhakamanugṛhṇāti, upadeśaparibhraṣṭā tu sādhyamānā sādhakameva vināśayati, evamihāpi yathopadeśaṃ śūnyatā mahatī vidyā sādhyamānā gṛhyamāṇā bhāvābhāvādigrāhatiraskāreṇa madhyamayā pratipadā grahītāraṃ parameṇa jātijarāmaraṇādiduḥkhahutāśanaśamanaikarasena nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇajaladharadhārāvarṣamukhena yojayati | yathopadeśaviśeṣavigamena tu gṛhyamāṇā niyataṃ yathoditena nyāyena grahītārameva vināśayati ||
body.translated_text: when grasped in disregard of the proper instruction, it destroys the very grasper. And just as an esoteric knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) practiced according to instruction benefits the practitioner, but when practiced in violation of instruction, it destroys the very practitioner — even so, the great knowledge of emptiness, when practiced and grasped according to instruction, by setting aside the grasping at existence, non-existence, and the like through the Middle Path, connects the grasper with that which has the single taste of quenching the fire of suffering — birth, old age, death, and the rest — namely the shower of rain-clouds of <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder. But when grasped in departure from the specific instruction, it certainly destroys the grasper by the reasoning described above. //

body.text: yataścaivaṃ śūnyatā durgṛhītā grahītāraṃ vināśayati, mandaprajñaiśca aśakyā samyaggrahītum-
body.translated_text: And since emptiness wrongly grasped destroys the grasper, and cannot be rightly grasped by those of dull wisdom —

children.translated_text: therefore the mind of the <s>Muni</s> (<s>Buddha</s>) turned back from teaching /
the <s>Dharma</s>, having considered the difficulty of penetration of this <s>Dharma</s> by the dull-witted. // 12 //

body.text: yasmādayaṃ śūnyatālakṣaṇo dharmo mandamedhasamalpaprajñaṃ sattvaṃ viparyāsagrahaṇādvināśayati, ata eva asya dharmasya mandairduravagāhatāṃ matvā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya sarvasattvadhātuṃ cāvalokya dharmasya cātigāmbhīryam, saddharmaṃ deśayituṃ cittaṃ pratinivṛttaṃ munerbuddhasya bhagavato mahopāyajñānaviśeṣaśālinaḥ | yathoktaṃ sūtre-
body.translated_text: Since this <s>Dharma</s>, characterized by emptiness, destroys a being of dull intellect, of meager wisdom, through the grasping of perversion — for this very reason, having attained unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) and having surveyed the entire realm of beings and the extreme depth of the <s>Dharma</s>, the mind of the <s>Muni</s>, the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>, possessing the special distinction of the great knowledge of skillful means, turned back from teaching the true <s>Dharma</s>. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>:

body.text: atha bhagavato 'cirābhisaṃbuddhasyaitadabhavat- adhigato mayā dharmo gambhīro gambhīrāvabhāso 'tarko 'tarkāvacaraḥ sūkṣmaḥ paṇḍitavijñavedanīyaḥ | sacettamahaṃ pareṣāmārocayeyam, pare ca me na vibhāvayeyuḥ, sa mama vighātaḥ syāt, klamathaḥ syāt, cetaso 'nudayaḥ syāt | yannvahamekākyaraṇye pravivikte dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāramanuprāpto vihareyam | iti vistaraḥ || 12 ||
body.translated_text: 'Then, shortly after attaining awakening, this thought arose in the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "The <s>Dharma</s> I have realized is profound, of profound appearance, beyond reasoning, beyond the scope of reasoning, subtle, to be understood by the wise and learned. If I were to proclaim it to others, and others did not understand me, that would be a hindrance for me, a weariness, a non-arising of [joy in] the mind. What if I were to dwell alone in the forest, in seclusion, abiding in the happiness of the present <s>Dharma</s>."' And so forth in detail. // 12 //

body.text: tadevaṃ satyadvayāviparītavyavasthāmavijñāya-
body.translated_text: Thus, without understanding the correct arrangement of the two truths —

children.translated_text: the objection that you now raise against emptiness — /
that consequence of faults does not apply to us; it does not hold for emptiness. // 13 //

body.text: yo 'yaṃ bhavatā mahān doṣaprasaṅgo 'smāsu prakṣiptaḥ-
body.translated_text: This great consequence of faults that you have hurled at us —

body.text: yadi śūnyamidaṃ sarvamudayo nāsti na vyayaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'If all this is empty, there is no arising and no passing away' /

body.text: ityādinā, sa yasmāt satyadvayavyavasthānabhijñena satā śūnyatāṃ śūnyatārthaṃ śūnyatāprayojanaṃ ca yathāvadabuddhā upakṣiptaḥ, so 'smākaṃ śūnye śūnyatāvāde nopapadyate | yataśca nopapadyate, ato yaṃ bhavān doṣaprasaṅgaṃ śūnyatāyāmudbhāvayan śūnyatāyāmadhilayamadhikṣepaṃ nirākaraṇaṃ pratikṣepaṃ karoti, so 'dhilayo 'smākaṃ nopapadyate | abhāvārthaṃ hi śūnyatārthamadhyāropya prasaṅga udbhāvito bhavatā | na ca vayamabhāvārthaṃ śūnyatārthaṃ vyācakṣmahe, kiṃ tarhi pratītyasamutpādārtham | ityato na yuktametat śūnyatādarśanadūṣaṇam || 13 ||
body.translated_text: — and so forth — since it has been hurled by one who does not comprehend the arrangement of the two truths, who has not understood emptiness, the meaning of emptiness, and the purpose of emptiness as they truly are — that does not hold for us, for our doctrine of emptiness. And since it does not hold, therefore the objection (<s>adhilaya</s>) — the reproach, the rejection, the repudiation — that you raise against emptiness by bringing out the consequence of faults, does not hold for us. For you have raised the consequence by superimposing the meaning of non-existence onto the meaning of emptiness. But we do not explain the meaning of emptiness as the meaning of non-existence; rather, [we explain it] as the meaning of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>). Therefore, this critique of the view of emptiness is not justified. // 13 //

body.text: na ca kevalaṃ yathoktadoṣaprasaṅgo 'smatpakṣe nāvatarati, api khalu sarvameva satyādi vyavasthānaṃ sutarāmupapadyate iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And not only does the stated consequence of faults not apply to our position, but rather all the designations beginning with [the four noble] truths are all the more tenable — demonstrating this, he says:

children.text: sarvaṃ ca yujyate tasya śūnyatā yasya yujyate |
children.translated_text: Everything is tenable for one for whom emptiness is tenable. /

children.text: sarvaṃna yujyate tasya śūnyaṃ yasya na yujyate || 14 ||
children.translated_text: Nothing is tenable for one for whom emptiness is not tenable. // 14 //

body.text: yasya hi sarvabhāvasvabhāvaśūnyateyaṃ yujyate, tasya sarvametad yathopavarṇitaṃ yujyate | kathaṃ kṛtvā? yasmāt pratītyasamutpādaṃ hi vayaṃ śūnyateti vyācakṣmahe-
body.translated_text: For one for whom this emptiness of the inherent nature of all entities is tenable, everything as described above is tenable. How so? Because we explain dependent origination as emptiness —

children.text: yaḥ pratyayairjāyati sa hyajāto na tasya utpādu svabhāvato 'sti |
children.translated_text: 'That which arises from conditions is indeed unarisen; its arising does not exist by own-nature. /

children.text: yaḥ pratyayādhīnu sa śūnya ukto yaḥ śūnyatāṃ jānati so 'pramattaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That which depends on conditions is declared to be empty; one who knows emptiness is heedful.' //

body.text: iti gāthāvacanāt | "śūnyāḥ sarvadharmā niḥsvabhāvayogena" iti prajñāpāramitābhidhānāt ||
body.translated_text: — thus by the authority of the verse. And by the statement of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are empty by the method of being without inherent nature.' //

body.text: tasmādyasyeyaṃ śūnyatā yujyate rocate kṣamate, tasya pratītyasamutpādo yujyate | yasya pratītyasamutpādo yujyate, tasya catvāryāryasatyāni yujyante | kathaṃ kṛtvā? yasmāt pratītyasamutpannaṃ hi duḥkhaṃ bhavati nāpratītyasamutpannam | tacca niḥsvabhāvatvācchūnyam | sati ca duḥkhe duḥkha samudayo duḥkhanirodho duḥkhanirodhagāminī ca pratipad yujyate | tataśca duḥkhaparijñānaṃ samudayaprahāṇaṃ nirodhasākṣātkaraṇaṃ mārgabhāvanā ca yujyate | sati ca duḥkhādisatyaparijñānādike phalāni yujyante | satsu ca phaleṣu phalasthā yujyante | satsu ca phalastheṣu pratipannakā yujyante | satsu ca pratipannakaphalastheṣu saṃgho yujyate | āryasatyānāṃ ca sadbhāve sati saddharmo 'pi yujyate | sati ca saddharme saṃghe ca buddho 'pi yujyate | tataśca trīṇyapi ratnāni yujyante | laukikalokottarāśca padārthāḥ sarve viśeṣādhigamā yujyante | dharmādharmaṃ tatphalaṃ sugatidurgatiḥ laukikāśca sarvasaṃvyavahārā yujyante | tadevam-
body.translated_text: Therefore, for one for whom this emptiness is tenable, acceptable, and satisfying — for him, dependent origination is tenable. For one for whom dependent origination is tenable, the Four Noble Truths (<s>catvāryāryasatyāni</s>) are tenable. How so? Because suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>) is dependently originated, not non-dependently-originated. And it is empty, because of being without inherent nature. When suffering exists, the origination of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the path leading to the cessation of suffering are tenable. And from that, the full knowledge of suffering, the abandonment of origination, the direct realization of cessation, and the cultivation of the path are tenable. And when the full knowledge of suffering and the rest exist, the fruits [of the path] are tenable. When the fruits exist, those abiding in the fruits are tenable. When those abiding in the fruits exist, those on the path are tenable. When those on the path and those abiding in the fruits exist, the <s>Saṃgha</s> is tenable. And when the Noble Truths exist, the true <s>Dharma</s> too is tenable. When the true <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Saṃgha</s> exist, the <s>Buddha</s> too is tenable. And from that, all three jewels (<s>ratnas</s>) are tenable. All worldly and supramundane things, all special attainments, are tenable. <s>Dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, their fruits — the happy and unhappy destinies — and all worldly conventions are tenable. Thus —

body.text: sarvaṃ ca yujyate tasya śūnyatā yasya yujyate |
body.translated_text: Everything is tenable for one for whom emptiness is tenable. /

body.text: yasya sarvabhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā yujyate, tasya sarvametad yathoditaṃ yujyate, saṃpadyate ityarthaḥ | yasya tu śūnyatā yathoditā na yujyate, tasya pratītyasamutpādābhāvāt sarvaṃ na yujyate | yathā ca na yujyate, tathā vistareṇa pratipādayiṣyati || 14 ||
body.translated_text: For one for whom the emptiness of the inherent nature of all entities is tenable, everything as stated is tenable — meaning: it is accomplished. But for one for whom emptiness as stated is not tenable, because of the non-existence of dependent origination, nothing is tenable. And how it is not tenable — that he will demonstrate in detail. // 14 //

body.text: tadevamāsmākīne supariśuddhatare sarvavyavasthāsu aviruddhe vyavasthite, atisthūle atyāsanne tadviruddhe ca svakīye pakṣe doṣavati atimogho yathāvadavasthitau guṇadoṣāvapaśyan-
body.translated_text: Thus, when our position — which is extremely well-purified and free from contradiction with respect to all designations — is established, and when your own position — which is exceedingly gross, exceedingly near [at hand], contradictory to that, and beset with faults — [is also established], you, being utterly reckless, not seeing the merits and faults as they actually stand —

children.translated_text: You, casting the faults that belong to yourself upon us, /
are like one who, having mounted a horse, has forgotten that very horse. // 15 //

body.text: yathā hi kaścid yamevāśvamārūḍhaḥ, tameva vismṛtaḥ san, tadapahāradoṣeṇa parānupālabhate, evameva bhavān pratītyasamutpādalakṣaṇaśūnyatādarśanāśvamārūḍha eva atyantavikṣepāttamanupalambhamāno 'smān parivadati || 15 ||
body.translated_text: Just as someone who has mounted a particular horse, having forgotten that very horse, blames others for the fault of [supposedly] stealing it — even so, you, having mounted the very horse of the view of emptiness characterized by dependent origination, from extreme distraction fail to perceive it, and reproach us. // 15 //

body.text: ke punaste parasya doṣāḥ, yānanupalabhamānaḥ śūnyatāvādinameva upālabhate iti, tān pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: What, then, are those faults of the other [i.e., the opponent], which — while failing to perceive — he reproaches the proponent of emptiness? Demonstrating those, he says:

children.translated_text: If you see entities as existing by their inherent nature, /
then you see entities as being without causes and conditions. // 16 //

body.text: yadi tvaṃ svabhāvena vidyamānān bhāvān paśyasi, tadā svabhāvasya hetupratyayanirapekṣatvāt ahetupratyayān avidyamānahetupratyayān padārthān bāhyādhyātmikabhedabhinnān nirhetukān tvamevaṃ sati paśyasi || 16 ||
body.translated_text: If you see entities as existing by their inherent nature, then — since inherent nature is independent of causes and conditions — you see things, both external and internal in their various divisions, as without causes and conditions, as being without a cause. // 16 //

body.text: sati ca ahetukatvābhyupagame-
body.translated_text: And when the acceptance of causelessness [obtains] —

children.text: kāryaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ caiva kartāraṃ karaṇaṃ kriyām |
children.translated_text: You contradict the effect, the cause, the agent, the instrument, the action, /

children.text: utpādaṃ ca nirodhaṃ ca phalaṃ ca pratibādhase || 17 ||
children.translated_text: the arising, the cessation, and the fruit. // 17 //

body.text: kathaṃ kṛtvā? yadīha ghaṭaḥ svabhāvato 'stīti parikalpayasi, tadā asya svabhāvato vidyamānasya kiṃ mṛdādibhirhetupratyayaiḥ prayojanamiti teṣāmabhāvaḥ syāt | nirhetukaṃ ca kāryaṃ ghaṭākhyaṃ nopapadyate | asati cāsmiṃścakrādikasya karaṇasya, kartuḥ kumbhakārasya ghaṭakaraṇakriyāyāścābhāvā dutpādanirodhayorabhāvaḥ | asatoścotpādanirodhayoḥ kutaḥ phalam? iti sasvabhāvābhyupagame sati sarvametat kāryādikaṃ pratibādhase | tadevaṃ bhavataḥ sasvabhāvābhyupagame sati sarvameva na yujyate || 17 ||
body.translated_text: How so? If you imagine that a pot exists by its own nature, then, for this [pot] that exists by its own nature, what would be the purpose of causes and conditions such as clay and the like? — thus they would be non-existent. And an effect called 'pot' that is without a cause is not tenable. And when this [effect] does not exist, there would be non-existence of the instrument — the wheel and the like, of the agent — the potter, of the action of making the pot, and consequently non-existence of arising and cessation. And when arising and cessation do not exist, whence would the fruit come? Thus, when accepting inherent nature, you contradict all this — the effect and the rest. Thus, when you accept inherent nature, nothing at all is tenable. // 17 //

body.text: asmākaṃ tu bhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatāvādināṃ sarvametadupapadyate | kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmādvayam-
body.translated_text: But for us, who maintain the emptiness of the inherent nature of entities, all this is tenable. For what reason? Because we —

children.translated_text: declare dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) to be emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). /
That [emptiness] is designation in dependence (<s>prajñaptirupādāya</s>); that itself is the Middle Path (<s>madhyamā pratipad</s>). // 18 //

body.text: yo 'yaṃ pratītyasamutpādo hetupratyayānapekṣya aṅkuravijñānādīnāṃ prādurbhāvaḥ, sa svabhāve nānutpādaḥ | yaśca svabhāvenānutpādo bhāvānāṃ sā śūnyatā | yathā bhagavatoktam-
body.translated_text: This dependent origination — the appearance of sprouts, consciousness, and the like in dependence on causes and conditions — that is non-arising by own-nature. And the non-arising of entities by own-nature — that is emptiness. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said:

body.text:
yaḥ pratyatyairjāyati sa hyajāto na tasya utpādu svabhāvato 'sti |
yaḥ pratyayādhīnu sa śūnya ukto yaḥ śūnyatāṃ jānati so 'pramattaḥ || iti |
body.translated_text:
'That which arises from conditions is indeed unarisen; its arising does not exist by own-nature.
