That which depends on conditions is declared to be empty; one who knows emptiness is heedful.' //

body.text: tathā āryalaṅkāvatāre- "svabhāvānutpattiṃ saṃdhāya mahāmate sarvadharmāḥ śūnyā iti mayā deśitāḥ" || iti vistareṇoktam ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the noble <s>Laṅkāvatāra</s>: 'With reference to the non-arising of inherent nature, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, I have taught that all <s>dharmas</s> are empty.' This is stated in detail. //

body.text: dvayardhaśatikāyām- "śūnyāḥ sarvadharmā niḥsvabhāvayogena" || iti ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Dvayardhaśatikā</s> (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>): 'All <s>dharmas</s> are empty by the method of being without inherent nature.' //

body.text: yā ceyaṃ svabhāvaśūnyatā sā prajñaptirupādāya, saiva śūnyatā upādāya prajñaptiriti vyavasthāpyate | cakrādīnyupādāya rathāṅgāni rathaḥ prajñapyate | tasya yā svāṅgānyupādāya prajñaptiḥ, sā
body.translated_text: And this emptiness of inherent nature is designation in dependence (<s>prajñaptirupādāya</s>) — that very emptiness is established as 'dependent designation.' Just as, in dependence on the parts of a chariot — the wheel and the rest — a 'chariot' is designated. Its designation in dependence on its own parts — that

body.text: svabhāvenānutpattiḥ, yā ca svabhāvenānutpattiḥ, sā śūnyatā | saiva svabhāvānutpattilakṣaṇā śūnyatā madhyamā pratipaditi vyavasthāpyate | yasya hi svabhāvenānutpattiḥ, tasya astitvābhāvaḥ, svabhāvena cānutpannasya vigamābhāvānnāstitvābhāva iti | ato bhāvābhāvāntadvayarahitatvāt sarvasvabhāvānutpattilakṣaṇā śūnyatā madhyamā pratipat, madhyamo mārga ityucyate | tadevaṃ pratītyasamutpādasyaivaitā viśeṣa saṃjñāḥ- śūnyatā, upādāya prajñaptiḥ, madhyamā pratipad iti || 18 ||
body.translated_text: non-arising by own-nature — and that which is non-arising by own-nature is emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). That very emptiness, characterized by the non-arising of own-nature, is established as the middle path (<s>madhyamā pratipad</s>). For that which does not arise by own-nature has no existence [by own-nature], and since what has not arisen by own-nature cannot depart, there is no non-existence either. Therefore, because it is free from the duality of existence and non-existence, emptiness characterized by the non-arising of all own-natures is the middle path — it is called the middle way (<s>madhyamo mārga</s>). Thus, these are merely specific designations of dependent origination itself: emptiness, designation in dependence (<s>upādāya prajñapti</s>), and the middle path. // 18 //

body.text: vicāryamāṇaśca sarvathā-
body.translated_text: And when examined in every way —

children.translated_text: There is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that has not arisen in dependence;
therefore there is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that is non-empty. // 19 //

body.text: yo hi apratītyasamutpanno dharmaḥ, sa na saṃvidyate | yathoktaṃ śatake-
body.translated_text: For a <s>dharma</s> that has not arisen in dependence does not exist. As stated in the <s>Śataka</s>:

children.translated_text: Existence independent of dependence does not belong to anything, at any time, anywhere.
Nothing is anywhere at any time permanent — therefore [all is impermanent]. //

body.text:
ākāśādīni kalpyante nityānīti pṛthagjanaiḥ |
laukikenāpi teṣvarthānna paśyanti vicakṣaṇāḥ || iti |
body.translated_text: Space and the like are imagined as permanent by ordinary persons; but the wise do not see real things even in those, even by worldly [standards]. //

body.text: uktaṃ ca bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: And it has been stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

children.text: pratītya dharmānadhigacchate vidū na cāntadṛṣṭīya karoti niśrayam |
children.translated_text: The wise one understands <s>dharmas</s> as dependent; he does not resort to extreme views.

children.text: sahetu sapratyaya dharma jānati ahetu apratyaya nāsti dharmatā ||
children.translated_text: He knows <s>dharmas</s> as having causes and conditions; where there are no causes and conditions, there is no <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of things). //

body.text: evam-
body.translated_text: Thus —

body.text: apratītya samutpanno dharmaḥ kaścinna vidyate |
body.translated_text: There is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that has not arisen in dependence;

body.text: apratīsamutpannaśca śūnyaḥ | tasmādaśūnyo dharmo nāsti | yata etadevam, ato 'smākaṃ sarvadharmāścaśūnyāḥ, na ca paroktadoṣaprasaṅgaḥ || 19 ||
body.translated_text: and what has not arisen in dependence is empty. Therefore no <s>dharma</s> is non-empty. Since this is so, for us all <s>dharmas</s> are empty, and the faults alleged by the opponent do not follow. // 19 //

body.text: bhavatastu sasvabhāvavādinaḥ-
body.translated_text: But for you, the proponent of inherent nature —

body.text: yadyaśūnyamidaṃ sarvamudayo nāsti na vyayaḥ |
body.translated_text: If all this were non-empty, there would be no arising and no passing away;

body.text: tadā niyatamudayavyayayorabhāve sati-
body.translated_text: then, necessarily, when arising and passing away are absent,

body.text: caturṇāmāryasatyānāmabhāvaste prasajyate || 20 ||
body.translated_text: the non-existence of the four noble truths follows for you. // 20 //

body.text: kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmāt-
body.translated_text: For what reason? Because —

children.translated_text: Suffering that has not arisen in dependence — whence would it exist?

children.text: anityamuktaṃ duḥkhaṃ hi tatsvābhāvye na vidyate || 21 ||
children.translated_text: Suffering has been declared to be impermanent — in what has inherent nature, it does not exist. // 21 //

body.text: yaddhi sasvabhāvam, na tatpratītyotpadyate | yacca apratītya samutpannam, na tadanityaṃ bhavati | na hi gaganakusumamavidyamānamanityam | anityaṃ ca duḥkhamuktaṃ bhavagatā- yadanityaṃ tadduḥkhamiti | tathā ca śatakaśāstre-
body.translated_text: For what has inherent nature does not arise in dependence. And what has not arisen in dependence is not impermanent. For a sky-flower, being non-existent, is not impermanent. And suffering has been declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> to be impermanent: 'Whatever is impermanent, that is suffering.' And likewise in the <s>Śatakaśāstra</s>:

body.text:
anityasya dhruvā pīḍā pīḍā yasya na tatsukham |
tasmādanityaṃ yatsarvaṃ duḥkhaṃ taditi jāyate || iti |
body.translated_text: What is impermanent is certainly afflicted; what is afflicted is not pleasant. Therefore, whatever is impermanent — all of that is born as suffering. //

body.text: yacca anityaṃ svābhāvye sasvabhāvatve 'bhyupagamyamāne bhāvānām, tanna vidyata iti || 21 ||
body.translated_text: And impermanence, when the inherent nature of entities is accepted as having own-nature, does not exist. // 21 //

body.text: evaṃ tāvat sasvabhāvatve sati bhāvānāṃ duḥkhaṃ na yujyate | na ca kevalaṃ duḥkhameva na yujyate, sati sasvabhāvābhyupagame samudayo 'pi na yujyate iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Thus, when entities have inherent nature, suffering is not tenable. And not only is suffering alone not tenable — when the acceptance of inherent nature obtains, the origin (<s>samudaya</s>) too is not tenable. Demonstrating this, he says:

body.text: svabhāvato vidyamānaṃ kiṃ punaḥ samudeṣyate |

children.translated_text: Therefore the origin does not exist for one who opposes emptiness. // 22 //

body.translated_text: What exists by its own nature — how could it arise again?

body.text: iha samudetyasmādduḥkhamiti duḥkhasya hetu [taḥ] samudaya ityucyate | tadasya duḥkhasya śūnyatāṃ pratibādhamānasya sasvabhāvaṃ duḥkhamabhyupagacchataḥ tasya punarutpādavaiyarthyāt taddhetukalpanāvaiyarthyameva, ityevaṃ śūnyatāṃ pratibādhamānasya samudayo 'pi bhavato na yujyate || 22 ||
body.translated_text: Here, 'origin' (<s>samudaya</s>) is called [so] because suffering arises from it — it is the cause of suffering. For one who opposes emptiness and accepts suffering as having inherent nature, since the re-arising [of what already exists] would be purposeless, the imagining of its cause too is purposeless. Thus, for one who opposes emptiness, the origin too is not tenable for you. // 22 //

body.text: svābhāvikameva duḥkhamabhyupagacchato duḥkhanirodho 'pi na yujyate iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Demonstrating that for one who accepts suffering as having inherent nature, the cessation of suffering (<s>duḥkhanirodha</s>) too is not tenable, he says:

children.text: na nirodhaḥ svabhāvena sato duḥkhasya vidyate |
children.translated_text: The cessation of suffering that exists by its own nature is not possible.
Because of your being fixed in inherent nature, you oppose cessation. // 23 //

body.text: yadi hi svabhāvato duḥkhaṃ syāt, tadā svabhāvasyānapāyitvāt kuto 'sya nirodhatvamiti? evaṃ svabhāvaparyavasthānāt svabhāvaṃ gṛhītvā pratyavatiṣṭhamāno duḥkhanirodhamapi pratibādhase || 23 ||
body.translated_text: For if suffering were to exist by its own nature, then, since own-nature cannot depart, how could there be its cessation? Thus, being fixed in inherent nature — having grasped inherent nature and persisting [in that view] — you oppose even the cessation of suffering. // 23 //

body.text: idānīmāryamārgo 'pi sasvabhāvavādino yathā nopapadyate tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, demonstrating how the noble path (<s>āryamārga</s>) too is not tenable for the proponent of inherent nature, he says:

children.translated_text: When there is inherent nature, the cultivation of the path is not tenable;

children.text: athāsau bhāvyate mārgaḥ svābhāvyaṃ te na vidyate || 24 ||
children.translated_text: but if that path is cultivated, then your [thesis of] inherent nature does not obtain. // 24 //

body.text: yadi hi sasvabhāvā bhāvā bhaveyuḥ, tadā mārgo 'pi sasvabhāva eveti kṛtvā abhāvita evāsāvasti | tasya kiṃ punarbhāvanayeti? evam-
body.translated_text: For if entities had inherent nature, then the path too would have inherent nature, and thus it would already be [established] without being cultivated. What would be the purpose of further cultivating it? Thus —

body.text: svābhāvye sati mārgasya bhāvanā nopapadyate |
body.translated_text: when there is inherent nature, the cultivation of the path is not tenable.

body.text: atha asya mārgasya bhāvanā abhyupagamyate bhavatā, evaṃ tarhi svabhāvatā āryamārgasya na syāt, kāryatvādityabhiprāyaḥ || 24 ||
body.translated_text: But if the cultivation of this path is accepted by you, then the inherent nature of the noble path would not exist, since it would be an effect — this is the intended meaning. // 24 //

body.text: api ca- duḥkhasya nirodhaprāptyarthaṃ samudayasya ca prahāṇārthaṃ bhāvanā mārgasyeṣyate | pūrvoktena tu nyāyena sasvabhāvavādino bhavataḥ-
body.translated_text: Moreover — the cultivation of the path is accepted for the purpose of attaining the cessation of suffering and for the purpose of abandoning the origin. But by the reasoning stated above, for you, the proponent of inherent nature —

children.text: yadā duḥkhaṃ samudayo nirodhaśca na vidyate |
children.translated_text: When suffering, the origin, and cessation do not exist,
which path will lead to the cessation of suffering? // 25 //

body.text: nāstyeva asau duḥkhanirodhaḥ, yannirodhānmārgo bhāvitaḥ san prāpayiṣyati | tasmādāryamārgo 'pyevaṃ nopapadyata iti | evaṃ sasvabhāvavādinaḥ caturṇāmāryasatyānāmabhāvaḥ prāpnoti || 25 ||
body.translated_text: That cessation of suffering simply does not exist, attaining which the path, when cultivated, would lead to. Therefore the noble path too is thus not tenable. In this way, for the proponent of inherent nature, the non-existence of the four noble truths follows. // 25 //

body.text: idānīṃ duḥkhādiparijñānādikamapi yathā parasya na saṃbhavati, tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, demonstrating how even the full knowledge (<s>parijñāna</s>) of suffering and so forth is not possible for the opponent, he says:

children.translated_text: If that [suffering] is not fully known by its own nature, how then
can there be full knowledge of it? Is not own-nature firmly established? // 26 //

body.text: yadi pūrvaṃ duḥkhamaparijñātasvabhāvaṃ tat paścāt parijñāyata iti kalpyate, tadayuktam | kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmānnanu kila svabhāvaḥ samavasthitaḥ | yo hi svabhāvaḥ, sa kila loke samavasthitaḥ, naivānyathātvamāpadyate, vahnerauṣṇyavat | yadā ca svabhāvasyānyathātvaṃ nāsti, tadā pūrvamaparijñātasvabhāvasya duḥkhasya paścādapi parijñānaṃ nopapadyata iti | ato duḥkhaparijñānamapi na saṃbhavati || 26 ||
body.translated_text: If it is imagined that suffering, whose nature was previously not-fully-known, is subsequently fully known — that is not proper. For what reason? Because own-nature is surely firmly established. For own-nature is surely established in the world and does not undergo change — like the heat of fire. And when there is no change of own-nature, then the full knowledge of suffering that was previously of not-fully-known nature is not tenable subsequently either. Therefore, even the full knowledge of suffering is not possible. // 26 //

body.text: yadā caitadduḥkhaparijñānamapi na saṃbhavati, tadā-
body.translated_text: And when this full knowledge of suffering too is not possible, then —

children.translated_text: Abandonment, direct realization, and cultivation too — for you, just like
full knowledge, are not tenable, and nor are the four fruits. // 27 //

body.text: yadetat samudayasya prahāṇaṃ nirodhasya ca sākṣātkaraṇam, te ete dve prahāṇasākṣātkaraṇe yā ca mārgasya bhāvanā, eṣāpi | evameva te duḥkhaparijñānāsaṃbhavānna yujyante | samudayasya svabhāvenāprahīṇasya svabhāvasyānapāyitvāt paścādapi prahāṇaṃ nopapadyate | evaṃ bhāvanāsākṣātkaraṇe 'pi yojyam | na ca kevalaṃ parijñānādikameva na saṃbhavati sasvabhāvavāde, api ca-
body.translated_text: The abandonment of the origin and the direct realization of cessation — these two, abandonment and direct realization, and also the cultivation of the path — these too, just like the full knowledge of suffering, are not tenable for you, because of the impossibility of the full knowledge of suffering. The abandonment of the origin that has not been abandoned by own-nature is not tenable subsequently either, since own-nature cannot depart. The same should be applied to cultivation and direct realization. And it is not only full knowledge and the rest that are not possible in the doctrine of inherent nature; moreover —

body.text: parijñāvanna yujyante catvāryapi phalāni ca |
body.translated_text: just as full knowledge [is not tenable], so too the four fruits are not tenable.

body.text: yathā svabhāvenāparijñātasya duḥkhasya parijñānaṃ na yuktam, evaṃ svabhāvenāvidyamānasya pūrvaṃ srotaāpattiphalasya paścādastitvaṃ na saṃbhavati | yathā srotaāpattiphalasya, evaṃ sakṛdāgāmyanāgāmyarhatphalānāmabhāvo veditavyaḥ || 27 ||
body.translated_text: Just as the full knowledge of suffering that is not fully known by own-nature is not proper, so too the subsequent existence of the fruit of stream-entry that did not previously exist by own-nature is not possible. Just as with the fruit of stream-entry, so the non-existence of the fruits of once-returning, non-returning, and <s>Arhatship</s> should be understood. // 27 //

body.text: na ca kevalametāni phalāni parijñāvanna yujyante, kiṃ tarhi adhigamo 'pyeṣāṃ na yujyata iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And not only are these fruits not tenable like full knowledge — their attainment too is not tenable. Demonstrating this, he says:

children.translated_text: A fruit that is not attained by own-nature — how could that
be attainable, for one who grasps inherent nature? // 28 //

body.text: svabhāvasyāvijahanaprakṛtikatvādbhāvasvabhāvavādamabhyupagacchataḥ pūrvamanadhigatasvabhāvānāṃ paścādapyadhigamo nopapadyate || 28 ||
body.translated_text: Since the nature of own-nature is to not depart, for one who accepts the doctrine of the own-nature of entities, the subsequent attainment of those [fruits] not previously attained by own-nature is not tenable. // 28 //

children.translated_text: And from that —

children.text: phalābhāve phalasthā no na santi pratipannakāḥ |
children.translated_text: In the absence of fruits, those established in the fruit do not exist, nor do the aspirants.

children.text: saṃgho nāsti na cetsanti te 'ṣṭau puruṣapudgalāḥ || 29 ||
children.translated_text: If those eight types of persons do not exist, the <s>Saṅgha</s> does not exist. // 29 //
And because of the non-existence of the noble truths, the true <s>Dharma</s> too does not exist.

children.text: dharme cāsati saṃghe ca kathaṃ buddho bhaviṣyati || 30 ||
children.translated_text: And when the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Saṅgha</s> do not exist, how will there be a <s>Buddha</s>? // 30 //

body.text: anayośca ślokayoḥ pūrvavadevārtho veditavyaḥ || 29-30 ||
body.translated_text: And the meaning of these two verses should be understood as before. // 29-30 //

body.text: api ca- sasvabhāvābhyupagame sati-
body.translated_text: Moreover, when inherent nature is accepted —

children.text: apratītyāpi bodhiṃ ca tava buddhaḥ prasajyate |
children.translated_text: Your <s>Buddha</s> would follow as being independent of <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening);

children.text: apratītyāpi buddhaṃ ca tava bodhiḥ prasajyate || 31 ||
children.translated_text: and your <s>Bodhi</s> would follow as being independent of the <s>Buddha</s>. // 31 //

body.text: yadi hi svabhāvato buddho nāma kaścid bhāvaḥ syāt, sa bodhiṃ sarvajñajñānamapratītyāpi anapekṣyāpi syāt |
body.translated_text: For if the <s>Buddha</s> were some entity existing by own-nature, he would exist even independently of, even without regard to, <s>Bodhi</s> — the knowledge of all things —

body.text: akṛtrimaḥ svabhāvo hi nirapekṣaḥ paratra ca |
body.translated_text: for own-nature is uncreated and independent of anything else. //

body.text: iti vacanāt | tathā vināpi buddhena bodhiḥ syāt, anapekṣyāpi buddhaṃ nirāśrayā bodhiḥ syāt || 31 ||
body.translated_text: — because of this statement. Likewise, even without a <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Bodhi</s> would exist; even independently of a <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Bodhi</s> would exist without a basis. // 31 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat-
body.translated_text: What is more —

children.translated_text: One who is a non-<s>Buddha</s> by own-nature, even striving for awakening,
will not attain <s>Bodhi</s> through the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice. // 32 //

body.text: iha hi buddhatvātpūrvamabuddhasvabhāvasya sataḥ pudgalasya satyāmapi bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ bodhyarthaṃ ghaṭamānasyāpi naiva bodhiḥ syāt, abuddhasvabhāvasya vyāvartayitumaśakyatvāt || 32 ||
body.translated_text: For here, a person who prior to <s>Buddhahood</s> exists with the own-nature of a non-<s>Buddha</s>, even when there is <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice, even when striving for awakening — there would simply be no <s>Bodhi</s>, since the own-nature of a non-<s>Buddha</s> cannot be reversed. // 32 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat-
body.translated_text: What is more —

children.text: na ca dharmamadharmaṃ vā kaścijjātu kariṣyati |
children.translated_text: No one whatsoever will ever perform <s>dharma</s> or <s>adharma</s>.

children.text: kimaśūnyasya kartavyaṃ svabhāvaḥ kriyate na hi || 33 ||
children.translated_text: What is to be done by the non-empty? For own-nature is not something that is made. // 33 //

body.text: sati hi svabhāvavādābhyupagame dharmādharmayoḥ karaṇaṃ nopapadyate | kiṃ hi aśūnyasya kartavyam? na hi svabhāvasyāśūnyasya kāraṇamupapadyate vidyamānatvāt || 33 ||
body.translated_text: For when the acceptance of the doctrine of inherent nature obtains, the performance of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> is not tenable. For what is to be done by that which is non-empty? For own-nature, which is non-empty, has no cause, since it already exists. // 33 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat-
body.translated_text: What is more —

children.text: vinā dharmamadharmaṃ ca phalaṃ hi tava vidyate |
children.translated_text: For you, the fruit exists independently of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>;

children.text: dharmādharmanimittaṃ ca phalaṃ tava na vidyate || 34 ||
children.translated_text: and the fruit arising from <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> does not exist for you. // 34 //

body.text: yadetaddharmādharmanimittakamiṣṭāniṣṭaphalam, yadi tat svabhāvato 'sti, tad vināpi dharmādharmābhyāṃ syāt | yadā ca vinā dharmādharmaṃ phalaṃ tavāsti, tadā dharmādharmajaṃ phalaṃ tava na saṃbhavati | dharmādharmopārjanavaiyarthyaṃ syāt,
body.translated_text: This desirable and undesirable fruit that is caused by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — if it exists by own-nature, it would exist even without <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. And when the fruit exists for you independently of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, then a fruit born of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> is not possible for you. The earning of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> would be purposeless.

body.text: dharmādharmanimittaṃ ca phalaṃ tava na vidyate | iti |
body.translated_text: And the fruit arising from <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> does not exist for you.

body.text: atha dharmādharmanimittakaṃ phalaṃ bhavatīti parikalpyate, na tarhi tatphalamaśūnyamiti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: But if it is imagined that a fruit arising from <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> does exist — then, demonstrating that that fruit is not non-empty, he says:

children.text: dharmādharmanimittaṃ vā yadi te vidyate phalam |
children.translated_text: But if for you the fruit arising from <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> does exist,
how can the fruit arisen from <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> be non-empty for you? // 35 //

body.text: śūnyamevaitat, pratītyasamutpannatvāt, pratibimbavat, ityabhiprāyaḥ || 35 ||
body.translated_text: It is empty indeed, because of being dependently arisen — like a reflection. This is the intended meaning. // 35 //

body.text: api ca | sarva eva hyete 'gaccha, kuru, paca, paṭha, tiṣṭha'; ityevamādayo laukikā vyavahārāḥ pratītyasamutpannāḥ | tān yadi sasvabhāvānicchati bhavān, tadā bhavatā pratītyasamutpādo bādhito bhavati |tadbādhanācca sarva eva laukikā vyavahārā bādhitā bhavantīti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, all these worldly conventions such as 'Go!' 'Do!' 'Cook!' 'Read!' 'Stand!' — all such worldly transactions are dependently arisen. If you consider them as having inherent nature, then you would be obstructing dependent origination. And from obstructing that, all worldly transactions would be obstructed. Demonstrating this, he says:

children.translated_text: You obstruct all worldly conventions
when you obstruct the emptiness that is dependent origination. // 36 //

body.text: yacchabdaḥ kriyāviśeṣaṇam | yadbādhase ityanena saṃbadhyate || 36 ||
body.translated_text: The particle 'yat' qualifies the action. It connects with 'you obstruct.' // 36 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat-
body.translated_text: What is more —

children.translated_text: Nothing would be to be done; action would be uninitiated;
the agent would be non-acting — for one who opposes emptiness. // 37 //

body.text: yadi hi svarūpaśūnyāḥ padārthā na bhaveyuḥ, sasvabhāvā eva bhaveyuḥ, tadā svabhāvasya vidyamānatvānna kenacit kasyacit kiṃcit kartavyaṃ syāt | na hi nabhaso 'nāvaraṇatvaṃ kenacit kriyate | akriyamāṇā ca kriyā syāt | kriyāṃ cākurvāṇasya kārakatvaṃ syāt | na caitadevamiti | tasmānnāśūnyāḥ padārthāḥ || 37 ||
body.translated_text: For if entities were not empty of own-form, if they were possessed of intrinsic nature, then, since intrinsic nature would be present, nothing would need to be done by anyone to anything. For the unobstructed nature of space is not produced by anyone. And there would be action without performing. And there would be agency for one who does not perform any action. But this is not the case. Therefore, entities are not non-empty. // 37 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat-
body.translated_text: And what else —

children.translated_text: It would be unborn, undestroyed, and immutable; /
the world would be devoid of diverse states — for those who deny emptiness of own-nature. // 38 //

body.text: vicitrābhiravasthāmiḥ svabhāvaracitaṃ svabhāvenaiva racitamapratītyasamutpannaṃ jagat svabhāvaśūnyavādinām |
body.translated_text: The world would be devoid of diverse states, fabricated by own-nature, fabricated by own-nature alone, not dependently arisen — for those who deny emptiness of own-nature.

body.text: svabhāvenaiva yadi bhāvāḥ [sasvabhāvāḥ] syuḥ, tadā svabhāvasyākṛtrimatvādavyāvartanatvācca sarvamidaṃ jagadajātamaniruddhaṃ ca syāt | ajātāniruddhatvājjagat kūṭasthaṃ syāt | hetupratyayānapekṣaṃ vicitrābhiravasthābhī rahitamapratītyasamutpannaṃ jagadaśūnyavādināṃ syāt | yathoktaṃ pitāputrasamāgame-
body.translated_text: If entities existed with own-nature, then, since own-nature is unfabricated and unalterable, all this world would be unborn and undestroyed. And being unborn and undestroyed, the world would be immutable. Not depending on causes and conditions, the world would be devoid of diverse states, not dependently arisen — for those who deny emptiness. As stated in the <s>Pitāputrasamāgama</s> —

body.text: syādyadi kiṃcidaśūnyaṃ na vadejjinu tasya vyākaraṇam |
body.translated_text: 'If anything were non-empty, the <s>Jina</s> (conqueror) would not declare its explanation. /

body.text: tathāhi sthitaṃ tat svake svake bhāve |
body.translated_text: For such it would remain in its own respective state, /

body.text: kūṭasthamavikāraṃ na tasya vṛddhirna parihāṇiḥ || iti ||
body.translated_text: immutable and unchanging — there would be no increase or decrease for it.' //

body.text: tathā āryahastikakṣyasūtre-
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the noble <s>Hastikakṣyasūtra</s> —

body.text:
yadi koci dharmāṇa bhavetsvabhāvaḥ tatraiva gaccheya jinaḥ saśrāvakaḥ |
kūṭasthadharmāṇa siyā na nirvṛtī na niṣprapañco bhavi jātu paṇḍitaḥ || iti || 38 ||
body.translated_text:
'If <s>dharmas</s> had any intrinsic nature, the <s>Jina</s> together with his <s>Śrāvakas</s> would go there. /
For <s>dharmas</s> that are immutable, there would be no <s>nirvāṇa</s>, nor would a wise one ever be free from conceptual proliferation.' // 38 //

body.text: na ca kevalaṃ sasvabhāvavādābhyupagame laukikā eva vyavahārā nopapadyante, api ca lokottarā eva [api?] nopapadyante iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And it is not only that, when the doctrine of inherent nature is accepted, worldly conventions alone are untenable; moreover, even supramundane [conventions] are untenable — demonstrating this, he says —

children.translated_text: The attainment of what has not been attained, and the action that makes an end of suffering, /
and the abandonment of all afflictions — if non-empty, these would not exist. // 39 //

body.text: yadi hi aśūnyaṃ sasvabhāvaṃ sarvametat syāt, tadā yadasaṃprāptaṃ tadasaṃprāptameva, iti asaṃprāptasya ca phalasya prāptirna syāt | tadā duḥkhaparyantakāraṇaṃ ca pūrvaṃ nābhūditi sāṃpratamapi na syāt | sarveṣāṃ ca kleśānāṃ pūrvaṃ prahāṇaṃ nābhūditi paścādapi prahāṇaṃ na syāt || 39 ||
body.translated_text: For if all this were non-empty, possessed of intrinsic nature, then what has not been attained would remain not attained — thus the attainment of fruit that has not been attained would not exist. Then the making-an-end-of-suffering too would not exist, since it did not previously exist. And the abandonment of all afflictions too — since it did not exist previously — would not exist subsequently either. // 39 //

body.text: tadevaṃ yasmāt sasvabhāvavādābhyupagame sati sarvametanna yujyate, ataḥ-
body.translated_text: Thus, since all of this is untenable when the doctrine of inherent nature is accepted, therefore —

children.translated_text: One who sees dependent origination sees this — /

children.text: duḥkhaṃ samudayaṃ caiva nirodhaṃ mārgameva ca || 40 ||
children.translated_text: suffering and its origin, and cessation and the path as well. // 40 //

body.text: yo hi sarvadharmapratītyasamutpādalakṣaṇāṃ svabhāvaśūnyatāṃ samyak paśyati, sa catvāri āryasatyāni paśyati yathābhūtāni tattvataḥ |
body.translated_text: For one who correctly sees the emptiness of own-nature — which has the characteristic of the dependent origination of all <s>dharmas</s> — sees the four noble truths as they truly are, in reality.

body.text: yathoktamāryamañjuśrīparipṛcchāyām-
body.translated_text: As stated in the noble <s>Mañjuśrīparipṛcchā</s> —

body.text: yena mañjuśrīranutpādaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ dṛṣṭaḥ, tena duḥkhaṃ parijñātam | yena nāstitā sarvadharmāṇāṃ dṛṣṭā, tasya samudayaḥ prahīṇaḥ | yena atyantaparinirvṛtāḥ sarvadharmā dṛṣṭāḥ, tena nirodhaḥ sākṣātkṛtaḥ | yena mañjuśrīrabhāvaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ dṛṣṭaḥ, tena mārgo bhāvitaḥ || iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'By whomsoever, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s> has been seen — by that one, suffering has been fully known. By whomsoever the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s> has been seen — by that one, the origin has been abandoned. By whomsoever all <s>dharmas</s> have been seen as utterly ceased — by that one, cessation has been directly realized. By whomsoever, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s> has been seen — by that one, the path has been cultivated.' And so forth in detail.

body.text: uktaṃ ca āryadhyāyitamuṣṭisūtre-
body.translated_text: And it has been said in the noble <s>Dhyāyitamuṣṭisūtra</s> —

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat- caturṇā mañjuśrīrāryasatyānāṃ yathābhūtādarśanāccaturbhirviparyāsairviparyastacittāḥ sattvā evabhimamabhūtaṃ saṃsāraṃ nātikrāmanti | evamukte mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto bhagavantametadavocat- deśayatu bhagavān kasyopalambhataḥ sattvāḥ saṃsāraṃ nātikrāmanti? bhagavānāha- ātmātmīyopalambhato mañjuśrīḥ sattvāḥ saṃsāraṃ nātikrāmanti | tat kasya hetoḥ? yo hi mañjuśrīrātmānaṃ paraṃ ca samanupaśyati, tasya karmābhisaṃskārā bhavanti | bālo mañjuśrīraśrutavān pṛthagjano 'tyantaparinirvṛtān sarvadharmānaprajānānaḥ ātmānaṃ paraṃ ca upalabhate, upalabhya abhiniviśate, abhiniviṣṭaḥ san rajyate duṣyate muhyate | sa rakto duṣṭo mūḍhaḥ san trividhaṃ karma abhisaṃskaroti kāyena vācā manasā | saḥ asatsamāropeṇa vikalpayati- ahaṃ raktaḥ, ahaṃ duṣṭaḥ, ahaṃ mūḍhaḥ iti | tasya tathāgataśāsane pravrajitasya evaṃ bhavati- ahaṃ śīlavān, ahaṃ brahmacārī, saṃsāraṃ samatikrāmiṣyāmi, ahaṃ nirvāṇamanuprāpsyāmi, ahaṃ duḥkhebhyo mokṣyāmi | sa kalpayati- ime dharmāḥ kuśalāḥ, ime dharmā akuśalā iti, ime dharmāḥ prahātavyāḥ, ime dharmāḥ sākṣātkartavyāḥ, duḥkhaṃ parijñātavyam, samudayaḥ prahātavyaḥ, nirodhaḥ sākṣātkartavyaḥ, mārgo bhāvayitavyaḥ | sa kalpayati anityāḥ sarvasaṃskārāḥ, ādīptāḥ sarvasaṃskārāḥ | yannvahaṃ sarvasaṃskārebhyaḥ palāyeyam | tasyaiva mavekṣamāṇasya utpadyate nirvitsahagato manasikāraḥ animittapurogataḥ | tasyaivaṃ bhavati- eṣā sā duḥkhaparijñā, yeyameṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ parijñā | tasyaivaṃ bhavati- yannvahaṃ samudayaṃ prajaheyam | sa sarvadharmebhya artīyate jehrīyate vitarati vijugupsate uttrasyati saṃtrasyati saṃtrāsamāpadyate | tasyaivaṃ bhavati- iyameṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ sākṣātkriyā, idaṃ samudayaprahāṇam, yadidamebhyo dharmebhyo 'rtīyanā | tasyaivaṃ bhavati- nirodhaḥ sākṣātkartavyaḥ | samudayaṃ kalpayitvā nirodhaṃ saṃjānāti | tasyaivaṃ
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the young prince <s>Mañjuśrī</s>: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, because of not seeing the four noble truths as they truly are, beings, with minds perverted by the four perversions, do not transcend this false <s>saṃsāra</s>.' When this was said, the young prince <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> teach — through the apprehension of what do beings not transcend <s>saṃsāra</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Through the apprehension of self and what belongs to self, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, beings do not transcend <s>saṃsāra</s>. For what reason? For one who, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, perceives self and other — for that one, there are volitional formations of action. The foolish, unlearned ordinary person, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, not understanding that all <s>dharmas</s> are utterly ceased, apprehends self and other; having apprehended, he clings; being attached, he becomes passionate, hostile, and deluded. Being passionate, hostile, and deluded, he creates threefold action — by body, speech, and mind. He conceptualizes through false superimposition: "I am passionate, I am hostile, I am deluded." When he has gone forth in the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching, he thinks thus: "I am virtuous, I am a <s>brahmacārin</s>, I shall transcend <s>saṃsāra</s>, I shall attain <s>nirvāṇa</s>, I shall be freed from sufferings." He conceptualizes: "These <s>dharmas</s> are wholesome, these <s>dharmas</s> are unwholesome, these <s>dharmas</s> are to be abandoned, these <s>dharmas</s> are to be directly realized; suffering is to be fully known, the origin is to be abandoned, cessation is to be directly realized, the path is to be cultivated." He conceptualizes: "All formations are impermanent, all formations are ablaze. If only I could flee from all formations!" For him, thus examining, there arises a mental engagement accompanied by disenchantment, preceded by the signless. He thinks thus: "This is the full knowledge of suffering — namely, the full knowledge of these <s>dharmas</s>." He thinks thus: "If only I could abandon the origin." He becomes disgusted with, ashamed of, averse to, and repelled by all <s>dharmas</s>; he becomes terrified and frightened; he reaches a state of alarm. He thinks thus: "This is the direct realization of these <s>dharmas</s>; this is the abandonment of the origin — namely, the disgust with these <s>dharmas</s>." He thinks thus: "Cessation is to be directly realized." Having constructed the origin, he cognizes cessation. He thinks thus:

body.text: bhavati- eṣā sā nirodhasākṣātkriyā | tasyaivaṃ bhavati- yannūnamahaṃ mārgaṃ bhāvayeyam | sa eko rahogatastān dharmān manasi kurvan śamathaṃ pratilabhate | tasya tena nirvitsahagatena manasikāreṇa śamatha utpadyate | tasya sarvadharmeṣu cittaṃ na pralīyate prativahati pratyudāvartate | tebhyaścārtīyate jehrīyate, anabhinandanācittaṃ samutpadyate | tasyaivaṃ bhavati- mukto 'smi sarvaduḥkhebhyaḥ, na mama bhūyaḥ uttariṃ kiṃcitkaraṇīyam, arhannasmītyātmānaṃ saṃjānāti | sa maraṇakālasamaye utpattimātmano deveṣu paśyati | tasya kāṅkṣā vicikitsā ca bhavati buddhabodhau | sa vicikitsāmāpatitaḥ kālagato mahānirayeṣu prapatati | tatkasya hetoḥ? yathāpīdamanutpannān sarvadharmān vikalpayitvā tathāgate vicikitsāṃ vimatimutpādayati ||
body.translated_text: "This is the direct realization of cessation." He thinks thus: "If only I could cultivate the path." Alone, in seclusion, attending to those <s>dharmas</s> mentally, he attains <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility). For him, through that mental engagement accompanied by disenchantment, <s>śamatha</s> arises. His mind does not sink into all <s>dharmas</s>, but flows back and turns away. He becomes disgusted with and ashamed of them; a mind of non-delight arises. He thinks thus: "I am freed from all sufferings; there is nothing further to be done by me; I am an <s>Arhat</s>" — thus he cognizes himself. At the time of death, he sees arising for himself among the gods. He has doubt and uncertainty regarding the <s>Buddha</s>'s awakening. Having fallen into doubt, when he dies, he falls into the great hells. For what reason? Because, having conceptualized all <s>dharmas</s> that are unarisen, he generates doubt and uncertainty regarding the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto bhagavantametadavocat- kathaṃ punarbhagavan catvāri āryasatyāni draṣṭavyāni? bhagavānāha- yena mañjuśrīranutpannāḥ sarvadharmā dṛṣṭāḥ, tena duḥkhaṃ parijñātam | yena asamutthitāḥ sarvadharmā dṛṣṭāḥ, tasya samudayaḥ prahīṇaḥ | yena atyantaparinirvṛtāḥ sarvadharmā dṛṣṭāḥ, tena nirodhaḥ sākṣātkṛtaḥ | yena atyantaśūnyāḥ sarvadharmā dṛṣṭāḥ, tena mārgo bhāvitaḥ | yena mañjuśrīrevaṃ catvāri āryasatyāni dṛṣṭāni, sa na kalpayati- ime dharmāḥ kuśalāḥ, ime dharmā akuśalāḥ, ime dharmāḥ prahātavyāḥ, ime dharmāḥ sākṣātkartavyāḥ, duḥkhaṃ parijñātavyam, samudayaḥ prahātavyaḥ, nirodhaḥ sākṣātkartavyaḥ, mārgo bhāvayitavyaḥ iti | tat kasya hetoḥ? tathāhi sa taṃ dharmaṃ na samanupaśyati nopalabhate yaṃ parikalpayet | bālapṛthagjanāstvetān dharmān kalpayanto rajyanti ca dviṣyanti ca muhyanti ca | sa na kaṃciddharmamāvyūhati nirvyūhati | tasyaivamanāvyūhato 'nirvyūhatastraidhātuke cittaṃ na sajjati | ajātaṃ sarvatraidhātukaṃ samanupaśyati māyopamaṃ svapnopamaṃ pratiśrutkopamam || evaṃsvabhāvān sarvadharmān paśyan anunayapratidhāpagato bhavati sarvasattveṣu | tat kasya hetoḥ? tathāhi sa tān dharmān nopalabhate yatrānunīyeta vā pratihanyeta vā | sa ākāśasamena cittena buddhamapi na samanupaśyati, dharmamapi na samanupaśyati, saṃdhamapi na samanupaśyati | sarvadharmān śūnyāniti samanupaśyan na kvaciddharme vicikitsāmutpādayati | avicikitsan nirupādāno bhavati | nirupādāno 'nupādāya parinirvātīti vistaraḥ || 40 ||
body.translated_text: Then the young prince <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'How, then, <s>Bhagavān</s>, should the four noble truths be seen?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By whomsoever, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> have been seen as unarisen — by that one, suffering has been fully known. By whomsoever all <s>dharmas</s> have been seen as unoriginated — by that one, the origin has been abandoned. By whomsoever all <s>dharmas</s> have been seen as utterly ceased — by that one, cessation has been directly realized. By whomsoever all <s>dharmas</s> have been seen as utterly empty — by that one, the path has been cultivated. By whomsoever, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the four noble truths have been seen in this way — that one does not conceptualize: "These <s>dharmas</s> are wholesome, these <s>dharmas</s> are unwholesome, these <s>dharmas</s> are to be abandoned, these <s>dharmas</s> are to be directly realized; suffering is to be fully known, the origin is to be abandoned, cessation is to be directly realized, the path is to be cultivated." For what reason? For such a one does not perceive or find that <s>dharma</s> which he would conceptualize. But foolish ordinary persons, conceptualizing these <s>dharmas</s>, become passionate, hostile, and deluded. He neither adds to nor removes any <s>dharma</s>. For him, thus neither adding nor removing, the mind does not adhere to the triple world. He perceives the entire triple world as unborn, illusion-like, dream-like, echo-like.' Seeing all <s>dharmas</s> as being of such a nature, he becomes free from attraction and aversion toward all beings. For what reason? For such a one does not find those <s>dharmas</s> toward which he would feel attraction or aversion. He, with a mind equal to space, does not perceive even the <s>Buddha</s>, does not perceive even the <s>Dharma</s>, does not perceive even the <s>Saṅgha</s>. Perceiving all <s>dharmas</s> as empty, he does not generate uncertainty regarding any <s>dharma</s>. Not having uncertainty, he becomes free from appropriation. Free from appropriation, he attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without appropriation.' And so forth in detail. // 40 //

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacitāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau āryasatyaparīkṣā nāma caturviṃśatitamaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, 'The Examination of the Noble Truths,' in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary composed by <s>Ācārya Candrakīrtipāda</s>.

body.text:
25
nirvāṇaparīkṣā pañcaviṃśatitamaṃ prakaraṇam |
body.translated_text:
25
The Examination of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the Twenty-Fifth Chapter.

body.text: atrāha-
body.translated_text: Here one objects —

children.text: yadi śūnyamidaṃ sarvamudayo nāsti na vyayaḥ |
children.translated_text: If all this is empty, there is no arising and no cessation. /
Through the abandonment or cessation of what is <s>nirvāṇa</s> accepted? // 1 //

body.text: iha hi bhagavatā uṣitabrahmacaryāṇāṃ tathāgataśāsanapratipannānnāṃ dharmānudharmapratipattiyuktānāṃ pudgalānāṃ dvividhaṃ nirvāṇamupavarṇitaṃ sopadhiśeṣaṃ nirupadhiśeṣaṃ ca | tatra niravaśeṣasya avidyārāgādikasya kleśagaṇasya prahāṇāt sopadhiśeṣaṃ nirvāṇamiṣyate | tatra upadhīyate 'sminnātmasnehaḥ iti upadhiḥ | upadhiśabdena ātmaprajñaptinimittāḥ pañcopādānaskandhā ucyante | śiṣyata iti śeṣaḥ, upadhireva śeṣaḥ upadhiśeṣaḥ, saha upadhiśeṣeṇa vartate iti sopadhiśeṣam | kiṃ tat? nirvāṇam | tacca skandhamātrakameva kevalaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭayādikleśataskararahitamavaśiṣyate nihatāśeṣacauragaṇagrāmamātrāvasthānasādharmyeṇa | tat sopadhiśeṣaṃ nirvāṇam | yatra tu nirvāṇe skandhapañcakamapi nāsti, tannirupadhiśeṣaṃ nirvāṇam | nirgataḥ upadhiśeṣo 'sminniti kṛtvā | nihatāśeṣacauragaṇasya grāmamātrasyāpi vināśasādharmyeṇa | tadeva ca adhikṛtya ucyate-
body.translated_text: Here, by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, for persons who have lived the holy life, who have entered the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who are engaged in the practice of <s>dharma</s> in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, a twofold <s>nirvāṇa</s> has been described — with remainder (<s>sopadhiśeṣa</s>) and without remainder (<s>nirupadhiśeṣa</s>). Therein, through the abandonment of the entire group of afflictions — ignorance, passion, and so forth — without remainder, <s>nirvāṇa</s> with remainder is accepted. Therein, '<s>upadhi</s>' (remainder) is so called because self-love (<s>ātmasneha</s>) reposes in it. By the word '<s>upadhi</s>,' the five aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandha</s>) — which serve as the basis for the designation of self — are meant. 'That which remains' is the remainder (<s>śeṣa</s>); the <s>upadhi</s> itself is the remainder — <s>upadhiśeṣa</s>; that which exists together with the <s>upadhiśeṣa</s> is <s>sopadhiśeṣa</s>. What is it? <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. And that — merely the aggregates — alone remains, stripped of the thieves of afflictions such as the view of the perishable collection and so forth — by analogy with a mere village remaining after the entire band of robbers has been slain. That is <s>nirvāṇa</s> with remainder. But the <s>nirvāṇa</s> in which even the fivefold aggregate does not exist — that is <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder — because the <s>upadhiśeṣa</s> has departed from it — by analogy with the destruction of even the mere village after the entire band of robbers has been slain. And with reference to that very [nirvāṇa without remainder], it is said —

children.text: abhedi kāyo nirodhi saññā vedanā pi ti dahaṃsu sabbā |
children.translated_text: 'The body was broken, perception ceased, all feelings were consumed in the fire, /
the formations were calmed, consciousness came to an end.' //

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise —

body.text:
asaṃlīnena kāyena vedanāmadhyavāsayat |
pradyotasyeva nirvāṇaṃ vimokṣastasya cetasaḥ || iti |
body.translated_text:
'With a body that was not sunken, he endured feelings. /
Like the extinguishing of a lamp is the liberation of his mind.' //

body.text: tadevaṃ nirupadhiśeṣaṃ nirvāṇaṃ skandhānāṃ nirodhāllabhyate | etacca dvividhaṃ nirvāṇaṃ kathaṃ yujyate yadi kleśānāṃ skandhānāṃ ca nirodho bhavati? yadā tu sarvamidaṃ śūnyam, naiva kiṃcidutpadyate nāpi kiṃcinnirudhyate, tadā kutaḥ kleśāḥ, kuto vā skandhāḥ, yeṣāṃ nirodhe nirvāṇaṃ syāditi? tasmādvidyata eva bhāvānāṃ svabhāva iti || 1 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder is obtained through the cessation of the aggregates. And how is this twofold <s>nirvāṇa</s> tenable if there is cessation of afflictions and aggregates? But when all this is empty, nothing whatsoever arises and nothing whatsoever ceases — then whence are the afflictions, whence the aggregates, through whose cessation there would be <s>nirvāṇa</s>? Therefore, the intrinsic nature of entities does indeed exist. // 1 //

body.text: atrocyate | nanu evamapi sasvabhāvābhyupagame-
body.translated_text: Here it is replied: surely, even so, when the doctrine of inherent nature is accepted —

children.translated_text: If all this is non-empty, there is no arising and no destruction. /
Through the abandonment or cessation of what would <s>nirvāṇa</s> be desired? // 2 //

body.text: svabhāvena hi vyavasthitānāṃ kleśānāṃ skandhānāṃ ca svabhāvasyānapāyitvāt kuto nivṛttiḥ, yatastannivṛttyā nirvāṇaṃ syāditi? tasmāt svabhāvavādināṃ naiva nirvāṇamupapadyate | na ca śūnyatāvādinaḥ skandhanivṛttilakṣaṇaṃ kleśanivṛttilakṣaṇaṃ vā nirvāṇamicchanti yatasteṣāmayaṃ doṣaḥ syāditi | ataḥ anupālambha evāyaṃ śūnyavādinām || 2 ||
body.translated_text: For <s>kleśas</s> and <s>skandhas</s> that are established by <s>svabhāva</s> — since <s>svabhāva</s> does not depart — whence would there be cessation, such that through that cessation there would be <s>nirvāṇa</s>? Therefore, for the proponents of inherent nature, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is simply not tenable. And the proponents of emptiness do not accept <s>nirvāṇa</s> as characterized by the cessation of the <s>skandhas</s> or by the cessation of <s>kleśas</s>, such that this defect would apply to them. Therefore, this is an unfounded charge against the proponents of emptiness. // 2 //

body.text: yadi khalu śūnyatāvādinaḥ kleśānāṃ skandhānāṃ vā nivṛttilakṣaṇaṃ nirvāṇaṃ necchanti, kiṃlakṣaṇaṃ tarhi icchanti? ucyate-
body.translated_text: If the proponents of emptiness do not accept <s>nirvāṇa</s> as characterized by the cessation of <s>kleśas</s> or of <s>skandhas</s>, then what characteristic of <s>nirvāṇa</s> do they accept? The reply is:

children.translated_text: Not abandoned, not attained, not annihilated, not eternal, /
not ceased, not arisen — this is called <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // 3 //

body.text: yaddhi naiva prahīyate rāgādivat, nāpi prāpyate śrāmaṇyaphalavat, nāpyucchidyate skandhādivat, yaccāpi na nityamaśūnyavat, tat svabhāvato 'niruddhamanutpannaṃ ca sarvaprapañcopaśamalakṣaṇaṃ nirvāṇamuktam | tat kutastasminnitthaṃvidhe niṣprapañce kleśakalpanā yeṣāṃ kleśānāṃ prahāṇānnirvāṇaṃ bhavet? kuto vā skandhakalpanā tatra, yeṣāṃ skandhānāṃ nirodhāt tadbhavet? yāvaddhi etāḥ kalpanāḥ pravartante, tāvannāsti nirvāṇādhigamaḥ, sarvaprapañcaparikṣayādeva tadadhigamāt ||
body.translated_text: That which is neither abandoned, like passion and the rest; nor attained, like the fruits of the ascetic life; nor annihilated, like the <s>skandhas</s> and the rest; and which is not permanent, like [things that are] non-empty — that, which has not ceased and not arisen by <s>svabhāva</s>, characterized by the pacification of all conceptual proliferation (<s>prapañca</s>), is called <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Whence, then, in such a <s>nirvāṇa</s>, which is beyond conceptual proliferation, would there be the construction of <s>kleśas</s> through whose abandonment <s>nirvāṇa</s> would come about? Or whence would there be the construction of <s>skandhas</s> there, through whose cessation it would come about? For as long as these constructions operate, there is no realization of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — since its realization comes about only through the complete exhaustion of all conceptual proliferation.

body.text: atha syāt- yadyapi nirvāṇe na santi kleśāḥ, na cāpi skandhāḥ, tathāpi nirvāṇādarvāgvidyante | tatasteṣāṃ parikṣayānnirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | ucyate | tyajyatāmayaṃ grāhaḥ, yasmānnirvāṇādarvāk svabhāvato vidyamānānāṃ na punarabhāvaḥ śakyate kartum | tasmānnirvāṇābhilāṣiṇā tyājyaiṣā kalpanā | vakṣyati hi-
body.translated_text: Now, one might say: even though <s>kleśas</s> and <s>skandhas</s> do not exist in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, they do exist prior to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and from their complete exhaustion, <s>nirvāṇa</s> will come about. The reply is: let this grasping be abandoned, because things that exist by <s>svabhāva</s> prior to <s>nirvāṇa</s> cannot again be made non-existent. Therefore, one who aspires to <s>nirvāṇa</s> should abandon this conceptual construction. For he will say:

body.text:
nivāṇasya ca yā koṭiḥ koṭiḥ saṃsaraṇasya ca |
na tayorantaraṃ kiṃcitsusūkṣmamapi vidyate || iti |
body.translated_text:
'The limit of <s>nirvāṇa</s> and the limit of <s>saṃsāra</s> — /
between these two, not even the slightest [difference] exists.' //

body.text: tadevaṃ nirvāṇe na kasyacit prahāṇaṃ nāpi kasyacinnirodha iti vijñeyam | tataśca niravaśeṣakalpanākṣayarūpameva nirvāṇam | uktaṃ ca bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: Thus it should be understood that in <s>nirvāṇa</s> there is no abandonment of anything, nor cessation of anything. And therefore, <s>nirvāṇa</s> has precisely the form of the exhaustion of all conceptual constructions without remainder. And the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said:

body.text:
nirvṛtti dharmāṇa ca asti dharmā ye neha astī na te jātu asti |
astīti nāstīti ca kalpanāvatāmevaṃ carantāna na duḥkha śāmyati || iti |
body.translated_text:
'The cessation of <s>dharmas</s> — yet there exist <s>dharmas</s>; those that are not found here are never found. /
For those who proceed with the conceptual construction of "it exists" and "it does not exist" — for them, suffering is not pacified.' //

body.text: asyā gāthāyā ayamarthaḥ- nivṛtau nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau dharmāṇāṃ kleśakarmajanmalakṣaṇānāṃ skandhānāṃ vā sarvathā astaṃgamādastitvaṃ nāsti, evaṃ ca sarvavādināmabhimatam | ye tarhi dharmā iha nirvṛtau na santi, pradīpodayādandhakāropalabdharajjusarpabhayādivat, na te jātu asti, na te dharmāḥ kleśakarmajanmādilakṣaṇāḥ kasmiṃścit kāle saṃsārāvasthāyāmapi tattvato
body.translated_text: The meaning of this verse is: in cessation — in the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-element without remainder — because of the complete vanishing of <s>dharmas</s> characterized by <s>kleśas</s>, <s>karma</s>, and birth, or of <s>skandhas</s>, their existence does not obtain — and this is accepted by all schools. Now, those <s>dharmas</s> that are not found here in cessation — like fear of a rope-snake apprehended in darkness upon the arising of light — those <s>dharmas</s> characterized by <s>kleśas</s>, <s>karma</s>, birth, and the rest are never found — they do not exist in reality at any time, even in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text: vidyante | na hi rajjuḥ andhakārāvasthāyāṃ svarūpataḥ sarpo 'sti, sadbhūtasarpavat andhakāre 'pi āloke 'pi kāyacakṣurbhyāmagrahaṇāt | kathaṃ tarhi saṃsāraḥ iti cet, ucyate | ātmātmīyāsadgrahagrastānāṃ bālapṛthagjanānāmasatsvarūpā api bhāvāḥ satyataḥ pratibhāsante taimirikāṇāmiva asatkeśamaśakādaya iveti | āha-
body.translated_text: For the rope in the state of darkness does not actually exist as a snake in its own form — as a real snake would — because it is not grasped by the body or the eye either in darkness or in light. How then is there <s>saṃsāra</s>? The reply is: for foolish ordinary beings, seized by the false grasping of self and what belongs to self, even entities of unreal form appear as real — just as unreal hairs, flies, and the like [appear] to those with an eye-disease. He says:

body.text: astīti nāstīti ca kalpanāvatāmevaṃ carantāna na duḥkha śāmyati | iti |
body.translated_text: 'For those who proceed with the conceptual construction of "it exists" and "it does not exist" — for them, suffering is not pacified.' //

body.text: astīti bhāvasadbhāvakalpanāvatāṃ jaiminīyakāṇādakāpilādīnāṃ vaibhāṣikaparyantānām| nāstīti ca kalpanāvatāṃ nāstikānāmapāyagatiniṣṭhānām | tadanyeṣāṃ ca atītānāgatasaṃsthānāṃ vijñaptiviprayuktasaṃskārāṇāṃ nāstivādināṃ tadanyadastivādinām, parikalpitasvabhāvasya nāstivādinām, paratantrapariniṣpannasvabhāvayorastivādinām, evamastināstivādināmevaṃ caratāṃ na duḥkhaṃ saṃsāraḥ śāmyatīti | tathā-
body.translated_text: 'It exists' — for those with the conceptual construction of the real existence of entities — the <s>Jaiminīyas</s>, <s>Kāṇādas</s>, <s>Kāpilas</s>, and others up to the <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>. 'It does not exist' — for those with the conceptual construction of nihilists, who are destined for bad rebirths. And for others — those who assert the non-existence of the past and future, or of dissociated formations, or of cognition, while asserting the existence of other things; those who assert the non-existence of the imagined nature while asserting the existence of the dependent and the perfected natures — for such proponents of existence and non-existence, proceeding thus, suffering — <s>saṃsāra</s> — is not pacified. Likewise:

body.text:
yatha śaṅkitena viṣasaṃjña abhyupeti no cāpi koṣṭha gantu āviṣṭa papadyate |
evameva bālu 'pagato ..... jāyi mriyate sadā abhūto || iti |
body.translated_text:
'Just as a frightened person generates the perception of poison but it has not actually entered his innards, and what has been generated [as real] has occurred [only in imagination] — /
even so, the fool, being [in that state]... always dies and is born, though unreal.' //

body.text: tadevaṃ na kasyacinnirvāṇe prahāṇaṃ nāpi kasyacinnirodha iti vijñeyam | tataśca sarvakalpanākṣayarūpameva nirvāṇam | yathoktamāryaratnāvalyām-
body.translated_text: Thus it should be understood that in <s>nirvāṇa</s> there is no abandonment of anything, nor cessation of anything. And therefore, <s>nirvāṇa</s> has precisely the form of the exhaustion of all conceptual constructions. As stated in the Noble <s>Ratnāvalī</s>:

children.text: na cābhāvo 'pi nirvāṇaṃ kuta evāsya bhāvanā |
children.translated_text: '<s>Nirvāṇa</s> is not even non-existence — how then could there be a [meditative] cultivation of it? /
The exhaustion of the clinging to existence and non-existence is called <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' //

body.translated_text: Thus. // 3 //

body.text: ye tu sarvakalpanopaśamarūpaṃ nirvāṇamapratipadyamānāḥ bhāvābhāvatadubhayānubhayarūpaṃ nirvāṇaṃ parikalpayanti, tān prati ucyate-
body.translated_text: To those who, not understanding <s>nirvāṇa</s> as having the form of the pacification of all conceptual constructions, conceive <s>nirvāṇa</s> as having the form of existence, non-existence, both, or neither, it is said:

children.translated_text: <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is not, to begin with, an entity — [otherwise] it would have the characteristic of old age and death. /

children.text: prasajyetāsti bhāvo hi na jarāmaraṇaṃ vinā || 4 ||
children.translated_text: For there is indeed no entity without old age and death. // 4 //

body.text: tatraike bhāvato nirvāṇamabhiniviṣṭā evamācakṣate- iha kleśakarmajanmasaṃtānapravṛttiniyatarodhabhūto jalapravāharodhabhūtasetusthānīyo nirodhātmakaḥ padārthaḥ, tannirvāṇam | na ca avidyamānasvabhāvo dharmaḥ evaṃ kāryakārī dṛśyate | nanu ca yo 'syā nandīrāgasahagatāyāstṛṣṇāyāḥ kṣayo virāgo nirodho nirvāṇamityuktam, na ca kṣayamātraṃ bhāvo bhavitumarhati | tathā-
body.translated_text: Therein, some who are attached to <s>nirvāṇa</s> as an entity describe it thus: here, the entity that has the nature of cessation, that serves as a dam — like the damming of a water-flow — that definitively stops the operation of the continuum of <s>kleśas</s>, <s>karma</s>, and birth — that is <s>nirvāṇa</s>. And a <s>dharma</s> of non-existent own-nature is not observed to be efficacious in this way. But has it not been said: 'The destruction, dispassion, cessation of this craving accompanied by delight and passion — that is <s>nirvāṇa</s>' — and mere destruction cannot be an entity. Likewise:

body.text: pradyotasyeva nirvāṇaṃ vimokṣastasya cetasaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'The <s>nirvāṇa</s> of a lamp — that is the liberation of that mind.' /

body.text: ityuktam | na ca pradyotasya nivṛttirbhāva ityupapadyate | ucyate | naitadevaṃ vijñeyaṃ tṛṣṇāyāḥ kṣayaḥ tṛṣṇākṣayaḥ iti | kiṃ tarhi tṛṣṇāyāḥ kṣayo 'sminniti nirvāṇākhye dharme sati bhavati, sa tṛṣṇākṣaya iti vaktavyam | pradīpaśca dṛṣṭāntamātram | tatrāpi yasmin sati cetaso vimokṣo bhavatīti veditavyamiti ||
body.translated_text: — this has been said. And the extinction of a lamp cannot be an entity. The reply is: this should not be understood as 'the destruction of craving is the destruction-of-craving.' Rather, it should be said thus: the destruction of craving occurs in this — i.e., when the <s>dharma</s> called <s>nirvāṇa</s> exists, then craving is destroyed — hence it is 'the-destruction-of-craving.' And the lamp is merely an illustration. Even there, it should be understood as: when that [<s>nirvāṇa</s>] exists, the liberation of the mind occurs.

body.text: evaṃ bhāve nirvāṇa vyavasthāpite ācāryo nirūpayati- bhāvastāvanna nirvāṇam | kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmājjarāmaraṇalakṣaṇaṃ prasajyeta, bhāvasya jarāmaraṇalakṣaṇāvyabhicāritvāt | tataśca nirvāṇameva tanna syāt, jarāmaraṇalakṣaṇatvādvijñānavat, ityabhiprāyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: When <s>nirvāṇa</s> is thus established as an entity, the <s>Ācārya</s> examines: <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not, to begin with, an entity. Why? Because the consequence of having the characteristic of old age and death would follow, since an entity never deviates from the characteristic of old age and death. And consequently, that would not be <s>nirvāṇa</s> at all — because of having the characteristic of old age and death, like consciousness. This is the intended meaning.

body.text: tāmeva ca jarāmaraṇalakṣaṇavyabhicāritāṃ spaṣṭayannāha- asti bhāvo hi na jarāmaraṇaṃ vineti | yo hi jarāmaraṇarahitaḥ, sa bhāva eva na saṃbhavati, khapuṣpavat, jarāmaraṇarahitatvāt || 4 ||
body.translated_text: And making explicit this non-deviation from the characteristic of old age and death, he says: 'For there is indeed no entity without old age and death.' For that which is without old age and death is not even possible as an entity — like a sky-flower — because of being without old age and death. // 4 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat-
body.translated_text: What is more:

children.text: bhāvaśca yadi nirvāṇaṃ nirvāṇaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ bhavet |
children.translated_text: And if <s>nirvāṇa</s> were an entity, <s>nirvāṇa</s> would be conditioned. /

children.text: nāsaṃskṛto hi vidyate bhāvaḥ kvacana kaścana || 5 ||
children.translated_text: For there is nowhere found any entity whatsoever that is unconditioned. // 5 //

body.text: yadi nirvāṇaṃ bhāvaḥ syāt, tadā tannirvāṇaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ bhavet, vijñānādivat bhāvatvāt | yastu asaṃskṛtaḥ, nāsau bhāvaḥ, tadyathā kharaviṣāṇavaditi vyatirekamupadarśayannāha-
body.translated_text: If <s>nirvāṇa</s> were an entity, then that <s>nirvāṇa</s> would be conditioned — like consciousness and the rest, because of being an entity. And displaying the reason through exclusion, he says: that which is unconditioned — that is not an entity, just as a donkey's horn [is not an entity].

body.text: nāsaṃskṛto hi vidyate bhāvaḥ kvacana kaścana |
body.translated_text: 'For there is nowhere found any entity whatsoever that is unconditioned.' /

body.text: kvacanetyadhikaraṇe deśe kāle siddhānte vā | kaścanetyādheye | ādhyātmiko bāhyātmiko vetyarthaḥ || 5 ||
body.translated_text: 'Nowhere' — in a place, at a time, or in a philosophical system. 'Whatsoever' — the thing [said to be] located therein, whether internal or external. // 5 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat-
body.translated_text: What is more:

children.translated_text: And if <s>nirvāṇa</s> were an entity, how could <s>nirvāṇa</s> be without appropriation? /

children.text: nirvāṇaṃ nānupādāya kaścid bhāvo hi vidyate || 6 ||
children.translated_text: For there is no entity whatsoever that exists without appropriation. // 6 //

body.text: yadi bhavanmatena nirvāṇaṃ bhāvaḥ syāt, tadupādāya bhavet, svakāraṇasāmagrīmāśritya bhavedityarthaḥ | na caivamupādāya nirvāṇamiṣyate, kiṃ tarhi anupādāya | tadyadi bhāvo nirvāṇamanupādāya, tat kathaṃ nirvāṇaṃ syāt? naiva anupādāya syāt, bhāvatvāt, vijñānādivat | vyatirekakāraṇamāha- nānupādāya kaścidbhāvo hi vidyate iti || 6 ||
body.translated_text: If, according to your view, <s>nirvāṇa</s> were an entity, it would exist by appropriation — meaning, it would exist by depending on its own causal assemblage. But <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not accepted as existing by appropriation in this way — rather, it is [accepted] without appropriation. If <s>nirvāṇa</s>, being an entity, is without appropriation, how would it be <s>nirvāṇa</s>? It would simply not exist without appropriation, because of being an entity, like consciousness and the rest. Stating the reason through exclusion, he says: 'For there is no entity whatsoever that exists without appropriation.' // 6 //

body.text: atrāha- yadi bhāvo hi na nirvāṇam, yathoditadoṣaprasaṅgāt, kiṃ tarhi abhāva eva nirvāṇam, kleśajanmanivṛttimātratvāditi? ucyate | etadapyayuktam, yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: if <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not an entity, because of the stated consequences, then is <s>nirvāṇa</s> simply a non-entity — since it is merely the cessation of <s>kleśas</s> and birth? The reply is: this too is not correct, because:

children.text: yadi bhāvo na nirvāṇamabhāvaḥ kiṃ bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: If <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not an entity, will it be a non-entity? /

children.text: nirvāṇaṃ yatra bhāvo na nābhāvastatra vidyate || 7 ||
children.translated_text: Where entity-hood does not obtain, non-entity-hood too does not obtain. // 7 //

body.text: yadi bhāvo nirvāṇaṃ neṣyate, yadi nirvāṇaṃ bhāva iti neṣyate, tadā kimabhāvo bhaviṣyati nirvāṇam? abhāvo 'pi na bhaviṣyatītyarthaḥ | kleśajanmanorabhāvo nirvāṇamiti cet, evaṃ tarhi
body.translated_text: If <s>nirvāṇa</s> as an entity is not accepted — if it is not accepted that <s>nirvāṇa</s> is an entity — then will it be a non-entity? It will not be a non-entity either — this is the meaning. If the non-existence of <s>kleśas</s> and birth is <s>nirvāṇa</s>, then

body.text: kleśajanmanoranityatā nirvāṇamiti syāt | anityataiva hi kleśajanmanorabhāvo nānyat, ityataḥ anityataiva nirvāṇaṃ syāt | na caitadiṣṭam, ayatnenaiva mokṣaprasaṅgādityuktamevaitat || 7 ||
body.translated_text: the impermanence of <s>kleśas</s> and birth would be <s>nirvāṇa</s>. For the impermanence of <s>kleśas</s> and birth is itself their non-existence — nothing else. Therefore, impermanence itself would be <s>nirvāṇa</s>. But this is not desired, because of the consequence of liberation without effort — as has been stated. // 7 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat-
body.translated_text: What is more:

children.translated_text: And if <s>nirvāṇa</s> were a non-entity, how could <s>nirvāṇa</s> be without appropriation? /
For there is no non-entity whatsoever that exists without appropriation. // 8 //

body.text: tatra abhāvaḥ anityatā vā bhāvamupādāya prajñapyate, kharaviṣāṇādīnāmanityatānupalambhāt | lakṣaṇamāśritya lakṣyaṃ prajñapyate, lakṣyamāśritya ca lakṣaṇam | ataḥ parasparāpekṣikyāṃ lakṣyalakṣaṇapravṛttau kuto lakṣyaṃ bhāvamapekṣya anityatā bhaviṣyati? tasmādabhāvo 'pyupādāya prajñapyate | tato yadi abhāvaśca nirvāṇam, tat kathamanupādāya nirvāṇaṃ bhavet? upādāyaiva tadbhavet, abhāvatvādvināśavat | etadeva spaṣṭayannāha- na hyabhāvo 'sti yo 'nupādāya vidyate iti ||
body.translated_text: Therein, non-entity — or impermanence — is designated in dependence on an entity, because impermanence is not apprehended for donkey's horns and the like. The characterized is designated in dependence on the characteristic, and the characteristic in dependence on the characterized. Therefore, in this mutual dependence of characterized and characteristic, how will impermanence exist in dependence on the entity that is the characterized? Therefore, non-entity too is designated in dependence [on entity]. So if <s>nirvāṇa</s> is also a non-entity, how would it be without appropriation? It would exist only by appropriation, because of being a non-entity, like destruction. Making this explicit, he says: 'For there is no non-entity whatsoever that exists without appropriation.'

body.text: yadi tarhi abhāvaḥ anupādāya nāsti, kimidānīmupādāya bandhyāputrādayo 'bhāvā bhaviṣyanti? kenaitaduktaṃ vandhyāputrādayo 'bhāvā iti? uktaṃ hi pūrvam-
body.translated_text: If, then, non-entity does not exist without appropriation, will non-entities such as a barren woman's son become non-entities by appropriation? Who has said that a barren woman's son and the like are non-entities? For it was stated earlier:

body.text:
bhāvasya cedaprasiddhirabhāvo naiva sidhyati |
bhāvasya hyanyathābhāvamabhāvaṃ bruvate janāḥ || iti |
body.translated_text:
'If entity-hood is not established, non-entity-hood too is certainly not established. /
For people call the becoming-otherwise of an entity its non-entity-hood.' //

body.text: tasmānna bandhyāputrādīnāmabhāvatvam | yaccāpyucyate-
body.translated_text: Therefore, a barren woman's son and the like do not have the status of non-entities. And as for what is said:

children.text: ākāśaṃ śaśaśṛṅgaṃ ca vandhyāyāḥ putra eva ca |
children.translated_text: 'Space, a hare's horn, and a barren woman's son — /
these non-existents are spoken of, just as [there is] conceptual construction regarding entities.' //

body.text: tatrāpi bhāvakalpanāpratiṣedhamātram, na abhāvakalpanā, bhāvatvāsiddhereveti vijñeyam | vandhyāputra iti śabdamātramevaitat, na asya arthaḥ upalabhyate, yasyārthasya bhāvatvamabhāvatvaṃ vā syāditi | kutaḥ anupalabhyamānasvabhāvasya bhāvābhāvakalpanā yokṣyate? tasmāt na bandhyāputro 'bhāva iti vijñeyam | tataśca sthitameva na hyabhāvo 'sti yo 'nupādāya vidyate iti || 8 ||
body.translated_text: — even there, it is merely a negation of the construction of entities, not a construction of non-entities, because entity-hood itself is not established. This should be understood. 'Barren woman's son' — this is merely a word; no referent is apprehended for it, such that the referent could be said to be either an entity or a non-entity. How, then, would the construction of entity-hood or non-entity-hood be applicable to something whose own-nature is unapprehended? Therefore, it should be understood that a barren woman's son is not a non-entity. And therefore, the statement 'there is no non-entity whatsoever that exists without appropriation' stands firm. // 8 //

body.text: atrāha- yadi bhāvo nirvāṇaṃ na bhavati, abhāvo 'pi, kiṃ tarhi nirvāṇamiti? ucyate | iha hi bhagavadbhistathāgataiḥ-
body.translated_text: Here one objects: if <s>nirvāṇa</s> is neither an entity nor a non-entity, then what is <s>nirvāṇa</s>? The reply is: here, by the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>:

children.translated_text: That which is the coming and going — through appropriation or in dependence [on conditions] — /
that very [process], without dependence and without appropriation, is taught as <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // 9 //

body.text: tatra ājavaṃjavībhāvaḥ āgamanagamanabhāvajanmamaraṇaparaṃparetyarthaḥ | sa cāyamājavaṃjavībhāvaḥ kadāciddhetupratyayasāmagrīmāśritya astīti prajñapyate dīrghahrasvavat | kadācidutpadyata iti prajñapyate pradīpaprabhāvad bījāṅkuravat | sarvathā yadyayamupādāya prajñapyate, yadi vā pratītya jāyata iti vyavasthāpyate, sarvathāsya janmamaraṇaparaṃparāprabandhasya apratītya vā anupādāya vā apravṛttistannirvāṇamiti
body.translated_text: Therein, the 'incessant process' (<s>ājavaṃjavībhāva</s>) means the succession of coming and going, of birth and death. And this incessant process is sometimes designated as 'existing' (<s>asti</s>) in dependence on the aggregate of causes and conditions — like long and short. Sometimes it is designated as 'arising' — like the light of a lamp, like a seed and sprout. In every way, whether this is designated in dependence on [something], or established as 'arising in dependence' — in every way, the non-continuation of this succession of birth and death without dependence or without appropriation — that is established as <s>nirvāṇa</s>

body.text: vyavasthāpyate | na ca apravṛttimātraṃ bhāvo 'bhāvo veti parikalpitu pāryata iti | evaṃ na bhāvo nābhāvo nirvāṇam ||
body.translated_text: . And mere non-continuation cannot be imagined as either an entity or a non-entity. Thus <s>nirvāṇa</s> is neither entity nor non-entity. //

body.text: athavā | yeṣāṃ saṃskārāḥ saṃsarantīti pakṣaḥ, teṣāṃ pratītya pratītya ya utpādaśca vināśaśca, so 'pratītyāpravartamāno nirvāṇamiti kathyate | yeṣāṃ tu pudgalaḥ saṃsarati, teṣāṃ tasya nityānityatvenāvācyasya tattadupādānamāśritya ya ājavaṃjavībhāvaḥ sa upādāya pravartate, sa evopādāyopādāya pravartayamānaḥ sannidānīmanupādāyāpravartayamāno nirvāṇamiti vyapadiśyate | na ca saṃskārāṇāṃ pudgalasya vā apravṛttimātrakaṃ bhāvo 'bhāvo veti śakyaṃ parikalpayitum | ityato 'pi na bhāvo nābhāvo nirvāṇamiti yujyate || 9 ||
body.translated_text: Alternatively: for those whose position is that the formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) transmigrate, the arising and destruction that occurs dependently — that, when not continuing without dependence, is called <s>nirvāṇa</s>. For those whose [position is that] the <s>pudgala</s> (person) transmigrates, the incessant process of that [person] — who is inexpressible as either permanent or impermanent — continues in dependence on various appropriations; that very [process], having continued in dependence on successive appropriations, now not continuing without appropriation, is designated as <s>nirvāṇa</s>. And the mere non-continuation — whether of the formations or of the <s>pudgala</s> — cannot be imagined as either entity or non-entity. Therefore, from this reasoning too, it is justified that <s>nirvāṇa</s> is neither entity nor non-entity. // 9 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat-
body.translated_text: What more:

children.translated_text: The Teacher declared the relinquishing of both existence (<s>bhava</s>) and non-existence (<s>vibhava</s>). /
Therefore it is justified that <s>nirvāṇa</s> is neither entity nor non-entity. // 10 //

body.text: tatra sūtra uktam- ye kecidbhikṣavo bhavena bhavasya niḥsaraṇaṃ paryeṣante vibhavena vā, aparijñānaṃ [taṃ?] tatteṣāmiti | ubhayaṃ hyetat parityājyaṃ bhave tṛṣṇā vibhave tṛṣṇā ca | na caitannirvāṇaṃ prahātavyamuktaṃ bhagavatā, kiṃ tarhi aprahātavyam | tadyadi nirvāṇaṃ bhāvarūpaṃ syādabhāvarūpaṃ vā, tadapi prahātavyaṃ bhavet | na ca prahātavyam |
body.translated_text: Therein, in the <s>sūtra</s> it is said: 'Those monks who seek escape from existence through existence or through non-existence — that is non-comprehension on their part.' For both of these are to be abandoned — craving for existence and craving for non-existence. And this <s>nirvāṇa</s> has not been said by the <s>Bhagavān</s> to be something to be abandoned; rather, it is not to be abandoned. If <s>nirvāṇa</s> were of the form of entity or of non-entity, then it too would be something to be abandoned. But it is not to be abandoned.

body.text: tasmānna bhāvo nābhāvo nirvāṇamiti yujyate ||
body.translated_text: Therefore it is justified that <s>nirvāṇa</s> is neither entity nor non-entity. //

body.text: yeṣāmapi kleśajanmanostatrābhāvādabhāvarūpaṃ nirvāṇaṃ svayaṃ ca bhāvarūpatvādbhāvarūpamityubhayarūpam, teṣāmubhayarūpamiti nirvāṇaṃ nopapadyate, iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: For those who hold that <s>nirvāṇa</s> is of both forms — being of the form of non-entity because of the absence of afflictions and birth therein, and being of the form of entity because of being itself of the nature of entity — demonstrating that for them [the position of] 'both forms' of <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not tenable, he says:

children.translated_text: If <s>nirvāṇa</s> were both — non-entity and entity — /
then liberation would be both non-entity and entity; and that is not justified. // 11 //

body.text: yadi bhāvābhāvobhayarūpaṃ nirvāṇaṃ syāt, tadā bhāvaśca abhāvaśca mokṣa iti syāt | tataśca yaḥ saṃskārāṇāmātmalābhaḥ tasya ca vigamaḥ, sa eva mokṣaḥ syāt | na ca saṃskārā eva mokṣa iti yujyate | ata evāha- tacca na yujyate iti || 11 ||
body.translated_text: If <s>nirvāṇa</s> were of the form of both entity and non-entity, then liberation would be both entity and non-entity. And consequently, the self-acquisition of the formations and its cessation — that itself would be liberation. But it is not justified that the formations themselves are liberation. Hence he says: 'and that is not justified.' // 11 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat-
body.translated_text: What more:

children.translated_text: If <s>nirvāṇa</s> were both — non-entity and entity — /
<s>nirvāṇa</s> would not be without appropriation (<s>anupādāya</s>), for both [entity and non-entity] are dependent (<s>upādāya</s>). // 12 //

body.text: yadi bhāvābhāvarūpaṃ nirvāṇaṃ syāt, tadā hetupratyayasāmagrīmupādāya āśritya bhavet, na anupādāya | kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmādupādāyobhayaṃ hi tat | bhāvamupādāya abhāvaḥ, abhāvaṃ copādāya bhāvaḥ, iti kṛtvā ubhayametad bhāvaṃ ca abhāvaṃ ca upādāyaiva bhavati, na anupādāya | evaṃ nirvāṇaṃ bhaved bhāvābhāvarūpam | na caitadevam, iti na yuktametat || 12 ||
body.translated_text: If <s>nirvāṇa</s> were of the form of entity and non-entity, then it would exist in dependence on, relying on, the aggregate of causes and conditions — not without appropriation. For what reason? Because 'both are indeed dependent.' Non-entity exists in dependence on entity; and entity exists in dependence on non-entity — hence both, entity and non-entity, exist only in dependence, not without dependence. Thus <s>nirvāṇa</s> would be of the form of entity and non-entity [only dependently]. But this is not so — therefore this is not justified. // 12 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat-
body.translated_text: What more:

children.translated_text: How could <s>nirvāṇa</s> be both — non-entity and entity? /

children.text: asaṃskṛtaṃ ca nirvāṇaṃ bhāvābhāvau ca saṃskṛtau || 13 ||
children.translated_text: For <s>nirvāṇa</s> is unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>), while entity and non-entity are conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>). // 13 //

body.text: bhāvo hi svahetupratyayasāmagrīsaṃbhūtatvāt saṃskṛtaḥ | abhāvo 'pi [bhāvaṃ] pratītya saṃbhūtatvāt, jātipratyayajarāmaraṇavacanācca saṃskṛtaḥ | tadyadi bhāvābhāvasvabhāvaṃ nirvāṇaṃ syāt, tadā na asaṃskṛtam, [kiṃ tu] saṃskṛtameva | yasmānna ca saṃskṛtamiṣyate, tasmānna bhāvābhāvasvarūpaṃ nirvāṇaṃ yujyate || 13 ||
body.translated_text: For entity, being produced from the aggregate of its own causes and conditions, is conditioned. Non-entity too, being produced in dependence on entity, and because of the statement 'old age and death are conditioned by birth,' is conditioned. If <s>nirvāṇa</s> were of the nature of entity and non-entity, then it would not be unconditioned, but rather conditioned. And since it is not accepted as conditioned, therefore <s>nirvāṇa</s> of the nature of entity and non-entity is not justified. // 13 //

body.text: athāpi syāt- naiva hi nirvāṇaṃ bhāvābhāvasvarūpam, kiṃ tarhi nirvāṇe bhāvābhāvāviti | evamapi na yuktam | kutaḥ? yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Now one might say: <s>nirvāṇa</s> is indeed not of the nature of entity and non-entity; rather, entity and non-entity exist in <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Even so, it is not justified. Why? Because:

children.translated_text: How could both — non-entity and entity — exist in <s>nirvāṇa</s>? /
Those two do not exist in one place, like light and darkness.

body.text: bhāvābhāvayorapi parasparaviruddhayorekatra nirvāṇe nāsti saṃbhava iti, ataḥ,
body.translated_text: Entity and non-entity, being mutually contradictory, cannot co-exist in one [place], namely <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Therefore:

body.text: bhavedabhāvo bhāvaśca nirvāṇe ubhayaṃ katham |
body.translated_text: How could both — non-entity and entity — exist in <s>nirvāṇa</s>? /

body.text: naiva bhavedityabhiprāyaḥ || 14 ||
body.translated_text: They simply cannot — this is the intent. // 14 //

body.text: idānīṃ yathā naiva bhāvo naivābhāvo nirvāṇaṃ yujyate, tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, demonstrating that it is not justified that <s>nirvāṇa</s> is neither entity nor non-entity, he says:

children.translated_text: The notion that <s>nirvāṇa</s> is neither non-entity nor entity — /

children.text: abhāve caiva bhāve ca sā siddhe sati sidhyati || 15 ||
children.translated_text: that is established only if [both] entity and non-entity are established. // 15 //

body.text: yadi hi bhāvo nāma kaścit syāt, tadā tatpratiṣedhena naiva bhāvo nirvāṇamityeṣā kalpanā, yadi kaścidabhāvaḥ syāt, tadā tatpratiṣedhena naivābhāvo nirvāṇaṃ syāt | yadā ca bhāvābhāvāveva na staḥ, tadā tatpratiṣedho 'pi nāstīti | tasmānnaiva bhāvo naivābhāvo nirvāṇamiti yā kalpanā, sāpi nopapadyata eva | iti na yuktametat || 15 ||
body.translated_text: For if some entity existed, then, through its negation, the notion 'nirvāṇa is not entity' [would be possible]; and if some non-entity existed, then, through its negation, 'nirvāṇa is not non-entity' [would follow]. But when entity and non-entity themselves do not exist, their negation too does not exist. Therefore, the notion that <s>nirvāṇa</s> is neither entity nor non-entity is also not tenable at all. Thus this is not justified. // 15 //

body.text: kiṃ cānyat-
body.translated_text: What more:

children.text: naivābhāvo naiva bhāvo nirvāṇaṃ yadi vidyate |
children.translated_text: If <s>nirvāṇa</s> were to exist as neither non-entity nor entity, /

children.text: naivābhāvo naiva bhāva iti kena tadajyate || 16 ||
children.translated_text: by whom would it be known as 'neither non-entity nor entity'? // 16 //

body.text: yadi etannirvāṇaṃ naivābhāvarūpaṃ naiva bhāvarūpamastīti kalpyate, kena tadānīṃ taditthaṃvidhaṃ nobhayarūpaṃ nirvāṇamastīti ajyate gṛhyate prakāśate vā? kiṃ tatra nirvāṇe kaścidevaṃvidhaḥ pratipattāsti, atha nāsti? yadi asti, evaṃ sati nirvāṇe 'pi tavātmā syāt | na ceṣṭam, nirupādānasyātmano 'stitvābhāvāt | atha nāsti, kenaitaditthaṃvidhaṃ nirvāṇamastīti paricchidyate? saṃsārāvasthitaḥ paricchinattīti cet, yadi saṃsārāvasthitaḥ paricchinatti, sa kiṃ vijñānena paricchinatti, utta jñānena? yadi vijñāneneti parikalpyate, tanna yujyate | kiṃ kāraṇam?
body.translated_text: If this <s>nirvāṇa</s> is imagined as existing as neither of the form of non-entity nor of entity — by whom, then, would such a <s>nirvāṇa</s>, of neither form, be known, grasped, or revealed as existing? Is there in <s>nirvāṇa</s> someone of such a kind who cognizes [it], or not? If so, then even in <s>nirvāṇa</s> there would be a self for you. But this is not desired, because of the non-existence of a self that is without appropriation. But if there is no such person — by whom would such a <s>nirvāṇa</s> be discerned as existing? [Objection:] One situated in <s>saṃsāra</s> discerns it. [Reply:] If one situated in <s>saṃsāra</s> discerns it — does he discern it by consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) or by knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>)? If it is imagined that by consciousness — that is not justified. For what reason?

body.text: yasmānnimittālambanaṃ vijñānam, na ca nirvāṇe kiṃcinnimittamasti, tasmānna tattāvadvijñānenālambyate | jñānenāpi na jñāyate | kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmād jñānena hi śūnyatālambanena bhavitavyam, tacca anutpādarūpameveti, kathaṃ tenāvidyamānasvarūpeṇa naivābhāvo naiva bhāvo nirvāṇamiti gṛhyate, sarvaprapañcātītarūpatvād jñānasyeti | tasmānna kenacinnirvāṇaṃ naivābhāvo naiva bhāva ityajyate | anajyamānamaprakāśyamānamagṛhyamāṇaṃ tadevamastīti na yujyate || 16 ||
body.translated_text: Because consciousness has an apprehended mark (<s>nimitta</s>) as its object, and in <s>nirvāṇa</s> there is no mark whatsoever; therefore, to begin with, it is not apprehended by consciousness. Nor is it known by knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). For what reason? Because knowledge must have emptiness as its object; and that [emptiness] is of the very form of non-arising — so how could <s>nirvāṇa</s> be grasped as 'neither non-entity nor entity' by that [knowledge] whose own-form is non-existent, since knowledge transcends all conceptual proliferation in its nature? Therefore, by no one is <s>nirvāṇa</s> known as 'neither non-entity nor entity.' And what is not known, not revealed, not grasped — it is not justified to say 'it exists in just this way.' // 16 //

body.text: sarvathā yathā ca nirvāṇe etāścatasraḥ kalpanā na saṃbhavanti, evaṃ nirvāṇādhigantaryapi tathāgate etāḥ kalpanā naiva saṃbhavantīti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: And just as these four conceptual constructions regarding <s>nirvāṇa</s> are not possible in any way, so too regarding the <s>Tathāgata</s> who has attained <s>nirvāṇa</s> — demonstrating that these constructions are equally not possible, he says:

children.translated_text: It is not apprehended that the <s>Bhagavān</s> 'exists' after cessation. /
