children.text: na bhavatyubhayaṃ ceti nobhayaṃ ceti nohyate || 17 ||
children.translated_text: Nor 'does not exist,' nor 'both,' nor 'neither' is it apprehended. // 17 //

body.text: uktaṃ hi pūrvam-
body.translated_text: For it was said previously:

body.text:
ghanagrāhagṛhītastu yenāstīti tathāgataḥ |
nāstīti vā kalpayan sa nirvṛtasya vikalpayet |
body.translated_text:
'One who, seized by the grip of strong grasping, imagines the <s>Tathāgata</s> as "existing" or "not existing" —
he would construct [views] about the one who has attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' //

body.text: evaṃ tāvat paraṃ nirodhādbhavati tathāgato na bhavati ceti nohyate | etaddvayasyābhāvādubhayamityapi nohyate | ubhayasyābhāvādeva nobhayamiti nohyate na gṛhyate || 17|
body.translated_text: Thus, to begin with, after cessation, the <s>Tathāgata</s> 'exists' or 'does not exist' — this is not apprehended. Because of the absence of both, 'both' is also not apprehended. And because of the very absence of both, 'neither' is not apprehended, is not grasped. // 17 //

body.text: na ca kevalaṃ paraṃ nirodhāccaturbhiḥ prakārairbhagavānnohyate, api ca-
body.translated_text: And not only is the <s>Bhagavān</s> not apprehended through the four modes after cessation, but moreover:

children.translated_text: Even while living, the <s>Bhagavān</s> — 'exists' is not apprehended. /
Nor 'does not exist,' nor 'both,' nor 'neither' is it apprehended. // 18 //

body.text: yathā nājyaṃ na cohyaṃ tathā tathāgataparīkṣāyāṃ pratipāditam || 18 ||
body.translated_text: That it is neither knowable nor apprehendable — this was demonstrated in the Examination of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. // 18 //

body.text: ata eva-
body.translated_text: For this very reason:

children.translated_text: There is not the slightest distinction of <s>saṃsāra</s> from <s>nirvāṇa</s>. /
There is not the slightest distinction of <s>nirvāṇa</s> from <s>saṃsāra</s>. // 19 //

body.text: yasmāttiṣṭhannapi bhagavān bhavatītyevamādinā nohyate, parinirvṛto 'pi nohyate bhavatītyevamādinā, ata eva saṃsāranirvāṇayoḥ parasparato nāsti kaścidviśeṣaḥ, vicāryamāṇayostulyarūpatvāt | yaccāpīdamuktaṃ bhagavatā- anavarāgro hi bhikṣavo jātijarāmaraṇasaṃsāra iti, tadapi ata evopapannam, saṃsāranirvāṇayorviśeṣasyābhāvāt || 19 ||
body.translated_text: Since even the living <s>Bhagavān</s> is not apprehended through 'exists' and so forth, and even the one who has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> is not apprehended through 'exists' and so forth — for this very reason there is no distinction whatsoever between <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>, because when examined they are of equal nature. And what the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said — 'Without beginning, O monks, is the <s>saṃsāra</s> of birth, old age, and death' — that too is justified for this very reason, because of the absence of any distinction between <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // 19 //

body.text: tathāhi-
body.translated_text: Thus indeed:

children.text: nirvāṇasya ca yā koṭiḥ koṭiḥ saṃsaraṇasya ca |
children.translated_text: The limit of <s>nirvāṇa</s> is the limit of <s>saṃsāra</s>; /
between them there is not found even the subtlest difference. // 20 //

body.text: na ca kevalaṃ saṃsārasya nirvāṇenāviśiṣṭatvāt pūrvāparakoṭikalpanā na saṃbhavati, yā apyetāḥ-
body.translated_text: And not only is the imagination of a prior and posterior limit not possible because of the non-distinction of <s>saṃsāra</s> from <s>nirvāṇa</s>, but also these [views] —

children.translated_text: Views regarding what is after cessation, views of finitude and the rest, and of eternity and the rest, /
are based on <s>nirvāṇa</s>, on the posterior limit, and on the prior limit. // 21 //

body.text: tā api ata eva nopapadyante, saṃsāranirvāṇayorubhayorapi prakṛtiśāntatvenaikarasatvāt ||
body.translated_text: They too, for this very reason, are not tenable — because of the single taste of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>, both being peaceful by nature. //

body.text: tatra paraṃ nirodhādityanenopalakṣaṇena catasro dṛṣṭayaḥ parigṛhyante | tadyathā- bhavati tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāt, na bhavati tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāta, bhavati ca na bhavati ca tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāt, naiva bhavati na na bhavati tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇāditi | etāścatasro dṛṣṭayo nirvāṇaparāmarśena pravṛttāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, by the phrase 'after cessation,' four views are indicated: namely — the <s>Tathāgata</s> exists after death; the <s>Tathāgata</s> does not exist after death; the <s>Tathāgata</s> both exists and does not exist after death; the <s>Tathāgata</s> neither exists nor does not exist after death. These four views are directed toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>. //

body.text: antādyā api dṛṣṭayaḥ | tadyathā- antavān lokaḥ, anantavāṃśca, antavāṃścānantavāṃśca, naivāntavān nānantavān lokaḥ iti | etāścatasro dṛṣṭayo 'parāntaṃ samāśritya pravṛttāḥ | tatra ātmano lokasya vā anāgatamutpādamapaśyan antavān loka ityevaṃ kalpayan aparāntamālambya pravartate| evamanāgatamutpādaṃ paśyan anantavān loka ioti pravartate| paśyaṃśca apaśyaṃśca ubhayathā prātipadyate| dvayapratiṣedhena naivāntavān nānantavāniti pratipadyate | śāśvato lokaḥ, aśāśvato lokaḥ, śāśvataścāśāśvataśca, naivaśāśvato naivāśāśvāto lokaḥ, ityetāścatasro dṛṣṭayaḥ pūrvāntaṃ samāśritya pravartante| tatra ātmano lokasya vā atītamutpādaṃ paśyan śāśvato loka iti pratipadyate, apaśyannaśāśvata iti pratipadyate, paśyaṃśca apaśyaṃśca śāśvataścāśāśvataśceti pratipadyate, naiva paśyannaivāpaśyan naivaśāśvato nāśāśvataśceti pratipadyate pūrvāntamāaśritya | tāścaitā dṛṣṭayaḥ kathaṃ yujyante? yadi kasyacitpadārthasya kaścit svabhāvo bhavet, tasya bhāvābhāvakalpanāt syuretā dṛṣṭayaḥ | yadā tu saṃsāranirvāṇayoraviśeṣaḥ pratipāditaḥ, tadā-
body.translated_text: The 'views of finitude and the rest' are: the world is finite; the world is infinite; the world is both finite and infinite; the world is neither finite nor infinite. These four views operate with reference to the posterior limit. Therein, one who does not see a future arising of the self or of the world, conceiving 'the world is finite,' operates with reference to the posterior limit. One who sees a future arising similarly operates [conceiving] 'the world is infinite.' One who both sees and does not see maintains both positions. Through the negation of both, one maintains 'neither finite nor infinite.' [The views] 'the world is eternal,' 'the world is non-eternal,' 'the world is both eternal and non-eternal,' 'the world is neither eternal nor non-eternal' — these four views operate with reference to the prior limit. Therein, one who sees a past arising of the self or of the world maintains 'the world is eternal'; one who does not see [it] maintains 'the world is non-eternal'; one who both sees and does not see maintains 'both eternal and non-eternal'; one who neither sees nor does not see maintains 'neither eternal nor non-eternal,' with reference to the prior limit. And how are these views justified? If some entity had some inherent nature, through imagining it as entity or non-entity, these views would [arise]. But since the non-distinction of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s> has been demonstrated, then:

children.translated_text: When all <s>dharmas</s> are empty, what is infinite? What has a limit? /
What is both infinite and with a limit? What is neither infinite nor with a limit? // 22 //
What is identical? What is different? What is eternal? What is non-eternal? /

children.text: aśāśvataṃ śāśvataṃ ca kiṃ vā nobhayamapyataḥ || 23 ||
children.translated_text: non-eternal, or eternal, or both — from this? // 23 //

body.text: caturdaśāpyetāni avyākṛtavastūni asati bhāvasvarūpe naiva yujyante| yastu bhāvasvarūpamadhyāropya tadvigamāvigamataḥ etā dṛṣṭīrutpādya abhiniviśate, tasyāyamabhiniveśo nirvāṇapuragāminaṃ panthānaṃ niruṇaddhi, sāṃsārikeṣu ca duḥkheṣu niyojayatīti vijñeyam || 23 ||
body.translated_text: Even these fourteen indeterminate matters are not tenable in the absence of the real nature of an entity. But one who, having superimposed the real nature of an entity, generates these views from [the notions of] its disappearance and non-disappearance and clings [to them] — his clinging obstructs the path leading to the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s> and binds him to the sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s>. This should be understood. // 23 //

body.text: atrāha- yadi evaṃ bhavatā nirvāṇamapi pratiṣiddham, nanu ca ya eṣa bhavagatā anantacaritasattvarāśyanuvartakena viditāviparītasakalajagadāśayasvabhāvena mahākarūṇāparatantreṇa priyaikaputra kapremānugatāśeṣatribhuvanajanena caritapratipakṣānurūpo dharmo deśito lokasya nirvāṇādhigamārtham,
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: If <s>nirvāṇa</s> too has been refuted by you, then surely this <s>Dharma</s> that was taught to the world by the <s>Bhagavān</s> — who follows the multitude of beings who have wandered through beginningless [<s>saṃsāra</s>], who knows the nature of the intentions of the entire world as they truly are, who is governed by great compassion, who regards all beings in the three worlds with the love of [a parent for] a dear only child — this <s>Dharma</s> taught as the appropriate antidote for the purpose of attaining <s>nirvāṇa</s>,

body.text: sa evaṃ sati vyartha eva jāyate| ucyate- yadi kaściddharmo nāma svabhāvarūpataḥ syāt, kecicca sattvāstasya dharmasya śrotāraḥ syuḥ, kaścidvā deśitā buddho bhagavānnāma bhāvasvabhāvaḥ syāt, syādetadevam | yadā tu-
body.translated_text: that, this being so, would become entirely purposeless. [Reply:] If there were some entity called '<s>Dharma</s>' existing by its own nature, and if there were some beings who were hearers of that <s>Dharma</s>, or if there were some teacher — a <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s> — who were an entity with inherent nature, then this would be so. But when —

children.translated_text: The pacification of all apprehension, the pacification of conceptual elaboration (<s>prapañca</s>), is auspicious (<s>śiva</s>).
No <s>dharma</s> whatsoever was taught by the <s>Buddha</s> to anyone, anywhere. // 24 //

body.text: tadā kuto 'smākaṃ yathoktadoṣaprasaṅgaḥ? iha hi sarveṣāṃ prapañcānāṃ nimittānāṃ ya upaśamo 'pravṛttistannirvāṇam | sa eva copaśamaḥ prakṛtyaivopaśāntatvācchivaḥ | vācāmapravṛttervā prapañcopaśamaścittasyāpravṛtteḥ śivaḥ | kleśānāmapravṛttyā vā janmano 'pravṛttyā śivaḥ | kleśaprahāṇena vā prapañcopaśamo niravaśeṣavāsanāprahāṇe śivaḥ | jñeyānupalabdhyā vā prapañcopaśamo jñānānupalabdhyā śivaḥ | yadā caivaṃ buddhā bhagavantaḥ sarvaprapañcopaśāntarūpe nirvāṇe śive 'sthānayogena nabhasīva haṃsarājāḥ sthitāḥ svapuṇyajñānasaṃbhārapakṣapātavāte vātagagane vā gaganasyākiṃcanatvāt, tadā sarvanimittānupalambhānna kvaciddeveṣu vā manuṣyeṣu vā na kasyaciddevasya vā manuṣyasya vā na kaściddharmaḥ sāṃkleśiko vā vaiyavadāniko vā deśita iti vijñeyam | yathoktamāryatathāgataguhyasūtre- "yāṃ ca rātriṃ śāntamate tathāgato 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ, yāṃ ca rātrimanupādāya parinirvāsyati, atrāntare tathāgatenaikamapyakṣaraṃ nodāhṛtaṃ na vyāhṛtaṃ nāpi pravyāharati nāpi pravyāhariṣyati | atha ca yathādhimuktāḥ sarvasattvā nānādhātvāśayāstāṃ tāṃ vividhāṃ tathāgatavācaṃ niścarantīṃ saṃjānanti | teṣāmevaṃ pṛthak pṛthagbhavati- ayaṃ bhagavānasmabhyamimaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati, vayaṃ ca tathāgatasya dharmadeśanāṃ śṛṇumaḥ | tatra tathāgato na kalpayati na vikalpayati | sarvakalpavikalpajālavāsanāprapañcavigato hi śāntamate tathāgataḥ" | iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: — then whence would the consequence of the stated fault apply to us? For here, that which is the pacification — the non-occurrence — of all conceptual elaborations and signs, that is <s>nirvāṇa</s>. And that very pacification is auspicious (<s>śiva</s>), because of being quiescent by its very nature. Or: the pacification of conceptual elaboration because of the non-operation of speech, and auspicious because of the non-operation of mind. Or: auspicious because of the non-occurrence of afflictions, or because of the non-occurrence of birth. Or: the pacification of conceptual elaboration through the abandonment of afflictions, and auspicious through the abandonment of residual impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) without remainder. Or: the pacification of conceptual elaboration through the non-apprehension of the knowable, and auspicious through the non-apprehension of knowledge. And when the <s>Buddha Bhagavāns</s>, like royal swans (<s>haṃsarāja</s>) in the sky, abide through the connection of non-abiding in <s>nirvāṇa</s> which is the quiescence of all conceptual elaboration and is auspicious — [borne] by the wind of the spreading of the wings of their accumulation of merit and knowledge, or [abiding] in the wind-sky, because the sky is devoid of anything — then, because of the non-apprehension of all signs, no <s>dharma</s>, whether pertaining to defilement or purification, was taught anywhere — neither among <s>devas</s> nor among humans — to anyone, neither to a <s>deva</s> nor to a human. This should be understood. As stated in the noble <s>Tathāgataguhya Sūtra</s>: '<s>Śāntamati</s>, from the night the <s>Tathāgata</s> fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening, until the night he will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without remainder — in the interim, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has not uttered, has not spoken, does not speak, and will not speak even a single syllable. Yet, all beings, according to their own dispositions and with their various natures and intentions, understand that various speech of the <s>Tathāgata</s> as issuing forth. And each of them individually thinks: "This <s>Bhagavān</s> teaches this <s>Dharma</s> to us, and we hear the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharma</s>-teaching." Therein, the <s>Tathāgata</s> does not conceptualize and does not discriminate. For the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Śāntamati</s>, has gone beyond the conceptual elaboration of the residual impressions of the net of all conceptualizations and discriminations.' And so forth in detail.

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise —

children.translated_text: Speechless, syllable-less, entirely empty, quiescent from the beginning, and stainless —

children.text: ya evaṃ jānati dharmān kumāro buddha socyate ||
children.translated_text: the youth who knows <s>dharmas</s> thus is called a '<s>Buddha</s>.' //

body.text: yadi tarhyevaṃ na kvacitkasyacitkaściddharmo buddhena deśitaḥ, tatkathamime ete vicitrāḥ pravacanavyavahārāḥ prajñāyante? ucyate | avidyānidrānugatānāṃ dehināṃ svapnāyamānānāmiva svavikalpābhyudaya eṣaḥ- ayaṃ bhagavān sakalatribhuvanasurāsuranaranāthaḥ imaṃ dharmamasmabhyaṃ deśayatīti | yathoktaṃ bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: If, then, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever was taught by the <s>Buddha</s> to anyone anywhere, how are these diverse conventions of teaching perceived? [Reply:] For beings who are subject to the sleep of ignorance and are, as it were, dreaming, this is the appearance of their own conceptual constructions: 'This <s>Bhagavān</s>, the lord of all beings in the three worlds including <s>devas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, and humans, teaches this <s>Dharma</s> to us.' As stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text:
tathāgato hi pratibimbabhūtaḥ kuśalasya dharmasya anāsravasya |
naivātra tathatā na tathāgato 'sti bimbaṃ ca saṃdṛśyati sarvaloke || iti |
body.translated_text: For the <s>Tathāgata</s> is like a reflection of wholesome, undefiled <s>dharma</s>. Neither <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) nor the <s>Tathāgata</s> exists herein — yet the reflection is seen in the entire world. //

body.text: etacca tathāgatavāgguhyaparivarte vistareṇa vyākhyātam | tataśca nirvāṇārthaṃ dharmadeśanāyā abhāvāt kuto dharmadeśanāyāḥ sadbhāvena nirvāṇasyāstitvaṃ bhaviṣyati? tasmānnirvāṇamapi nāstīti siddham | uktaṃ ca bhagavatā-
body.translated_text: And this has been explained in detail in the chapter on the Secret of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s Speech. And therefore, because the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching for the purpose of <s>nirvāṇa</s> does not exist, how would <s>nirvāṇa</s> exist through the existence of <s>Dharma</s>-teaching? Therefore it is established that <s>nirvāṇa</s> too does not exist [as something with inherent nature]. And it has been stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text:
anirvāṇaṃ hi nirvāṇaṃ lokanāthena deśitam |
ākāśena kṛto granthirākāśenaiva mocitaḥ || iti |
body.translated_text: <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is non-<s>nirvāṇa</s> — so has the World-Protector taught. A knot tied in space is untied by space itself. //

body.text: tathā- na teṣāṃ bhagavan saṃsārasamatikramo ye nirvāṇaṃ bhāvataḥ paryeṣante | tatkasya hetoḥ? nirvāṇamiti bhagavan yaḥ praśamaḥ sarvanimittānāmuparatiḥ sarveñjitasamiñjitānām | tadime bhagavan mohapuruṣā ye svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajya tīrthikadṛṣṭau nipatitā nirvāṇaṃ bhāvataḥ paryeṣante tadyathā tilebhyastailaṃ kṣīrātsarpiḥ | atyantaparinirvṛteṣu bhagavan sarvadharmeṣu ye nirvāṇaṃ mārganti tānahamābhimānikān tīrthikāniti vadāmi | na bhagavan yogācāraḥ samyak pratipannaḥ kasyaciddharmasyotpādaṃ vā nirodhaṃ vā karoti, nāpi kasyaciddharmasya prāptimicchati nābhisamayamiti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: Likewise: 'Those who seek <s>nirvāṇa</s> as a real entity, <s>Bhagavān</s>, do not transcend <s>saṃsāra</s>. For what reason? Because <s>nirvāṇa</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the quiescence, the cessation, of all signs and all movements and stirrings. Those foolish persons, <s>Bhagavān</s>, who, having gone forth in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, have fallen into heretical views and seek <s>nirvāṇa</s> as a real entity — like oil from sesame seeds, like butter from milk — those, <s>Bhagavān</s>, who search for <s>nirvāṇa</s> when all <s>dharmas</s> are utterly passed beyond, I call conceited heretics. A yogic practitioner, <s>Bhagavān</s>, who is rightly practicing does not bring about the arising or cessation of any <s>dharma</s>, nor does he wish for the attainment or realization of any <s>dharma</s>.' And so forth in detail.

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacitāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau nirvāṇaparīkṣā nāma pañcaviṃśatitamaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, 'Examination of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>' (<s>Nirvāṇaparīkṣā</s>), in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary composed by the venerable <s>Ācārya Candrakīrti</s>. //

body.text:
26
dvādaśāṅgaparīkṣā ṣaḍviṃśatitamaṃ prakaraṇam |
body.translated_text:
26
'Examination of the Twelve Links' (<s>Dvādaśāṅgaparīkṣā</s>), the twenty-sixth chapter.

body.text: atrāha- yaduktam-
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: It was stated —

children.translated_text: 'That which is dependent origination, we declare to be emptiness.
It is designation in dependence — that itself is the middle path.' //

body.text: kaḥ punarasau pratītyasamutpādaḥ, yaḥ śūnyatetyucyate?
body.translated_text: What then is that dependent origination which is called emptiness?

body.text: athavā | yadetaduktam-
body.translated_text: Or alternatively: It was stated —

children.translated_text: 'One who sees dependent origination sees this:

children.text: duḥkhaṃ samudayaṃ caiva nirodhaṃ mārgameva ca || iti,
children.translated_text: suffering, and the origin, and cessation, and also the path.' //

body.text: tatkatamo 'sau pratītyasamutpādaḥ iti? atastadaṅgaprabhedavivakṣayedamucyate-
body.translated_text: What then is that dependent origination? Therefore, wishing to explain the division of its limbs, it is said —

children.translated_text: Obscured by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), one constructs the formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) in three ways
for the sake of renewed existence, and by those <s>karmas</s> one goes to a destiny. // 1 //

body.text: tatra avidyā ajñānaṃ tamo yathābhūtārthapracchādakaṃ stimitatā | avidyayā nivṛtaḥ chāditaḥ pudgalaḥ punarbhavāya punarbhavārthaṃ punarbhavotpattyarthamabhisaṃskaroti utpādayati yān kuśalādicetanāviśeṣāṃste punarbhavābhisaṃskārāt saṃskārāḥ | te ca trividhāḥ- kuśalā akuśalā ānejyāśca, yadi vā- kāyikā vācikā mānasāśceti | tāṃstrividhān karmalakṣaṇān saṃskārānavidyānivṛtaḥ pudgalaḥ karoti | taiśca saṃskārairabhisaṃskṛtaiḥ karmabhiḥ karmasaṃjñitaiḥ taddhetukāṃ gatiṃ gacchati || 1 ||
body.translated_text: Therein, ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is non-knowledge, darkness, that which obscures the nature of things as they are, dullness. A person obscured by ignorance, i.e. covered [by it], constructs — i.e. produces — for the sake of renewed existence, for the purpose of the arising of renewed existence, those particular volitions (<s>cetanā</s>) of wholesome and other [types]. These, because they construct renewed existence, are 'formations' (<s>saṃskāras</s>). And they are threefold: wholesome, unwholesome, and imperturbable (<s>ānejya</s>); or alternatively: bodily, verbal, and mental. A person obscured by ignorance performs these threefold formations having the character of <s>karma</s>. And by those formations that have been constructed — by those <s>karmas</s> designated as '<s>karma</s>' — one goes to a destiny caused by them. // 1 //

body.text: tato 'sya-
body.translated_text: Then, of this [being] —

body.text: vijñānaṃ saṃniviśate saṃskārapratyayaṃ gatau |
body.translated_text: Consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), conditioned by the formations, enters into the destiny.

body.text: kṛtopacitasaṃskārasyāsya pudgalasya saṃskārānurūpāyāṃ gatau devādikāyāṃ saṃskārahetukaṃ vijñānaṃ saṃniviśate praviśati upapadyate saṃsārānarthabījabhūtam | tata uttarakālam-
body.translated_text: For this person whose formations have been performed and accumulated, consciousness caused by the formations enters — i.e. comes into, takes rebirth in — a destiny such as that of <s>devas</s> and so forth, appropriate to the formations. [This consciousness is] the seed of the calamity of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Then, at a subsequent time —

body.text: saṃniviṣṭe 'tha vijñāne nāmarūpaṃ niṣicyate || 2 ||
body.translated_text: And when consciousness has entered, name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) is infused. // 2 //

body.text: tatra karmakleśāviddhaṃ tasmiṃstasminnupapattyāyatane nāmayatīti nāma, saṃjñāvaśena vā artheṣu nāmayatīti nāma |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'name' (<s>nāma</s>) is so called because, struck by <s>karma</s> and afflictions, it bends (<s>nāmayati</s>) toward that particular place of rebirth; or because, by the power of perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), it bends toward objects.

body.text: catvāro 'rūpiṇaḥ skandhā nāmeti vyapadiśyate |
body.translated_text: The four formless aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) are designated as 'name' (<s>nāma</s>).

body.text: rūpyata iti rūpam | bādhyata ityarthaḥ | idaṃ ca rūpaṃ pūrvakaṃ ca nāma, ubhayametadabhisaṃkṣipya nāmarūpamiti vyavasthāpyate | tatra bimbapratibimbanyāyena svādhyāyadīpamudrāpratimudrādinyāyena vā māraṇāntikeṣu skandheṣu nirudhyamāneṣu ekasminneva kṣaṇe tulādaṇḍanāmonnāmanyāyenaiva aupapattyāṃśikāḥ
body.translated_text: 'Form' (<s>rūpa</s>) is so called because it is harmed (<s>rūpyate</s>) — meaning it is afflicted. And this 'form' along with the aforementioned 'name' — both of these together are established as 'name-and-form.' Therein, by the analogy of an image and its reflection, or by the analogy of a seal and its counter-impression in recitation, when the aggregates at the time of death are ceasing, in a single moment, by the very analogy of the rising and falling of the arms of a balance,

body.text: skandhā yathākarmākṣepata upajāyante | evaṃ ca bimbapratibimbamudrāpratimudrānyāyena pratītyasamutpādaḥ sidhyati | tulādaṇḍanāmonnāmanyāyena tu yadvijñānaṃ saṃniviśate ityuktam, tad bālalokabodhānurodhena, samānakāla eva bhavapratisaṃdhiriti |
body.translated_text: the aggregates pertaining to birth arise according to the impetus of <s>karma</s>. And thus, by the analogy of image and reflection, seal and counter-impression, dependent origination is established. But the statement 'consciousness enters' by the analogy of the rising and falling of the arms of a balance — that was said in conformity with the understanding of the childish world, [meaning] that the reconnection to a new existence occurs at the very same time.

body.text:
tathā samānena samānakālaṃ lokasya duḥkhaṃ ca sukhodayaṃ ca |
hartuṃ ca kartuṃ ca sadāstu śaktistamaḥ prakāśaṃ ca yathaiva bhānoḥ || iti |
body.translated_text: Likewise: 'The power to both take away and bring about the suffering and the arising of happiness of the world at the same time always exists equally — like the darkness and light of the sun.' //

body.text: na tu punaḥ pratītyasamutpādasvarūpavicakṣaṇānāmevaṃ vaktuṃ yujyate sāhacaryāditvamekakṣaṇe tulādaṇḍanāmonnāmadṛṣṭānteneti |
body.translated_text: But it is not proper for those who are experts in the nature of dependent origination to speak in this way — [saying] that it is a case of co-occurrence and so forth in a single moment, using the analogy of the rising and falling of the arms of a balance.

children.text: janmonmukhaṃ na sadidaṃ yadi jāyamānaṃnāśonmukhaṃ sadapi nāma nirudhyamānam |
children.translated_text: If that which is on the verge of birth is not [yet] existent while being born, and that which is on the verge of destruction, though existent, is ceasing,

children.text: iṣṭaṃ tadā kathamidaṃ tulayā samānaṃ kartrā vinā janiriyaṃ na ca yuktarūpā ||
children.translated_text: then how is it accepted that this is like a balance? And this birth without a maker is not proper. //

body.text: ityādivacanāt | yathā bimbapratibimbamudrāpratimudrādinyāyena kṣaṇikatvaṃ neṣyate bhavadbhiḥ, tathā anyasyāpi bhāvasya utpādasamanantaradhvaṃsinaḥ kṣaṇikatvaṃ na yuktam | yataḥ jātijarāsthityanityatākhyāni catvāri saṃskṛtalakṣaṇāni utpadyamānasya bhāvasya bāhyasya ādhyātmikasya vā ekasminneva kṣaṇe bhavantītyabhidharmapāṭhaḥ | tatra jātijarayoḥ parasparavirodhāt sthityanityatayośca ekasminneva bhāve na yugapatsaṃbhava iṣyate sadbhiḥ |
body.translated_text: — because of such statements. Just as momentariness is not accepted by us through the analogy of image and reflection, seal and counter-impression, so too the momentariness of any other entity that is destroyed immediately upon arising is not proper. Because the four conditioned characteristics (<s>saṃskṛtalakṣaṇa</s>) called birth, aging, duration, and impermanence all belong to an arising entity, whether external or internal, in a single moment — so reads the <s>Abhidharma</s> text. Therein, since birth and aging are mutually opposed, and since duration and impermanence [are likewise], their simultaneous occurrence in a single entity is not accepted by the wise.

children.translated_text: For what is momentary, since it is entirely non-existent [at the next moment], whence any becoming old?
And for what is non-momentary too, because of permanence, whence any becoming old? //
Just as the end of a moment [is posited], so too should its beginning and middle be imagined.
Because the moment has [an end], therefore there is no momentary duration of the world. //
Beginning, middle, and end are to be analyzed just like a moment.
The state of having a beginning, middle, and end is neither from itself nor from another. //

body.text: iti madhyamakasiddhāntapāṭhāt kṣaṇikapadārthāsiddherasiddhiravaseyā | na ca jātimaraṇayoḥ parasparabhinnalakṣaṇayoḥ ekasmin kṣaṇe saṃbhavo bhavet, saṃśayaniścayajñānayorālokāndhakārayorjñānājñānayorbījāṅkurayormaraṇabhavopapattibhavayorbhinnalakṣaṇayorityādivat | parasparanirapekṣayoreva svahetupratyayasiddhayoḥ sahabhāvo yujyate savyetaragoviṣāṇayoryuvatistanayornarakarṇayorityādivat, na tu punaḥ kadācidapi parasparaviruddhayorvināśotpādayoḥ | yathoktaṃ rāgaraktaparīkṣāyām-
body.translated_text: — from this <s>Madhyamaka</s> doctrinal text, since momentary entities are not established, [their] non-establishment should be inferred. And the simultaneous occurrence of birth and death, which have mutually distinct characteristics, in a single moment cannot be — like doubt and certainty-knowledge, like light and darkness, like knowledge and ignorance, like seed and sprout, like the existence of dying and the existence of rebirth-linking, which have distinct characteristics — and so forth. Simultaneous existence is proper only for [things] that are mutually independent and established through their own respective causes and conditions — like the left and right horns [of a cow], like the two breasts of a young woman, like the two ears of a man — and so forth; but never for arising and destruction, which are mutually opposed. As stated in the Examination of Passion and the Passionate:

children.translated_text: The simultaneous arising of passion and the passionate is not proper.
For passion and the passionate would be mutually independent. //

children.text: naikatve sahabhāvo 'sti na tenaiva hi tatsaha |
children.translated_text: In unity, there is no co-existence — for a thing is not co-existent with itself.
And in separateness, how indeed could there be co-existence? //

children.text: evaṃ raktena rāgasya siddhirna saha nāsaha |
children.translated_text: Thus, the establishment of passion together with the passionate, or not together, [is not possible].
Like passion, the establishment of all <s>dharmas</s> is neither together nor not together. //

body.text: iti pratiṣedhāt kutaḥ samānakālatā bhāvānāṃ maraṇabhavopapattibhavayoriti? ataḥ sahabhāvo vineyajanabodhānurodhapravṛtta eveti lakṣyate | tena naikasminneva kṣaṇe nāmonnāmau tulāyāḥ saṃbhavataḥ nāmonnāmayoḥ kālabhedāt | balavatpuruṣācchaṭāmātreṇa pañcaṣaṣṭiḥ kṣaṇā atikrāmantīti pāṭhāt, utpalapatraśatasahasravedhavat sūcyagreṇeti | tathāpi atra utpalapatraśatasahasravedhaḥ sūcyagreṇa kramaśo vedho 'vaseyaḥ kṣaṇānāmatisūkṣmatvāt | ekakṣaṇena ślokākṣarapadodāharaṇavat ||
body.translated_text: — because of this refutation, whence the simultaneity of entities, namely of the death-existence and the rebirth-existence? Therefore, the [teaching of] simultaneity is seen to proceed in accordance with the understanding of those to be trained. Hence, just as the rising and falling of a balance do not occur at a single moment — since there is a temporal difference between the rising and the falling — [so too here]. From the reading that for a strong man, sixty-five moments pass in the [time of] a mere snap of the fingers, like the piercing of a hundred thousand lotus petals by a needle's tip — even so, here the piercing of a hundred thousand lotus petals by a needle's tip should be understood as a sequential piercing, because of the extreme subtlety of moments. Like the utterance of the syllables of a verse in a single moment. //

body.text: kiṃ ca-
body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.translated_text: Without cessation, without arising, without annihilation, without permanence, /
without unity of meaning, without diversity of meaning, without coming, without going, //

body.text: yaḥ pratītyasamutpādaṃ prapañcopaśamaṃ śivam |
body.translated_text: that <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), which is the pacification of <s>prapañca</s> (conceptual proliferation), auspicious — /

body.text: iti pāṭhādutpādanirodhayorasaṃbhava eva pratipāditaḥ śāstre madhyamake | āgamasūtreṣu-
body.translated_text: from this reading, the very impossibility of arising and cessation has been demonstrated in the <s>Madhyamaka</s> treatise. In the scriptural <s>sūtras</s> —

children.translated_text: Undestroyed, unarisen, equal to the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) is the world. /
Yet he teaches the realm of beings — this is [his] conformity to the world. //

body.text:
trīṣu adhvasu sattvānāṃ prakṛtiṃ nopalambhati |
sattvadhātuṃ ca deśeti eṣā lokānuvartanā || ityādi |
body.translated_text: In the three times he does not apprehend the nature of beings; / yet he teaches the realm of beings — this is [his] conformity to the world. // And so forth.

body.text: tathā-
body.translated_text: Likewise —

children.translated_text: Form is like a lump of foam; feeling is like a bubble; /
perception is like a mirage; formations are like a plantain tree; /
and consciousness is like an illusion — so declared the Kinsman of the Sun (<s>Āditya</s>). //

body.text:
evaṃ dharmān vīkṣamāṇo bhikṣurārabdhavīryavān |
divā vā yadi vā rātrau saṃprajānan pratismṛtaḥ |
pratividhyetpadaṃ śāntaṃ saṃskāropaśamaṃ śivam || iti |
body.translated_text: A monk who examines <s>dharmas</s> thus, energetic in effort, / whether by day or by night, fully comprehending and mindful, / would penetrate the peaceful state — the pacification of formations, auspicious. //

body.text: etāśca gāthāḥ sarvanikāyaśāstrasūtreṣu paṭhayante | ataḥ phenapiṇḍādīnāṃ hetupratyayasāmagrīṃ prāpya pratītya samutpannānāṃ sāravastuvigatānāṃ kutaḥ kṣaṇikākṣaṇikacinteti? mahāyānasūtreṣu ca-
body.translated_text: And these verses are recited in the <s>sūtras</s> and treatises of all schools. Therefore, for foam-lumps and the like — which are dependently arisen, having come into being through the assemblage of causes and conditions, and are devoid of solid substance — what is the point of thinking about whether they are momentary or non-momentary? And in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtras</s> —

body.text: supinopamā bhavagatī sakalā na hi kaści jāyati na co mriyate |
body.translated_text: All the courses of existence are like dreams, for no one is truly born, nor does anyone die. /

body.text: na ca karma naśyati kadāci kṛtaṃ phalu deti kṛṣṇaśubha saṃsarato ||
body.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> once done never perishes; it yields its fruit, whether black or bright, in <s>saṃsāra</s>. //

children.text: na ca śāśvataṃ na ca uccheda puno na ca karmasaṃcayu na cāpi sthitiḥ |
children.translated_text: It is neither permanent nor annihilation; there is neither accumulation of <s>karma</s> nor abiding. /

children.text: na ca so 'pi kṛtva punarāspṛśatī na ca anyu kṛtva puna vedayate ||
children.translated_text: Nor does that very one who did it experience [the result] again; nor does another who did it experience [it]. //

children.text: yathā kumārī supināntarasmiṃ svaputra jātaṃ ca mṛtaṃca paśyati |
children.translated_text: Just as an unmarried girl sees in a dream her son both born and dead, /

children.text: jāte 'tituṣṭā mṛti daurmanasyitā tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān ||
children.translated_text: delighted at his birth and sorrowful at his death — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like this. //

children.text: yathaiva grāmāntari lekhadarśanāt kriyāḥ pravartanti pṛthak śubhāśubhāḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as from seeing a letter in [another] village, various activities proceed, both wholesome and unwholesome, /

children.text: na lekhasaṃkrānti girāya vidyate tathopamān jānatha sarvadharmān ||
children.translated_text: yet no transference of the letter's speech is found — know all <s>dharmas</s> to be like this. //
From a seal, a counter-impression is seen, yet no transference of the seal is apprehended. /

children.text: na ca tatra na caiva sānyato evaṃ saṃskāra 'nucchedaśāśvatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is neither therein nor from elsewhere — thus formations are neither annihilation nor permanence. //

children.text: bījasya sato yathāṅkuro na ca yo bīju sa caiva aṅkuro |
children.translated_text: Just as from an existing seed there is a sprout, yet what is the seed is not that very sprout, /

children.text: na ca anyu tato na caiva tat evamanuccheda aśāśvata dharmatā ||
children.translated_text: yet it is not other than it, nor is it that — thus <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of things) is neither annihilation nor permanence. //

children.text: yatha muñja pratītya balbajaṃ rajju vyāyāmabalena vartitā |
children.translated_text: Just as, depending on <s>muñja</s>-grass and <s>balbaja</s>-grass, a rope is produced by the force of twisting, /

children.text: ghaṭiyantra sacakra vartate teṣu ekaikasu nāsti vartanā ||
children.translated_text: and a water-wheel with its wheel turns — yet in each individual [component] there is no turning; //
so too, functioning through all the limbs of existence, dependent on mutual accumulation, /
the turning in each individual [limb] — the prior end is not apprehended. //

body.text: ata evoktamācāryanāgārjunapādaiḥ-
body.translated_text: For this very reason, the <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Nāgārjuna</s> has stated:

body.text:
svādhyāyadīpamudrādarpaṇaghoṣārkakāntabījāmlaiḥ |
skandhapratisaṃdhirasaṃkramaśca vidvadbhirupadhāryau || iti |
body.translated_text: 'Through [the analogies of] recitation, lamp, seal, mirror, sound, sun-crystal, seed, and sour [taste], / the rebirth-linking of the aggregates as non-transference should be ascertained by the wise.' //

body.text: śatakaśāstre ca āryadevapādairmahābodhicaryāsthiraprasthānasthitaiḥ-
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Śataka</s> treatise, by <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Āryadeva</s>, established in the firm course of great awakening —

children.translated_text: 'By [the analogies of] a whirling firebrand, magical creation, dream, illusion, the moon in water, /
mist, echo, mirage, and cloud — existence is comparable.' //

body.text: tadevaṃ bimbapratibimbādinyāyena mātuḥ kukṣau vijñāne saṃmūrcchite vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpaṃ niṣicyate, kṣarati prādurbhavatītyarthaḥ | yadi iha gatau vijñānaṃ na saṃmūrchitaṃ syāt, tadā nāmarūpaprādurbhāvo na syāt |
body.translated_text: Thus, by the analogy of image and reflection and so forth, when consciousness congeals in the mother's womb, <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), conditioned by consciousness, is poured out — meaning: it flows forth, comes into existence. If, in this [birth-]destination, consciousness were not to congeal, then the manifestation of name-and-form would not occur.

body.text: sacedānanda vijñānaṃ mātuḥ kukṣiṃ nāvakrāmeta, na tat kalalaṃ kalalatvāya saṃvarteta | iti vacanāt || 2 ||
body.translated_text: 'If, <s>Ānanda</s>, consciousness were not to descend into the mother's womb, that embryo (<s>kalala</s>) would not develop into an embryo.' — because of this statement. // 2 //

body.text: tadevam-
body.translated_text: Thus indeed —

body.text: niṣikte nāmarūpe tu ṣaḍāyatanasaṃbhavaḥ |
body.translated_text: When name-and-form has been poured forth, the six sense-bases come into existence. /

body.text: duḥkhotpattyā āyadvārabhāvena darśanaśravaṇaghrāṇarasasparśamanaākhyaṃ ṣaḍāyatanaṃ nāmarūpahetukamupajāyate | sa cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā saumanasyasthānīyānyabhiniviśate, abhiniviṣṭaḥ san rāgajaṃ dvevajaṃ mohajaṃ karma karotītyādinā duḥkhotpattāvāyadvāratvaṃ ṣaṇṇāmāyatanānām | tadevaṃ saṃbhūte ṣaḍāyatane uttarakālam-
body.translated_text: As the doorways of the future through which suffering arises, the six sense-bases — called seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting, touching, and mind — arise from name-and-form as their cause. Having seen forms with the eye, he becomes attached to those that are grounds for pleasure. Being attached, he performs <s>karma</s> born of passion, <s>karma</s> born of aversion, <s>karma</s> born of delusion — and so forth. Thus the six sense-bases are doorways of the future in the arising of suffering. When the six sense-bases have thus come into being, subsequently —

body.text: ṣaḍāyatanamāgamya saṃsparśaḥ saṃpravartate || 3 ||
body.translated_text: Dependent on the six sense-bases, contact proceeds. // 3 //

body.text: kaḥ punarayaṃ saṃsparśaḥ, kathaṃ vā saṃpravartate iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: What, moreover, is this contact? And how does it proceed? Explaining this, he says —

children.text: cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpaṃ ca samanvāhārameva ca |
children.translated_text: In dependence on the eye and form and also mental engagement, /
in dependence on name-and-form, consciousness thus proceeds. // 4 //

body.text:
saṃnipātasrayāṇāṃ yo rūpavijñānacakṣuṣām |
sparśaḥ saḥ
body.translated_text: Contact is the coming-together of the three — form, consciousness, and the eye. / That contact —

body.text: cakṣurindriyaṃ pratītya rūpāṇi ca samanvāhāraṃ ca pratītya manaskāraṃ viṣayādivilakṣaṇaṃ samanantarapratyayaṃ vijñānabījabhūtaṃ cakṣurvijñānamutpadyate | tatra cakṣuśca rūpāyatanaṃ ca rūpam | samanvāhāraścatuḥskandhalakṣaṇaṃ nāma | tadetattrayaṃ pratītyotpadyamānaṃ cakṣurvijñānaṃ nāmarūpaṃ pratītyotpadyate | tadevameṣāmindriyaviṣayavijñānānāṃ trayāṇāṃ yaḥ saṃnipātaḥ sahotpādaḥ anyonyopakāreṇa tulyaṃ yā pravṛttiḥ, sa spṛṣṭilakṣaṇaḥ sparśaḥ | tata uttarakālam-
body.translated_text: in dependence on the eye faculty, forms, and mental engagement — [i.e.,] mental attention, which is distinct from the object and so forth, which is the immediately preceding condition and which serves as the seed of consciousness — eye-consciousness arises. Therein, the eye and the form-base constitute form (<s>rūpa</s>). Mental engagement, characterized by the four aggregates, is name (<s>nāma</s>). This triad — arising in dependence on these three — the eye-consciousness arises in dependence on name-and-form. Thus the coming-together — the simultaneous arising through mutual assistance, the equal functioning — of these three: faculty, object, and consciousness — that contact is characterized by touching. Then, subsequently —

body.text: tasmātsparśācca vedanā saṃpravartate || 5 ||
body.translated_text: From that contact, feeling proceeds. // 5 //

body.text: iṣṭāniṣṭobhayaviparītaviṣayānubhūtirviṣayānubhavo vedanaṃ vittirvedanetyucyate | duḥkhā sukhā aduḥkhāsukhā ca trividhā | yathā caiṣāṃ rūpavijñānacakṣuṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ saṃnipātalakṣaṇaṃ sparśamāgamya
body.translated_text: The experience of desired, undesired, both, and contrary objects — the experiencing of objects, the feeling, awareness, sensation — is called <s>vedanā</s> (feeling). It is threefold: painful, pleasant, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant. And just as feeling has been stated as arising from the contact characterized by the coming-together of form, consciousness, and the eye —

body.text: vedanā uktā, evaṃ śeṣendriyaviṣayavijñānatrayasaṃnipātalakṣaṇasparśahetukā vedanā vyākhyeyā || 5 ||
body.translated_text: so too, feeling caused by the contact characterized by the coming-together of the remaining [five] triads of faculty, object, and consciousness should be explained. // 5 //

body.text: tata uttarakālam-
body.translated_text: Then, subsequently —

body.text: vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇā
body.translated_text: <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), conditioned by feeling, /

body.text: saṃpravartate iti vartate | vedanā pratyayo yasyāstṛṣṇāyāḥ sā vedanāpratyayā | kiṃviṣayā punaḥ sā tṛṣṇā? vedanāviṣayaiva | kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmādasau tṛṣṇāluḥ
body.translated_text: proceeds — this is the continuation. That craving for which feeling is the condition — that is 'conditioned by feeling.' Now, what is the object of that craving? It is feeling itself. For what reason? Because the one who craves

body.text: vedanārthaṃ hi tṛṣyate |
body.translated_text: craves for the purpose of feeling. /

body.text: vedanānimittameva abhilāṣaṃ karotītyarthaḥ | kathaṃ kṛtvā? yadi tāvat sukhā vedanā asyopajāyate, sa tasyāḥ punaḥ punaḥ saṃyogārthaṃ paritṛṣyate | atha duḥkhā, tadā tasyā visaṃyogārthaṃ paritṛṣyate | atha aduḥkhāsukhā, tasyā api nityamaparibhraṃśārthaṃ paritṛṣyate | sa evam-
body.translated_text: — meaning: he has desire for the very sake of feeling. How so? First, if pleasant feeling arises for him, he thirsts again and again for union with it. If [there is] painful [feeling], then he thirsts for separation from it. If [there is] neither-painful-nor-pleasant [feeling], he thirsts constantly for its non-deterioration. He thus —

body.text: tṛṣyamāṇa upādānamupādatte caturvidham || 6 ||
body.translated_text: while craving, takes up the fourfold <s>upādāna</s> (clinging). // 6 //

body.text: sa evaṃ vedanāsvabhiniviṣṭaḥ saktaḥ tṛṣṇāpratyayaṃ kāmadṛṣṭiśīlavratātmavādopādānākhyaṃ caturvidhaṃ karmākṣepakāraṇaṃ parigṛhṇāti | tadevamasya tṛṣṇāpratyayamupādānaṃ bhavati || 6 ||
body.translated_text: Thus attached and clinging to feelings, he grasps the fourfold [clinging] — called clinging to sense-desires, clinging to views, clinging to rules and vows, and clinging to the doctrine of self — which is the cause that propels <s>karma</s>, conditioned by craving. Thus his <s>upādāna</s>, conditioned by craving, comes about. // 6 //

body.text: tata uttarakālam-
body.translated_text: Then, subsequently —

children.translated_text: When there is clinging, <s>bhava</s> (existence) of the one who clings proceeds. /
For if he were without clinging, he would be liberated; there would be no existence. // 7 //

body.text: pañca skandhāḥ sa ca bhavaḥ
body.translated_text: The five aggregates — that is existence. /

body.text: caturvidhasya yathoktasya upādānasya upādātā grahītā utpādayitā | tasya upādātuḥ upādānapratyayo bhavaḥ upajāyate | kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmāt, yo hi anutpāditavedanātṛṣṇaḥ pratisaṃkhyānabalena tṛṣṇāmasvīkurvan, caturvidhamupādānaṃ pravihāya upādātā amalādvayajñānasaṃmukhībhāvāt syāddhi yadyanupādāno mucyeta saḥ | tadānīṃ tasya na bhavedbhavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The one who clings — the grasper, the producer — of the fourfold clinging as described; for that one who clings, existence conditioned by clinging arises. For what reason? Because one who, without generating the craving that is [based on] feeling, by the power of discernment does not embrace craving, having abandoned the fourfold clinging, that one who clings — through coming face to face with the stainless, non-dual knowledge — if he were without clinging, he would be liberated; then there would be no existence for him. //

body.text: kaḥ punarayaṃ bhavaḥ? pañca skandhāḥ sa ca bhavaḥ | yaḥ upādānāt pravartate, sa pañcaskandha svabhāvo veditavyaḥ | trividhamapi kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ mānasikaṃ ca karma bhavatyasmādanāgataṃ skandha pañcakaṃ bhavaḥ iti vyapadiśyate | tatra kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ karma rūpaskandhasvabhāvaṃ karmavijñaptitvāt | mānasaṃ tu catuḥskandhasvabhāvamiti | evaṃ sa bhavaḥ pañca skandhā iti vijñeyam | tasmāt-
body.translated_text: What, then, is this existence? The five aggregates — that is existence. What proceeds from clinging should be understood as having the nature of the five aggregates. Because threefold <s>karma</s> — bodily, vocal, and mental — gives rise to the future set of five aggregates, it is designated as existence. Therein, bodily and vocal <s>karma</s> have the nature of the form-aggregate, being the informative action of <s>karma</s>. Mental [karma], however, has the nature of the four [name-]aggregates. Thus, that existence should be understood as the five aggregates. Therefore —

body.text: bhavājjātiḥ pravartate |
body.translated_text: From existence, birth proceeds. /

body.text: anāgataskandhotpādo jātiḥ | sā ca bhavāt pravartate | tata uttarakālam-
body.translated_text: The arising of the future aggregates is birth. And that proceeds from existence. Then, subsequently —

body.text: jarāmaraṇaduḥkhādi śokāḥ saparidevanāḥ || 8 ||
body.translated_text: Old age, death, suffering, and the like — grief, together with lamentation, // 8 //

body.text: daurmanasyamupāyāsā jāteretatpravartate |
body.translated_text: despondency, and distress — these proceed from birth. /

body.text: jātihetukā ete jarāmaraṇādayaḥ pravartante | eṣāṃ ca yathāsūtrameva vyākhyānaṃ veditavyam | tatra skandhaparipāko jarā | jīrṇasya skandhabhedo maraṇam | mriyamāṇasya vigacchataḥ saṃmūḍhasya sāmiṣaṅgo hṛdayasaṃtāpaḥ śokaḥ | śokasamutthito vākpralāpaḥ paridevaḥ | pañcendriyāsātanipāto
body.translated_text: These — old age, death, and so forth — having birth as their cause, proceed. And their explanation should be understood according to the <s>sūtra</s> itself. Therein, the maturation of the aggregates is old age. The breaking apart of the aggregates of one who has grown old is death. The heart-burning, accompanied by attachment to 'what is mine,' of one who is dying and departing, bewildered — that is grief. The outpouring of speech arising from grief is lamentation. The impinging of unpleasantness upon the five senses

body.text: duḥkham | manoniṣṭanipāto daurmanasyam | duḥkhadaurmanasyabahutvasaṃbhūtā upāyāsāḥ | iti | tadevaṃ yathopavarṇitena nyāyena
body.translated_text: is suffering. The impinging upon the mind of what is undesired is despondency. The distresses that arise from the multitude of suffering and despondency — these are distresses. Thus, by the method as described —

body.text: kevalasyaivametasya duḥkhaskandhasya saṃbhavaḥ || 9 ||
body.translated_text: There is the arising of this entire mass of suffering alone. // 9 //

body.text: kevalasyeti ātmātmīyasvabhāvavigatasya bālapṛthagjanaparikalpitamātrasya | duḥkhātmakasya sukhāvyāmiśrasyaivetyarthaḥ | evamiti hetupratyayamātrabalenaivetyarthaḥ | duḥkhaskandhasyeti duḥkhasamudāyasya duḥkhasamūhasya duḥkharāśerityarthaḥ || 9 ||
body.translated_text: 'Entire' (<s>kevala</s>) means: devoid of the nature of self and what belongs to self, merely imagined by foolish ordinary persons. Of the nature of suffering alone, unmixed with any pleasure — this is the meaning. 'Thus' means: merely by the force of causes and conditions alone. 'Mass of suffering' means: the collection of suffering, the aggregate of suffering, the heap of suffering. // 9 //

body.text: yataścaivaṃ yathopavarṇitādavidyādikādeva bhavāṅgānāṃ pravṛttiḥ, ataḥ-
body.translated_text: And since thus, from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and so forth alone, the limbs of existence proceed, therefore —

children.translated_text: The formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>), which are the root of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the ignorant one constructs; therefore /
the ignorant one is the doer, not the wise one, because of seeing reality. // 10 //

body.text: tatra saṃsārasya vijñānādipravṛttilakṣaṇasya mūlaṃ pradhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ saṃskārāḥ | tataśca saṃsāramūlān saṃskārānavidvān saṃskaroti ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the root — the chief, the cause — of <s>saṃsāra</s>, characterized by the proceeding of consciousness and so forth, are the formations. And therefore, the ignorant one constructs the formations that are the root of <s>saṃsāra</s>. //

body.text: avidyānugato yaḥ pudgalo bhikṣavaḥ puṇyānapi saṃskārānabhisaṃskaroti, apuṇyānapi saṃskārānabhisaṃskaroti, āneñjyānapi saṃskārānabhisaṃskaroti ||
body.translated_text: 'The person who is accompanied by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), O monks, constructs meritorious formations, constructs demeritorious formations, constructs imperturbable formations.' //

body.text: iti bhagavadvacanāt | yataścaivamavidvān kārakaḥ, tasmādavidvāneva pudgalaḥ kārako bhavati saṃskārāṇām, na vidvāṃstattvadarśī prahīṇāvidyaḥ | kiṃ kāraṇam? tattvadarśanāt tattvadarśane hi sarvapadārthanāmevānupalambhāt nāsti kiṃcid yadālambya karma kuryāditi || 10 ||
body.translated_text: — because of this statement of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. And since thus the ignorant one is the doer, therefore the ignorant <s>pudgala</s> (person) alone is the doer of formations, not the wise one who sees reality, who has abandoned ignorance. For what reason? Because of seeing reality — for in the seeing of reality, since all entities whatsoever are not apprehended, there is nothing upon which one would seize and perform action. // 10 //

body.text: yataścaivamavidyāyāmeva satyāṃ saṃskārāḥ pravartante, asatyāṃ na pravartante, ataḥ-
body.translated_text: And since thus formations proceed only when ignorance exists, and do not proceed when it does not exist, therefore —

body.text: avidyāyāṃ niruddhāyāṃ saṃskārāṇāmasaṃbhavaḥ |
body.translated_text: When <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) has ceased, formations do not come into being. /

body.text: hetuvaiyarthyāt | tasyāḥ punaravidyāyāḥ kuto nirodhaḥ ityāha-
body.translated_text: — because of the purposelessness of the cause. Whence, moreover, does the cessation of that ignorance come? He says —

body.text: avidyāyā nirodhastu jñānenāsyaiva bhāvanāt || 11 ||
body.translated_text: The cessation of <s>avidyā</s>, however, is through knowledge — through the cultivation of this very [knowledge]. // 11 //

body.text: asyaiva pratītyasamutpādasya yathāvadaviparītabhāvanātaḥ avidyā prahīyate | yo hi pratītyasamutpādaṃ samyak paśyati, sa sūkṣmasyāpi bhāvasya na svarūpamupalabhate | pratibimbasvaprālātacakramudgādivattu svabhāvaśūnyatāṃ sarveṣāṃ bhāvānāmavatarati | sa eva svabhāvaśūnyatāṃ sarveṣāṃ bhāvānāmavatīrṇo na kiṃcidvastu upalabhate bāhyamādhyātmikaṃ vā | so 'nupalabhamāno na kvaciddharme muhyati, amūḍhaśca karma na karotīti | evaṃ pratītyasamutpādabhāvanayā tattvamavatarati |tattvadarśinoyogino niyatameva avidyā prahīyate | prahīṇāvidyasya saṃskārā nirudhyante || 11 ||
body.translated_text: Through the correct, non-distorted cultivation of this very dependent origination, ignorance is abandoned. For one who correctly sees dependent origination does not find the own-form of even a subtle entity. Rather, like a reflection, a whirling firebrand, or a magic trick, he enters into the emptiness of own-nature of all entities. That very one who has entered into the emptiness of own-nature of all entities does not find any thing whatsoever, whether external or internal. Not finding it, he is not deluded regarding any <s>dharma</s>; and being undeluded, he does not create action. Thus, through the cultivation of dependent origination, one enters into reality. For the yogin who sees reality, ignorance is necessarily abandoned. When ignorance has been abandoned, formations cease. // 11 //

body.text: yathā caivamavidyānirodhāt saṃskārā nirudhyante, evam-
body.translated_text: And just as formations cease through the cessation of ignorance, even so —

children.translated_text: Through the cessation of each [prior link], each [subsequent link] does not proceed. /
This entire mass of suffering is thus correctly ceased. // 12 //

body.text: pūrvasya pūrvasya aṅgasya nirodhena utarasyottarasya aṅgasya nirodho bhavatīti vijñeyam | anayā cānupūrvyā ayaṃ yogī ātmātmīyādyadarśanāyāsanirastaḥ kārakavedakavirahitaṃ bhāvasvabhāvaśūnyaṃ duḥkharāśiṃ punaranutpattyā samyaṅnirodhayati | yathoktamāryaśālistambasūtre-
body.translated_text: Through the cessation of each prior link, the cessation of each subsequent link occurs — this should be understood. And by this progression, this yogin, free from the toil of seeing self, what belongs to self, and the like, correctly ceases — through non-re-arising — the heap of suffering, which is devoid of agent and experiencer and empty of the own-nature of entities. As stated in the noble <s>Śālistambasūtra</s> —

body.text: evamādhyātmiko 'pi pratītyasamutpādo dvābhyāmeva kāraṇābhyāmutpadyate | katamābhyāṃ dvābhyām? hetūpanibandhataḥ pratyayopanibandhataśca | tatrādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya hetūpanibandhaḥ katamaḥ? yadidamavidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ, saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānam, vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpam, nāmarūpapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanam, ṣaḍāyatanapratyayaḥ sparśaḥ, sparśapratyayā vedanā, vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇā, tṛṣṇāpratyayamupādānam, upādānapratyayo bhavaḥ, bhavapratyayā jātiḥ, jātipratyayā jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ saṃbhavanti | evamasya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati | avidyā cennābhaviṣyannaiva saṃskārāḥ prajñāsyante | evaṃ yāvajjātiścennābhaviṣyajjarāmaraṇaṃ na prajñāsyate | athavā, satyāmavidyāyāṃ saṃskārāṇāmabhinirvṛttirbhavati | evaṃ yāvajjātyāṃ satyāṃ jarāmaraṇasyābhinirvṛttirbhavati | atrāvidyāyā naivaṃ bhavati ahaṃ saṃskārānabhinirvartayāmīti | saṃskārāṇāmapi naivaṃ bhavati vayamavidyayābhinirvartitā iti | evaṃ yāvajjāterapi naivaṃ bhavati ahaṃ jarāmaraṇamabhinirvartayāmīti | jarāmaraṇasyāpi naivaṃ bhavatyahaṃ jātyābhinirvartitamiti | atha ca satyāmavidyāyāṃ saṃskārāṇābhinirvṛtti rbhavati prādurbhāvaḥ | evaṃ yāvajjātyāṃ satyāṃ jarāmaraṇasyābhinirvṛttirbhavati prādurbhāvaḥ | evamādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya hetūpanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Even so, the internal dependent origination arises from just two causes. Which two? From the connection with causes and from the connection with conditions. Therein, what is the connection with causes of internal dependent origination? Namely: formations are conditioned by ignorance; consciousness is conditioned by formations; name-and-form is conditioned by consciousness; the six sense-bases are conditioned by name-and-form; contact is conditioned by the six sense-bases; feeling is conditioned by contact; craving is conditioned by feeling; appropriation is conditioned by craving; becoming is conditioned by appropriation; birth is conditioned by becoming; old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, mental distress, and affliction arise conditioned by birth. Thus there is the arising of this entire great mass of suffering. If ignorance were not to exist, formations would not be discerned. Even so, up to: if birth were not to exist, old age and death would not be discerned. Alternatively, when ignorance exists, the production of formations occurs. Even so, up to: when birth exists, the production of old age and death occurs. Therein, ignorance does not think: "I produce formations." Nor do formations think: "We are produced by ignorance." Even so, up to: birth does not think: "I produce old age and death." Nor does old age and death think: "I am produced by birth." Nevertheless, when ignorance exists, the production, the appearance, of formations occurs. Even so, up to: when birth exists, the production, the appearance, of old age and death occurs. Thus the connection with causes of internal dependent origination should be seen.

body.text: kathamādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya pratyayopanibandho draṣṭavya iti? ṣaṇṇāṃ dhātūnāṃ samavāyāt | katameṣāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ dhātūnāṃ samavāyāt? yadidaṃ pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśavijñānadhātūnāṃ samavāyādādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya pratyayopanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ | tatrādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya pṛthivīdhātuḥ katamaḥ? yaḥ kāyasya saṃśleṣātkaṭhinabhāvamabhinirvartayati, ayamucyate pṛthivīdhātuḥ | yaḥ kāyasyānuparigrahakṛtyaṃ karoti, ayamucyate 'bdhātuḥ | yaḥ kāyasyāśitabhakṣitaṃ paripācayati, ayamucyate tejodhātuḥ | yaḥ kāyasya āśvāsapraśvāsakṛtyaṃ karoti, ayamucyate vāyudhātuḥ | yaḥ kāyasyāntaḥ śauṣīryamabhinirvartayati, ayamucyate ākāśadhātuḥ | yo nāmarūpamabhinirvartayati naḍakalāpayogena pañcavijñānakāyasaṃyuktaṃ sāsravaṃ ca manovijñānam, ayamucyate bhikṣavo vijñānadhātuḥ | tatra asatāmeṣāṃ pratyayānāṃ kāyasyotpattirna bhavati | yadā tvādhyātmikaḥ pṛthivīdhāturavikalo bhavati, evamaptejovāyvākāśavijñānadhātavaścāvikalā bhavanti, tataḥ sarveṣāṃ samavāyātkāyasyotpattirbhavati | tatra pṛthivīdhātornaivaṃ bhavati- ahaṃ kāyasya kaṭhinabhāvamabhinirvartayāmīti | abdhātornaivaṃ bhavati- ahaṃ kāyasyānuparigrahakṛtyaṃ karomīti | tejodhātornaivaṃ bhavati- ahaṃ kāyasyāśitapītakhāditaṃ paripācayāmīti | vāyudhātornaivaṃ bhavati- ahaṃ kāyasyāśvāsapraśvāsakṛtyaṃ karomīti | ākāśadhātornaivaṃ bhavati- ahaṃ kāyasyāntaḥśauṣīryamabhinirvartayāmīti | vijñānadhātornaivaṃ bhavati- ahaṃ kāyasya nāmarūpamabhinirvartayāmīti | kāyasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati ahamemiḥ pratyayairjanita iti | atha ca punaḥ satāmeṣāṃ pratyayānāṃ samavāyātkāyasyotpatti rbhavati | tatra pṛthivīdhāturnātmā na sattvo na jīvo na janturna manujo na mānavo na strī na pumān na napuṃsakaṃ na cāhaṃ na mama na cānyasya kasyacit | evamabdhātustejodhāturvāyudhāturākāśadhāturvijñānadhāturnātmā
body.translated_text: 'How should the connection with conditions of internal dependent origination be seen? Through the coming together of six elements. Through the coming together of which six elements? Namely: through the coming together of the elements of earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness, the connection with conditions of internal dependent origination should be seen. Therein, what is the earth-element of internal dependent origination? That which produces the state of hardness from the cohesion of the body — that is called the earth-element. That which performs the function of holding the body together — that is called the water-element. That which digests what has been eaten and drunk — that is called the fire-element. That which performs the function of inhalation and exhalation of the body — that is called the wind-element. That which produces the hollowness within the body — that is called the space-element. That which produces name-and-form, the five groups of consciousness in conjunction with name-and-form as a bundle of reeds, and the contaminated mind-consciousness — that is called, monks, the consciousness-element. When these conditions do not exist, the arising of the body does not occur. But when the internal earth-element is not lacking, and likewise the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are not lacking — then from the coming together of all of them, the arising of the body occurs. Therein, the earth-element does not think: "I produce the state of hardness of the body." The water-element does not think: "I perform the function of holding the body together." The fire-element does not think: "I digest what the body has eaten, drunk, and consumed." The wind-element does not think: "I perform the function of inhalation and exhalation of the body." The space-element does not think: "I produce the hollowness within the body." The consciousness-element does not think: "I produce the name-and-form of the body." The body too does not think: "I am produced by these conditions." Nevertheless, when these conditions exist, from their coming together, the arising of the body occurs. Therein, the earth-element is not a self, not a being, not a life-force, not a creature, not a person, not a human, not a woman, not a man, not a neuter, not "I," not "mine," and not anyone else's. Even so, the water-element, fire-element, wind-element, space-element, and consciousness-element

body.text: na sattvo na jīvo na janturna manujo na mānavo na strī na pumān na napuṃsakaṃ na cāhaṃ na mama na cānyasya kasyacit ||
body.translated_text: are not a self, not a being, not a life-force, not a creature, not a person, not a human, not a woman, not a man, not a neuter, not "I," not "mine," and not anyone else's.

body.text: tatra avidyā katamā? yā eṣāmevaṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ dhātūnāyamaiksaṃjñā piṇḍasaṃjñā nityasaṃjñā dhruvasaṃjñā śāśvatasaṃjñā sukhasaṃjñā ātmasaṃjñā sattvasaṃjñā jīvapudgalamanujamānavasaṃjñā ahaṃkārasaṃjñā mamakārasaṃjñā evamādi vividhamajñānam | iyamucyate 'vidyeti | evamavidyāyāṃ satyāṃ viṣayeṣu rāgadveṣamohāḥ pravartante | tatra ye rāgadveṣamohā viṣayeṣu, amī saṃskārā ityucyante | vastuprativijñaptirvijñānam | vijñānasahabhuvaścatvāraḥ skandhā arūpiṇaḥ upādānākhyāḥ, tannāmarūpaṃ catvāri mahābhūtāni, tāni copādāya rūpam | tacca nāma rūpam | aikadhyamabhisaṃkṣipya tannāmarūpam | nāmarūpasaṃniśritānīndriyāṇi ṣaḍāyatanam | trayāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ saṃnipātaḥ sparśaḥ | sparśānubhavo vedanā | vedanādhyavasānaṃ tṛṣṇā | tṛṣṇāvaipulyamuipādānam | upādānanirjātaṃ punarbhavajanakaṃ karma bhavaḥ | bhavahetukaḥ skandhaprādurbhāvo jātiḥ | jātasya skandhasya paripāko jarā | jīrṇasya skandhasya vināśo maraṇam | mriyamāṇasya saṃmūḍhasya sābhiṣvaṅgasyāntardāhaḥ śokaḥ | śokotthamālapanaṃ paridevaḥ | pañcavijñānakāyasaṃyuktamasātamanubhavanaṃ duḥkham | manasā saṃyuktaṃ mānasaṃ duḥkhaṃ dārmanasyam | ye cāpyanye evamādaya upakleśāste upāyāsā iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Therein, what is ignorance? That which, with regard to these six elements, is the perception of unity, the perception of a mass, the perception of permanence, the perception of stability, the perception of eternity, the perception of pleasure, the perception of self, the perception of a being, the perception of a life-force, person, man, and human, the perception of I-making, the perception of mine-making, and such diverse forms of unknowing — this is called ignorance. When ignorance thus exists, passion, hatred, and delusion operate with regard to objects. Therein, whatever passion, hatred, and delusion there is with regard to objects — these are called formations. The cognition of a thing is consciousness. The four formless aggregates that co-exist with consciousness, designated as <s>upādāna</s> (appropriation) — that is name. The four great elements and the form derived from them — that is form. Name and form together, compressed into one — that is name-and-form. The sense-faculties that are supported by name-and-form are the six sense-bases. The coming together of the three <s>dharmas</s> is contact. The experience of contact is feeling. The determination regarding feeling is craving. The expansion of craving is appropriation. The action born from appropriation that generates renewed existence is becoming. The appearance of the aggregates caused by becoming is birth. The maturation of the aggregate that has been born is old age. The destruction of the aged aggregate is death. The inner burning of one who is dying, who is confused, who has attachment — that is sorrow. The wailing born from sorrow is lamentation. The unpleasant experience connected with the five groups of consciousness is suffering. The mental suffering connected with the mind is mental distress. And whatever other secondary afflictions of this kind — they are afflictions.'

body.text: tatra mohāndhakārārthenāvidyā | abhisaṃskārārthena saṃskārāḥ | vijñāpanārthena vijñānam | anyonyopastambhanārthena nāmarūpam | āyadvārārthena ṣaḍāyatanam | sparśanārthena sparśaḥ | anubhavanārthena vedanā | paritarṣaṇārthena tṛṣṇā | upādānārthenopādānam | punarbhavārthena bhavaḥ | janmārthena jātiḥ | paripākārthena jarā | vināśārthena maraṇam | śocanārthena śokaḥ | paridevanārthena paridevaḥ kāyaparipīḍanārthena duḥkham | cittasaṃpīḍanārthena daurmanasyam | upakleśārthenopāyāsāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Therein, ignorance has the meaning of the darkness of delusion. Formations have the meaning of constructing. Consciousness has the meaning of making known. Name-and-form has the meaning of mutual support. The six sense-bases have the meaning of being the doors of entry. Contact has the meaning of touching. Feeling has the meaning of experiencing. Craving has the meaning of thirsting. Appropriation has the meaning of grasping. Becoming has the meaning of renewed existence. Birth has the meaning of being born. Old age has the meaning of maturation. Death has the meaning of destruction. Sorrow has the meaning of grieving. Lamentation has the meaning of lamenting. Suffering has the meaning of bodily torment. Mental distress has the meaning of mental torment. Afflictions have the meaning of secondary defilements.'

body.text: athavā tattve 'pratipattirmithyāpratipattirajñānamavidyā | evamavidyāyāṃ satyāṃ trividhāḥ saṃskārā abhinirvartante puṇyopagā apuṇyopagā āneñjyopagāḥ | tatra puṇyopagānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ puṇyopagameva vijñānaṃ bhavati | apuṇyopagānāṃ saṃskārāṇāmapuṇyopagameva vijñānaṃ bhavati | āneñjyopagānāṃ saṃskārāṇāmāneñjyopagameva vijñānaṃ bhavati | idamucyate vijñānam | vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpamiti vedanādayo 'rūpiṇaścatvāraḥ skandhāstatra tatra bhave nāmayantīti nāma | saharūpaskandhena ca nāma rūpaṃ ceti nāmarūpamucyate | nāmarūpavivṛddhayā ṣaḍbhirāyatanadvāraiḥ kṛtyakriyāḥ pravartante prajñāyante, tannāmarūpapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanamityucyate | ṣaḍbhyaścāyataṃebhyaḥ ṣaṭ sparśakāyāḥ pravartante, ayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanapratyayaḥ sparśa ityucyate | yajjātīyaḥ sparśo bhavati tajjātīyā vedanā pravartate | iyamucyate bhikṣavaḥ sparśapratyayā vedaneti | yastāṃ vedanāṃ viśeṣeṇāsvādayati abhinandati adhyavasyati adhyavasāya tiṣṭhati, sā vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇetyucyate | āsvādanābhinandanādhyavasānasthānādātmapriyarūpasātarūpairviyogo mā bhūnnityamaparityāgo bhavediti yaivaṃ prārthanā idamucyate bhikṣavastṛṣṇāpratyayamupādānam | yatra vastuni satṛṣṇastasya vastuno 'rjanāya viṭhapanāyopādānamupādatte, tatra tatra prārthayate, evaṃ prārthayamānaḥ punarbhavajanakaṃ karma samutthāpayati kāyena vācā manasā ca, sa upādānapratyayo bhava ityucyate |
body.translated_text: 'Alternatively, the failure to understand reality, false understanding, and unknowing — this is ignorance. When ignorance thus exists, three types of formations are produced: those leading to merit, those leading to demerit, and those leading to the imperturbable. Therein, for formations leading to merit, there is consciousness leading to merit. For formations leading to demerit, there is consciousness leading to demerit. For formations leading to the imperturbable, there is consciousness leading to the imperturbable. This is called consciousness. Name-and-form conditioned by consciousness means: the four formless aggregates beginning with feeling that are named in each respective existence — that is name. Name together with the form-aggregate — name and form — is called name-and-form. Through the growth of name-and-form, activities and functions operate through the six sense-doors and become discernible — that which is conditioned by name-and-form, the six sense-bases, is so called. From the six sense-bases, six groups of contact operate — this contact conditioned by the six sense-bases is so called. Whatever kind of contact there is, feeling of that kind operates. This, monks, is called feeling conditioned by contact. One who savors, delights in, determines, and abides in that feeling — that is called craving conditioned by feeling. Through savoring, delighting, determining, and abiding [in feeling], the wish that there be no separation from what is dear and pleasant to the self, that there be permanent non-relinquishment — this, monks, is called appropriation conditioned by craving. Where there is an object regarding which the one with craving appropriates for the sake of obtaining and securing that object, there he yearns; thus yearning, he sets in motion action that generates renewed existence by body, speech, and mind — that is called becoming conditioned by appropriation.

body.text: tatkarmanirjātānāṃ skandhānāmabhinirvṛtiryā sā bhavapratyayā jātirityucyate | jātyābhinirvṛttānāṃ skandhānāmupacayanaparipākādvināśo bhavati | tadidaṃ jātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇamityucyate ||
body.translated_text: The production of the aggregates born from that action — that is called birth conditioned by becoming. The destruction through the accumulation, maturation, and the like of the aggregates produced through birth — this is called old age and death conditioned by birth.'

body.text: evamayaṃ dvādaśāṅgaḥ pratītyasamutpādo 'nyonyahetuko 'nyonyapratyayo naivānityo naiva nityo na saṃskṛto nāsaṃskṛto nāhetuko nāpratyayo na vedayitā nāvedayitā na pratītyasamutpanno nāpratītyasamutpanno na kṣayadharmo nākṣayadharmo na vināśadharmo nāvināśadharmo na nirodhadharmo nānirodhadharmo 'nādikālapravṛtto 'nucchinno 'nupravartate nadīsrotavat ||
body.translated_text: 'Thus this twelve-membered dependent origination — mutually causing, mutually conditioning — is neither impermanent nor permanent, neither conditioned nor unconditioned, neither without a cause nor without conditions, neither an experiencer nor a non-experiencer, neither dependently arisen nor not dependently arisen, neither of the nature of destruction nor not of the nature of destruction, neither of the nature of passing away nor not of the nature of passing away, neither of the nature of cessation nor not of the nature of cessation — having proceeded since beginningless time, uncut off, it continues like the current of a river.'

body.text: yadyapyayaṃ dvādaśāṅgaḥ pratītyasamutpādo 'nucchinno 'nupravartate nadīsrotavat, atha cemānyasya dvādaśāṅgasya pratītyasamutpādasya catvāryaṅgāni saṃghātakriyāyai hetutvena pravartante | katamāni catvāri? yaduta avidyā tṛṣṇā karma vijñānaṃ ca | tatra vijñānaṃ bījasvabhāvatvena hetuḥ | karma kṣetrasvabhāvatvena hetuḥ | avidyā tṛṣṇā ca kleśasvabhāvatvena hetuḥ | karmakleśā vijñānabījaṃ janayanti | tatra karma vijñānabījasya kṣetrakāryaṃ karoti | tṛṣṇā vijñānabījaṃ snehayati | avidyā vijñānabījamavakirati | asatāṃ teṣāṃ pratyayānāṃ vijñānabījasyabhinirvṛttirna bhavati | tatra karmaṇo naivaṃ bhavati- ahaṃ vijñānabījasya kṣetrakāryaṃ karomīti | tṛṣṇāyā api naivaṃ bhavati- ahaṃ vijñānasya snehakāryaṃ karomiti | avidyāyā api naivaṃ bhavati- ahaṃ vijñānabījamavakirāmīti | vijñānabījasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati- ahamebhiḥ pratyayairjanitamiti ||
body.translated_text: Although this twelvefold dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) continues uninterrupted, like the current of a river, nevertheless four limbs of this twelvefold dependent origination operate as causes for the function of aggregation. Which four? Namely: <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), <s>karma</s> (action), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). Therein, consciousness is a cause in the nature of a seed. <s>Karma</s> is a cause in the nature of a field. <s>Avidyā</s> and <s>tṛṣṇā</s> are causes in the nature of afflictions. <s>Karma</s> and the afflictions generate the seed of consciousness. Therein, <s>karma</s> performs the field-function for the consciousness-seed. <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> moistens the consciousness-seed. <s>Avidyā</s> scatters [i.e. plants] the consciousness-seed. In the absence of those conditions, the production of the consciousness-seed does not occur. Therein, <s>karma</s> does not have the thought: 'I perform the field-function for the consciousness-seed.' <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> too does not have the thought: 'I perform the moistening function for consciousness.' <s>Avidyā</s> too does not have the thought: 'I scatter the consciousness-seed.' And the consciousness-seed too does not have the thought: 'I have been generated by these conditions.' //

body.text: atha ca vijñānabījaṃ karmakṣetrapratiṣṭhitaṃ tṛṣṇāsnehābhiṣyanditamavidyayā svavakīrṇaṃ vibhajyamānaṃ virohati | tatratatropapattyāṃyatanapratisaṃdhau mātuḥ kukṣau nāmarūpāṅkuramabhinirvartayati | sa ca nāmarūpāṅkuro na svayaṃ kṛtoa na parakṛto nobhayakṛto neśvarakṛto na kālapariṇāmito na prakṛtisaṃbhūto na caikakāraṇādhīno nāpyahetusamutpannaḥ | atha ca mātāpitṛsaṃyogād, ṛtusamavāyād, anyeṣāṃ pratyayānāṃ samavāyād āsvādānuviddhaṃ vijñānabījaṃ mātuḥ kukṣau nāmarūpāṅkuramabhinirvartayati asvāmikeṣu dharmeṣvaparigraheṣvamameṣvākāśasameṣu māyālakṣaṇasvabhāveṣu hetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt ||
body.translated_text: Nevertheless, the consciousness-seed — established in the field of <s>karma</s>, moistened by the sap of <s>tṛṣṇā</s>, scattered by <s>avidyā</s> — germinates through differentiation. At the rebirth-linking (<s>pratisaṃdhi</s>) in one or another birth-destination, it produces the sprout of <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) in the mother's womb. And that sprout of <s>nāmarūpa</s> is not self-made, nor made by another, nor made by both, nor made by <s>Īśvara</s> (God), nor [arisen] from the transformation of time, nor originated from <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), nor dependent on a single cause, nor arisen without a cause. Nevertheless, from the union of mother and father, from the concurrence of the season, and from the concurrence of other conditions, the consciousness-seed — infused with relish — produces the sprout of <s>nāmarūpa</s> in the mother's womb, among <s>dharmas</s> that are ownerless, without possession, without 'mine,' equal to space, having the nature characterized by illusion — because of the non-deficiency of causes and conditions. //

body.text: tadyathā pañcabhiḥ kāraṇaiścakṣurvijñānamutpadyate | katamaiḥ pañcabhiḥ? yaduta cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpaṃ cālokaṃ cākāśaṃ ca tajjamanasikāraṃ ca pratītyotpadyate cakṣurvijñānam | tatra cakṣurvijñānasya cakṣurāśrayakṛtyaṃ karoti | rūpamālambanakṛtyaṃ karoti | āloko 'vabhāsakṛtyaṃ karoti | ākāśamanāvaraṇakṛtyaṃ karoti | tajjamanasikāraḥ samanvāharaṇakṛtyaṃ karoti | asatāmeṣāṃ pratyayānāṃ cakṣurvijñānaṃ notpadyate | yadā tu cakṣurādhyātmikamāyatanamavikalaṃ bhavati, evaṃ rūpālokākāśatajjamanasikārāścāvikalā bhavanti, tataḥ sarveṣāṃ samavāyāccakṣurvijñānamutpadyate | tatra cakṣuṣo naivaṃ bhavati- ahaṃ cakṣurvijñānasyāśrayakṛtyaṃ karomīti | ālokasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati- ahaṃ cakṣurvijñānasyāvabhāsakṛtyaṃ karomīti | ākāśasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati- ahaṃ cakṣurvijñānasyānāvaraṇakṛtyaṃ karomiti | tajjamanasikārasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati- ahaṃ cakṣurvijñānasya samanvāharaṇakṛtyaṃ karomīti | cakṣurvijñānasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati- ahamebhiḥ pratyayairjanitamiti | atha ca satāmeṣāṃ pratyayānāṃ samavāyāccakṣurvijñānasyotpattirbhavati | evaṃ śeṣāṇāmindriyāṇāṃ yathāyogaṃ karaṇīyam ||
body.translated_text: For example: eye-consciousness arises from five causes. Which five? Namely: in dependence on the eye, form, light, space, and the mental engagement born from that [contact] — eye-consciousness arises. Therein, the eye performs the function of support for eye-consciousness. Form performs the function of object. Light performs the function of illumination. Space performs the function of non-obstruction. The mental engagement born from that performs the function of directing attention. In the absence of these conditions, eye-consciousness does not arise. But when the internal sense-base of the eye is intact, and likewise form, light, space, and the mental engagement born from that are intact, then from the concurrence of all of them, eye-consciousness arises. Therein, the eye does not have the thought: 'I perform the support-function for eye-consciousness.' Nor does light have the thought: 'I perform the illumination-function for eye-consciousness.' Nor does space have the thought: 'I perform the non-obstruction-function for eye-consciousness.' Nor does the mental engagement born from that have the thought: 'I perform the directing-attention function for eye-consciousness.' Nor does eye-consciousness have the thought: 'I have been generated by these conditions.' Nevertheless, from the concurrence of these conditions, the arising of eye-consciousness occurs. And the same should be applied, as appropriate, to the remaining sense faculties. //

body.text: tatra na kaściddharmo 'smāllokātparalokaṃ saṃkrāmati | asti ca karmaphalaprativijñaptirhetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt | tadyathā bhikṣavaḥ supariśuddhe ādarśamaṇḍale mukhapratibimbakaṃ dṛśyate, na ca tatrādarśamaṇḍale mukhaṃ saṃkrāmati, asti ca mukhaprativijñaptirhetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt, evamasmāllokānna kaściccyuto nāpyanyatropapannaḥ, asti ca karmaphalaprativijñaptirhetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt | tadyathā bhikṣavaścandramaṇḍalaṃ catvāriṃśadyojanaśatamūrdhvaṃ vrajati, atha ca punaḥ parītte 'pyudakabhājane candrasya pratibimbaṃ dṛśyate, na ca tasmātsthānādūrdhvaṃ nabhasaścyutaṃ parītte udakasya bhājane saṃkrāntaṃ bhavati asti ca candramaṇḍalaprativijñaptirhetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt | evamasmāllokānna kaściccyuto nānyatropapannaḥ, asti ca karmaphalaprativijñaptirhetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt ||
body.translated_text: Therein, no <s>dharma</s> transmigrates from this world to the next world. Yet there is the manifestation of <s>karma</s> and its fruit, because of the non-deficiency of causes and conditions. Just as, O monks, in a well-polished mirror-surface, the reflection of a face is seen, and the face does not transmigrate into the mirror-surface, yet there is the manifestation of the face because of the non-deficiency of causes and conditions — even so, no one has departed from this world nor been reborn elsewhere, yet there is the manifestation of <s>karma</s> and its fruit, because of the non-deficiency of causes and conditions. Just as, O monks, the moon-disc travels four hundred <s>yojanas</s> above, and yet even in a small vessel of water the reflection of the moon is seen, and from that place high in the sky [the moon] has not departed, nor has it transmigrated into the small vessel of water, yet there is the manifestation of the moon-disc because of the non-deficiency of causes and conditions — even so, no one has departed from this world nor been reborn elsewhere, yet there is the manifestation of <s>karma</s> and its fruit, because of the non-deficiency of causes and conditions. //

body.text: tadyathā- agnirupādānapratyaye sati jvalati, upādānavaikalyānna jvalati, evameva bhikṣavaḥ karmakleśajanitaṃ vijñānabījaṃ tatratatropapattyāyatanapratisaṃdhau mātuḥ kukṣau nāmarūpāṅkuramabhinirvartayati asvāmikeṣu dharmeṣvaparigraheṣu māyālakṣaṇasvabhāveṣu amameṣu kṛtrimeṣu hetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt ||
