body.translated_text: Just as fire burns when the condition of fuel is present, and does not burn when fuel is lacking — even so, O monks, the consciousness-seed, generated by <s>karma</s> and the afflictions, at the rebirth-linking in one or another birth-destination, produces the sprout of <s>nāmarūpa</s> in the mother's womb, among <s>dharmas</s> that are ownerless, without possession, having the nature characterized by illusion, without 'mine,' fabricated — because of the non-deficiency of causes and conditions. //

body.text: tatrādhyātmikaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ pañcabhiḥ kāraṇairdraṣṭavyaḥ | katamaiḥ pañcabhiḥ? na śāśvatato nocchedato na saṃkrāntitaḥ parīttahetuvipulaphalābhinirvṛttitastatsadṛśānuprabandhataśceti | kathaṃ na śāśvatataḥ? yasmādanye māraṇāntikāḥ skandhāḥ, anye aupapattyaṃśikāḥ skandhāḥ | na tu ya eva māraṇāntikāḥ skandhāsta evaupapattyaṃśikāḥ | api tu māraṇāntikāḥ skandhā nirudhyante, tasminneva ca samaye aupapattyaṃśikāḥ skandhāḥ prādurbhavanti | ato na śāśvatataḥ | kathaṃ nocchedataḥ? na ca pūrvaniruddheṣu māraṇāntikeṣu skandheṣu aupapattyaṃśikāḥ skandhāḥ prādurbhavanti nāpyaniruddheṣu | api tu māraṇāntikāḥ skandhā nirudhyante, tasminneva ca samaye aupapattyaṃśikāḥ skandhāḥ prādurbhavanti tulādaṇḍonnābhāvanāmavat candrabimbapratibimbavat | ato nocchedataḥ | kathaṃ na saṃkrāntitaḥ? visadṛśāḥ sattvanikāyāḥ sabhāgāyāṃ jātyāṃ jātimabhinirvartayanti | ato na saṃkrāntitaḥ | kathaṃ parīttahetuto vipulaphalābhinirvṛttitaḥ | parīttaṃ karma kriyate, vipulaḥ phalavipāko 'nubhūyate | ataḥ parīttahetuto vipulaphalābhinirvṛttitaḥ | kathaṃ tatsadṛśānuprabandhataḥ? yathāvedanīyaṃ karma kriyate, tathāvedanīyo vipāko 'nubhūyate | atastatsadṛśānuprabandhataśca | iti vistaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, internal dependent origination should be seen through five causes. Which five? Not through eternalism, not through annihilationism, not through transmigration, through the production of vast fruit from a small cause, and through the continuation of what is similar to that. How not through eternalism? Because the <s>skandhas</s> at the moment of death are different from the <s>skandhas</s> at the moment of rebirth. It is not the case that the very <s>skandhas</s> at the moment of death are the <s>skandhas</s> at the moment of rebirth. Rather, the <s>skandhas</s> at the moment of death cease, and at that very moment the <s>skandhas</s> at the moment of rebirth come into existence. Therefore, not through eternalism. How not through annihilationism? The <s>skandhas</s> at the moment of rebirth do not come into existence when the <s>skandhas</s> at the moment of death have previously ceased, nor when they have not yet ceased. Rather, the <s>skandhas</s> at the moment of death cease, and at that very moment the <s>skandhas</s> at the moment of rebirth come into existence — like the rising and falling of the arm of a balance, like the moon-disc and its reflection. Therefore, not through annihilationism. How not through transmigration? Dissimilar classes of beings bring about birth in a similar birth-class. Therefore, not through transmigration. How through the production of vast fruit from a small cause? A small <s>karma</s> is performed, [and] a vast ripening of fruit is experienced. Therefore, through the production of vast fruit from a small cause. How through the continuation of what is similar? As the <s>karma</s> is to be experienced, so the ripening is experienced. Therefore, through the continuation of what is similar. Thus the detailed exposition. //

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacitāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau dvādaśāṅgaparīkṣā nāma ṣaḍviṃśatitamaṃ prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter, 'Examination of the Twelve Links' (<s>Dvādaśāṅgaparīkṣā</s>), in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary composed by the venerable <s>Ācārya Candrakīrti</s>. //

body.text:
27
dṛṣṭiparīkṣā saptaviṃśatitamaṃ prakaraṇam |
body.translated_text:
27
'Examination of Views' (<s>Dṛṣṭiparīkṣā</s>), the twenty-seventh chapter.

body.text: yaścaivaṃ pratītyasamutpādaṃ yathābhūtaṃ samyak paśyati, sa na pūrvāntaṃ pratisarati, nāparāntaṃ pratisarati,- ityādi sūtre paṭhayate, tatra katamaḥ pūrvāntaḥ, katamo 'parāntaḥ, kathaṃ na pratisaratīti? tadvayutpatyarthamidamārabhyate | tatra vartamānamātmabhāvamapekṣya atītā ātmabhāvāḥ pūrvānta ityucyate | pūrvo hi janmaparaṃparāṃśaḥ pūrvāntaḥ | taṃ na pratisarati, dṛṣṭiprakārairnālambate | pratītyasamutpādasya yathāvadavasthitatattvadarśanāt nānyathāvasthitaṃ vastu anyathā abhiniviśate | tatra aṣṭau dṛṣṭayaḥ pūrvāntamālambya anyathā pravṛttāḥ | tadyathā-
body.translated_text: And one who thus sees dependent origination correctly, as it truly is — he does not resort to the prior limit (<s>pūrvānta</s>), nor to the posterior limit (<s>aparānta</s>). Thus it is read in the <s>sūtra</s>. Therein, what is the prior limit? What is the posterior limit? How does one not resort [to them]? For the purpose of explaining this, this [chapter] is undertaken. Therein, with reference to the present state of being, past states of being are called the 'prior limit' (<s>pūrvānta</s>). For the prior portion of the succession of births is the prior limit. One 'does not resort to it' — does not grasp it through the various types of views. Because of seeing the reality of dependent origination as it actually is, one does not attach to a thing that is otherwise-situated in an otherwise way. Therein, eight views operate otherwise with reference to the prior limit. Namely:

children.translated_text: 'I existed in the past'; 'I did not exist' — these are the views, /
such as 'the world is eternal' and the rest, that are based on the prior limit. // 1 //

body.text: tatra itiśabdaḥ ādyarthaḥ | athavā dṛṣṭidvayopādānamupalakṣaṇārtham | catastrastvetā dṛṣṭayaḥ | tadyathā- kiṃ nvahamabhūvamatītamadhvānam, nābhūvamatītamadhvānam, abhūvaṃ ca nābhūvaṃ ca, naivābhūvaṃ na nābhūvam, iti | etāścatasro dṛṣṭayaḥ pūrvāntaṃ samāśritāḥ | aparā api catasra ityāha-
body.translated_text: Therein, the word 'iti' has the sense of 'and the rest.' Or it is for the purpose of indicating [that] the taking up of the two views [is representative]. But these are four views. Namely: 'Did I exist in the past? Did I not exist in the past? Did I both exist and not exist? Did I neither exist nor not exist?' These four views are based on the prior limit. And there are four more — hence he says:

body.text: yāstāḥ śāśvatalokādyāḥ
body.translated_text: 'The world is eternal' and the rest —

body.text: pūrvaṃ prasaṅgena upavarṇitāḥ, tā api
body.translated_text: were previously described in passing; they too are

body.text: pūrvāntaṃ samupāśritāḥ ||
body.translated_text: based on the prior limit. //

body.text: tatra yadyapi pūrvāntād dṛṣṭicatuṣṭayāduttaraṃ dṛṣṭicatuṣṭayaṃ nātibhidyate, tathāpi tāvanmātraviśeṣamāśritya pṛthagupādīyate | tacca uttaratra vyākhyāsyāmaḥ | tatra śāśvato lokaḥ ityetat, abhūvamatītamadhvānam, ityetasmānnātibhidyate | athavā ayaṃ viśeṣaḥ- yacchāśvato lokaḥ ityeṣāṃ dṛṣṭiḥ sāmānyena pūrvāntamāśritā | abhūvamatītamadhvānam, ityeṣā tu ātmana eva pūrvāntaparāmarśena pravṛttā, na sāmānyeneti | evamanyāsvapi dṛṣṭiṣu viśeṣo vaktavyaḥ | ityevaṃ tāvat aṣṭāvetā dṛṣṭayaḥ pūrvāntaṃ samupāśritāḥ || 1 ||
body.translated_text: Therein, although the second set of four views regarding the prior limit does not greatly differ from the first set of four views, nevertheless, based on just that much distinction, they are taken up separately. And that we shall explain below. Therein, 'the world is eternal' — this does not greatly differ from 'I existed in the past.' Or, the distinction is this: the view 'the world is eternal' is based on the prior limit in a general way; but 'I existed in the past' operates through the apprehension of the prior limit of the self alone, not in a general way. The same distinction should be stated regarding the other views as well. Thus, these eight views are based on the prior limit. // 1 //

body.text: uktaḥ pūrvāntastadālambikābhirdṛṣṭibhiḥ sārdham | idānīmaparānta ucyate | tatra vartamānamātmabhāvamapekṣya bhāvinaḥ ātmabhāvāḥ aparānta ityucyate | aparo hi janmaparaṃparāṃśo 'parāntaḥ, taṃ na pratisarati, dṛṣṭiprakārairnālambate | pratītyasamutpādasya yathāvadavasthitatattvadarśanāt, nānyathāvasthitaṃ vastu anyathābhiniviśate | tatra aṣṭau dṛṣṭayaḥ aparāntamālambya anyathā pravṛttāḥ | tadyathā-
body.translated_text: The prior limit has been stated together with the views that take it as their object. Now the posterior limit is stated. Therein, with reference to the present state of being, future states of being are called the 'posterior limit' (<s>aparānta</s>). For the later portion of the succession of births is the posterior limit. One 'does not resort to it' — does not grasp it through the various types of views. Because of seeing the reality of dependent origination as it actually is, one does not attach to a thing that is otherwise-situated in an otherwise way. Therein, eight views operate otherwise with reference to the posterior limit. Namely:

children.translated_text: The views 'I shall not exist' and 'What other [will I be]?' in the future time, /
'I shall exist,' and those of finitude and the rest — are based on the posterior limit. // 2 //

body.text: ihāpi dṛṣṭidvayopādānamupalakṣaṇārtham | catastrastvetā dṛṣṭayaḥ | tadyathā- kiṃ nu bhaviṣyāmyanāgatamadhvānam, na bhaviṣyāmi, bhaviṣyāmi ca na bhaviṣyāmi ca, naiva
body.translated_text: Here too, the taking up of two views is for the purpose of indication [of the full set]. But these are four views. Namely: 'Shall I exist in the future? Shall I not exist? Shall I both exist and not exist? Shall I

body.text: bhaviṣyāmi na ca na bhaviṣyāmyanāgatamadhvānam, ityetāścatasro dṛṣṭayaḥ aparāntaṃ samāśritāḥ | kimetā eva catasro dṛṣṭayaḥ aparāntaṃ samāśritāḥ? netyāha | kiṃ tarhi aparā api catasro vidyante antādyā aparāntaṃ samāśritāḥ | tatra antādyāścatasro dṛṣṭayaḥ sāmānyena aparāntamāaśritya pravṛttāḥ, kiṃ tu bhaviṣyāmyanāgatamadhvānamityetāstu ātmana evāparāntamāśritya pravṛttāḥ, ityevaṃ dṛṣṭicatuṣṭayasya viśeṣa iti boddhavyam || 2 ||
body.translated_text: neither exist nor not exist in the future?' These four views are based on the posterior limit. Are only these four views based on the posterior limit? No, he says. Rather, there are four more — those of finitude and the rest — based on the posterior limit. Therein, the four views of finitude and the rest operate with reference to the posterior limit in a general way; but 'I shall exist in the future' and so forth operate with reference to the posterior limit of the self alone. Thus the distinction between the two sets of four views should be understood. // 2 //

body.text: tatra ādyasya tāvat pūrvāntālambikasya dṛṣṭicatuṣṭayasya yathā na saṃbhavaḥ, tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Therein, demonstrating how the first set of four views based on the prior limit does not obtain, he says:

children.translated_text: 'I existed in the past' — this is not tenable. /

children.text: yo hi janmasu pūrveṣu sa eva na bhavatyayam || 3 ||
children.translated_text: For one who was [present] in former births is not this very same [person]. // 3 //

body.text: tatra ya eva atīteṣu janmasu babhūva, yadi sa evāyamadhunā syāt, tadā yuktamasya grahītum- abhūvamahamatītamadhvānamiti | na caitadevaṃ saṃbhavati nityatvaprasaṅgāt, nityasya ca saṃsaraṇānupapatteḥ, ekagatisthasyāpi nānāgatisaṃgṛhītatvaprasaṅgāt | iha hi pūrvaṃ yadi narakādigatiko bhūtvā idānīṃ karmavaicitryāt manuṣyeṣu upapannaḥ evaṃkalpayet- ahamevāsau nāraka āsam iti, tadasya na yuktam | kathaṃ hi nāma manuṣyaḥ san nārakādikaḥ syāt?
body.translated_text: Therein, if the very one who existed in past births were this same one now, then it would be proper to grasp: 'I existed in the past age.' But this is not possible, because it would entail permanence, and because a permanent [self] cannot transmigrate, and because even one established in a single destiny would entail being included in many destinies. For here, if one who was previously in a destiny such as hell and so forth is now, through the diversity of <s>karma</s>, reborn among humans and were to imagine thus: 'I was that very being in hell' — that would not be proper. For how could one who is a human be a hell-being and so forth?

body.text: yattarhi idaṃ paṭhayate sūtre- ahameva sa tena kālena tena samayena māndhātā nāma rājā cakravartī abhūvam iti, tat kathaṃ veditavyamiti? anyatvapratiṣedhaparaṃ tadvacanaṃ naikatvapratipādakamiti vijñeyam | ata eva hi nānyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayeneti paṭhayate | yadi punaḥ sa evāyamiti pūrvakasya cādhunātanasya ca ekatvaṃ syāt, ko doṣaḥ syāt? uktastāvadatra doṣaḥ- nityatvaṃ syāditi || 3 ||
body.translated_text: As for what is recited in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'I myself was at that time, at that period, a king named <s>Māndhātā</s>, a wheel-turning monarch' — how is this to be understood? That statement has the purpose of negating otherness, not of establishing identity. This is to be understood. For precisely [the text] reads: 'It was none other than [I] at that time, at that period.' But if there were identity of the former and the present, what fault would there be? The fault has already been stated: there would be permanence. // 3 //

body.text: tathāpi bhūya ucyate-
body.translated_text: Even so, further it is said:

body.text: sa evātmeti tu bhavedupādānaṃ viśiṣyate |
body.translated_text: If the self were that same one, then the appropriation (<s>upādāna</s>) would be distinguished [while the self would not].

body.text: yadi sa eva pūrvaka ātmāyamidānīṃ syāt, tadā upādānasya pañcaskandhalakṣaṇasya viśeṣo na syāt upādāturaviśeṣātpūrvāvasthāyāmiva | na caivamupādānāviśeṣo 'syātmanaḥ, kiṃ tarhi viśiṣyata eva upādānamupādātuḥ karmabhedāt kārakabhedācca | tataśca upādānaviśeṣāt sa evāyamātmeti na yujyate ||
body.translated_text: If this very former self were the present one, then the appropriation, characterized by the five aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), would not differ — because of the non-difference of the one who appropriates, as in the previous state. But in fact the appropriation of this self does differ; rather, the appropriation is distinguished from the one who appropriates, because of the differentiation of <s>karma</s> and of the agent. And therefore, because of the distinction of the appropriation, 'this is that same self' is not tenable.

body.text: atha manyase- viśiṣyatāmupādānam, ātmā tu eka eveti | ataḥ ātmano 'viśiṣṭatvādabhūmatītamadhvānamityetad bhaviṣyatyeva | ucyate-
body.translated_text: Now, if you think: 'Let the appropriation be distinguished, but the self is one and the same' — [and] therefore, because of the non-difference of the self, the statement 'I existed in the past age' will indeed hold — [reply:]

body.text: upādānavinirmukta ātmā te katamaḥ punaḥ || 4 ||
body.translated_text: What, then, is your self that is free from the appropriation? // 4 //

body.text: yadi hi anyadupādānam, anyaścātmā syāt, tadā upādānaviśeṣe 'pi ātmano 'viśeṣāt syādetadevam | na caitad bhedena darśayituṃ śakyam- ayamasāvātmā, idamasyopādānamiti,
body.translated_text: For if the appropriation were one thing and the self another, then even when the appropriation is distinguished, because of the non-difference of the self, this would be so. But this cannot be demonstrated as separate — 'This is the self, and this is its appropriation' —

body.text: upādānaviśiṣṭasvabhāvatvādātmano 'hetukatvaprasaṅgāt, pṛthaggrahaṇaprasaṅgācca | yadā caivamupādānavinirmukta ātmā darśayituṃ na śakyate, tadā upādānaviśeṣe 'pi ātmāviśeṣa iti na śakyate kalpayitum || 4 ||
body.translated_text: because the self has the nature of being characterized by the appropriation, [and] because [otherwise] there would be the consequence that the self is uncaused, and also the consequence that it could be grasped separately. And when thus the self cannot be shown as free from the appropriation, then it is not possible to imagine that even when the appropriation is distinguished, the self is undistinguished. // 4 //

body.text: athāpi kaścit parikalpayet- satyam, upādānavinirmukta iti evaṃ na saṃbhavati, kimupādānameva ātmatvena parikalpyate iti? etadapi na yuktamiti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, one might imagine: 'True, "free from the appropriation" is not possible in this way — but what if the appropriation itself is imagined to be the self?' This too is not proper. Demonstrating this, he says:

children.translated_text: Given that there is no self free from the appropriation,
the appropriation itself would be the self — but then, according to you, there is no self. // 5 //

body.text: yathā tāvadupādānamevātmā na saṃbhavati tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Demonstrating how the appropriation itself cannot be the self, he says:

children.translated_text: And the appropriation itself is not the self, for it arises and ceases.
How indeed could the appropriation become the one who appropriates? // 6 //

body.text: tatra yadetat pañcopādānaskandhākhyamupādānam, tat pratikṣaṇamutpadyate ca vinaśyati ca | na caivamātmā pratikṣaṇamutpadyate ca vinaśyati ca | ātmā skandhebhyastattvānyatvādinā ca nityānityatvenāpyaśakya eva vaktum, anekadoṣaprasaṅgāt | nityatve hi ātmanaḥ śāśvatavādaḥ syāt, anityatve ca ucchedavādaprasaṅgaḥ | tataśca tadubhayaṃ śāśvatocchedākhyaṃ mahānarthakaramiti nopagantavyam | ataḥ upādānamevātmeti tāvanna yujyate ||
body.translated_text: Therein, this appropriation designated as the five appropriation-aggregates (<s>upādānaskandha</s>) — it arises and perishes at every moment. But the self does not arise and perish at every moment in this way. The self is simply impossible to describe as being identical with or other than the aggregates, or as permanent or impermanent, because of the consequence of many faults. For if the self were permanent, there would be the doctrine of eternalism; if impermanent, the consequence of annihilationism. And therefore, both of these — called eternalism and annihilationism — being productive of great harm, should not be adopted. Therefore, 'the appropriation itself is the self' is not tenable.

body.text: api ca-
body.translated_text: Moreover —

body.text: kathaṃ hi nāmopādānamupādātā bhaviṣyati |
body.translated_text: How indeed could the appropriation become the one who appropriates?

body.text: iha upādīyate ityupādānaṃ karma | tasya ca avaśyamupādātrā upārjakena bhavitavyam | tasya copādānasya yadi ātmatvamiṣyate, tatra upādānameva upādātā ityapi vidyate | tataśca kartṛkarmaṇoraikye sati chetṛcchettavyaghaṭakumbhakārāgnīndhanādīnāmapi aikyaṃ syāt | na caitad dṛṣṭaṃ yuktaṃ vā iti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Here, 'appropriation' is a <s>karma</s> (an object/action) — 'that which is appropriated.' And there must necessarily be an appropriator — an earner [of it]. If the selfhood of the appropriation is accepted, then 'the appropriation itself is the appropriator' — this follows. And from that, since there would be identity of agent and object, there would also be identity of the cutter and what is to be cut, of a pot and a potter, of fire and fuel, and so forth. But this is neither observed nor proper. Demonstrating this, he says:

body.text: kathaṃ hi nāmopādānamupādātā bhaviṣyati | iti |
body.translated_text: How indeed could the appropriation become the one who appropriates? //

body.text: api tu atyantāsaṃbhava evāsya pakṣasyetyabhiprāyaḥ || 6 ||
body.translated_text: Rather, this position is utterly impossible — this is the intended meaning. // 6 //

body.text: atrāha- satyamupādānamātramātmā na yujyate, kiṃ tarhi upādānavyatirikta eva ātmā bhaviṣyati | etadapi na yuktam | kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmāt-
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: True, the appropriation alone is not the self. Rather, the self is different from the appropriation. This too is not proper. For what reason? Because —

children.translated_text: A self other than the appropriation is simply not tenable.

children.text: gṛhyate hyanupādāno yadyanyo na ca gṛhyate || 7 ||
children.translated_text: For if it were other, it would be grasped without the appropriation — but it is not [so] grasped. // 7 //

body.text: yadi upādānādātmā vyatiriktaḥ syāt, gṛhyeta sa upādānavyatiriktaḥ, ghaṭādiva paṭaḥ | na caivaṃ gṛhyate | tasmādupādānavyatirikto 'pi nāsti | anupādānaḥ upādānavyatirekeṇa agṛhyamāṇatvāt khapuṣpavat, ityabhiprāyaḥ || 7 ||
body.translated_text: If the self were distinct from the appropriation, it would be grasped as distinct from the appropriation, like a cloth [is grasped] apart from a pot. But it is not grasped in this way. Therefore, there is no self distinct from the appropriation either. [The self] without appropriation [would be] like a flower in the sky, since it is not grasped apart from the appropriation. This is the intended meaning. // 7 //

body.text: idānīṃ yathopapāditamarthaṃ nigamayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, concluding the very meaning as demonstrated, he says:

body.text:
evaṃ nānya upādānānna copādānameva saḥ |
ātmā nāstyanupādānaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus the self is neither other than the appropriation, nor is it the appropriation itself. The self does not exist without appropriation,

body.text: atha syāt- yadi ātmā upādānasvarūpo na bhavati, upādānopādātrorekatvaprasaṅgāt | udayavyayaprasaṅgācca | sa hi anyo 'pi na bhavati upādānamanapekṣya bhedena grahaṇaprasaṅgāt | na cāpyanupādānaḥ, upādānanirapekṣasya grahaṇaprasaṅgāt | evaṃ tarhi nāsti ātmetyastu | ucyate-
body.translated_text: Now one might say: if the self is not of the nature of the appropriation — because of the consequence of identity of appropriation and appropriator, and the consequence of arising and ceasing — and if it is not other either — because of the consequence of being grasped without regard to the appropriation — and if it is not without appropriation — because of the consequence of being grasped independently of the appropriation — then, let it be that the self does not exist. [Reply:]

body.text: nāpi nāstyeṣa niścayaḥ || 8 ||
body.translated_text: nor is 'it does not exist' a certainty. // 8 //

body.text: yo hi nāma skandhānupādāya prajñapyate, sa kathaṃ nāstīti syāt? na hi avidyamāno vandhyātanayaḥ skandhānupādāya prajñapyate | kathaṃ sati upādāne upādātā nāstīti yujyate | tasmānnāstitvamapyasya na yujyate | tasmānnāsti ātmeti niścayo 'pyeṣa nopapadyate | asya tvātmano vyavasthānaṃ vistareṇa madhyamakāvatārādavaseyam | ihāpi ca pūrvameva sthānasthāneṣu kṛtā vyavastheti na punariha tadvayavasthāne yatna āsthīyate || 8 ||
body.translated_text: For that which is designated in dependence on the aggregates — how could it be said not to exist? For a non-existent son of a barren woman is not designated in dependence on the aggregates. How is it proper that there is no appropriator when there is appropriation? Therefore, non-existence too is not proper for this [self]. Therefore, the certainty that 'the self does not exist' is also not tenable. But the determination of this self should be understood in detail from the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s>. And here too, the determination has already been made at the appropriate places earlier, therefore no effort is made here again for that determination. // 8 //

body.text: evaṃ tāvadabhūvamatītamadhvānamityeṣā kalpanā nopapadyate | idānīṃ nābhūvamatītamadhvānamityedapi yathā nopapadyate tathā pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Thus, the imagining 'I existed in the past age' is not tenable. Now, demonstrating how 'I did not exist in the past age' too is not tenable, he says:

children.translated_text: 'I did not exist in the past age' — this is not tenable.

children.text: yo hi janmasu pūrveṣu tato 'nyo na bhavatyayam || 9 ||
children.translated_text: For one who was in previous births is not other than this one now. // 9 //

body.text: yadi pūrvakādātmanaḥ asya adhunātanasya ātmano 'nyatvaṃ syāt, tadānīṃ nābhūmatītamadhvānamiti syāt | na caitadevaṃ saṃbhavati | tasmānnābhūvamatītamadhvānamityetannopapadyate || 9 ||
body.translated_text: If there were otherness of this present self from the former self, then 'I did not exist in the past age' would be [tenable]. But this is not possible in this way. Therefore 'I did not exist in the past age' is not tenable. // 9 //

body.text: yadi punaḥ pūrvakādātmanaḥ asya anyatvaṃ syāt, ko doṣa iti? ucyate-
body.translated_text: If, however, there were otherness of this [self] from the former self, what fault would there be? [Reply:]

children.text: yadi hyayaṃ bhavedanyaḥ pratyākhyāyāpi taṃ bhavet |
children.translated_text: If this one were other, he would exist even having repudiated that [former self].

children.text: tathaiva ca sa saṃtiṣṭhettatra jāyeta vāmṛtaḥ || 10 ||
children.translated_text: And likewise, that [former self] would remain; or he would be born there immortal. // 10 //

body.text: yadi hi ayamadhunātana ātmā pūrvakādātmanaḥ anyaḥ syāt, tadā taṃ pūrvakamātmānaṃ pratyākhyāya parityajya tannirapekṣaḥ ataddhetuka eva syāt | kiṃ cānyat | tathaiva ca sa saṃtiṣṭhettatra yadi pūrvakādātmanaḥ asya anyatvaṃ syāt, tadā anyatvād ghaṭotpāde paṭāvināśavat pūrvasyātmanā uttarasminnapi ātmani samutpadyamāne 'pi anirodhaḥ syāt | aniruddhatvācca yatra pūrvaṃ devamanuṣyādijanmasu upapannaḥ, yena varṇasaṃsthānādinā pūrvamupalabhyamānaḥ, tenaiva prakāreṇa tathaiva sa tatrāvatiṣṭheta tathaivāvatiṣṭheteti | tasmānnābhūvamatītamadhvānamityetannopapadyate ||
body.translated_text: If this present self were other than the former self, then, having repudiated — having abandoned — that former self, [this self] would exist independently of it, uncaused by it. What is more — 'And likewise, that [former self] would remain there' — if there were otherness of this [self] from the former self, then, just as when a pot arises the destruction of a cloth does not [follow], because of their otherness, so too even when this subsequent self arises, the former self would not cease. And because of not ceasing, where it was previously born — in births as <s>devas</s>, humans, and so forth — by whatever form, configuration, and so forth it was formerly perceived, in that very manner it would remain there. Therefore 'I did not exist in the past age' is not tenable.

body.text: atrāha- tatra yaduktam-
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: Regarding what was stated —

body.text: yadi hyayaṃ bhavedanyaḥ pratyākhyāyāpi taṃ bhavet | iti,
body.translated_text: 'If this one were other, he would exist even having repudiated that [former self]' —

body.text: yadi puna pūrvakamātmānaṃ pratyākhyāya [ayamiha bhavet, ko doṣaḥ syāt? tatra doṣā bahavaḥ syuḥ | kathamiti cet, yasmādevaṃ sati-
body.translated_text: if, having repudiated the former self, [this one] were to exist here, what fault would there be? Many faults would follow. How so? Because, this being the case —

children.translated_text: There would be the annihilation of <s>karmas</s> [and their] destruction; and of <s>karmas</s> done by another,
there would be the experience by another — and so forth would follow. // 11 //

body.text: yadi pūrvakamātmānaṃ pratyākhyāya ayamātmā bhavet, tadā] pūrvakasya ātmanaḥ tatra naṣṭatvād, iha ca anyasyaiva cotpādanātpūrvakasyātmana ucchedaḥ syāt | tasmiṃśca ātmani ucchinne karmaṇāmadattaphalānāmevāśrayavicchedena vicchedāt, bhoktaścābhāvānnāśa eva syāt | atha pūrvakenātmanā kṛtasya karmaṇaḥ uttareṇātmanā phalaparibhogaḥ parikalpyate, tathāpi anyena kṛtasya karmaṇaḥ phalasya anyenopabhogaḥ syāt | tataśca-
body.translated_text: If, having repudiated the former self, this self were to exist, then, since the former self would be destroyed there and an entirely different one arises here, there would be the annihilation of the former self. And when that self is annihilated, since <s>karmas</s> that have not [yet] given their fruit are cut off through the severance of their support, and since the experiencer is absent, there would simply be destruction. And if it is imagined that the fruit of <s>karma</s> done by the former self is experienced by the subsequent self, even so, there would be the enjoyment by another of the fruit of <s>karma</s> done by another. And from that —

body.text: akṛtābhyāgamabhayaṃ syātkarmākṛtakaṃ yadi |
body.translated_text: there would be the fear of encountering [the fruit of] what was not done, if <s>karma</s> were unperformed —

body.text: ityevamādi aniṣṭamāpadyate || 11 ||
body.translated_text: and so forth, undesirable [consequences] would follow. // 11 //

body.text: api ca | yadi ayamātmā pūrvakādātmanaḥ anya eva atropapannaḥ syāt, tadā pūrvamabhūtvā paścādutpanna iti syāt | na caitadyuktamiti pratipādayannāha-
body.translated_text: Moreover, if this self, being entirely other than the former self, were born here, then it would be 'having not existed before, [it] subsequently arose.' And this is not proper. Demonstrating this, he says:

children.translated_text: Nor is it [tenable that the self] has come into being having not existed before, for a fault follows:
the self would be either manufactured, or it would have arisen without a cause. // 12 //

body.text: iti | yadi hi ātmā pūrvamabhūtvā paścādutpannaḥ syāt, tadā kṛtaka eva ātmā syāt | na ca kṛtaka ātmeṣyate, anityatvaprasaṅgāt | vyatiriktasya ca tanniṣpādakasya karturabhāvāt kutaḥ kṛtakatvamātmano yojyeta? kṛtake cātmani parikalpyamāne ādimān saṃsāraḥ syādeva, apūrvasattvasya prādurbhāvaśca | na caitadevam | tasmānna kṛtaka ātmā | api ca | saṃbhūto vāpyahetukaḥ | abhūtvā prāgātmā samutpadyamāno nirhetuka evopapadyate | pūrvaṃ hi ātmā nāstīti akṛtako nirhetukaḥ syāt | vāśabdo vikalpe | kṛtako vā bhavedātmā yadi vā nābhūvamatītamadhvānamityetannābhyupeyam | saṃbhūto vāpyahetukaḥ, yadi vā-
body.translated_text: For if the self, having not existed before, subsequently arose, then the self would be manufactured. But a manufactured self is not accepted, because it would entail impermanence. And since there is no distinct maker who would produce it, how could the manufactured nature of the self be justified? And if a manufactured self is imagined, <s>saṃsāra</s> would have a beginning, and there would be the appearance of a previously non-existent being. But this is not so. Therefore the self is not manufactured. Moreover: 'Or it would have arisen without a cause.' A self that arises having not existed before is simply established as uncaused. For since the self did not exist before, it would be uncreated [and] uncaused. The particle 'or' (<s>vā</s>) is for [presenting] an alternative. Either the self would be manufactured, or else the [view] 'I did not exist in the past age' should not be accepted; either 'it would have arisen without a cause,' or else —

body.text: nābhūmatītamadhvānamityetannopapadyate |
body.translated_text: 'I did not exist in the past age' — this is not tenable.

body.text: ityabhyupagamyatām || 12 ||
body.translated_text: — this should be accepted. // 12 //

body.text: idānīṃ yathopavarṇitamevārthaṃ nigamayannāha-
body.translated_text: Now, concluding the very meaning as described, he says:

children.translated_text: Thus, the view regarding the past — 'I did not exist,' 'I did exist,'
'both,' and 'neither' — this is not tenable. // 13 //

body.text: evaṃ yathopavarṇitena nyāyena abhūmatītamadhvānamiti yā dṛṣṭiḥ, eṣāpi naivopapadyate | etaddvayasyābhāvācca ubhayamapi nopapadyate | kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmād dvayaṃ hyetatsamāhatamubhayamiti kalpyate | ekaikasya ca pṛthakpṛthagabhāvāt kutastatsamāhāra iti ubhayamapi na saṃbhavati |
body.translated_text: Thus, by the reasoning as described, the view 'I existed in the past age' is also not tenable. And because of the non-existence of both of these, 'both' too is not tenable. For what reason? Because 'both' is imagined as the combination of two. And since each individually does not exist separately, whence the combination? Therefore 'both' too is not possible.

body.text: ubhayasyābhāvāt kutastatpratiṣedhena nobhayaṃ bhaviṣyatīti? tasmānnaivābhūvaṃ na nābhūvamityetadapi nopapadyate || 13 ||
body.translated_text: And because of the non-existence of 'both,' how, through the negation of that, will 'neither' come about? Therefore 'I neither existed nor did not exist' — this too is not tenable. // 13 //

body.text: tadevaṃ pūrvāntaṃ samāśritasya dṛṣṭicatuṣṭayasya asaṃbhavamudbhāvya idānīmaparāntasamāśritasya pratiṣedhamāha-
body.translated_text: Having thus brought out the impossibility of the tetrad of views based on the past, now he states the refutation of [views] based on the future:

children.translated_text: The views 'Will I exist in the future age?'
and 'Will I not exist?' — these are the same as [those regarding] the past age. // 14 //

body.text: yathaiva hi atīte 'dhvani dṛṣṭicatuṣṭayaṃ niṣiddham, evamanāgate 'pyadhvani dṛṣṭicatuṣṭayaṃ niṣedhanīyamuktapāṭhaparivartanena | tadyathā-

children.text: aiṣyajanmani yo bhāvo sa eva na bhavatyayam ||

body.text: ityevamādinā sarvaṃ samaṃ yojyamekatvapratiṣedhe | evamanyatvapratiṣedhe 'pi samaṃ yojyam-

na syāmanāgate kāle ityetannopapadyate
aiṣya janmani yo bhāvo tato 'nyo na bhavatyayam ||
ityevamādinā pūrvaślokapāṭhaparivartanena || 14 ||
idānīṃ pūrvāntaṃ samāśritasya śāśvatādidṛṣṭicatuṣṭayasya pratiṣedhārthamāha-

children.text: sa devaḥ sa manuṣyaścedevaṃ bhavati śāśvatam |
anutpannaśca devaḥ syājjāyate na hi śāśvatam || 15 ||

body.text: iha hi kaścinmanuṣyagatisthaḥ kuśalaṃ karma kṛtvā devagatiṃ gacchati | tatra yadi sa eva devaḥ sa eva manuṣya iti evamubhayoraikyaṃ syāt, tadā śāśvataṃ syāt | na caitadevaṃ yadeva eva manuṣyo bhavediti | ato nāsti kiṃcicchāśvatam | api ca | śāśvatavāde sati asamutpannaśca devaḥ syāt | kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmājjāyate na hi śāśvatam | yaddhi vastu śāśvatam, tadvidyamānatvānnaiva jāyate | tataśca anutpanno devaḥ syāt, anutpanno devo na yujyate iti || evaṃ tāvacchāśvataṃ na yujyate || 15 ||
idānīmaśāśvatamapi yathā na saṃbhavati tathā pratipādayannāha-

yadi hi anyo devo 'nyaśca manuṣyaḥ syāt, tadā pūrvakasya manuṣyātmanastatra naṣṭatvādiha ca anyasyaivotpādāt sa pūrvako manuṣyātmā tatra vinaṣṭa ityaśāśvataṃ syāt | tatsaṃtānānuvṛttyā nāśāśvatamiti cet, ucyate-
devādanyo manuṣyaścetsaṃtatirnopapadyate |
yadi devādanyo manuṣyo bhavet, tadā yathā nimbasya na āmratarusaṃtāno bhavati, evaṃ manuṣyasya devaḥ ekasaṃtānapatito na syāt | tataśca pūrvakasya vināśādaśāśvatameva bhavet | athavā |

yadi devādanyo manuṣyo bhavet, tadā saṃtānānuvṛttirna syāt | asti ceyaṃ saṃtānānuvṛttiḥ devasya manuṣyaḥ ekasaṃtānapatita iti | tasmāt saṃtānābhāvaprasaṅgāt devādanyo manuṣyo na bhavati | yataścaivam, ato 'śāśvatamapi nāsti || 16 ||
idānīṃ śāśvatāśāśvatapratiṣedhārthamāha-
divyo yadyekadeśaḥ syādekadeśaśca mānuṣaḥ

children.text: aśāśvataṃ śāśvataṃ ca bhavettacca na yujyate || 17 ||

body.text: yadi ayaṃ manuṣyaḥ aṃśena manuṣyatāṃ vijahyāt, aṃśena vihāya manuṣyatāṃ devātmabhāvamupādadyāt, tadā ekadeśasya nāśādaśāśvataṃ syāt, ekadeśasya ca avasthānācchāśvataṃ syāt | etacca ayuktaṃ yadekasya divyagatisaṃgṛhītaḥ ekadeśaḥ syāt, ekadeśaśca manuṣyaḥ syāt | tasmācchāśvataṃ ca aśāśvataṃ ca etadubhayaṃ nopapadyate || 17 ||
idānīṃ naśāśvatanaivāśāśvatadṛṣṭipratiṣedhārthamāha-

yadi śāśvataṃ kiṃcidvastu syāt, tadā paścādaśāśvatadarśanānnaiva śāśvatamiti syāt | evaṃ yadi kiṃcidaśāśvataṃ syāt, tadā tasya paścācchāśvatopapattito nāśāśvatamiti syāt | yadā tu śāśvatāśāśvatamevāprasiddham, tadā kutastatpratiṣedhena naivaśāśvataṃ nāśāśvatam syāditi? tasmādetadapyayuktam || 18 ||

atha syāt- anādijanmamaraṇaparaṃparāpravṛttamavicchinnakamaṃ saṃsāraprabandhamupalabhya śāśvata mātmānaṃ parikalpayāmaḥ | astyasau śāśvataḥ kaścit padārthaḥ, yo hi nāma evamanādimati saṃsāre paribhramannadyāpyupalabhyate iti | ucyate | etadapi nopapadyate | kiṃ kāraṇam? yo hi nāma-

children.text: yadi tasmādanādistu saṃsāraḥ syānna cāsti saḥ || 19 ||

body.text: yadi hi saṃskārāṇāmātmano va kutaścidgatyantarād gamanaṃ gatyantaramāgamanaṃ syāt, tataśca gantyantarāt punaḥ kvacid gamanaṃ syāt, tadānīmanādiḥ saṃsāraḥ syāt | na ca kutaścit kasyacidāgamanaṃ saṃbhavati, nityasya vā anityasya vā āgamanānupapatteḥ | na cāpi itaḥ punaḥ kasyacit kvacid gamanaṃ saṃbhavati, nityasya vā anityasya gamanānupapatteḥ | yadā caivaṃ na saṃbhavati, tadā kuto janmamaraṇaparaṃparāyā atidīrghatvena ādyanupalambhādanādimān saṃsāraḥ syāt? saṃsarturabhāvāt kutaḥ anādimattvamādimatvaṃ vā saṃsārasya saṃbhavet? yadā ca na saṃbhavati, tadā yaduktam- astyasau śāśvataḥ kaścitpadārthaḥ, yo hi nāma evamanādimati saṃsāre paribhramannadyāpyupalabhyate iti, tanna yuktam ||
ataśca, evaṃ yathoditanyāyena-

yadā caivaṃ śāśvata eva padārtho na saṃbhavati, tadā kasya vigamanādaśāśvataḥ syāt | śāśvatāśāśvatānupalambhācca kutaḥ ubhayaṃ kuto nobhayamiti? tasmādevaṃ śāśvatādidṛṣṭicatuṣṭayaṃ pūrvānte saṃsārasya na saṃbhavati || 20 ||
idānīmantānantādicatuṣṭayamaparānte yathā na saṃbhavati, tathā pratipādayannāha-

children.text: antavān yadi lokaḥ syātparalokaḥ kathaṃ bhavet |

body.text: yadi hi antavān, vināśādūrdhvaṃ pūrvaloko na syāt, tadā paraloko na syāt asti ca paraloka iti antavāṃlloka iti nopapadyate | athāpi anantavāṃllokaḥ syāt, tadānīmapi paralokaḥ kathaṃ bhavet? naiva paralokaḥ syādityabhiprāyaḥ | na ca paraloko nāsti | ataḥ paralokasadbhāvādantavānapi loko na bhavati || 21 ||
idānīmantavattvamanantavatvaṃ ca ubhayametallokasya yathā na saṃbhavati, tathā pratipādayannāha-

pūrvottarahetuphalabhāvasaṃbandhanairantaryāvicchinnakamavartī yasmādayaṃ pradīpavat pratikṣaṇavināśī skandhasaṃtānaḥ pravartate, tasmāddhetuphalapravṛttidarśanānnāntavattvaṃ nānantavattvaṃ ca yujyate || 22 ||
kathaṃ kṛtvā?

yadi pūrve manuṣyaskandhā naśyeyuḥ, tāṃśca pratītya uttare devagatyupapattisaṃgṛhītā nopapadyeran, tadā antavān loko bhavet tailavartikṣayaniruddhapradīpavat | uttarātmabhāvotpādānnāsti antavattvam || 23 ||

atha yadi pūrvakāḥ skandhā na naśyeṣuḥ, tān pratītya uttare phalabhūtāḥ skandhā notpadyeran tadā ananto 'vināśī lokaḥ syāt svarūpādapracyutatvāt | yadā tu pūrvakāḥ skandhā nirudhyante taddhetukāścāpare skandhā uttarakālaṃ jāyante, tadā pūrvakānāmanavasthānāt kuto 'nantavattvaṃ saṃsārasya syāt? || 24 ||
idānīṃ tṛtīyamubhayapakṣabhāvaṃ pratipādayannāha-

yadi hi kasyacidekadeśasya vināśaḥ syāt, ekadeśasya ca gatyantaragamanaṃ syāt, yāttadānīmantavāṃśca loko 'nantavāṃśca | na caitadevaṃ saṃbhavati yadekadeśo naśyati, ekadeśo na naśyatīti | ataḥ antavāṃśca anantavāṃśca loka iti na yujyate || 25 ||
kasmāt punarekadeśasya vināśaḥ ekadeśasya cāvasthānaṃ na yujyate iti pratipādayannāha-
kathaṃ tāvadupādāturekadeśo vinaṅkṣyate|

children.text: na naṅkṣyate caikadeśa evaṃ caitanna yujyate || 26 ||

body.text: iha ekadeśasya vināśe ekadeśasya cāvasthāne parikalpyamāne yadi vā upādāturekadeśasya vināśaḥ avasthānaṃ vā parikalpyeta, yadi vā upādānasya? tatra yadi tāvadupādāturekadeśasya vināśaḥ ekadeśasya cāvasthānaṃ parikalpyate, tanna yujyate | kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmāt-

kathaṃ tāvadupādāturekadeśo vinaṅkṣyate |
na naṅkṣyate caikadeśaḥ
naiva hi atra kācidupapattirasti yayā ekadeśasya vināśamekadeśasya cāvināśaṃ parikalpayiṣyāmaḥ | ata eva upapattimapaśyannācārya āha-
evaṃ caitanna yujyate || iti |

athavā | upādātā hi nāma ātmā | sa ca skandheṣu pañcadhā mṛgyamāṇo na saṃbhavati | yaśca na saṃbhavati, tasya kathamekadeśo vinaṅkṣyate, ekadeśaśca na naṅkṣyate? ata evāha- evaṃ caitanna yujyate iti | athavā yadi upādāturekadeśo naśyedekadeśaśca na naśyet, tadā ekasyaiva upādāturdevatvamaṃśenānyena manuṣyatvaṃ syāt | na caitadiṣyate ityāha- evaṃ caitanna yujyate iti | evaṃ tāvadupādāturantavattvamanantavattvaṃ ca na yuktamiti || 26 ||
idānīmupādānasyāpi yathā na saṃbhavati tathā pratipādayannāha-
upādātṛvadetadapi vyākhyeyam || 27 ||
tadevamubhayadarśanāsaṃbhavaṃ pratipādya idānīṃ yathā nobhayamapi na saṃbhavati tathā pratipādayannāha-

pratiṣedhyasya vastuno 'saṃbhavāt pratiṣedhasyāpyasaṃbhava iti | ataḥ antavattve ca anantavattve ca ubhayasminnapratīte kasya pratiṣedhena naivāntavān nānantavān lokaḥ iti dṛṣṭisaṃbhavaḥ syāditi || 28 ||

evaṃ tāvat sāṃvṛtaṃ pratibimbākāramupādātāramupādānaṃ cābhyupetyāpi śāśvatādidṛṣṭayasaṃbhavaṃ pratipādya idānīṃ sarvathā bhāvasvabhāvānupalambhena bandhyāputraśyāmagauratādivat śāśvatādidṛṣṭīnāmasaṃbhavaṃ pratipipādayiṣurāha-
body.translated_text: Thus, having first accepted conventionally the appropriator and appropriation in the form of a reflection, and having demonstrated the impossibility of views such as eternalism and the rest, now, wishing to demonstrate the impossibility of views such as eternalism through the complete non-apprehension of the own-nature of entities in every way — like the dark or fair complexion of a barren woman's son — he says:

children.translated_text: Or alternatively, because all entities are empty, the views of eternalism and the rest — /
where, for whom, which ones, and from what cause will they arise? // 29 //

body.text: iha sarvabhāvānāṃ pratītyasamutpannatvāt śūnyatvaṃ sakalena śāstreṇa pratipāditam | tataśca sarvabhāvānāṃ śūnyatvāt katamāstāḥ sarvabhāvabāhyāḥ śāśvatādyā dṛṣṭayo bhaviṣyanti, yāḥ kaścid grahīṣyati yatastannirākaraṇamārapsyāmahe? tathā kiṃ vā ālambanaṃ yat sarvabhāvānantargataṃ yatraitā dṛṣṭaya utpatsyante yatraitā dṛṣṭīrnivārayiṣyāmaḥ? katamaścāsau bhāvaḥ pudgalo vā sarvabhāvabāhyāḥ yasyaitā dṛṣṭayaḥ utpatsyante yaṃ dṛṣṭibhyo nivārayiṣyāmaḥ? kiṃ vā dṛṣṭīnāmutpattikāraṇamālambananimittaṃ sarvabhāvabāhyaṃ yasmānnimittādutpadyamānāḥ śāśvatādikāḥ dṛṣṭīḥ vārayiṣyāmaḥ? sarveṣāmeva hi padārthānāṃ sarvabhāvāntargatatvāt śūnyatvam, śūnyatvācca sarve eva hi te padārthā nopalabhyanta iti,
body.translated_text: Here, the emptiness of all entities has been demonstrated by the entire treatise, because they are dependently arisen. And since all entities are empty, which views of eternalism and the rest — being outside all entities — will there be, that someone will grasp, and for the refutation of which we would undertake? Likewise, what object — not included among all entities — is there, in which these views would arise, and in which we would prevent these views? And what entity or <s>pudgala</s> (person) — outside all entities — is there, for whom these views would arise, and whom we would restrain from views? And what cause or objective condition for the arising of views — outside all entities — is there, on account of which condition we would prevent the arising of views of eternalism and the rest? For since all things whatsoever are included among all entities, they are empty; and since they are empty, all those things whatsoever are simply not apprehended. Thus:

body.text: kva kasya katamāḥ kasmātsaṃbhaviṣyanti dṛṣṭayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Where, for whom, which ones, and from what cause will views arise? /

body.text: naiva kāścit, naiva kvacit, naiva kasyacit, nāpi kenacidākāreṇa saṃbhaviṣyantītyabhiprāyaḥ | asaṃbhave ca sati āsāṃ parikalpanaiva notpadyate ityayuktā evaitā dṛṣṭayaḥ || 29 ||
body.translated_text: None whatsoever, nowhere whatsoever, for no one whatsoever, and in no manner whatsoever will they arise — this is the intended meaning. And when they cannot arise, the very conceptual construction of these [views] does not come about — thus these views are simply untenable. // 29 //

body.text: tadevam-
body.translated_text: Thus indeed —

children.translated_text: He who taught the true <s>Dharma</s> for the abandonment of all views, /
out of compassion — to that <s>Gautama</s> I pay homage. // 30 //

body.text: tatra saṃsāranirvāṇaprahāṇādhigamopalambhaprapātapatanasaṃdhāraṇāt dharmaḥ | satāmāryāṇāṃ kṛtakāryāṇāṃ dharmaḥ saddharmaḥ | yadi vā śobhano dharmaḥ saddharmaḥ, sakalasaṃsāraduḥkhakṣayakaratvena praśaṃsanīyatvāt || yaḥ saddharmam-
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>Dharma</s> is that which, through the comprehension of the abandonment and attainment of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>, sustains [beings] from falling into the precipice. The <s>Dharma</s> of the good ones — the noble ones who have accomplished their task — is the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharma</s>). Alternatively, the good <s>Dharma</s> is the true <s>Dharma</s>, because it is praiseworthy on account of bringing about the complete exhaustion of all the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>. He who [taught] the true <s>Dharma</s> —

children.translated_text: non-cessation, non-arising, non-annihilation, non-permanence, /
non-plurality-of-meaning, non-singularity-of-meaning, non-coming, non-going, //

body.text: prapañcopaśamaṃ śivaṃ pratītyasamutpādasaṃjñayā hi deśitavān sarvadṛṣṭiprahāṇārthaṃ jagatāmanukampāmupādāya mahākaruṇāmevāśritya priyaikaputrādhikatarapremapātrasakalatribhuvanajanaḥ na lābhasatkārapratyupakārādilipsayā, taṃ namasyāmi niruttaramadvitīyaṃ śāstāram | kiṃnāmadheyam? gautamam | paramarṣigotrasaṃbhūtamityarthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: — the pacification of conceptual proliferation, the auspicious — taught under the designation of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), for the purpose of the abandonment of all views, out of compassion for the world — having relied solely on great compassion, he for whom all beings in the three worlds are objects of love surpassing even [the love for] a dearest only son, not out of desire for gain, honor, reciprocation, or the like — to him I pay homage, the unsurpassed, incomparable teacher. By what name? <s>Gautama</s>. The meaning is: born in the lineage of the supreme <s>ṛṣis</s>.

body.text: yathoktamāryaśālistambasūtre āryamaitreyeṇa mahābodhisattvena-
body.translated_text: As stated in the noble <s>Śālistambasūtra</s> by the noble <s>Maitreya</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>:

body.text: ya imaṃ pratītyasamutpādamevaṃ yathābhūtaṃ samyakprajñayā satatasamitamajīvaṃ nirjīvaṃ yathāvadaviparītamajātamabhūtamakṛtamasaṃskṛtamapratighamanāvaraṇaṃ śivamabhayamanāhāryamavyayamavyupaśamasvabhāvaṃ paśyati asatastucchataḥ riktato 'sārato rogato gaṇḍataḥ śalyato 'ghato 'nityato duḥkhataḥ śūnyato 'nātmataḥ, na sa pūrvāntaṃ pratisarati | kiṃ nvahamabhūvamatīte 'dhvani, āhosvinnābhūvamatīte 'dhvani, ko nvahamabhūvamatīte 'dhvani, kathaṃ nvahamabhūvamatīte 'dhvani | aparāntaṃ vā punarna pratisarati kiṃ nvahaṃ bhaviṣyāmyanāgate 'dhvani,
body.translated_text: 'One who sees this dependent origination thus as it truly is — with correct wisdom, constantly, continuously — as without a living principle, without a life-force, as it actually is, without distortion, as unborn, as unproduced, as unmade, as unconditioned, as unobstructed, as unimpeded, as auspicious, as fearless, as unassailable, as imperishable, as having the nature of non-cessation — sees it as unreal, as vain, as hollow, as without essence, as a disease, as a boil, as a thorn, as a misfortune, as impermanent, as suffering, as empty, as non-self — he does not run back to the past [thinking]: "Did I exist in the past, or did I not exist in the past? What was I in the past? How was I in the past?" Nor does he run forward to the future [thinking]: "Will I exist in the future?

body.text: āhosvinna bhaviṣyāmyanāgate 'dhvani, ko nu bhaviṣyāmyanāgate 'dhvani, kathaṃ nu bhaviṣyāmyanāgate 'dhvani | pratyutpannaṃ vā punarna pratisarati kiṃ nvidaṃ kathaṃ nvidaṃ ke santaḥ ke bhaviṣyāmaḥ ayaṃ sattvaḥ kutaṃ āgataḥ, sa itaścyutaḥ kutra gamiṣyatīti yānyekeṣāṃ śramaṇabrāhmaṇānāṃ pṛthagloke dṛṣṭigatāni bhaviṣyanti tadyathā- ātmavādapratisaṃyuktāni jīvavādapratisaṃyuktāni kautukamaṅgalapratisaṃyuktāni, tānyasya tasmin samaye prahīṇāni bhavanti parijñātāni samucchinnamūlāni tālamastakavadanābhāsagatāni āyatyāmanutpādānirodhadharmāṇi ||
body.translated_text: Will I not exist in the future? What will I be in the future? How will I be in the future?" Nor does he run back to the present [thinking]: "What is this? How is this? Being what, what will we become? This being — from where has it come? Having departed from here, where will it go?" — whatever views certain <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> in the world at large may have, such as those connected with the doctrine of self, those connected with the doctrine of a life-force, and those connected with superstitious omens and rituals — these are for him at that time abandoned, fully understood, cut off at the root, made like the top of a palm tree, brought to a state of non-appearance, having the nature of non-arising and non-cessation in the future.

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputro maitreyasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bhāṣitamabhinandya anupramodya utthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ, prakrāntāste ca bhikṣava iti ||
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, having rejoiced in and expressed his appreciation for the words of <s>Maitreya</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, rose from his seat and departed. Those monks too departed.' //

body.text: ityācāryacandrakīrtipādoparacitāyāṃ prasannapadāyāṃ madhyamakavṛttau dṛṣṭiparīkṣā nāma saptaviṃśatitamaṃ prakaraṇaṃ samāptam ||
body.translated_text: Thus concludes the twenty-seventh chapter, the Examination of Views, in the <s>Prasannapadā</s>, the <s>Madhyamaka</s> commentary composed by the venerable <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Candrakīrti</s>.

body.text: || samāptaṃ cedaṃ madhyamakaśāstraṃ sakalalaukikalokottarapravacananītaneyārthavyākhyānanaipuṇya viśāradaṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhānuttarasamyaksaṃbuddhabodhimaṇḍāsanadāyakamiti ||
body.translated_text: Thus is completed this <s>Madhyamaka</s> treatise, endowed with expertise in the elucidation of the definitive and provisional meanings of all mundane and supramundane discourses, the bestower of the seat of awakening of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and unsurpassed perfect <s>Buddhas</s>.
